apical_ectodermal_ridge.name: Apical ectodermal ridge (AER)
apical_ectodermal_ridge.summary: The AER is the pseudostratified ectodermal thickening at the distal limb bud tip that maintains outgrowth by secreting FGF4/FGF8; it is maintained in turn by mesenchymal FGF10 (min1998). Its atlas relevance is confined to one result: an allelic series reducing AER Fgf4/Fgf8 in mouse deletes PROXIMAL skeletal elements while distal elements survive, which excludes the simple timer reading of the AER and shows FGF acts instructively on proximodistal identity and on survival of the proximal domain (mariani2008). The consequence for the postnatal plate is therefore that the AER determines which elements exist and what positional identity they carry, and it stops signalling long before any growth plate forms. No AER manipulation has been carried through to a postnatal growth plate measurement in any species, and there is no human AER data at all. This node is deliberately not a signalling review: FGF ligand-receptor mechanism belongs to L3.
apical_ectodermal_ridge.human_evidence_note: No human AER experiment exists; human relevance is inferred from the conserved consequence of limb-field disruption in congenital limb reduction defects.
apical_ectodermal_ridge.translation_risk_reason: Avian and murine embryology only, and the readout is limb morphology at birth rather than any growth plate parameter.
localization: chick and mouse distal limb bud ectoderm, E9.5-E12.5 mouse: confirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Genetic reduction of AER Fgf4/Fgf8 deletes proximal rather than distal limb elements, showing an instructive not permissive role
Fgf10 is required to induce and maintain the AER; without it the bud regresses

bone_collar_formation.name: Bone collar formation
bone_collar_formation.summary: The bone collar is the cuff of intramembranous bone laid down by the perichondrium around the hypertrophic midshaft, and it is the first bone in a long bone. Its formation requires Indian hedgehog: Ihh-null mice fail to form a bone collar and additionally show disorganised chondrocyte proliferation and premature hypertrophy (stjacques1999), which makes IHH the coupling point between the cartilage template and its osseous sleeve. Two inheritances follow into the postnatal plate. First, the collar is the mechanical constraint that converts diffuse cartilage swelling into directional elongation, and the perichondrium at the plate periphery persists postnatally as the groove of Ranvier and the perichondrial ring of LaCroix (L1). Second, the collar's inner surface is the source of the osteoblast precursors that will occupy the primary ossification centre: Osterix+ precursors, not mature osteoblasts, travel into the cartilage with the invading vessels (maes2010). The perichondrium is therefore not scaffolding but a progenitor reservoir the plate keeps for life.
bone_collar_formation.human_evidence_note: No human bone collar lineage or requirement experiment exists; human relevance is inferred from conserved anatomy and from the perichondrial structures visible in human growth plate histology.
bone_collar_formation.translation_risk_reason: Requirement and lineage claims are murine knockout and Cre-lineage results with no human counterpart.
localization: mouse midshaft perichondrium from E14.5: confirmed (stjacques1999, maes2010)
human: inferred, no direct fate mapping possible

key_refs.one_line_finding: Ihh-null mice fail to form a bone collar and show disorganised proliferation with premature hypertrophy
Osterix-expressing precursors, not mature osteoblasts, enter developing bone with invading vessels

cranial_neural_crest.name: Cranial neural crest
cranial_neural_crest.summary: The skull vault is built from two embryologically distinct populations, and the boundary between them is a suture. Wnt1-Cre and Mesp1-Cre fate mapping in mouse shows the frontal bone is neural-crest derived while the parietal bone is paraxial-mesoderm derived, with the coronal suture sitting exactly at the lineage interface (jiang2002). This node exists as the atlas's contrast case: the neural-crest-derived skeleton grows by intramembranous ossification at sutures, has no growth plate, no resting zone, no hypertrophic chondrocytes and no estrogen-driven fusion, yet it must coordinate its growth with an endochondral cranial base and with the brain. The comparison makes visible which constraints on limb growth are intrinsic to endochondral ossification rather than to bone growth as such. In human embryos the two ossification programmes are separable at the regulatory level: paired transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of 5-11 post-conception week embryos resolves regionally distinct cranial and limb osteoprogenitor trajectories with different regulatory networks for intramembranous and endochondral ossification (to2024). Cranial-crest lineage identity is thus a real human distinction, not only a mouse one.
cranial_neural_crest.human_evidence_note: Human embryonic cranial osteoprogenitors are transcriptionally and epigenetically distinct from limb ones (to2024), but germ-layer fate mapping is only possible in mouse.
cranial_neural_crest.translation_risk_reason: The lineage boundary is a mouse Cre result; the human data establish regional distinctness but not germ-layer origin.
localization: mouse frontal bone: neural crest derived (jiang2002)
mouse parietal bone: paraxial mesoderm derived (jiang2002)
human cranium 5-11 post-conception weeks: distinct cranial osteoprogenitor trajectories (to2024)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Wnt1-Cre and Mesp1-Cre fate mapping places the mouse frontal bone in the neural crest lineage and the parietal bone in paraxial mesoderm, with the coronal suture at the boundary

cranial_suture.name: Cranial suture
cranial_suture.summary: A cranial suture is the fibrous joint between two calvarial bones and it is the site of calvarial growth: osteogenic fronts deposit bone appositionally on both sides of a central mesenchyme that houses the progenitor pool. The coronal suture sits at the neural-crest / paraxial-mesoderm lineage boundary (jiang2002), so a suture is a lineage interface as well as a growth site. Functionally the suture is defined by its stem cells: Gli1+ suture mesenchyme cells supply the osteogenic fronts, and their ablation produces craniosynostosis with arrest of skull growth (zhao2015), while Axin2+ suture cells are long-term self-renewing skeletal stem cells that also repair calvarial injury by direct differentiation (maruyama2016). The contrast with the growth plate is exact and instructive. Both structures are stem-cell-dependent growth engines; but suture growth is bidirectional, matrix-depositing and reversible in principle, whereas growth plate elongation is unidirectional and consumes the very cartilage it depends on. Premature loss of suture stem cells causes synostosis and stops growth; premature loss of resting zone cells is hypothesised (not shown) to cause epiphyseal fusion. The suture is the case where the stem-cell-exhaustion argument HAS been tested by ablation, which is precisely what the growth plate literature lacks.
cranial_suture.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is the existence of syndromic and non-syndromic craniosynostosis and the in silico mapping of craniosynostosis genes onto human embryonic osteoprogenitor states (to2024); no human suture stem cell has been prospectively isolated in the retrieved literature.
cranial_suture.translation_risk_reason: Both stem cell populations are defined by mouse reporter and ablation genetics; human suture biology is inferred from disease phenotypes.
localization: mouse coronal and sagittal sutures: Gli1+ and Axin2+ populations confirmed (zhao2015, maruyama2016)
human sutures: no stem cell characterisation retrieved in this sweep

endochondral_ossification.name: Endochondral ossification
endochondral_ossification.summary: Endochondral ossification is the sequence by which a cartilage template is progressively replaced by bone: condensation, chondrocyte differentiation, central hypertrophy, bone collar formation, vascular invasion and primary ossification centre, then epiphyseal cartilage canals and a secondary ossification centre, leaving a growth plate trapped between the two ossified territories (long2013, rivas2002). It is retained here as the spine of the layer because the postnatal growth plate is the residue of this sequence rather than a structure built de novo. Two facts about the sequence constrain everything downstream. First, the process is ancient and conserved - longitudinally oriented metaphyseal trabeculae indicating endochondral elongation are present in the 380-million-year-old lobe-finned fish Eusthenopteron - whereas the SECONDARY ossification centre that separates growth plate from articular cartilage first appears in amniotes (xie2020). The growth plate as a discrete disc is therefore a late and contingent arrangement, not an intrinsic feature of endochondral growth. Second, the embryonic plate is not a small version of the postnatal one: Confetti clonal analysis shows embryonic mouse chondrocytes form clusters oriented perpendicular to the growth axis rather than the stacked columns that define postnatal architecture, and the cluster-to-column ratio tracks the switch from radial expansion to elongation (rubin2024).

endochondral_ossification.human_evidence_note: Human embryonic endochondral trajectories are directly resolved by paired transcriptomic/epigenomic and spatial profiling at 5-11 post-conception weeks (to2024), and human fetal ossification timing is measurable by ultrasound (funaki2020).
endochondral_ossification.translation_risk_reason: The sequence itself is directly observed in human embryos and fetuses; the species caveats attach to the mechanistic steps, not to the sequence.

gdf5_gene.name: GDF5
gdf5_gene.summary: GDF5 is the BMP-family ligand that marks and is required for the interzone. Human mutations resolve its dose-response in both directions: mutations that ACTIVATE the receptor interaction site cause proximal symphalangism, where the interphalangeal joint never forms and the phalanges fuse into one longer element, while mutations that DEACTIVATE it cause brachydactyly type A2 with a short middle phalanx (seemann2005). One gene therefore controls both whether a segmentation boundary is placed and how long the element on either side becomes, which is precisely the kind of L0 decision the postnatal plate inherits without being able to revise. In mouse, Gdf5-driven lineage tracing establishes that GDF5-expressing interzone cells make joint tissues and not growth plate chondrocytes (koyama2008), and that they are recruited continuously rather than clonally expanded (shwartz2016). GDF5 is also one of the best-replicated common-variant loci for human height and osteoarthritis, which is handled in L8; the protein's postnatal signalling is held by L3 gdf5_protein and is not duplicated here.
gdf5_gene.human_evidence_note: Human GDF5 activating and inactivating mutations produce opposite, well-characterised digit phenotypes (symphalangism; brachydactyly type A2).
gdf5_gene.translation_risk_reason: Bidirectional human mendelian evidence anchors the gene's skeletal role; mouse data are congruent.
localization: mouse presumptive joint interzone: confirmed
human: inferred from symphalangism and brachydactyly A2 phenotypes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Activating and deactivating GDF5 receptor-interaction-site mutations cause symphalangism and brachydactyly type A2 respectively

hox_code_limb.name: HOX code, proximodistal limb specification
hox_code_limb.summary: Posterior HOX paralogue groups 9-13 assign proximodistal identity in the limb bud: Hox9/10 to the stylopod, Hox11 to the zeugopod, Hox13 to the autopod. The atlas cares about this only because the identity is not discarded at birth. Hoxa11/Hoxd11 compound mutants that retain one wild-type allele develop normally to the newborn stage and then diverge: radial and ulnar elongation rate falls, growth plate height falls, senescent involution is premature, and terminal bone length is reduced, while proliferation in the resting and proliferative zones is paradoxically ELEVATED - the signature of accelerated consumption of a progenitor pool rather than of a slow one (mouse, pineault2015). The mutant phenotype is region-restricted: Hox11 loss impairs zeugopod fracture repair while stylopod fractures heal normally (mouse, rux2017), and Hox overexpression restores periosteal stem cell behaviour only when the Hox gene matches the anatomical origin of the cell (mouse, leclerc2023). Where the retained HOX protein actually sits is contested: Hoxa11-EGFP in the adult mouse marks PDGFRa+CD51+ LepR-lineage marrow MSCs of the zeugopod and is reported as exclusive to them (rux2016), whereas Hoxa11 is also maintained in zeugopod ARTICULAR chondrocytes to at least six months (rux2021). No study has reported zone-resolved HOX expression inside a growth plate in any species, and none in human. The correlative human-relevant link is that Hoxd13, Shox and Tbx5 are differentially expressed between one-week phalangeal and tibial growth plates in a way that is age-INDEPENDENT, i.e. not explained by the differing senescence state of the two plates (mouse and rat, lui2018). That is the closest anything comes to HOX identity predicting growth rate, and it is an expression difference, not a demonstrated cause.

hoxa11_gene.name: HOXA11
hoxa11_gene.summary: HOXA11 is a Hox11-paralogue transcription factor that specifies the zeugopod (radius/ulna, tibia/fibula). Its atlas value is that expression persists long after patterning. In mouse, Hoxa11-CreERT2 lineage marking shows Hoxa11-expressing cells arise at the earliest stages of skeletal development and continue to generate osteoblasts, chondrocytes and adipocytes for the life of the animal, sitting upstream of the LepR-Cre and Osx-CreER progenitor pools (pineault2019). In the adult, Hoxa11-EGFP marks PDGFRa+CD51+ marrow MSCs specifically in the zeugopod, and Hox11 loss produces a zeugopod-restricted fracture repair defect with reduced cartilage formation and delayed ossification (rux2016). Hoxa11 is also retained in zeugopod articular chondrocytes to at least six months and tracks their postnatal reorganisation into columns in the tibial plateau, while remaining silent in the elbow (rux2021). The single human phenotype is a missense mutation segregating with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia and radio-ulnar synostosis - a zeugopod-specific skeletal defect, consistent with the mouse domain, but with no reported growth velocity data (thompson2000). Whether HOXA11 is expressed in growth plate chondrocytes at all is unreported.
hoxa11_gene.human_evidence_note: One human pedigree with a HOXA11 missense mutation causing radio-ulnar synostosis with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia; no human expression or growth-rate data.
hoxa11_gene.translation_risk_reason: All functional and lineage data are murine conditional-allele and reporter experiments; the human allele is a single family with a haematological presentation.

mouse zeugopod articular chondrocyte: confirmed to 6 months (rux2021)

hoxa13_gene.name: HOXA13
hoxa13_gene.summary: HOXA13 specifies the autopod, the limb segment whose growth plates are the slowest and the earliest to senesce. Human heterozygous HOXA13 homeodomain mutations cause hand-foot-genital syndrome, whose skeletal phenotype is size-specific rather than count-specific: a short first metacarpal and small distal phalanges with normal digit number (mortlock1997). This is the cleanest human statement that an autopod HOX gene sets how much a defined set of elements grows. The mechanistic bridge to the growth plate is not established: nobody has measured elongation rate, plate height or chondrocyte kinetics in a HOXA13 carrier or in a Hoxa13 mutant mouse growth plate. What is measured is that autopod plates (metacarpal, phalanx) run at roughly half the elongation rate of tibia and femur at one week in mouse and fuse at 3-4 weeks while tibia and femur are still open at 12 weeks (lui2018), and that a distal-limb HOX-cluster gene, Hoxd13, is one of the genes differentially expressed between phalangeal and tibial plates independently of age. HOXA13 is therefore a candidate for the autopod's distinct growth programme, not a demonstrated cause of it.

claim_grades.claim: HOXA13 sets the autopod growth plate's distinctive kinetics

hoxd11_gene.name: HOXD11
hoxd11_gene.summary: HOXD11 is the HoxD-cluster partner of HOXA11 in zeugopod specification; the two act as a paralogue group and single mutants are near-normal. The decisive experiment for the atlas is a conditional Hoxd11 allele deleted in the ADULT mouse on a Hox11-sensitised background: normal lamellar bone in the radius and ulna is replaced by disorganised woven-bone-like matrix, the Hox-expressing stem cell pool is NOT lost, Runx2 induction is normal, but osteoblasts fail to progress to osteopontin or osteocalcin expression and the resulting osteocytes lack dendrites, a lacuno-canalicular network and SOST (song2020). Hox11 therefore acts on differentiation, region-specifically, in a fully formed skeleton - the strongest available evidence that embryonic positional identity is a continuing instruction rather than a memory. In the growing animal, Hoxa11/Hoxd11 compound loss slows radial and ulnar elongation postnatally with premature growth plate senescence (pineault2015). The bowing of the mutant radius is explicitly attributed to mechanical constraint from the disproportionately slower ulna, which makes the phenotype a natural experiment in paired-bone growth mismatch. No human HOXD11 skeletal phenotype is established.
hoxd11_gene.human_evidence_note: No human HOXD11 variant with a skeletal growth phenotype has been reported; the human HOXD cluster evidence is limited to HOXD13 synpolydactyly.
hoxd11_gene.translation_risk_reason: Entirely murine conditional genetics with no human counterpart; mice also do not fuse their growth plates, so the adult-skeleton phenotype cannot be mapped onto a human post-fusion state.
localization: mouse zeugopod: confirmed (song2020, pineault2015)
human: unreported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Adult conditional Hoxd11 deletion causes region-specific woven bone and an osteoblast maturation block without depleting the stem cell pool

hoxd13_gene.name: HOXD13
hoxd13_gene.summary: HOXD13 is the most 5' HoxD gene and, with HOXA13, specifies the autopod. Human polyalanine-tract expansions in HOXD13 cause synpolydactyly, in which the digit skeleton shows altered growth AND altered branching - i.e. the mutation changes how much elements grow, not only how many form (muragaki1996). The reason HOXD13 matters more than its paralogues here is a single specific observation: in laser-capture RNA-seq of separated proliferative and hypertrophic zones, Hoxd13 is among the genes whose expression differs between the one-week proximal phalangeal growth plate and the one-week proximal tibial growth plate in a manner that is NOT explained by the phalanx being developmentally older, because its expression in the 1-week phalanx differs from both 1-week and 4-week tibia (mouse and rat, lui2018). Positional HOX identity is therefore demonstrably still readable inside a postnatal growth plate, at bulk-zone resolution. What the same study shows is that the growth rate difference between those plates is accounted for by differential progression of the senescence programme, not by Hoxd13; the link from retained HOX identity to rate remains a hypothesis.
hoxd13_gene.human_evidence_note: HOXD13 polyalanine expansions cause human synpolydactyly with documented alteration of digit element growth and branching.
hoxd13_gene.translation_risk_reason: The human mutation phenotype is direct; the postnatal zonal expression evidence is rodent bulk RNA-seq and has not been confirmed by in situ localization or in human tissue.
localization: mouse phalangeal growth plate PZ and HZ: differential expression vs tibia, age-independent (lui2018)
human growth plate: unreported

key_refs.one_line_finding: HOXD13 polyalanine expansion causes human synpolydactyly with altered growth and branching of digit elements

interzone_formation.name: Interzone formation and joint positioning
interzone_formation.summary: A joint site is specified by the appearance of an interzone: a three-layered flattened-cell domain that interrupts a continuous cartilage rod and thereby DEFINES where one skeletal element ends and the next begins. Because element length is bounded by the two joints that flank it, interzone position is the earliest determinant of how much bone each growth plate has to build. Gdf5-Cre lineage tracing in mouse shows the interzone gives rise to articular cartilage, synovium and intra-articular ligaments but NOT to growth plate chondrocytes: the joint lineage and the growth plate lineage separate at this point (koyama2008). Inducible Gdf5-CreERT2 pulses then showed the joint is not built by expansion of a single founder pool but by continuous, wave-like recruitment of new Gdf5-expressing cells from adjacent tissue (shwartz2016), so 'interzone' names a rolling state, not a fixed clone. Human evidence that interzone signalling sets element length is genetic: activating GDF5 mutations cause proximal symphalangism, in which the joint never forms and adjacent phalanges fuse, and inactivating mutations cause brachydactyly type A2, in which the middle phalanx is short (seemann2005). Whether interzone position predicts the eventual elongation rate of the plate at that element's other end is untested.
interzone_formation.human_evidence_note: Human GDF5 gain- and loss-of-function mutations produce joint fusion and short middle phalanges respectively, implying the same interzone-dependent segmentation, but no human interzone has been fate mapped.
interzone_formation.translation_risk_reason: Lineage claims are murine and cannot be made in humans; the human genetic phenotypes are concordant with the murine mechanism.
localization: mouse presumptive joint sites E12.5 onward: confirmed by Gdf5-Cre and Gdf5-CreERT2 (koyama2008, shwartz2016)
human: inferred from GDF5 mutation phenotypes

intramembranous_ossification.name: Intramembranous ossification
intramembranous_ossification.summary: In intramembranous ossification mesenchymal cells differentiate directly into osteoblasts with no cartilage intermediate. It builds the calvaria, most of the face and the clavicle, and it also builds the bone collar around every long bone, so the two programmes are not anatomically segregated. The contrast that matters for a growth atlas is architectural: intramembranous growth occurs at sutures, which are bidirectional appositional fronts with a resident stem cell population, whereas endochondral growth occurs at a unidirectional cartilage disc that is consumed as it works. A suture can in principle keep depositing bone as long as its stem cells persist; a growth plate cannot elongate without regenerating cartilage from its resting zone. In human embryos the two programmes are driven by demonstrably different regulatory networks, and in silico perturbation of monogenic craniosynostosis genes in the human osteolineage trajectory implicates specific progenitor states (to2024). Because calvarial and long-bone growth cease by different mechanisms and on different schedules, intramembranous ossification is the control condition against which endochondral constraints - finite resting zone, estrogen-driven fusion, site-specific senescence - should be read.
intramembranous_ossification.human_evidence_note: Human embryonic intramembranous osteoprogenitor trajectories and their regulatory networks are directly resolved by snRNA/snATAC and spatial profiling (to2024).
intramembranous_ossification.translation_risk_reason: The process and its anatomical distribution are directly documented in human embryos; the cellular mechanisms of suture stem cells are murine and are flagged in their own node.
localization: human calvaria, face, clavicle: confirmed
mouse and human long bone perichondrium (bone collar): confirmed
human embryo 5-11 post-conception weeks: distinct regulatory network from endochondral (to2024)

limb_bud_initiation.name: Limb bud initiation
limb_bud_initiation.summary: The limb bud is initiated when lateral plate mesoderm at defined axial levels expresses Fgf10, which induces Fgf8 in the overlying ectoderm to form the apical ectodermal ridge; the two maintain each other. Fgf10-null mice form a bud that fails to grow out, no AER is induced, and limbs are absent at birth (min1998). Forelimb versus hindlimb identity is imposed at this step by TBX5 and by TBX4/PITX1 respectively, and the identity is segment-wide: human TBX5 mutations produce Holt-Oram syndrome, in which malformation is confined to the upper limb and heart with the lower limb spared (basson1997). For this atlas the initiation step matters for one reason: it is where the set of skeletal elements, and their forelimb/hindlimb identity, is fixed, and human upper and lower limb growth plates run different programmes thereafter - the proximal humerus supplies about 80% of humeral length while the distal femur supplies about 70% of femoral length, and their relative shares move in opposite directions with age. Nothing in the initiation literature measures a growth plate, so the connection from initiation to postnatal rate is an inference, not a result.
limb_bud_initiation.human_evidence_note: Human TBX5 mutation restricts malformation to the upper limb, and the human embryonic multi-omic atlas shows limb osteoprogenitor trajectories distinct from cranial ones; no human initiation experiment exists.
limb_bud_initiation.translation_risk_reason: The molecular logic is murine and avian, but the segment-restricted human syndromes indicate the same limb-field partition operates in humans.
localization: mouse and chick lateral plate mesoderm at forelimb and hindlimb levels: confirmed
human embryo 5-11 post-conception weeks: limb osteoprogenitor trajectories are regionally distinct from cranial ones (to2024)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Fgf10-null mice form a limb bud that fails to grow out and never induces an AER, giving limbless newborns

mesenchymal_condensation.name: Mesenchymal condensation
mesenchymal_condensation.summary: Every endochondral element begins as a local aggregation of limb bud mesenchyme that raises cell density and turns on SOX9. The single most load-bearing recent result for this atlas is that the condensation is already spatially partitioned in a way the postnatal growth plate inherits: Fgfr3-creER pulsed at the condensation stage in mouse marks cells that contribute exclusively to hypertrophic chondrocytes and to the DORSAL side of the resting and proliferative zones, and their descendants remain dorsally restricted through growth plate chondrocytes, trabecular and cortical osteoblasts and marrow stroma; diphtheria-toxin ablation of these cells at the condensation stage severely disrupts long bone development (wu2025). The postnatal plate is therefore not a homogeneous field seeded at random - it carries a dorsoventral compartment map laid down before cartilage exists. A second, older claim is repeated widely and is NOT supported by a measurement: that all long bone condensations start at a similar size and diverge only later. It is cited as such (lui2018 citing Hall and Miyake), but no study retrieved reports condensation cell number, volume or density measured across elements that end up 10-20 fold different in length. That quantitative hole is logged as g_l0dev_003.

claim_grades.claim: Condensation-stage progenitors are spatially compartmentalised and their descendants occupy restricted territories of the postnatal growth plate
claim_grades.basis: single mouse study with Fgfr3-creER and Dlx5-creER lineage tracing plus DTA ablation (wu2025)

claim_grades.claim: Condensation is required for long bone formation
claim_grades.basis: condensation-stage DTA ablation abolishes normal long bone development in mouse; Sox9-null cells excluded from condensations never form cartilage

claim_grades.claim: All long bone condensations start at similar size and diverge later
claim_grades.basis: repeated in reviews and in the introduction of lui2018 but no primary measurement across elements was retrievable

mesenchymal_condensation.human_evidence_note: Human condensation-stage cells have been profiled transcriptionally and spatially in 5-11 post-conception week embryos (to2024), but no human lineage tracing or ablation is possible, so no human cell-fate claim can be made.
mesenchymal_condensation.translation_risk_reason: The compartment-inheritance result is a single mouse study using two inducible Cre lines; humans cannot be lineage traced and the dorsoventral compartmentalisation of the human plate is unexamined.
localization: mouse limb bud E11.5-E12.5 condensation: Fgfr3-creER marks dorsally restricted progenitors (wu2025)
human embryo 5-11 post-conception weeks: condensation-stage osteoprogenitor trajectories resolved by snRNA/snATAC and spatial transcriptomics (to2024)

pitx1_gene.name: PITX1
pitx1_gene.summary: PITX1 is the bicoid-related homeodomain factor that imposes hindlimb identity. Pitx1-null mice show hindlimb-specific defects with partial transformation of hindlimb structures toward forelimb morphology, and the forelimb is unaffected (szeto1999). Together with TBX5 on the forelimb side, PITX1 is the reason the atlas can treat upper-limb and lower-limb growth plates as separately programmed rather than as instances of one plate. That separation is quantitatively real in humans: the proximal humeral physis supplies about 80% of humeral length whereas the distal femoral physis supplies about 70% of femoral length, and the two shares move differently with age (see L1 site_specific_growth_rate). What is missing is any experiment connecting the two: no Pitx1 or Tbx5 manipulation has been read out as a growth plate elongation rate, and no human PITX1 variant has been assessed against limb segment growth velocity. The identity-to-rate step is an inference this layer flags rather than asserts.
pitx1_gene.human_evidence_note: No human PITX1 variant has been characterised with limb growth measurements; human relevance rests on the conservation of forelimb/hindlimb identity genes.
pitx1_gene.translation_risk_reason: Murine null phenotype only; the human counterpart of a hindlimb-to-forelimb identity shift has never been described.
localization: mouse hindlimb field lateral plate mesoderm: confirmed (szeto1999)
human: no expression data in limb tissue retrieved

key_refs.one_line_finding: Pitx1-null mice have hindlimb-specific defects with partial transformation toward forelimb morphology

primary_ossification_center.name: Primary ossification centre (POC)
primary_ossification_center.summary: The POC is the mid-diaphyseal territory where cartilage is first replaced by bone and marrow, and it is the event that splits one cartilage rod into two growth plates. In rabbit it is stage 4a of a 16-stage sequence, appearing well before epiphyseal cartilage canals (stage 7) and the secondary centre (stages 9-10) (rivas2002). Its timing is the clock against which all later skeletal maturity scoring is calibrated. The functional inheritance for the postnatal plate is geometric rather than molecular: once the POC exists, each plate has a fixed polarity - resting zone facing the epiphysis, hypertrophic zone facing the marrow - and elongation can only add bone at the metaphyseal side. Where an element forms a POC but only ONE growth plate is a patterning decision made at this stage and it is not incidental: in mouse metatarsals Pthlh is expressed in the reserve zone only at the growth-plate-forming end, while the opposite end lacks a PTHrP+ reserve zone and shows premature Ihh expression and no plate (reno2025). The presence of a PTHrP+ reserve pool is therefore the operational definition of a growth plate, and its patterning is an L0 event with a direct L2 consequence.
primary_ossification_center.human_evidence_note: Human POC appearance is directly observable radiographically, but the patterning claim about which ends form plates rests on mouse in situ hybridization.
primary_ossification_center.translation_risk_reason: Anatomy transfers; the PTHrP-reserve-zone patterning result is murine and has not been checked in human metacarpals, which are likewise single-ended.
localization: mouse and rabbit mid-diaphysis: confirmed
mouse metatarsal: single-ended reserve zone patterning (reno2025)
human fetus: POCs of long bones present from the first trimester

key_refs.one_line_finding: POC formation is stage 4a of 16 in the rabbit sequence, preceding cartilage canals and the secondary centre
Pthlh marks the reserve zone only at the growth-plate-forming end of the mouse metatarsal; the opposite end has no PTHrP+ reserve zone and shows premature Ihh

progress_zone.name: Progress zone model of proximodistal specification
progress_zone.summary: How a limb bud decides which segment a cell will build determines which HOX code, and therefore which growth programme, each future growth plate inherits. Two models compete. The progress zone model holds that mesenchyme under the AER keeps an internal timer and acquires progressively more distal identity the longer it stays there. The prespecification/expansion model holds that stylopod, zeugopod and autopod domains are laid down early in the small bud and are then progressively expanded. Fate mapping and cell-death experiments in chick favour the second: removing cells does not shift identity as the timer model predicts, and the early bud already contains separable domains (dudley2002). Mouse genetics then showed that reducing AER Fgf4/Fgf8 deletes PROXIMAL rather than distal skeletal elements, which is the opposite of what a distal-timer model predicts and indicates FGF acts instructively on identity and on survival of the proximal domain (mariani2008). The practical consequence for this atlas is that positional identity, and hence any inherited difference between the distal femoral and the metacarpal plate, is set very early - before any cartilage exists - and is not a running consequence of how long growth continues. This node is retained as a hypothesis because the debate is not formally closed and because it constrains when a site-specific intervention could act.
progress_zone.human_evidence_note: No human experiment addresses proximodistal specification mechanism; human relevance is limited to the segment-restricted distribution of HOX limb malformation syndromes.
progress_zone.translation_risk_reason: Avian and murine embryology with no human counterpart, and the models were built on limb morphology, not on any growth plate readout.
localization: chick limb bud: fate mapping (dudley2002)
mouse limb bud: AER Fgf allelic series (mariani2008)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chick fate mapping and cell ablation contradict the progress zone timer and support early prespecification of proximodistal domains
Reducing AER Fgf4/Fgf8 in mouse deletes proximal, not distal, limb elements, indicating an instructive role for FGF in PD identity

secondary_ossification_center.name: Secondary ossification centre (SOC)
secondary_ossification_center.summary: The SOC is the ossified island that forms inside the epiphyseal cartilage after vessels enter through cartilage canals, and its appearance is what physically separates the growth plate from the articular surface (blumer2008, rivas2002). Timing is species- and bone-specific and is measurable in humans: in 199 Japanese pregnancies the distal femoral centre was invisible before 30 weeks gestation and present in 100% of fetuses after 35 weeks, while the proximal tibial centre was invisible before 33 weeks and present in only 73.7% at 37 weeks (funaki2020). In mouse the tibial SOC is well developed by P30 and absent in size-matched P10 rat tibia, a difference exploited as a natural SOC+/SOC- pair (xie2020). The best-evidenced FUNCTION of the SOC is mechanical, not stem-cell-related: the SOC first appears in amniotes, is absent in anamniotes, and its ontogenetic timing tracks limb-specific load - newborn bats ossify feet and wing thumbs (used for clinging) ahead of the rest of the wing, and jerboa forelimb SOCs precede hindlimb SOCs, matching the order in which the limbs are used. Finite-element analysis and ex vivo loading show the SOC stiffens the epiphysis and shields hypertrophic chondrocytes, the least stiff cells in the plate; 40% of chondrocytes died under a 1 N load in the SOC- model while SOC+ bones tolerated a tenfold higher load, and delaying SOC formation in vivo with axitinib at P18 or with Prx-Cre:GnasR201H raised hypertrophic-zone apoptosis (xie2020). The separate and widely repeated claim that SOC formation TRIGGERS acquisition of resting-zone stemness rests only on temporal coincidence in mouse (mizuhashi2018, newton2019) and is treated here as a hypothesis (see L2 soc_formation_triggers_stemness, gap g_l2stem_003). Note for that gap: SOC-delaying tools already exist and are validated, so the discriminating experiment is tractable - what is missing is a stemness readout, not a method.

claim_grades.claim: The SOC stiffens the epiphysis and protects hypertrophic chondrocytes from load-induced death

claim_grades.claim: SOC formation triggers acquisition of resting-zone stemness

secondary_ossification_center.human_evidence_note: Human SOC appearance timing is directly measured by fetal ultrasound with n=199 and explicit percentile criteria; no human functional experiment exists.

sox9_chondrogenic_commitment.name: SOX9 chondrogenic commitment
sox9_chondrogenic_commitment.summary: SOX9 is the gate on chondrogenic fate and it acts twice. Sox9-null cells in mouse chimeras are excluded from mesenchymal condensations altogether and never express Col2a1 or form cartilage (bi1999); conditional deletion after condensation shows a second, separable requirement for overt chondrocyte differentiation, and SOX9 is required for expression of its own partners Sox5 and Sox6 (akiyama2002). Dose matters and this is where the node earns its place in a growth atlas: Sox9 heterozygous mice have hypoplastic cartilage primordia and PREMATURE skeletal mineralization (bi2001), the mouse model of human campomelic dysplasia, which is caused by SOX9 haploinsufficiency. A halved dose of one transcription factor at the condensation stage therefore produces both a smaller starting template and an accelerated conversion of that template to bone - the two variables the postnatal plate has to work with. The postnatal, zone-resolved role of SOX9 (its requirement in proliferative chondrocytes and its block on osteoblast differentiation) belongs to L3 sox9_tf and is not duplicated here.
sox9_chondrogenic_commitment.human_evidence_note: Human SOX9 haploinsufficiency causes campomelic dysplasia with bowed, hypoplastic long bones; the mouse heterozygote reproduces the cartilage hypoplasia and premature mineralization, but no human cartilage has been assayed for SOX9 dose effects directly.
sox9_chondrogenic_commitment.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism is murine conditional genetics, but human SOX9 haploinsufficiency gives a concordant skeletal phenotype, so the dose-sensitivity claim transfers.
localization: mouse condensation and cartilage: confirmed by conditional deletion (bi1999, akiyama2002)
human embryonic chondrocyte trajectories: confirmed transcriptionally (to2024)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Sox9-null cells are excluded from condensations and cannot form cartilage

suture_mesenchyme_stem_cell.name: Suture mesenchyme stem cell
suture_mesenchyme_stem_cell.summary: Two independently defined populations occupy the cranial suture mesenchyme and behave as skeletal stem cells. Gli1+ cells supply the osteogenic fronts of the growing calvaria; conditional ablation of the Gli1+ population causes craniosynostosis, arrest of skull growth and impaired injury repair, which is a direct demonstration that a stem cell pool is load-bearing for continued skeletal growth (zhao2015). Axin2+ suture cells are long-term self-renewing, generate calvarial bone by direct differentiation, and reconstitute the suture on transplantation (maruyama2016). The atlas keeps this node because it is the methodological benchmark the growth plate literature has not met: in the suture, the stem-cell-depletion-causes-growth-cessation claim has been tested by ablating the cells and observing the predicted synostosis, whereas in the growth plate the equivalent claim (resting zone depletion causes epiphyseal fusion, L2 rz_depletion_causes_fusion) rests on correlation. Whether the two populations are one cell or two is unresolved, and both are murine; no human suture stem cell has been prospectively isolated in the literature retrieved here.
suture_mesenchyme_stem_cell.human_evidence_note: No human suture stem cell isolation or functional assay was retrieved; human relevance rests on the craniosynostosis phenotype these mouse ablations reproduce.
suture_mesenchyme_stem_cell.translation_risk_reason: Both populations are defined by mouse reporter alleles and inducible ablation; marker transfer to human calvarial tissue has not been demonstrated.
localization: mouse suture mesenchyme: Gli1+ (zhao2015) and Axin2+ (maruyama2016) populations confirmed
human: unreported in retrieved literature

tbx5_gene.name: TBX5
tbx5_gene.summary: TBX5 is the T-box transcription factor that specifies forelimb identity and is required for forelimb bud initiation. Human heterozygous TBX5 mutations cause Holt-Oram syndrome, in which skeletal malformation is confined to the upper limb - most often radial ray and thumb defects - together with cardiac septation defects, with the lower limb entirely spared (basson1997). This restriction is the point: it establishes in humans that the forelimb and hindlimb skeletons run on separable genetic programmes from the moment the buds appear, which is the developmental precondition for arm and leg growth plates behaving differently. There is one further hook into the postnatal plate: Tbx5 is among the genes differentially expressed between one-week phalangeal and tibial growth plates in a manner independent of the plates' differing senescence state (lui2018), so forelimb identity genes are still transcribed inside a postnatal growth plate. No study links TBX5 genotype to any growth velocity measurement.
tbx5_gene.human_evidence_note: TBX5 loss-of-function causes Holt-Oram syndrome with strictly upper-limb-restricted skeletal malformation in humans.
tbx5_gene.translation_risk_reason: The human syndrome defines the gene's skeletal domain directly; the mouse data are congruent.
localization: mouse forelimb field lateral plate mesoderm: confirmed
mouse postnatal growth plate PZ/HZ: differential Tbx5 expression between phalanx and tibia (lui2018)
human: inferred from Holt-Oram phenotype distribution

key_refs.one_line_finding: TBX5 mutations cause Holt-Oram syndrome with upper-limb and cardiac malformation and normal lower limbs

vascular_invasion_poc.name: Vascular invasion of the primary ossification centre
vascular_invasion_poc.summary: Blood vessels breach the bone collar and enter the hypertrophic core of the cartilage template, converting the mid-diaphysis into the primary ossification centre and creating the chondro-osseous junction that will remain the plate's lower boundary for the rest of growth. The invading front carries its own osteoprogenitors: lineage tracing shows Osterix-expressing precursors move in ALONG the vessels and become the trabecular osteoblasts, whereas mature osteoblasts do not migrate (maes2010). This is the developmental precedent for the postnatal coupling of angiogenesis to ossification at the metaphysis (L1 metaphyseal_vasculature, type_h_vessel) and for the pharmacological observation that anti-VEGFR agents can arrest ossification-centre expansion without altering cartilage stiffness (xie2020). In the epiphysis the same logic operates a second time through cartilage canals (blumer2008). The postnatal plate therefore inherits a fixed geometry: an ossified territory below, an ossified territory above, and a cartilage disc between them whose only escape from consumption is renewal from its own resting zone.
vascular_invasion_poc.human_evidence_note: Human primary ossification centres are directly observable by fetal imaging and histology, but the lineage claim about vessel-borne osteoprogenitors is murine only.
vascular_invasion_poc.translation_risk_reason: The anatomical event is directly observed in humans; the cellular mechanism is murine lineage tracing.
localization: mouse diaphysis E14.5-E15.5: confirmed (maes2010)
rabbit: stage 4a of 16 (rivas2002)
human fetus: radiographically visible from the first trimester onward

key_refs.one_line_finding: Osterix+ osteoblast precursors move into developing bone along invading blood vessels; mature osteoblasts do not

zone_of_polarizing_activity.name: Zone of polarizing activity (ZPA)
zone_of_polarizing_activity.summary: The ZPA is the posterior distal mesenchyme of the limb bud whose grafting to the anterior margin produces mirror-image digit duplication. Sonic hedgehog is expressed there and is sufficient to reproduce that polarizing activity in chick (riddle1993), establishing SHH as the anteroposterior organiser. In the human, the strongest evidence is regulatory rather than coding: point mutations in the ZRS, a conserved limb-specific SHH enhancer roughly 1 Mb away inside intron 5 of LMBR1, segregate with preaxial polydactyly (lettice2003). The ZPA therefore sets digit number and anteroposterior identity. It is retained in this layer only as the anteroposterior counterpart to the proximodistal HOX axis, because digit identity determines which HOX13-domain growth plates exist; it does not set any measured growth plate property. No ZPA or SHH-enhancer manipulation has been followed to a postnatal growth-plate rate measurement. Postnatal hedgehog signalling in the plate is an L3 matter (Ihh, Gli, Patched) and is not duplicated here.
zone_of_polarizing_activity.human_evidence_note: Human ZRS point mutations cause preaxial polydactyly, implying a conserved SHH limb organiser, but no human ZPA has been assayed directly.
zone_of_polarizing_activity.translation_risk_reason: Organiser function is avian/murine; the human evidence is genetic and concerns digit number, not growth rate.
localization: chick and mouse posterior limb bud mesenchyme: confirmed
human: inferred from ZRS mutation phenotypes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Sonic hedgehog expressed in the ZPA is sufficient to reproduce polarizing activity and mirror-image digit duplication in chick

zrs_enhancer.name: ZRS (ZPA regulatory sequence) SHH limb enhancer
zrs_enhancer.summary: The ZRS is a conserved cis-regulatory element inside intron 5 of LMBR1, approximately 1 Mb from the SHH promoter, that drives SHH expression specifically in the limb ZPA. Single-nucleotide changes within it segregate with human preaxial polydactyly and with the equivalent mouse and cat phenotypes, while the SHH coding sequence remains intact (lettice2003). It is kept in this layer as the atlas's worked example that a skeletal patterning decision can be made by a distant non-coding element whose disruption produces a purely limb-restricted phenotype with no midline or CNS involvement - the modular, tissue-specific regulatory architecture that any genetic explanation of site-specific growth (L8) has to work within. What the ZRS does NOT do, on current evidence, is set a growth rate: no ZRS allele has been assayed for elongation rate, growth plate height, or chondrocyte kinetics in any species.
zrs_enhancer.human_evidence_note: Human families with preaxial polydactyly carry ZRS point mutations that co-segregate with the limb phenotype.
zrs_enhancer.translation_risk_reason: The element and its phenotype were defined in human pedigrees first and are conserved across mammals and birds.
localization: human LMBR1 intron 5: confirmed by mutation mapping
mouse and chick limb bud posterior mesenchyme: confirmed by enhancer reporter

altitude_hypoxia_growth.name: High altitude and growth
altitude_hypoxia_growth.summary: Chronic hypoxia is the environmental exposure with the most attractive candidate molecular entry point in this layer and the least evidence that the entry point is used. Andean field studies from Nunoa, Peru (4000 m) established that indigenous children grow slowly in body size with delayed skeletal maturation while lung volume growth is accelerated, and that acclimatisation during the developmental period rather than in adulthood is what produces the adult functional phenotype (frisancho2025). The obvious mechanistic candidate is HIF-1alpha, which the atlas carries at L3 as hif1a_chondrocyte, but the inference has a specific and disqualifying problem: L3 records that the oxygen tension of the human growth plate has never been measured, so there is no baseline against which to say whether residence at 4000 m changes physeal pO2 at all. The plate is avascular and already hypoxic at sea level; a reduction in arterial pO2 need not translate into a change in the interior of cartilage. Meanwhile the population signal is dominated by the environment rather than by altitude: in Tibetan children at ~3600 m surveyed in 2005, 2010, 2014 and 2019 (Chinese National Survey on Students' Constitution and Health), height rose across survey years in most age groups of both sexes despite unchanged altitude, with the largest gains in 13-year-old boys and 10-year-old girls (zhang2026). Altitude is therefore not a fixed ceiling.

calcium_intake_growth.name: Dietary calcium intake and linear growth
calcium_intake_growth.summary: Dietary calcium has a large effect on bone mineral accrual and a small-to-absent effect on linear growth, and the cleanest experimental separation of the two comes from the milk fractionation trials. In a 2x2 factorial randomised trial in 57 eight-year-old boys, drinks delivering the calcium and phosphorus content of 1.5 L of skim milk were compared with low-mineral drinks against the same protein background: there were no independent effects of high milk-mineral intake on serum IGF-1 or on fasting insulin, and no interaction between the mineral and protein factors (hoppe2009). Since the IGF-1 rise seen with milk is carried entirely by casein, the growth-relevant component of milk is not its calcium. Calcium's genuine entry point into the atlas is through the L4 calcium homeostasis loop - ionised calcium sets PTH secretion through CASR, and PTH plus calcitriol control phosphate, which is required for hypertrophic chondrocyte apoptosis. Below the rachitic threshold, calcium deficiency therefore deranges the growth plate through the same phosphate route as vitamin D deficiency; above it, calcium is not a linear growth variable.

claim_grades.claim: Milk-derived calcium and phosphorus do not raise serum IGF-1 or insulin in prepubertal boys.
claim_grades.basis: 2x2 factorial randomised design that separates minerals from protein, n=57 (hoppe2009).

claim_grades.claim: Calcium deficiency below the rachitic threshold deranges the growth plate through the phosphate route.

dohad_hypothesis.name: Developmental origins of health and disease
dohad_hypothesis.summary: DOHaD holds that the early-life environment permanently sets adult physiology, and for stature the claim is that size attained by about 2 years of age largely fixes adult height. The pooled evidence is strong for the association: across five long-running birth cohorts in Brazil, Guatemala, India, the Philippines and South Africa, maternal height, birthweight, intrauterine growth restriction and weight, height and BMI at 2 years were all related to adult height, schooling, income and offspring birthweight, with undernutrition strongly associated with shorter adult height and reduced economic productivity (victora2008). The mechanistic claim - permanent programming rather than continuous exposure - is much less secure, because in most settings the environment at age 2 and the environment at age 12 are the same environment. The Dutch Hunger Winter provides the design that separates them, and there the finding is a gene-environment interaction on fetal growth: a birthweight polygenic index explained 14% of birthweight variance in unexposed controls (r=0.38, p<0.001) but had no detectable effect in famine-exposed individuals, particularly those exposed in mid-to-late gestation (r=0.10) (taeubert2026). A severe environmental insult can therefore erase the expression of genetic influence on growth altogether. No DOHaD study has measured a growth plate, and the proposed epigenetic mediators have never been assayed in physeal cartilage; L8 carries dna_methylation_growth_plate as the corresponding placeholder.

claim_grades.claim: Size at 2 years predicts adult height, schooling and income across diverse populations.
claim_grades.basis: Pooled analysis of five prospective birth cohorts with adult follow-up plus systematic reviews (victora2008).

claim_grades.claim: Severe prenatal undernutrition suppresses the expression of genetic influence on fetal growth.
claim_grades.basis: Genotyped famine cohort with obstetric records and prespecified gene-environment interaction test (taeubert2026); single cohort, n=589 total.

claim_grades.claim: Early-life exposure programmes the growth plate epigenetically.
claim_grades.basis: No DOHaD study has measured DNA methylation, chromatin or transcription in growth plate cartilage in any species.

dohad_hypothesis.human_evidence_note: Five prospective LMIC birth cohorts with adult follow-up, plus a genotyped famine natural experiment with obstetric records.
dohad_hypothesis.translation_risk_reason: The evidence cited here is entirely human cohort and natural-experiment data.
localization: human SYS: whole-organism developmental programming

key_refs.one_line_finding: In five LMIC birth cohorts, maternal height, birthweight, IUGR and size at 2 years predicted adult height, schooling, income and offspring birthweight.
A birthweight polygenic index explained 14% of birthweight variance in Dutch Hunger Winter controls but had no detectable effect in famine-exposed individuals.

dutch_hunger_winter.name: Dutch Hunger Winter natural experiment
dutch_hunger_winter.summary: The Dutch Hunger Winter of November 1944 to May 1945 is the best-documented famine natural experiment in human growth biology because rations were recorded, obstetric records survive, the population was previously well nourished, and the famine ended abruptly - so exposure timing within gestation can be resolved to weeks. The Dutch Hunger Winter Families Study comprises 283 individuals conceived before the famine and therefore exposed in mid-to-late gestation, 145 conceived during the famine and exposed in early gestation, and 161 unexposed controls, all with obstetric records and genotypes (taeubert2026). Its most incisive result for this atlas is not an effect size but a loss of one: a birthweight polygenic index explained 14% of birthweight variance in controls (r=0.38, p<0.001) yet had no detectable influence in famine-exposed individuals, especially those exposed in mid-to-late gestation (r=0.10). Severe substrate restriction did not merely shift the mean of fetal growth; it abolished the genotype-phenotype relationship. The comparison case for postnatal famine and adult stature comes from Ethiopia: 40 years after the 1984-85 Great Ethiopian Famine, exposed survivors were 1.4 cm shorter (95% CI -2.4 to -0.3) than matched controls and 2.4 cm shorter (-3.7 to -1.1) than post-famine-born controls, with lower weight and handgrip strength (abera2026). A one-to-two-year famine therefore costs on the order of 1-2 cm of adult height - an order of magnitude smaller than the ~20 cm secular range.

claim_grades.claim: Prenatal famine exposure abolishes the detectable genetic contribution to birthweight.
claim_grades.basis: Prespecified gene-environment interaction in a genotyped famine cohort with obstetric records (taeubert2026); single cohort.

claim_grades.claim: Famine exposure in childhood costs 1-2 cm of adult height measured four decades later.
claim_grades.basis: Retrospective cohort with two independent control groups and adjusted differences with CIs (abera2026).

claim_grades.claim: The famine effect on stature is mediated by suppressed IGF-1 at the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: No famine cohort has a contemporaneous endocrine or skeletal measurement; the mediator is imported from nutrition-IGF-1 studies.

dutch_hunger_winter.human_evidence_note: Genotyped human famine cohorts with contemporaneous obstetric records and 40-80 year follow-up anthropometry.
localization: human SYS: whole-organism famine exposure with resolvable gestational timing

key_refs.one_line_finding: In the Dutch Hunger Winter Families Study a birthweight polygenic index explained 14% of variance in controls but had no detectable effect in famine-exposed individuals.
Forty years after the 1984-85 Great Ethiopian Famine, exposed survivors were 1.4 cm shorter than matched and 2.4 cm shorter than post-famine controls, with lower weight and handgrip strength.

endocrine_disrupting_chemicals.name: Endocrine disrupting chemicals and growth
endocrine_disrupting_chemicals.summary: Endocrine disrupting chemicals are the exposure most often asserted to act on the growth plate through the estrogen receptor and least often demonstrated to do so. The human evidence is on pubertal timing, not on stature or on cartilage. In 1424 Korean children and adolescents (Korea Environmental Exposure and Health Survey) with blood lead, mercury and cadmium and urinary bisphenol A and phthalate metabolites, precocious puberty was identified in 50 (3.5%) and delayed puberty in 54 (3.8%); a higher mono-benzyl phthalate concentration was associated with delayed puberty in girls (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.34-5.66), and in quantile g-computation mixture models the BPA-plus-phthalate mixture was associated with precocious puberty in boys and delayed puberty in both sexes (choe2025). Because pubertal timing sets both the growth spurt and epiphyseal fusion, any real effect on puberty is an effect on adult height. The proposed molecular entry points - ERalpha (L4 estrogen_receptor_alpha) and aromatase (L4 aromatase_cyp19a1) - are biologically apt, since estrogen is the fusion signal and BPA is a weak ER agonist. But a targeted literature search returns no study in which a bisphenol or phthalate was applied to growth plate chondrocytes with an ERalpha or aromatase readout in any mammal; the cartilage work that exists is zebrafish craniofacial or adult articular osteoarthritis. This is registered as a search-established gap.

claim_grades.claim: Phthalate and bisphenol exposure is associated with altered pubertal timing in children.
claim_grades.basis: Single cross-sectional national survey with self-measured Tanner staging and 50-54 cases per outcome (choe2025).

claim_grades.claim: EDCs act on the growth plate via ERalpha or aromatase.
claim_grades.basis: Universally asserted; a targeted Europe PMC search returns no mammalian growth plate study with an ERalpha or aromatase readout under EDC exposure. Logged as g_l10env_011.

endocrine_disrupting_chemicals.human_evidence_note: Human biomonitoring cohort with measured urinary and blood exposure biomarkers and Tanner-staged pubertal outcomes.
endocrine_disrupting_chemicals.translation_risk_reason: There is no animal growth plate EDC experiment to translate from; the zebrafish cartilage literature concerns craniofacial rather than endochondral growth.
localization: human SYS: urinary BPA and phthalate metabolites; blood lead, mercury, cadmium
human growth plate: no EDC exposure has ever been coupled to a physeal ERalpha or aromatase readout

key_refs.one_line_finding: In 1424 Korean children, mono-benzyl phthalate was associated with delayed puberty in girls (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.34-5.66), and BPA-phthalate mixtures with precocious puberty in boys and delayed puberty in both sexes.

energy_availability_growth.name: Energy availability and linear growth
energy_availability_growth.summary: Energy sufficiency is a gate rather than a dose on linear growth: below a threshold the GH-IGF and reproductive axes are switched down, and above it added energy buys very little extra height. The clearest quantitative statement of the ceiling comes from supplementation trials: pooled across 15 randomised trials of small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements in 10 low- and middle-income countries (n=36970), the gain in length-for-age Z was 0.15 (95% CI 0.12-0.17), corresponding to 12 days of height-age and 11% of the maximal attainable benefit (watson2025). In the INCAP village-randomised trial in Guatemala, a high-quality protein-energy supplement (Atole) improved nutrient intakes and reduced stunting, but only in children under 3 years of age, and the durable adult effects were on schooling, cognition and wages (men's wages +46% for those supplemented through age 2) rather than on a large height gain (martorell2017). The mechanistic entry points are endocrine and are held in L4: leptin as the adiposity-dependent permissive signal for the reproductive axis, and portal insulin with IGFBP-1 as the acute nutritional gate on IGF-1 bioavailability. No study has measured any of these in a randomised energy-supplementation trial with a linear-growth endpoint.

claim_grades.claim: Energy and micronutrient supplementation in undernourished populations produces a small linear growth gain, about 11% of the attainable deficit.
claim_grades.basis: Pooled 15 RCTs with prespecified proportion-of-maximal-benefit metric (watson2025).

claim_grades.claim: Supplementation benefits are confined to the first ~3 years of life.
claim_grades.basis: Village-randomised INCAP trial; the age restriction is reported in a review of that trial rather than from a within-trial age interaction test (martorell2017).

claim_grades.claim: The energy signal reaches the growth plate via leptin and insulin/IGFBP-1 control of IGF-1 bioavailability.
claim_grades.basis: Endocrine intermediates were not measured in any of these trials; the mechanism is imported from L4 endocrine nodes.

energy_availability_growth.human_evidence_note: Randomised human supplementation trials with measured linear growth, pooled across 36970 children.
energy_availability_growth.translation_risk_reason: Human intervention data; only the endocrine intermediates are imported from L4 rather than measured in these trials.
localization: human SYS: energy balance -> leptin, insulin, IGFBP-1 -> IGF-1 bioavailability

key_refs.one_line_finding: SQ-LNS raised LAZ by 0.15 (95% CI 0.12-0.17) across 15 RCTs (n=36970), equal to 12 days of height-age and 11% of maximal attainable benefit.
Reviews the INCAP village-randomised Atole vs Fresco trial: reduced stunting only in children under 3 y, and +46% adult male wages for those supplemented through age 2.

environmental_enteric_dysfunction.name: Environmental enteric dysfunction
environmental_enteric_dysfunction.summary: Environmental enteric dysfunction is subclinical small-intestinal inflammation with increased permeability, and it is the proposed reason that water, sanitation and hygiene interventions improve infection rates without improving height. The Indonesian Action Against Stunting Hub birth cohort provides the mechanistic chain in humans: faecal myeloperoxidase, faecal alpha-1 antitrypsin and plasma intestinal fatty-acid binding protein (IFABP) were measured at 6 months with anthropometry at 6 and 12 months, elevated EED markers were present in more than 80% of infants, and structural equation modelling showed IFABP positively associated with soluble CD14 and CD14 negatively associated with IGF-1, with maternal height, birth weight and IGF-1 the significant determinants of length-for-age Z at 12 months (htet2026). The pathway is therefore gut barrier failure -> microbial translocation -> systemic inflammation -> suppressed IGF-1 -> shorter children, with each link measured rather than assumed. A systematic review of 81 studies covering 31996 children found all EED domains - intestinal damage and repair, absorption and permeability, microbial translocation, intestinal inflammation and systemic inflammation - associated with linear growth, while noting that the measured association depends strongly on which biomarker is used (lowe2025). The last step, from suppressed IGF-1 to the chondrocyte, remains inferential.

claim_grades.claim: EED influences linear growth indirectly, through systemic inflammation and suppressed IGF-1.
claim_grades.basis: Structural equation modelling in a single longitudinal human cohort with measured mediators (htet2026); the mediation model is one cohort, not replicated.

claim_grades.claim: All measured EED domains are associated with child linear growth.
claim_grades.basis: Systematic review of 81 studies and 31996 children (lowe2025).

environmental_enteric_dysfunction.human_evidence_note: Human longitudinal birth cohort with faecal and plasma EED biomarkers, systemic inflammatory markers, IGF-1 and serial anthropometry.
environmental_enteric_dysfunction.translation_risk_reason: Every measured link in the chain is human; only the final chondrocyte step is extrapolated.
localization: human small intestine: barrier damage and inflammation
human SYS: soluble CD14 -> suppressed circulating IGF-1

key_refs.one_line_finding: In an Indonesian birth cohort, IFABP was positively associated with CD14 and CD14 negatively with IGF-1; IGF-1, maternal height and birth weight determined LAZ at 12 months, with >80% of infants showing elevated EED markers.
Systematic review of 81 studies (31996 children) finding all EED domains associated with child linear growth, with the association depending on biomarker choice.

gut_microbiome_growth.name: Gut microbiome and juvenile growth
gut_microbiome_growth.summary: The gut microbiome is causally sufficient to change juvenile body length in gnotobiotic mice and has not been shown to do so in humans. Three 2016 experiments define the state of evidence. Colonising germ-free mice with a conventional specific-pathogen-free microbiota increased both bone formation and resorption; with long-term colonisation, bone formation and growth plate activity predominated, giving increased longitudinal and radial bone growth, and serum IGF-1 rose substantially with increased IGF-1 production in liver and adipose tissue (yan2016). Conversely, antibiotic treatment of conventional mice lowered serum IGF-1 and inhibited bone formation, and supplying short-chain fatty acids to antibiotic-treated mice restored both IGF-1 and bone mass - which identifies SCFA production as a candidate mechanism (yan2016). Monocolonisation showed the effect is strain-specific: selected lactobacilli promoted juvenile growth in a strain-dependent way that recapitulated the whole microbiota's effect on the somatotropic axis, and buffered the growth cost of chronic undernutrition in germ-free mice (schwarzer2016). Transplanting microbiota from 6- and 18-month-old undernourished Malawian infants into germ-free mice fed a Malawian diet transmitted impaired growth, and adding Ruminococcus gnavus and Clostridium symbiosum ameliorated it (blanton2016) - the closest existing link between a human microbiota and a growth phenotype, but the phenotype is still read out in mice.

claim_grades.claim: Gut microbiota causally increase serum IGF-1 and longitudinal bone growth.
claim_grades.basis: Germ-free colonisation, antibiotic depletion and SCFA rescue in mice, replicated across two independent 2016 studies (yan2016, schwarzer2016).

claim_grades.claim: Microbiota immaturity in undernourished children is causally related to their growth impairment.
claim_grades.basis: Faecal transplant from Malawian donors into gnotobiotic mice transmits the phenotype (blanton2016); causality is established in the recipient mouse, not the donor child.

claim_grades.claim: Manipulating the microbiome raises IGF-1 and linear growth in humans.
claim_grades.basis: No randomised human trial reports an IGF-1 and linear growth endpoint after microbiota manipulation. Logged as g_l10env_001.

gut_microbiome_growth.human_evidence_note: The only human input is donor microbiota from undernourished Malawian children; the growth phenotype is measured in gnotobiotic mice, not in the donors.
gut_microbiome_growth.translation_risk_reason: Every causal demonstration is in germ-free or antibiotic-treated mice on defined diets. Mice do not fuse their growth plates and the germ-free state has no human counterpart.
localization: mouse growth plate: increased growth plate activity after long-term colonisation (yan2016)
human growth plate: never examined in relation to microbiota

key_refs.one_line_finding: Conventionalisation of germ-free mice increased serum IGF-1, growth plate activity and longitudinal and radial bone growth; antibiotics lowered IGF-1 and bone formation, and SCFA supplementation restored both.
The infant mouse microbiota sustains weight gain and longitudinal growth via the somatotropic axis; selected Lactobacillus plantarum strains recapitulate the effect and buffer chronic undernutrition.
Microbiota from undernourished Malawian infants transmitted impaired growth to gnotobiotic mice; Ruminococcus gnavus and Clostridium symbiosum ameliorated it.

infection_burden_growth.name: Infection burden and linear growth
infection_burden_growth.summary: Repeated infection is the environmental exposure that most plausibly explains why feeding children more food closes only about a tenth of their linear growth deficit, and its entry point into the graph is the inflammatory suppression of IGF-1. In 740 stunted Ugandan children aged 12-59 months, inflammation markers (C-reactive protein and alpha-1 acid glycoprotein) were the strongest negative correlates of serum IGF-1 in Tobit regression, and a positive rapid malaria test was associated with serum IGF-1 lower by 4.7 ug/L (95% CI -7.8 to -1.6) - an association that did not survive adjustment for inflammation, which is the point: the infection acts through the inflammatory response rather than beside it (madigan2026). The same cohort showed that plasma concentrations of 18 of 21 amino acids were lower in children with elevated inflammatory markers (larnkjr2026), so infection depletes substrate and blocks the anabolic signal at once. Downstream of this the mechanism is the SOCS/STAT5 and IGF1R-AKT/ERK interference documented in inflammation_growth_suppression, all of it rodent. No human study has measured SOCS2, SOCS3 or phospho-STAT5 in any tissue during a childhood infection with a linear growth endpoint.

claim_grades.claim: Infection lowers circulating IGF-1 in stunted children, and does so through the inflammatory response rather than independently of it.
claim_grades.basis: Malaria-IGF-1 association attenuated by inflammation adjustment in a cohort of 740 children with measured markers (madigan2026).

claim_grades.claim: Infection-driven IGF-1 suppression is transduced at the growth plate by SOCS-mediated STAT5 blockade.
claim_grades.basis: Mechanism demonstrated only in rodent liver and rodent chondrocytes (denson2003, choukair2014); untested in humans.

infection_burden_growth.human_evidence_note: Human cross-sectional cohort with rapid malaria testing, measured CRP and AGP, and measured serum IGF-1 in 740 stunted children.
infection_burden_growth.translation_risk_reason: The human data establish the association; the molecular interference steps between cytokine and chondrocyte are rodent-derived.
localization: human SYS: infection -> acute-phase response -> suppressed circulating IGF-1

key_refs.one_line_finding: Inflammation markers were the strongest negative correlates of serum IGF-1 in 740 stunted Ugandan children; malaria positivity was associated with -4.7 ug/L before inflammation adjustment.
Plasma concentrations of 18 of 21 amino acids were lower in stunted children with elevated inflammatory markers.
Endotoxin blocks hepatic GH-STAT5 signalling via IL-6-dependent induction of CIS and SOCS-3 in mice.

inflammation_growth_suppression.name: Inflammatory suppression of linear growth
inflammation_growth_suppression.summary: Chronic inflammation suppresses linear growth through two mechanistically distinct and independently demonstrated routes. The hepatic route is SOCS-mediated interruption of GH signalling: LPS pretreatment abolished GH-induced STAT5 activation in wild-type and TNFR1-null mice but not in IL-6-null mice, GHR abundance was unchanged, and the loss of STAT5 activation was temporally coupled to STAT3 phosphorylation and upregulation of CIS and SOCS-3 protein (denson2003). The plate-intrinsic route is direct cytokine interference with IGF-I signalling in chondrocytes: in the RCJ3.1C5.18 rat chondrogenic line, IL-1beta (10 ng/mL), IL-6 (100 ng/mL) or TNF-alpha (50 ng/mL) co-incubated with IGF-I cut IGF-I-driven proliferation by 50% without altering baseline proliferation, attenuated IGF-I-induced AKT phosphorylation by 30-50% and ERK phosphorylation by 50-75%, and blocked IGF-I-enhanced differentiation (choukair2014). At the organ level, 8 days of IL-1beta or TNF-alpha reduced murine metatarsal growth by 71% and 45% respectively, with an additive 110% reduction in combination; a 2-day single-cytokine exposure was fully reversible, but the combination left growth 59% below control after 6 days of recovery (macrae2006). SOCS2 is the specific brake: TNF-alpha exposure of growth plate chondrocytes increased SOCS2 protein (macrae2009), SOCS2 is the only SOCS induced by GH in chondrocytes and its loss increases chondrocyte STAT1/3/5 phosphorylation, growth plate width and bone growth rate (pass2012), and Socs2-null mice are protected from the skeletal effects of DSS colitis (dobie2018). The therapeutic irony is quantified: 4-6 years of inhaled budesonide from age 5-13 left adult height 1.2 cm lower (95% CI -1.9 to -0.5) in 943 CAMP participants (kelly2012).

claim_grades.claim: IL-6 is required for endotoxin-induced loss of hepatic GH-STAT5 signalling, and the loss is mediated by CIS and SOCS-3 rather than by GHR downregulation.
claim_grades.basis: Mouse genetic dissection with IL-6-null and TNFR1-null strains, immunoblot, EMSA and RT-PCR (denson2003); no human replication.

claim_grades.claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines halve IGF-I-driven chondrocyte proliferation and attenuate AKT and ERK phosphorylation.
claim_grades.basis: Single study in one rat chondrogenic cell line (choukair2014).

claim_grades.claim: Combined IL-1beta and TNF-alpha exposure produces growth suppression that does not fully recover after withdrawal.
claim_grades.basis: Murine metatarsal organ culture with washout design (macrae2006); not tested in vivo or in human tissue.

claim_grades.claim: SOCS2 is the specific negative regulator of GH action in growth plate chondrocytes.
claim_grades.basis: Socs2-null mouse genetics with metatarsal culture, growth plate histomorphometry and phospho-STAT quantification (pass2012, macrae2009, dobie2015, dobie2018).

claim_grades.claim: Suppressing childhood inflammation with inhaled glucocorticoid costs about 1.2 cm of adult height.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised trial with adult height measured in 943 of 1041 participants and a dose-response (kelly2012).

inflammation_growth_suppression.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is the association of inflammatory markers with low IGF-1 in stunted children and the randomised adult-height cost of inhaled glucocorticoid; the SOCS/STAT5 and chondrocyte signalling steps are rodent and rodent-cell-line only.
inflammation_growth_suppression.translation_risk_reason: Every mechanistic step - SOCS3/CIS induction, STAT5 blockade, AKT/ERK attenuation, metatarsal growth arrest - is rodent. Mice do not fuse their growth plates, so the irreversibility observed in metatarsal culture cannot be mapped onto human final height.
localization: mouse growth plate: TNF-alpha increases SOCS2 protein in growth plate chondrocytes (macrae2009)
mouse growth plate: SOCS2 loss increases phospho-STAT5-positive hypertrophic chondrocytes (pass2012)
human growth plate: no cytokine, SOCS or phospho-STAT5 measurement in human physeal tissue exists

key_refs.one_line_finding: LPS abolished GH-induced hepatic STAT5 activation in wild-type and TNFR1-null but not IL-6-null mice, with unchanged GHR and upregulated CIS and SOCS-3.
IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha each cut IGF-I-driven chondrocyte proliferation by 50% and attenuated IGF-I-induced AKT (30-50%) and ERK (50-75%) phosphorylation.
IL-1beta and TNF-alpha reduced murine metatarsal growth by 71% and 45% over 8 days, additively by 110%, with incomplete recovery (59% deficit) after combined exposure.
SOCS2, not SOCS1 or SOCS3, is GH-induced in chondrocytes; its deletion increases chondrocyte STAT1/3/5 phosphorylation, growth plate width, chondrocyte proliferation and bone growth rate.
TNF-alpha exposure of growth plate chondrocytes for 48 h increased SOCS2 protein; Socs2-null mice were 6% longer with 24% wider growth plates.
Socs2 deletion protected mouse trabecular bone from DSS colitis, placing SOCS2 in the inflammation-to-skeleton pathway.
Budesonide 400 ug/day for 4-6 years in childhood lowered adult height by 1.2 cm (95% CI -1.9 to -0.5) in 943 CAMP participants, with a dose-response of -0.1 cm per ug/kg/day.

intrauterine_growth_restriction.name: Intrauterine growth restriction
intrauterine_growth_restriction.summary: Intrauterine growth restriction is failure to achieve the genetically expected fetal growth trajectory, and it is the point at which environmental exposure and the fetal IGF axis meet most directly. Its importance for adult stature is quantified through birth size: in a population-based Swedish cohort of 3650 healthy full-term singletons followed to final height at about 18 years, infants short at birth (birth length below -2 SDS) carried a 7.1-fold higher risk of short adult stature (95% CI 3.7-13.6) than non-short-at-birth infants, and 22% of the short 18-year-olds had been short at birth while only 14% had been light at birth (karlberg1995) - birth length, not birth weight, is the informative measure. Across five long-running birth cohorts, intrauterine growth restriction was among the indices most strongly related to shorter adult height (victora2008). The Dutch Hunger Winter shows what the restriction does to the genotype-phenotype map: severe mid-to-late gestational famine abolished the detectable influence of a birthweight polygenic index (taeubert2026). The mechanistic entry point is the fetal IGF system - IGF-2 dominates fetal growth and PAPP-A2 sets IGF bioavailability - but no human study links a measured IUGR exposure to a measured fetal IGF-axis parameter and a growth plate readout.

claim_grades.claim: Short birth length carries a seven-fold risk of short adult stature.
claim_grades.basis: Population-based cohort of 3650 followed to final height with a reported relative risk and CI (karlberg1995).

claim_grades.claim: Birth length is a better predictor of adult short stature than birth weight.
claim_grades.basis: Within-cohort comparison of the two definitions in the same 3650 children (karlberg1995).

claim_grades.claim: IUGR acts through suppressed fetal IGF-2/IGF-1 signalling at the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Not measured in these cohorts; imported from L4 igf2_hormone and pappa2_protease.
