intrauterine_growth_restriction.human_evidence_note: Population-based human birth cohort followed to final height, plus pooled multi-country cohort analyses.
intrauterine_growth_restriction.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype with human longitudinal follow-up.
localization: human SYS: fetal growth trajectory; entry via the fetal IGF-2/IGF-1 axis (L4)

key_refs.one_line_finding: In 3650 full-term Swedish singletons, birth length below -2 SDS carried a 7.1-fold risk of short final stature (95% CI 3.7-13.6); 22% of short 18-year-olds had been short at birth.
Intrauterine growth restriction was among the indices most strongly associated with shorter adult height across five LMIC birth cohorts.
Severe mid-to-late gestational famine abolished the detectable influence of a birthweight polygenic index on birthweight.

iodine_deficiency_growth.name: Iodine deficiency and linear growth
iodine_deficiency_growth.summary: Iodine is the micronutrient whose route to the growth plate is fully specified by an existing endocrine node: iodine is the substrate for thyroxine, and thyroid hormone acting through THRA on prehypertrophic chondrocytes is required for hypertrophic differentiation. The human interventional evidence closes the loop at the level of the GH-IGF axis. Three prospective double-blind intervention studies - severely deficient Moroccan children aged 7-10 given iodised salt for 10 months (n=71), moderately deficient Albanian children aged 10-12 given 400 mg iodine as oral iodised oil for 6 months (n=310), and mildly deficient South African children aged 5-14 given two 200 mg doses (n=188) - all raised median urinary iodine above 100 ug/L, and iodine repletion increased IGF-I and IGFBP-3 concentrations and improved somatic growth, with the smallest effect in the mildly deficient South African group where IGF-I rose only modestly (zimmermann2007). A systematic review of 18 studies (13 RCTs, n=5729) found iodine supplementation of severely deficient pregnant women increased mean birthweight by 200 g, while postnatal growth effects in non-cretinous children were inconsistent (farebrother2018). Iodine therefore behaves as a threshold nutrient like vitamin D: severe deficiency has large effects, mild deficiency has small and inconsistent ones.

claim_grades.claim: Iodine repletion raises IGF-I and IGFBP-3 and improves somatic growth in iodine-deficient school-age children.
claim_grades.basis: Three prospective double-blind interventions across three severity strata with exposure verified by urinary iodine (zimmermann2007).

claim_grades.claim: Postnatal growth benefit is inconsistent in non-cretinous, mildly deficient children.
claim_grades.basis: Systematic review with GRADE assessment of 18 studies, n=5729 (farebrother2018).

claim_grades.claim: The growth effect is transduced by T3 acting on THRA in prehypertrophic chondrocytes.
claim_grades.basis: Thyroid hormone action at the plate is established in the L4 thra_receptor and thyroid_hormone_t3 nodes; not measured in any iodine trial.

iodine_deficiency_growth.human_evidence_note: Three prospective double-blind iodine repletion trials with measured urinary iodine, thyroid function, IGF-I, IGFBP-3 and growth, plus a systematic review of 18 studies.
iodine_deficiency_growth.translation_risk_reason: Human interventional data with human endocrine endpoints; only the chondrocyte-level thyroid hormone step is imported from L4.
localization: human SYS: dietary iodine -> T4/T3 -> THRA in prehypertrophic chondrocytes (L4)
human growth plate: thyroid hormone receptor action inferred from L4, not measured under iodine repletion

key_refs.one_line_finding: Iodine repletion in three double-blind trials (n=71, 310, 188) raised urinary iodine above 100 ug/L and increased IGF-I and IGFBP-3 with improved somatic growth; the mildly deficient South African group showed only a modest IGF-I rise.

Systematic review of 18 studies (n=5729): iodine supplementation of severely deficient pregnant women raised mean birthweight by 200 g; postnatal growth effects in non-cretinous children were uncertain.

iron_deficiency_growth.name: Iron deficiency and linear growth
iron_deficiency_growth.summary: Iron deficiency is the most prevalent single-nutrient deficiency in children and has the weakest case of any classical micronutrient for a direct effect on the growth plate. Iron status is entangled with the two factors that do have demonstrated entry points: chronic inflammation raises hepcidin and lowers serum iron while independently suppressing IGF-1, and poor-quality diets that are iron-poor are also protein-poor and zinc-poor. In the Ugandan stunting cohort (n=740), which measured iron, B12, folate and vitamin A status alongside infections and animal-source-food intake as correlates of serum IGF-1, inflammation markers were the strongest negative correlates of IGF-1 (madigan2026), so any iron-IGF-1 association must be adjusted for inflammation before it can be interpreted. No experiment in any species has shown an iron-dependent step in chondrocyte proliferation, hypertrophy or matrix mineralisation at physiologically attainable iron concentrations, and none of the candidate routes - prolyl hydroxylase (an Fe(II)- and 2-oxoglutarate-dependent enzyme that destabilises HIF-1alpha, which L3 carries as hif1a_chondrocyte) or the Fe-dependent lysyl hydroxylases of collagen crosslinking - has been tested under dietary iron restriction with a growth plate readout. This node exists to name that absence rather than to assert an epidemiological association without a mechanism.

claim_grades.claim: Iron status is measured alongside, and confounded by, inflammation in stunted children.
claim_grades.basis: Cross-sectional cohort of 740 stunted Ugandan children with iron, B12, folate, vitamin A, CRP, AGP and IGF-1 (madigan2026).

claim_grades.claim: Iron deficiency has a demonstrated molecular entry point at the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: No primary experiment exists; the prolyl-hydroxylase/HIF and lysyl-hydroxylase routes are untested under dietary iron restriction. Logged as g_l10env_007.

iron_deficiency_growth.human_evidence_note: Human cohort data measure iron status alongside IGF-1 and inflammation in stunted children, but no human study isolates an iron effect on linear growth from inflammation and diet quality.
iron_deficiency_growth.translation_risk_reason: There is no animal growth plate experiment on dietary iron restriction to translate from.
localization: human SYS: iron status confounded with inflammation and with diet quality
human growth plate: no iron-dependent step demonstrated

key_refs.one_line_finding: In 740 stunted Ugandan children iron, B12, folate and vitamin A status were assessed as correlates of serum IGF-1 alongside infections; inflammation markers were the strongest negative correlates.

lead_exposure_growth.name: Lead exposure and linear growth
lead_exposure_growth.summary: Blood lead is inversely associated with stature at concentrations that were once considered unremarkable, and the association has no established molecular entry point at the growth plate. In 1454 Mexican-American children aged 5-12 from the Hispanic Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (1982-1984), blood lead across the range 0.14-1.92 umol/L was inversely related to stature, the authors' point being that growth retardation appears at moderate and not merely at toxic concentrations (frisancho1991). A clinical series of 880 children referred for short stature found blood lead higher, and height, weight and serum IGF-1 lower, in the GH-deficient group than in the idiopathic-short-stature group (P<0.05), and in a companion rat lead-exposure model the phosphorylation of ERK1/2, JNK, p38, Akt(S473) and Akt(T308) was increased (P<0.01) (xu2014) - a result whose direction is the opposite of what a simple IGF-I-signalling blockade would predict and which has not been replicated. Nothing connects lead to a named growth plate protein. Lead is a calcium mimic that accumulates in mineralising tissue, which makes hydroxyapatite nucleation and the calcium-sensing receptor plausible targets, but neither has been tested with a physeal readout. Recorded here as an epidemiological association with an explicitly missing mechanistic link.

claim_grades.claim: Blood lead is inversely associated with stature in children at moderate concentrations.
claim_grades.basis: National survey sample of 1454 children with measured blood lead and measured height (frisancho1991); observational and confounded with socioeconomic position.

claim_grades.claim: Lead lowers serum IGF-1 in children.
claim_grades.basis: Single clinical series in which the low-IGF-1 group also had higher blood lead; no adjustment for referral bias or socioeconomic position reported in the abstract (xu2014).

claim_grades.claim: Lead has a molecular entry point at the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: No study identifies a lead target in physeal cartilage; the rat data show increased, not decreased, MAPK and Akt phosphorylation. Logged as g_l10env_007.

lead_exposure_growth.human_evidence_note: Two human datasets with measured blood lead and measured stature, one national survey and one clinical series with serum IGF-1.
lead_exposure_growth.translation_risk_reason: The only mechanistic data are a rat lead-poisoning model with whole-tissue phosphoprotein immunoblots, not chondrocyte-resolved and not replicated.
localization: human SYS: blood lead, bone lead stores
human growth plate: no lead target identified

key_refs.one_line_finding: In 1454 Mexican-American children aged 5-12, blood lead over 0.14-1.92 umol/L was inversely related to stature.

In 880 children with short stature, the GH-deficient group had lower height, weight and serum IGF-1 and higher blood lead than the idiopathic group; a rat lead model showed increased ERK1/2, JNK, p38 and Akt phosphorylation.

maternal_nutrition_offspring_height.name: Maternal nutrition and offspring height
maternal_nutrition_offspring_height.summary: Maternal nutrition sets offspring size, and the intergenerational transmission of stature is one of the strongest correlations in human growth epidemiology. Across five long-running birth cohorts, maternal height was one of the indices most strongly related to offspring birthweight and adult outcomes, and undernutrition in mothers and children was strongly associated with shorter adult height in the next generation (victora2008). In the Indonesian Action Against Stunting Hub birth cohort, maternal height, birth weight and infant IGF-1 were the significant determinants of length-for-age Z at 12 months (htet2026). The interventional evidence is the INCAP village-randomised trial in Guatemala (1969-1977), in which a high-quality protein-energy-micronutrient supplement (Atole) was given to pregnant and lactating women and to children under 7 in two villages while two control villages received a low-energy drink (Fresco): Atole improved nutrient intakes and reduced stunting, but only in children under 3 years of age, and the durable adult effects were on schooling, reading, intelligence and wages rather than on a large stature gain (martorell2017). The mechanistic entry point at the fetal stage is the IGF-2/IGF-1 and placental IGFBP-protease system carried in L4, none of which was measured in these studies.

claim_grades.claim: Maternal height and maternal nutrition predict offspring linear growth.
claim_grades.basis: Five-cohort pooled analysis (victora2008) and a longitudinal cohort with structural equation modelling (htet2026).

claim_grades.claim: Maternal and early-child protein-energy supplementation reduces stunting only before age 3.
claim_grades.basis: Village-randomised trial reported through a narrative review of its own results (martorell2017).

claim_grades.claim: Maternal nutrition acts on the fetal growth plate through the IGF-2/PAPP-A2 system.
claim_grades.basis: Neither IGF-2 nor PAPP-A2 was measured in any of these studies; the route is imported from L4.

maternal_nutrition_offspring_height.human_evidence_note: Village-randomised human supplementation trial with 30-year follow-up plus pooled birth cohort analyses with measured maternal height.
localization: human SYS: maternal nutrition -> placental transfer -> fetal IGF axis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Maternal height and undernutrition indices predicted offspring birthweight and adult height across five LMIC birth cohorts.
The INCAP Atole trial reduced stunting only in children under 3 y and raised adult male wages 46% for those supplemented through age 2.
Maternal height, birth weight and infant IGF-1 were the significant determinants of length-for-age Z at 12 months in an Indonesian birth cohort.

microbiome_igf1_axis.name: Microbiome-IGF-1 axis
microbiome_igf1_axis.summary: The proposed molecular link from gut bacteria to the growth plate is short-chain fatty acids raising hepatic and adipose IGF-1 production. In mice, colonisation of germ-free animals substantially increased serum IGF-1 with increased IGF-1 production in liver and adipose tissue; antibiotic treatment of conventional mice decreased serum IGF-1 and inhibited bone formation; and supplementing antibiotic-treated mice with short-chain fatty acids - products of microbial fermentation - restored IGF-1 and bone mass to untreated levels (yan2016). That restoration experiment is the load-bearing evidence: it converts a correlation between microbiota and IGF-1 into a sufficiency claim for a specific class of microbial metabolite. The somatotropic axis is also the route by which monocolonising lactobacilli promote juvenile growth (schwarzer2016). Two things are missing before this can be used as a human entry point. No SCFA receptor or transporter has been localised or functionally tested in growth plate chondrocytes in any species, so the metabolite may act entirely on the liver. And no human study has manipulated the microbiota and measured IGF-1 and linear growth together, so the entire axis is a mouse construct with a human motivation.

claim_grades.claim: Short-chain fatty acids are sufficient to restore serum IGF-1 and bone mass after microbiota depletion.
claim_grades.basis: Antibiotic depletion plus SCFA repletion in mice, single study (yan2016).

claim_grades.claim: The microbiome-IGF-1 axis operates in humans.
claim_grades.basis: Asserted throughout the review literature; no human interventional test exists. Logged as g_l10env_001.

microbiome_igf1_axis.human_evidence_note: No human study measures a microbiota manipulation, circulating IGF-1 and linear growth together.
microbiome_igf1_axis.translation_risk_reason: Germ-free and antibiotic-depleted mouse states have no human equivalent, and the human IGF axis differs from the mouse in carrying abundant postnatal IGF-2.
localization: mouse liver and adipose tissue: increased IGF-1 production after colonisation (yan2016)
mouse and human growth plate: no SCFA receptor localisation or function reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Microbial colonisation raised serum IGF-1 with increased hepatic and adipose IGF-1 production; antibiotics lowered it and SCFA supplementation restored IGF-1 and bone mass.
Selected lactobacilli sustain juvenile growth through the somatotropic hormone axis in monocolonised mice.

migration_studies_height.name: Migrant population height studies
migration_studies_height.summary: Migration is the cleanest natural experiment separating population environment from population genotype, because it moves a genotype into a new environment within one generation. The Dutch surveys carry the sharpest version: between 1997 and 2009 Turkish- and Moroccan-origin children living in the Netherlands gained 2-3 cm in mean height at age 18, reaching 177 cm for boys and 163 cm for girls, during exactly the interval in which Dutch-origin children showed no gain at all (schnbeck2015, schnbeck2013). At the same time these adolescents remained 5.5 cm (boys) to 7 cm (girls) shorter than Dutch-origin peers, and within the migrant groups height showed no significant difference across parental educational level, geographical region, home language or immigrant generation (schnbeck2015). Two conclusions follow. The continuing gain in the migrant groups shows the Dutch environment was not saturated for everyone in that decade, which is evidence against reading the Dutch plateau as a property of the environment. The persisting 5.5-7 cm gap, flat across the measured social covariates, is either genetic, a lagged effect of maternal and intergenerational environment, or an unmeasured exposure; this design cannot separate them.

claim_grades.claim: Migrant-origin children in the Netherlands continued to gain height while Dutch-origin children plateaued.
claim_grades.basis: Same nationwide surveys, same decade, measured height, n>16000 (schnbeck2015).

claim_grades.claim: The residual 5.5-7 cm gap reflects genotype rather than a lagged environmental effect.
claim_grades.basis: Not tested; the absence of a gradient by parental education, region, language or generation is compatible with either explanation.

migration_studies_height.human_evidence_note: Nationwide measured-height surveys of >5000 migrant-origin and >11000 Dutch-origin children at two time points.
localization: human SYS: population phenotype

key_refs.one_line_finding: Turkish- and Moroccan-origin children in the Netherlands gained 2-3 cm between 1997 and 2009 while the Dutch secular trend had halted; they remained 5.5-7 cm shorter than Dutch peers with no gradient by parental education, region, language or generation.
Dutch-origin height by age in 2009 was unchanged from 1997.

milk_consumption_height.name: Cow's milk intake and linear growth
milk_consumption_height.summary: Cow's milk is the single dietary item with a reproducible, source-specific effect on the human GH-IGF axis, and it is the best-characterised environmental input into that axis. In a randomised 7-day intervention in 24 healthy 8-year-old boys, 1.5 L/day of skimmed milk raised serum IGF-I by 19% (P=0.001) and IGF-I/IGFBP-3 by 13% (P<0.0001), while the same quantity of protein as lean meat raised neither, even though protein intake rose by 54-61% in both arms (hoppe2004). A 2x2 factorial trial in 57 boys localised the effect to the casein fraction (+15% IGF-1, P<0.0001) and separated it from the whey fraction, which instead raised fasting insulin by 21% (P=0.006); high milk-mineral content had no independent effect on IGF-1 or insulin (hoppe2009). The growth-promoting component of milk is therefore neither its total protein nor its calcium and phosphorus. Observationally, milk intake associates with linear growth in both undernourished and well-nourished populations, an association the field reads through the IGF axis (hoppe2006). What is missing is any demonstration that the milk-induced increment in circulating IGF-1 changes chondrocyte proliferation or hypertrophy - no milk intervention has ever been coupled to a growth plate readout.

claim_grades.claim: Milk raises circulating IGF-I in prepubertal children and an isonitrogenous meat load does not.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised human intervention, weighed dietary records (hoppe2004).

claim_grades.claim: The IGF-1-raising component is casein, not whey and not milk minerals.
claim_grades.basis: 2x2 factorial randomised trial, n=57 (hoppe2009).

claim_grades.claim: Milk-induced IGF-1 elevation translates into faster chondrocyte proliferation at the plate.
claim_grades.basis: Never measured; inferred from IGF-1 action in other systems.

milk_consumption_height.human_evidence_note: Two randomised controlled dietary interventions in prepubertal boys with measured serum IGF-I, IGFBP-3 and insulin.
milk_consumption_height.translation_risk_reason: The endocrine response is a direct human measurement; only the plate-level consequence is inferred.
localization: human SYS: diet -> hepatic IGF-1 and IGFBP-3
human growth plate: never measured under a milk intervention

key_refs.one_line_finding: Skimmed milk but not meat raised serum IGF-I (19%) and IGF-I/IGFBP-3 (13%) in 8-year-old boys over 7 days.
Casein raised IGF-1 15%, whey raised fasting insulin 21%, milk minerals had no independent effect (n=57).
Reviews observational and intervention evidence that cow's milk stimulates linear growth in developing and industrialised settings, proposing IGF-I as the mediator.

ncd_risc_height_dataset.name: NCD-RisC pooled height database
ncd_risc_height_dataset.summary: NCD-RisC is the reference source for population height and the only one pooling measured rather than self-reported stature at global scale. The adult analysis covers 1472 population-based studies with measured height on 18.6 million adults in 200 countries, modelled by a Bayesian hierarchical model to give mean height by birth cohort from 1896 to 1996 (ncd2016). The child and adolescent analysis pools 2181 studies with height and weight on 65 million participants aged 5-19 in 200 countries and territories, giving mean height by single year of age from 1985 to 2019 (ncd2020). Two structural features matter for anyone using these numbers. First, the model borrows strength across countries within a region, so estimates in data-sparse regions are partly regional and must be quoted with their credible intervals. Second, adult height for early birth cohorts is estimated from participants who were measured at older ages, so the divergence between the fitted line and the raw data in early cohorts is an age effect built into the model, not a data error (ncd2016). The database contains no biological covariate - no IGF-1, no bone age, no dietary measure - so it can bound the size of environmental effects on stature but cannot attribute them to a mechanism.
ncd_risc_height_dataset.human_evidence_note: The dataset is a corpus of human measurements; height is measured by trained staff in the contributing surveys.
localization: human SYS: global population dataset

key_refs.one_line_finding: 1472 studies, 18.6M measured adult heights, 200 countries, birth cohorts 1896-1996, Bayesian hierarchical model.
2181 studies, 65M participants aged 5-19, 200 countries and territories, 1985-2019; >=20 cm between-country range in mean height at age 19 in 2019.

aliases: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration height data

netherlands_tallest_population.name: The Dutch height plateau
netherlands_tallest_population.summary: Dutch men born in the last quarter of the 20th century have the highest population mean height ever recorded, above 182.5 cm (ncd2016), and the Dutch series is the only one long enough to show a clean stop. In the fifth Dutch nationwide growth study (2009; 5811 boys and 6194 girls aged 0-21) mean final height was 183.8 cm (SD 7.1) in men and 170.7 cm (SD 6.3) in women, and height-by-age was the same as in the 1997 survey after 150 years of continuous increase (schnbeck2013). The decisive observation against reading this as a shared environmental ceiling comes from the same surveys: Turkish- and Moroccan-origin children living in the Netherlands gained 2-3 cm between 1997 and 2009 while Dutch-origin children were flat, and at age 18 remained 5.5 cm (boys) to 7 cm (girls) shorter than their Dutch peers (schnbeck2015). Two populations sharing one country, food supply and health system sat on opposite sides of the plateau in the same decade. Within the Dutch population height still correlates with the child's and the parents' educational level (schnbeck2013), so a social gradient persists inside the plateaued population, which a saturated environment does not predict. Whether the plateau is a genetic ceiling or an unmeasured persisting constraint has never been tested.

claim_grades.claim: Dutch height stopped increasing between 1997 and 2009 after 150 years of rise.
claim_grades.basis: Nationwide measured survey, n=12005, direct comparison with the 1997 survey (schnbeck2013).

claim_grades.claim: The plateau is population-specific and not a property of the Dutch environment.
claim_grades.basis: Turkish- and Moroccan-origin children in the same country and the same surveys continued to gain 2-3 cm over the same interval (schnbeck2015).

claim_grades.claim: The plateau represents an attained genetic ceiling for Dutch stature.
claim_grades.basis: Offered by the authors as one of two alternatives; no discriminating test has been performed. Logged as g_l10env_005.

netherlands_tallest_population.human_evidence_note: Five serial nationwide measured-height surveys of Dutch children (1955, 1965, 1980, 1997, 2009), 12005 children in the final Dutch-origin wave.
localization: human SYS: national population phenotype

key_refs.one_line_finding: Dutch height-by-age in 2009 (n=12005) was identical to 1997; mean final height 183.8 cm (men) and 170.7 cm (women); height correlates with child and parental education.
Turkish- and Moroccan-origin children in the Netherlands gained 2-3 cm between 1997 and 2009 while Dutch-origin children did not, and remained 5.5-7 cm shorter at age 18.
Dutch men born in the last quarter of the 20th century have the highest mean adult height on record, above 182.5 cm.

placental_function_growth.name: Placental function and fetal growth
placental_function_growth.summary: The placenta is the organ through which every prenatal environmental exposure in this layer must pass, and it is the least-instrumented node in the chain. Its measurable output is fetal size, and in the Indonesian Action Against Stunting Hub cohort birth weight and maternal height were, with infant IGF-1, the significant determinants of length-for-age Z at 12 months (htet2026). The Dutch Hunger Winter shows the placenta failing as a buffer: mid-to-late gestational famine reduced fetal growth and, more strikingly, abolished the detectable expression of a birthweight polygenic index, which explained 14% of birthweight variance in unexposed controls (taeubert2026). Mechanistically the placenta is where the atlas's IGF bioavailability machinery is most concentrated - PAPP-A and PAPP-A2 are named for their pregnancy-associated plasma abundance and are the proteases that liberate IGF from IGFBP-4 and from IGFBP-3/IGFBP-5 respectively (L4 pappa_protease, pappa2_protease), and HSD11B2 forms the placental barrier that shields the fetus from maternal cortisol (L4 hsd11b2_enzyme). But none of the human cohorts cited here measured a placental protein, and no study links a measured placental PAPP-A2 activity to a measured fetal or infant linear growth outcome. This node is deliberately thin: it names the entry points rather than claiming them.

claim_grades.claim: Birth weight, as the placenta's integrated output, predicts infant linear growth.
claim_grades.basis: Longitudinal cohort with structural equation modelling (htet2026); pooled cohorts (victora2008).

claim_grades.claim: Placental PAPP-A2 activity sets fetal IGF bioavailability and hence fetal linear growth in humans.
claim_grades.basis: No study measures placental PAPP-A2 activity against a fetal or infant linear growth endpoint; the protease biology is established in L4 from postnatal human genetics.

placental_function_growth.human_evidence_note: Human cohorts measure the placenta's output (birth weight) rather than the placenta; the molecular entry points are named from L4 rather than measured here.
placental_function_growth.translation_risk_reason: Placental structure and IGF-2 imprinting differ substantially between human and mouse, so rodent placental data do not transfer cleanly.
localization: human placenta: PAPP-A, PAPP-A2 and HSD11B2 are placentally expressed (see L4 nodes)
human placenta: no cohort in this layer measured any placental protein

key_refs.one_line_finding: Birth weight and maternal height, together with infant IGF-1, were the significant determinants of length-for-age Z at 12 months in an Indonesian birth cohort.
Prenatal famine, acting through the maternal-placental supply line, abolished the detectable genetic contribution to birthweight.

population_height_variation.name: Between-population variation in height
population_height_variation.summary: The spread of mean adult height across human populations is about 19-20 cm and it has not narrowed. A century ago the tallest and shortest national means differed by 19-20 cm; a century later the differential is unchanged for women and has widened for men, despite a near-complete reshuffling of the country ranking (ncd2016). The extremes are Dutch men born in the last quarter of the 20th century (>182.5 cm) and Guatemalan women born in 1896 (140.3 cm, 95% CrI 135.8-144.8). The same spread is present in adolescents: in 2019 the difference between the tallest and shortest national means at age 19 was 20 cm or more (ncd2020). The structural point for the atlas is that the between-population range (~20 cm) and the largest observed within-population secular gain (~20 cm) are the same magnitude, so environmental change alone can move a population across essentially the entire observed between-population range. That does not make the differences purely environmental - the ranking changed while the spread did not - but it does mean that inferring a genetic difference from a contemporary height difference between two populations is unidentified without cohort data.
population_height_variation.human_evidence_note: Measured heights from 200 countries pooled by NCD-RisC.
localization: human SYS: population phenotype

key_refs.one_line_finding: The tallest-to-shortest national mean adult height differential was 19-20 cm a century ago, unchanged for women and larger for men today; lowest recorded mean 140.3 cm (Guatemalan women, 1896).
Difference of 20 cm or more between the tallest and shortest national mean heights at age 19 in 2019.

preterm_birth_growth.name: Preterm birth and linear growth
preterm_birth_growth.summary: Preterm birth removes the fetus from the intrauterine environment during the period of fastest linear growth and costs adult height. A systematic review of 27 studies of adults born prematurely found reduced height among the endocrine outcomes, alongside hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysfunction, lower bone mineral density and increased odds of hypothyroidism (claffey2025). The most informative exposure in this population is iatrogenic rather than gestational: antenatal glucocorticoid, given to accelerate fetal lung maturation, is a direct environmental manipulation of the L4 glucocorticoid receptor at a defined developmental moment. In a single-centre cohort recruited from 1994 with a median of 19 height measurements per child to a median age of 15.8 years, SITAR modelling of 202 children found that in girls (n=59 with covariates) antenatal steroid exposure was positively associated with the SITAR size and intensity random effects, equating to a predicted final height 2.8 cm greater (95% CI 0.3-5.3) than in unexposed girls after adjustment for gestational age and both parents' heights (lawrence2025). The direction is opposite to the growth suppression produced by postnatal glucocorticoid, which makes it a sharp test case: the same receptor, opposite sign, different developmental window. The result is sex-restricted, from one centre, and needs replication before it can be treated as a general property of prenatal GR activation.

claim_grades.claim: Adults born preterm are shorter than term-born adults.
claim_grades.basis: Systematic review of 27 studies of long-term endocrine outcomes after prematurity (claffey2025); heterogeneous designs, no pooled effect size given.

claim_grades.claim: Antenatal glucocorticoid exposure is associated with 2.8 cm greater final height in girls.
claim_grades.basis: Single-centre observational cohort, girls only, n=59 with complete covariates, not randomised to steroid (lawrence2025).

preterm_birth_growth.human_evidence_note: Longitudinal human cohort with ~19 serial height measurements per child and SITAR growth-curve modelling, plus a systematic review of 27 studies of adults born preterm.
localization: human SYS: antenatal glucocorticoid -> fetal GR (L4 glucocorticoid_receptor)
human growth plate: never examined in preterm-born children

key_refs.one_line_finding: SITAR modelling of 202 children (median 19 height measurements each) found antenatal steroid exposure associated with 2.8 cm (95% CI 0.3-5.3) greater predicted final height in girls, adjusted for gestational age and parental heights.
Systematic review of 27 studies: adults born preterm show reduced height, HPA axis dysfunction, lower bone mineral density and increased odds of hypothyroidism.

protein_intake_growth.name: Dietary protein intake and linear growth
protein_intake_growth.summary: Dietary protein reaches the growth plate through two verified molecular entry points and one unverified one. The verified systemic route is hepatic IGF-1: in 24 healthy 8-year-old boys randomised to 1.5 L skimmed milk or an isonitrogenous quantity of lean meat for 7 days, protein intake rose 61% and 54% respectively, yet serum IGF-I rose 19% (P=0.001) and the IGF-I/IGFBP-3 ratio 13% (P<0.0001) only in the milk arm and not at all in the meat arm (hoppe2004). Protein quantity is therefore not the operative variable; protein source is. A 2x2 factorial follow-up in 57 boys separated the fractions: casein raised serum IGF-1 by 15% (P<0.0001) with no change in fasting insulin, while whey raised fasting insulin by 21% (P=0.006) with no change in IGF-1, and milk minerals (Ca, P) had no independent effect on either (hoppe2009). The second entry point is amino-acid substrate itself: in 711-730 stunted Ugandan children plasma concentrations of 18 of 21 amino acids were lower where inflammatory markers were elevated, and plasma amino acids were examined as correlates of serum IGF-1 and linear growth (larnkjr2026). The third proposed entry point, direct leucine-sensing by mTORC1 in growth plate chondrocytes, has not been demonstrated for a dietary protein manipulation in any species and is registered as a gap.

claim_grades.claim: Milk protein, but not an equal quantity of meat protein, raises serum IGF-I in prepubertal children within 7 days.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised human intervention with weighed dietary records and RIA IGF-I (hoppe2004), fraction-resolved in a second randomised trial (hoppe2009).

claim_grades.claim: The casein fraction carries the IGF-1 effect and the whey fraction carries the insulin effect.
claim_grades.basis: 2x2 factorial randomised design in 57 boys with no protein x mineral interaction (hoppe2009).

claim_grades.claim: Dietary amino acid supply acts on the growth plate through chondrocyte mTORC1.
claim_grades.basis: No dietary protein manipulation has been coupled to a growth plate mTORC1 readout in any species. Logged as g_l10env_002.

protein_intake_growth.human_evidence_note: Two randomised human dietary interventions in prepubertal boys with serum IGF-I, IGFBP-3 and insulin as endpoints.
protein_intake_growth.translation_risk_reason: The IGF-1 response was measured directly in human children; only the chondrocyte-level step is extrapolated.
localization: human SYS: diet -> liver -> circulating IGF-1
human growth plate: no direct measurement of any dietary protein effect exists

key_refs.one_line_finding: 1.5 L/day skimmed milk for 7 days raised serum IGF-I 19% and IGF-I/IGFBP-3 13% in 8-year-old boys; an isonitrogenous meat load raised neither.
Casein raised serum IGF-1 15% with no insulin change; whey raised fasting insulin 21% with no IGF-1 change; milk minerals had no independent effect (n=57).

In 711-730 stunted Ugandan children plasma amino acids were examined as correlates of serum IGF-1, linear growth and fat-free mass; 18 of 21 amino acids were lower where inflammatory markers were elevated.

psychosocial_dwarfism.name: Psychosocial short stature
psychosocial_dwarfism.summary: Psychosocial short stature is the strongest evidence in this layer that an environmental exposure with no nutritional component can shut down linear growth through the GH axis, and it is the only exposure here whose removal reverses the phenotype. The defining description is the two-part 1967 New England Journal of Medicine series by Powell and colleagues, which characterised children with emotional deprivation whose growth retardation clinically simulated idiopathic hypopituitarism (Part I, clinical evaluation) and whose endocrine testing was abnormal (Part II, endocrinologic evaluation) - the observation that named the syndrome and placed its lesion in GH secretion rather than in nutrition. Neither record carries an abstract in Europe PMC, so the specific hormone values, sample size and recovery kinetics reported in those papers have not been verified here; the full text is queued for retrieval and this node's confidence is reduced accordingly. The mechanistic significance for the atlas is that psychosocial short stature enters the graph at gh_secretion_pulsatility rather than at the growth plate: the pituitary is the lesion, the plate is normal, and removal of the child from the environment restores growth. That entry point is asserted from the title-level content of the 1967 series and from the syndrome's clinical definition, not from a number verified in this sweep.

claim_grades.claim: Emotional deprivation can produce growth retardation clinically indistinguishable from idiopathic hypopituitarism.
claim_grades.basis: The defining two-part clinical and endocrinologic case series (powell1967a, powell1967); read at title and citation level only in this sweep.

claim_grades.claim: The lesion is in GH secretion and is reversed by removal from the environment.
claim_grades.basis: Asserted by the syndrome definition and the title of the endocrinologic paper; the supporting hormone data were not verified here. Full text queued in sources/access_queue.md.

psychosocial_dwarfism.human_evidence_note: An entirely human clinical syndrome defined by endocrine evaluation of emotionally deprived children; the quantitative endocrine findings were not verifiable from the indexed record in this sweep.
psychosocial_dwarfism.translation_risk_reason: A human psychosocial syndrome with no animal model that reproduces the reversible GH suppression.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamic-pituitary GH secretion
human growth plate: never examined in this syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: Part I: clinical evaluation of emotional deprivation and growth retardation simulating idiopathic hypopituitarism (title-level only; no abstract in the indexed record).
Part II: endocrinologic evaluation of the same syndrome (title-level only; no abstract in the indexed record).

secular_trend_height.name: Secular trend in adult height
secular_trend_height.summary: Between the 1896 and 1996 birth cohorts, mean adult height rose in almost every country for which measured data exist, and the size of that rise is the tightest empirical bound the atlas has on how much of human stature is environmentally set. In a Bayesian pooled reanalysis of 1472 population-based studies with measured (not self-reported) height on 18.6 million adults in 200 countries, the largest century-scale gains were +20.2 cm in South Korean women (95% CrI 17.5-22.7) and +16.5 cm in Iranian men (13.3-19.7) - about 2.0 and 1.65 cm per decade sustained for a hundred years (ncd2016). The rate is not constant: in German armed-forces conscripts born 1865-1975 it moved from 0.45 mm/yr before 1916 to 2.15 mm/yr in 1916-1933, 1.87 mm/yr in the early Federal Republic, 1.45 mm/yr in the late Federal Republic, and 4 mm/yr in East German conscripts after 1989 (scheffler2025), so the trend tracks political and economic discontinuities rather than a smooth nutritional ramp. The trend is also age-structured: in the Zurich Longitudinal Studies (n=236, born 1978-1993) height rose 0.35-0.46 SD per decade at ages 4, 9 and 14 but was no longer detectable at age 18 (eichelberger2024), so part of the secular change is tempo rather than final size. No study has measured the growth plate, the GH-IGF axis or any chondrocyte parameter across a secular gradient, so the route from a population's improving environment to a longer femur is an inference, not an observation.

claim_grades.claim: Mean adult height rose by up to about 20 cm over the 20th century in the fastest-changing populations.
claim_grades.basis: 1472 measured-height studies, 18.6M participants, Bayesian pooled estimates with credible intervals (ncd2016).

claim_grades.claim: The rate of secular gain changes step-wise with political and economic regime rather than smoothly.
claim_grades.basis: German conscript series 1865-1975 with period-specific slopes and coherence analysis (scheffler2025); single country, ecological design.

claim_grades.claim: The secular gain is transduced through the GH-IGF axis acting at the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: No measurement of GH, IGF-1, bone age or growth plate morphology across a secular gradient exists; inference from nutrition-IGF-1 intervention studies.

secular_trend_height.human_evidence_note: Entirely human: 18.6 million measured adult heights across 200 countries and 100 birth cohorts, plus national conscript and longitudinal cohort series.
secular_trend_height.translation_risk_reason: A human population measurement; no animal extrapolation is involved.
localization: human SYS: population-level phenotype, not zone-localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: Pooled 1472 measured-height studies (18.6M adults, 200 countries, 1896-1996 birth cohorts); largest gains +20.2 cm in South Korean women and +16.5 cm in Iranian men.
German conscript height slopes by period: 0.45, 2.15, 1.87, 1.45 and 4 mm/yr, with the largest increments in periods of political upheaval.
In 236 Zurich Longitudinal Study participants the positive secular trend in height was present at ages 4-14 (0.35-0.46 SD/decade) but absent at age 18.

secular_trend_reversal.name: Reversal of the secular height trend
secular_trend_reversal.summary: The secular increase in height is neither monotonic nor irreversible, and the reversals are the most informative part of the record because they show the trend depends on a continuously supplied environmental input rather than on a ratchet. In the NCD-RisC century reanalysis, mean adult height decreased or stopped rising in many sub-Saharan African countries for cohorts born after the early 1960s, falling by around 5 cm from its peak in Niger, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Uganda (ncd2016). The same pattern appeared later in men but not women in parts of Central Asia (Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan) and the Middle East and North Africa (Egypt, Yemen), while both sexes continued to gain in Iran (ncd2016). A loss of about 5 cm within two to three birth cohorts is a quarter of the largest century gain ever recorded, which constrains any model treating population stature as a slowly moving genetic quantity. The reversals are attributed to deteriorating nutrition, infection burden and conflict, but no study has measured IGF-1, IGFBP-3 or inflammatory markers in a declining birth cohort against its taller predecessor, so the mechanism of the reversal is imported from the mechanism proposed for the rise rather than demonstrated.

claim_grades.claim: Mean adult height fell by about 5 cm from its peak in several sub-Saharan African countries for cohorts born after the early 1960s.
claim_grades.basis: ncd2016 pooled measured-height model with per-country credible intervals.

claim_grades.claim: Reversals are sex-asymmetric, appearing in men before or without women in Central Asia and MENA.
claim_grades.basis: Reported country-by-country in ncd2016; not independently replicated outside that pooling.

claim_grades.claim: The reversal runs through the same nutrition and infection channel that drove the rise.
claim_grades.basis: No biomarker or mechanistic measurement in a declining cohort; inference only.

secular_trend_reversal.human_evidence_note: Measured adult heights in national surveys pooled by NCD-RisC; the declines are in measured, not reported, height.
localization: human SYS: population-level phenotype

key_refs.one_line_finding: Adult height decreased or stalled in many sub-Saharan African countries for cohorts born after the early 1960s, by ~5 cm from peak in Niger, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Uganda; later in men only in parts of Central Asia and MENA.

sga_catch_up.name: Catch-up growth after small-for-gestational-age birth
sga_catch_up.summary: Catch-up growth after SGA birth is fast, early and mostly complete, and its timing constrains any mechanism proposed for it. In a Goteborg population series, 82.9% of SGA infants showed catch-up during the first 6 months and 94.3% reached a final height within the normal range; of the 66 infants still short at 6 months (21 SGA and 45 non-SGA), 10 (15.2%) remained short into adulthood while 56 caught up spontaneously - which led the authors to argue that fetal growth should be defined by body size at 6 months rather than at birth (karlberg2002). In the larger 3650-child cohort, catch-up in length-defined SGA infants occurred during the first 6 months, cutting the proportion below -2 SDS to 13.4% by 1 year and 7.9% by 18 years, and the magnitude of catch-up depended on mid-parental target height and on birth length but not on birth weight or BMI at birth (karlberg1995). Two features matter mechanistically. Catch-up is essentially over before the infancy-to-childhood transition, so it is completed while growth is still nutrition- and IGF-dependent rather than GH-dependent. And it is target-height dependent, meaning the recovering child grows towards a set point rather than simply growing fast - which is the phenotype the L2 catch_up_growth and delayed_senescence_hypothesis nodes have to explain at the level of the plate.

claim_grades.claim: Catch-up growth after SGA birth is largely complete by 6 months of age.
claim_grades.basis: Two population-based Swedish series (karlberg1995, karlberg2002); the 6-month figures come from an abstract-only record.

claim_grades.claim: The magnitude of catch-up depends on mid-parental target height and on birth length, not on birth weight or BMI at birth.
claim_grades.basis: Multiple linear regression in the 3650-child cohort with final height (karlberg1995).

claim_grades.claim: Catch-up reflects a growth plate that retains proliferative capacity because senescence was delayed during restriction.
claim_grades.basis: The delayed-senescence account is an L2 hypothesis; no human growth plate has been examined during or after catch-up.

sga_catch_up.human_evidence_note: Population-based Swedish longitudinal growth series with measured serial length and final height.
localization: human SYS: postnatal growth velocity, first 6 months
human growth plate: never sampled during catch-up

key_refs.one_line_finding: 82.9% of SGA infants caught up within 6 months and 94.3% reached a normal final height; 15.2% of infants still short at 6 months remained short into adulthood (abstract only).
Catch-up occurred during the first 6 months; the magnitude depended on target height and birth length but not on birth weight or BMI at birth.

small_for_gestational_age.name: Small for gestational age
small_for_gestational_age.summary: Small for gestational age is birth size below -2 SDS for gestational age and is the population-scale readout of a restricted intrauterine environment. In a population-based Swedish cohort of 3650 healthy full-term singletons followed from birth to final height at about 18 years, infants defined SGA on birth length (SGAL) showed catch-up growth in the first 6 months, so that by 1 year only 13.4% remained below -2 SDS in height, falling further to 7.9% at 18 years; SGAL infants nevertheless carried a 7.1-fold higher relative risk of short final stature (95% CI 3.7-13.6), and those who failed to catch up constituted 21% of all short prepubertal children (karlberg1995). Definition matters: 22% of short 18-year-olds had been short at birth by length, but only 14% had been light at birth by weight. In a second population-based Swedish series, 88% of healthy full-term singleton SGA infants achieved catch-up during the first 2 years, most of the increase occurring by 2 months, and the SGA children still short at 2 years had a markedly higher risk of short stature later; about 20% of all short children had been born SGA (karlberg2002 and its companion series). The endocrine entry point is the fetal-to-infant transition of the IGF system, which no SGA cohort has measured longitudinally alongside height.

claim_grades.claim: Most length-defined SGA infants catch up, leaving 7.9% short at 18 years.
claim_grades.basis: Population-based cohort of 3650 with final height (karlberg1995).

claim_grades.claim: SGA defined by birth length identifies future short stature better than SGA defined by birth weight.
claim_grades.basis: Within-cohort comparison of definitions (karlberg1995).

small_for_gestational_age.human_evidence_note: Two population-based Swedish birth cohorts with serial measured height from birth to final height.
small_for_gestational_age.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype defined against human birth size references.
localization: human SYS: birth size phenotype

key_refs.one_line_finding: In 3650 Swedish full-term singletons, 13.4% of length-defined SGA infants were still below -2 SDS at 1 year and 7.9% at 18 years, with a 7.1-fold relative risk of short final stature.

Most SGA infants (82.9%) showed catch-up during the first 6 months and 94.3% reached a final height within the normal range; 15.2% of infants still short at 6 months remained short into adulthood (abstract only).

socioeconomic_gradient_height.name: Socioeconomic gradient in height
socioeconomic_gradient_height.summary: Height tracks socioeconomic position within populations, including populations whose nutrition is nominally adequate, and the part of that gradient surviving nutritional adjustment is the mechanistically interesting residual. In the Netherlands in 2009 - the world's tallest population, at its plateau - mean height was still positively correlated with both the child's and the parents' educational level (schnbeck2013). In the INCAP Guatemalan birth cohort (n=1386, followed 1967-2018) adults who were upwardly wealth-mobile from birth were 1.88 cm taller (95% CI 1.04-2.72) in middle adulthood than the stable-low group, with the exposure defined by household wealth rather than by diet (varghese2021). Across five long-running low- and middle-income-country birth cohorts, undernutrition indices were strongly associated with shorter adult height, less schooling and lower income, but those analyses do not separate the nutritional from the non-nutritional component of social position (victora2008), and a social gradient in linear growth persists in high-income countries where frank undernutrition is rare (freer2026). No published analysis reports the socioeconomic-height gradient with and without adjustment for measured energy and protein intake in the same cohort, so the size of the non-nutritional residual - the part that would have to run through infection, stress, sleep or care rather than substrate - is unknown.

claim_grades.claim: Height is positively associated with socioeconomic position within populations, including affluent ones.
claim_grades.basis: Nationwide Dutch survey (schnbeck2013), INCAP cohort with 50-year follow-up (varghese2021), five-cohort pooled analysis (victora2008).

claim_grades.claim: A quantifiable component of the gradient is not explained by nutritional intake.
claim_grades.basis: No cohort reports the gradient with and without adjustment for measured intake; the residual is inferred from persistence of the gradient in well-fed populations. Logged as g_l10env_003.

socioeconomic_gradient_height.human_evidence_note: Human observational data from nationwide growth surveys and birth cohorts with measured height and measured household wealth.
localization: human SYS: population phenotype

key_refs.one_line_finding: In the INCAP Guatemalan cohort (n=1386) upward wealth mobility since birth was associated with +1.88 cm adult height (95% CI 1.04-2.72) versus stable-low wealth.
In the 2009 Dutch nationwide survey height correlated positively with the educational level of both the child and the parents.
Pooled analysis of five LMIC birth cohorts: undernutrition indices were strongly associated with shorter adult height, less schooling and reduced economic productivity.
Reviews the persistence of a social gradient in linear growth within high-income countries where frank undernutrition is uncommon.

stunting.name: Stunting
stunting.summary: Stunting is height-for-age below -2 SD of the WHO standard and is the population-scale phenotype this layer has to connect to the growth plate. Its proximate biochemical correlate in humans is a low circulating IGF-1: in 740 stunted Ugandan children aged 12-59 months (mean HAZ -3.02, SD 0.74) median serum IGF-1 was 37.4 ug/L (IQR 24.2-53.3), inflammation markers were the strongest negative correlates of IGF-1, and a positive malaria test was associated with -4.7 ug/L (95% CI -7.8 to -1.6) before inflammation adjustment (madigan2026). In the same cohort plasma concentrations of 18 of 21 amino acids were lower in children with elevated inflammatory markers (larnkjr2026), which puts substrate limitation and inflammatory GH resistance on the same node rather than in competition. Supplementation moves the phenotype only slightly: pooled across 15 randomised trials of small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements in 10 countries (n=36970) the effect on length-for-age Z was +0.15 (95% CI 0.12-0.17), equal to 12 days of height-age (95% CI 9-14) and 11% of the maximal attainable benefit (95% CI 9.4-12; between-trial I2 = 90%) (watson2025). That 11% is the most important number about stunting: the deficit is overwhelmingly not closed by adding energy and micronutrients to the diet.

claim_grades.claim: Stunted children have low circulating IGF-1 and inflammation is its strongest negative correlate.
claim_grades.basis: Cross-sectional human cohort n=740 with measured IGF-1, CRP, AGP and malaria testing (madigan2026).

claim_grades.claim: Nutrient supplementation recovers about one tenth of the attainable linear growth deficit.
claim_grades.basis: Pooled 15 RCTs, n=36970, prespecified proportion-of-maximal-benefit metric (watson2025).

claim_grades.claim: The low circulating IGF-1 acts by reducing IGF1R occupancy on growth plate chondrocytes.
claim_grades.basis: No human growth plate measurement in stunted children exists; inferred from IGF1R biology in other systems.

stunting.human_evidence_note: Human anthropometry with paired serum IGF-1 and inflammatory markers, plus pooled randomised supplementation trials.
stunting.translation_risk_reason: A human phenotype defined against a human growth reference.
localization: human SYS: whole-organism phenotype, no zonal localization

key_refs.one_line_finding: In 740 stunted Ugandan children median serum IGF-1 was 37.4 ug/L, inflammation markers were the strongest negative correlates and malaria positivity was associated with -4.7 ug/L.
SQ-LNS raised length-for-age Z by 0.15 across 15 RCTs (n=36970), equal to 12 days of height-age and 11% of the maximal attainable benefit.
Undernutrition indices in five LMIC birth cohorts were strongly associated with shorter adult height, less schooling and lower income.
In 711-730 stunted Ugandan children plasma concentrations of 18 of 21 amino acids were lower in those with elevated inflammatory markers.

vitamin_a_growth.name: Vitamin A status and linear growth
vitamin_a_growth.summary: Vitamin A supplementation does not increase linear growth, and this negative result is a useful boundary on the nutrition-to-plate story. In a meta-analysis of 12 randomised controlled trials in 6340 children aged 0-14 years in low- and middle-income countries, vitamin A supplementation alone had no significant effect on height-for-age Z, weight-for-age Z or weight-for-height Z; in the same analysis vitamin D3 alone also failed to change height-for-age Z (Z=0.43, P=0.67), improving only weight-for-age Z (Z=2.72, P=0.007) (peng2025). Vitamin A is nevertheless the one micronutrient with an unambiguous pharmacological effect on the growth plate at supraphysiological doses, since retinoids act through nuclear RAR/RXR receptors that repress SOX9-driven chondrogenesis - but the atlas carries no RAR or RXR node in L3 or L4, and no study has shown that a dietary vitamin A deficit reaches the plate through those receptors. The honest position is that vitamin A deficiency has a molecular receptor system in principle and no demonstrated dietary entry point at the human growth plate, while the randomised evidence says supplementation does not make children taller.

claim_grades.claim: Vitamin A supplementation does not improve linear growth in children in LMIC settings.
claim_grades.basis: Meta-analysis of RCTs, 6340 children, prespecified HAZ endpoint (peng2025).

claim_grades.claim: Dietary vitamin A status reaches the growth plate through RAR/RXR signalling.
claim_grades.basis: Retinoid receptor biology is established in other systems; no study links dietary vitamin A status to a receptor-level readout at the plate. Logged as g_l10env_007.

vitamin_a_growth.human_evidence_note: Randomised controlled supplementation trials pooled across 6340 children with anthropometric endpoints.
vitamin_a_growth.translation_risk_reason: No animal dietary vitamin A restriction experiment with a growth plate readout is available to translate from.
localization: human SYS: retinol status
human growth plate: RAR/RXR present in principle but never assayed under dietary vitamin A manipulation

key_refs.one_line_finding: Vitamin A supplementation alone had no significant effect on HAZ, WAZ or WHZ; vitamin D3 alone did not change HAZ (Z=0.43, P=0.67) but modestly improved WAZ (12 RCTs, 6340 children).

vitamin_d_deficiency_rickets.name: Vitamin D deficiency and nutritional rickets
vitamin_d_deficiency_rickets.summary: Vitamin D deficiency is the environmental exposure in this layer with the most completely specified molecular entry point, and the entry point is not the one usually assumed. Calcitriol acts through the vitamin D receptor (L4 vitamin_d_receptor) to raise intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption; when it fails, serum phosphate falls, and it is hypophosphataemia rather than a direct chondrocyte effect that produces the rachitic growth plate, because normal phosphate is required for apoptosis of terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes and hence for orderly resorption of the hypertrophic zone (L4 phosphate_homeostasis). The consequence is the widened, disorganised hypertrophic zone and flared metaphysis of rickets. This mechanism is specific to frank deficiency: in randomised trials, vitamin D3 supplementation of children in low- and middle-income countries did not change height-for-age Z (Z=0.43, P=0.67) and improved only weight-for-age Z (Z=2.72, P=0.007) (peng2025). Vitamin D therefore behaves as a threshold nutrient for the growth plate: below the rachitic threshold the plate is structurally deranged, above it additional vitamin D buys no extra linear growth.

claim_grades.claim: Vitamin D supplementation above the rachitic threshold does not increase linear growth.
claim_grades.basis: Meta-analysis of randomised trials with prespecified HAZ endpoint (peng2025).

claim_grades.claim: The rachitic growth plate lesion is produced by hypophosphataemia acting on hypertrophic chondrocyte apoptosis rather than by a direct chondrocyte vitamin D effect.
claim_grades.basis: Mechanism established in the L4 phosphate_homeostasis and vitamin_d_receptor nodes; not re-derived here from a primary in this shard.

vitamin_d_deficiency_rickets.human_evidence_note: Nutritional rickets is a human clinical and radiographic phenotype; the supplementation null is from randomised human trials.
vitamin_d_deficiency_rickets.translation_risk_reason: The rachitic phenotype and the vitamin D endocrine axis are both directly characterised in humans.
localization: human HZ: widened and disorganised hypertrophic zone is the defining rachitic lesion
human SYS: skin/dietary vitamin D -> calcitriol -> VDR -> intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption

key_refs.one_line_finding: Vitamin D3 supplementation alone did not change height-for-age Z (Z=0.43, P=0.67) in a meta-analysis of RCTs in children in LMICs.

zinc_deficiency_growth.name: Zinc deficiency and linear growth
zinc_deficiency_growth.summary: Zinc supplementation produces one of the largest micronutrient effects on child height that has ever been demonstrated in randomised trials, and it has no established molecular entry point at the growth plate. In a meta-analysis of 33 randomised controlled trials in prepubertal children, supplemental zinc increased height with a weighted mean effect size of 0.350 SD (95% CI 0.189-0.511) and weight by 0.309 SD (0.178-0.439), with no effect on weight-for-height (-0.018, 95% CI -0.132 to 0.097); serum zinc rose by 0.820 SD (0.499-1.14), confirming exposure, and the growth response was larger in children with low baseline status (brown2002). The selectivity is informative: zinc lengthens children without fattening them, which is what a growth plate effect rather than a general anabolic effect looks like. Despite this, no study has identified which zinc-dependent protein at the plate is rate-limiting. Zinc is a structural cofactor of hundreds of enzymes and of every zinc-finger transcription factor, including those in the SOX and RUNX families that the atlas already carries at L3, but no experiment has shown that dietary zinc restriction changes SOX9, RUNX2 or IGF1R signalling in chondrocytes at physiologically attainable concentrations. This is registered as a scale gap, not papered over.

claim_grades.claim: Zinc supplementation increases linear growth in prepubertal children by about 0.35 SD.
claim_grades.basis: Random-effects meta-analysis of 33 RCTs with meta-regression on baseline status (brown2002).

claim_grades.claim: The effect is specific to linear growth rather than to general weight gain.
claim_grades.basis: Height and weight both increased while weight-for-height did not (brown2002).

claim_grades.claim: Zinc acts on chondrocytes through a named zinc-dependent protein.
claim_grades.basis: Widely asserted in reviews; no primary experiment identifies a rate-limiting zinc-dependent target at the growth plate. Logged as g_l10env_007.

zinc_deficiency_growth.human_evidence_note: Meta-analysis of 33 randomised controlled supplementation trials with measured height increments and serum zinc.
zinc_deficiency_growth.translation_risk_reason: The effect estimate is entirely from human randomised trials.
localization: human SYS: dietary zinc -> serum zinc
human growth plate: no zinc-dependent target identified or localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: Zinc supplementation increased height by 0.350 SD (95% CI 0.189-0.511) and weight by 0.309 SD across 33 RCTs, with no change in weight-for-height and a larger response at low baseline status.

acan_related_short_stature.name: ACAN-related short stature with advanced bone age
acan_related_short_stature.summary:
ACAN haploinsufficiency is mechanistically the most important entry in this layer because it
DISSOCIATES height from skeletal maturation - the two variables that are normally assumed to be
coupled. In 103 individuals from 20 families with heterozygous ACAN mutations, adult height was
a median -2.8 SDS (range -5.9 to -0.9) while childhood height was less affected at a median
-2.0 SDS, and bone age was ADVANCED by a median of 1.3 years (range 0 to +3.7). Growth stops
early, so the adult deficit exceeds the childhood deficit: the growth plate both grows less per
year and exhausts sooner. Variants cosegregated perfectly with phenotype, and the syndrome
extends to early-onset osteoarthritis (12 of 20 families) and intervertebral disc disease (9 of
20 families), pointing to a shared aggrecan-dependent failure across growth plate, articular
and disc cartilage. Two caveats keep the phenotype honest: advanced bone age is NOT obligate -
ACAN mutations also occur in nonfamilial short stature without accelerated skeletal maturation -
and no genotype-phenotype correlation was found for joint disease. The cellular mechanism has
been resolved only in mouse: in Acan+/- growth plates the defect is reduced extracellular
matrix and impaired chondrocyte HYPERTROPHY with proliferation largely spared, associated with
suppressed Akt signalling downstream of increased Camk1D. That is a mouse result, and the
corresponding human growth plate has never been examined. Merged in from the former L5 node
`acan_dosage_effect`: independent exome studies gave adult heights of -2.3 to -4.2 SDS in three
further families (nilsson2014_2); whole-gene and multi-exon ACAN deletions sit at the more severe
end with a high burden of osteochondritis dissecans (sentchordimont2025); and targeted screening
establishes ACAN as one of the commonest monogenic causes of clinically labelled idiopathic short
stature (hauer2017). The full allelic series therefore runs normal - dominant short stature with
advanced bone age - lethal spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (aggrecan type) at biallelic loss.
acan_related_short_stature.human_evidence_note: 103 genotyped humans with adult height, childhood height and bone age reported; the cellular mechanism is mouse-only.
acan_related_short_stature.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node. The hypertrophy-versus-proliferation partition is a mouse finding and must not be restated as human fact.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in ACAN-related short stature (gap g_l11path_010)
mouse PHZ/HZ: impaired hypertrophic differentiation with proliferation largely unaffected in Acan+/- (bendre2025)

key_refs.one_line_finding: 103 ACAN carriers: adult height -2.8 SDS, childhood height -2.0 SDS, bone age +1.3 y.
ACAN mutations also cause nonfamilial short stature WITHOUT accelerated skeletal maturation.
Acan+/- mouse: growth failure from reduced matrix and impaired hypertrophy, not reduced proliferation.
Heterozygous ACAN variants cause short stature with advanced bone age and early growth cessation.
ACAN whole-gene and intragenic deletions give moderate-to-severe short stature with severe joint disease.
ACAN heterozygous mutations are a major cause of idiopathic short stature on targeted screening.
Prospective 3-year rhGH in 10 treatment-naive ACAN-deficient children.

aliases: ACAN dosage effect on longitudinal growth

achondroplasia.name: Achondroplasia
achondroplasia.summary:
Achondroplasia is the human loss-of-brake experiment on FGFR3. The causal chain is unusually
complete: a heterozygous G-to-A (or G-to-C) transition at cDNA nucleotide 1138 substitutes
arginine for glycine at residue 380 in the FGFR3 transmembrane domain (Gly380Arg), found on 15
of 16 and 16 of 16 achondroplasia chromosomes in the two original mutation series; the
substitution stabilises receptor dimers and produces ligand-independent tyrosine
autophosphorylation, demonstrated in transfected cells alongside the thanatophoric alleles;
constitutive FGFR3 signalling through MAPK/ERK and STAT1 suppresses chondrocyte proliferation
and hypertrophic differentiation in the proliferative and prehypertrophic zones. The human
growth plate phenotype - shortened proliferative columns and a truncated hypertrophic zone -
is described from autopsy series of the lethal FGFR3 disorders rather than from living
achondroplasia patients, so the cellular link in the chain is the weakest one in humans.
The stature outcome is precise and reproducible across four continents: adult height is
approximately 132 cm in men and 124 cm in women in the largest European cohort (n=466), with
population-normal variance around that reduced mean. Loss of height position is not gradual -
it occurs almost entirely in the first two postnatal years, while pubertal growth is normal
when scaled to the reduced adult height. Birth prevalence is on the order of 1 in 25,000; over
80 percent of cases are de novo and arise on the paternal allele.
achondroplasia.human_evidence_note: Mutation, receptor biochemistry and adult height are all established directly in humans; only the growth plate cellular phenotype rests on autopsy material from the lethal allelic variants and on mouse models.
achondroplasia.translation_risk_reason: This is a human phenotype node. The residual risk concerns the zonal/cellular mechanism, which is imported from mouse and from lethal-variant autopsy tissue rather than measured in living achondroplasia growth plates.
localization: human PZ: shortened proliferative columns inferred from the lethal FGFR3 allelic series, not directly documented in living achondroplasia growth plates
human HZ: truncated hypertrophic zone described in thanatophoric dysplasia autopsy material (wilcox1998)
mouse RZ: resting-zone chondrocyte turnover disrupted by excess Fgfr3 signalling via CREB (horike2026)

key_refs.one_line_finding: G380R in the FGFR3 transmembrane domain on 16/16 achondroplasia chromosomes.
G380R and K650E both constitutively activate FGFR3, with K650E stronger - a graded biochemical series.
European cohort n=466: adult height 132 cm (M) / 124 cm (F); height SDS loss confined to the first 2 years.
First achondroplasia-specific growth standards from 400 individuals.
Excess FGFR3 signalling disrupts resting-zone chondrocyte turnover via CREB (mouse).

acromegaly.name: Acromegaly
acromegaly.summary:
Acromegaly is the same lesion as pituitary gigantism read after the growth plates have closed,
and is therefore this layer's cleanest human demonstration that epiphyseal fusion is
irreversible. GH and IGF-I excess of comparable magnitude produces no increase in height once
the physes are fused; instead it produces acral and periosteal apposition, soft-tissue
overgrowth and cartilage hypertrophy at articular rather than growth-plate sites. Onset before
versus after fusion is the only variable that separates the two syndromes, and overlapping
phenotypes occur when GH excess begins peripubertally. The genetic architecture partly overlaps
gigantism: a recurrent GPR101 p.E308D change was identified in 11 of 248 acromegaly patients,
mostly in tumour rather than germline DNA, and transfection of the mutation into rat GH3 cells
increased GH release and somatotroph proliferation. For the atlas, acromegaly is the boundary
condition for any claim about reactivating longitudinal growth in adults: an endogenous,
lifelong, high-amplitude GH/IGF-I stimulus does not lengthen a fused long bone in humans.
acromegaly.human_evidence_note: Large human cohorts define the phenotype and its genetic contributors; the absence of height gain after fusion is universally observed clinically.
acromegaly.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; the GH3 cell work is rat and is used only for the receptor mechanism.
localization: human growth plate: fused; the target tissue of acromegalic overgrowth is periosteum, articular cartilage and soft tissue, not the physis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Recurrent GPR101 p.E308D in 11 of 248 acromegaly patients; increases GH release in GH3 cells.
Onset relative to epiphyseal fusion is the variable separating gigantism from acromegaly.

acromesomelic_dysplasia_maroteaux.name: Acromesomelic dysplasia, Maroteaux type
acromesomelic_dysplasia_maroteaux.summary:
AMDM is the human NPR2 null experiment and the zero point of the CNP dosage series. Biallelic
loss-of-function NPR2 mutations - 21 distinct lesions in 21 families in the defining study,
comprising 4 nonsense, 4 frameshift, 2 splice-site and 11 missense changes - abolish or
severely reduce guanylyl cyclase B activity, so C-type natriuretic peptide can no longer raise
cGMP in growth plate chondrocytes. Three of the missense alleles were tested functionally and
had markedly deficient guanylyl cyclase activity, establishing the molecular consequence
directly rather than by inference. The cellular consequence in humans is not documented: no
AMDM growth plate has been described histologically, and everything known about which zone
fails comes from Npr2-deficient mice and rats. The phenotype is acromesomelic - the middle and
distal limb segments are disproportionately shortened relative to the proximal segment, the
mirror image of the rhizomelia of achondroplasia, which is itself a clue that CNP and FGFR3
signalling are not simply the same axis read in opposite directions. A downstream biochemical
signature is diagnostic: the AMDM proband in the Olney series had very high plasma CNP and
NT-proCNP with low IGF-I and evidence of GH resistance, i.e. ligand accumulates because the
receptor cannot clear or transduce it. NPR2 is also the target of the approved CNP analogue
vosoritide (L12), making AMDM the mechanistic negative control for that drug.
acromesomelic_dysplasia_maroteaux.human_evidence_note: Biallelic NPR2 loss of function with functional confirmation in patient-derived alleles across 21 families; the cellular growth plate phenotype has never been observed in a human.
acromesomelic_dysplasia_maroteaux.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; zonal mechanism is imported from rodent Npr2 models.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in AMDM (gap g_l11path_005)
human plasma: CNP and NT-proCNP elevated in the affected proband, normal in heterozygous carriers (olney2006)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Biallelic NPR2 loss of function causes AMDM in 21 families; obligate carriers are shorter than matched controls.
AMDM proband has very high plasma CNP/NT-proCNP with low IGF-I and GH resistance; carriers are normal biochemically.

allan_herndon_dudley.name: Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (MCT8 deficiency)
allan_herndon_dudley.summary:
MCT8 deficiency is the human thyroid hormone TRANSPORTER experiment and dissociates circulating
thyroid hormone from tissue thyroid hormone action - something congenital hypothyroidism cannot
do. Loss-of-function mutations in SLC16A2, which encodes the monocarboxylate transporter 8, block
T3 entry into cells that depend on MCT8 for uptake, above all neurons. The serum signature is
unique and diagnostic: HIGH T3, low-normal or low T4 and normal or mildly raised TSH - i.e. the
patient is hyperthyroxinaemic in the blood and hypothyroid in the brain simultaneously. The
phenotype is severe central hypotonia, absent speech and profound intellectual disability, with
poor weight gain and impaired linear growth. For this atlas the key inference is the reverse of
the usual one: because tissues differ in their dependence on MCT8 versus alternative
transporters (OATP1C1, MCT10), the growth plate's own T3 supply route can in principle be
inferred from whether growth is affected in proportion to the brain. The elevated serum T3 also
causes peripheral thyrotoxicosis in MCT8-independent tissues, so the skeletal phenotype in AHDS
is a mixture of local hypothyroidism and systemic hyperthyroidism - which is exactly why it is
informative and exactly why it has not been cleanly quantified.
allan_herndon_dudley.human_evidence_note: Human SLC16A2 loss-of-function mutations with a characteristic and diagnostic serum thyroid profile; the skeletal component is described clinically rather than quantitatively.
localization: human growth plate: MCT8 dependence of chondrocyte T3 uptake has not been established in humans

key_refs.one_line_finding: Novel SLC16A2 variants in Chinese Allan-Herndon-Dudley patients and the MCT8-deficiency phenotype.

aromatase_deficiency_human.name: Aromatase (CYP19A1) deficiency - stature outcome
aromatase_deficiency_human.summary:
Aromatase deficiency is the human estrogen-synthesis null and, with ESR1 estrogen resistance,
one of the two experiments that established estrogen rather than androgen as the fusion signal
in both sexes. Read from the L11 angle the chain is: biallelic CYP19A1 mutation -> failure to
aromatise androgens to estrogens, so estradiol is undetectable while testosterone and
gonadotropins are elevated -> the growth plate never receives the estrogen signal that drives
epiphyseal fusion -> absent pubertal growth spurt, delayed bone maturation, unfused epiphyses,
continued linear growth into adult life and tall final stature, in XX as well as XY individuals.
The pharmacological closure is what makes this decisive rather than correlative: in an
aromatase-deficient man, estradiol - not testosterone - advanced bone maturation and closed the
epiphyses. The detailed analysis of how estrogen terminates growth belongs to Layer L7 (fusion
and cessation) and is not duplicated here; this node exists to record the human perturbation,
its molecular consequence and its stature outcome, and to point at L7.
aromatase_deficiency_human.human_evidence_note: Molecularly defined human CYP19A1 mutations in both sexes with radiographic epiphyseal status and an estradiol-versus-testosterone intervention in one patient.
aromatase_deficiency_human.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node. Cross-reference: the fusion mechanism is analysed in L7, not here.
localization: human growth plate: not examined; the phenotype is read from bone age and epiphyseal closure on radiographs

key_refs.one_line_finding: Novel CYP19A1 mutation in XX and XY siblings defines the human aromatase deficiency syndrome.
In an aromatase-deficient man, estradiol but not testosterone closed the epiphyses and stopped linear growth.

aromatase_excess_syndrome.name: Aromatase excess syndrome
aromatase_excess_syndrome.summary:
Aromatase excess syndrome is the opposite-sign estrogen experiment to aromatase deficiency and
completes the human estrogen dose series in the growth plate. Rearrangements upstream of
CYP19A1 place the aromatase coding sequence under constitutively active promoters, raising
estrogen production. In males the consequences are pre- or peripubertal gynaecomastia and, of
direct relevance to this layer, ACCELERATED skeletal maturation with premature epiphyseal
fusion and consequent SHORT adult stature - the mirror image of the tall stature of aromatase
deficiency and ESR1 resistance, produced by the same signalling axis read in the opposite
direction. Aromatase inhibitor treatment is the therapeutic test of the mechanism: long-term
inhibition in aromatase excess patients has been reported with follow-up of the skeletal
outcome. Together with aromatase deficiency, ESR1 resistance and precocious puberty, this node
establishes that in humans estrogen exposure is the dominant determinant of when the growth
plate stops, and that its effect on final height is biphasic in time - accelerating growth
early and terminating it sooner.
aromatase_excess_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Human CYP19A1 promoter rearrangements with clinical bone-age and stature outcomes and reported long-term aromatase inhibitor follow-up.
localization: human growth plate: not examined; skeletal maturation assessed by bone age radiography

key_refs.one_line_finding: Long-term aromatase inhibitor treatment in aromatase excess syndrome and its skeletal outcome.
Reference point for the opposite-sign phenotype: estrogen absence gives tall stature and unfused epiphyses.

beckwith_wiedemann_syndrome.name: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
beckwith_wiedemann_syndrome.summary:
Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is the gain-of-dosage arm of the same 11p15.5 imprinting experiment
that produces Silver-Russell syndrome when read in the opposite direction, and the pairing is
one of the cleanest reciprocal dose series in human growth biology. Gain of methylation at the
IGF2/H19 imprinting centre, paternal uniparental disomy of 11p15, loss of methylation at
