KCNQ1OT1 and CDKN1C mutations all converge on increased IGF2 dosage and/or reduced CDKN1C
(p57KIP2) cell-cycle restraint. The phenotype is prenatal and postnatal overgrowth,
macroglossia, abdominal wall defects, hyperinsulinism and a substantially increased risk of
embryonal tumours. Hemihyperplasia is the feature most directly relevant to this layer: growth
excess can be regionally restricted, and bone age can differ between the affected and
unaffected limb of the same patient - an internally controlled human experiment in which one
individual carries both the perturbed and the reference growth plate. Overgrowth in BWS is
prominent in infancy and childhood and attenuates with age, so adult heights are much less
extreme than childhood height SDS would predict; this decoupling of childhood and adult
overgrowth is the analogue, in the opposite direction, of the ACAN early-cessation effect.
beckwith_wiedemann_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Multiple molecularly defined human 11p15 lesions with a consistent overgrowth phenotype; within-patient limb comparisons in hemihyperplasia provide internal controls.
localization: human growth plate: not examined directly; regional growth excess is inferred from limb-length and bone-age asymmetry in hemihyperplasia

key_refs.one_line_finding: Cytogenetic and imprinting anomalies dominate non-familial tall stature and overgrowth.
Reference for the reciprocal 11p15 imprinting logic linking Silver-Russell and Beckwith-Wiedemann.

blomstrand_chondrodysplasia.name: Blomstrand chondrodysplasia
blomstrand_chondrodysplasia.summary:
Blomstrand chondrodysplasia is the inactivating half of the PTH1R pair and the exact
phenotypic mirror of Jansen. Where Jansen delays chondrocyte hypertrophy and mineralisation,
Blomstrand ACCELERATES it: the defining feature is extremely advanced endochondral bone
maturation, lethal in the perinatal period. Two independent human mechanisms were reported in
1998. In one patient a homozygous P132L substitution in the receptor's N-terminal extracellular
domain abolished both PTH- and PTHrP-stimulated cAMP accumulation and radioligand binding, and
critically the mutant protein was shown to be expressed at the cell surface both in transfected
COS-1 cells and in growth plate chondrocytes taken from the affected infant - so the defect is
binding, not trafficking. In a second patient a point mutation created a novel splice site that
deleted the first 11 amino acids of exon M5 (transmembrane domain 5), and PTH-induced inositol
phosphate accumulation was undetectable as well as cAMP. Read against Jansen, the pair
establishes in humans what the Pthrp and Pth1r mouse knockouts establish in mice: PTH1R
signalling sets the timing of the proliferative-to-hypertrophic transition, more signal delays
it and less signal advances it, and human stature is the integral of that timing decision.
blomstrand_chondrodysplasia.human_evidence_note: Two independent human homozygous PTH1R loss-of-function alleles with binding and second-messenger assays, one including immunodetection in the patient's own growth plate chondrocytes.
localization: human growth plate: mutant PTH1R protein detected at the surface of growth plate chondrocytes from the affected infant (karaplis1998) - one of very few direct human growth plate observations in this layer

key_refs.one_line_finding: Homozygous PTH1R P132L abolishes ligand binding and cAMP response; mutant protein reaches the surface of the patient's growth plate chondrocytes.
A splice mutation deleting 11 residues of transmembrane domain 5 gives a non-functional PTH/PTHrP receptor with advanced endochondral maturation.
Homozygous PTH1R allelic series from lethal Blomstrand to milder Eiken and primary failure of tooth eruption.

camptodactyly_arthropathy_syndrome.name: Camptodactyly-arthropathy-coxa vara-pericarditis syndrome
camptodactyly_arthropathy_syndrome.summary:
CACP syndrome is the human lubricin knockout and is included in this layer as the negative
control that separates ARTICULAR from GROWTH PLATE cartilage. Biallelic loss-of-function
mutations in PRG4 abolish proteoglycan 4 (lubricin), the boundary lubricant secreted by
superficial-zone articular chondrocytes and synoviocytes. The consequences are non-inflammatory
joint failure - congenital camptodactyly, large-joint arthropathy with sterile effusions, coxa
vara and pericarditis - and the disorder is routinely misdiagnosed as juvenile idiopathic
arthritis, from which it must be distinguished because immunosuppression does not help.
Critically, longitudinal growth is not the primary problem: PRG4 is a superficial-zone articular
gene, not a growth plate gene, so its loss destroys joint surfaces while leaving the physis to
run. Coxa vara does shorten the effective limb, and secondary immobility can affect growth, but
there is no primary chondrodysplasia. Read against ACAN deficiency, which damages growth plate
and articular cartilage together, CACP shows that the two cartilage compartments have distinct
essential proteins and that early-onset arthropathy is not evidence of a growth plate lesion.
camptodactyly_arthropathy_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Human biallelic PRG4 mutations with a consistent articular phenotype and preserved longitudinal growth.
localization: human articular cartilage superficial zone and synovium: PRG4/lubricin absent
human growth plate: not primarily affected - longitudinal growth is largely preserved

key_refs.one_line_finding: PRG4-related CACP syndrome mimicking juvenile idiopathic arthritis - case-based review.

cancer_survivor_growth.name: Childhood cancer survivor growth failure
cancer_survivor_growth.summary:
Childhood cancer survivorship is the human multi-insult experiment on the growth plate, and its
value is that the insults are documented, dated and dose-quantified in a way that no other
condition in this layer allows. Four separable mechanisms operate: hypothalamic-pituitary
irradiation causing GH deficiency, direct spinal or limb irradiation damaging the physis itself,
chemotherapy toxicity to proliferating chondrocytes, and gonadal damage altering the timing of
the pubertal estrogen exposure that terminates growth. Because radiotherapy fields and cumulative
doses are recorded, the direct physeal component can in principle be separated from the endocrine
component within the same patient - for example by comparing sitting height with leg length after
spinal irradiation. GH replacement is effective but incompletely restorative, and a nationwide
longitudinal study of GH therapy after childhood haematopoietic cell transplantation quantifies
the response and its predictors. An informative pharmacological probe in this population is
adjuvant aromatase inhibition: in 92 GH-deficient male survivors, 22 treated with combination
aromatase inhibitor plus GH were compared with 70 on GH alone for final adult height - a direct
human test of whether delaying estrogen-driven fusion can recover height lost to an earlier
insult.
cancer_survivor_growth.human_evidence_note: Human cohorts with documented radiation fields and doses, GH replacement outcomes and a comparative aromatase inhibitor intervention with a final-adult-height endpoint.
localization: human physis in the irradiated field: direct radiation damage; distinguishable in principle from endocrine GH deficiency by segment-specific measurement

key_refs.one_line_finding: 92 GH-deficient male cancer survivors: aromatase inhibitor plus GH vs GH alone, final adult height compared.

celiac_disease_growth.name: Coeliac disease growth failure
celiac_disease_growth.summary:
Coeliac disease is the reversible-nutrition experiment and the human demonstration that growth
plate output can be restored after a period of arrest, provided the arrest ends before the plate
fuses. Gluten-driven villous atrophy causes malabsorption and chronic mucosal inflammation;
growth failure is frequently the presenting sign in children and may be the ONLY sign, which is
why coeliac serology is standard in the short-stature work-up. Withdrawal of the antigen is a
complete removal of the cause, and a longitudinal Swedish study of children aged 0-6 years
characterises the growth trajectory around diagnosis and treatment. The mechanistically
interesting element is catch-up growth: after the constraint is removed, height velocity
transiently exceeds the age-appropriate rate and children return toward their pre-illness
centile, implying that the growth plate retains a memory of its target trajectory and has not
irreversibly consumed its proliferative capacity during the arrest. This makes coeliac disease
the counterexample to disorders such as ACAN deficiency and precocious puberty, where the
capacity or the time is genuinely lost. Adherence determines the outcome; incomplete adherence
converts a reversible arrest into a permanent height deficit.
celiac_disease_growth.human_evidence_note: Longitudinal human growth trajectories around diagnosis and gluten withdrawal in a population-based paediatric cohort.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in coeliac disease

key_refs.one_line_finding: Longitudinal growth patterns 0-6 years in Swedish children with coeliac disease.

central_precocious_puberty.name: Central precocious puberty
central_precocious_puberty.summary:
Central precocious puberty is the human timing experiment: the growth plate is normal, the
hormones are normal in kind, and only the SCHEDULE is altered. Premature reactivation of the
GnRH pulse generator brings forward the pubertal estrogen exposure, which simultaneously
accelerates growth velocity and accelerates skeletal maturation. Because estrogen advances bone
age faster than it advances height age, the net effect on ADULT height is negative even though
the child is temporarily tall for age - the clearest human dissociation of growth rate from
growth duration anywhere in this layer, and the exact converse of the delayed-fusion tall stature
of aromatase deficiency and ESR1 resistance. GnRH analogue therapy is the interventional test:
suspending the estrogen exposure preserves remaining growth potential, and final adult height in
girls treated for precocious puberty starting around age eight has been reported directly. The
age at which treatment stops being beneficial - around eight in girls in most series - is
informative in itself, because it marks the point at which the height already gained offsets the
duration already lost. For the atlas the general principle is that adult height is the integral
of velocity over duration, and any intervention that changes one must be evaluated against the
other.
central_precocious_puberty.human_evidence_note: Human cohorts followed to final adult height with and without GnRH analogue suppression, stratified by age at treatment start.
localization: human growth plate: structurally normal; the perturbation is the timing of estrogen exposure, read out as bone age advance

key_refs.one_line_finding: Final adult height in girls treated with GnRH analogues for precocious puberty starting around age eight.
Converse experiment: absent estrogen signalling leaves epiphyses unfused and growth continuing at 204 cm.

chronic_kidney_disease_growth.name: Chronic kidney disease growth failure
chronic_kidney_disease_growth.summary:
Paediatric chronic kidney disease is the multi-hit systemic growth experiment and the human case
in which several of this layer's single-lesion mechanisms operate simultaneously in one patient:
acidosis, protein-energy wasting, secondary hyperparathyroidism, disordered vitamin D and
phosphate handling, inflammation, and an acquired GH-resistant state with high GH and low
bioactive IGF-I. Because the lesions coexist, CKD is where their relative weights can be
estimated. A nationwide cohort of paediatric dialysis patients found growth failure associated
with parathyroid hormone levels - a direct human link between the PTH1R axis that Jansen and
Blomstrand chondrodysplasia perturb genetically and the growth plate of a systemically ill
child, since chronically elevated PTH acting on PTH1R would be expected to delay the
proliferative-to-hypertrophic transition exactly as the Jansen activating mutation does. A
separate observational study quantifies the burden of protein-energy wasting in CKD stages 3-5D.
rhGH is effective in CKD because the defect is GH resistance rather than GH deficiency, and
supraphysiological dosing can overcome it - the pharmacological signature of a receptor-level
rather than secretion-level lesion.
chronic_kidney_disease_growth.human_evidence_note: Nationwide human cohort data linking parathyroid hormone levels to growth failure in paediatric dialysis, plus prospective nutritional cohorts.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in paediatric CKD

key_refs.one_line_finding: Nationwide cohort: growth failure in paediatric dialysis patients associates with parathyroid hormone levels.
Reference point: constitutive PTH1R activation in Jansen chondrodysplasia delays metaphyseal mineralisation.

cleidocranial_dysplasia.name: Cleidocranial dysplasia
cleidocranial_dysplasia.summary:
Cleidocranial dysplasia is the human RUNX2 dosage experiment and dissects intramembranous from
endochondral ossification. RUNX2 haploinsufficiency - by point mutation, whole-gene deletion, or
as recently shown a 4.2 kb deletion of the 3' untranslated region that presumably destabilises
the transcript - produces absent or hypoplastic clavicles, delayed closure of cranial sutures
and fontanelles, wormian bones, supernumerary and unerupted teeth, and only mild to moderate
short stature. The distribution of the lesion is the point: bones formed by intramembranous
ossification (clavicle, cranial vault) are severely affected, whereas long bones formed by
endochondral ossification through a growth plate are comparatively spared. RUNX2 is
nevertheless required in the growth plate - it drives chondrocyte hypertrophy - so the mild
stature deficit shows that one functional RUNX2 allele is nearly sufficient for the
hypertrophic transition while being clearly insufficient for intramembranous bone. That
asymmetric dose sensitivity between two ossification programmes in the same individual is what
makes CCD useful here, and the 3'UTR deletion adds a regulatory rather than coding mechanism to
the allelic series.
cleidocranial_dysplasia.human_evidence_note: Human RUNX2 coding and non-coding lesions with a consistent, anatomically selective skeletal phenotype.
cleidocranial_dysplasia.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; RUNX2's role in chondrocyte hypertrophy is established largely in mouse and is flagged as such.
localization: human cranial vault and clavicle (intramembranous): severely affected
human long bone growth plate (endochondral): comparatively spared, with only mild short stature

key_refs.one_line_finding: A 4.2 kb RUNX2 3'UTR deletion causes cleidocranial dysplasia - a regulatory mechanism in the allelic series.

congenital_adrenal_hyperplasia.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
congenital_adrenal_hyperplasia.summary:
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is the human two-sided iatrogenic experiment: the disease
accelerates growth plate maturation and the treatment suppresses growth, so final height is set
by the balance between two opposing errors. Untreated or undertreated 21-hydroxylase deficiency
produces adrenal androgen excess; androgens are aromatised to estrogens, which advance bone age,
so the child is initially TALL for age with an even more advanced skeletal age, then fuses early
and ends up SHORT. Overtreatment with glucocorticoids suppresses growth directly, as in Cushing
syndrome. The result is that adult height in CAH sits below target height in most cohorts even
under modern management, and the deficit is a treatment-quality metric rather than a fixed
disease property. A QEPS growth-model analysis decomposes CAH growth into its infancy, childhood
and pubertal components, which is the analysis needed to say WHICH phase is lost, and
disease-specific growth charts have been developed for the same reason. Non-classical CAH is the
milder arm: a single-centre series reports pubertal characteristics and final height in NCCAH,
where androgen exposure is later and lower and the height cost correspondingly smaller. CAH is
this layer's best example of estrogen-driven premature fusion arising from a non-gonadal source.
congenital_adrenal_hyperplasia.human_evidence_note: Human cohorts followed to final height with growth-model decomposition and disease-specific references; the classical and non-classical forms provide an internal dose comparison.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in CAH; the phenotype is read from bone age advance and early fusion

key_refs.one_line_finding: QEPS growth-model decomposition of growth in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
Pubertal characteristics and final height in non-classical CAH.

congenital_hypothyroidism.name: Congenital hypothyroidism
congenital_hypothyroidism.summary:
Congenital hypothyroidism is the human thyroid hormone experiment and the disorder in which the
growth plate's dependence on T3 was first recognised. Untreated, absent thyroid hormone arrests
the growth plate at the resting/proliferative stage: chondrocytes fail to undergo terminal
hypertrophy and the secondary ossification centres fail to appear, giving the epiphyseal
dysgenesis that is the radiological hallmark, together with profoundly delayed bone age and
severe disproportionate short stature with a relatively long trunk. Because newborn screening
now detects almost all cases before the phenotype develops, congenital hypothyroidism has become
a natural experiment in TIMING rather than in presence or absence: the residual variance in
adult height and body proportionality tracks the age at which treatment started and the adequacy
of early dosing. Two studies from this sweep make that point directly - one reports age at
menarche and final height in permanent congenital hypothyroidism, and one shows that timely
diagnosis and treatment determine growth AND body proportionality. Thyroid hormone acts on the
growth plate both directly, via TR-alpha in chondrocytes, and permissively through the GH-IGF-I
axis, and the two contributions have not been separated in humans.
congenital_hypothyroidism.human_evidence_note: Human treated cohorts with final height and body proportionality outcomes stratified by age at diagnosis; the untreated phenotype is documented historically.
localization: human SOC: epiphyseal dysgenesis - absent or fragmented secondary ossification centres - is the classical human radiographic finding of untreated congenital hypothyroidism
human HZ: terminal hypertrophic differentiation arrested (inferred from radiology and from animal models)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Age at menarche and final height in permanent congenital hypothyroidism.
Timely diagnosis and treatment determine growth and body proportionality in congenital hypothyroidism.

cushing_syndrome_growth.name: Cushing syndrome growth failure
cushing_syndrome_growth.summary:
Cushing syndrome is the human glucocorticoid-excess experiment and the disorder with the most
diagnostically specific auxological signature in paediatrics: growth failure occurring together
with WEIGHT GAIN. Every other cause of growth failure in this layer either spares weight or
reduces it, so the crossing of the height and weight centiles in opposite directions is close to
pathognomonic and is the reason paediatric Cushing syndrome is usually detected on the growth
chart before it is detected biochemically. The mechanism is multi-level: glucocorticoids
directly suppress growth plate chondrocyte proliferation and hypertrophy, suppress GH secretion
and induce peripheral GH resistance, suppress IGF-I bioactivity, and inhibit osteoblast
function. Exogenous glucocorticoid excess produces the same phenotype and is far commoner than
endogenous disease, which makes iatrogenic Cushing the largest natural experiment of all -
including the inhaled and intra-articular routes, where systemic absorption is often assumed to
be negligible. Growth recovery after cure of endogenous Cushing disease is incomplete in many
patients, so a period of glucocorticoid excess imposes a permanent height cost.
cushing_syndrome_growth.human_evidence_note: The height-failure-with-weight-gain signature and incomplete catch-up after cure are consistent human clinical observations; the cellular mechanism is not human-derived.
cushing_syndrome_growth.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; growth plate cellular mechanism is imported from animal work and is flagged as such.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Cushing syndrome; suppression of proliferation and hypertrophy is inferred from animal and in vitro work

key_refs.one_line_finding: Paediatric Cushing syndrome: growth failure with weight gain is the cardinal presentation.

delayed_puberty_constitutional.name: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
delayed_puberty_constitutional.summary:
Constitutional delay of growth and puberty is the mirror of central precocious puberty and the
control that shows the pubertal timing effect is bidirectional. Late activation of the GnRH pulse
generator delays the estrogen exposure, so growth velocity stays low for longer, bone age lags
chronological age, and the growth plate remains open beyond the usual age - producing a child who
is short for age but has proportionally more growth remaining. Adult height in CDGP is usually
close to target height precisely because the delay in fusion compensates for the delay in the
growth spurt: the integral of velocity over duration is preserved even though both terms are
shifted. This makes CDGP the clearest human demonstration that a temporary reduction in growth
velocity need not cost adult height, provided the plate is not prematurely closed - and therefore
the reference case against which every growth-promoting intervention should be judged. Low-dose
androgen therapy is used to accelerate the pubertal growth spurt in boys, and a meta-analysis of
retrospective cohorts assesses its effect on final adult height specifically, which is the right
endpoint: an agent that advances the spurt without advancing fusion helps, an agent that advances
both does not.
delayed_puberty_constitutional.human_evidence_note: Human cohorts followed to final adult height, plus a meta-analysis of androgen therapy with a final-adult-height endpoint.
localization: human growth plate: structurally normal, open for longer than average; bone age delayed relative to chronological age

key_refs.one_line_finding: Meta-analysis of androgen therapy effects on final adult height in constitutional delay of growth and puberty.

estrogen_resistance_esr1.name: ESR1 estrogen resistance - stature outcome
estrogen_resistance_esr1.summary:
ESR1 estrogen resistance is the receptor-side counterpart of aromatase deficiency and rules out
the alternative explanation that aromatase deficiency acts through some non-estrogenic product
of the enzyme. Read as an L11 perturbation: a disruptive homozygous mutation in the estrogen
receptor gene -> estrogen signal cannot be transduced despite normal or elevated circulating
estrogen -> the growth plate receives no estrogen input -> incomplete epiphyseal closure and
continued linear growth into adulthood -> adult height 204 cm in the index 28-year-old man,
despite otherwise normal masculinisation. The dissociation between normal virilisation and
absent epiphyseal closure in the same individual is the decisive observation: androgen action
was intact and did not fuse the plates. Six months of transdermal estrogen and studies of
pituitary-gonadal function and bone density were reported in the same patient. Because he was
resistant rather than deficient, exogenous estrogen did not rescue fusion - the mirror-image
result to the aromatase-deficient man in whom it did. The fusion mechanism itself is analysed
in Layer L7; this node records the human genotype, the molecular consequence and the stature
outcome only.
estrogen_resistance_esr1.human_evidence_note: A single molecularly defined human ESR1 loss-of-function case with measured adult height, radiographic epiphyseal status and a six-month estrogen challenge.
estrogen_resistance_esr1.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node. Cross-reference: the fusion mechanism is analysed in L7.
localization: human growth plate: unfused epiphyses documented radiographically at age 28 (smith1994)

key_refs.one_line_finding: ESR1 disruptive mutation: 204 cm, unfused epiphyses, continued growth into adulthood despite normal virilisation.

gh_deficiency.name: Growth hormone deficiency (childhood-onset)
gh_deficiency.summary:
GH deficiency is the reversible arm of the GH-IGF axis series: unlike Laron syndrome the
receptor is intact, so the lesion can be corrected pharmacologically and the counterfactual
adult height can be measured. The comparison that matters for this atlas is treated versus
untreated within the same diagnostic category. In a cohort of 169 individuals with idiopathic
GHD followed to adult height, rhGH-treated patients reached a higher adult height than
untreated patients with the same diagnosis, which is the human demonstration that the deficit
is a consequence of the hormone rather than of the condition that caused the deficiency. GH
acts on the growth plate through two routes that this layer can distinguish only indirectly:
endocrine IGF-I from the liver, and local IGF-I induced in the growth plate itself. Laron
syndrome (GHR null, no IGF-I) and STAT5B deficiency (no IGF1 transcription) bracket the
severity of complete axis failure at roughly -6 to -12 SDS in childhood, whereas idiopathic GHD
typically presents at -2 to -4 SDS, so partial and complete axis loss are quantitatively as
well as mechanistically distinct. A further human dissection comes from mid-puberty
withdrawal: adolescents with transient idiopathic GHD who stopped rhGH in mid-puberty reached
the same near-adult height as those who continued, showing that the axis requirement is not
uniform across the growth period.
gh_deficiency.human_evidence_note: Adult-height outcomes in treated and untreated humans with the same diagnosis, plus randomised and preference-based withdrawal studies.
localization: human growth plate: no direct histological study of GH-deficient human physes

key_refs.one_line_finding: 169 idiopathic GHD individuals to adult height: rhGH-treated exceed untreated adult height.
Systematic review of hormonal treatment effectiveness across paediatric growth disorders.

homocystinuria_tall.name: Classical homocystinuria (CBS deficiency)
homocystinuria_tall.summary:
Classical homocystinuria is the metabolic overgrowth experiment: a biallelic defect in
cystathionine beta-synthase raises homocysteine, and the skeletal phenotype is marfanoid -
tall stature, dolichostenomelia, arachnodactyly, scoliosis and osteoporosis - closely enough
to Marfan syndrome that patients are routinely misdiagnosed, and late diagnosis is common. The
mechanistic interest for this atlas is that the lesion is neither a matrix gene nor a growth
factor: homocysteine is thought to interfere with collagen and fibrillin cross-linking, so the
connective tissue phenotype is a downstream chemical consequence of an amino-acid metabolic
block. That makes homocystinuria the human demonstration that skeletal proportion can be
distorted by a purely metabolic perturbation acting on matrix chemistry. It is also the only
tall-stature disorder in this layer that is treatable metabolically - pyridoxine responsiveness
and methionine restriction modify the course - which is why diagnostic delay is the dominant
clinical variable and why the untreated adult height distribution is poorly characterised.
Ectopia lentis and thromboembolism, not stature, drive the clinical burden.
homocystinuria_tall.human_evidence_note: A biochemically and molecularly defined human inborn error with a consistently described marfanoid skeletal phenotype; quantitative untreated adult heights were not retrievable in this sweep.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in homocystinuria

key_refs.one_line_finding: Diagnostic delay in classical homocystinuria and its clinical consequences.

hypochondroplasia.name: Hypochondroplasia
hypochondroplasia.summary:
Hypochondroplasia is the weak allele of the FGFR3 series and therefore the human dose control
for achondroplasia. The commonest lesion is c.1620C>A or C>G giving Asn540Lys in the proximal
tyrosine kinase domain, found in 8 of 14 unrelated hypochondroplasia patients in the original
screen and accounting for 50-70 percent of cases; a second, rarer class sits at the Lys650
codon (K650N, K650Q) and produces weaker constitutive kinase activation than the K650E and
K650M substitutions that cause thanatophoric dysplasia type II and SADDAN. The molecular
consequence is the same as in achondroplasia - ligand-independent FGFR3 activity - but of
smaller magnitude, and the phenotype scales with it: milder rhizomelia, less lumbar
interpedicular narrowing, macrocephaly that may be absent, and adult stature that overlaps the
lower end of the normal range rather than falling to 130 cm. No human growth plate histology
has been reported for hypochondroplasia. Growth hormone raises first-year velocity but a
six-patient long-term series concluded the gain was not sufficient to secure an adequate final
height, consistent with an FGFR3-intrinsic ceiling rather than a GH-axis defect. Neurological
comorbidity (temporal lobe seizures, intellectual disability) is more frequent than in
achondroplasia, which is mechanistically notable because FGFR3 is also expressed in the
developing cortex.
hypochondroplasia.human_evidence_note: Genotype and clinical phenotype are established directly in humans; the growth plate cellular phenotype has never been described in a hypochondroplasia patient.
hypochondroplasia.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node. Mechanistic statements about zone-specific chondrocyte behaviour derive from the Fgfr3 N534K mouse, not from human tissue.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in hypochondroplasia (see gap g_l11path_003)

key_refs.one_line_finding: FGFR3 N540K in 8/14 unrelated hypochondroplasia patients; hypochondroplasia is allelic to achondroplasia.
K650N and K650Q give hypochondroplasia-like disease with weaker kinase activation than K650E/K650M.
20 Korean N540K patients: clinical spectrum and GH response.
GeneReviews clinical and radiological definition of hypochondroplasia.

hypophosphatasia.name: Hypophosphatasia
hypophosphatasia.summary:
Hypophosphatasia is the human experiment on the mineralisation step of endochondral
ossification, and it isolates that step from cartilage growth itself. Loss-of-function ALPL
mutations reduce tissue-non-specific alkaline phosphatase, so inorganic pyrophosphate - a
potent physiological inhibitor of hydroxyapatite nucleation - is not hydrolysed and accumulates.
The direct cellular consequence is failure of matrix vesicle-mediated mineralisation at the
zone of provisional calcification; the growth plate continues to produce hypertrophic
chondrocytes and matrix, but that matrix is not converted to bone, so unmineralised cartilage
accumulates in the metaphysis. The radiographic result is rickets-like metaphyseal fraying and
tongues of radiolucency, occurring at NORMAL calcium and phosphate concentrations - the feature
that distinguishes hypophosphatasia from nutritional and from FGF23-mediated rickets. Severity
spans perinatal-lethal through infantile and childhood forms to adult odontohypophosphatasia,
with dominant-negative alleles producing severe disease in the heterozygous state; intrafamilial
variability is marked even for the same genotype, which limits genotype-based prognosis.
Enzyme replacement with asfotase alfa reverses the skeletal phenotype, closing the causal loop
pharmacologically.
hypophosphatasia.human_evidence_note: Human ALPL mutations with a defined biochemical mechanism (pyrophosphate accumulation), characteristic radiology at normal calcium and phosphate, and reversal by enzyme replacement.
localization: human ZPC: failure of matrix-vesicle mineralisation with accumulation of unmineralised hypertrophic cartilage in the metaphysis
human serum: alkaline phosphatase LOW with normal calcium and phosphate - the diagnostic signature separating HPP from other rickets

key_refs.one_line_finding: Intrafamilial phenotypic variability of hypophosphatasia across two ALPL families plus literature.

idiopathic_short_stature.name: Idiopathic short stature
idiopathic_short_stature.summary:
Idiopathic short stature is not a disease but the residual category left after the disorders in
this layer have been excluded, and its progressive dissolution is one of the strongest arguments
that the layer works. Defined as height more than 2 SD below the mean without an identifiable
cause, ISS has been repeatedly re-partitioned by sequencing: NPR2 haploinsufficiency accounts
for somewhere between 0 and 1 in 26 of ISS patients depending on cohort and ascertainment; ACAN
mutations account for a further tranche and are recognisable by advanced bone age; NPPC, SHOX,
IHH, BMP2, PTPN11 and the RASopathies, and PAPPA2 have each been carved out of the same
residual. The pattern that emerges is that most of the recovered causes are growth-plate-intrinsic
(matrix, CNP/cGMP, FGF/RAS) rather than endocrine - the opposite of the historical clinical
assumption that unexplained short stature is a hormone problem. Two lessons follow for the atlas.
First, ISS is a moving denominator, so any prevalence quoted for a monogenic cause is a function
of when and how the cohort was ascertained. Second, the remaining ISS is expected to be
polygenic, connecting this layer directly to the height GWAS architecture of Layer L8.
idiopathic_short_stature.human_evidence_note: Sequencing studies of defined human short-stature cohorts with functional validation of recovered variants; the category is defined by exclusion and shrinks as sequencing improves.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in idiopathic short stature

key_refs.one_line_finding: NPR2 haploinsufficiency prevalence in ISS estimated at 0 to 1/26 with functional verification.
NPR2 mutations in ~3% of SHOX-negative disproportionate short stature referrals.
ACAN mutations recovered from short-stature cohorts by advanced bone age.
Systematic review of hormonal treatment across paediatric growth disorders including ISS.

igf1_deficiency_human.name: IGF1 gene defects (biallelic deletion and haploinsufficiency)
igf1_deficiency_human.summary:
The IGF1 gene dosage series separates the prenatal from the postnatal action of IGF-I in
humans. The homozygous state was defined by a single patient from a consanguineous pedigree
with a partial IGF1 deletion removing exons 4 and 5 and producing a severely truncated peptide:
severe intrauterine growth failure, continued postnatal growth failure, undetectable serum
IGF-I with elevated GH secretion, normal IGFBP-3, ALS and GH-binding activity, plus
sensorineural deafness and intellectual disability. Because growth failure begins before birth,
this establishes that IGF-I acts on the human fetal skeleton independently of GH, which is not
true of GH itself. rhIGF-I treatment in the same patient raised linear growth and improved
insulin sensitivity, closing the loop pharmacologically in one individual. The heterozygous
state has only recently been characterised: nine patients from six families carrying whole or
partial IGF1 gene deletions and other pathogenic heterozygous variants, with milder growth
impairment and a documented response to rhGH. The dose series - two null alleles, one null
allele, none - is therefore complete in humans but sparse: sample sizes are 1 and 9. No human
growth plate has been examined in either state.
igf1_deficiency_human.human_evidence_note: A molecularly defined human homozygous IGF1 deletion with full endocrine phenotyping, plus a nine-patient heterozygous series.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in IGF1 deficiency

key_refs.one_line_finding: Homozygous IGF1 exon 4-5 deletion: intrauterine plus postnatal growth failure with undetectable IGF-I and high GH.
Nine patients with heterozygous IGF1 defects: milder phenotype and rhGH response.

igf1r_mutation_human.name: IGF1R mutations
igf1r_mutation_human.summary:
IGF1R mutations move the lesion from the ligand to its receptor and give the reciprocal
biochemical signature: growth failure WITH high circulating IGF-I, because the feedback loop
cannot be closed. In the defining study two mechanisms were found in two children. One girl
was a compound heterozygote for Arg108Gln and Lys115Asn in exon 2, and her cultured fibroblasts
had reduced IGF-I receptor FUNCTION; one boy carried a nonsense Arg59stop allele that reduced
the NUMBER of receptors on fibroblasts. Both had intrauterine growth retardation followed by
poor postnatal growth, and neither mutation class was present in 43 birth-weight-normal
controls. The two mechanisms - fewer receptors versus worse receptors - producing the same
phenotype is the human demonstration that IGF-I signalling capacity, not receptor identity,
sets prenatal and postnatal skeletal growth. The screened populations were 42 children with
unexplained IUGR plus short stature and 50 short children with elevated circulating IGF-I; the
yield of one case each indicates that IGF1R defects are a rare but mechanistically decisive
cause. Adult heights are not reported as a cohort statistic, and no growth plate has been
examined.
igf1r_mutation_human.human_evidence_note: Two molecularly defined human cases with functional assays in patient fibroblasts and a screened control group.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in IGF1R deficiency

key_refs.one_line_finding: IGF1R mutations reducing receptor function or number both cause intrauterine plus postnatal growth retardation.

irradiation_growth_plate_damage.name: Irradiation damage to the growth plate
irradiation_growth_plate_damage.summary:
Therapeutic irradiation is the only deliberate, dose-quantified, spatially targeted perturbation
ever applied to the human growth plate, which makes it the single most under-exploited data
source in this layer. Ionising radiation kills proliferating chondrocytes preferentially, so the
proliferative zone is the primary target; the resulting injury is dose- and age-dependent, with
younger children more susceptible because more residual growth remains. The clinical signatures
map onto the geometry of the field: craniospinal irradiation for medulloblastoma produces a
disproportionate loss of SITTING height relative to leg length, because the vertebral growth
plates are inside the field and the femoral and tibial plates are not; hemi-field or asymmetric
irradiation produces limb-length discrepancy and angular deformity from partial physeal arrest;
total body irradiation before haematopoietic transplantation produces generalised loss. The
segment-specific dissociation is the key analytic asset: within one patient, an irradiated
physis and a non-irradiated physis experience the same endocrine environment, so any difference
between them isolates the DIRECT radiation effect from the GH-deficiency effect. This is a
within-subject control that no genetic disorder in this layer provides, and it has not been
exploited systematically with modern dosimetry.
irradiation_growth_plate_damage.human_evidence_note: Radiation field geometry, dose and age are documented in human treatment records and the segmental growth consequences are clinically observed; systematic dosimetry-linked physeal outcome analyses are lacking.
localization: human PZ: proliferating chondrocytes are the primary radiosensitive target
human vertebral physes vs limb physes: differentially included in craniospinal fields, producing a measurable within-patient dissociation of sitting height from leg length

key_refs.one_line_finding: Final adult height outcomes in irradiated, GH-deficient childhood cancer survivors.

jansen_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.name: Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia
jansen_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.summary:
Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is one half of a matched human activating/inactivating pair
at PTH1R; together with Blomstrand chondrodysplasia it tests the PTHrP/IHH negative-feedback
loop in humans without any animal model being required for the causal claim. The lesion is a
heterozygous activating mutation in PTH1R - His223Arg in the first intracellular loop was the
founding allele, and five activating mutations are now known (H223R in 18 of 24 patients in the
natural-history series, plus T410P, T410R in a father and two sons, I458R and I458K). The
molecular consequence is ligand-independent cAMP accumulation, shown directly in COS-7 cells
expressing the mutant receptor. The systemic consequence follows mechanistically: PTH- and
PTHrP-INDEPENDENT hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria and hypophosphataemia, with nephrocalcinosis
and declining renal function later in life. The skeletal consequence is the interesting one for
this atlas: constitutive PTH1R signalling holds chondrocytes in the proliferative state and
DELAYS their exit into hypertrophy, giving markedly delayed and disorganised metaphyseal
mineralisation with severe short stature. Bone histomorphometry has now been performed in two
paediatric JMC patients, which is the only direct human bone-tissue characterisation in this
disorder; the growth plate itself remains undescribed in living patients.
jansen_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.human_evidence_note: Human activating PTH1R alleles with in vitro cAMP assays, a 24-patient natural history series and bone histomorphometry in two patients.
jansen_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; the COS-7 cAMP assay is a heterologous expression system, not a species claim.
localization: human growth plate: not described in living JMC patients
human bone (iliac/biopsy): microarchitecture and turnover characterised in 2 paediatric patients (pereira2025)

key_refs.one_line_finding: PTH1R H223R gives ligand-independent cAMP accumulation - the founding activating allele of JMC.
24 JMC patients across five activating PTH1R mutations with in vitro receptor characterisation.
Bone histomorphometry and turnover markers in two paediatric JMC patients.

juvenile_idiopathic_arthritis_growth.name: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis growth failure
juvenile_idiopathic_arthritis_growth.summary:
Juvenile idiopathic arthritis is the human inflammation experiment on the growth plate, and it
operates at two anatomically distinct scales that must be kept separate. Systemically, IL-6 and
TNF-driven inflammation causes generalised growth failure with an acquired GH-resistant state,
compounded by glucocorticoid therapy - and the historical shift to biologic cytokine blockade
has substantially reduced this component, which is itself the interventional evidence that the
cytokines were causal. Locally, inflammation adjacent to an inflamed joint can either
ACCELERATE growth of the adjacent physis (hyperaemia causing limb overgrowth and leg-length
discrepancy in oligoarticular disease) or destroy it, producing localised undergrowth and
micrognathia when the temporomandibular joint is involved. The same disease therefore produces
opposite-signed local growth effects depending on whether the physis is stimulated by
hyperaemia or damaged directly, which no systemic model can explain. Methotrexate, the
first-line disease-modifying drug, has been examined prospectively for its own effect on growth
plate development, an important control since a drug that suppresses inflammation may
independently affect chondrocyte proliferation.
juvenile_idiopathic_arthritis_growth.human_evidence_note: Human paediatric cohorts with growth outcomes, plus a prospective study of methotrexate effects on growth plate development.
localization: human physis adjacent to an inflamed joint: local hyperaemia can accelerate growth (limb overgrowth) or inflammation can destroy the plate (localised undergrowth)
human growth plate, systemic: not examined histologically in JIA

key_refs.one_line_finding: Prospective observational cohort of methotrexate use in JIA and its impact on growth plate development.

klinefelter_syndrome.name: Klinefelter syndrome
klinefelter_syndrome.summary:
Klinefelter syndrome is the opposite-sign arm of the same PAR1 dosage experiment as Turner
syndrome: an extra X chromosome means an extra SHOX copy, and the phenotype is tall stature.
The dosage effect has been isolated quantitatively in the 928,605-person biobank analysis that
included 505 adults with 47,XXY, and the same analysis shows that the height contribution of an
inactive X is real but smaller than that of a Y - the asymmetry that explains part of normal
sexual dimorphism. Two recent auxological studies pin down when the extra height appears rather
than merely that it does. Reference growth charts were built from 1,279 males under 20 years
with Klinefelter syndrome across six US paediatric centres. A QEPS growth-model decomposition
of 55 boys with 47,XXY, of whom 35 reached final height (34 on testosterone replacement),
partitions the excess into the infancy, childhood and pubertal functions - the kind of analysis
that distinguishes a growth plate that grows faster from one that grows for longer.
Klinefelter is therefore the human case where extra SHOX dosage and hypogonadism (which delays
fusion) push height in the SAME direction, which is why the effect is larger and more
consistent than the SHOX dosage alone would predict.
klinefelter_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Population-scale aneuploidy dosage modelling plus disorder-specific growth references and a growth-phase decomposition to final height.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Klinefelter syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: Inactive-X dosage raises height, but by 3.1 cm less per copy than Y dosage.
Klinefelter-specific growth charts from 1,279 boys across six US centres.
QEPS decomposition of growth in 55 boys with 47,XXY; 35 reached final height.

laron_syndrome.name: Laron syndrome (growth hormone receptor deficiency)
laron_syndrome.summary:
Laron syndrome is the human GH-receptor knockout and the experiment that separates GH from
IGF-I. Biallelic GHR mutations - in the large Ecuadorian cohort a homozygous change at
codon 180 of exon 6 - abolish GH signal transduction, so circulating GH is normal or high,
biologically normal and completely ineffective, while IGF-I is low to undetectable. The
molecular consequence is failure of hepatic and local IGF-I generation; the growth plate
consequence has never been described histologically in a human. The most mechanistically
surprising human result is not the shortness but the shape: in 201 adults, GH-insensitive
individuals had the LOWEST lower-segment/height and the HIGHEST upper-segment/height and
head-circumference/height ratios, and serum IGF-I correlated positively (logarithmically) with
every body measurement while correlating negatively with head-circumference/height. GH-IGF-I
loss therefore produces DISproportionate growth, contradicting the textbook assumption that
the axis scales the body uniformly - it acts preferentially on the long bones of the lower
limb. Adult heights in the classic series fall in the 120-130 cm range with childhood height
SDS of -6 to -12, but that range is stated in secondary sources rather than as a primary
cohort mean with SD, which is a quantitative gap. rhIGF-1 replacement partially rescues
growth: in the global registry only 10.5 percent of Laron patients reached near-adult height
within the normal range.
laron_syndrome.human_evidence_note: A geographically clustered homozygous GHR cohort with anthropometry in 201 adults and internal carrier and non-carrier controls.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in Laron syndrome (gap g_l11path_007)

key_refs.one_line_finding: 201 adults: GHR deficiency causes DISproportionate growth - lowest lower-segment/height, highest head-circumference/height.
Adult height in treated vs untreated GH-axis deficiency (idiopathic GHD comparator cohort, n=169).

loeys_dietz_syndrome.name: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
loeys_dietz_syndrome.summary:
Loeys-Dietz syndrome perturbs the TGF-beta receptor directly rather than the microfibrils that
sequester the ligand, and is therefore the receptor-level control for Marfan syndrome.
Heterozygous mutations in TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD3, TGFB2 and TGFB3 produce a marfanoid habitus
with skeletal overgrowth, arachnodactyly and scoliosis alongside aggressive arterial disease.
One human observation links this node directly to the CNP axis in this layer: the patient with
the t(1;2)(q41;q37.1) translocation who developed CNP-driven skeletal overgrowth had the
chromosome 1 breakpoint disrupting TGFB2, so that individual carried both an NPPC gain and a
TGFB2 haploinsufficiency - a natural human double perturbation whose overgrowth phenotype could
not be attributed to either lesion alone. TGFB2 haploinsufficiency is the molecular basis of
Loeys-Dietz syndrome type IV. The atlas-relevant point is that TGF-beta superfamily dose and
CNP/cGMP dose converge on the same tall-marfanoid endpoint by different routes, which is why
clinical differentiation of overgrowth syndromes on habitus alone is unreliable. No
disorder-specific growth reference or adult height distribution is available.
loeys_dietz_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Human TGF-beta pathway mutations with a marfanoid skeletal phenotype; one informative human case carries a combined NPPC gain and TGFB2 disruption.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Loeys-Dietz syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: t(1;2) patient with CNP overexpression AND TGFB2 disruption - a natural human double perturbation of two overgrowth pathways.
Positions Loeys-Dietz within the marfanoid overgrowth differential.

marfan_syndrome.name: Marfan syndrome
marfan_syndrome.summary:
Marfan syndrome is a matrix perturbation with an overgrowth phenotype, and the mechanistic
interest for this atlas is that it is the opposite sign to every other structural-matrix
disorder here. Heterozygous FBN1 mutations reduce or alter fibrillin-1 microfibrils; because
microfibrils sequester latent TGF-beta, the dominant model is that fibrillin deficiency
increases free TGF-beta signalling. The stature outcome is tall stature with dolichostenomelia
- limbs disproportionately long relative to trunk, giving a reduced upper-to-lower segment
ratio and an arm span exceeding height - i.e. the growth plates of the long bones grow more
than the vertebral plates. This segment-specific overgrowth is the mirror image of achondroplasia
(rhizomelic shortening) and of AMDM (acromesomelic shortening), and taken together the three
disorders show that different signalling lesions act on anatomically distinct subsets of growth
plates. Marfan sits in the same TGF-beta family as Loeys-Dietz syndrome, whose growth phenotype
overlaps. Overgrowth in Marfan is not driven by GH excess, which is what makes it a useful
control for pituitary gigantism. Disorder-specific growth references and quantitative adult
height distributions by FBN1 genotype are not established in the sources retrieved here.
marfan_syndrome.human_evidence_note: The tall, dolichostenomelic phenotype and its FBN1 basis are established in humans; a quantitative adult-height distribution stratified by genotype was not retrievable in this sweep.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Marfan syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: Cytogenetic and monogenic causes dominate non-familial tall stature; positions syndromic overgrowth against familial tall stature.
Tall stature and gigantism in the transition age, including the marfanoid overgrowth differential.

mucopolysaccharidosis_growth.name: Mucopolysaccharidosis growth failure
mucopolysaccharidosis_growth.summary:
The mucopolysaccharidoses are the human experiment in which the growth plate matrix is
progressively poisoned from within by undegraded substrate. Deficiency of a lysosomal enzyme
causes glycosaminoglycans - keratan sulphate and chondroitin-6-sulphate in MPS IVA (Morquio A),
heparan sulphate in MPS IIIA (Sanfilippo A) - to accumulate in chondrocyte lysosomes and in the
extracellular matrix, distorting the cartilage template and producing dysostosis multiplex. The
auxological signature is a POSTNATALLY ACQUIRED and progressive growth failure: birth length is
normal, growth is near normal for the first one to two years, and then velocity falls, with the
severity and timing differing between subtypes - a longitudinal single-centre study contrasting
MPS IVA and MPS IIIA shows exactly this divergence. MPS is therefore the temporal opposite of
Silver-Russell syndrome (prenatal onset, no catch-up) and of achondroplasia (deficit acquired
almost entirely in the first two years). Enzyme replacement and haematopoietic stem cell
transplantation modify growth, and a systematic review of transplantation outcomes shows that
the growth benefit depends heavily on age at treatment, which is the clinical corollary of a
matrix that becomes progressively harder to rescue.
mucopolysaccharidosis_growth.human_evidence_note: Longitudinal human growth data by MPS subtype plus systematic review of growth outcomes after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
localization: human growth plate: glycosaminoglycan-laden vacuolated chondrocytes and disorganised columns are the classical description in MPS, from autopsy and surgical material

key_refs.one_line_finding: Longitudinal growth patterns diverge between MPS IVA and MPS IIIA in a single-centre cohort.

multiple_epiphyseal_dysplasia.name: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia
multiple_epiphyseal_dysplasia.summary:
Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is the mild end of the same matrix-proteostasis continuum as
pseudoachondroplasia and is the disorder in this layer where the growth plate fails structurally
WITHOUT costing much height. In a 22-patient series from 17 unrelated families, disease genes
were COMP (47 percent), COL9A2 and COL9A3 (11.8 percent each, monoallelic), SLC26A2 (17.6
percent) and MATN3 and CANT1 (11.8 percent each, biallelic); in 15 children followed to ages
11-18 height decreased slightly with age but remained normal or at the lower limit of normal,
except in the intermediate PSACH-like form. The joint-specific pattern is mechanistically
informative: MED2 and MED3 (COL9A2/COL9A3) predominantly affect the knee, while the other
genotypes predominantly affect the hip - so different matrix components are rate-limiting at
different anatomical sites. The same series showed COMP mutations previously assigned to
pseudoachondroplasia producing a typical MED1 or intermediate phenotype, and biallelic MATN3
variants producing MED5. MED is therefore the human demonstration that epiphyseal cartilage can
be structurally abnormal enough to cause early osteoarthritis and a waddling gait while
longitudinal growth remains close to normal - the growth plate's height output and its
mechanical competence are separable.
multiple_epiphyseal_dysplasia.human_evidence_note: A genotyped human series with median 5.5 years of longitudinal follow-up and site-specific joint involvement by gene.
localization: human epiphysis: irregular, delayed and fragmented ossification with the growth plate itself structurally near-normal on radiographs
human knee vs hip: MED2/MED3 (COL9A2/COL9A3) affect the knee; other genotypes predominantly the hip (taner2026)

key_refs.one_line_finding: 22 MED patients: height normal or at the lower limit through ages 11-18; gene predicts which joint fails.
EDM1 vs PSACH separated statistically across 830 COMP patients.

noonan_syndrome.name: Noonan syndrome and the RASopathies
noonan_syndrome.summary:
Noonan syndrome is the human test of what constitutive RAS/MAPK activation does to the growth
plate, and it is mechanistically adjacent to achondroplasia because FGFR3 signals through the
same cascade. Germline gain-of-function mutations in PTPN11 (the commonest), SOS1, RAF1, RIT1
and others increase RAS/MAPK flux; birth length is usually normal and growth failure is
postnatal, with adult height approaching the lower limit of normal rather than falling into the
dysplasia range. A genetically defined multicentre cohort of 101 patients (76 PTPN11, 7 SOS1,
18 other) on GH therapy, of whom 23 reached final height, found parental heights that were
themselves below average (fathers -0.33 SDS), which matters because it warns that the apparent
disease effect in family-based cohorts is partly polygenic background. A national Turkish
cohort of 67 patients reaching final height compared GH-treated and untreated patients
stratified by sex. Mechanistically the interesting feature is that GH response is modest and
genotype-dependent, consistent with the block being downstream of the receptor in the growth
plate itself rather than in GH secretion - the same argument that applies to hypochondroplasia.
Noonan patients have also been enrolled in a CNP-analogue basket trial, an explicit test of
whether the CNP axis can antagonise excess MAPK output in a non-FGFR3 RASopathy.
noonan_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Genetically confirmed multicentre human cohorts followed to final height with treated and untreated comparisons.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Noonan syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: 101 genetically defined Noonan-spectrum patients on GH; 23 to final height; parental heights below average.
67 Noonan patients reaching final height, stratified by sex and GH treatment.
GeneReviews: birth length usually normal; final adult height approaches the lower limit of normal.

nppc_duplication_tall_stature.name: NPPC dosage disorders (CNP overexpression and CNP loss)
nppc_duplication_tall_stature.summary:
NPPC dosage completes the CNP axis from the ligand side and shows that the growth plate reads
CNP quantitatively in both directions. Overexpression: a de novo balanced t(2;7)(q37.1;q21.3)
with a breakpoint adjacent to NPPC doubled plasma CNP concentration relative to five controls
and substantially raised NPPC expression in the proband's fibroblasts, and the girl had a
marfanoid habitus with skeletal anomalies; a transgenic mouse targeting Nppc overexpression to
bone reproduced the phenotype. A second, independent translocation, t(1;2)(q41;q37.1), with a
breakpoint 200,365 bp downstream of NPPC, raised serum NT-proCNP and caused the same skeletal
overgrowth syndrome with macrodactyly of the great toe, scoliosis, ankle valgus and slipped
capital femoral epiphysis. Two independent rearrangements at the same locus producing the same
phenotype with the same measured biomarker is strong human causal evidence. Loss: screening
668 short-stature patients found two heterozygous NPPC mutations located in the highly
conserved CNP ring, both with significantly reduced cGMP synthesis, cosegregating with short
stature and small hands - the first demonstration that NPPC mutations cause autosomal dominant
short stature in humans. One of the two had already been described in the spontaneous Nppc
lbab mouse, a rare exact genotype match between a human and a mouse allele. The clearance
receptor completes the picture: loss-of-function variants in NPR3 (NPR-C) also cause extreme
tall stature, i.e. failing to remove CNP mimics making too much of it.
nppc_duplication_tall_stature.human_evidence_note: Two independent human chromosomal rearrangements at NPPC with measured circulating CNP/NT-proCNP elevation and matching skeletal overgrowth, plus human loss-of-function NPPC mutations with functional cGMP assays.
nppc_duplication_tall_stature.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; mouse transgenics are corroborative.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology for any NPPC dosage disorder
human plasma: CNP doubled (bocciardi2007) and NT-proCNP elevated (ko2015) in the two overexpression cases

key_refs.one_line_finding: t(2;7) near NPPC doubles plasma CNP and causes marfanoid overgrowth with skeletal anomalies.
Independent t(1;2) 200 kb downstream of NPPC raises NT-proCNP and causes skeletal overgrowth.
Heterozygous NPPC CNP-ring mutations reduce cGMP synthesis and cause autosomal dominant short stature with small hands.
Loss-of-function NPR3 (CNP clearance receptor) variants cause extreme tall stature.

npr2_gain_of_function_tall.name: NPR2 gain-of-function tall stature
npr2_gain_of_function_tall.summary:
NPR2 gain of function is the three-copy-equivalent end of the CNP dosage series and completes
the human dose-response without any pharmacology. Three mechanistically distinct classes of
activating mutation have been reported. p.Val883Met in the guanylyl cyclase domain generates
cGMP in the complete absence of CNP ligand; the three-generation family carrying it had tall
stature, scoliosis and macrodactyly of the great toes, and blood cGMP was elevated in the
patients - the transducer and the phenotype were measured in the same people.
p.Arg655Cys in the kinase homology domain instead amplifies the CNP response and its allosteric
stabilisation by ATP, wild-type and mutant receptors heterodimerise (a dominant-positive
mechanism), and the proband was extremely tall WITHOUT skeletal deformity; his plasma
NT-proCNP was reduced, i.e. increased receptor activity feeds back onto ligand production. A
third class is an activating deletion in the submembrane region. The phenotypic split between
V883M (tall with deformity) and R655C (tall without deformity) is the interesting part: it
suggests ligand-independent basal signalling and amplified ligand-dependent signalling are not
interchangeable in the growth plate. Adult heights in cm are reported only per-individual;
there is no pooled effect size for NPR2 gain of function, which is the single largest
quantitative hole in this axis.
npr2_gain_of_function_tall.human_evidence_note: Human pedigrees with functionally validated activating NPR2 alleles and, for V883M, a measured downstream second messenger (blood cGMP) in the affected individuals.
npr2_gain_of_function_tall.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; the transgenic mouse in the V883M study is corroborative, not the basis of the human claim.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in NPR2 gain of function

key_refs.one_line_finding: NPR2 V883M is constitutively active; three-generation tall-stature family with elevated blood cGMP.
NPR2 R655C in the kinase homology domain: extreme tall stature without skeletal deformity; NT-proCNP reduced.
An activating deletion in the NPR2 submembrane region causes tall stature - a third activating class.
One NPR2 gain-of-function variant found in tall individuals; NPR2 GoF may be an underrecognised cause of tall stature.

npr2_heterozygous_short_stature.name: NPR2 heterozygous short stature
npr2_heterozygous_short_stature.summary:
NPR2 heterozygotes are the one-copy point of the CNP dosage series and the reason the series
is quantitative rather than anecdotal. In a single extended family containing an AMDM
proband, the 16 heterozygous carriers had a mean height z-score of -1.8 +/- 1.1 versus -0.4
+/- 0.8 in 23 non-carrier relatives (P < 0.0005) and versus the general population (P <
0.0005) - a roughly 1.4 SD effect of losing one functional NPR2 allele, with no change in body
proportion. That effect size was subsequently verified in unrelated cohorts: seven
heterozygous NPR2 missense or splice-site variants were found in 192 short-stature patients
and none in 192 height-normal controls, with eight of the tested variants shown to be
loss-of-function in a cGMP assay. A separate screen of SHOX-negative referrals for
Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis found pathogenic NPR2 mutations in about 3 percent, showing that
NPR2 haploinsufficiency can present as DISproportionate short stature clinically
indistinguishable from SHOX deficiency but WITHOUT Madelung deformity. Estimates of the
contribution to idiopathic short stature have converged from an early 1-in-30 down to a range
of 0 to 1/26. Because vosoritide agonises this exact receptor, NPR2 heterozygotes are the
mechanistically cleanest non-achondroplasia indication for CNP analogues, and they have been
included in a phase II basket trial.
npr2_heterozygous_short_stature.human_evidence_note: Within-family carrier versus non-carrier height comparison plus case-control variant burden with functional cGMP assays in human cells.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in NPR2 haploinsufficiency (gap g_l11path_005)

key_refs.one_line_finding: NPR2 carriers -1.8 +/- 1.1 SDS vs -0.4 +/- 0.8 in non-carrier relatives (n=16 vs 23, P<0.0005).
7 heterozygous NPR2 variants in 192 short patients and 0 in 192 controls; 8 loss-of-function, 1 gain-of-function.
NPR2 mutations in ~3% of SHOX-negative Leri-Weill referrals; disproportion without Madelung deformity.
Obligate AMDM carriers have heights below matched control means.

osteogenesis_imperfecta_growth.name: Osteogenesis imperfecta growth failure
osteogenesis_imperfecta_growth.summary:
Osteogenesis imperfecta separates bone matrix quality from growth plate function. Type I
collagen is the principal organic matrix of BONE but is not the structural collagen of the
growth plate, where type II predominates - so in OI the physis is comparatively normal while the
bone it produces is defective. Short stature in OI is therefore largely a consequence rather
than a cause: repeated fractures, long-bone deformity, vertebral compression and spinal
deformity subtract height mechanically, and severity tracks OI type, with the mildest type I
often near-normal in stature and the severe types III and IV markedly short. A large Italian
registry study characterises this severity gradient across a national cohort. Two secondary
mechanisms complicate the picture and are worth flagging: bisphosphonate treatment alters
vertebral morphology and craniofacial growth, and reduced mobility and muscle loading feed back
onto bone via mechanotransduction (Layer L6). OI is the clearest human demonstration that adult
height is not a pure readout of growth plate output - it is growth plate output minus the
structural losses accumulated in the bone the plate has already made.
osteogenesis_imperfecta_growth.human_evidence_note: A national registry cohort documents the OI-type-dependent clinical and skeletal severity gradient in humans.
localization: human growth plate: comparatively preserved; type I collagen is the matrix of bone, not of growth plate cartilage
human bone: defective type I collagen matrix with fractures and progressive deformity

key_refs.one_line_finding: Registry-based clinical characterisation of a large Italian osteogenesis imperfecta cohort.

pappa2_deficiency.name: PAPP-A2 deficiency
pappa2_deficiency.summary:
PAPP-A2 deficiency is the human experiment that separates total IGF-I from BIOAVAILABLE IGF-I.
Members of two unrelated families carried homozygous PAPPA2 mutations, p.D643fs25* and
p.Ala1033Val, and both abolished PAPP-A2 proteolytic activity against IGFBP-3 and IGFBP-5 in
vitro. The resulting human biochemistry is diagnostic and counterintuitive: total IGF-I,
IGF-II, IGFBP-3, IGFBP-5 and acid-labile subunit are all ELEVATED, size-exclusion
chromatography shows significantly more IGF-I retained in the ternary complex, and free IGF-I
is DECREASED. The phenotype is progressive postnatal growth failure with moderate microcephaly,
thin long bones and mildly decreased bone density. This is the first pathogenic human mutation
in the IGFBP system or its regulators, and it is the cleanest available demonstration that the
growth plate responds to free rather than total IGF-I - a distinction that ordinary clinical
assays cannot make and that therefore silently mis-classifies patients. rhIGF-1 treatment
improved growth in two of the affected siblings, and plasma transfusion or recombinant PAPP-A2
raises free IGF-I, providing the pharmacological confirmation.
pappa2_deficiency.human_evidence_note: Two unrelated human families with homozygous PAPPA2 mutations, functional proteolysis assays and direct measurement of free versus total IGF-I.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in PAPP-A2 deficiency

key_refs.one_line_finding: Homozygous PAPPA2 mutations abolish IGFBP-3/-5 proteolysis: growth failure with HIGH total but LOW free IGF-I.

pituitary_gigantism.name: Pituitary gigantism
pituitary_gigantism.summary:
Pituitary gigantism is the positive-dose arm of the GH axis and the human proof that the growth
plate remains responsive to GH excess until it fuses. The defining variable is timing relative
to epiphyseal fusion, not the hormone: identical GH excess produces gigantism before fusion and
acromegaly after it. In the only standardised international series (208 patients), 78.4 percent
were male, the median age at onset of rapid growth was 13 years and onset was significantly
earlier in females, adenomas were macroadenomas in 84 percent, and pituitary adenomas were
diagnosed at 15.8 years in females versus 21.5 years in males. Inclusion required GH excess
plus either an abnormal growth velocity for age or a final height more than 2 SD above the
country mean. The genetic causes overlap with the atlas elsewhere: AIP mutations, X-LAG
(Xq26.3 duplication involving GPR101), McCune-Albright and Carney complex, with a genetic cause
identifiable in a substantial minority. The mechanistic contrast with the FGFR3 and NPR2 series
is important: gigantism is an ENDOCRINE overdrive acting on a structurally normal growth plate,
so proportions are preserved and the excess height is distributed across all segments, whereas
the chondrodysplasias distort segment ratios.
pituitary_gigantism.human_evidence_note: A retrospective international multicentre series of 208 patients with standardised inclusion criteria based on growth velocity or final height.
localization: human growth plate: no histology; the phenotype is inferred from stature and radiology

key_refs.one_line_finding: 208 pituitary gigantism patients: median onset of rapid growth 13 y, 78.4% male, 84% macroadenoma.
Review of tall stature and gigantism in the transition age with clinical and genetic recommendations.

prader_willi_growth.name: Prader-Willi syndrome growth failure
prader_willi_growth.summary:
Prader-Willi syndrome is the hypothalamic arm of the GH-axis experiment: loss of paternally
expressed genes at 15q11-q13, by deletion, maternal uniparental disomy or imprinting defect,
produces hypothalamic dysfunction that includes GH deficiency in about 90 percent of patients
alongside hypogonadism, hyperphagia and hypotonia. The untreated adult height is reduced and
disorder-specific growth references have been constructed from patients never treated with
growth hormone, which is the correct comparator now that GH is standard of care. GH therapy in
PWS is a mechanistically instructive case because its benefits are not confined to height: a
systematic review and meta-analysis of long-term GH effects finds improvements in body
composition and cognition as well as growth. Two features distinguish PWS from isolated GH
deficiency in this layer. First, the growth failure is combined with hypogonadism, which delays
fusion and partially offsets it. Second, PWS patients carry a documented risk of respiratory
compromise on GH initiation, which is why the untreated natural-history references remain
essential.
prader_willi_growth.human_evidence_note: Disorder-specific growth charts from GH-naive patients plus a systematic review and meta-analysis of long-term GH effects.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Prader-Willi syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: Disease-specific growth charts for Argentine Prader-Willi patients never treated with growth hormone.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of long-term GH effects in Prader-Willi syndrome.

pseudoachondroplasia.name: Pseudoachondroplasia
pseudoachondroplasia.summary:
Pseudoachondroplasia is the human COMP experiment and a proteostasis rather than a signalling
disorder. Heterozygous mutations in cartilage oligomeric matrix protein, overwhelmingly in the
type 3 (calcium-binding) repeat domain, produce a misfolded protein that is retained in the
chondrocyte endoplasmic reticulum; the disease mechanism is therefore intracellular retention
and ER stress, not simple loss of an extracellular structural protein. The largest genotype
compilation - 830 patients (471 probands) carrying 224 distinct COMP variants from 106
publications - resolves the allelic series: missense variants account for 80.8 percent, exon 13
is hit in 38.9 percent of probands and the T3 repeat domain in 87.7 percent, and the single
commonest lesion is the in-frame deletion c.1417_1419del (p.Asp473del). Pseudoachondroplasia
and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 1 are the two ends of one COMP phenotypic continuum, and
the compilation separates them statistically: PSACH has significantly earlier onset, shorter
stature, more lower-limb deformity and joint laxity, while EDM1 has more joint pain and
osteoarthritis; in-frame variants and p.Asp473del specifically are PSACH, whereas missense
changes in subdomains T3-4 and T3-5 give EDM1. Birth length is normal - growth failure appears
in the second year - which is the auxological fingerprint that distinguishes it from
achondroplasia at presentation.
pseudoachondroplasia.human_evidence_note: 830 genotyped human patients with statistically compared phenotypes across the PSACH-EDM1 continuum.
localization: human growth plate chondrocyte: COMP is retained in the rough endoplasmic reticulum; lamellar inclusion bodies in chondrocytes are the classical human histological finding in PSACH

key_refs.one_line_finding: 830 PSACH/EDM1 patients: in-frame COMP variants and p.Asp473del are PSACH-specific; T3-4/T3-5 missense give EDM1.
Some COMP mutations previously called PSACH give a typical MED1 or intermediate phenotype.

pseudohypoparathyroidism.name: Pseudohypoparathyroidism
pseudohypoparathyroidism.summary:
Pseudohypoparathyroidism is the human Gs-alpha experiment and the third member of the PTH1R
series in this layer, sitting one step below the receptor that Jansen and Blomstrand
chondrodysplasia perturb. Inactivating GNAS mutations or GNAS imprinting defects reduce Gs-alpha
signalling, so PTH1R cannot generate cAMP - functionally the same lesion as Blomstrand
chondrodysplasia but partial and tissue-restricted by imprinting. The skeletal phenotype is
Albright hereditary osteodystrophy: brachydactyly, most characteristically of the fourth and
fifth metacarpals, round face, subcutaneous ossifications and short stature. The mechanism of
the brachydactyly is PREMATURE closure of the affected growth plates, because reduced
PTHrP-PTH1R-cAMP signalling accelerates the exit of proliferative chondrocytes into hypertrophy -
the exact opposite of the delayed hypertrophy of Jansen. Pseudohypoparathyroidism therefore
completes a three-point human dose series on one signalling axis: constitutive activation
(Jansen, delayed maturation, severe short stature), complete inactivation (Blomstrand,
accelerated maturation, lethal), and partial downstream inactivation (PHP, accelerated closure
of selected plates, brachydactyly and mild short stature). Height and weight trajectories have
been characterised in a large single-centre paediatric Chinese cohort.
pseudohypoparathyroidism.human_evidence_note: Human GNAS lesions with a characteristic selective growth plate closure phenotype and a large paediatric growth cohort.
localization: human metacarpal/metatarsal growth plates: premature closure, giving the selective brachydactyly of Albright hereditary osteodystrophy
human long bone growth plates: less affected, giving only mild overall short stature

key_refs.one_line_finding: Height and weight development in a large single-centre Chinese paediatric pseudohypoparathyroidism cohort.
Places PHP within the PTH1R/Gs-alpha signalling disease spectrum alongside Blomstrand and Jansen.

russell_silver_syndrome.name: Silver-Russell syndrome
russell_silver_syndrome.summary:
Silver-Russell syndrome is the human imprinting experiment at the IGF2/H19 locus and the
mirror image of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. The two commonest molecular subtypes are loss of
methylation at the paternally methylated 11p15.5 IGF2/H19 domain, which reduces IGF2
expression, and maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7. Growth restriction begins in utero
and persists postnatally without catch-up, distinguishing SRS from the ~85-90 percent of
small-for-gestational-age children who do catch up. Body asymmetry, relative macrocephaly and
feeding difficulty complete the phenotype. Two features make SRS mechanistically informative
here. First, paternally inherited IGF2 missense variants also cause SRS, which localises
causality within the imprinted domain to IGF2 itself and closes the loop to the IGF1/IGF1R
nodes of this layer from a different direction - ligand dose set by imprinting rather than by
mutation. Second, puberty tends to start EARLY in SRS relative to gestational-age-matched SGA
controls, so the growth plate is both underdriven and prematurely terminated, and adult height
is worse than the childhood deficit implies. Phenotype beyond childhood has been characterised
in genetically confirmed adults.
russell_silver_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Molecularly defined human imprinting subtypes with longitudinal growth and pubertal timing data and an adult follow-up series.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Silver-Russell syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: Phenotype of genetically confirmed Silver-Russell syndrome followed beyond childhood.
GeneReviews Silver-Russell syndrome: molecular subtypes, growth and management.

saddan_syndrome.name: SADDAN syndrome
saddan_syndrome.summary:
SADDAN is the single most informative point in the FGFR3 allelic series because it breaks the
assumption that receptor activation strength predicts lethality. The lesion is A1949T giving
Lys650Met, one nucleotide away from the A1948G/Lys650Glu substitution that causes lethal
thanatophoric dysplasia type II. In transient transfection K650M produces roughly three times
the constitutive receptor kinase activity of K650E - yet the four originally reported
individuals survived past infancy without prolonged life support, developed extensive
acanthosis nigricans from early childhood, had severe neurological impairment, and had a
skeletal phenotype approaching but not equalling TD type I. The dissociation implies that
lethality in thanatophoric dysplasia is driven by something other than the scalar magnitude of
FGFR3 kinase output - candidate explanations are differential substrate/pathway bias (MAPK vs
STAT1), differential receptor trafficking, or the tissue distribution of the activated
receptor including the thoracic cage and cranial base. Acanthosis nigricans is itself a
signalling readout: the same activated FGFR3 acting in keratinocytes. No systematic adult
height series exists for SADDAN and no growth plate histology has been published, so the
distal end of the causal chain is empty in humans.

claim_grades.claim: K650M produces roughly three times the constitutive FGFR3 kinase activity of K650E in transient transfection, yet is survivable while K650E (thanatophoric II) is lethal.
claim_grades.basis: In-vitro kinase activity plus human phenotype in the four originally reported individuals; small n but the phenotypic contrast is unambiguous.
