claim_grades.claim: Phenotypic severity is therefore NOT monotonic in constitutive kinase activity across the FGFR3 KINASE-DOMAIN allelic series.
claim_grades.basis: Rests on the K650E/K650M pair specifically. Both are kinase-domain alleles.

claim_grades.claim: Severity is non-monotonic in activation across the whole FGFR3 allelic series including transmembrane variants.
claim_grades.basis: CONTRADICTED IN PART: the biochemical ordering K650E > G380R matches the phenotypic ordering thanatophoric > achondroplasia. Monotonicity HOLDS across that comparison and breaks only within the kinase-domain pair. The general claim is not supported.

saddan_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Genotype, receptor biochemistry and clinical survival are all documented in the four index patients; no cohort-level auxology exists.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in SADDAN (gap g_l11path_004)

key_refs.one_line_finding: SADDAN = FGFR3 K650M with ~3x the constitutive activity of the lethal K650E allele, yet non-lethal.
The Lys650 codon generates a graded series: K650N/Q mild, K650E/M severe.

contradicts: SCOPE LIMIT: the non-monotonicity result is specific to the kinase-domain pair K650E/K650M. Across the kinase-domain-to-transmembrane comparison (K650E vs G380R) activation and severity DO track together. Any therapeutic inference drawn from non-monotonicity must state which alleles it applies to - see g_mr002_allele.
aliases: severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans

schmid_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.name: Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia
schmid_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.summary:
Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is the human collagen X experiment and localises the lesion
to a single growth plate zone. COL10A1 encodes type X collagen, which is expressed ONLY by
hypertrophic chondrocytes; mutations - concentrated in the C-terminal NC1 trimerisation domain
and confirmed as the disease locus by an early multi-mutation series - prevent normal trimer
assembly. Because the gene is expressed nowhere else, the phenotype is a pure hypertrophic-zone
readout: irregular, widened, cupped metaphyses with normal epiphyses and a normal spine, coxa
vara, bowed legs and mild-to-moderate short stature. The contrast with type II collagen
disorders (spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, where the epiphyses and spine are the affected
compartments) is one of the sharpest structure-function mappings in human skeletal genetics: the
zone in which a matrix gene is expressed predicts which radiographic compartment fails. Modern
work shows the pathogenic mechanism is not simple haploinsufficiency but ER stress from
misfolded collagen X retained in hypertrophic chondrocytes, which is why carbamazepine, an
autophagy-inducing proteostasis modulator, has been proposed as a treatment. Adult height is
usually only mildly reduced, so Schmid also shows that eliminating a hypertrophic-zone matrix
protein costs surprisingly little final height.

Two independent designs establish the locus and then quantify it. Warman 1993 mapped a 13 bp
COL10A1 deletion segregating with the disorder in a large Mormon kindred at lod 18.2 (theta = 0),
producing a frameshift that shortens the alpha-1(X) chain by nine residues in the conserved NC1
domain. Meng 2025 assembled 4 new cases and 124 published ones and converted the locus into a
dose-resolved phenotype: patients carrying missense variants had height Z of -3.62 +/- 1.95 versus
-1.99 +/- 1.28 for those with truncating variants (P = 0.013), and more metaphyseal irregularity of
the distal radius and ulna (P = 0.019); NC1-domain variants presented at a median of 12 months
against 72 months for non-NC1 variants (P = 0.0014). Because truncating transcripts are removed by
nonsense-mediated decay while missense alleles make a stable chain that disrupts trimerisation of
the wild-type product - shown directly for p.W651fsX666 by Yang 2025 - this is the only place in
the atlas where dominant-negative interference and haploinsufficiency at one locus have measured
stature effects in the same cohort, and interference costs about 1.6 SDS more.

claim_grades.claim: COL10A1 mutations cause Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia.
claim_grades.basis: Single-kindred linkage at lod 18.2 with an identified 13 bp deletion (warman1993) and an independent 128-case unrelated-patient mutation series (meng2025) - different designs, different cohorts, different eras.

claim_grades.claim: COL10A1 missense variants reduce stature about 1.6 SDS more than truncating variants.
claim_grades.basis: One pooled 128-case cohort with P=0.013 (meng2025), mechanistically corroborated by an independent trimerisation assay (yang2025); the height comparison itself has not been repeated in a second cohort.

claim_grades.claim: The phenotype is a pure hypertrophic-zone readout because collagen X is expressed only there.
claim_grades.basis: Inference from the restricted expression of collagen X plus the radiographic metaphyseal-only distribution; no zone-resolved human MCDS growth plate has been examined.

schmid_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.human_evidence_note: Human COL10A1 mutation series established the locus; the zone-specific expression of collagen X and the metaphysis-restricted radiology are both human observations.
schmid_metaphyseal_chondrodysplasia.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node; the ER-stress mechanism is supported by mouse models and is flagged as such.
localization: human HZ: type X collagen is expressed exclusively by hypertrophic chondrocytes, and the radiographic lesion is confined to the metaphysis, i.e. immediately distal to the hypertrophic zone
human epiphysis and spine: spared, distinguishing COL10A1 from COL2A1 disorders

key_refs.one_line_finding: Additional COL10A1 mutations confirm COL10A1 as the Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia locus.
GeneReviews: NC1-domain COL10A1 mutations, coxa vara, metaphyseal changes and mild short stature.
A 13 bp COL10A1 deletion segregates with autosomal dominant Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia at lod 18.2, truncating the conserved NC1 domain.
In 128 COL10A1 cases, missense variants gave height Z -3.62 +/- 1.95 versus -1.99 +/- 1.28 for truncating variants (P=0.013), with NC1-domain variants presenting earlier.
COL10A1 p.W651fsX666 impairs trimerisation of normal collagen X, demonstrating a dominant-negative effect on the wild-type allele.

sotos_syndrome.name: Sotos syndrome
sotos_syndrome.summary:
Sotos syndrome is a chromatin-level overgrowth experiment: haploinsufficiency for NSD1, a
histone H3K36 methyltransferase, produces prenatal and childhood overgrowth with macrocephaly,
a distinctive facial gestalt and learning difficulties. The mechanistically important growth
feature is the dissociation between growth RATE and growth DURATION. Height and head
circumference are markedly increased in infancy and childhood, but bone age is ADVANCED, so the
growth period is shortened and eventual adult height is usually only at the upper limit of
normal rather than in the gigantism range. Sotos is therefore the overgrowth mirror of ACAN
deficiency: in both, bone age runs ahead of chronological age and the adult height deviates
from the childhood height in the direction that shortening the growth period predicts. In Sotos
the advanced maturation partially cancels an excess; in ACAN it compounds a deficit. Central
precocious puberty has been reported in Sotos and would further truncate the growth period.
Because NSD1 acts on chromatin rather than on a growth factor or matrix protein, Sotos also
demonstrates that generic transcriptional dysregulation can produce a specific auxological
signature.
sotos_syndrome.human_evidence_note: NSD1 haploinsufficiency is molecularly defined in humans and the height/bone-age dissociation is a consistent clinical observation; no quantitative adult-height cohort was retrieved in this sweep.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Sotos syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: Genetic architecture of non-familial tall stature including NSD1-related overgrowth.
Tall stature differential including Sotos and the advanced-bone-age overgrowth group.

spondyloepiphyseal_dysplasia.name: Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia (COL2A1 type II collagenopathy)
spondyloepiphyseal_dysplasia.summary:
Type II collagenopathies are the human collagen II experiment and the compartmental complement
to Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia. COL2A1 encodes the principal collagen of all hyaline
cartilage - resting, proliferative and articular - and the resulting disorders therefore hit the
epiphyses and the vertebral bodies rather than the metaphyses: platyspondyly, delayed epiphyseal
ossification, coxa vara, short trunk with relatively preserved limb length, myopia and retinal
detachment (because COL2A1 is also the collagen of the vitreous), and hearing loss. The
allelic series runs from perinatal-lethal achondrogenesis type II and hypochondrogenesis
through spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita to Kniest dysplasia and mild Stickler syndrome,
and the severity gradient tracks the mutation class: glycine substitutions in the triple helix
that produce dominant-negative misfolded trimers are severe, whereas haploinsufficiency alleles
are mild. This is the same allele-class logic as the FGFR3 series but operating through protein
misfolding rather than receptor activation. The short stature is disproportionate and
trunk-dominant, the opposite proportional signature to AMDM and to the FGFR3 disorders, which is
why segment ratios rather than height alone are diagnostically informative.
spondyloepiphyseal_dysplasia.human_evidence_note: Human COL2A1 mutation series with genotype-phenotype correlation across the allelic spectrum.
localization: human RZ/PZ and articular cartilage: type II collagen is the principal structural collagen throughout hyaline cartilage, and the radiographic lesion is epiphyseal and vertebral
human metaphysis: relatively spared, distinguishing COL2A1 from COL10A1 disorders

key_refs.one_line_finding: Seven COL2A1 variants in Chinese children with type II collagen disorders: clinical spectrum.

stat5b_deficiency.name: STAT5B deficiency
stat5b_deficiency.summary:
STAT5B deficiency places the lesion one step below the GH receptor and shows that the entire
growth-promoting output of GH runs through a single transcription factor. In the second
reported case, a homozygous single-nucleotide insertion in STAT5B exon 10 caused a frameshift,
early termination and complete absence of immunodetectable STAT5b protein. The biochemical
signature is GH insensitivity with an intact receptor: GH and GH-binding protein normal to
elevated, IGF-I 7.2 ng/mL against a normal range of 242-600, IGFBP-3 543 ng/mL against
2500-4800, acid-labile subunit 1.22 ug/mL against 5.6-16, and no rise in an IGF-I generation
test. The stature outcome is extreme: 114 cm at age 16.4 years, a height SDS of -7.8. A
separate natural missense allele, A630P in the SH2 domain, was shown to be unable to function
either as a signal transducer or as a transcription factor, confirming that the growth defect
maps to loss of STAT5b transcriptional activity on the IGF1 locus rather than to some
secondary effect. STAT5B deficiency is also an immunodeficiency, because STAT5b transduces
IL-2 family cytokines - one of the clearest examples in this layer of a growth gene whose
pleiotropy is a mechanistic clue rather than noise.
stat5b_deficiency.human_evidence_note: Molecularly confirmed human null with complete hormonal profiling and measured stature; a second human allele independently shown to abolish transducer and transcription-factor function.
localization: human growth plate: no published histology in STAT5B deficiency

key_refs.one_line_finding: STAT5B null: 114 cm (-7.8 SDS) at 16.4 y, IGF-I 7.2 ng/mL, flat IGF-I generation test.

thanatophoric_dysplasia.name: Thanatophoric dysplasia types I and II
thanatophoric_dysplasia.summary:
Thanatophoric dysplasia is the lethal end of the FGFR3 allelic series and the only member of
the series in which the human growth plate has actually been examined. Two mutation classes
map onto the two clinical types: type II is caused by Lys650Glu in the tyrosine kinase
activation loop, found in 16 of 16 TD2 cases in the defining study; type I is caused by
substitutions that create an unpaired cysteine in the extracellular domain, Arg248Cys in 22 of
39 cases plus Ser371Cys, which drive ligand-independent covalent dimerisation. Both classes
constitutively activate the receptor more strongly than the achondroplasia G380R allele, and
the biochemical ordering K650E > G380R matches the phenotypic ordering. In 91 registry cases
with matched radiology and histopathology, the mutation predicted the anatomy: K650E cases had
straight femora, craniosynostosis and frequently a cloverleaf skull, whereas all other
genotypes had curved femora; critically, the K650E growth plates were BETTER preserved than
the R248C and Y373C plates, so severity of receptor activation and severity of growth plate
disorganisation are not monotonically related. Death is normally in the perinatal period from
thoracic insufficiency, so no adult height exists; birth length is profoundly reduced and the
disorder affects about 1 in 20,000 live births.
thanatophoric_dysplasia.human_evidence_note: Genotype-radiology-histopathology correlation was performed on 91 human cases with autopsy growth plate material - the only place in the FGFR3 series where human growth plate tissue has been systematically read.
thanatophoric_dysplasia.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype node with human tissue evidence.
localization: human growth plate (autopsy): disorganised with shortened proliferative columns in all TD genotypes; better preserved in K650E than in R248C/Y373C cases (wilcox1998)

key_refs.one_line_finding: TD2 = K650E (16/16); TD1 = R248C (22/39) or S371C - different FGFR3 domains, different lethal phenotypes.
91 TD cases: K650E gives straight femora, craniosynostosis and BETTER-preserved growth plates than R248C/Y373C.
Graded constitutive activation: K650E (TD) exceeds G380R (achondroplasia).
K650M gives ~3x the constitutive activity of K650E yet is non-lethal (SADDAN).

turner_syndrome.name: Turner syndrome
turner_syndrome.summary:
Turner syndrome is the human SHOX gene-dosage experiment plus an estrogen-timing experiment in
the same patient. The primary skeletal lesion is haploinsufficiency for SHOX in the
pseudoautosomal region PAR1, which escapes X inactivation and is therefore normally expressed
from two copies; loss of one copy removes roughly the SHOX contribution to stature. A
biobank analysis of 928,605 individuals including 1,225 adults with sex-chromosome
aneuploidies (45,X n=95; 47,XXY n=505; 47,XYY n=290; 47,XXX n=335) separated the components
quantitatively: a unit increase in Y-chromosome dosage adds 3.1 cm (95% CI 1.9-4.3) more height
than a unit increase in inactive-X dosage, independent of hormonal variables, and this
asymmetry accounts for 22.6 percent of the 13 cm mean height difference between 46,XY men and
46,XX women. Because the same PAR1 dosage logic applies in reverse in Turner syndrome, this is
the strongest available human quantification of the SHOX contribution to stature. The second
lesion is gonadal: ovarian failure removes the pubertal estrogen surge, so untreated girls have
no growth spurt but also no early fusion, and growth continues into the late teens - a pattern
that is visible in the spontaneous-growth references built from girls never given GH or
oxandrolone (n=259 Brazilian, n=842 Turkish). Turner is therefore the disorder in which SHOX
dosage and estrogen timing can be dissociated by treatment.
turner_syndrome.human_evidence_note: Population-scale human aneuploidy modelling of PAR1 dosage plus two large untreated national growth references.
localization: human growth plate: not examined in Turner syndrome

key_refs.one_line_finding: One extra Y adds 3.1 cm (95% CI 1.9-4.3) more than one extra inactive X; explains 22.6% of the sex difference in height.
Brazilian Turner growth charts from 259 girls never treated with GH or oxandrolone.
Turkish Turner growth charts from 842 girls measured before any therapy.

x_linked_hypophosphatemia.name: X-linked hypophosphatemia
x_linked_hypophosphatemia.summary:
X-linked hypophosphatemia is the human FGF23 experiment and, read alongside hypophosphatasia, it
shows that the growth plate can fail to mineralise for two entirely different reasons.
Inactivating PHEX mutations lead to excess circulating FGF23, which suppresses renal phosphate
reabsorption and 1-alpha-hydroxylation of vitamin D; the result is chronic hypophosphataemia and
therefore an insufficient extracellular phosphate supply for apatite deposition at the zone of
provisional calcification, plus impaired hypertrophic chondrocyte apoptosis, giving rickets with
widened, frayed growth plates and progressive lower-limb bowing. Two auxological findings from
this sweep sharpen the phenotype. First, short stature is already established BEFORE puberty in
XLH, so the deficit is not a pubertal phenomenon. Second, bone age is DELAYED in XLH - the
opposite direction to ACAN-related short stature, where bone age is advanced. XLH therefore
provides the contrasting arm of the height/maturation dissociation that makes ACAN interesting:
here a short child has extra growing time and still ends up short, whereas in aggrecanopathy a
short child loses growing time. Burosumab, an anti-FGF23 antibody, prevents further height
deficit in treated toddlers, which is the interventional confirmation.
x_linked_hypophosphatemia.human_evidence_note: Human PHEX mutations with a defined endocrine mechanism, pre-pubertal auxology, bone-age data and an interventional anti-FGF23 antibody result.
localization: human ZPC and HZ: rachitic widening with unmineralised hypertrophic cartilage; the lesion is substrate (phosphate) limitation rather than inhibitor (pyrophosphate) excess

key_refs.one_line_finding: Short stature in XLH is already present in pre-pubertal children.
Bone age is DELAYED in X-linked hypophosphatemia - the opposite of ACAN-related short stature.

xlag_gpr101.name: X-linked acrogigantism (X-LAG)
xlag_gpr101.summary:
X-LAG is the earliest-onset human overgrowth disorder of the GH axis and a structural-variant
experiment in enhancer hijacking. Microduplications of chromosome Xq26.3 containing GPR101 were
found in 13 of 43 gigantism patients; four came from two unrelated kindreds and nine were
sporadic. The duplication contains four protein-coding genes but only GPR101 was overexpressed
in the patients' pituitary lesions, isolating the causal gene within the interval. The
mechanism is now understood as disruption of the topologically associating domain containing
GPR101 and formation of a neo-TAD that lets VGLL1-adjacent enhancers drive ectopic pituitary
GPR101 expression - which is why not every GPR101-containing duplication is pathogenic, a point
of direct clinical consequence in prenatal diagnosis. The phenotype is defined by age: every
X-LAG patient had disease onset in early childhood, whereas none of the gigantism patients
without an Xq26.3 duplication presented before age 5. Somatic mosaicism explains sporadic male
cases. X-LAG is therefore the human demonstration that the growth plate's total elongation
capacity is very large when GH drive begins in infancy rather than at puberty.
xlag_gpr101.human_evidence_note: Human structural variants with tissue-level expression evidence localising causality to GPR101, replicated in independent cohorts.
localization: human pituitary lesion: GPR101 overexpressed (trivellin2014)
human growth plate: not examined

key_refs.one_line_finding: Xq26.3 microduplication containing GPR101 in 13/43 gigantism patients, all with onset in early childhood.

abaloparatide.name: Abaloparatide (PTHrP 1-34 analogue)
abaloparatide.summary:
Abaloparatide is a synthetic analogue of PTHrP(1-34) acting as a PTH1R agonist, given
once daily at 80 mcg subcutaneously for osteoporosis. Because PTHrP is the endogenous
ligand that maintains the proliferative pool of the growth plate through PTH1R, an
exogenous PTHrP analogue is the most direct pharmacological mimic of the plate's own
pace-setting signal available as an approved drug - and, like teriparatide, it is barred
from the growing skeleton. The FDA label states abaloparatide is not recommended in
paediatric patients with open epiphyses or hereditary disorders predisposing to
osteosarcoma because of increased baseline osteosarcoma risk, and that safety and
effectiveness in paediatric patients have not been established. The result is a
structural hole in the atlas: the two approved PTH1R agonists both target the receptor
whose ligand sets growth plate output, and neither has ever been given to a human growth
plate. Whether an abaloparatide-like PTHrP analogue would expand the proliferative zone,
delay hypertrophy and lengthen bones in a child is therefore unknown and, under current
regulatory constraints, not directly testable.

claim_grades.claim: Abaloparatide is a PTH1R agonist acting through cAMP in target cells.
claim_grades.basis: Mechanism established in the approved label and supported by adult bone turnover marker data.

claim_grades.claim: Abaloparatide is not recommended in patients with open epiphyses.
claim_grades.basis: Explicit FDA label statement.

claim_grades.claim: A PTHrP analogue would expand the proliferative zone and lengthen bone in a growing human.
claim_grades.basis: Inference from PTHrP-PTH1R growth plate biology; no human data of any kind.

abaloparatide.human_evidence_note: No human paediatric exposure and no growth endpoint; all human data are adult osteoporosis outcomes.
abaloparatide.translation_risk_reason: The anabolic effect is characterised in rats and monkeys and in adult human bone density; nothing is known about its action on a growing plate, and the rodent carcinogenicity signal that motivates the paediatric restriction is itself a species-translation question.
localization: human growth plate: PTH1R present on prehypertrophic chondrocytes; no human pharmacological exposure

key_refs.one_line_finding: PTHrP(1-34) analogue at 80 mcg/day; not recommended in paediatric patients with open epiphyses because of osteosarcoma risk.
The same open-epiphyses restriction applies to the other approved PTH1R agonist, teriparatide.
Constitutive PTH1R activation in mouse - the closest available model of chronic PTH1R agonism at the growth plate.

aromatase_inhibitor_anastrozole.name: Anastrozole
aromatase_inhibitor_anastrozole.summary:
Anastrozole is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor used off-label in boys and in
congenital adrenal hyperplasia to reduce oestrogen-driven skeletal maturation. Compared
head to head with letrozole over 3 years in 79 pubertal boys with idiopathic short
stature it produced smaller deviations in testosterone, oestradiol, IGF-1, growth
velocity and bone age advance - that is, a weaker biochemical effect - yet there was no
difference between the drugs in change in predicted adult height, and the combined
3-year gain was only +1.3 cm. The dissociation is the point: a threefold difference in
the intensity of oestrogen suppression bought no additional predicted height, which
argues that oestrogen suppression is not the rate-limiting variable for height gain in
this population. In two settings anastrozole does have attained-height data. In
propensity-matched ISS boys with bone age >=13 y, anastrozole plus rhGH gave the highest
target-height-adjusted adult height SDS of three regimens (0.81 +/- 0.34 versus 0.60 for
letrozole+rhGH and 0.48 for GnRHa+rhGH). And in 21-hydroxylase-deficiency congenital
adrenal hyperplasia, where androgen excess drives premature fusion, anastrozole improved
height outcomes in growing children.

claim_grades.claim: Anastrozole suppresses oestradiol and slows bone age advance less than letrozole at conventional doses.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised head-to-head trial with annual hormone and bone age data, n=79.

claim_grades.claim: The weaker oestrogen suppression yields no less predicted-adult-height gain.
claim_grades.basis: Same trial reports no between-group difference in change in predicted adult height; a null within a small trial, so not a strong equivalence claim.

claim_grades.claim: Anastrozole plus rhGH improves attained adult height in ISS boys with advanced bone age.
claim_grades.basis: Single-centre propensity-matched cohort, 32 per arm, not randomised.

claim_grades.claim: Anastrozole improves height outcomes in 21-hydroxylase-deficiency CAH.
claim_grades.basis: Dedicated clinical study in growing children with CAH; single report.

aromatase_inhibitor_anastrozole.human_evidence_note: Randomised head-to-head trial against letrozole with predicted adult height as primary outcome, plus attained-height cohorts in ISS and in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
aromatase_inhibitor_anastrozole.translation_risk_reason: All evidence is human interventional or matched-cohort. The chief limitation is that the randomised evidence uses predicted rather than attained adult height.
localization: human growth plate: acts by lowering oestrogen available for the fusion programme; no plate-level measurement in treated children

key_refs.one_line_finding: Anastrozole caused smaller hormonal and bone-age deviations than letrozole but identical change in predicted adult height.
Anastrozole+rhGH gave the highest target-height-adjusted adult height SDS (0.81 +/- 0.34) of three matched regimens.
Anastrozole improved height outcomes in growing children with 21-hydroxylase-deficiency congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

aromatase_inhibitor_letrozole.name: Letrozole
aromatase_inhibitor_letrozole.summary:
Letrozole is a non-steroidal third-generation aromatase inhibitor used off-label in boys
to block conversion of androgens to oestrogen and so delay the oestrogen-driven
epiphyseal fusion that terminates growth. It is the most direct available human
pharmacological test of the oestrogen-fusion hypothesis, and the result is a
cautionary one. In a 3-year open-label randomised trial at Stanford (n=79 pubertal boys
with idiopathic short stature, bone age <=14 y, letrozole 2.5 mg daily) letrozole
produced higher testosterone and lower oestradiol and IGF-1 than anastrozole, together
with slower growth velocity and slower bone age advance - exactly the intended
biochemical and skeletal-maturation profile. Yet the increase in predicted adult height
seen at year 1 did not persist at years 2 or 3, and the combined 3-year gain in predicted
adult height across both arms was only +1.3 cm (p=0.043). This is the clearest example
in the layer of an interim surrogate gain that does not convert. In combination with
rhGH in boys with bone age >=13 y, letrozole gave a target-height-adjusted adult height
SDS of 0.60 +/- 0.28, less than anastrozole plus rhGH at 0.81 +/- 0.34.

claim_grades.claim: Letrozole slows bone age advance and lowers oestradiol in pubertal boys.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised trial with annual hormone and bone age measurement, n=79.

claim_grades.claim: Letrozole monotherapy meaningfully increases predicted adult height in boys with ISS.
claim_grades.basis: The year-1 gain did not persist; the 3-year combined gain was +1.3 cm and the authors conclude efficacy as monotherapy may be limited.

claim_grades.claim: Letrozole combined with rhGH increases attained adult height.
claim_grades.basis: Propensity-matched single-centre cohort of 32 per arm; not randomised, and letrozole underperformed anastrozole.

aromatase_inhibitor_letrozole.human_evidence_note: A 3-year randomised head-to-head trial in 79 boys with predicted adult height as the primary outcome, plus propensity-matched adult-height cohorts.
aromatase_inhibitor_letrozole.translation_risk_reason: All data are human and interventional. The interpretive risk is endpoint-related: the randomised trial's primary outcome is PREDICTED adult height, itself a bone-age-derived surrogate, while the cohort study reports attained adult height without randomisation.
localization: human growth plate: acts indirectly by lowering local and systemic oestrogen exposure; no plate-level oestrogen measurement in treated boys

key_refs.one_line_finding: 3-year randomised trial - year-1 predicted adult height gain did not persist; combined 3-year gain only +1.3 cm.
Letrozole+rhGH adult height SDS 0.60 +/- 0.28 versus anastrozole+rhGH 0.81 +/- 0.34 and GnRHa+rhGH 0.48 +/- 0.17.
Systematic review placing aromatase inhibitors among paediatric growth-modifying hormonal therapies with moderate-to-serious risk of bias.

bisphosphonate_growth_plate.name: Bisphosphonates and the growth plate
bisphosphonate_growth_plate.summary:
Bisphosphonates bind hydroxyapatite and inhibit osteoclast-mediated resorption, and in
children they are used chiefly in osteogenesis imperfecta. Their relevance to this layer
is that they act precisely at the chondro-osseous junction, where the mineralised
cartilage template of the hypertrophic zone is normally resorbed and replaced by bone.
Blocking that resorption leaves radiographically visible metaphyseal bands - one per
cycle - which are the only routinely produced human image of drug action timed to the
growth plate. Whether this changes linear growth is not established: growth in
osteogenesis imperfecta is impaired by the underlying collagen defect, and published
growth trajectories in treated reference-centre cohorts do not isolate a bisphosphonate
effect on height from disease severity. Bone microstructure and strength changes over
one year in treated children with OI have been reported as comparable to healthy
age- and sex-matched controls. The mechanistically interesting recent observation is
combinatorial: in growing osteogenesis imperfecta mice, a CNP analogue plus a
bisphosphonate enhanced bone growth beyond either alone, implying that resorption
blockade and chondrocyte stimulation act on separable steps rather than competing.
That experiment has not been done in humans.

claim_grades.claim: Bisphosphonates deposit at the mineralising front of the hypertrophic zone and produce metaphyseal bands in growing children.
claim_grades.basis: Universally observed radiographic finding in treated children; a direct human image of drug localisation timed to the plate.

claim_grades.claim: Bisphosphonates alter linear growth in children with osteogenesis imperfecta.
claim_grades.basis: No study isolates the effect from disease severity; growth trajectory cohorts are observational and unstratified by treatment.

claim_grades.claim: Resorption blockade and CNP-mediated chondrocyte stimulation act additively on bone growth.
claim_grades.basis: Single pilot study in growing osteogenesis imperfecta mice; no human data.

bisphosphonate_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: Children receive bisphosphonates routinely and their skeletal effects are well documented, but no human study isolates the effect on linear growth.
bisphosphonate_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: The human evidence is about bone quality, not longitudinal growth; the growth-relevant combinatorial result is murine, and mice do not undergo epiphyseal fusion, so a claim about additive growth effects cannot be carried across without testing.
localization: human chondro-osseous junction: bisphosphonates concentrate in newly mineralised matrix, producing metaphyseal sclerotic bands timed to each dosing cycle

key_refs.one_line_finding: Combined CNP analogue and bisphosphonate enhanced bone growth in growing osteogenesis imperfecta mice beyond either alone.
Growth trajectories of children and adolescents with osteogenesis imperfecta at a reference centre, not stratified to isolate a bisphosphonate growth effect.
One-year bone microstructure and strength changes in children with osteogenesis imperfecta comparable to matched healthy controls.

chemotherapy_growth_plate_toxicity.name: Chemotherapy and growth plate toxicity
chemotherapy_growth_plate_toxicity.summary:
Cytotoxic chemotherapy damages the growth plate through several partly separable routes,
and childhood cancer survivorship is the human dataset in which they can be told apart.
High-dose methotrexate has direct antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects on
chondrocytes and osteoblasts and produces a recognised osteopathy; a prospective
observational cohort in juvenile idiopathic arthritis has examined its effect on growth
plate development at conventional low doses. Platinum agents such as cisplatin induce
oxidative stress, apoptosis and pro-inflammatory responses in chondrocytes in vitro.
Distinct from direct cytotoxicity are the endocrine routes: cranial and total body
irradiation produce growth hormone deficiency, and the nationwide Japanese survey of
growth hormone therapy after haematopoietic cell transplantation exists precisely because
the post-transplant plate is both hormonally deprived and directly damaged. That
combination is the reason growth hormone replacement only partially rescues these
children: an irradiated plate is a damaged effector, so restoring the systemic signal
cannot restore the response. Quantifying the split between direct plate injury and
endocrine deficiency in an individual survivor remains unsolved, and no study measures
cytotoxic drug concentration within human growth plate cartilage.

claim_grades.claim: Childhood cancer treatment causes growth failure that persists into survivorship.
claim_grades.basis: Population-scale survivorship data and the existence of dedicated GH replacement programmes after transplantation.

claim_grades.claim: Methotrexate has a direct adverse effect on growth plate development at therapeutic doses.
claim_grades.basis: A prospective observational cohort in JIA plus a narrative review of bone metabolism effects; not randomised.

claim_grades.claim: Growth hormone replacement incompletely rescues growth after irradiation because the plate itself is damaged.
claim_grades.basis: Consistent with post-transplant GH cohorts but not formally partitioned between effector damage and residual endocrine deficit.

chemotherapy_growth_plate_toxicity.human_evidence_note: Growth failure in childhood cancer survivors is documented at population scale, and a prospective cohort has examined methotrexate and growth plate development in JIA.
chemotherapy_growth_plate_toxicity.translation_risk_reason: The clinical growth failure is human and unambiguous, but the cellular mechanisms (cisplatin-induced chondrocyte apoptosis, methotrexate antiproliferation) come from in vitro and animal work, and the relative contribution of each route in a treated child has not been apportioned.
localization: human growth plate: direct cytotoxic injury to proliferative chondrocytes is the proposed mechanism for antimetabolites and platinums
human hypothalamic-pituitary axis: irradiation-induced GH deficiency is a separate and additive route to growth failure

key_refs.one_line_finding: Prospective observational cohort on methotrexate use in juvenile idiopathic arthritis and its impact on growth plate development.
Narrative review of the effects of high-dose methotrexate on bone metabolism.
Nationwide survey and longitudinal cohort of GH therapy after childhood haematopoietic cell transplantation.
Endocrine late effects of targeted and immune-based therapies in paediatric oncology.

cnp_analog_pk_challenge.name: CNP analogue pharmacokinetic challenge
cnp_analog_pk_challenge.summary: Vosoritide has a plasma half-life of 21-28 minutes; navepegritide releases CNP with a half-life of 5.3 days, roughly 300-fold longer. At their respective effective doses the two produce similar annualised growth gains (+1.57 and +1.49 cm/yr). That cross-trial similarity is CORROBORATION ONLY and is the weakest available comparative design - different cohorts, control arms, baselines and eras - so it is not the basis for any mechanistic claim here. The load-bearing evidence is within-drug and within-cohort, and it points in two directions that must both be reported. In the ACcomplisH four-arm dose-escalation (6/20/50/100 ug CNP/kg/week, single cohort) navepegritide showed a DOSE-DEPENDENT AGV improvement in which only the 100 ug arm separated from placebo (5.42 vs 4.35 cm/yr, p=0.0218) - so exposure demonstrably matters across that range and the drug is NOT saturated below its top dose. Against that, a vosoritide PK/PD analysis found that drug exposure correlated with urine cGMP, i.e. with systemic target engagement, but did NOT correlate with growth outcome within the treated cohort. Exposure therefore predicts receptor engagement but not effect, at least across the vosoritide dose range studied. The reconciling reading is a shared efficacy CEILING reached by both agents at their effective doses, with navepegritide's lower arms sitting below it - not that exposure duration is irrelevant.

claim_grades.claim: Navepegritide produces a dose-dependent increase in annualised growth velocity across 6-100 ug CNP/kg/week, with only the 100 ug arm separating from placebo.
claim_grades.basis: ACcomplisH phase 2, randomised, placebo-controlled, four dose arms in a single cohort, n=42 treated + 15 placebo.

claim_grades.claim: Within the vosoritide dose range studied, drug exposure correlates with urine cGMP but not with growth outcome.
claim_grades.basis: Single PK/PD analysis in hypochondroplasia; within-cohort but one study, and in a different indication from the pivotal achondroplasia trial.

claim_grades.claim: Vosoritide and navepegritide reach a comparable efficacy ceiling despite ~300-fold different exposure duration.
claim_grades.basis: Cross-trial comparison only: different cohorts, controls, baselines and eras. Corroborative, not primary.

claim_grades.claim: The efficacy ceiling is set downstream of NPR2 rather than by drug delivery or tolerability.
claim_grades.basis: Inference. Three mechanisms predict the same observation (H1/H2/H3 below); none has been discriminated.

cnp_analog_pk_challenge.human_evidence_note: Both pharmacokinetic profiles are human label data from patients with achondroplasia, and both efficacy estimates are from human placebo-controlled RCTs.
cnp_analog_pk_challenge.translation_risk_reason: All the numbers are human. The inference that draws them together - that similar efficacy despite dissimilar exposure implies a saturable downstream step - is a cross-trial comparison, not a randomised contrast, and is graded accordingly.
localization: human growth plate: exposure profile at the target never measured for either agent

key_refs.one_line_finding: Vosoritide mean apparent half-life 21.0-27.9 minutes, Tmax 15 min; urinary cGMP near saturation at 15 ug/kg/day.
Released CNP half-life 5.3 days, steady state after ~3 weekly doses, Cmax 36.0 pmol/L.
Vosoritide +1.57 cm/yr vs placebo (95% CI 1.22-1.93).
Navepegritide +1.49 cm/yr vs placebo (95% CI 1.05-1.93).
Pooled CNP-analogue AGV effect 1.36 cm/yr (95% CI 1.05-1.68) across 4 RCTs, n=326.
Vosoritide exposure correlated with urine cGMP but NOT with growth outcomes - within-cohort dissociation of target engagement from effect.
ACcomplisH four-arm dose escalation: dose-dependent AGV improvement, only 100 ug/kg/wk separated from placebo (5.42 vs 4.35 cm/yr, p=0.0218).

contradicts: INTERNAL TENSION: navepegritide shows a clear within-trial dose-response (ACcomplisH) while vosoritide exposure does not predict growth within its cohort (galetaki2026). Both cannot be simple exposure-response relationships over the same effective range. The most economical resolution is a shared ceiling with navepegritide sampling the sub-saturating region and vosoritide sitting at or above it - but that is inference, not measurement.

deflazacort.name: Deflazacort
deflazacort.summary:
Deflazacort is an oxazoline-derivative glucocorticoid prodrug whose active metabolite,
21-desDFZ, acts through the glucocorticoid receptor; it is approved for Duchenne muscular
dystrophy at approximately 0.9 mg/kg/day from age 2 years. It was introduced in DMD on
the claim of being bone- and growth-sparing relative to prednisone at equipotent
anti-inflammatory doses, which would make the pair a controlled human test of whether the
growth-suppressive and anti-inflammatory arms of glucocorticoid action are separable at
the receptor. The claim is only partly supported. Growth suppression remains a
recognised feature of long-term deflazacort in DMD, and joint modelling of growth and
motor function centiles in corticosteroid-treated boys shows the two travel together, so
the drug that preserves ambulation also constrains stature. The FOR-DMD trial and its
cross-trial comparison against vamorolone provide the closest thing to a controlled
contrast between glucocorticoids in this population. The FDA label carries no
growth-sparing claim, and the approval rested on a randomised, placebo- and
active-controlled study in 196 boys aged 5-15 years. Deflazacort therefore belongs in the
atlas as an incompletely successful attempt at glucocorticoid dissociation, not as a
solved one.

claim_grades.claim: Deflazacort at 0.9 mg/kg/day improves outcomes in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised, placebo- and active-controlled trial in 196 boys underpinning FDA approval.

claim_grades.claim: Deflazacort is growth-sparing relative to prednisone at equipotent doses.
claim_grades.basis: The US label makes no such claim, and growth suppression persists in treated cohorts; the comparison has not been settled by a dedicated randomised growth endpoint.

claim_grades.claim: Growth suppression and functional benefit are inseparable for classical glucocorticoids in DMD.
claim_grades.basis: Joint modelling of growth and motor function centiles shows them tracking together, but this is observational within treated boys.

deflazacort.human_evidence_note: Approved on a randomised placebo- and active-controlled trial in 196 boys, with longitudinal growth centile modelling available from corticosteroid-treated DMD cohorts.
deflazacort.translation_risk_reason: All the relevant data are human clinical trial and cohort data in DMD; the unresolved question is a comparative one within humans, not a species one.
localization: human growth plate: glucocorticoid receptor-mediated suppression of chondrocyte proliferation and of the GH-IGF-1 axis; not measured in treated boys

key_refs.one_line_finding: 0.9 mg/kg/day for DMD from age 2; prodrug acting via 21-desDFZ at the glucocorticoid receptor; no growth-sparing claim.
Joint modelling of growth and motor function centiles in corticosteroid-treated boys with DMD.
Cross-trial efficacy comparison of vamorolone against classic corticosteroids using FOR-DMD data.

estrogen_low_dose_therapy.name: Low-dose oestrogen therapy
estrogen_low_dose_therapy.summary:
Oestrogen has a biphasic action on the growth plate: at low concentrations it supports
the pubertal growth spurt, at higher and more sustained concentrations it drives
epiphyseal fusion. Low-dose oestrogen therapy exploits the first arm while trying to
avoid the second, and its main clinical arena is Turner syndrome, where the same patients
also receive rhGH. The therapeutic problem is a scheduling one that the biphasic
pharmacology creates directly: oestrogen must be introduced late enough not to truncate
the GH-driven height gain and early enough to allow normally timed puberty and bone
mineral accrual. This makes low-dose oestrogen the clearest human demonstration that
growth plate closure is a dose- and duration-dependent pharmacological endpoint rather
than a fixed developmental clock. The evidence base is dominated by protocolised
cohorts and consensus guidance rather than randomised dose-ranging: current management
reviews describe rhGH plus timed low-dose oestrogen as standard, but do not provide a
randomised comparison of oestrogen introduction ages with attained adult height as
outcome. The complementary experiment - deliberately high-dose oestrogen given to reduce
excessive height in constitutionally tall adolescents - has largely been abandoned in
practice, removing the upper arm of the dose-response from contemporary human data.

claim_grades.claim: Oestrogen acts biphasically on human linear growth, supporting the spurt at low exposure and driving fusion at higher exposure.
claim_grades.basis: Coherent with aromatase-inhibitor and oestrogen-resistance human data; not demonstrated by a dose-ranging trial with plate readouts.

claim_grades.claim: Timing of low-dose oestrogen introduction materially affects adult height in Turner syndrome.
claim_grades.basis: Guideline and cohort evidence; no randomised comparison of introduction ages with attained adult height.

estrogen_low_dose_therapy.human_evidence_note: Low-dose oestrogen with rhGH is standard, guideline-endorsed practice in Turner syndrome with published height outcomes, though not from randomised dose-ranging trials.
estrogen_low_dose_therapy.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical practice and human outcome data throughout. The biphasic concentration-response is inferred from clinical dosing behaviour and from the natural experiments of aromatase and oestrogen receptor deficiency rather than from a dose-ranging trial.
localization: human growth plate: oestrogen receptor alpha in chondrocytes is the presumed mediator of both the spurt and fusion; not measured in treated patients

key_refs.one_line_finding: Current clinical approach to Turner syndrome including rhGH plus timed low-dose oestrogen and the timing trade-off.
rhGH is licensed to improve adult height in Turner syndrome, the population in which oestrogen timing is managed.

fgfr3_tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor.name: FGFR3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor class
fgfr3_tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor.summary:
FGFR3 tyrosine kinase inhibitors are ATP-competitive small molecules repurposed from
oncology to reduce the constitutive kinase output of mutant FGFR3. Infigratinib is the
only member with a positive phase 3 result in achondroplasia; TYRA-300 is an
FGFR3-selective agent with mouse efficacy only. The class rests on a premise the human
genetics does not support: that phenotype severity tracks kinase output monotonically.
FGFR3 K650M (SADDAN) has roughly three times the constitutive kinase activity of the
lethal K650E (thanatophoric dysplasia type II) yet is survivable, so reducing kinase
output is not by itself predictive of benefit. The pharmacology makes the same point
from the other side: in a radiometric kinase panel infigratinib inhibits wild-type
FGFR3 at IC50 0.66 nM and K650E at 0.5 nM but K650M at 44.4 nM - an ~89-fold loss of
potency against the allele with the higher kinase activity - and 505.9 nM against the
V555M gatekeeper mutant. Potency is therefore allele-specific in a way that does not
parallel severity. Class-wide, selectivity is the limiting problem: pan-FGFR inhibition
reduced male trabecular bone in mice, and chronic kinase inhibition in children is the
same manoeuvre that causes growth failure when TKIs are used in paediatric leukaemia.

claim_grades.claim: Infigratinib inhibits FGFR3 K650M ~89-fold less potently than K650E in a radiometric kinase assay.
claim_grades.basis: Single biochemical panel, ATP concentration not stated for these values; not independently replicated.

claim_grades.claim: FGFR3 phenotype severity is not monotonic in constitutive kinase activity.
claim_grades.basis: K650M has ~3x the activity of the lethal K650E yet is survivable (Tavormina 1999); replicated by the graded Lys650 allelic series.

claim_grades.claim: Reducing FGFR3 kinase output increases growth velocity in achondroplasia.
claim_grades.basis: Phase 3 RCT of infigratinib, n=114, +1.74 cm/yr vs placebo.

fgfr3_tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor.human_evidence_note: One class member, infigratinib, has a completed placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in children with achondroplasia; the kinase potency data are biochemical.
fgfr3_tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor.translation_risk_reason: Human efficacy exists for one agent, but the class rationale, the allele-selectivity data and the skeletal safety signals are biochemical and murine. Chronic pan-FGFR inhibition in a growing child has no long-term human safety dataset in a non-malignant indication, and the closest human analogue - paediatric TKI exposure in CML - reduces final height.
localization: human growth plate: no measurement of intraplate TKI concentration for any member of the class

key_refs.one_line_finding: Kinase panel giving infigratinib IC50 0.66 nM wild-type, 0.5 nM K650E, 44.4 nM K650M, 505.9 nM V555M.
Discovery and selectivity optimisation of NVP-BGJ398 (infigratinib) as an FGFR1-3 inhibitor.
SADDAN K650M has ~3x the constitutive activity of the lethal K650E allele yet is non-lethal.
FGFR3-selective TYRA-300 increased long bone length and foramen magnum size in two Fgfr3 mouse models.
Infigratinib lengthened femora and the proliferative zone in Aga2/+ mice but reduced male trabecular bone - a class selectivity cost.
Curated FGFR3 potency series including an ATP=Km mobility-shift IC50 of 1.0 nM.

contradicts: ALLELE MISMATCH: published FGFR3-inhibitor potency data are on kinase-domain alleles (K650E, K650M, N540K). The clinical achondroplasia target is the transmembrane G380R. Whether potency rank order transfers across activation mechanism is untested - see g_mr002_allele.

final_adult_height_endpoint.name: Final adult height as a trial endpoint
final_adult_height_endpoint.summary:
Final adult height is the only endpoint in this layer that cannot be gamed by
redistribution: it integrates everything the growth plate did before it closed. It is
also the endpoint almost no growth-promoting drug programme has reached. Across the
whole layer, attained final or near-adult height has been reported for GnRH agonists in
central precocious puberty (+3.5 to +4.5 cm), androgens in constitutional delay
(+1.78 cm, 95% CI 0.47-3.08), rhIGF-1 in severe primary IGF-1 deficiency (+0.9 height
SDS, 1.4 in treatment-naive prepubertal patients), aromatase inhibitors with rhGH in
ISS boys, and - as a negative - inhaled budesonide (-1.2 cm, 95% CI -1.9 to -0.5). It
has not been reported for any CNP analogue, for any FGFR3 inhibitor, or for any
long-acting growth hormone. The two categories must be kept apart in this atlas. Where
attained height is available, the interventions cluster at 1-4 cm, an order of magnitude
smaller than the cumulative integral of the velocity gains that preceded them. That
systematic shrinkage - most starkly in the aromatase inhibitor trial where a year-1
predicted-height gain vanished by years 2-3 - is the strongest available evidence that
the growth plate has a largely fixed total elongation capacity that pharmacology
redistributes in time more readily than it expands.

claim_grades.claim: Interventions with attained-height data cluster at 1-4 cm of gain.
claim_grades.basis: Direct comparison of the meta-analytic and registry estimates listed above.

claim_grades.claim: No CNP analogue or FGFR3 inhibitor has reported attained final or near-adult height.
claim_grades.basis: Established by search across Europe PMC and ClinicalTrials.gov; the relevant extensions are registered as active.

claim_grades.claim: Adult height gains are systematically smaller than the cumulative integral of the velocity gains that produced them.
claim_grades.basis: Consistent across the interventions with both measures - most clearly the aromatase inhibitor trial where a year-1 predicted gain did not persist - but no intervention has both a velocity integral and an attained height measured in the same cohort with a control arm.

final_adult_height_endpoint.human_evidence_note: Attained final or near-adult height has been measured in randomised trials, registries and meta-analyses for several interventions in this layer, and not at all for others.
final_adult_height_endpoint.translation_risk_reason: A human endpoint with no animal counterpart - mice do not undergo epiphyseal fusion, so final adult height cannot be modelled in the standard preclinical species at all.
localization: not applicable: whole-organism endpoint

key_refs.one_line_finding: GnRHa final adult height +3.5 to +4.5 cm across 20 studies, 21,812 participants.
Androgen therapy in constitutional delay +1.78 cm final adult height (95% CI 0.47-3.08).
rhIGF-1 near-adult height gain 0.9 HtSDS in 102 registry patients.
The only randomised trial in this layer with attained adult height as the endpoint - and it measures a loss, not a gain.
Year-1 predicted adult height gain did not persist to years 2-3 - the clearest documented non-conversion of an interim gain.
The FGFR3-inhibitor extension registered as the designed route to final height data, not yet reporting.

glucocorticoid_sparing_strategy.name: Glucocorticoid-sparing strategies for growth
glucocorticoid_sparing_strategy.summary:
The central pharmacological question raised by chronic glucocorticoid therapy in children
is whether the anti-inflammatory transrepression arm of glucocorticoid receptor signalling
can be separated from the transactivation arm that suppresses growth and bone. Three
strategies have been tried in humans. First, alternative classical steroids: deflazacort
was introduced with a bone- and growth-sparing rationale that its US label does not
support. Second, route and schedule modification: inhaled rather than systemic delivery
in asthma, which the CAMP adult-height result shows reduces but does not abolish the
height cost (-1.2 cm of adult height at budesonide 400 ug/day). Third, and most directly,
dissociative agents: vamorolone is a structurally modified steroid designed to retain
anti-inflammatory activity while reducing growth suppression and bone loss, now compared
with prednisone and deflazacort through cross-trial analysis of FOR-DMD, with real-world
criteria published for transitioning patients to it. The strategy space is therefore
moving from dose reduction toward receptor-level dissociation, but no agent has yet
demonstrated preserved anti-inflammatory efficacy with a randomised adult-height endpoint,
and CAMP remains the only glucocorticoid study in any indication that measured attained
adult height.

claim_grades.claim: Changing the route of glucocorticoid administration reduces but does not abolish the adult-height cost.
claim_grades.basis: CAMP randomised trial with attained adult height in 943 participants.

claim_grades.claim: Dissociative steroids such as vamorolone retain anti-inflammatory efficacy with less growth suppression.
claim_grades.basis: Supported by cross-trial comparison against FOR-DMD corticosteroid arms and by real-world transition criteria; not by a randomised head-to-head with a growth endpoint.

claim_grades.claim: Glucocorticoid transactivation and transrepression are pharmacologically separable at the human growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Flagged inference from receptor biology; no human plate-level demonstration exists.

glucocorticoid_sparing_strategy.human_evidence_note: Each strategy has human trial data - CAMP for the inhaled route, FOR-DMD and its vamorolone cross-trial comparison for dissociative steroids - but none with an adult-height endpoint except CAMP.
glucocorticoid_sparing_strategy.translation_risk_reason: Human trials throughout. The receptor-level dissociation rationale is derived from transactivation/transrepression biology in cells and is asserted rather than demonstrated in the treated human plate.
localization: human growth plate: glucocorticoid receptor transactivation is the proposed growth-suppressive arm; the dissociation has never been demonstrated at the plate in humans

key_refs.one_line_finding: Inhaled budesonide still cost 1.2 cm of adult height - route change reduces but does not remove the effect.
Vamorolone compared with prednisone and deflazacort through cross-trial analysis of FOR-DMD.
Deflazacort's approved label carries no growth-sparing claim, so the earliest sparing strategy is unsupported at the regulatory level.
Growth and motor function centiles track together in corticosteroid-treated DMD, quantifying the cost side of the trade-off.

gnrh_analog_leuprolide.name: Leuprolide acetate
gnrh_analog_leuprolide.summary:
Leuprolide acetate is a GnRH agonist that, given continuously as a depot, desensitises
pituitary gonadotrophs and shuts down gonadal sex steroid production. In central
precocious puberty it is used to remove the sex-steroid drive to skeletal maturation and
so preserve growth potential that would otherwise be spent early. It is therefore a
human loss-of-function experiment on the sex-steroid arm of growth plate senescence, run
at scale. The height result is real but modest: across a systematic review of 20 studies
and 21,812 participants, GnRH agonist therapy improved final adult height by +3.5 to
+4.5 cm and slowed bone age advancement by 0.6-1.3 years. In boys with central precocious
puberty treated for a mean 2.7 +/- 1.3 years, final adult height exceeded target height
by only 1.2 +/- 5.9 cm (p=0.047) and predicted adult height rose by 1.3 +/- 4.9 cm
(p=0.012) - statistically detectable, but with a standard deviation four times the mean
effect, so the individual response is close to unpredictable. Population pharmacokinetic
work now justifies fixed rather than weight-based dosing, which is itself evidence that
the exposure-response relationship at the plate is flat over the clinical range.

claim_grades.claim: GnRH agonist therapy increases final adult height in central precocious puberty by roughly 3.5-4.5 cm.
claim_grades.basis: Systematic review of 20 studies, 21,812 participants, with attained final height.

claim_grades.claim: The individual height response is highly variable and only weakly predictable.
claim_grades.basis: In boys, final height exceeded target by 1.2 +/- 5.9 cm - the SD dwarfs the mean.

claim_grades.claim: The height benefit is produced by delaying oestrogen-driven growth plate senescence rather than by any direct plate action.
claim_grades.basis: Mechanistically coherent with the bone-age slowing measured in the same cohorts, but not separable from other consequences of gonadal suppression in humans.

gnrh_analog_leuprolide.human_evidence_note: Tens of thousands of treated children, with attained final adult height reported in multiple cohorts and pooled in a systematic review.
gnrh_analog_leuprolide.translation_risk_reason: Entirely human. The residual risk is confounding by indication - treated children are selected for advanced puberty - since randomised withholding of therapy is not ethical.
localization: human pituitary gonadotroph: site of action
human growth plate: no direct drug action; effect is removal of sex steroid input to the fusion programme

key_refs.one_line_finding: GnRHa improved final adult height +3.5 to +4.5 cm and reduced bone age advancement 0.6-1.3 years.
92 boys with CPP - final adult height exceeded target height by only 1.2 +/- 5.9 cm.
Population pharmacokinetic justification for fixed rather than weight-based leuprolide dosing in children.
Head-to-head comparison of 3-monthly leuprolide acetate versus triptorelin pamoate in central precocious puberty.

gnrh_analog_triptorelin.name: Triptorelin
gnrh_analog_triptorelin.summary:
Triptorelin pamoate is a depot GnRH agonist used interchangeably with leuprolide acetate
to suppress central precocious puberty. Because the two drugs share a mechanism but
differ in peptide sequence, depot formulation and release kinetics, head-to-head studies
are a controlled test of whether the growth plate cares about the shape of gonadotrophin
suppression or only about its completeness. Direct comparisons at 3-monthly dosing find
comparable suppression and comparable growth outcomes, and a comparison in overweight and
obese girls likewise found the two effective. Quarterly versus monthly triptorelin has
also been compared over 12 months in Chinese girls without a signal that the less
frequent schedule is inferior. The consistent picture across formulations is that within
the range that achieves gonadotrophin suppression, the height outcome is insensitive to
the dosing schedule - the same pattern seen with CNP analogues and with long-acting
growth hormone, and evidence that these endocrine interventions operate at the top of a
saturating exposure-response curve. Final adult height data specific to triptorelin, as
opposed to the GnRH agonist class, remain sparse.

claim_grades.claim: Triptorelin suppresses central puberty as effectively as leuprolide at equivalent dosing intervals.
claim_grades.basis: Direct comparative studies at 3-monthly dosing, but not formally powered equivalence trials.

claim_grades.claim: Height outcome is insensitive to GnRH agonist dosing schedule once suppression is achieved.
claim_grades.basis: Consistent across quarterly-versus-monthly and agent-versus-agent comparisons, all of which are observational and use interim endpoints.

claim_grades.claim: Triptorelin specifically increases final adult height.
claim_grades.basis: Inherited from class-level pooled data; triptorelin-specific attained-height cohorts are sparse.

gnrh_analog_triptorelin.human_evidence_note: Multiple comparative clinical studies in children with central precocious puberty, including head-to-head against leuprolide and quarterly-versus-monthly dosing.
gnrh_analog_triptorelin.translation_risk_reason: All human. The interpretive limit is that most triptorelin studies report interim auxology and bone age rather than attained adult height.
localization: human pituitary gonadotroph: site of action
human growth plate: no direct action; effect is mediated entirely by withdrawal of gonadal sex steroids

key_refs.one_line_finding: 3-monthly leuprolide acetate and triptorelin pamoate compared directly for central precocious puberty.
Class-level GnRHa final adult height gain +3.5 to +4.5 cm; agents not disaggregated.

growth_plate_drug_exposure.name: Drug exposure at the growth plate
growth_plate_drug_exposure.summary: Not one of the twelve audited growth-promoting agents has a published growth plate tissue concentration in any species. Every dose-selection rationale in this field therefore rests on plasma exposure as a surrogate for exposure at an avascular, alymphatic, diffusion-limited tissue, and the validity of that surrogate has never been measured for any of them. This is not a limitation of technique. The drug-delivery literature measures growth-plate accumulation routinely: chondrocyte-membrane-coated nanoparticles bearing the collagen-II-binding peptide WYRGRL demonstrably delivered purmorphamine into growth plate cartilage in a hypochondroplasia mouse model, and a collagen-binding-domain CNP fusion was shown to localise to cartilage in fetal murine tibiae. Both papers open by naming the avascular and alymphatic character of the plate as the delivery problem they exist to solve. So the measurement is feasible, is being done, and is simply not being done for the approved therapeutics at clinical doses. That makes this an unasked question rather than a blocked one - a materially more damning position, because nothing but attention is missing. The same delivery literature independently names hypotension as the liability of systemic CNP distribution, which is direct support for the tolerability-cap hypothesis competing to explain the exposure-duration observation.

claim_grades.claim: No approved or investigational growth-promoting agent has a published growth plate tissue concentration in any species.
claim_grades.basis: Systematic audit of 12 agents plus three targeted follow-up searches; a null established by search, not assumed.

claim_grades.claim: Measuring drug concentration in growth plate cartilage is technically feasible and is performed in the drug-delivery literature.
claim_grades.basis: Two independent 2026 mouse studies demonstrate targeted delivery into growth plate / cartilage with localisation readouts.

claim_grades.claim: Plasma exposure is therefore an unvalidated surrogate for exposure at the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Follows from the two claims above; the surrogate is universally used and its validity is unmeasured.

growth_plate_drug_exposure.human_evidence_note: No human study reports a drug concentration measured within growth plate cartilage; all human exposure data in this layer are plasma.
growth_plate_drug_exposure.translation_risk_reason: Rodent growth plates are thin enough that diffusion limitation may be negligible, so even a positive animal delivery result would not transfer to the much thicker human plate. Any measurement that matters has to be made in a large-animal or human plate.
localization: human growth plate: avascular, diffusion-fed from epiphyseal and metaphyseal vascular fronts; no measured drug concentration-versus-depth profile for any agent
human metaphysis: bisphosphonate deposition at the mineralising front is radiographically visible, the only routine human image of drug arrival at the plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: Retinoid-impregnated nanoparticles achieved site-specific modulation of endochondral ossification in mice - a direct attempt to solve plate delivery rather than assume it.
Full plasma PK for vosoritide with no tissue distribution data for the target organ.
Full plasma PK for navepegritide and released CNP with no tissue distribution data for the target organ.
Recifercept failed at every dose with no tissue exposure measurement, leaving mechanism failure and delivery failure indistinguishable.
Cartilage-targeting nanoparticles delivered purmorphamine into growth plate cartilage in an HCH mouse model; opens by naming avascular/alymphatic delivery limits.
Collagen-binding-domain CNP localised to cartilage in fetal murine tibiae; names hypotension as the liability of systemic CNP distribution.

igf1_gh_combination_therapy.name: Combined rhGH plus rhIGF-1 therapy
igf1_gh_combination_therapy.summary:
Giving recombinant GH and recombinant IGF-1 together is the direct human test of whether
the growth plate responds to GH and to IGF-1 through separable mechanisms, or whether
IGF-1 is simply GH's messenger. If IGF-1 were purely downstream, adding it to a full GH
dose should add nothing. A six-year randomised, multicentre, open-label dose-selection
trial (NCT00572156, n=106) tested rhGH 45 ug/kg/day alone against rhGH 45 plus rhIGF-1 at
50, 100 or 150 ug/kg/day in children with short stature and IGF-1 deficiency. The posted
year-1 mean height velocities were 9.3 cm/yr (SD 1.7) for rhGH alone, 10.1 (1.3) with
50 ug/kg rhIGF-1, 9.7 (2.5) with 100 and 11.2 (2.1) with 150 - a dose-related increment
of roughly 1-2 cm/yr over GH alone, non-monotonic across the middle dose. The same rank
order persisted at years 2-4 with the gaps narrowing (year 4: 7.7 vs 8.1, 8.4, 8.3 cm/yr).
The trial was then terminated for "strategic reasons", so it never reached the adult
height endpoint it was designed for. The combination therefore shows a real but
diminishing incremental effect that was never converted into a height outcome, and the
clean answer to the separability question was lost to a commercial decision rather than
to biology.

claim_grades.claim: Adding rhIGF-1 to a full rhGH dose increases first-year height velocity by roughly 1-2 cm/yr.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised open-label multi-arm trial with posted results, n=106, but non-monotonic across doses and no confidence intervals posted.

claim_grades.claim: The incremental effect of added rhIGF-1 wanes with continued treatment.
claim_grades.basis: Between-arm spread narrows from ~1.9 cm/yr at year 1 to ~0.7 cm/yr at year 4 in the posted data; not formally tested for interaction.

claim_grades.claim: Combination therapy increases adult height.
claim_grades.basis: The trial was designed to answer this over six years and was terminated for strategic reasons; no adult-height data exist.

igf1_gh_combination_therapy.human_evidence_note: A randomised multi-arm dose-selection trial in 106 children with posted height-velocity results by arm and year.
igf1_gh_combination_therapy.translation_risk_reason: Entirely human data. The unresolved part is not species translation but early termination: velocity was measured for four years and adult height never.
localization: human growth plate: both agents presumed to act on chondrocytes; no tissue-level partition measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Six-year randomised trial TERMINATED for strategic reasons; posted year-1 HV 9.3 / 10.1 / 9.7 / 11.2 cm/yr across GH-alone and three combination arms.
rhIGF-1 monotherapy near-adult height data against which any combination benefit would have to be judged.
Systematic review of paediatric hormonal growth therapies; combination GH/IGF-1 does not appear among established regimens.

igf1_gh_combination_therapy.termination_note: NCT00572156, a 6-year GH+IGF-1 trial, terminated for "strategic reasons" while posting year-1 height velocities of 9.3/10.1/9.7/11.2 cm/yr. NOT evidence about biology - a 6-year dataset with positive interim signal exists and appears unanalysed for this question. P1 access item.

infigratinib_growth.name: Infigratinib
infigratinib_growth.summary:
Infigratinib is an orally bioavailable ATP-competitive FGFR1-3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor,
originally an oncology compound, repositioned to achondroplasia at a dose roughly two
orders of magnitude below its oncology exposure. In the 52-week phase 3 trial
(NCT06164951, n=114 randomised 2:1, ages 3-17 y, 0.25 mg/kg once daily by mouth) the
least-squares mean difference from placebo in annualised height velocity was
1.74 cm/yr (95% CI 1.31-2.17, p<0.001), with height z-score difference 0.32
(96% CI 0.23-0.41). It is the first oral agent and the first upstream agent to show
this, and the point estimate is numerically larger than the CNP analogues, though no
head-to-head trial exists. Two things are unresolved. Potency against achondroplasia's
own G380R allele in a stated-ATP kinase assay is not published alongside the clinical
programme, and the published mutant panel shows potency does not track severity:
K650E IC50 0.5 nM versus K650M 44.4 nM. And the extension to hypochondroplasia is
actively contested - one group reports potent inhibition of hypochondroplasia-associated
variants and mouse efficacy, another reports that infigratinib is a weak inhibitor of
the FGFR3-N540K hypochondroplasia mutant. No final adult height data exist; the
long-term extension (NCT05145010) is the designed route to them. ALLELE CAVEAT, load-bearing: the potency figures above were measured against KINASE-DOMAIN alleles (K650E, K650M), and the low-dose efficacy work is in hypochondroplasia (N540K, also kinase-domain). Achondroplasia is caused by G380R, a TRANSMEMBRANE-domain variant that activates the receptor by a different mechanism. Potency measured on kinase-domain alleles does not automatically govern the clinical case, and no IC50 against G380R-activated FGFR3 was located in the literature. The non-monotonicity argument against 'lower kinase output equals benefit' is well supported for kinase-domain alleles and UNTESTED for G380R.

claim_grades.claim: Infigratinib is 89-fold less potent against FGFR3 K650M (IC50 44.4 nM) than against K650E (IC50 0.5 nM), despite K650M carrying ~3x the constitutive kinase activity.
claim_grades.basis: In-vitro kinase/cell potency against KINASE-DOMAIN alleles. Replicated in vitro; no human data at these alleles.

claim_grades.claim: Inhibitor potency therefore does not track constitutive kinase activity across the FGFR3 kinase-domain allelic series, so "reduce kinase output" is not a sufficient design rule for those alleles.
claim_grades.basis: Follows from the potency data above; established only for kinase-domain alleles.

claim_grades.claim: That same non-monotonicity governs the CLINICAL target allele in achondroplasia, G380R.
claim_grades.basis: UNTESTED INFERENCE. G380R is a TRANSMEMBRANE-domain activating variant with a different activation mechanism (altered receptor dimerisation/downregulation), not a kinase-domain change. No published IC50 against G380R-activated FGFR3 was located. See g_mr002_allele.

claim_grades.claim: Infigratinib increases growth velocity in children with achondroplasia.
claim_grades.basis: Clinical trial evidence in the G380R population, independent of the in-vitro allele question.

infigratinib_growth.human_evidence_note: Completed multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in 114 children with achondroplasia with a prespecified annualised height velocity endpoint.
infigratinib_growth.translation_risk_reason: The efficacy claim is human and randomised. Translation risk attaches instead to the extension claims - hypochondroplasia and osteogenesis imperfecta - which rest on mouse and in vitro data and are contradicted in the hypochondroplasia case.
localization: human growth plate: presumed site of action; intraplate drug concentration unmeasured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Phase 3, n=114, +1.74 cm/yr annualised height velocity vs placebo (95% CI 1.31-2.17).
Registry record for the completed phase 3 programme.
Phase 2 dose escalation (n=84) that selected 0.25 mg/kg/day.
Claims in silico, in vitro and Fgfr3-N534K/+ mouse support for infigratinib in hypochondroplasia.
Reports infigratinib is a WEAK inhibitor of the FGFR3-N540K hypochondroplasia mutant.
Infigratinib IC50 0.5 nM on K650E but 44.4 nM on K650M - potency does not track allele severity.

inhaled_corticosteroid_growth.name: Inhaled corticosteroids and adult height
inhaled_corticosteroid_growth.summary:
Inhaled corticosteroids are the definitive human experiment on whether a transient
glucocorticoid-induced slowing of growth velocity is recovered. The Childhood Asthma
Management Program randomised children aged 5-13 years to budesonide 400 ug/day,
nedocromil, or placebo for 4-6 years and then measured adult height in 943 of 1041
participants (90.6%) at a mean age of 24.9 +/- 2.7 years. Mean adult height was 1.2 cm
lower in the budesonide group than placebo (95% CI -1.9 to -0.5, p=0.001); nedocromil
showed no effect (-0.2 cm, 95% CI -0.9 to 0.5). Three features make this the most
informative dataset in the layer. First, the adult deficit (-1.2 cm) is essentially
identical to the deficit already present after two years of treatment (-1.3 cm, 95% CI
-1.7 to -0.9), so the loss was incurred early and was neither recovered nor compounded.
Second, it was dose-dependent: -0.1 cm of adult height per ug/kg/day of inhaled
glucocorticoid in the first two years (p=0.007). Third, the velocity reduction occurred
primarily in prepubertal participants, identifying a window of susceptibility. The
general lesson - that a growth velocity deficit becomes a permanent height deficit
unless catch-up occurs - is the mirror image of the unresolved question for every
growth-promoting agent in this layer.

claim_grades.claim: Inhaled budesonide 400 ug/day in childhood reduces adult height by about 1.2 cm.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised trial, n=943 with adult height, 90.6% follow-up, adjusted analysis.

claim_grades.claim: The deficit is incurred within the first two years of treatment and is neither recovered nor progressive.
claim_grades.basis: The 2-year deficit (-1.3 cm) and the adult deficit (-1.2 cm) coincide within their confidence intervals.

claim_grades.claim: Prepubertal children are the susceptible group.
claim_grades.basis: Reported within the trial as the subgroup in which velocity fell; a subgroup observation rather than a prespecified test.

inhaled_corticosteroid_growth.human_evidence_note: Randomised controlled trial with 90.6% follow-up to attained adult height at a mean age of nearly 25 years - the longest and most complete growth follow-up in this layer.
inhaled_corticosteroid_growth.translation_risk_reason: Human randomised trial with a human adult-height endpoint.
localization: human growth plate: glucocorticoid receptor-mediated suppression presumed; no plate measurement in treated children

key_refs.one_line_finding: CAMP adult height - budesonide -1.2 cm (95% CI -1.9 to -0.5), deficit set in the first 2 years, not progressive.
Registry record for the CAMP trial underlying the adult-height analysis.

limb_lengthening_surgery.name: Surgical limb lengthening
limb_lengthening_surgery.summary:
Distraction osteogenesis lengthens a bone by osteotomy followed by gradual separation of
the fragments, so that new bone forms in the distraction gap by a regenerate mechanism
that is intramembranous rather than endochondral. It is included in this layer as the
quantitative benchmark against which every pharmacological effect must be judged: it is
the only intervention that produces large, certain height gains, and it does so without
using the growth plate at all. A meta-analysis of 14 studies and 1149 patients with
achondroplasia gives pooled mean gains of 8.85 cm at the femur (95% CI 7.42-10.28),
7.36 cm at the tibia (95% CI 6.21-8.52) and 8.38 cm at the humerus (95% CI 7.01-9.74),
with a fixator index of 37.1 days/cm (95% CI 32.37-41.82) and a mean fixation duration
of 7.71 months. The cost is a pooled complication rate of 56.1% (95% CI 26.9-85.2), and
quality of life scores are only moderately improved (pooled PedsQL 75.69). Set against
drug effects of 1.4-1.7 cm/yr of velocity with no confirmed adult-height gain, surgery
is one to two orders of magnitude more effective per intervention and one to two orders
of magnitude more harmful. The two are now used together, and CNP analogues may alter
callus consolidation and medullary canal geometry, so the interaction is a live surgical
question rather than a hypothetical one.

claim_grades.claim: Limb lengthening produces 7-9 cm of segmental gain per treated bone in achondroplasia.
claim_grades.basis: Pooled meta-analysis of 1149 patients with narrow confidence intervals on the length outcomes.

claim_grades.claim: The complication rate is above 50%.
claim_grades.basis: Pooled estimate 56.1% but with a 95% CI from 26.9 to 85.2, reflecting inconsistent complication definitions across studies.

claim_grades.claim: CNP analogues alter bone healing and callus consolidation during lengthening.
claim_grades.basis: Based on animal fracture-healing data and reviewer synthesis; not demonstrated in treated patients undergoing lengthening.

limb_lengthening_surgery.human_evidence_note: Meta-analysis of 14 studies and 1149 patients with achondroplasia reporting attained length gains, fixation times, complications and quality of life.
limb_lengthening_surgery.translation_risk_reason: A human surgical intervention with human outcome data throughout.
localization: human diaphysis/metaphysis: regenerate bone forms in the distraction gap by intramembranous ossification, bypassing the growth plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: 14 studies, 1149 patients - femoral 8.85 cm, tibial 7.36 cm, humeral 8.38 cm gains; 56.1% complication rate.
CNP analogues may affect bone density, callus consolidation and medullary canal area, with implications for lengthening surgery.
Contemporary achondroplasia management guidance covering the coexistence of surgical and pharmacological growth strategies.

mecasermin_igf1.name: Mecasermin (recombinant human IGF-1)
mecasermin_igf1.summary:
Mecasermin is recombinant human IGF-1 given twice daily subcutaneously, and it is the
only way to test in humans what IGF-1 does to the growth plate when the GH signal
upstream of it is broken. It is licensed narrowly: growth failure in children aged 2 y
and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, defined by the FDA label as height SDS
<= -3.0 AND basal IGF-1 SDS <= -3.0 AND normal or elevated GH, or with GH gene deletion
plus neutralising anti-GH antibodies. Dosing is 0.04-0.08 mg/kg twice daily, escalating
