to a maximum of 0.12 mg/kg twice daily, with hypoglycaemia the dose-limiting toxicity.
The near-adult height data are the informative part: in 102 registry patients reaching
near-adult height (mean age at start 11.8 y, median treatment 3.9 y) the mean height SDS
gain was 0.9 (SD 1.1), rising to 1.4 (SD 1.0) in treatment-naive prepubertal patients,
of whom almost half reached near-adult height within the normal range. In Laron syndrome
only 10.5% reached the normal range. IGF-1 replacement therefore restores a substantial
but incomplete fraction of growth, and the gap is largest where GH signalling is
completely absent - consistent with a GH contribution to the plate that IGF-1 does not
reproduce. The evidence base has also been limited by supply rather than biology: the
IGFD registry was terminated because of an Increlex shortage.

claim_grades.claim: rhIGF-1 raises near-adult height in severe primary IGF-1 deficiency by about 0.9 height SDS, and 1.4 SDS if started prepubertally and treatment-naive.
claim_grades.basis: Registry of 102 patients reaching near-adult height, with prespecified subgroups and linear regression on predictors.

claim_grades.claim: IGF-1 replacement alone does not fully substitute for GH action on the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Only 10.5% of Laron patients reached the normal range despite improvement; confounded by late treatment start, so not a clean test.

claim_grades.claim: rhIGF-1 acts directly on growth plate chondrocytes via IGF1R.
claim_grades.basis: Stated in the FDA label from receptor biology; no human plate measurement.

mecasermin_igf1.human_evidence_note: Licensed on paediatric growth data, with a global registry reporting near-adult height in 102 treated patients and independent long-term cohorts.
mecasermin_igf1.translation_risk_reason: Efficacy, dosing and adult-height outcome are all human. Mechanistic attribution to a direct chondrocyte action is asserted in the label rather than measured in treated patients.
localization: human growth plate: acts on the type 1 IGF-1 receptor on chondrocytes per the FDA label; no zonal data in treated humans

key_refs.one_line_finding: 102 registry patients at near-adult height gained 0.9 HtSDS (1.4 if naive prepubertal); only 10.5% of Laron patients reached the normal range.
Narrow indication (height SDS <=-3.0 and IGF-1 SDS <=-3.0 with normal/elevated GH); 0.04-0.12 mg/kg twice daily.
22-year single-centre cohort of 28 patients with GH insensitivity treated with IGF-1 at 40-120 ug/kg twice daily.
European real-world data on rhIGF-1 in severe primary IGF-I deficiency.
IGFD registry TERMINATED because of an Increlex supply shortage - a manufacturing, not scientific, limit on the evidence.

mecasermin_igf1.termination_note: The IGF-1 deficiency registry NCT00747604 was terminated for Increlex SUPPLY SHORTAGE. No evidential content about efficacy whatsoever; must never be cited as a negative result.

mecasermin_rinfabate.name: Mecasermin rinfabate (rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 complex)
mecasermin_rinfabate.summary:
Mecasermin rinfabate is recombinant IGF-1 pre-complexed 1:1 with recombinant IGFBP-3.
The design rationale is pharmacokinetic and directly relevant to the growth plate: free
IGF-1 has a half-life of minutes and causes hypoglycaemia, whereas binary complex with
IGFBP-3 extends the circulating half-life and buffers acute insulin-like effects,
permitting once-daily rather than twice-daily dosing. It was approved in the US in the
mid-2000s for severe primary IGF-1 deficiency and then withdrawn from that indication;
the surviving literature on the complex is almost entirely about other diseases
(myotonic dystrophy type 1, and now bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm neonates as
OHB-607). A systematic search finds no cohort reporting adult or near-adult height in
children treated with the complex for short stature. This node is therefore a record of
a growth-plate pharmacological probe that was built, licensed and then lost for
non-scientific reasons, leaving the central question - whether buffering free IGF-1 with
its binding protein changes the growth response or only the hypoglycaemia risk -
unanswered in humans.

claim_grades.claim: Complexing IGF-1 with IGFBP-3 extends its circulating half-life and permits once-daily dosing.
claim_grades.basis: Formulation rationale supported by pharmacokinetic reasoning and contemporaneous review; the underlying human PK comparison is not retrievable.

claim_grades.claim: Mecasermin rinfabate improves adult height in children with IGF-1 deficiency.
claim_grades.basis: Widely asserted in the historical literature but traceable to no published adult-height cohort; see gap g_l12b_012.

mecasermin_rinfabate.human_evidence_note: The compound was licensed on paediatric growth-failure data but the primary efficacy reports are not retrievable through the current indexed literature and no adult-height cohort was ever published.
mecasermin_rinfabate.translation_risk_reason: There is no current human growth dataset to translate from or to. Contemporary development of the same molecule is in preterm neonatal lung disease, where the endpoint is not linear growth at all.
localization: human growth plate: no data; the complex was never studied with a growth plate readout

key_refs.one_line_finding: Contemporaneous appraisal of the efficacy and safety of mecasermin rinfabate around its short-lived approval.
The surviving IGF-1 product is uncomplexed mecasermin dosed twice daily - the complexed alternative is absent from current labelling.

meclizine_repurposing.name: Meclizine repurposing for achondroplasia
meclizine_repurposing.summary:
Meclizine is an over-the-counter H1 antihistamine for motion sickness, identified by
drug repositioning screening as an inhibitor of FGFR3 signalling. It has the best
human pharmacokinetic characterisation of any repurposed achondroplasia candidate and
the weakest efficacy signal. A 14-day repeat-dose phase 1b in 12 children with
achondroplasia aged 5-10 y gave, at 12.5 mg/day, Cmax 167 ng/mL (95% CI 83-250),
Tmax 3.7 h, AUC0-24 1170 ng*h/mL and terminal half-life 7.4 h, with no serious adverse
events. The 26-week open-label single-arm phase 2 in nine children, meclizine 12.5-25
mg/day co-administered with growth hormone, moved height velocity from 4.35 +/- 1.36 to
4.46 +/- 1.54 cm/yr - a change of about 0.1 cm/yr with only one of nine children
reaching the 6 cm/yr threshold. Arm span velocity was 6.93 +/- 2.50 cm/yr with six of
nine exceeding 6 cm/yr, a dissociation between segment measurements that the small
single-arm design cannot interpret. The mouse data are far stronger: 2 mg/kg/day
meclozine five days a week from postnatal day 7 to 56 reduced death or paralysis and
increased body, cranial and long-bone length in Fgfr3-ach mice of both sexes. This is
a clean example of an agent with adequate systemic exposure and no toxicity that still
produces no measurable linear growth effect in humans.

claim_grades.claim: Meclizine at 12.5-25 mg/day achieves measurable systemic exposure in children with achondroplasia without serious adverse events.
claim_grades.basis: Dedicated paediatric phase 1b with full PK parameters and 95% CIs, n=12.

claim_grades.claim: Meclizine increases linear growth velocity in children with achondroplasia.
claim_grades.basis: Single-arm, uncontrolled, n=9, with concomitant growth hormone; observed change ~0.1 cm/yr. Does not support the claim.

claim_grades.claim: Meclizine inhibits FGFR3 signalling in growth plate chondrocytes.
claim_grades.basis: Mouse growth plate and survival data replicated across sexes; no human tissue evidence.

meclizine_repurposing.human_evidence_note: A dedicated paediatric phase 1b pharmacokinetic study and a 26-week open-label phase 2 in children with genetically confirmed achondroplasia.
meclizine_repurposing.translation_risk_reason: Mouse efficacy was substantial (survival, spinal canal and long-bone length) while the human height-velocity change was about 0.1 cm/yr in nine children on concomitant growth hormone. Plasma exposure was adequate and tolerability good, so the failure is not a dosing failure; either the murine effect does not exist in the human plate or the drug does not reach it.
localization: human growth plate: no measurement of meclizine concentration in cartilage

key_refs.one_line_finding: 26-week phase 2 (n=9): height velocity 4.35 to 4.46 cm/yr, arm span velocity 6.93 cm/yr.
Phase 1b PK in 12 children: Cmax 167 ng/mL, t1/2 7.4 h, AUC0-24 1170 ng*h/mL at 12.5 mg/day.
Meclozine 2 mg/kg/d reduced death or paralysis and increased body, cranial and long-bone length in Fgfr3-ach mice.

methylphenidate_growth.name: Methylphenidate and growth suppression
methylphenidate_growth.summary:
Methylphenidate is a dopamine and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor and the first-line
drug for ADHD, given daily for years across the exact window in which linear growth is
accrued. It is therefore an unintentional but very large human experiment on whether
chronic central stimulant exposure constrains growth. A meta-analysis of 33 studies
(16 rated high quality) finds methylphenidate monotherapy associated with a reduction in
height Z score of -0.13 (95% CI -0.18 to -0.09), weight Z of -0.25 (95% CI -0.36 to
-0.15) and BMI Z of -0.26 (95% CI -0.32 to -0.20), with substantial heterogeneity
(I-squared 91-97%) that subgroup and regression analysis could not explain. The
magnitude ordering is informative: the weight deficit is roughly twice the height
deficit, which is the signature of an appetite-mediated nutritional mechanism acting on
the plate rather than a direct pharmacological action on chondrocytes. No stimulant
concentration has been measured in growth plate tissue, and none would be expected to
matter if the pathway is nutritional. The unresolved question is whether the height Z
deficit persists to adult height or is recovered after discontinuation, which the
meta-analysis does not address.

claim_grades.claim: Methylphenidate monotherapy is associated with a small reduction in height Z score of about 0.13.
claim_grades.basis: Meta-analysis of 33 studies with consistent direction, though I-squared 91% and unexplained heterogeneity.

claim_grades.claim: The growth effect is mediated by reduced appetite and energy intake rather than by a direct action on the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Flagged inference from the weight-to-height deficit ratio; not directly tested in any of the pooled studies.

claim_grades.claim: The height deficit persists to adult height.
claim_grades.basis: Widely debated but not addressed by this meta-analysis, which reports only on-treatment Z scores.

methylphenidate_growth.human_evidence_note: Meta-analysis of 33 clinical studies with pre- and post-treatment anthropometry in children and adolescents receiving methylphenidate monotherapy.
methylphenidate_growth.translation_risk_reason: A human pharmacoepidemiological finding in humans; there is no animal claim being carried across.
localization: human growth plate: no direct drug action demonstrated; the plausible route is reduced energy intake acting on the systemic growth axis

key_refs.one_line_finding: 33 studies - height Z -0.13 (95% CI -0.18 to -0.09), weight Z -0.25, BMI Z -0.26 on methylphenidate monotherapy.

navepegritide.name: Navepegritide
navepegritide.summary:
Navepegritide is a TransCon prodrug in which unmodified human CNP-38 is bound to a
methoxy-PEG carrier by a linker that auto-cleaves with first-order kinetics, releasing
native CNP continuously over a one-week dosing interval. The released peptide is
chemically identical to endogenous CNP and therefore has the same NPR2 affinity and
activity - the engineering is entirely pharmacokinetic, not pharmacodynamic. FDA
labelling gives an apparent elimination half-life of 6.7 days for the prodrug and
5.3 days for released CNP, with steady-state CNP Cmax 36.0 pmol/L and weekly AUC
4410 h*pmol/L at 0.1 mg/kg/week; steady state is reached after about three weekly
doses. In the pivotal 52-week placebo-controlled APPROACH trial (NCT05598320, n=84,
ages 2-11 y, 100 ug/kg/week) least-squares mean annualised growth velocity was
5.89 cm/yr versus 4.41 cm/yr on placebo, a difference of 1.49 cm/yr (95% CI 1.05-1.93,
p<0.0001). US approval is accelerated and rests on that surrogate; no final adult
height data exist for this or any CNP analogue. The concentration of released CNP
actually reaching growth plate chondrocytes has never been measured in any species,
so the entire dose-selection rationale rests on plasma exposure.

claim_grades.claim: Once-weekly navepegritide 100 ug/kg raises annualised growth velocity by 1.49 cm/yr over 52 weeks versus placebo in achondroplasia aged 2-11 y.
claim_grades.basis: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT with posted results, n=84.

claim_grades.claim: The growth benefit is produced by sustained CNP occupancy of NPR2 in growth plate chondrocytes.
claim_grades.basis: Mechanism is inferred from NPR2 biology and animal work; no human growth plate pharmacodynamic measurement, and plasma cGMP is the only engagement biomarker.

claim_grades.claim: Continuous weekly exposure is pharmacologically superior to daily peak dosing.
claim_grades.basis: Contradicted by cross-trial comparison - see cnp_analog_pk_challenge; the 1.49 cm/yr effect overlaps the 1.57 cm/yr from once-daily vosoritide despite a ~300-fold difference in exposure duration.

navepegritide.human_evidence_note: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2b trial with a prespecified annualised growth velocity endpoint and posted results, followed by US accelerated approval.
navepegritide.translation_risk_reason: The efficacy estimate comes from a human RCT with posted results. The residual risk is not species translation but endpoint translation: growth velocity at 52 weeks is a surrogate for adult height, and the target-tissue exposure that supposedly drives it has never been measured.
localization: human growth plate: presumed site of action via NPR2; drug concentration at the plate unmeasured

key_refs.one_line_finding: APPROACH phase 2b RCT of once-weekly navepegritide in 84 children with achondroplasia.
Posted results give LS mean AGV difference 1.49 cm/yr (95% CI 1.05-1.93).
Prodrug t1/2 6.7 d, released CNP t1/2 5.3 d, steady-state CNP Cmax 36.0 pmol/L; accelerated approval on AGV.
ACcomplisH dose escalation 6-100 ug CNP/kg/week over 52 weeks established the 100 ug/kg dose.
ACcomplisH registry record, n=57, four dose levels.

npr2_agonist_class.name: NPR2 agonist drug class
npr2_agonist_class.summary:
All approved growth-promoting drugs for achondroplasia are NPR2 (NPR-B) agonists:
vosoritide, a NEP-resistant CNP analogue, and navepegritide, a prodrug releasing
unmodified CNP. Both act by raising intracellular cGMP and signalling through protein
kinase G to inhibit the RAF-1 step of the FGFR3-driven MAPK cascade, as stated in both
FDA labels. The class is therefore a downstream antagonist of FGFR3 output, not a
correction of the receptor. Two structural facts limit it. First, NPR2 protein is
distributed relatively uniformly across growth plate zones whereas PKG-I/II is
hypertrophic-biased (L3), so receptor occupancy and pathway output need not be
co-located and efficacy may be gated downstream of the receptor the drug binds.
Second, FGFR3-to-NPR2 crosstalk is post-translational only, so an FGFR3 gain-of-function
allele does not reduce NPR2 transcript and the receptor is present to be agonised in
achondroplasia - which explains why the class works at all. The pooled placebo-controlled
effect across four RCTs (n=326) is 1.36 cm/yr (95% CI 1.05-1.68), and the class ceiling
has not moved with a 300-fold change in exposure duration.

claim_grades.claim: NPR2 agonism raises annualised growth velocity in achondroplasia by roughly 1.4 cm/yr versus placebo.
claim_grades.basis: Meta-analysis of four RCTs, n=326, low overall risk of bias.

claim_grades.claim: The effect is mediated by cGMP/PKG inhibition of RAF-1 within growth plate chondrocytes.
claim_grades.basis: Stated in FDA labels on the basis of animal and biochemical work; the only human engagement biomarker is systemic cGMP.

claim_grades.claim: Class efficacy is gated by a step downstream of NPR2 rather than by receptor occupancy.
claim_grades.basis: Inference from the zonal mismatch between uniform NPR2 and hypertrophic-biased PKG-I/II (L3 contradiction C-L3-03) plus the exposure-independence of the clinical effect.

npr2_agonist_class.human_evidence_note: Two agents in the class have completed placebo-controlled RCTs in children with achondroplasia and hold accelerated approvals based on annualised growth velocity.
npr2_agonist_class.translation_risk_reason: Class efficacy is established in humans. The mechanistic reading - that PKG-mediated RAF-1 inhibition in chondrocytes is what produces the growth - is taken from animal and in vitro work and is asserted in the labels rather than demonstrated in treated humans.
localization: human growth plate: NPR2 expressed across zones; class engagement measured only as urinary or plasma cGMP, never in plate tissue

key_refs.one_line_finding: Class effect 1.36 cm/yr (95% CI 1.05-1.68); injection site reaction RR 1.65, urticaria RR 4.04.
States the RAF-1 step as the mechanism and reports cGMP saturation at 15 ug/kg/day.
States identical NPR-B/cGMP/PKG mechanism for released CNP.
Basket trial extending NPR2 agonism beyond FGFR3 disease to RASopathies, ACAN and NPR2 deficiency.

octreotide_somatostatin_analog.name: Octreotide and somatostatin analogues
octreotide_somatostatin_analog.summary:
Somatostatin analogues suppress pituitary GH secretion through somatostatin receptor
subtypes 2 and 5, lowering circulating GH and consequently IGF-1. Unlike pegvisomant,
which blocks the receptor at the target tissue, they act one level up at the source, so
the pair together dissect where in the axis a growth effect is generated. In paediatric
practice their growth-relevant use is in GH-secreting adenoma and pituitary gigantism,
including McCune-Albright syndrome and AIP-mutation macroadenoma, where the aim is to
stop excessive linear growth before epiphyseal fusion. Reported paediatric experience is
case-level: surgical series with adjunctive somatostatin analogue, and case reports of
gigantism controlled by combined modalities. X-linked acrogigantism is the instructive
negative: it responds poorly to somatostatin analogues and has been controlled instead by
GH receptor blockade with pegvisomant, indicating that suppressing secretion and blocking
the receptor are not interchangeable in humans. No cohort reports final adult height in
children treated with a somatostatin analogue as the primary growth-limiting agent, and
no measurement of somatostatin analogue exposure at the growth plate exists - which is a
smaller problem here than for direct-acting drugs, since the mechanism is endocrine.

claim_grades.claim: Somatostatin analogues lower GH and IGF-1 in children with GH-secreting adenomas.
claim_grades.basis: Consistent across paediatric case series and adult acromegaly trials; the biochemical effect is not in dispute.

claim_grades.claim: Somatostatin analogues limit final adult height in pituitary gigantism.
claim_grades.basis: Only case-level evidence; no cohort reports final height with a somatostatin analogue as the primary agent.

claim_grades.claim: Suppressing GH secretion and blocking the GH receptor are interchangeable growth-limiting strategies.
claim_grades.basis: Contradicted in X-linked acrogigantism, which responds poorly to somatostatin analogues but was controlled to final height by pegvisomant.

octreotide_somatostatin_analog.human_evidence_note: Human paediatric use is documented in case reports and small series of pituitary gigantism and GH-secreting macroadenoma, not in controlled trials with growth endpoints.
octreotide_somatostatin_analog.translation_risk_reason: The pharmacology is entirely human and endocrine; the limitation is sample size and the absence of controlled growth endpoints, not species.
localization: human pituitary somatotroph: site of action via SSTR2/SSTR5
human growth plate: no direct action claimed; effect is entirely through reduced GH and IGF-1

key_refs.one_line_finding: X-linked acrogigantism controlled to final height by pegvisomant, the comparator that shows somatostatin analogues are not interchangeable.
Defines the alternative mechanism - receptor blockade titrated to IGF-1 rather than suppression of secretion.

oxandrolone.name: Oxandrolone
oxandrolone.summary:
Oxandrolone is a synthetic androgen that is poorly aromatised to oestrogen, which makes
it a specific human probe: it separates the androgenic contribution to growth from the
oestrogenic one, because it should promote growth without delivering the oestrogen that
closes the plate. It is used in constitutional delay of growth and puberty and, with
rhGH, in Turner syndrome. A meta-analysis of 13 retrospective cohorts (803 boys with
constitutional delay) found androgen therapy overall increased measured final adult
height by 1.78 cm (95% CI 0.47-3.08, p=0.0076) and final height Z score by 0.24
(95% CI 0.07-0.41). The internal structure of that result is the interesting part:
low-dose regimens gave the largest gain (1.88 cm, 95% CI 0.63-3.12) while medium and
high doses were not significant, short courses outperformed long courses (2.70 cm,
95% CI 1.30-4.09), and testosterone - which IS aromatised - outperformed oxandrolone by
2.64 cm (95% CI 1.44-3.80). The non-aromatisable androgen was therefore the weaker agent,
which is the opposite of what the oestrogen-fusion model predicts if androgen acts
independently, and points to a genuine oestrogen requirement for the pubertal height gain.

claim_grades.claim: Short-term androgen therapy increases final adult height in constitutional delay by about 1.8 cm.
claim_grades.basis: Meta-analysis with attained final height, 803 boys, but all 13 constituent studies are retrospective cohorts.

claim_grades.claim: The non-aromatisable androgen oxandrolone is less effective than testosterone for final height.
claim_grades.basis: Subgroup comparison within a retrospective meta-analysis; not a randomised head-to-head.

claim_grades.claim: The oestrogen produced by aromatisation of testosterone is required for the full pubertal height gain.
claim_grades.basis: Flagged inference from the testosterone-versus-oxandrolone subgroup difference; consistent with oestrogen-deficiency natural experiments but not directly tested here.

oxandrolone.human_evidence_note: Meta-analysis of 13 retrospective cohorts with attained final adult height in 803 boys, plus long-standing use with rhGH in Turner syndrome.
oxandrolone.translation_risk_reason: All human with attained-height endpoints. The limitation is design: every included study is retrospective, so allocation to treatment was not random.
localization: human growth plate: androgen receptor-mediated effects presumed; no measurement in treated boys

key_refs.one_line_finding: 13 cohorts, 803 boys - androgen therapy +1.78 cm final adult height; testosterone beat oxandrolone by 2.64 cm.
Places oxandrolone alongside rhGH among adult-height-directed therapies in non-GH-deficient children.

pegvisomant.name: Pegvisomant
pegvisomant.summary:
Pegvisomant is a pegylated analogue of human growth hormone engineered as a competitive
GH receptor antagonist: it binds the receptor at site 1 but cannot productively engage
site 2, so it blocks receptor dimerisation and signal transduction rather than
activating it. Its pharmacological readout is the fall in serum IGF-1, free IGF-1,
IGFBP-3 and the acid-labile subunit, and dosing is titrated to IGF-1 rather than to GH,
which rises during treatment. It is a mechanistic probe running the growth axis
backwards, and unlike almost every other agent in this layer it is used deliberately to
reduce growth. In X-linked acrogigantism, pegvisomant monotherapy has been carried
through to final height in a paediatric patient, demonstrating that blocking the GH
receptor is sufficient to arrest pathological linear overgrowth in a human with open
epiphyses. The FDA label states that safety and effectiveness in paediatric patients
have not been established, so all paediatric use is off-label and the human paediatric
evidence is case-level. Pharmacokinetics are slow: peak serum concentration is not
reached until 33-77 hours after subcutaneous dosing and absolute bioavailability of a
20 mg dose is about 57% relative to intravenous.

claim_grades.claim: Pegvisomant blocks GH receptor signalling and lowers serum IGF-1 in a dose-dependent way.
claim_grades.basis: Mechanism and IGF-1 titration are the basis of the approved label and of the full ACROSTUDY cohort.

claim_grades.claim: GH receptor blockade is sufficient to arrest pathological linear overgrowth in a child with open epiphyses.
claim_grades.basis: Demonstrated to final height in a single X-linked acrogigantism patient; no paediatric cohort exists and the label states paediatric effectiveness is not established.

pegvisomant.human_evidence_note: Large adult acromegaly cohorts including the full ACROSTUDY dataset, plus case-level paediatric use carried to final height.
pegvisomant.translation_risk_reason: All pharmacology and outcome data are human. The paediatric growth claim rests on case reports rather than a cohort, which is a sample-size limit rather than a species one.
localization: human growth plate: no direct measurement; effect on the plate is inferred from arrest of linear overgrowth

key_refs.one_line_finding: GH receptor antagonist, Tmax 33-77 h, 57% relative bioavailability; paediatric safety and effectiveness not established.
Pegvisomant monotherapy carried to final height in paediatric X-linked acrogigantism.
Final ACROSTUDY data on long-term safety and efficacy of pegvisomant monotherapy in acromegaly.

recombinant_human_gh.name: Recombinant human growth hormone (somatropin)
recombinant_human_gh.summary:
Recombinant human growth hormone is the oldest and most widely used pharmacological
probe of the human growth plate: an unlimited supply after 1985 turned a scarce
pituitary extract into a systematically testable intervention across a dozen conditions.
Somatropin binds the GH receptor and acts on the plate both indirectly, by raising
hepatic IGF-1, and directly on chondrocytes, and its skeletal effect requires open
epiphyses. Across indications a systematic review of 20 studies (21,812 participants)
reports growth velocity gains of +3.0 to +5.0 cm/yr and height SDS gains of +0.3 to
+0.9, largest in idiopathic short stature and Prader-Willi syndrome, with discontinuation
rates below 2%. The instructive case is achondroplasia, where GH is licensed only in
Japan: it produces a real short-term velocity response but the effect on adult height is
explicitly described as unsatisfactory, and real-world cohorts have since transitioned
patients from GH to vosoritide. That dissociation - a hormone that reliably accelerates
velocity but does not reliably convert velocity into adult height in an FGFR3-driven
plate - is the single most important thing GH tells the atlas, because it shows the
systemic axis can push a plate whose intrinsic ceiling is set elsewhere.

claim_grades.claim: rhGH increases growth velocity by roughly 3-5 cm/yr in children with growth disorders.
claim_grades.basis: Systematic review of 20 studies, 21,812 participants, though with moderate-to-serious risk of bias.

claim_grades.claim: rhGH raises adult height in achondroplasia to a clinically satisfactory degree.
claim_grades.basis: Japanese licensure with published statements that the adult-height effect is unsatisfactory; no placebo-controlled adult-height trial in achondroplasia.

claim_grades.claim: The plate effect is partly direct on chondrocytes rather than wholly IGF-1-mediated.
claim_grades.basis: Rests on animal and cell work; not separable in treated humans.

recombinant_human_gh.human_evidence_note: Decades of randomised and post-marketing data in tens of thousands of children across licensed indications, with adult height reported in several.
recombinant_human_gh.translation_risk_reason: Efficacy, safety and dosing are all established in humans. The residual uncertainty is about mechanism partition - how much of the effect is direct on chondrocytes versus IGF-1-mediated - which is not resolvable from clinical data.
localization: human growth plate: acts on GH-receptor-bearing chondrocytes and via hepatic IGF-1; no zonal localisation demonstrated in treated humans

key_refs.one_line_finding: 20 studies, 21,812 participants - rhGH +3.0 to +5.0 cm/yr velocity, +0.3 to +0.9 height SDS.
rhGH is licensed to improve adult height in Turner, SHOX deficiency, Noonan, Prader-Willi, ISS, CKD and SGA.
Single-centre cohort documenting transition from growth hormone to vosoritide in achondroplasia with age-dependent effectiveness.
Nationwide survey and cohort of GH therapy after childhood haematopoietic cell transplantation - GH used against an irradiated plate.

regulatory_review_document.name: Regulatory review documents as an evidence source
regulatory_review_document.summary:
Regulatory dossiers carry quantitative pharmacology that the peer-reviewed literature
systematically omits, and for this layer they are the difference between a described
drug and a characterised one. Four categories of number were obtainable only from
labelling in this sweep: full plasma pharmacokinetics with dispersion (vosoritide mean
apparent half-life 21.0-27.9 minutes, Tmax 15 minutes, apparent clearance
79.4-104 mL/min/kg; navepegritide prodrug half-life 6.7 days and released CNP 5.3 days);
the exposure-response position of the chosen dose (vosoritide urinary cGMP near
saturation and CXM maximal at 15 ug/kg/day, so the approved dose sits on the plateau);
the exact population definition of an indication (mecasermin requires height SDS <= -3.0
AND IGF-1 SDS <= -3.0 AND normal or elevated GH); and explicit statements of what is not
established, including the paediatric contraindications for both PTH1R agonists and the
accelerated-approval language making continued approval contingent on confirmatory
benefit. Two access routes were used and both worked without authentication: the openFDA
drug label API for structured labelling, and the Drugs@FDA overview pages for approval
chronology. Neither the full multidisciplinary review nor the clinical pharmacology
review PDFs were retrieved in this sweep, so review-level details such as the sponsor's
tissue distribution studies remain unread.

claim_grades.claim: Label pharmacokinetics for the agents in this layer are retrievable without authentication via the openFDA drug label API.
claim_grades.basis: Eight labels retrieved directly in this sweep with structured sections including clinical pharmacology and pediatric use.

claim_grades.claim: Regulatory documents contain quantitative pharmacology absent from the primary literature.
claim_grades.basis: The vosoritide and navepegritide half-lives and the vosoritide cGMP saturation dose appear in labelling and not in the pivotal trial reports.

claim_grades.claim: No agent's regulatory dossier contains growth plate tissue distribution data.
claim_grades.basis: True of the labelling retrieved, but the full pharmacology/toxicology review PDFs were not read, so a sponsor tissue distribution study could exist unread.

regulatory_review_document.human_evidence_note: Regulatory dossiers summarise human trial and human pharmacokinetic data reviewed by an agency, and are the authoritative record of dose, indication and what remains unproven.
localization: not applicable: an evidence-source node

key_refs.one_line_finding: Source of vosoritide half-life, clearance, volume of distribution and the cGMP/CXM exposure-response statement.
Source of navepegritide and released-CNP half-lives, Cmax, AUC and accumulation ratios.
Source of the exact numeric definition of severe primary IGF-1 deficiency used to gate mecasermin.
Approval chronology for NDA 214938 including the 2023 new-patient-population supplement.
Source of the open-epiphyses osteosarcoma restriction that keeps PTH1R agonists out of paediatric growth research.

soluble_fgfr3_decoy.name: Soluble FGFR3 decoy (recifercept)
soluble_fgfr3_decoy.summary:
Recifercept is a recombinant soluble FGFR3 extracellular domain designed to act as a
ligand trap, sequestering FGF ligands before they can activate mutant FGFR3 at the cell
surface. It is the cleanest available human test of the ligand-dependence of
achondroplasia, because a decoy can only work if the mutant receptor still requires
ligand. It failed. The phase 2 trial (NCT04638153, n=60) and its open-label extension
(NCT05116046, n=35) were both terminated on 18 November 2022, with the registry
whyStopped field reading "terminated due to lack of efficacy at any of the tested doses
... not related to a safety concern". Posted results show the ratio of observed to
expected height change was 1.0 at month 12 in every arm - 1 mg/kg weekly, 2 mg/kg twice
weekly and 1.5 mg/kg daily - with 95% CIs spanning 0.8-1.1, i.e. growth indistinguishable
from the untreated reference. The accompanying natural-history study (NCT03794609) and a
Chinese phase 1 (NCT05061277) were terminated and withdrawn alongside it. The failure is
informative in two independent directions: either FGFR3-G380R signalling in the human
growth plate is substantially ligand-independent, or a ~100 kDa glycoprotein cannot reach
chondrocytes inside avascular, proteoglycan-dense cartilage at a useful concentration.
These were not distinguished, because plate exposure was never measured.

claim_grades.claim: Recifercept did not increase growth at any tested dose in children with achondroplasia.
claim_grades.basis: Posted phase 2 results, observed/expected height ratio 1.0 (95% CI 0.8-1.1) at month 12 in all arms, and an explicit registry termination statement.

claim_grades.claim: The failure shows FGFR3-G380R signalling in the human growth plate is ligand-independent.
claim_grades.basis: One of two competing explanations; not distinguishable from a delivery failure without tissue exposure data.

claim_grades.claim: Soluble FGFR3 decoys engage FGF ligands in growth plate cartilage in vivo.
claim_grades.basis: Supported only by mouse synchondrosis histology, not by any human or large-animal tissue measurement.

soluble_fgfr3_decoy.human_evidence_note: Two terminated interventional trials in children with achondroplasia with posted results and an explicit registry statement of lack of efficacy at all tested doses.
soluble_fgfr3_decoy.translation_risk_reason: The mouse data were positive - recifercept prevented premature synchondrosis closure in Fgfr3-ach/+ mice - and the human trials were null at every dose. This is a documented mouse-to-human translation failure, and the reason for it was not established because target-tissue exposure was never measured in either species.
localization: human growth plate: intended target; no measured penetration of a ~100 kDa decoy into avascular cartilage
mouse cranial base synchondrosis: recifercept prevented premature ossification in Fgfr3-ach/+ mice

key_refs.one_line_finding: TERMINATED for lack of efficacy at any tested dose; posted observed/expected height ratio 1.0 (95% CI 0.8-1.1) at month 12.
Open-label extension terminated the same day for the same reason, explicitly not safety-related.
Healthy-volunteer PK study withdrawn with zero enrolment for strategic reasons.
The programme's observational natural-history study was terminated on the same date.
Recifercept prevented premature ossification of skull base synchondroses in Fgfr3-ach/+ mice - the positive animal result that did not translate.

soluble_fgfr3_decoy.termination_note: Recifercept NCT04638153/NCT05116046 stopped for "lack of efficacy at any of the tested doses"; posted observed/expected height ratio 1.0 (95% CI 0.8-1.1) in all three arms. This IS negative evidence about soluble FGFR3 decoys.

statin_ipsc_achondroplasia.name: Statins in iPSC models of FGFR3 skeletal dysplasia
statin_ipsc_achondroplasia.summary:
Statins entered the achondroplasia field through a human induced pluripotent stem cell
model rather than through a mouse. Fibroblasts from patients with thanatophoric dysplasia
type I and with achondroplasia were reprogrammed to iPSCs; chondrogenic differentiation
of both produced degraded cartilage, and statin treatment corrected that degradation in
both genotypes. Statin treatment of achondroplasia model mice produced a significant
recovery of bone growth. The proposed mechanism is enhanced degradation or reduced
accumulation of the mutant FGFR3 protein rather than kinase inhibition, which would make
it mechanistically distinct from both the CNP analogues (downstream antagonism) and the
TKIs (catalytic inhibition). Despite being published in 2014 and despite statins being
cheap, oral and extensively characterised in adults, no randomised trial of a statin for
linear growth in achondroplasia has reported. The reason is not obviously biological:
statins are contraindicated in pregnancy, have limited paediatric safety data outside
familial hypercholesterolaemia, and there is no commercial sponsor. This node therefore
records an unrepeated human-cell finding, not an intervention.

claim_grades.claim: Statin treatment corrects the degraded-cartilage phenotype of TD1 and achondroplasia patient iPSC chondrogenic cultures.
claim_grades.basis: Single high-profile study, not independently replicated in the twelve years since.

claim_grades.claim: Statins increase bone growth in achondroplasia model mice.
claim_grades.basis: Same single study; no independent replication located.

claim_grades.claim: Statins would increase linear growth in children with achondroplasia.
claim_grades.basis: Repeated in reviews as a candidate therapy but traceable to no human in vivo data at all.

statin_ipsc_achondroplasia.human_evidence_note: The human evidence is patient-derived iPSC chondrogenic cultures, not treated patients; no human in vivo growth data exist.
statin_ipsc_achondroplasia.translation_risk_reason: An iPSC chondrogenic pellet has no vasculature, no zonal architecture, no mechanical loading and no systemic endocrine input, so it cannot report on the diffusion-limited delivery problem that defeats other agents. The supporting in vivo data are murine.
localization: in vitro human iPSC-derived cartilage: degraded cartilage phenotype corrected by statin
human growth plate: no in vivo human data of any kind

key_refs.one_line_finding: Statins corrected degraded cartilage in TD1 and achondroplasia iPSC chondrogenic cultures and increased bone growth in achondroplasia model mice.
Contemporary review of achondroplasia therapies lists only vosoritide, infigratinib and navepegritide as clinical agents - statins are absent from the clinical landscape.

teriparatide.name: Teriparatide (PTH 1-34)
teriparatide.summary:
Teriparatide is recombinant human parathyroid hormone 1-34, an intermittently dosed
PTH1R agonist. The PTH1R is the receptor through which PTHrP holds prehypertrophic
chondrocytes in the proliferative pool, so teriparatide is in principle the most
mechanistically apt drug in this layer - and it is the one that cannot be given to
children for growth. The FDA label instructs avoidance in patients with open epiphyses
because of increased baseline osteosarcoma risk, and states that safety and effectiveness
in paediatric patients have not been established. The barrier is not the growth plate's
unresponsiveness but the fact that the same anabolic signal in a growing skeleton is an
oncogenic one, an inference drawn from rat carcinogenicity data and from the elevated
background osteosarcoma incidence during the adolescent growth spurt. Paediatric human
exposure exists only where the indication is severe and the alternative worse:
hypoparathyroidism, activating calcium-sensing receptor mutations, and off-label
osteotomy healing in osteogenesis imperfecta. None of these report linear growth as an
endpoint. Consequently the human growth plate has never been probed with a PTH1R agonist
under conditions that would answer whether pharmacological PTH1R activation delays
hypertrophic differentiation in vivo, which the mouse and the human Jansen metaphyseal
chondrodysplasia phenotype both predict it would.

claim_grades.claim: Teriparatide is contraindicated in growing children because of osteosarcoma risk with open epiphyses.
claim_grades.basis: Explicit FDA label statement and warnings section.

claim_grades.claim: PTH1R agonism would delay hypertrophic differentiation and lengthen the human growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Inference from PTHrP-PTH1R mouse biology and from Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia; never tested pharmacologically in a human.

teriparatide.human_evidence_note: There is no human evidence on teriparatide and linear growth; the only paediatric exposures are for calcium disorders and report calcium, not height, outcomes.
teriparatide.translation_risk_reason: Everything known about PTH1R agonism and the growth plate comes from mouse genetics and from the human Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia phenotype (constitutive PTH1R activation), not from a pharmacological human exposure. The regulatory barrier means this gap cannot be closed by an ordinary trial.
localization: human growth plate: PTH1R is expressed in prehypertrophic chondrocytes; teriparatide has never been administered to a growing human plate with a growth readout

key_refs.one_line_finding: Avoid in patients with open epiphyses because of increased baseline osteosarcoma risk; paediatric safety and effectiveness not established.
Systematic review of teriparatide in children with hypoparathyroidism - the only substantial paediatric exposure, and without growth endpoints.
Mouse model of Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia - constitutive PTH1R activation - for testing candidate therapeutics.

transcon_growth_hormone.name: Lonapegsomatropin (TransCon hGH)
transcon_growth_hormone.summary:
Lonapegsomatropin is a TransCon prodrug that releases unmodified somatropin from a PEG
carrier, converting daily growth hormone into a once-weekly 0.24 mg/kg subcutaneous
injection. Because the released hormone is chemically identical to somatropin, it is a
controlled test of whether the growth plate integrates GH exposure or responds to its
pulsatility. The answer from the largest head-to-head trial is that weekly dosing is at
least as effective: in the 52-week phase 3 briGHt trial (NCT04326374, n=153 treatment-naive
prepubertal Chinese children with GHD, randomised 2:1) annualised height velocity was
10.66 +/- 0.22 cm/yr on weekly lonapegsomatropin versus 9.75 +/- 0.26 cm/yr on daily
somatropin, a difference of 0.91 cm/yr (95% CI 0.37-1.45, p=0.0010), meeting both
non-inferiority and superiority. Class-level meta-analysis of 16 RCTs (2435 children)
finds only modest differences between long-acting and daily preparations. The
counter-example matters as much: somavaratan, a different long-acting GH, was terminated
in phase 3 because "the primary endpoint of non-inferiority to daily therapy ... was not
achieved", so long-acting GH is not automatically equivalent. Lonapegsomatropin is also
being combined with navepegritide in achondroplasia (COACH), where the combination gave
an AGV of 8.69 cm/yr versus 5.95 cm/yr for matched navepegritide monotherapy.

claim_grades.claim: Weekly lonapegsomatropin is non-inferior and in one phase 3 superior to daily somatropin on annualised height velocity.
claim_grades.basis: Randomised active-controlled phase 3, n=153, difference 0.91 cm/yr (95% CI 0.37-1.45).

claim_grades.claim: Long-acting GH preparations as a class are equivalent to daily GH.
claim_grades.basis: 16-RCT meta-analysis finds modest differences, but somavaratan failed phase 3 non-inferiority - the class is not uniform.

claim_grades.claim: Adding lonapegsomatropin to navepegritide increases growth beyond CNP monotherapy in achondroplasia.
claim_grades.basis: n=21, open-label, comparator is a matched cohort from a different trial.

transcon_growth_hormone.human_evidence_note: Randomised active-controlled phase 3 trials against daily somatropin, plus US and EU approval for paediatric GHD.
transcon_growth_hormone.translation_risk_reason: All efficacy and PK data are human. The combination result in achondroplasia carries higher risk because its comparator is a matched external cohort rather than a randomised arm.
localization: human growth plate: acts via GH receptor and hepatic IGF-1; no plate-level exposure or pharmacodynamic measurement

key_refs.one_line_finding: briGHt phase 3 - weekly lonapegsomatropin AHV 10.66 vs 9.75 cm/yr for daily somatropin.
0.24 mg/kg/week paediatric dose; approval on 161 treatment-naive children aged 3-13 y.
16 RCTs, 2435 children - modest advantage of long-acting over daily GH on HV-SDS and Ht-SDS.
COACH - navepegritide plus lonapegsomatropin AGV 8.69 vs 5.95 cm/yr for matched navepegritide monotherapy.
Somavaratan phase 3 TERMINATED - non-inferiority to daily GH not achieved; long-acting GH is not automatically equivalent.

transcon_growth_hormone.termination_note: Somavaratan NCT02413138/NCT02068521 stopped because "non-inferiority to daily therapy not achieved" - a genuine efficacy finding about that long-acting GH construct.

trial_endpoint_annualized_growth_velocit.name: Annualised growth velocity as a trial endpoint
trial_endpoint_annualized_growth_velocit.summary:
Annualised growth velocity is the endpoint on which every modern growth drug has been
licensed. It is computed as (height minus baseline height) divided by elapsed time,
scaled to 365.25 days, and it has three properties that make it attractive and one that
makes it dangerous. It is continuous, it is measurable within 52 weeks, and it is
sensitive - the CNP analogues, infigratinib and the long-acting growth hormones all
separate from control on it. What it cannot do is distinguish growth that is added from
growth that is merely brought forward, because a drug that also advances skeletal
maturation raises velocity while shortening the remaining growth period. Both US
accelerated approvals in achondroplasia state this explicitly by making continued
approval contingent on confirmatory verification of clinical benefit. The measurement
itself carries structural noise: annualised velocity computed over a single 52-week
window inherits seasonal growth variation and measurement error amplified by the short
interval, which is why trials use least-squares means with imputation and why the
standard deviations around individual responses are large. It is also strongly
age-dependent - untreated achondroplasia natural history gives 9.3 cm/yr (male) and
10.4 cm/yr (female) at age 1 falling to 4.1 and 4.6 cm/yr at age 4 - so a velocity
difference is uninterpretable without a matched-age comparator.

claim_grades.claim: Annualised growth velocity is the licensing endpoint for current achondroplasia and GH therapies.
claim_grades.basis: Stated in both FDA labels and used as the primary endpoint in every pivotal trial cited in this layer.

claim_grades.claim: The endpoint cannot distinguish added growth from redistributed growth.
claim_grades.basis: Structural property of the measure, made explicit by the accelerated-approval requirement for confirmatory clinical benefit.

claim_grades.claim: Age-related decline in untreated velocity is of the same magnitude as the drug effects being measured.
claim_grades.basis: ACHieve natural history - 9.3 to 4.1 cm/yr between ages 1 and 4 in untreated males, versus drug effects of 1.4-1.7 cm/yr.

trial_endpoint_annualized_growth_velocit.human_evidence_note: The endpoint is defined and used in human regulatory trials, and its age dependence is quantified by prospective human natural history data.
localization: not applicable: whole-organism auxological measure, not zone-localised

key_refs.one_line_finding: ACHieve natural history - untreated achondroplasia AGV falls from 9.3/10.4 cm/yr at age 1 to 4.1/4.6 at age 4.
Accelerated approval based on improvement in annualised growth velocity, contingent on confirmatory verification of clinical benefit.
Same accelerated-approval construction for the second agent in the class.
Pools the endpoint across four RCTs at 1.36 cm/yr (95% CI 1.05-1.68).

tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor_growth_toxicit.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor growth toxicity
tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor_growth_toxicit.summary:
Children treated with imatinib for chronic myeloid leukaemia are the natural experiment
that constrains the entire FGFR3-inhibitor programme, because they are humans given a
chronic ATP-competitive kinase inhibitor across the whole growth period. In one of the
longest follow-ups reported (13 patients diagnosed before age 13 and followed to skeletal
maturity, median imatinib duration 14.3 years, IQR 14.2-16, 184.4 patient-years), mean
height Z score fell from -0.6 +/- 1.2 at diagnosis to -1.1 +/- 0.9 at maturity (p=0.04).
The effect was timing-dependent: in those started before the pubertal growth spurt the
decline was significant (-0.5 +/- 0.6 to -1.3 +/- 0.6, p=0.03), whereas in those started
after it there was no significant change (p=0.60). Crucially, adolescent catch-up growth
occurred and was insufficient - final height Z remained reduced. The mechanism is
attributed to off-target inhibition of PDGFR and KIT in growth plate chondrocytes and
osteoblasts rather than to BCR-ABL. This matters directly for infigratinib and the FGFR3
TKI class: the same drug class, the same chronic paediatric dosing, and the same
prepubertal window of susceptibility - but the intended target is now a growth brake
rather than a growth driver, so the net effect is the sum of an on-target gain and an
off-target loss that no achondroplasia trial has yet run long enough to separate.

claim_grades.claim: Prepubertal initiation of imatinib reduces final height Z score by roughly 0.8 despite adolescent catch-up.
claim_grades.basis: Long follow-up to skeletal maturity but n=13, single centre, no untreated CML control.

claim_grades.claim: Growth toxicity of kinase inhibitors is confined to prepubertal initiation.
claim_grades.basis: The post-spurt subgroup showed no significant change, but that subgroup is small and a null in a small subgroup is weak evidence of absence.

claim_grades.claim: Chronic FGFR3 inhibition in achondroplasia carries the same off-target growth toxicity risk.
claim_grades.basis: Flagged inference by class and by dosing pattern; infigratinib is more FGFR-selective than imatinib and no long-term paediatric height data exist.

tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor_growth_toxicit.human_evidence_note: A cohort of children treated with a kinase inhibitor from before puberty to skeletal maturity with attained final height Z scores.
tyrosine_kinase_inhibitor_growth_toxicit.translation_risk_reason: Human exposure with a human final-height endpoint.
localization: human growth plate: off-target PDGFR and KIT inhibition in chondrocytes and osteoblasts is the proposed mechanism; not measured in treated children

key_refs.one_line_finding: 13 children on imatinib to skeletal maturity - height Z -0.6 to -1.1, decline significant only with prepubertal initiation.
Review of endocrine late effects of targeted and immune-based therapies in paediatric oncology, including TKI effects on growth.
The FGFR3 TKI now given chronically to growing children with achondroplasia, with 52-week rather than final-height follow-up.

vosoritide.name: Vosoritide
vosoritide.summary:
Vosoritide is a recombinant CNP analogue engineered for resistance to
neutral-endopeptidase degradation, giving it a plasma half-life long enough for
once-daily subcutaneous dosing where native CNP is cleared within minutes. It
acts on NPR2 in growth plate chondrocytes, raising cGMP and activating PKG-II,
which antagonises the FGFR3-MAPK/ERK brake that is constitutively overactive in
achondroplasia. Mechanistically it is therefore a downstream bypass rather than
a correction of the causal receptor: it does not reduce FGFR3 signalling, it
opposes its output. The pivotal 52-week phase 3 trial (NCT03197766, n=121,
ages 5 to <18y, 15.0 ug/kg/day) raised annualised growth velocity by an adjusted
mean 1.57 cm/year versus placebo (95% CI 1.22-1.93). Efficacy has since been
extended to children under 5 years, and a phase 2 basket trial has tested the
same agent in other genetic short stature causes including ACAN and NPR2
deficiency - the latter being a direct mechanistic test, since NPR2 haploinsufficiency
impairs the very receptor vosoritide agonises. The critical unresolved question is
stated by the pivotal trial's own authors: growth velocity is a surrogate, and
whether final adult height increases is not established by these data.
vosoritide.human_evidence_note: Multiple randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in children with achondroplasia with a prespecified growth-velocity endpoint; regulatory approval followed.
vosoritide.translation_risk_reason: The efficacy claim rests on human RCTs, not on animal inference. Residual translation risk concerns MECHANISM rather than effect: the zonal site of action and the partition between proliferation, matrix synthesis and hypertrophic volume are inferred from mouse work, not measured in treated human plates.
localization: human growth plate: acts on NPR2-expressing chondrocytes; zonal site of action not directly demonstrated in treated humans

key_refs.one_line_finding: Phase 3 RCT (n=121): +1.57 cm/yr annualised growth velocity vs placebo (95% CI 1.22-1.93) at 52 weeks; authors state final adult height effect unknown.
Phase 2 RCT extending vosoritide to children aged 3-59 months across three sequential age cohorts.
Phase II basket trial testing vosoritide in RASopathies, ACAN and NPR2 deficiency - extending the agent beyond FGFR3 disease.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of vosoritide efficacy and safety.

atomic_force_microscopy_cartilage.name: Atomic force microscopy of cartilage and physis
atomic_force_microscopy_cartilage.summary:
AFM nanoindentation measures elastic modulus at spatial scales below the cell, resolving the
pericellular matrix separately from the interterritorial matrix - a distinction no bulk
mechanical test can make. Spatial mapping in porcine articular cartilage showed the
pericellular matrix is measurably softer than the surrounding territorial matrix when probed
in situ (darling2010), and zone-specific micromechanical mapping of rabbit growth plate
matrix demonstrated that stiffness varies by zone (radhakrishnan2004). Against the
dimensions that matter, AFM operates at 10 nm to 1 um contact radii, three orders of
magnitude finer than a chondrocyte, so its limitation is not resolution but sampling: each
indentation samples a micrometre-scale patch, and building a zonal map of a 1 mm plate
requires thousands of points on a cryosectioned or freshly cut surface, which introduces
cutting artefact and depth-of-tissue dehydration. In human physis the method has essentially
not been used; the nearest human measurement is nanoindentation across the growth-
plate/epiphysis and growth-plate/metaphysis interfaces in ten paediatric donors, which found
a sharp modulus transition at the epiphyseal interface and a gradual rise at the metaphyseal
one (xie2025). That single study is the human anchor for gap g_l5matrix_001, and it measured
interfaces rather than a full zonal profile.
atomic_force_microscopy_cartilage.human_evidence_note: AFM zonal mapping of growth plate exists in rabbit and pig; the only human physeal micromechanics is interface nanoindentation in ten donors.
atomic_force_microscopy_cartilage.translation_risk_reason: Cartilage modulus depends on hydration, fixed charge density and collagen crosslinking, all of which differ with species and age, and the rabbit plate is an order of magnitude thinner than the human one.
localization: porcine PERI: pericellular matrix resolved as mechanically distinct
rabbit RZ/PZ/HZ: zonal modulus differences demonstrated

key_refs.one_line_finding: Pericellular matrix mapped as mechanically distinct from territorial matrix by in situ AFM.
Zone-specific micromechanical properties of growth plate extracellular matrix.
Sharp modulus step at the human growth-plate/epiphysis interface and a gradual rise at the metaphyseal interface, ten paediatric donors.

brdu_edu_labeling.name: BrdU and EdU labelling of proliferating chondrocytes
brdu_edu_labeling.summary:
Thymidine-analogue labelling is how proliferative kinetics in the growth plate are actually
measured, as opposed to inferred. Cumulative and pulse BrdU labelling determined
proliferative characteristics of growth plate chondrocytes directly (farnum1993), and cell
cycle analysis of proliferative zone chondrocytes across plates elongating at different
rates established that cycle time varies with elongation rate rather than being fixed
(wilsman1996a). Short-term nutritional and mechanical perturbations have been read out the
same way (farnum2003, farnum2000). In humans the method has been applied essentially once:
in vitro tritiated thymidine labelling of human and porcine growth plates in the same study
(thurston1985). The reason is that BrdU/EdU administration requires systemic dosing of a
mutagenic nucleoside analogue followed by tissue harvest at a controlled interval, which
cannot be done in a child. The consequence is precise and load-bearing: the human
proliferative cycle time of roughly 20 days that this atlas quotes is NOT a labelling
measurement but an inference from column cell counts divided by radiographic elongation rate
(kember1976), which is why gap g_l1arch_012 exists and why the human cell cycle structure -
G1, S, G2, M durations and growth fraction - is entirely unknown.
brdu_edu_labeling.human_evidence_note: One in vitro human labelling study exists; no in vivo human labelling is possible.
brdu_edu_labeling.translation_risk_reason: Cycle time differs roughly tenfold between rodent and human, so rodent labelling kinetics cannot be carried across even in order of magnitude.
localization: multiple PZ: labelling index measured directly in animal models
human PZ: not measurable in vivo

key_refs.one_line_finding: Proliferative characteristics of growth plate chondrocytes determined by BrdU labelling.
Cell cycle analysis of proliferative zone chondrocytes in plates elongating at different rates.
In vitro tritiated thymidine labelling in human and porcine growth plates.
Human cycle time derived from column counts and radiographic growth rate, not from labelling.

cartilage_organoid.name: Cartilage and skeletal organoids
cartilage_organoid.summary:
Skeletal organoids and assembloids are the most serious current attempt to build a human
growth plate outside a human. Region-specific skeletal organoids differentiated from human
pluripotent stem cells via PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchyme generate GDF5+PRG4+
interzone/articular progenitors and SP7+ growth plate chondrocytes, with transcriptional
similarity to human embryonic skeletal tissue (GSE288042-46 series). Human PSC-derived
osteochondral fusion constructs transplanted under the mouse kidney capsule contain a full
endochondral spectrum including the hypertrophic-to-osteoblast transition (GSE275943), which
is the human counterpart of a claim otherwise established only by murine lineage tracing.
iPSC-derived pellets can be directed either to articular chondrocytes or along the growth
plate pathway to hypertrophic cells that transdifferentiate to osteoblasts and mineralise a
collagen I matrix (GSE219215). What no organoid has produced is the thing the atlas is
about: a stacked, columnar, zonally organised plate with a resting zone, a proliferative
column, a hypertrophic gradient, and a mineralisation front, generating unidirectional
elongation - explicitly identified as an unmet challenge (zhang2025_2). Organoids therefore
currently model the endochondral differentiation trajectory in human cells, not the growth
plate as an organ.
cartilage_organoid.human_evidence_note: These are human cells differentiating along a human endochondral trajectory, which is direct human evidence about the trajectory but not about the organ.
cartilage_organoid.translation_risk_reason: Human genetics and human cells, but no zonal architecture, no mechanical loading and no systemic endocrine input, so organ-level claims do not follow.
localization: ipsc_derived: hypertrophic differentiation achieved; columnar zonal axis not achieved

key_refs.one_line_finding: Engineering a functional growth plate in vitro remains an unresolved challenge.
Collagen X dispensable for hypertrophic differentiation and endochondral ossification of human iPSC-derived cartilage.

key_refs.first_author: Human Growth System Atlas L13 sweep
key_refs.one_line_finding: Human iPSC skeletal organoid and assembloid deposits catalogued in the dataset inventory.

chondrocyte_dissociation_bias.name: Dissociation bias in growth plate single-cell RNA-seq
chondrocyte_dissociation_bias.summary:
Growth plate scRNA-seq requires enzymatic release of cells from a dense, partly mineralised
proteoglycan matrix, and the cell most likely to be destroyed is the one the matrix is
stiffest around and which is largest and most fragile: the terminal hypertrophic
chondrocyte, roughly 5,900 um3 in a human distal tibia (white2008) against a proliferative
chondrocyte an order of magnitude smaller. Two structural facts make the bias hard to
dismiss. First, hypertrophic cells sit within the calcifying zone, so their release requires
either longer digestion (which kills them) or decalcification (which destroys RNA). Second,
standard 10x-style droplet capture excludes particles above roughly 40-50 um, which is
within the diameter range of a terminal hypertrophic chondrocyte. The field's own
methodological reviews name mineralised-matrix dissociation as the principal barrier to
single-cell profiling of skeletal tissue and recommend single-nucleus sequencing to
circumvent it (li2025, delos2026). The quantitative form of the problem has not been
measured in growth plate: no published study compares the zonal composition recovered by
scRNA-seq against the zonal composition counted histologically in the SAME plate, which is
what would convert this from a plausible bias into a correction factor. Until that is done,
every statement of the form "population X is Y% of growth plate cells" derived from
dissociated scRNA-seq should be read as a statement about cells that survived dissociation.

claim_grades.claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes are large and sit in mineralising matrix.
claim_grades.basis: Direct stereological measurement in human tissue and in multiple species.

claim_grades.claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes are systematically lost in growth plate scRNA-seq.
claim_grades.basis: Mechanistically compelled by cell size and matrix, and named as a barrier in methodological reviews, but never quantified against a histological ground truth.

chondrocyte_dissociation_bias.human_evidence_note: Human hypertrophic cell dimensions are measured (white2008) but no human study quantifies recovery loss during dissociation.
chondrocyte_dissociation_bias.translation_risk_reason: The physical basis of the bias (cell size, matrix stiffness) is species-general, but its magnitude scales with hypertrophic cell volume, which is larger in human and large mammals than in mouse.
localization: multiple HZ: systematically under-recovered by dissociation-based protocols (inferred)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mean human hypertrophic chondrocyte volume 5,900 um3 by stereology in a closing distal tibial physis.
Mineralised matrix dissociation is the principal barrier to single-cell profiling of skeletal tissue.
Musculoskeletal spatial and single-cell work is constrained by decalcification and low RNA integrity.
217 cells in the first growth plate scRNA-seq deposit.

computational_model_growth_plate.name: Computational models of the growth plate
computational_model_growth_plate.summary:
Computational models of the growth plate come in two families with different epistemic
status. Cell-kinetic models simulate clone behaviour and column formation from proliferation
and hypertrophy rules - the earliest simulated chondrocytic clone behaviour in rabbit plates
(mosssalentijn1991) - and are parameterised almost entirely from rodent labelling data,
which means they inherit a proliferative cycle time that is roughly tenfold shorter than the
human value inferred from column counts (kember1976). Whole-bone growth models predict
femoral shape and length from personalised multi-scale simulation with reported validation
(koller2025) and have been used to ask how gait modification changes growth plate mechanical
stimulus (koller2026), and canine physeal growth dynamics have been modelled quantitatively
(mcbrien2011). The recurring weakness across the literature is not the mathematics but the
parameter provenance: models of HUMAN growth are routinely fitted with rodent cell-kinetic
constants and rabbit or porcine mechanical constants because the human values do not exist
(g_l1arch_002, g_l5matrix_001). A model built this way can be internally consistent, fit its
calibration data and still be a formalisation of mouse biology. The atlas therefore treats
any in silico human growth plate result as no stronger than the weakest species assumption
in its parameter set.
computational_model_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: Human validation exists at the level of bone shape and length, not at the level of cell kinetics.
computational_model_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: Parameter sets for human models are predominantly rodent, so model outputs about human growth carry rodent cell kinetics inside them.
localization: in_silico: zonal structure is imposed by the model, not derived from human data

key_refs.one_line_finding: Computer simulation of chondrocytic clone behaviour in rabbit growth plates.
Personalised multi-scale femoral growth prediction with validation and sensitivity analysis.
Quantitative growth dynamics of the canine proximal tibial physis.
Human proliferative cycle time about tenfold longer than rodent - the parameter most often transferred.

cre_lox_lineage_tracing.name: Cre-lox lineage tracing in the growth plate
cre_lox_lineage_tracing.summary:
Cre-lox fate mapping is the method that produced the modern growth plate stem cell model,
and it exists only in mouse. Permanent reporter activation in a Cre-expressing cell and its
descendants established that PTHrP-expressing resting zone chondrocytes form columnar clones
after secondary ossification centre formation (mizuhashi2018) and that hypertrophic
chondrocytes transdifferentiate into osteoblasts rather than uniformly dying (zhou2014a).
Both claims are central to L2 and neither has a human counterpart. Three interpretive limits
apply even within mouse. Cre driver specificity is rarely absolute, so a "PTHrP+ lineage" is
really a "PTHrP-promoter-active lineage", including any cell in which the promoter fired
transiently. Reporter recombination efficiency is never 100%, so absence of label is not
absence of contribution. And clone identity requires either sparse labelling or multicolour
reporters; dense labelling produces adjacent same-colour cells that can be miscounted as one
clone. The transfer problem is stated precisely in lineage_tracing_limitations: the property
being measured - long-term clonal behaviour of a progenitor pool - is measured in a species
whose plate never exhausts that pool, because mice do not fuse
(mouse_model_translation_risk).
cre_lox_lineage_tracing.human_evidence_note: The method cannot be applied in humans; all results are murine.
cre_lox_lineage_tracing.translation_risk_reason: Clonal exhaustion is the mechanism proposed for human fusion and cannot occur in the species where clones can be traced.
localization: mouse RZ: PTHrP+ cells traced to columnar clones

key_refs.one_line_finding: PTHrP+ resting zone chondrocytes form columnar clones after secondary ossification centre formation.
Hypertrophic chondrocytes transdifferentiate into osteoblasts during endochondral bone formation.
Timing of resting zone PTHrP expression affects maintenance of the progenitor pool.

dxa_body_composition.name: DXA body composition and skeletal measurement
dxa_body_composition.summary:
DXA measures areal bone mineral density, bone mineral content, lean mass and fat mass at low
radiation dose, which makes it the standard longitudinal skeletal measurement in paediatric
cohorts. Its relationship to the growth plate is entirely indirect and its principal failure
mode in growing children is well defined: areal BMD in g/cm2 is a projection, so it scales
with bone SIZE as well as with true volumetric density, and a short child is systematically
assigned a lower areal BMD for the same tissue-level mineralisation. Any DXA comparison
across children of different stature therefore confounds the exposure of interest - growth -
with the measurement. For this atlas the relevant uses are as covariates and as phenotype
anchors: body composition changes track pubertal stage, and lean mass is the strongest
correlate of bone mass accrual, which is one route by which mechanical loading enters
growth. DXA cannot see the physis: its in-plane resolution is millimetric and it produces no
cartilage signal at all, so it contributes nothing to zonal questions and should never be
used as evidence about growth plate mechanism.
dxa_body_composition.human_evidence_note: DXA is a human clinical measurement, used here only as a covariate and never as growth plate evidence.
localization: human SYS: whole-body or regional bone mineral only

key_refs.one_line_finding: Long bone size and thickness measured in children with cerebral palsy and other neuromuscular conditions - an example of skeletal measurement used as a growth phenotype.

key_refs.first_author: Human Growth System Atlas L13 sweep
key_refs.one_line_finding: Modality coverage audit: DXA contributes no cartilage or zonal signal.

finite_element_model_physis.name: Finite element models of the physis
finite_element_model_physis.summary:
Finite element modelling is how mechanical stress inside a growth plate is estimated,
because it cannot be measured in a living human (g_l6mech_003). Models have been used to
compute how tension-band plates alter mechanical loading of the femoral physis during guided
growth for coronal-plane deformity (hucke2023), how mechanical stimuli shape growth plate
morphology and trabecular adaptation (rodrguez2025), and how gait modification such as
changing foot progression angle alters hip contact forces and physeal mechanics
(koller2026). The models are only as good as three inputs, and each is weak for human
physis. Geometry is usually derived from clinical MRI or CT, which resolves plate thickness
but not zonal boundaries (mri_physis_imaging). Material properties are taken from animal
testing - porcine unconfined compression (sergerie2009), rabbit heterogeneous properties
(eckstein2022), ovine tensile properties (williams2001) - because zonal human physeal moduli
have never been measured, which is exactly gap g_l5matrix_001. And boundary conditions
require joint contact forces that are themselves modelled rather than measured. The output
stress fields are therefore best read as relative comparisons between surgical
configurations in the same model, not as absolute stresses in a real child's physis.
finite_element_model_physis.human_evidence_note: Human geometry is used, human material properties are not available and are substituted from animal testing.
finite_element_model_physis.translation_risk_reason: Absolute stress predictions depend on material constants that are animal-derived; only relative comparisons within a model are defensible.
localization: in_silico RZ/PZ/HZ: zonal material properties assigned from animal data

key_refs.one_line_finding: Tension-band plates modelled to alter femoral growth plate loading during guided growth.
Mechanical stimuli modelled against growth plate morphology and trabecular adaptation.
Foot progression angle modification alters hip contact forces and femoral growth plate mechanics in silico.
Porcine growth plate zonal mechanical properties - a standard source for FE material assignment.

geo_accession_inventory.name: Public dataset inventory for growth plate research (GEO, SRA, ArrayExpress, HCA)
geo_accession_inventory.summary:
A direct census of NCBI GEO quantifies the species bias that constrains every mechanistic
claim in this atlas. Querying GEO DataSets on 2026-08-05, the term "growth plate" returns
1,472 records; restricting to Mus musculus returns 919 and to Homo sapiens returns 141, a
mouse-to-human ratio of roughly 6.5 to 1. The bias sharpens with method sophistication:
growth plate single-cell records number 60, of which 18 are human, while growth plate
spatial-transcriptomics records number 7, of which ZERO are human. Spatial transcriptomics
is precisely the modality that would resolve the zonal questions this atlas repeatedly finds
unanswered - PDE isoform distribution, oxygen-responsive gene gradients, zonal receptor
occupancy - and it has never been applied to human growth plate tissue in any publicly
deposited dataset. Human records that do exist are weighted toward development and disease
rather than normal postnatal zonal architecture; notable exceptions are GSE267139 (human
cartilage development at single-cell resolution, 25 samples) and GSE288028 (growth hormone
action on cartilage stem cells in the human pubertal growth plate, 14 samples, human and
mouse). The practical consequence is that human zonal claims in this atlas rest on histology
and inference, not on transcriptomic measurement. EXTENSION 2026-08-05 (shard l13b): the
census has been converted into an actionable catalogue at atlas/quant/dataset_inventory.csv
- 61 rows spanning GEO, SRA/BioProject, ArrayExpress/BioStudies, the Human Cell Atlas, GTEx,
the Human Protein Atlas and supplementary data from key papers, each row carrying species,
age, anatomical site, sample and cell counts, platform, modality, whether zonal identity is
resolvable, and the existing atlas gap_id the dataset could close on reanalysis. Forty-five
of the 61 rows map to at least one existing gap, and together they touch 36 distinct gap_ids
across L1, L2, L3, L4, L5, L6, L7, L8, L11 and L13. Three results dominate. (1) GSE9160 is
the highest-value entry in the atlas: laser-microdissected resting, proliferative,
prehypertrophic, hypertrophic and perichondrial samples from the distal femoral growth
plates of two normal children, which answers "is transcript X present in human zone Y" for
any probed gene without new tissue - and the entire human zonal transcriptome therefore
rests on n=2 donors. (2) The one human growth plate scRNA-seq deposit, GSE288028, states in
its own GEO record that raw human files were withheld for identifiability reasons, so the
flagship human dataset is not reanalysable at read level. (3) Two documented nulls carry
mechanistic consequences: GTEx's 54 tissues include no cartilage and no paediatric donors,
which is why height-GWAS variants cannot be colocalised in the tissue that produces height,
and the Human Cell Atlas organ vocabulary contains no cartilage or growth plate term at all.
geo_accession_inventory.human_evidence_note: The census itself is a direct, reproducible measurement of the public data landscape, executed against the live NCBI E-utilities API.
geo_accession_inventory.translation_risk_reason: This node measures translation risk rather than incurring it - it is the quantitative basis for the high translation_risk grades used elsewhere.
localization: not applicable: this node describes the data landscape, not a tissue

key_refs.one_line_finding: Census of GEO DataSets: 1,472 growth plate records, 919 mouse vs 141 human; 7 spatial-transcriptomics records of which 0 are human.
Human cartilage development at single-cell resolution, 25 samples.
Growth hormone directly stimulates cartilage stem cells in the human pubertal growth plate; 14 samples, human and mouse.

key_refs.first_author: Human Growth System Atlas L13 sweep
key_refs.one_line_finding: 61-row multi-repository inventory; 45 rows map to 36 distinct existing gap_ids.
Zone-resolved human growth plate transcriptome from two normal children - the only one that exists.
Human growth plate biopsies under controlled mechanical loading, three donors, 18 biopsies.

growth_plate_explant_culture.name: Growth plate explant culture
growth_plate_explant_culture.summary:
Explant culture keeps a piece of intact growth plate alive with its zonal architecture and
matrix intact, which is the only way to apply a defined stimulus to a growth plate without
systemic confounding. It is the format in which the two most informative human growth plate
experiments were done: human biopsies from three epiphysiodesis patients were mechanically
loaded at 0.4 N and 0.77 Hz for 30 seconds then cultured 24 hours before RNA-seq (gse246390,
zhang2024a), and human growth plate cartilage from five donors was exposed to radial
shockwave with unexposed tissue from the same limb as control (ramesh2022). Both designs use
within-subject controls, which is the correct response to n being small. In animals the
format supports controlled compression with viability and strain readouts (kaviani2015,
kaviani2016, sergerie2011, zimmermann2017) and matrix-turnover measurement (xu2026,
shapses1994). The limits are stated by the format: no blood supply, so oxygen and nutrient
gradients differ from in vivo and the hypertrophic zone - already the most hypoxic - is the
first to suffer; no systemic endocrine input unless supplied; and viable culture windows
measured in days, so anything slower than a few cell cycles is inaccessible. For human
tissue the binding constraint remains supply, not technique.
growth_plate_explant_culture.human_evidence_note: Two human growth plate explant experiments exist, both with within-subject controls and n of 3 and 5 donors.
growth_plate_explant_culture.translation_risk_reason: Where the explant is human the tissue is human; risk enters only when porcine or bovine explant parameters are used to set expectations for human tissue.
localization: human PZ/HZ: intact zonal architecture retained in explant

key_refs.one_line_finding: Human growth plate biopsies from three donors loaded under controlled conditions then RNA-sequenced.
Human growth plate cartilage from five donors exposed to radial shockwave with same-limb controls.
Growth plate cartilage shows different strain patterns under static versus dynamic loading.
In situ chondrocyte deformation measured in stress-controlled compression of explants.

growth_velocity_measurement_interval.name: Growth velocity measurement interval
growth_velocity_measurement_interval.summary:
Growth velocity is a derivative, and the interval over which it is computed sets both its
noise and the biology it can see. Because measurement error propagates as roughly twice the
single-measurement error divided by the interval, halving the interval doubles the velocity
noise; this is the arithmetic behind the clinical convention of computing height velocity
over intervals of at least six months, and behind the fact that short-interval trials use
knemometry rather than stadiometry. The interval also determines which growth model is
testable. The saltation-and-stasis model claims that human growth occurs in discrete
elongation events separated by true-zero stasis (lampl1992); testing it requires daily-to-
sub-weekly resolution, which stadiometry cannot supply and which rabbit measurements at high
