frequency contradicted by finding continuous growth (klein1994). Seasonal variation adds a
further constraint: an interval shorter than a year confounds treatment effect with season.
The practical rule this atlas applies is that a reported velocity without a stated interval
and a stated measurement technique is not a usable number, and that velocities computed over
intervals under three months should be treated as instrument noise unless obtained by
knemometry.
growth_velocity_measurement_interval.human_evidence_note: All the constraints are properties of human clinical measurement.
growth_velocity_measurement_interval.translation_risk_reason: Human measurement statistics; the rabbit comparison is flagged explicitly as the animal counterweight to the human saltation claim.
localization: human SYS: whole-body or segment-level only

key_refs.one_line_finding: Saltation-and-stasis model of human growth requiring sub-weekly measurement to test.
Rabbit linear growth is continuous, not saltatory, when measured at high frequency.
Precision comparison of knemometric techniques, the alternative to long-interval stadiometry.

histomorphometry_physis.name: Growth plate histomorphometry
histomorphometry_physis.summary:
Histomorphometry - measuring zone heights, cell counts per column, cell dimensions and
matrix fractions on stained sections - is the method that produced almost every quantitative
statement about the human growth plate in this atlas, and it has been applied to a very
small number of human plates. Kember and Sissons estimated 24 cells per column in the human
proliferative zone and, combined with a distal femoral growth rate of about 1.4 cm/year from
serial radiographs, derived a mean proliferative cell cycle time of 20 days, explicitly
warning that the corresponding rodent figure is 2 days and that extrapolation from mouse to
man is unwise (kember1976). Byers measured zone heights and matrix volume fractions in human
rib from birth to adolescence and found the largest change in the first postnatal year
(byers2000). Rodriguez measured plate thickness falling from 1.15 mm at 20 weeks to 0.6 mm
at 38 weeks across 125 perinatal donors (rodriguez1992). Emons quantified the pubertal
narrowing of total plate height and of each zone, with increasing intercolumnar space,
within a single girl studied at Tanner B2 and B3 (emons2011_2). The method's optical
resolution (roughly 0.25 um lateral) far exceeds every dimension of interest, so its limits
are not optical: they are section-plane obliquity, shrinkage during fixation and
decalcification, and the fact that a two-dimensional section cannot recover a three-
dimensional cell volume without stereological correction (breur1994, white2008).

claim_grades.claim: Human proliferative zone columns contain about 24 cells.
claim_grades.basis: Direct count in kember1976; never independently replicated in human tissue.

claim_grades.claim: Human proliferative chondrocyte cycle time is about 20 days.
claim_grades.basis: Derived from a column count and a radiographic growth rate, not measured by labelling; see gap g_l1arch_002.

histomorphometry_physis.human_evidence_note: All three quantitative anchors were measured on human tissue sections.
histomorphometry_physis.translation_risk_reason: Human measurements; the node exists partly to flag that the rodent equivalent differs tenfold.
localization: human PZ: cells per column measured directly
human HZ: cell volume requires stereological correction

key_refs.one_line_finding: 24 cells per column and a derived 20-day cycle time in human distal femur, with an explicit warning against rodent extrapolation.
Zone heights and matrix volume fractions in human rib from birth to adolescence, largest change in the first year.
Plate thickness 1.15 mm to 0.6 mm across the second half of gestation in 125 donors.
Total and zonal plate height fall and intercolumnar space rises between Tanner B2 and B3 within one girl.

human_cell_atlas_skeletal.name: Skeletal coverage of the Human Cell Atlas
human_cell_atlas_skeletal.summary:
The Human Cell Atlas does not contain the growth plate. Its organ vocabulary, queried on
2026-08-05, includes bone marrow (9 projects), bone tissue (6), bone element (1), femur (1),
hindlimb (3), limb (1), skeletal element (1) and musculoskeletal system (1) - and contains
no term for cartilage or growth plate at all, so no project is indexed to physeal tissue.
The projects returned under skeletal terms are a fetal bone marrow haematopoiesis atlas, a
multiple-myeloma study, a lung-metastasis study, an adult femoral head, a neuroblastoma
study and Tabula Muris. The nearest relevant HCA resource is the human embryonic limb atlas,
which does contain chondrocyte lineages resolved in space and time at 5-9 post-conception
weeks (zhang2024_2), and an adult intervertebral disc atlas that includes vertebral endplate
cartilage. Neither covers a postnatal growth plate. The practical effect is that the
reference cell atlas the rest of biology uses to annotate human cell states cannot annotate
a growth plate chondrocyte; annotation is done instead against mouse growth plate
references, which is the species-transfer step that recurs throughout this layer.
human_cell_atlas_skeletal.human_evidence_note: Direct enumeration of the live HCA index.
human_cell_atlas_skeletal.translation_risk_reason: Measures the human reference resource itself.
localization: human SYS: growth plate absent from the reference human cell atlas

key_refs.first_author: Human Growth System Atlas L13 sweep
key_refs.one_line_finding: HCA organ vocabulary contains no cartilage or growth plate term; 6 bone tissue and 9 bone marrow projects.
Human embryonic limb cell atlas - the nearest HCA resource containing chondrocyte lineages.

human_growth_plate_biobank.name: Absence of a human growth plate biobank
human_growth_plate_biobank.summary:
No dedicated, catalogued, openly accessible biobank of human growth plate tissue was located
in this sweep. What exists instead is a set of single-centre, investigator-held collections
accumulated from surgical discard, each visible only through the papers that used it: a
Stockholm epiphysiodesis series (nilsson1999, nilsson2003, ramesh2022, zhang2024a, chu2026),
a Vienna polydactyly series (walzer2014, zoehrer2025), and assorted single-specimen holdings
(white2008, wang2014, sales2009). The consequences are measurable rather than rhetorical.
Donor counts per study run from 1 to 24 (human_gp_donor_census_20260805). The one
transcriptomic study that did profile human growth plate cells at single-cell resolution
explicitly withheld its raw human data from GEO - the accession states that raw files were
not submitted because of identifiability concerns (gse288028) - so the flagship human
dataset cannot be reanalysed at the read level. Tissue-derived measurements that would
answer standing atlas questions (zonal oxygen tension, zonal modulus, zonal receptor
occupancy) each require fresh tissue, and each investigator must therefore re-solicit tissue
from scratch. The absence is not technological: bone-tumour biobanks, fetal tissue
programmes and paediatric orthopaedic services already handle this material; what is missing
is a shared, consented, age- and site-annotated repository with a public catalogue.

claim_grades.claim: No public human growth plate biobank exists.
claim_grades.basis: Reproducible null across three repositories plus a literature sweep; a private or unpublicised collection cannot be excluded.

claim_grades.claim: Raw human sequence data from the only human growth plate scRNA-seq deposit are withheld.
claim_grades.basis: Stated in the GEO series record for GSE288028.

human_growth_plate_biobank.human_evidence_note: The absence was established by direct search of the repositories that would hold such a collection.
human_growth_plate_biobank.translation_risk_reason: Describes human research infrastructure; nothing is transferred from an animal.
localization: human SYS: not applicable - infrastructure, not anatomy

human_growth_plate_tissue_scarcity.name: Scarcity and provenance bias of human growth plate tissue
human_growth_plate_tissue_scarcity.summary:
A donor census executed on 2026-08-05 across the atlas bibliography and a Europe PMC title
sweep located 30 studies that examined human growth plate tissue directly. Twenty-one of
them state a donor count; those 21 sum to 259 distinct human donors. Of these, 157 are fetal
or perinatal autopsy specimens - 125 from a single 1992 series of 46 stillborns and 79
newborns (rodriguez1992), 20 sudden-infant-death sternochondral specimens (werther1990) and
12 fetal to 13-month bodies (strangevognsen1997). Only 102 donors contributed a POSTNATAL,
still-growing growth plate, and every one of those came from surgical waste: epiphysiodesis
or epiphyseal surgery, polydactyly digit resection, amputation for osteosarcoma or trauma,
or transplant salvage. The largest single postnatal series is 24 proximal tibial biopsies
(16 boys, 8 girls, Tanner 1-5) from a 2003 immunohistochemistry study that was never
deposited in any repository (nilsson2003). The 102 figure is an upper bound because several
Stockholm-based studies (nilsson1999, nilsson2003, ramesh2022, zhang2024a, chu2026)
plausibly draw on one accumulating biopsy bank; it is also a lower bound in the sense that 9
further located studies do not state their donor count. Two consequences follow directly.
First, "the normal human growth plate" is a composite of tissue from children who were
having surgery, most often for limb-length discrepancy, excessive predicted height, a
supernumerary digit or a bone tumour, so normality is assumed rather than demonstrated.
Second, the mouse-to-human asymmetry is not merely literary: GEO holds 919 mouse growth
plate records against 141 human (geo_census_20260805), while the entire human histological
corpus rests on roughly one hundred growing plates.

claim_grades.claim: At most about 100 postnatal growing human growth plates have been examined in studies that state a donor count.
claim_grades.basis: Arithmetic over stated donor counts in 21 located primary studies; reproducible from atlas/quant/human_growth_plate_donor_census.csv.

claim_grades.claim: The true number of distinct postnatal donors is lower than 102 because of cohort overlap.
claim_grades.basis: Inference from shared authorship and single-centre recruitment; not verified against patient identifiers.

claim_grades.claim: Essentially all postnatal human growth plate tissue is surgical waste.
claim_grades.basis: Provenance is stated in each source: epiphysiodesis, polydactyly, amputation, transplant salvage.

human_growth_plate_tissue_scarcity.human_evidence_note: The census counts human donors in human studies; it is a direct measurement of the human evidence base.
human_growth_plate_tissue_scarcity.translation_risk_reason: This node measures the size of the human evidence base rather than transferring an animal claim.
localization: human PERI: not applicable - this node describes tissue supply, not anatomy

key_refs.first_author: Human Growth System Atlas L13 sweep
key_refs.one_line_finding: 30 human growth-plate tissue studies located; 21 state donor counts summing to 259 donors, of which 102 are postnatal.
Proximal tibial growth plate histology in 46 stillborns and 79 newborns - the largest human series in existence, and entirely perinatal.
Proximal tibial growth plate biopsies from 16 boys and 8 girls across Tanner 1-5 - the largest postnatal series located.
GH receptor localised in sternochondral growth cartilage from 20 sudden-infant-death donors.
919 mouse versus 141 human growth plate records in GEO DataSets.

immunohistochemistry_cartilage_artifact.name: Artefact modes of cartilage immunohistochemistry
immunohistochemistry_cartilage_artifact.summary:
Most of what is asserted about protein localisation in the HUMAN growth plate rests on
immunohistochemistry, and the human growth plate is close to a worst case for that method.
The matrix is a dense polyanionic proteoglycan gel that binds cationic antibodies non-
specifically; decalcification, required wherever the hypertrophic zone or chondro-osseous
junction is included, degrades epitopes and the effect is agent- and duration-dependent; and
antigen retrieval protocols that work in soft tissue must be re-optimised for cartilage. The
field's own record shows the consequence. Estrogen receptor localisation in the human growth
plate was described as "controversial" in the paper that set out to resolve it
(nilsson2003): one group reported ER-alpha and ER-beta restricted to hypertrophic
chondrocytes (egerbacher2002), while another, counting positive cells across zones in 24
donors, found 64% ER-alpha positivity in resting and proliferative zones against 38% in the
hypertrophic zone - the opposite gradient (nilsson2003). Both used polyclonal antibodies of
the era on epiphysiodesis tissue. The discrepancy has never been resolved by an orthogonal
method in human tissue, because the orthogonal methods - zonal transcriptomics with in situ
validation, or spatial proteomics - have been applied to human physis in only two studies
(gse9160, xie2025). The practical rule this atlas applies: a human zonal localisation
supported only by IHC, without a stated antibody validation and without an independent
method, does not exceed grade D.

claim_grades.claim: Human growth plate ER-alpha zonal distribution is reported in mutually exclusive ways by two IHC studies.
claim_grades.basis: Both primary reports read; quantitative gradient in nilsson2003 versus hypertrophic-only restriction in egerbacher2002.

claim_grades.claim: The discrepancy is caused by antibody and decalcification artefact.
claim_grades.basis: Plausible and consistent with the known chemistry, but not experimentally demonstrated.

immunohistochemistry_cartilage_artifact.human_evidence_note: The contradiction is between two human-tissue immunohistochemistry studies, so the evidence at issue is human throughout.
immunohistochemistry_cartilage_artifact.translation_risk_reason: A methodological property of human tissue staining; nothing is transferred across species.
localization: human RZ: ER-alpha reported positive by nilsson2003 and negative by egerbacher2002 - unresolved

key_refs.one_line_finding: ER-alpha and ER-beta more frequent in resting and proliferative than hypertrophic zone, quantified across 24 donors.
ER-alpha and ER-beta immunostaining restricted to hypertrophic chondrocytes in four epiphysiodesis donors.
ER-beta positive only in hypertrophic chondrocytes in four female pubertal donors - agreeing with egerbacher2002 and not with nilsson2003.
Zone-resolved human transcriptome that could adjudicate zonal expression claims at the RNA level.

in_situ_hybridization_cartilage.name: In situ hybridization in growth plate cartilage
in_situ_hybridization_cartilage.summary:
In situ hybridization is the reference method for assigning a transcript to a zone, and it
is the method by which the mouse zonal map of the growth plate was built (stjacques1999,
long2001). Its application to human physis is sparse and technically constrained. The
proteoglycan-rich matrix retains probe non-specifically; the hypertrophic and calcifying
zones require decalcification, which fragments RNA; and post-mortem or delayed-fixation
surgical tissue starts with degraded RNA before any processing. The consequences are visible
in the atlas's evidence base: human zonal expression statements are dominated by protein
immunohistochemistry, which has its own artefact modes
(immunohistochemistry_cartilage_artifact), rather than by transcript localisation. Where
human transcript-level zonal data do exist, they come from laser-capture microdissection
followed by array (gse9160) rather than from ISH, so they carry dissection-boundary error
rather than probe-specificity error. Modern branched-probe chemistries (RNAscope-class)
tolerate degraded RNA far better than classical riboprobes and are the obvious route to a
human zonal transcript map, but no systematic RNAscope survey of human growth plate zones
was located in this sweep.
in_situ_hybridization_cartilage.human_evidence_note: No systematic ISH-based zonal transcript map of the human growth plate was located; human zonal transcript data come from microdissection arrays instead.
in_situ_hybridization_cartilage.translation_risk_reason: The entire zonal transcript map that the field reasons with is murine, and the murine plate differs from the human one in cycle time, cell size and terminal fate.
localization: mouse PHZ: Ihh and Ptch1 zonal assignment established by ISH
human PHZ: no equivalent transcript map

key_refs.one_line_finding: Ihh zonal expression and function established in mouse growth plate.
Hedgehog signalling manipulated and mapped in the mouse endochondral skeleton.
Human zonal transcript data obtained by laser capture rather than in situ hybridization.

ipsc_chondrogenesis.name: iPSC-derived chondrogenesis as a human model system
ipsc_chondrogenesis.summary:
iPSC chondrogenesis is the only system in which a HUMAN genotype can be studied
prospectively in growth plate-like cells, which makes it the natural test bed for the
skeletal dysplasia alleles catalogued in L11. Directed differentiation through sclerotome to
chondroprogenitors in 3D pellet culture yields either articular chondrocytes or, along the
growth plate pathway, hypertrophic chondrocytes that transdifferentiate to osteoblasts and
deposit a mineralising collagen I matrix (GSE219215). The system has already produced a non-
trivial negative result relevant to L5: collagen X is dispensable for hypertrophic
differentiation and endochondral ossification of human iPSC-derived cartilage
(kamakura2023), which parallels the mild human phenotype of COL10A1 mutation in Schmid
metaphyseal chondrodysplasia and speaks directly to gap g_l5matrix_005. Three limits are
decisive. Directed differentiation produces a developmental-stage cell resembling fetal
cartilage, not a postnatal growth plate chondrocyte, and the transcriptional comparison in
the assembloid work is explicitly against human EMBRYONIC skeletal tissue. Line-to-line
variability between iPSC clones is large relative to many effect sizes of interest, so
isogenic controls are mandatory. And no protocol produces zonal organisation (zhang2025_2), so
allele effects on column formation or on the hypertrophic set point cannot be assayed.
ipsc_chondrogenesis.human_evidence_note: Human cells carrying human genotypes; the evidence is human but the developmental stage is fetal-like.
ipsc_chondrogenesis.translation_risk_reason: Human genotype and human cells, but fetal-like stage, no zonal architecture and substantial line-to-line variance.
localization: ipsc_derived HZ: hypertrophic phenotype reproducible; zonal context absent

key_refs.one_line_finding: Collagen X dispensable for hypertrophic differentiation and endochondral ossification in human iPSC-derived cartilage.
No protocol yields zonal growth plate organisation in vitro.
hPSC-derived articular and growth plate chondrocytes benchmarked against human fetal femur cells.

knemometry.name: Knemometry
knemometry.summary:
Knemometry measures lower leg length - knee to heel - with a purpose-built device, at a
precision high enough to detect growth over days to weeks rather than months, which is what
standing-height stadiometry cannot do. Its clinical use is as a short-term growth bioassay:
it is more sensitive to the systemic effects of inhaled corticosteroids in asthmatic
children than 24-hour urinary cortisol excretion (chawes2017), and it is the standard
readout in two-week corticosteroid growth-suppression crossover trials (wolthers2017). Two
knemometric techniques have been formally compared for precision in childhood (ahmed1995),
and mini-knemometry has been applied in premature infants (keller2004) and in field settings
outside a clinic (urlacher2016). The limits that matter for this atlas are three. It
measures ONE segment, the tibia, so it does not report whole-stature growth and cannot
detect differential segment growth. Its precision is purchased by immobilising the leg and
applying a defined axial force, so soft-tissue compression is part of the signal. And it is
a tissue-level output measure: it tells you the plate elongated, never which zone did it,
which is the general limitation of every non-invasive human growth measurement
(g_l1arch_014).
knemometry.human_evidence_note: Knemometry is exclusively a human clinical measurement.
localization: human SYS: tibial segment length only

key_refs.one_line_finding: Knemometry more sensitive to systemic corticosteroid effect than 24-hour urinary cortisol in asthmatic children.
Two-week randomised placebo-controlled crossover knemometry of short-term growth under fluticasone furoate.
Precision of two knemometric techniques compared in childhood.
Knemometry applied to measure childhood short-term growth in a field population.

laser_capture_microdissection_zonal.name: Laser capture microdissection of growth plate zones
laser_capture_microdissection_zonal.summary:
Laser capture microdissection is the technique that produced the only zone-resolved
transcriptome of a human growth plate. Cells corresponding to hypertrophic, prehypertrophic,
proliferative and resting zones plus perichondrium were separately isolated from cryostat
sections of distal femoral growth plate from two normal children (an 11-year-10-month girl
and a 13-year-3-month boy), amplified by T7 linear amplification and hybridised to
Affymetrix arrays; 12,193 and 18,454 probe sets were called present in patients 1 and 2,
with homologous inter-array correlations of at least 0.91 (gse9160). The rodent counterpart,
built the same way, comprises 35 arrays from microdissected rat plates (gse16981), and it is
that rat dataset - not the human one - that has been used to interpret height GWAS loci
(lui2012). The method's limits are boundary error and RNA yield: zone boundaries are
assigned by morphology on a frozen section, so prehypertrophic and early hypertrophic
capture inevitably overlap, and picogram RNA inputs require linear amplification with its
own 3' bias. Its strength is decisive for this atlas: because the capture is spatial,
GSE9160 answers "is transcript X present in human zone Y" for any probed gene without new
tissue, which is why it is flagged in the dataset inventory as the single highest-value re-
analysis target.

claim_grades.claim: Zone-resolved human growth plate transcriptomes exist and are public.
claim_grades.basis: GSE9160 is deposited with raw CEL files.

claim_grades.claim: Any given transcript detected in GSE9160 is genuinely zone-restricted.
claim_grades.basis: n=2 donors, morphological boundary assignment and 3prime-biased linear amplification; single-gene conclusions need independent confirmation.

laser_capture_microdissection_zonal.human_evidence_note: GSE9160 is a direct human zone-resolved measurement, albeit from two donors.
laser_capture_microdissection_zonal.translation_risk_reason: For human-derived conclusions the data are human; risk enters only when the rat dataset is substituted for the human one, which is common practice.
localization: human RZ/PZ/PHZ/HZ/PERI: all five captured separately in gse9160

key_refs.one_line_finding: Zone-specific expression profiles of human distal femoral growth plate from two normal children.
Rat growth plate microdissected into constituent zones, 35 arrays.
Height GWAS loci interpreted using rodent growth plate expression data, implicating 78 genes.
Microdissection-based zonal analysis applied to CNP signalling in growth plate.

lineage_tracing_limitations.name: Unavailability of lineage tracing in humans
lineage_tracing_limitations.summary:
Every clonal claim in L2 - that resting zone chondrocytes self-renew, that a single
progenitor generates a column, that hypertrophic chondrocytes transdifferentiate into
osteoblasts - was established by genetic lineage tracing in mice (mizuhashi2018, zhou2014a)
and cannot be tested by the same method in humans, because it requires germline recombinase
alleles and a reporter locus. The human substitutes are all weaker in a specific, statable
way. (1) Xenograft barcoding: human fetal skeletal stem cells were lentivirally barcoded and
their clones read out by scRNA-seq after transplantation into mice (gse233188). This
measures potency under ectopic graft conditions, not native fate in a growth plate. (2)
Somatic mutation phylogenies from bulk or single-cell sequencing require tissue at
sufficient depth and have not been applied to human physis. (3) Static marker colocalisation
- the approach used in the only human growth plate single-cell study (chu2026) - identifies
candidate stem populations by expression profile, then infers lineage from the mouse. The
consequence is that human clonal claims are, without exception, either mouse claims
transferred by homology or human correlations whose direction cannot be established. The
atlas therefore grades every clonal statement about human growth plate cells no higher than
C unless it rests on a human-tissue readout, and gap g_l2stem_001 is a method_blocked gap
for exactly this reason.

claim_grades.claim: Genetic lineage tracing cannot be performed in humans.
claim_grades.basis: Categorical: the method requires engineered germline alleles.

claim_grades.claim: Xenograft barcoding measures potency rather than native fate.
claim_grades.basis: Design of gse233188: readout is in an ectopic mouse graft, not a human growth plate.

lineage_tracing_limitations.human_evidence_note: No human in vivo clonal fate data exist; the nearest human data are xenograft barcode experiments that measure potency, not native fate.
lineage_tracing_limitations.translation_risk_reason: Clonal architecture is exactly the property that differs between a lifelong-open murine plate and a fusing human plate, so transferring murine clonal dynamics is transferring the property most likely to diverge.
localization: human RZ: clonal behaviour untestable in situ

key_refs.one_line_finding: PTHrP+ resting zone chondrocytes form columnar clones - established by Cre-lox tracing in mouse.
Hypertrophic chondrocytes transdifferentiate into osteoblasts - a lineage-tracing result, mouse only.
Barcoded human fetal growth plate skeletal stem cells clonally tracked after xenotransplantation.
Human resting-zone stem-like populations identified by expression profile; the clonal claim is supplied by parallel mouse tracing.

metatarsal_explant_culture.name: Fetal metatarsal explant culture
metatarsal_explant_culture.summary:
Cultured fetal rodent metatarsals are the workhorse pharmacological assay for longitudinal
bone growth: whole rudiments grow measurably in culture over days, so a compound's effect on
elongation can be read as a length change without confounding by appetite, systemic
endocrine feedback or skeletal loading. The format established that androgen receptor
modulation does not affect longitudinal growth of cultured fetal rat metatarsals
(chagin2009), and it is the system in which FGF signalling was shown to inhibit chondrocyte
proliferation through STAT signalling (sahni1999). Its principal structural caveat is
anatomical rather than technical: in mammalian metatarsals the growth plate occupies an
unusual location, and the PTHrP/Ihh feedback loop operates there in a configuration that is
not the standard long-bone one (reno2025), so metatarsal results are not automatically
statements about femoral or tibial physes. Two further limits matter for translation. The
rudiments are fetal, so they have no secondary ossification centre and therefore no resting
zone in the postnatal sense - which is the compartment L2 is about. And they are rodent,
inheriting the full mouse/rat translation risk. No human equivalent exists, because fetal
human rudiments are not available at the scale a dose-response requires.
metatarsal_explant_culture.human_evidence_note: No human counterpart; all metatarsal culture pharmacology is rodent.
metatarsal_explant_culture.translation_risk_reason: Fetal, rodent, and located at a site where the PTHrP/Ihh loop configuration differs from the standard long-bone physis.
localization: rat PZ/HZ: present in cultured rudiment; RZ in the postnatal sense absent

key_refs.one_line_finding: Androgen receptor modulation does not affect longitudinal growth of cultured fetal rat metatarsals.
FGF signalling inhibits chondrocyte proliferation via STAT in cultured rudiments.
The PTHrP/Ihh feedback loop operates in an unusual configuration at the mammalian metatarsal growth plate.

micro_ct_growth_plate.name: Micro-CT of the growth plate
micro_ct_growth_plate.summary:
Micro-CT images mineral, and the growth plate is the one part of a long bone that is
deliberately not mineralised, so the modality reports the plate as a radiolucent gap bounded
by two mineralised surfaces. What it measures well is therefore the geometry of that gap and
the mineralised structures crossing it: transphyseal bony bridges in mouse tibiae have been
counted and their density quantified, giving 495 bridges at density 1.2 in wild-type sham
tibiae versus 187 bridges at density 14.4 in Socs2-/- (samvelyan2022). Against the
dimensions that matter, a laboratory micro-CT at 5-10 um voxel resolves plate thickness
(0.6-1.15 mm in the human fetal proximal tibia, rodriguez1992) and zone heights comfortably,
sits at the edge of resolving a chondrocyte lacuna (a human terminal hypertrophic cell is
about 5,900 um3, roughly 22 um equivalent diameter, white2008), and cannot resolve a cell
without contrast staining because soft cartilage generates almost no X-ray attenuation
contrast. Contrast-enhanced protocols (phosphotungstic acid, iodine, ionic contrast agents)
recover cartilage contrast but require fixation and full penetration, so they are terminal
and are not applicable in vivo. Clinical CT inherits none of this resolution: it images the
physis at sub-millimetre voxels at best and at a radiation dose that forbids serial
paediatric use, which is why growth plate imaging in living children is done by MRI or
ultrasound.
micro_ct_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: Human physeal micro-CT is confined to ex vivo surgical or autopsy specimens; the quantitative bridge data cited are murine.
micro_ct_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: The physics is species-independent, but bridge counts and plate geometry are not: the murine plate never completes bridging, so murine bridge metrics do not index human fusion.
localization: multiple ZPC: micro-CT resolves the mineralisation front directly
multiple PZ: invisible without contrast agent

key_refs.one_line_finding: Transphyseal bony bridges counted and their density quantified by micro-CT in mouse tibiae.
Human proximal tibial plate thickness falls from 1.15 mm to 0.6 mm across the second half of gestation.
Human terminal hypertrophic chondrocyte volume 5,900 um3 - the cellular target dimension.

micromass_culture.name: Micromass chondrogenic culture
micromass_culture.summary:
Micromass culture plates mesenchymal cells at high density so that condensation and
chondrogenesis occur in vitro, reproducing the earliest step of endochondral development in
a format that supports dozens of parallel conditions. Its value in this atlas is upstream:
it models condensation and early differentiation, not the zonal growth plate. The
distinction is not pedantic, because the properties the atlas cares about - column
formation, a resting-zone progenitor pool, a hypertrophic volume set point, terminal fusion
- are all emergent properties of a spatially organised tissue with a secondary ossification
centre and a mechanical environment, and none of them appears in micromass. Monolayer
expansion before micromass compounds the problem: growth plate chondrocytes dedifferentiate
rapidly in monolayer, which is visible in the atlas's own dataset inventory, where the human
growth plate chondrocyte microarray deposits are monolayer-expanded cells whose zonal
identity has already been destroyed (GSE1277, GSE1278). Micromass therefore answers
questions about chondrogenic competence and about the response of chondrocytes to a soluble
factor, and does not answer questions about zonal organisation.
micromass_culture.human_evidence_note: Human cells can be used, but the structure being modelled is not the human growth plate.
micromass_culture.translation_risk_reason: Reproduces condensation, not zonal architecture, so any inference about growth plate organisation is unsupported by the model itself.
localization: in_vitro_human_cell: no zonal axis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Engineering a functional growth plate in vitro remains unachieved; existing constructs lack zonal organisation.
Zonal identity of human growth plate cells is a spatial property that culture formats do not preserve.

mouse_model_translation_risk.name: Mouse model translation risk
mouse_model_translation_risk.summary:
The mouse supplies roughly 90% of growth plate mechanism and cannot express the endpoint
that defines human growth: the mouse growth plate is never replaced by bone. At 55 weeks the
murine plate is still a discrete cartilaginous band with raised mineral content but retained
aggrecan glycosaminoglycan, and with type X collagen and MMP-13 - present at 10 weeks - now
absent, so the terminal differentiation programme is switched off rather than completed
(yu2025). Mice do form countable transphyseal bridges (495 at density 1.2 in wild-type sham
tibiae; 187 at density 14.4 in Socs2-/-), so bridging is real and quantifiable but never
proceeds to plate destruction (samvelyan2022). Tempo diverges as sharply: the proliferative
chondrocyte cycle time is about 2 days in rodent against about 20 days inferred in human
(kember1976), a tenfold difference in the rate constant that every model of column kinetics
uses. Scale diverges too - a murine plate is a few hundred micrometres thick against 1-10 mm
in human. Translation risk score used in this layer runs 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest) and is
the mean of four sub-scores, each 1-5: (A) fusion competence - can the species express
epiphyseal fusion at all; (B) plate architecture - columnar organisation and secondary
ossification centre; (C) scale - plate thickness and hypertrophic cell volume relative to
human; (D) tempo - proliferative cycle time and growth duration relative to human. Mouse
scores A=5, B=2, C=4, D=5, mean 4.0, giving translation_risk high. The one compensating
strength is decisive and should not be understated: mouse is the only species in which
conditional genetics and lineage tracing are available, so it is the only place mechanism
can be established at all - which is exactly why the transfer problem cannot be avoided by
choosing a different species.
mouse_model_translation_risk.human_evidence_note: The node is about transferability; the human comparator facts come from human histology and imaging, not from mouse.
mouse_model_translation_risk.translation_risk_reason: Mice cannot fuse, so no murine experiment can be an experiment about fusion; tempo and scale differ by roughly an order of magnitude in the same direction.
localization: mouse HZ: type X collagen and MMP-13 present at 10 weeks, absent at 55 weeks

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mouse growth plate persists as calcified cartilage at 55 weeks with loss of collagen X and MMP-13.
Countable transphyseal bridges in mouse tibiae that never complete plate replacement.
Human proliferative cycle time about 20 days against 2 days in rodent; explicit warning against extrapolation.
Murine conditional genetics established the resting zone stem cell, an experiment impossible in human.

mri_physis_imaging.name: MRI of the human physis
mri_physis_imaging.summary:
MRI is the only modality that images a growth plate repeatedly in a living child, and it
operates one to two orders of magnitude coarser than the cells it would need to see. At 7 T
with a 28-channel knee coil, gradient-echo phase imaging of six healthy children aged 6-15
resolved veins and LAYERS within growth cartilage - the zonal scale - in all children up to
age 13, but not individual chondrocytes (dymerska2018). Clinical-field MRI is used to stage
physeal closure rather than to measure cellular events: cartilage-weighted and T1-weighted
sequences give reliable closure staging across readers (kvist2020), and cross-sectional MRI
cohorts have been used to determine what governs closure timing (kvist2021). Quantitative MR
has reached tissue composition in animal physis - T1 mapping calibrated water content in
porcine growth plate (shiguetomimedi2013) - and fixed charge density has been measured by
NMR in cartilage (lesperance1992), so composition is in principle accessible. Against the
dimensions that matter: plate thickness (1-10 mm) and zone heights (100-1000 um) are within
reach at 7 T; a 10-20 um chondrocyte is not, at any field strength usable in a child. The
consequence is precise. MRI can tell you that a plate narrowed, or that a bridge formed, or
that closure advanced a Sanders-equivalent stage - it cannot tell you whether the resting
zone lost cells, which is the mechanism every fusion hypothesis in L7 turns on.
mri_physis_imaging.human_evidence_note: All cited physeal MRI studies are in living human children.
mri_physis_imaging.translation_risk_reason: The imaging claims are human; only the T1-water-content calibration is porcine and is flagged as such.
localization: human PZ: zone-scale layering visible at 7 T
human RZ: cell-level events invisible at all clinical field strengths

key_refs.one_line_finding: 7 T phase imaging resolves veins and layers within growth cartilage in children up to age 13; six subjects.
Cartilage-weighted and T1-weighted MRI sequences give reliable growth plate closure staging.
Cross-sectional MRI study of factors influencing growth plate closure.
MR T1 mapping calibrated to water content in porcine growth plate.

nonhuman_primate_growth.name: Non-human primate growth plate model
nonhuman_primate_growth.summary:
Non-human primates are the only laboratory species whose growth plate biology is
phylogenetically close to human, and the closest available check on whether murine results
transfer at all. The postnatal development of organ systems in cynomolgus monkeys, including
skeletal maturation timing, is documented in a form usable for comparative work (li2023).
The comparison is not uniformly reassuring: unclosed vertebral growth plate cartilage was
found in every lumbar endplate of 11 normal cynomolgus monkeys aged approximately 9-15
years, in explicit contrast with complete epiphyseal closure in adult humans (iwata2018) -
so closure is site-specific in the macaque in a way it is not in human, and a "primate model
of fusion" cannot be assumed to fuse at the site being studied. Practical limits are severe
and are the reason this species is nearly absent from the growth plate literature: cost,
ethics, small sample sizes, long developmental timelines matching human tempo (which is the
point, but also the obstacle), and no conditional genetics. Scored on the four-axis scheme
defined in mouse_model_translation_risk (fusion competence, plate architecture, scale,
tempo; each 1-5, mean reported). Non-human primate scores A=2, B=1, C=1, D=1, mean 1.25, the
lowest translation risk of any model - but the number of growth plate mechanism studies
performed in NHP is close to zero, so low risk is currently unrealised.
nonhuman_primate_growth.human_evidence_note: NHP data are used as the nearest phylogenetic comparator for human closure; no paired human-NHP experiment exists.
nonhuman_primate_growth.translation_risk_reason: Closest phylogeny, human-like tempo and dimensions; residual risk is site-specific persistence of vertebral plates and the near-total absence of mechanistic NHP studies.
localization: multiple: lumbar vertebral endplate cartilage remains unclosed in adult macaque

key_refs.one_line_finding: Postnatal organ system development of cynomolgus monkeys including skeletal maturation timing.
Unclosed vertebral growth plate cartilage in every lumbar endplate of 11 normal adult cynomolgus monkeys.

ovine_growth_plate_model.name: Ovine growth plate model
ovine_growth_plate_model.summary:
Sheep are used where a large, weight-bearing, surgically accessible physis is needed over
months rather than weeks, principally for mechanically modulated growth and for tissue
mechanics. Tensile properties of the physis were characterised across anatomical location,
thickness, strain rate and age in ovine tissue alongside human comparison, establishing that
physeal tensile behaviour is site-dependent and strain-rate dependent (williams2001). Ovine
and bovine cartilage supplied the zonal biochemistry that underpins matrix models -
differential aggrecan synthesis and breakdown rates by zone (shapses1994) and collagen
fibril composition (mendler1989, keene1995). Growth modulation by sustained compression has
been compared across three species at two anatomical locations, which is the closest thing
the field has to a cross-species dose-response for mechanical growth suppression
(stokes2006). Lamb studies provided the recumbency-growth observations behind the growing-
pains literature (noonan2004). Scored on the four-axis scheme defined in
mouse_model_translation_risk (fusion competence, plate architecture, scale, tempo; each 1-5,
mean reported). Sheep score A=3, B=1, C=1, D=2, mean 1.75, translation_risk moderate. The
weak axis is fusion: ovine epiphyseal closure timing is documented for veterinary purposes
but the terminal cellular events have not been characterised, so sheep cannot currently
substitute for rabbit as a fusion model.
ovine_growth_plate_model.human_evidence_note: Ovine physeal tensile data were generated alongside human comparison in the same study.
ovine_growth_plate_model.translation_risk_reason: Large weight-bearing physis with human-comparable dimensions, but terminal fusion biology is uncharacterised in sheep.
localization: ovine PHZ: tensile failure occurs preferentially near the hypertrophic zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Physeal tensile properties vary with anatomical location, thickness, strain rate and age.
Endochondral growth modulated by sustained compression compared across three species at two anatomical locations.
Differential aggrecan synthesis and breakdown rates between growth plate zones.
Recumbency-associated growth documented in a lamb model.

porcine_growth_plate_model.name: Porcine growth plate model
porcine_growth_plate_model.summary:
The pig is the large-animal model whose growth plate most closely matches human dimensions
and loading, and it is the model of choice for physeal mechanics. Unconfined compression of
porcine growth plate and its three zones has been used to derive zone-specific mechanical
properties (sergerie2009), and porcine explants have supplied the controlled loading
experiments the human plate cannot be subjected to: compressive modulation alters
chondrocyte viability (kaviani2015), static and dynamic loading produce different strain
fields (kaviani2016), and in situ chondrocyte deformation has been measured under stress-
controlled static versus dynamic compression (zimmermann2017). Morphological and X-ray
microprobe studies of the porcine plate established zonal mineral chemistry (althoff1982),
and porcine tissue supplied the T1-mapping calibration used to infer water content by MRI
(shiguetomimedi2013). Human comparative data exist directly: in vitro thymidine labelling
was performed in human AND porcine growth plates in the same study (thurston1985). Scored on
the four-axis scheme defined in mouse_model_translation_risk (fusion competence, plate
architecture, scale, tempo; each 1-5, mean reported). Pig scores A=2, B=1, C=1, D=2, mean
1.5, giving translation_risk moderate; the residual risk is that pig growth completes far
faster than human and that pigs are usually studied as juveniles well before any fusion
event.
porcine_growth_plate_model.human_evidence_note: One study labelled human and porcine growth plates side by side, which is the strongest direct human-porcine comparison available.
porcine_growth_plate_model.translation_risk_reason: Dimensional and mechanical similarity to human is high, but pigs are studied juvenile, growth completes much faster, and fusion is rarely the endpoint.
localization: porcine RZ/PZ/HZ: zone-specific compressive properties measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mechanical properties of the porcine growth plate and its three zones from unconfined compression.
Compressive mechanical modulation alters growth plate chondrocyte viability in porcine explants.
In situ growth plate chondrocyte deformation under static versus dynamic compression.
Thymidine labelling performed in human and porcine growth plates in the same study.

proteomics_growth_plate.name: Proteomics of the growth plate
proteomics_growth_plate.summary:
Growth plate proteomics is small, and the human component is essentially one study.
Proteomic and elemental mapping of human growth plate from ten paediatric donors (six
amputations for osteosarcoma or trauma, four polydactyly) identified a protein network that
polarises mineralisation: SPP1 and AHSG concentrated at the growth-plate/epiphysis interface
where mineralisation is inhibited, and ENPP1 and ALPL coexisting with them at the growth-
plate/metaphysis interface where mineralisation is promoted (xie2025). Chemical rather than
proteomic imaging has been applied to three polydactyly specimens by time-of-flight
secondary ion mass spectrometry, mapping a sharp fall in organic markers and a concurrent
rise in CaPO2+ and Ca+ across the calcified cartilage front (zoehrer2025). Both are cross-
sectional, terminal and low-n. The structural obstacles are the same as for transcriptomics
with one addition: cartilage is dominated by a small number of extremely abundant matrix
proteins (collagen II, aggrecan), so dynamic range compresses and low-abundance regulatory
proteins - receptors, phosphatases, transcription factors - fall below detection unless
depleted or enriched. No zone-resolved human growth plate proteome exists; the zonal
information available is transcript-level (gse9160) and cannot substitute, because the
matrix proteins that determine mechanics have half-lives far longer than their mRNAs.
proteomics_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: Both human proteomic and chemical-imaging studies used human paediatric growth plate tissue.
proteomics_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: The cited proteomic evidence is human; risk arises only when murine matrix proteomics is used to fill the zonal gap.
localization: human ZPC: SPP1/AHSG inhibitory and ENPP1/ALPL promoting interfaces mapped by proteomics

key_refs.one_line_finding: SPP1 and AHSG inhibit and ENPP1/ALPL promote mineralisation at opposite human growth plate interfaces; ten donors.
ToF-SIMS maps the organic-to-mineral transition across the human calcified cartilage front in three polydactyly specimens.
Zone-resolved human transcript data; no proteomic equivalent exists.

rabbit_growth_plate_model.name: Rabbit growth plate model
rabbit_growth_plate_model.summary:
The rabbit is the small mammal that actually fuses, and that single fact makes it the most
under-used model in this field. Estrogen treatment accelerates growth plate senescence and
brings on fusion in rabbits, and the fusion event is abrupt, with remaining chondrocytes
rapidly replaced by bone (weise2001); estrogen hastens fusion by exhausting the
proliferative capacity of the plate rather than by acting acutely (nilsson2014). The rabbit
also supplied the foundational catch-up growth experiments: glucocorticoid-induced growth
suppression is followed by delayed senescence and catch-up (baron1994, gafni2001), and
resting zone chondrocytes are depleted as senescence proceeds (schrier2006), with senescence
accompanied by loss of DNA methylation (nilsson2005). Rabbit growth is continuous rather
than saltatory when measured directly (klein1994), which is the animal counterweight to the
human saltation-and-stasis claim (lampl1992). Limits: the rabbit plate is thin relative to
human, growth is complete within months, and no conditional genetics exist, so the rabbit
can test whether an endpoint occurs but not which cell produced it. Translation risk score
used in this layer runs 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest) and is the mean of four sub-scores, each
1-5: (A) fusion competence - can the species express epiphyseal fusion at all; (B) plate
architecture - columnar organisation and secondary ossification centre; (C) scale - plate
thickness and hypertrophic cell volume relative to human; (D) tempo - proliferative cycle
time and growth duration relative to human. Rabbit scores A=1, B=2, C=3, D=3, mean 2.25,
giving translation_risk moderate - the lowest of any tractable laboratory mammal.
rabbit_growth_plate_model.human_evidence_note: Rabbit results are supported in humans only by correlative endocrine data; no human interventional counterpart exists.
rabbit_growth_plate_model.translation_risk_reason: Rabbit expresses true epiphyseal fusion and estrogen-driven senescence, matching the human endpoint; scale and tempo still differ substantially and no lineage tools exist.
localization: rabbit RZ: progenitor depletion demonstrated during senescence

key_refs.one_line_finding: Estrogen accelerates growth plate senescence and produces abrupt fusion in rabbits.
Estrogen hastens fusion by exhausting proliferative capacity rather than acting acutely.
Catch-up growth in rabbits is associated with delayed growth plate senescence.
Resting zone chondrocytes are depleted during rabbit growth plate senescence.

rat_growth_plate_model.name: Rat growth plate model
rat_growth_plate_model.summary:
The rat is the model most often described loosely as "closing", and it does not. In Wistar
rats aged 62-80 weeks the femoral and tibial growth plates remain histologically present
after longitudinal growth has ceased, with four features absent from young plates: a bone
band sealing the metaphyseal edge, extensive acellular resorption-resistant areas,
remodelling and bone formation within still-cellular regions, and direct bone formation by
former growth plate chondrocytes (roach2003). Proliferation continues sporadically; what
stops is synchrony and net expansion. This is a mechanistically distinct endpoint from human
fusion, in which the plate is destroyed. The rat's compensating strengths are real: it
supplies the only zone-resolved mammalian growth plate transcriptome with adequate
replication (35 arrays, gse16981), and that rat dataset - not the two-donor human one - is
what has actually been used to interpret height GWAS loci (lui2012), which makes the rat-to-
human step a load-bearing and largely unexamined inference. Fetal rat metatarsal culture
also provides the workhorse pharmacological assay for growth (chagin2009). Translation risk
score used in this layer runs 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest) and is the mean of four sub-scores,
each 1-5: (A) fusion competence - can the species express epiphyseal fusion at all; (B)
plate architecture - columnar organisation and secondary ossification centre; (C) scale -
plate thickness and hypertrophic cell volume relative to human; (D) tempo - proliferative
cycle time and growth duration relative to human. Rat scores A=5, B=2, C=3, D=4, mean 3.5,
giving translation_risk high, marginally lower than mouse on scale and tempo but identical
on the decisive fusion axis.
rat_growth_plate_model.human_evidence_note: No human data in this node beyond the comparator; the rat terminal morphology has never been sought in human tissue (g_l7fuse_011).
rat_growth_plate_model.translation_risk_reason: Rats cease growth without fusing, so rat cessation mechanisms are surrogate mechanisms; the rat zonal transcriptome is nonetheless routinely used as a proxy for the human one.
localization: rat PC: bone band seals the metaphyseal edge at cessation

key_refs.one_line_finding: Rat growth plates persist at 62-80 weeks with a sealed metaphyseal edge and acellular regions after growth ceases.
35-array zone-resolved rat growth plate transcriptome.
Height GWAS loci interpreted through rodent growth plate expression, implicating 78 genes.
Cultured fetal rat metatarsals as the standard pharmacological growth assay.

scrna_seq_growth_plate.name: Single-cell RNA-seq of the growth plate
scrna_seq_growth_plate.summary:
Growth plate single-cell RNA-seq is a mouse literature with a thin human appendix. A GEO
census on 2026-08-05 returns 60 growth plate single-cell records, of which 18 are human
(geo_census_20260805), and inspection shows that most of the human records are fetal, iPSC-
derived or tumour-adjacent rather than postnatal normal physis. The field began with 217
cells from mouse growth plate (gse76157) - fewer cells than one modern droplet lane. The
only human postnatal growth plate scRNA-seq deposit profiles four epiphysiodesis patients
aged 11-14, with and without ex vivo growth hormone, and the GEO record states that raw
human files were not submitted because of identifiability concerns (gse288028, chu2026).
Three structural biases apply to every dataset in this class. Dissociation preferentially
destroys large hypertrophic cells (chondrocyte_dissociation_bias). Dissociation itself
induces stress-response transcription, so immediate-early genes are not interpretable. And
single-cell data have no spatial axis, so zonal assignment is made by mapping onto marker
sets that were themselves defined in mouse - which converts a species-transfer step into
what looks like an annotation step. Human clonal readout is available only through xenograft
barcoding (gse233188), not in situ.
scrna_seq_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: Human postnatal growth plate scRNA-seq exists but rests on four donors and its raw data are not public.
scrna_seq_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: Cluster identities are named using murine marker panels, so a human cluster labelled "resting zone stem cell" inherits the murine definition rather than testing it.
localization: human RZ: two stem-like populations reported, zonal assignment inferred from marker sets

key_refs.one_line_finding: 60 growth plate single-cell records, 18 human.
Human pubertal growth plate scRNA-seq from four epiphysiodesis donors; raw human files withheld.

snrna_seq_growth_plate.name: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of the growth plate
snrna_seq_growth_plate.summary:
Single-nucleus RNA-seq is the technical answer to the growth plate's central sampling
problem: nuclei can be released from frozen, archival or mineralised tissue without the
enzymatic digestion that destroys large hypertrophic chondrocytes, and methodological
reviews of musculoskeletal omics name it explicitly as the way around mineralised-matrix
dissociation (li2025, delos2026). It buys that access at a stated cost - loss of cytoplasmic
transcripts, lower transcript capture per cell, and depletion of mitochondrial and many
secreted-protein mRNAs - which matters in a tissue whose defining cells are secretory. The
decisive point for this atlas is that the buy has not been made: no single-nucleus dataset
from HUMAN growth plate tissue was located in this sweep, and the human growth plate single-
cell corpus remains dissociation-based (gse288028). Because archival human physeal blocks
exist in pathology departments in far greater numbers than the roughly 100 postnatal plates
ever studied prospectively (human_growth_plate_tissue_scarcity), snRNA-seq on archived
material is the single cheapest available route to enlarging the human evidence base, and it
has not been taken.
snrna_seq_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate single-nucleus dataset was located.
snrna_seq_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: The method is species-agnostic; the risk is that its absence in human keeps the human cell census dependent on murine annotation.
localization: human HZ: recoverable in principle by nuclear isolation; never attempted

key_refs.one_line_finding: Single-nucleus sequencing named as the route around mineralised-matrix dissociation in skeletal tissue.
Decalcification and low RNA integrity constrain musculoskeletal single-cell and spatial work.
The human growth plate single-cell corpus is dissociation-based, not nucleus-based.

spatial_transcriptomics_growth_plate.name: Spatial transcriptomics of the growth plate
spatial_transcriptomics_growth_plate.summary:
Spatial transcriptomics is the modality that would answer most of the atlas's open zonal
questions in one experiment, and as of 2026-08-05 it had never been applied to a postnatal
human growth plate. A GEO census returns 7 records matching growth plate AND spatial, all
non-human, including mouse datasets identifying ApoE as a marker of all resting-zone
chondrocytes (GSE288529) and mapping ADGRG6 control of the PTHrP/IHH axis (GSE275252);
restricting the same query to Homo sapiens returns zero (geo_census_20260805). Two
qualifications sharpen rather than soften that null. First, human spatial transcriptomics of
LIMB cartilage does exist: the human embryonic limb atlas combines scRNA-seq with Visium
across 5-9 post-conception weeks and maps chondrocyte lineages in situ (zhang2024_2) - but at
that stage there is no growth plate with resting, proliferative and hypertrophic zones, so
it cannot answer zonal questions. Second, the human study that reports "spatial analyses" of
pubertal growth plate (chu2026) deposited no spatial dataset in GEO, and withheld even its
raw single-cell human data (gse288028). The technical barrier is specific and solvable:
physeal tissue must be decalcified, which destroys RNA integrity, and polyA-capture spatial
platforms require high RIN. RNA-Rescue Spatial Transcriptomics was developed for exactly
this class of degraded sample (gse221571) and is the obvious route in.
spatial_transcriptomics_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: No spatially resolved transcriptomic dataset from a postnatal human growth plate exists in any public repository.
spatial_transcriptomics_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: Every spatially resolved zonal marker claim in the field is murine, and the murine plate never fuses, so the zonal programme that terminates growth cannot be observed in the species where the data exist.
localization: mouse RZ: ApoE identified as a pan-resting-zone marker by spatial transcriptomics
human RZ: no spatial data of any kind

key_refs.one_line_finding: 7 growth plate spatial records, none human.
Human embryonic limb atlas with Visium spatial transcriptomics at 5-9 post-conception weeks.
RNA-Rescue Spatial Transcriptomics recovers spatial profiles from low-RNA-integrity tissue.
Reports spatial analysis of human pubertal growth plate but deposits no spatial dataset.

stadiometry_measurement_error.name: Stadiometry measurement error
stadiometry_measurement_error.summary:
Every clinical statement about human growth velocity is a difference between two stadiometer
readings, so the measurement error propagates directly into the velocity and does so
amplified by the reciprocal of the interval. Two systematic sources dominate and both are
biological rather than instrumental. Stature varies diurnally: human height falls measurably
across the waking day and recovers with recumbency (reilly1984), so a morning and an
afternoon measurement are not measurements of the same quantity, and diurnal loss originates
partly in vertebral and epiphyseal cartilage (see gap g_l6mech_014). Posture and stretch
technique alter the reading by a comparable amount. The practical consequence is
quantitative: with a typical technical error of measurement of a few millimetres, a three-
month interval implies a velocity uncertainty of order centimetres per year - which is the
same order as the treatment effects routinely reported in growth-promoting trials. This is
why knemometry exists, why growth velocity is conventionally computed over intervals of at
least six months (growth_velocity_measurement_interval), and why single-visit velocity
claims should be treated as uninterpretable regardless of how they are reported.
stadiometry_measurement_error.human_evidence_note: Stadiometry is a human clinical measurement and the error sources are documented in human subjects.
localization: human SYS: whole-body measurement, no zonal resolution

key_refs.one_line_finding: Human stature varies circadianly, falling across the waking day and recovering with recumbency.
Precision of two knemometric techniques compared in childhood - the response to stadiometric imprecision.

stereology_growth_plate.name: Stereology of the growth plate
stereology_growth_plate.summary:
Stereology converts two-dimensional section measurements into unbiased three-dimensional
estimates, and it is the only correct way to obtain chondrocyte volume, which is the
quantity that drives longitudinal growth. Serial-section and stereological analysis
established that hypertrophic chondrocyte enlargement is the dominant contributor to
elongation, with the volume of the terminal hypertrophic chondrocyte scaling linearly with
elongation rate across sites and species (breur1991, breur1994). Applied to human tissue,
the method has been used exactly once in a quantitative published form: a single adolescent
distal tibial physis undergoing physiological epiphysiodesis, in which mean hypertrophic
chondrocyte volume was 5,900 um3 and did not differ significantly between anterior, central
and posterior regions, while 46% of the volume of the central region was already occupied by
transphyseal bridging bone (white2008). Everything the atlas says about the human
hypertrophic volume set point therefore rests on n=1, and on a plate that was in the act of
closing rather than growing normally. The methodological requirements are severe and are why
this is rare: optimally fixed tissue with minimal shrinkage, known section thickness,
systematic random sampling and disector-type probes. Section obliquity alone biases apparent
cell height upward, which is the commonest error in the older growth plate literature.
stereology_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: The only human stereological growth plate dataset is a single distal tibial physis.
stereology_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: The linear volume-to-elongation relationship was established across species including pig and rodent; the human anchor is a single closing plate, so transferring the relationship to a normally growing human plate is an extrapolation.
localization: human HZ: only one plate ever measured stereologically

key_refs.one_line_finding: Stereological hypertrophic chondrocyte volume of 5,900 um3 in one human distal tibial physis, 46% bridged centrally.
Volume of hypertrophic chondrocytes varies linearly with rate of longitudinal bone growth.
Stereological and serial-section analysis of chondrocytic enlargement in the proximal tibial growth plate.

synchrotron_imaging_cartilage.name: Synchrotron phase-contrast imaging of cartilage
synchrotron_imaging_cartilage.summary:
Synchrotron X-ray phase-contrast microtomography is the only three-dimensional imaging
method that resolves individual chondrocytes inside intact, unsectioned cartilage. Human
knee cartilage from 49 deceased donors plus 4 arthroplasty patients was imaged at 2.75 um
voxel size with validation tomographs at 0.65 um, and chondrocytes were segmented
automatically with cell density, cell angle and cell shape recovered as functions of tissue
depth (b2026). A separate study segmented chondrocyte and osteocyte lacunae in calcified
cartilage and subchondral bone of human knees at 650 nm voxel (xu2024). Placed against the
dimensions that matter, 0.65-2.75 um voxels resolve a 10-20 um chondrocyte with 4-30 voxels
across its diameter, resolve zone heights of 100-1000 um trivially, and image a whole 1-10
mm plate only by mosaicking, since field of view trades against resolution. Two limits are
decisive for growth plate work. First, the technique is terminal: it requires excised,
usually fixed tissue, so it can never produce a longitudinal series in a living child.
Second, clustered cells were not reliably separated even at 2.75 um (b2026), which matters
because the chondrocyte cluster is exactly the structure that distinguishes a fusing human
plate from a growing one (white2008). No synchrotron study of a HUMAN growth plate, as
opposed to articular cartilage, was located in this sweep.
synchrotron_imaging_cartilage.human_evidence_note: Both cited studies imaged human cartilage; neither imaged a human growth plate.
synchrotron_imaging_cartilage.translation_risk_reason: Method description applied to human tissue.
localization: human PZ: chondrocyte-level 3D resolution demonstrated in articular cartilage, not yet in physis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Human articular cartilage imaged at 2.75 um voxel with 0.65 um validation; chondrocytes segmented in 3D but clusters not separable.
650 nm synchrotron phase-contrast micro-CT segments chondrocyte and osteocyte lacunae at the human osteochondral interface.
Chondrocyte clustering with intervening acellular areas is the histological signature of a closing human physis.

tamoxifen_inducible_creert2.name: Tamoxifen-inducible CreERT2 in cartilage
tamoxifen_inducible_creert2.summary:
CreERT2 adds temporal control to fate mapping: recombination happens only in cells
expressing the driver during a tamoxifen pulse, which is what makes it possible to ask
whether a progenitor population is established before or after a developmental event. It is
the tool behind the postnatal-versus-embryonic distinction in resting zone stem cell
biology, and behind chondrocyte-specific conditional deletions used throughout L6 (chen2025,
chen2025a, coveney2022, ely2025) and L4 (tu2014). Three quantitative caveats are routinely
under-reported and each can invert a conclusion. Tamoxifen itself perturbs cartilage: it is
an estrogen receptor modulator, and estrogen is the dominant regulator of growth plate
senescence, so tamoxifen dosing in a growing animal is a pharmacological intervention on the
system under study, not an inert trigger. Recombination is leaky in the absence of tamoxifen
in many lines, producing labelled cells that were never induced. And the labelling pulse has
a finite duration in tissue (tamoxifen metabolites persist for days), so "a single time
point" is in practice a window, which blurs precisely the before/after distinction the
method was chosen for. No human equivalent exists.

claim_grades.claim: CreERT2 gives temporal control of lineage labelling.
claim_grades.basis: Established method property.

claim_grades.claim: Tamoxifen dosing perturbs growth plate biology in growing animals.
claim_grades.basis: Follows from tamoxifen being a selective estrogen receptor modulator and estrogen being the dominant senescence regulator; the confound is rarely measured in growth plate studies.

tamoxifen_inducible_creert2.translation_risk_reason: Murine-only, and the inducing agent is itself an estrogen receptor modulator acting on the pathway that terminates human growth.
localization: mouse RZ: inducible labelling used to time progenitor establishment

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chondrocyte-specific inducible disruption of glucocorticoid signalling.
Inducible ciliary IFT88 deletion in adolescent growth plate.
Inducible PIEZO1 deletion used to test mechanotransduction in growth plate.
Inducible PTHrP-CreER labelling defined the resting zone stem cell.

tetracycline_labeling.name: Tetracycline labelling of the mineralisation front
tetracycline_labeling.summary:
Tetracyclines chelate calcium and are incorporated at active mineralisation fronts, so two
doses separated by a known interval leave two fluorescent lines whose separation divided by
the interval gives a direct, in vivo mineral apposition rate. In the growth plate context
this measures the rate at which the chondro-osseous junction advances - that is,
longitudinal growth rate at the tissue level - and it is the standard readout in short-term
growth perturbation experiments in animals (farnum2003). Its strengths are that it is truly
in vivo, truly rate-resolved, and independent of any assumption about cell behaviour. Its
limits for this atlas are three. It labels mineral, not cartilage, so it reports the output
of the plate rather than any process inside it. It requires a second harvest, so in humans
it has been used almost exclusively in bone histomorphometry on iliac crest biopsies in
metabolic bone disease, not in physis. And the interval sets the temporal resolution: a 5-14
day interval is standard, which means it cannot resolve the sub-weekly saltatory elongation
events proposed for human growth (lampl1992) and disputed on rabbit data (klein1994). No
human growth plate tetracycline labelling study was located in this sweep.
tetracycline_labeling.human_evidence_note: Tetracycline labelling of the human physis was not located; human use is confined to iliac crest bone histomorphometry.
tetracycline_labeling.translation_risk_reason: The chemistry is species-independent, but what it measures - mineral apposition rate - has values that differ with growth rate, so the numbers do not transfer even though the method does.
localization: multiple PC: mineral apposition at the chondro-osseous junction measured directly

key_refs.one_line_finding: Short-term fasting and catch-up growth analysed with fluorochrome-based rate measurement in young animals.
Saltation and stasis model of human growth, requiring sub-weekly temporal resolution to test.
Rabbit linear growth measured as continuous rather than saltatory.

zebrafish_skeletal_model.name: Zebrafish skeletal model
zebrafish_skeletal_model.summary:
Zebrafish do not have a mammalian growth plate. Their endochondral growth zones are
architecturally distinct - they lack the stacked columnar proliferative zone bounded by a
secondary ossification centre that defines the mammalian physis - and their skeletal growth
is indeterminate, continuing through adult life (le2022). What zebrafish offer instead is
throughput and transparency: forward and reverse genetics at scale, live imaging of skeletal
element formation, and rapid phenotyping of candidate genes emerging from human skeletal
dysplasia sequencing. A concrete example in this atlas's domain is PAPP-A, whose requirement
for IGF-dependent chondrocyte differentiation and organisation was established in zebrafish
(harboe2024). Zebrafish are also the only vertebrate in which a growth plate gene can be
screened in hundreds of animals per week. The transfer problem is categorical rather than
quantitative: because there is no columnar proliferative zone, no hypertrophic volume set
point and no epiphyseal fusion, a zebrafish result can establish that a gene is required for
chondrocyte differentiation but cannot establish anything about zonal organisation, growth
cessation or adult height. Scored on the four-axis scheme defined in
mouse_model_translation_risk (fusion competence, plate architecture, scale, tempo; each 1-5,
mean reported). Zebrafish score A=5, B=5, C=5, D=5, mean 5.0, the highest translation risk
of any model considered.
zebrafish_skeletal_model.human_evidence_note: No human counterpart; zebrafish results enter human reasoning only through gene-level orthology.
zebrafish_skeletal_model.translation_risk_reason: The structure whose behaviour the atlas is about does not exist in zebrafish, so only gene-level requirement claims transfer, never architectural or terminal-fate claims.
localization: zebrafish: no RZ/PZ/PHZ/HZ equivalent to score

key_refs.one_line_finding: Zebrafish endochondral growth zones differ architecturally from the mammalian growth plate.
PAPP-A required for IGF-dependent chondrocyte differentiation and organisation in zebrafish.

appositional_growth.name: Appositional (circumferential) growth
appositional_growth.summary: Appositional growth widens a bone, in contrast to the longitudinal growth generated by the physis. Two distinct processes contribute: periosteal bone apposition on the outer cortex, which thickens the diaphysis, and latitudinal enlargement of the cartilaginous plate itself, to which the groove of Ranvier supplies cells at the plate margin. The two modes are quantitatively separable in mouse by micro-CT: measuring the equivalent radius of the chondro-osseous junction against its axial displacement gives an expansion-to- elongation ratio that falls from 0.18 (distal femur) and 0.16 (proximal tibia) at E17.5-E18.5 to 0 and 0.04 respectively by P32-P40. In other words, embryonic bones widen almost a fifth as fast as they lengthen, and postnatal bones essentially stop widening at the plate while continuing to elongate. The same study connects this to cellular architecture: embryonic clones are mostly orthogonally oriented clusters and postnatal ones are mostly columns, suggesting that whether the division plane rotation is completed determines whether a clone contributes to widening or to lengthening.
appositional_growth.human_evidence_note: No human study separates plate latitudinal enlargement from periosteal apposition quantitatively; human data exist only for total bone width.
appositional_growth.translation_risk_reason: The expansion-to-elongation ratios are mouse micro-CT values and the cellular explanation is mouse clonal analysis; nothing equivalent has been measured in human bone.
localization: mouse: quantified across eight growth plates and three time windows (rubin2024)
rabbit: groove of Ranvier as the source of latitudinal cells (shapiro1977)
human: not quantified separately from total bone width

key_refs.one_line_finding: Expansion-to-elongation ratio falls from 0.16-0.18 embryonically to 0-0.04 by P40, correlating with the shift from clusters to columns.
The groove of Ranvier is the perichondrial source of cells for latitudinal growth of the plate in rabbit.
Contrasts longitudinal growth plate output with periosteal appositional growth and its role in bone stability.

bone_modeling_drift.name: Bone modelling drift
bone_modeling_drift.summary: Modelling drift is the coordinated apposition on one surface and resorption on the opposite surface that moves a bone cross-section through space without changing its shape, and it is what allows the wide metaphysis produced by the growth plate to be reshaped into the narrow diaphysis as the plate moves away. Where longitudinal growth is a cartilage process, drift is entirely an osteoblast-osteoclast process on periosteal and endosteal surfaces, so the two can be dissociated pharmacologically and genetically: a drug that blocks osteoclasts will leave elongation intact while preventing funnelisation, producing the club-shaped metaphyses seen in osteopetrosis. Rauch frames longitudinal and appositional growth as complementary determinants of bone stability, with drift providing the mechanical adaptation that longitudinal growth alone cannot. This node is architectural context for the growth plate rather than a growth plate mechanism, and its own quantitative parameters (drift rates, surface-specific apposition) belong to bone remodelling rather than to physeal biology.
bone_modeling_drift.human_evidence_note: Modelling drift in humans is inferred from bone histomorphometry and from the metaphyseal deformities of osteoclast-deficient disorders rather than from direct measurement at the physis.
bone_modeling_drift.translation_risk_reason: Surface-based modelling is a general vertebrate bone process well documented in human histomorphometry; the risk here is only that this node is contextual rather than physeal.
localization: human and rodent metaphysis and diaphysis: periosteal and endosteal surfaces

key_refs.one_line_finding: Frames longitudinal and appositional growth and the modelling drift that reshapes the metaphysis as complementary determinants of bone stability.
Quantifies the width of new bone generated at the chondro-osseous junction relative to elongation across development.

borderline_zone.name: Borderline zone (peripheral borderline chondrocytes)
borderline_zone.summary: At the outer margin of the growth plate, immediately adjacent to the perichondrium and the groove of Ranvier, sits a population of chondrocytes that are aligned perpendicular to the columnar chondrocytes rather than parallel to the growth axis. Inducible lineage tracing in mouse shows these borderline chondrocytes are not simply mis-oriented columnar cells: they behave as transient mesenchymal precursors, leaving the cartilage and contributing to marrow stromal cells and osteoblasts in the metaphysis. This is a route from cartilage to bone lineage that is distinct from the transdifferentiation of terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes at the chondro-osseous junction. Independently, 3D clonal analysis in mouse finds that postnatal growth plates retain small, disorganised, orthogonally oriented clusters specifically at the outer edges while the interior is columnar, which is architecturally consistent with a distinct peripheral compartment that supports lateral rather than longitudinal growth. Nothing equivalent has been shown in human tissue; the borderline compartment is defined entirely by mouse genetics.
borderline_zone.human_evidence_note: No study identifies a borderline chondrocyte population in human growth plate tissue; the compartment is defined by mouse inducible lineage tracing.
borderline_zone.translation_risk_reason: Defined solely by mouse Cre-based lineage tracing, a method with no human equivalent, and not yet corroborated by any human histological or single-cell description.
localization: mouse BZ: lineage traced (mizuhashi2019)
human BZ: not described

key_refs.one_line_finding: Peripheral borderline chondrocytes, oriented perpendicular to columns, act as transient mesenchymal precursors giving rise to marrow stromal cells and osteoblasts in mouse.
Postnatal mouse growth plates retain small disorganised clusters specifically at the outer edges while the interior is columnar.

cartilage_canal.name: Cartilage canal
cartilage_canal.summary: Cartilage canals are vascularised connective-tissue channels that invade the epiphyseal cartilage before the secondary ossification centre appears. They carry arterioles, venules, capillaries and mesenchymal cells into an otherwise avascular tissue, form a discrete network within the epiphysis, and determine where the secondary centre will form: in mouse, cartilage canals establish the marrow space that the secondary centre subsequently occupies, and they influence the fate of the resting chondrocytes they pass. Their mesenchymal cells express bone-relevant proteins and can become osteocytes, so the canals are not merely a plumbing system but a delivery route for osteogenic precursors. In human epiphyses, the vessels that build the ossification centres arise by sprouting from the bone collar or by intussusception rather than from circulating CD133+ endothelial progenitors, and vascular invasion of the joint anlage is delayed relative to the surrounding tissue. Canals are also the point of vulnerability in osteochondrosis of large animals, where failure of canal blood supply causes focal ischaemic chondronecrosis.
cartilage_canal.human_evidence_note: The origin and phenotype of epiphyseal vessels have been characterised directly in human polydactylous digit specimens (walzer2014).
cartilage_canal.translation_risk_reason: Canal function in determining secondary centre position is mouse work; the human data establish vessel origin but not canal fate.
localization: mouse femoral epiphysis: canals determine secondary centre site (blumer2007)
human epiphysis: vessel origin characterised (walzer2014)
