The same study found that global DNA methylation declined with in vivo growth plate senescence but not during rapid proliferation in vitro or across the resting-to-hypertrophic transition, which argues for an epigenetic timer coupled specifically to slow in vivo resting-zone division rather than for telomere-driven crisis. This node is therefore a negative result that is frequently re-asserted as positive in secondary literature; treat 'growth plate chondrocytes undergo replicative senescence' as unsupported in its cell-autonomous form.
replicative_senescence_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate chondrocyte replicative-capacity measurement exists.
replicative_senescence_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Rabbit in vitro behaviour, and rodent telomere biology differs markedly from human, so neither a positive nor a negative rodent result settles the human case.
localization: rabbit RZ chondrocytes in vitro: tested and negative (nilsson2005)
human chondrocytes: untested in growth plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: Population doublings of rabbit RZ chondrocytes in culture are independent of donor age, arguing against cell-autonomous replicative senescence
Contextualises the finite-capacity model that this negative result constrains

resting_zone_niche.name: Resting zone as a stem cell niche
resting_zone_niche.summary: The resting (reserve) zone is the epiphyseal-most stratum of the growth plate, containing small round chondrocytes in an abundant matrix that divide rarely and sit immediately below the secondary ossification centre. In mouse it functions as a niche rather than a passive reserve: it holds at least three partially overlapping slow-cycling populations (PTHrP/Pthlh+, FoxA2+, and label-retaining Col2a1-lineage cells) that seed the proliferative columns below. Its niche signals are defined negatively as much as positively - resting chondrocytes sit in a Wnt-inhibitory microenvironment (enriched for secreted Wnt inhibitors; forced beta-catenin activation drives them out of the zone), and their fate is instructed in reverse by Indian hedgehog from the hypertrophic zone, since both Smoothened agonism and antagonism reduce the number of columns formed from labelled resting cells. Loss of niche integrity is phenotypically visible: partial diphtheria-toxin ablation of PTHrP+ resting cells in mouse shrinks the proliferative zone and expands the hypertrophic and resting zones, and Adgrg6 loss shortens the resting zone and produces intra-plate cell clusters. In humans the resting zone has been mapped only transcriptionally and histologically; no human cell has ever been shown to behave as a resting-zone stem cell, because clonal lineage tracing cannot be performed in people.
resting_zone_niche.human_evidence_note: Human resting zone cells have been profiled by single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in adolescent surgical specimens and show quiescence-associated features, but no functional stem-cell assay has been performed in human tissue in situ.
resting_zone_niche.translation_risk_reason: Every functional claim about the niche (clonality, self-renewal, ablation, Hedgehog and Wnt manipulation) rests on mouse genetics. Mice never fuse their growth plates, so the terminal behaviour of the human niche has no murine counterpart.
localization: mouse RZ: confirmed, PTHrP-mCherry knock-in reporter and PTHrP-creER lineage (mizuhashi2018)
mouse RZ: confirmed, H2B-EGFP label-retaining cells concentrated at the top of the plate (hallett2021_2)
human RZ: transcriptionally defined only, spatial transcriptomics of adolescent biopsies (avijgan2025, chu2026)
rabbit RZ: FoxA2+ cells present at the cartilage/SOC interface (muruganandan2022)

key_refs.one_line_finding: PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes are slow-cycling, clonogenic and generate columns; partial ablation distorts zone heights
Label-retaining resting chondrocytes occupy a Wnt-inhibitory microenvironment and exit on beta-catenin activation
FoxA2+ cells at the top of the resting zone are a second, longer-lived stem population
ADGRG6 is required to maintain slow-cycling resting zone cells and normal zone architecture
Human adolescent resting zone contains transcriptionally quiescent sub-populations (CHRDL2+, SFRP5+)

rz_depletion_causes_fusion.name: Hypothesis: resting zone stem cell depletion causes epiphyseal fusion
rz_depletion_causes_fusion.summary: Two readings of the same correlation compete. In the causal reading, resting zone progenitors have a finite proliferative capacity; when it is exhausted, chondrocyte production stops and the plate is resorbed and bridged by bone. In the consequence reading, fusion is an independently triggered event - in humans, an oestrogen-driven one - that terminates the plate while proliferative capacity may still remain, so the observed depletion at fusion is an endpoint, not a cause. Supporting the causal reading: in rabbit, resting-zone chondrocyte proliferation rate and cell number per unit area both fall with age, and growth-inhibiting treatments that slow resting-cell proliferation slow senescence. Against it: growth plate senescence in rodents proceeds to near-cessation without fusion at all, so depletion is clearly not sufficient for fusion in every mammal; and oestrogen accelerates senescence while simultaneously slowing resting-zone proliferation, which is the opposite of what a pure proliferation-consumption model predicts. What discriminates: measure resting-zone cell number and proliferative capacity in human or rabbit plates at matched chronological age with and without oestrogen exposure. If depletion causes fusion, plates that fuse early under oestrogen must be more depleted at the moment of fusion; if fusion is imposed, they will fuse while less depleted than age-matched controls.
rz_depletion_causes_fusion.human_evidence_note: No study has quantified human resting zone cell number or proliferative capacity across the fusion transition; human evidence about fusion timing is radiographic and endocrine.
rz_depletion_causes_fusion.translation_risk_reason: Rodents do not fuse, so the species in which senescence is best measured cannot exhibit the outcome being explained; rabbits fuse but have not been examined with modern clonal tools.
localization: rabbit RZ: age-related numerical depletion measured (schrier2006)
human RZ: unmeasured across the fusion transition

key_refs.one_line_finding: Rabbit resting zone chondrocytes decline in proliferation rate and number with age; glucocorticoid slows both
States the depletion-then-fusion sequence as the field's working model
Emphasises that rodents senesce without fusing, separating the two events
Clonal tracing showing postnatal acquisition of self-renewal, which weakens a simple monotonic depletion account

skeletal_stem_cell.name: Skeletal stem cell (SSC)
skeletal_stem_cell.summary: 'Skeletal stem cell' names an operational result, not a single cell: a cell that self-renews and generates bone, cartilage and hematopoiesis-supportive stroma in a transplantation or lineage-tracing assay. At least five mutually incompatible definitions are in current use - the FACS-defined mouse mSSC hierarchy, PTHrP+/FoxA2+ resting-zone chondrocytes, Grem1+ osteochondroreticular cells, LepR+ perisinusoidal stroma, and CTSK-lineage periosteal stem cells - and they disagree on anatomy, markers, adipogenic potential and developmental window. The disagreements are not semantic. Whether the SSC makes marrow adipocytes separates the CD146+ adventitial-reticular-cell definition (yes) from the mSSC/Grem1 definitions (no). Whether the growth plate SSC lies in the resting zone (mouse tracing) or in the pre-hypertrophic/hypertrophic zone (human FACS/scRNA homology mapping) is a straight contradiction in anatomy. Dual-recombinase fate mapping showed that even the dominant osteoblast source changes with age, from chondrocytes before adolescence to LepR+ stroma after - so 'the' skeletal stem cell is time-dependent as well as site-dependent. Human work rests on xenotransplantation of prospectively sorted cells, never on in-situ tracing.
skeletal_stem_cell.human_evidence_note: Human SSCs are defined by prospective sorting followed by renal-capsule xenotransplantation in immunodeficient mice; their behaviour in situ in a human skeleton is inferred, not observed.
skeletal_stem_cell.translation_risk_reason: The mouse and human panels share no marker, and mouse assays are in-situ genetic while human assays are ectopic transplantation - two different questions given the same name.
localization: mouse growth plate: mSSC phenotype enriched (chan2015)
mouse metaphysis: Grem1+ OCR cells concentrated, not perisinusoidal (worthley2015)
mouse perisinusoidal marrow: LepR+ stroma (zhou2014)
mouse periosteum: CTSK-lineage PSC (debnath2018)
human fetal pre-hypertrophic/hypertrophic zone: hSSC enriched (chan2018)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Defines mSSC as CD45- Ter119- Tie2- AlphaV(CD51)+ Thy(CD90)- 6C3- CD105- CD200+ at the apex of an eight-population hierarchy
Defines hSSC as CD45- CD235a- TIE2- CD31- PDPN+ CD146- CD73+ CD164+, sorted from human fetal growth plate
Argues the bona fide SSC is the CD146+ marrow adventitial reticular cell, which does make adipocytes
Osteoblast source switches from chondrocytes to LepR+ stroma at adolescence, so no single SSC accounts for postnatal bone

soc_formation_triggers_stemness.name: Hypothesis: secondary ossification centre formation triggers resting-zone stem cell acquisition
soc_formation_triggers_stemness.summary: The claim is that resting-zone chondrocytes are not stem cells from the outset but acquire self-renewal when the secondary ossification centre forms, which in mouse is roughly the second postnatal week. The evidence is entirely temporal coincidence in two mouse studies. First, PTHrP-mCherry+ resting chondrocytes appear at P3 and expand sharply between P6 and P9, and PTHrP-creER colony-forming cells acquire robust in vitro self-renewal between a P9 pulse (17/518, 3.3% secondary colonies, none passageable) and a P12 pulse (16/98, 16.3% secondary colonies, 2/16 passageable nine times) - the authors describe this as occurring 'when the secondary ossification centre actively develops'. Second, multicolour clonal tracing found that fetal and neonatal growth depletes chondroprogenitors whereas later growth produces large stable monoclonal columns with symmetric division and stem cell marker expression, 'coinciding with the formation of the secondary ossification centre'. Neither study manipulated the SOC. A targeted Europe PMC search for any experiment that ablates, blocks, prevents or delays SOC formation and then assays resting-zone stemness returned zero records (see search log for g_l2stem_003). The hypothesis is therefore correlational in one species. It is load-bearing for fusion models in L7 and should be cited as a hypothesis, not a mechanism.
soc_formation_triggers_stemness.human_evidence_note: Human SOC timing is well described radiographically and varies by bone (distal femur around term, others through childhood), but no human study has related SOC appearance to any property of resting zone cells.
soc_formation_triggers_stemness.translation_risk_reason: Two mouse studies with coincident timing; humans form SOCs at bone-specific times over years, which would predict staggered, bone-by-bone acquisition of resting-zone stemness - a prediction nobody has tested.
localization: mouse RZ/SOC interface: temporal association only

key_refs.one_line_finding: In vitro self-renewability of PTHrP+ colony-forming cells rises between P9 and P12, described as coinciding with active SOC development
Clonal switch from progenitor depletion to stable monoclonal columns is reported as coinciding with SOC formation
FoxA2+ long-term stem cells sit precisely at the cartilage/SOC interface, consistent with but not demonstrating an SOC-derived niche

stem_cell_niche_vascular_coupling.name: Vascular coupling of the skeletal stem cell niche
stem_cell_niche_vascular_coupling.summary: Skeletal progenitor behaviour is set in part by a specific vessel type. Type H capillaries (CD31-high, endomucin-high) in the murine metaphysis are surrounded by osteoprogenitors, couple angiogenesis to osteogenesis, and decline with age in parallel with bone formation. This is the vascular arm of the argument that the secondary ossification centre creates the resting zone niche: the SOC is itself a vascular invasion event, and cartilage canals carrying vessels precede it. The strongest mechanistic link demonstrated so far is indirect - in the mSSC scheme, VEGF blockade during BMP2-induced ossicle formation shifts the output from bone with a marrow cavity to predominantly cartilage, showing that vascular signalling steers skeletal progenitor fate. What has not been shown is that manipulating the epiphyseal vasculature specifically changes resting-zone stem cell acquisition, which is the experiment that would test the SOC hypothesis (gap g_l2stem_003).
stem_cell_niche_vascular_coupling.human_evidence_note: Type H vessel biology and VEGF-blockade fate switching are murine; no human epiphyseal equivalent has been tested functionally.
stem_cell_niche_vascular_coupling.translation_risk_reason: Depends on mouse vascular subtype markers and pharmacological blockade in mice; human epiphyseal vascular anatomy differs in timing and canal structure.
localization: mouse metaphysis: type H vessels confirmed (kusumbe2014)
mouse epiphysis/SOC: vascular invasion precedes SOC formation; niche consequence unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Type H capillaries couple angiogenesis to osteogenesis and decline with age in mouse bone
VEGF inhibition during BMP2-induced ossicle formation shifts mSSC output from bone to cartilage
Gli1+ stromal cells are fetal precursors of long-lived cartilage progenitors, linking perichondrial/stromal compartments to the plate

telomere_attrition_chondrocyte.name: Telomere attrition in growth plate chondrocytes
telomere_attrition_chondrocyte.summary: Telomere shortening is the most commonly invoked molecular clock for a finite proliferative capacity, and it is routinely asserted for the growth plate in review literature. A targeted Europe PMC search for measurements of telomere length or telomerase activity in human growth plate or resting-zone chondrocytes as a function of age returned no qualifying primary study (see search log for g_l2stem_007): the hits are osteoarthritis cartilage, general skeletal ageing reviews, and rodent work. The nearest positive datum is murine and indirect - mTert-GFP marks a transitional skeletal progenitor population whose expression peaks during adolescent bone growth rather than persisting - and the nearest negative datum is that rabbit resting-zone chondrocyte replicative capacity in vitro does not decline with donor age, which is hard to reconcile with progressive telomere-driven exhaustion in vivo. Treat telomere attrition in the growth plate as an untraceable claim in its human form.
telomere_attrition_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No primary measurement of telomere length or telomerase activity in human growth plate chondrocytes was found.
telomere_attrition_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Laboratory mice have long telomeres and broader somatic telomerase expression than humans, so murine telomere data are among the least transferable in skeletal biology.
localization: human growth plate: no measurement located
mouse growth plate, metaphyseal stroma, marrow: mTert-GFP+ cells present (carlone2021)

key_refs.one_line_finding: mTert expression in mouse long bone peaks during adolescent growth and marks a transitional progenitor, not a permanent stem pool
Age-independent in vitro replicative capacity of rabbit RZ chondrocytes constrains any telomere-clock account

amino_acid_sensing_chondrocyte.name: Amino acid sensing in chondrocytes
amino_acid_sensing_chondrocyte.summary: Growth plate chondrocytes are avascular, highly anabolic and therefore acutely dependent on amino acid supply. Stegen 2020 shows the sensing is not merely permissive but identity-forming and runs as a feedforward loop: SOX9 raises glutamine consumption and glutaminase 1 (GLS1) levels, and GLS1 activity is then required for chondrocyte function through three separable routes - glutamate-dehydrogenase-derived acetyl-CoA for histone acetylation at chondrogenic genes, transaminase-derived aspartate for proliferation and matrix synthesis, and glutamine-derived glutathione for survival in the avascular core (mouse and cell-based). This is a direct metabolic-to-transcriptional convergence: the master chondrogenic transcription factor sets its own nutrient flux, and the flux is required to keep the chromatin state that supports the transcription factor. mTORC1 is the canonical amino-acid-responsive kinase in the same cell and controls translational output (Chen and Long 2014), but the two axes have not been tested against each other in the growth plate. No human growth plate metabolite measurement exists.
amino_acid_sensing_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate amino acid or glutamine flux measurement.
amino_acid_sensing_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Mouse genetics plus tracer metabolomics in cultured cells; human physeal metabolism is unmeasured.
localization: mouse growth plate: GLS1 dependence demonstrated (stegen2020)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: SOX9 drives glutamine uptake and GLS1, and GLS1 flux is required for chondrocyte epigenetic state, proliferation and survival.
mTORC1 converts nutrient status into chondrocyte protein synthesis rate and cell size.

autophagy_chondrocyte.name: Autophagy in growth plate chondrocytes
autophagy_chondrocyte.summary: Autophagy is the lysosomal recycling pathway that maintains cells under nutrient and oxygen restriction - exactly the condition of the avascular mid-plate. Cartilage-specific deletion of Atg5 or Atg7 in mouse (Col2a1-Cre) causes growth retardation with increased chondrocyte death and reduced proliferation, and the effect is mild rather than catastrophic, i.e. autophagy is a survival buffer rather than an essential differentiation step (Vuppalapati 2015). The same study provides one of the few pieces of direct human evidence in this layer: pharmacological autophagy inhibition with bafilomycin A1 or 3-methyladenine promoted cell death in cultured slices of HUMAN growth plate tissue, and impaired growth of mouse metatarsal explants with caspase-3 and caspase-9 processing and cytochrome c release. Upstream, autophagic flux in chondrocytes is set by matrix sulfation state and FGF signalling: proteoglycan desulfation in the diastrophic dysplasia sulfate transporter mutant changes autophagy efficiency and FGF signalling extent during endochondral ossification (Settembre 2008, mouse). Autophagy is not constitutive across the plate: immunohistochemistry localises the autophagic phenotype to the postmitotic maturing zone, making it a transient stage of the maturation programme rather than a background housekeeping state, and pharmacological/siRNA work places its induction under mTOR and AMPK control in a HIF-1-dependent manner (Srinivas 2009, mouse and chondrocytic cells). The genetic test of the mTORC1-autophagy link in growth plate chondrocytes in vivo has still not been done.
autophagy_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: Autophagy inhibitors killed chondrocytes in cultured human growth plate tissue slices - an ex vivo human interventional result.
autophagy_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Human data are ex vivo pharmacology on explanted tissue with non-specific inhibitors; the genetics are mouse.
localization: mouse maturing/postmitotic zone: autophagic phenotype localised by immunohistochemistry (srinivas2009)
human growth plate (cultured tissue slices): autophagy inhibition causes chondrocyte death (vuppalapati2015)
mouse growth plate: Atg5/Atg7 required for chondrocyte survival (vuppalapati2015)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chondrocyte Atg5/Atg7 deletion causes mild mouse growth retardation with caspase-dependent death; autophagy inhibitors kill chondrocytes in human growth plate slices.
Autophagy is a transient stage confined to the postmitotic maturing zone and is regulated by mTOR and AMPK in a HIF-1-dependent way.
Proteoglycan desulfation sets the efficiency of chondrocyte autophagy and the extent of FGF signalling in mouse.

beta2_adrenoceptor_chondrocyte.name: Beta-2 adrenoceptor in chondrocytes
beta2_adrenoceptor_chondrocyte.summary:
The atlas had NO autonomic or neural input to the growth plate at all - the strings 'adrenergic' and 'catecholamine' resolved to zero nodes across 614 - and no gap asserted the absence. The Phase 7 falsification run found the hole (item P08) and it was logged as a coverage gap; this node closes it with the primary that motivated the search.
Chondrocyte-specific deletion of the beta-2 adrenoceptor in mouse REDUCES long bone growth, and the authors attribute it to a FASTER transition of proliferative to hypertrophic chondrocytes rather than to a proliferation deficit - which places catecholamine input on the same control variable (time spent proliferating before hypertrophy) that thyroid hormone, CNP and glucocorticoid act on. Tibiae and femora were analysed at 6, 12 and 40 weeks in both sexes. Older knockouts additionally showed an osteopenic phenotype with reduced osteoblast number, and fracture healing was delayed with reduced cartilage area at an intermediate time point. An in vitro expression experiment implicated WNT and TGF-beta signalling (kuhn2026).
The wider context is that systemic and osteoblast-specific beta-2 adrenoceptor knockouts INCREASE bone mass, so the cartilage-specific effect is not the same sign as the skeletal one and cannot be inferred from it - which is exactly why a chondrocyte-specific allele was needed.
NOTHING HUMAN. There is no human genetic, pharmacological or observational evidence in this atlas connecting beta-blockade or sympathetic tone to longitudinal growth, and beta-blockers are prescribed to children. That is a gap this node opens rather than closes.

claim_grades.claim: Beta-2 adrenoceptor signalling in chondrocytes is required for normal long bone growth.
claim_grades.basis: One mouse conditional knockout, both sexes, three ages (kuhn2026). No replication.

claim_grades.claim: The mechanism is a faster proliferative-to-hypertrophic transition rather than reduced proliferation.
claim_grades.basis: Author interpretation of the same single study; stated as "most likely" in the source and not independently tested.

claim_grades.claim: Sympathetic tone or beta-blockade affects human longitudinal growth.
claim_grades.basis: Not traceable to any primary data in humans. Recorded because beta-blockers are prescribed to children and the question has apparently not been asked.

beta2_adrenoceptor_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human data of any kind. The mechanism is one mouse conditional knockout.
beta2_adrenoceptor_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: A single mouse conditional knockout, with the additional complication that the systemic and osteoblast-specific knockouts of the same receptor move bone mass in the OPPOSITE direction. Nothing licenses transferring the cartilage-specific sign to humans.
localization: mouse growth plate chondrocyte: functional requirement demonstrated by conditional deletion (kuhn2026)
human growth plate: not examined by any retrieved study

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chondrocyte-specific beta-2 adrenoceptor knockout reduces long bone growth in mouse, attributed to faster proliferative-to-hypertrophic transition; osteopenia at 40 weeks and delayed fracture healing.

aliases: adrenergic input to the growth plate

beta_catenin_ctnnb1.name: beta-catenin (CTNNB1)
beta_catenin_ctnnb1.summary: beta-catenin is the transducer whose cytoplasmic pool is destroyed by the APC/AXIN/GSK3B destruction complex unless WNT-receptor engagement inhibits it. In chondrocytes its level is read as a dose, not a switch. Deleting it in committed growth plate chondrocytes lowers proliferation and delays hypertrophy; stabilising it accelerates hypertrophy and, if raised further or earlier, blocks chondrogenesis altogether (Akiyama 2004; Dao 2012, mouse). Deleting it only from Col10a1-expressing hypertrophic chondrocytes leaves hypertrophic zone height normal but reduces Mmp13 and Vegfa and produces less trabecular bone, showing a distinct late requirement in the terminal cell (Golovchenko 2013, mouse). beta-catenin and SOX9 are mutually antagonistic: SOX9 binds beta-catenin through its C-terminal transactivation domain, blocks TCF/LEF-dependent transcription and promotes beta-catenin degradation (Akiyama 2004), and SOX9 promotes nuclear phosphorylation of beta-catenin to speed its turnover (Topol 2009). This reciprocal inhibition is the single most important convergence in the layer: the same molecular ratio sets both chondrocyte identity and the hypertrophy decision.
beta_catenin_ctnnb1.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate beta-catenin localisation or perturbation data; human CTNNB1 variants cause neurodevelopmental disease, not a defined physeal phenotype.
beta_catenin_ctnnb1.translation_risk_reason: All causal data are mouse conditional alleles; the human dose-response is unmeasured.
localization: mouse HZ: functionally required for Mmp13/Vegfa expression in Col10a1+ cells (golovchenko2013)
mouse PZ/PHZ: functionally required for normal proliferation and hypertrophy timing (akiyama2004, chen2008)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: SOX9 binds beta-catenin via its C-terminal transactivation domain, inhibits TCF/LEF transcription and promotes beta-catenin degradation.
SOX9 inhibits WNT signalling by promoting phosphorylation of beta-catenin in the nucleus.
Deleting beta-catenin only in Col10a1+ hypertrophic chondrocytes lowers Mmp13/Vegfa and reduces trabecular bone without changing HZ size.
Cartilage-specific beta-catenin gain of function accelerates maturation and ossification centre formation.

bmp2_ligand.name: BMP2
bmp2_ligand.summary: BMP2 is expressed in mouse perichondrium and in prehypertrophic/hypertrophic chondrocytes. Chondrocyte-restricted Bmp2 deletion (Col2-Cre) in mouse shortens long bones, reduces chondrocyte proliferation and delays hypertrophic maturation, whereas the equivalent Bmp4 deletion produces a much weaker phenotype, so within cartilage BMP2 is the non-redundant member of the pair (Shu 2011). Germline analysis of the limb bud shows Bmp2 and Bmp7 are individually dispensable for skeletal element formation but Bmp2;Bmp4 double loss in limb mesenchyme blocks skeletogenesis, i.e. redundancy is compartment-specific (Bandyopadhyay 2006, mouse). BMP2 is also the ligand through which chondrocyte beta-catenin appears to act on maturation: Col2CreERT2-driven beta-catenin stabilisation raises Bmp2 in cartilage (Dao 2012, mouse), and VEGF induction in chondrocytes requires BMP2 and beta-catenin signalling together (Chen 2008, mouse). No human BMP2 loss-of-function short-stature syndrome is established from growth plate material.
bmp2_ligand.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate localisation or interventional data for BMP2 in longitudinal growth.
bmp2_ligand.translation_risk_reason: All causal data are mouse conditional knockouts; recombinant BMP2 human use is in fusion/nonunion, not physis.
localization: mouse PERI: confirmed by in situ hybridisation (bandyopadhyay2006)
mouse PHZ/HZ: confirmed by in situ hybridisation (shu2011)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Cartilage-specific Bmp2 but not Bmp4 deletion impairs chondrocyte proliferation and maturation in mouse.
Bmp2 and Bmp4 are redundantly required in limb mesenchyme for skeletogenesis; Bmp7 is dispensable.
Cartilage beta-catenin gain-of-function raises Bmp2 and accelerates chondrocyte maturation in mouse.

bmp6_ligand.name: BMP6
bmp6_ligand.summary: BMP6 is expressed by hypertrophic chondrocytes in the mouse growth plate. Germline Bmp6-null mice are viable and modestly affected: Perry 2008 reports delayed ossification and altered growth plate architecture with reduced hypertrophic zone function rather than gross dwarfism, consistent with heavy redundancy inside the BMP family. BMP6 is the ligand most cleanly linked to systemic iron handling (hepcidin), so any growth phenotype in Bmp6 mutants must be interpreted against a possible iron-status confounder, which the skeletal literature has not controlled. There is no human BMP6 skeletal dysplasia. This node is retained as a component of the BMP ligand inventory rather than as an established control point of human longitudinal growth.
bmp6_ligand.human_evidence_note: No human BMP6 growth-plate data and no BMP6-linked human short stature syndrome.
bmp6_ligand.translation_risk_reason: Single mouse germline knockout with a mild phenotype; no human correlate.
localization: mouse HZ: reported (perry2008)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Bmp6-null mice show impaired growth plate function with delayed hypertrophic differentiation.

bmp7_ligand.name: BMP7
bmp7_ligand.summary: BMP7 is expressed in mouse perichondrium and, unlike BMP2/BMP4, is individually dispensable for limb skeletal element formation: Bmp7-null limb buds pattern and ossify essentially normally, and removing Bmp7 on top of Bmp2/Bmp4 loss does not add a distinguishable limb phenotype (Bandyopadhyay 2006, mouse). Its non-redundant role appears postnatally and in articular rather than growth plate cartilage: conditional elimination of Bmp7 from limb mesenchyme leaves the growth plate grossly intact but leads to articular cartilage degeneration with age (Abula 2015, mouse). BMP7 is therefore a weak candidate as a growth-plate rate-setting ligand and is included here to close the ligand inventory and to mark the articular-versus-physeal divergence explicitly.
bmp7_ligand.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate data; recombinant BMP7 clinical use was in spinal fusion, not physiological growth.
bmp7_ligand.translation_risk_reason: Mouse-only genetics; the phenotype is articular, and articular and physeal chondrocytes are not interchangeable.
localization: mouse PERI: confirmed by in situ hybridisation (bandyopadhyay2006)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Bmp7 is dispensable for limb skeletogenesis in mouse, unlike Bmp2/Bmp4.
Removing Bmp7 from limb mesenchyme causes articular cartilage degeneration in mouse.

bmp_signaling_growth_plate.name: BMP signalling in the growth plate
bmp_signaling_growth_plate.summary: BMP ligands act on chondrocytes through the type I receptors BMPR1A and BMPR1B, which phosphorylate SMAD1/5/8; Bmpr1a;Bmpr1b double-null mouse limbs form only condensations and generate essentially no cartilage, while either single null is comparatively mild, establishing receptor redundancy (Yoon 2005, mouse). Downstream, chondrocyte-restricted loss of Smad1 plus Smad5 in mouse reproduces a severe chondrodysplasia with a disorganised, thinned proliferative zone, whereas Smad8 is dispensable (Retting 2009). In mouse limb explant culture BMP2 raises the proliferation rate of columnar chondrocytes and delays the onset of hypertrophy, and it does so in part by raising Ihh expression - yet BMP still increases proliferation in explants where Ihh signalling is blocked, so the BMP and Ihh/PTHrP arms are parallel rather than strictly serial (Minina 2001, mouse). BMP signalling and FGFR3 signalling are antagonistic on both proliferation and the hypertrophy decision in the same explant system (Minina 2002, mouse). The pathway is dose-limited in vivo by the secreted antagonists Noggin and Chordin and by intracellular SMAD7. Zonally, laser-capture microdissection of postnatal mouse proximal tibia followed by direct mRNA counting shows Bmp2 and Bmp6 expression rising to a maximum in the hypertrophic zone, yet phospho-SMAD1/5/8 immunostaining is HIGHER in the proliferative and prehypertrophic zones than in the hypertrophic zone - ligand abundance and pathway activity run in opposite directions across the plate, apparently because the inhibitory SMAD7 is concentrated in the hypertrophic zone (Garrison 2017, mouse). Human evidence is genetic and indirect: NOG, GDF5, BMPR1B and LTBP3 variants cause recognisable skeletal phenotypes, but no human growth plate has been assayed for zonal pSMAD1/5/8 activity.
bmp_signaling_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is entirely genetic (NOG symphalangism, GDF5/CDMP1 chondrodysplasia, LTBP3 brachyolmia); no direct measurement of BMP pathway activity in human growth plate tissue.
bmp_signaling_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: Receptor and SMAD genetics are mouse-only; the human read-out is dysmorphology from germline variants, which cannot separate growth-plate-autonomous from patterning effects.
localization: mouse PZ/PHZ: pSmad1/5/8 immunostaining highest here, above the hypertrophic zone (garrison2017)
mouse HZ: Bmp2 and Bmp6 mRNA highest, but pSmad1/5/8 lower and Smad7 high (garrison2017)
mouse PERI: confirmed - Bmp2/Bmp4/Bmp7 expressed in perichondrium (bandyopadhyay2006)
human growth plate: unconfirmed - no zonal pSMAD1/5/8 immunostaining series published

key_refs.one_line_finding: Bmpr1a/Bmpr1b double conditional-null mouse limbs fail to form cartilage; single nulls are mild.
Chondrocyte Smad1/Smad5 double deletion causes severe chondrodysplasia; Smad8 loss adds nothing.
Zonal LCM plus IHC in mouse tibia: Bmp2/Bmp6 mRNA peaks in HZ but pSmad1/5/8 activity peaks in PZ/PHZ, with Smad7 high in HZ.
BMP2 in mouse limb explants increases chondrocyte proliferation and delays hypertrophy, partly Ihh-independent.
BMP and FGF signalling act antagonistically on proliferation and on the hypertrophy decision in the same explants.

cgmp_second_messenger.name: cGMP
cgmp_second_messenger.summary:
cGMP is the sole second messenger of the CNP/NPR2 arm of growth plate control. Its concentration is
set by the balance of synthesis by NPR2 (and, at high CNP, by NPR1/GC-A) against hydrolysis by
cyclic-nucleotide phosphodiesterases, and it acts through PKG-II and PKG-I. Because production and
hydrolysis are both regulated, cGMP amplitude and duration - not receptor occupancy - are the
proximate variable, and both directions have been demonstrated in vivo: FGF signalling lowers growth
plate cGMP by dephosphorylating NPR2, measured directly in intact mouse tibia with a cGMP biosensor
(Shuhaibar 2017), while PDE inhibition raises it. In newborn rat epiphyseal chondrocytes tadalafil
raised the peak CNP-stimulated cGMP by 37% and whole-tissue cGMP by 52%, yet produced no increase in
long bone length over three weeks (Wang 2018), whereas in mouse the PDE3 inhibitor cilostazol raised
chondrocyte cGMP, elongated cultured bones and enlarged juvenile animals (Kawabe 2025). The
mismatch between measured cGMP elevation and growth output is unexplained and is the strongest
argument that compartmentalised, PDE-defined cGMP microdomains rather than bulk cGMP set growth.
cgmp_second_messenger.human_evidence_note: cGMP has never been measured in human growth plate tissue; human evidence for the axis is genetic and pharmacological, not biochemical.
cgmp_second_messenger.translation_risk_reason: All direct cGMP measurements in cartilage are rodent; rat and mouse already disagree on whether raising cGMP raises growth.
localization: mouse growth plate, measured in intact tibia with a cGMP biosensor: confirmed (shuhaibar2017)
human growth plate: cGMP has never been measured in situ

key_refs.one_line_finding: In vivo cGMP imaging in intact mouse tibia shows FGF lowers growth plate cGMP via NPR2 dephosphorylation.
Tadalafil raised rat chondrocyte cGMP 37% and tissue cGMP 52% without increasing long bone length.
PDE3 inhibitors raise chondrocyte cGMP, elongate cultured bones and enlarge juvenile mice.

chordin_antagonist.name: Chordin (CHRD)
chordin_antagonist.summary: Chordin is a secreted BMP antagonist that shares substrate ligands with Noggin. In mouse, Chrd-null animals have craniofacial and pharyngeal defects; the appendicular skeleton is comparatively spared until Noggin is also removed, at which point mandibular and skeletal morphogenesis fails, demonstrating redundancy between the two antagonists (Stottmann 2001). There is no established human CHRD skeletal dysplasia and no report of zonal CHRD protein or transcript distribution in human growth plate. Chordin is therefore included as an inventory node with an explicit negative: within the growth plate proper, Noggin dominates the published antagonist evidence and Chordin's physeal role is assumed rather than demonstrated.
chordin_antagonist.human_evidence_note: No human CHRD skeletal phenotype and no human growth plate expression data.
chordin_antagonist.translation_risk_reason: Mouse-only, and even in mouse the demonstrated territory is craniofacial rather than physeal.
localization: mouse craniofacial mesenchyme: confirmed (stottmann2001)
mouse growth plate: unconfirmed
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chordin and Noggin act redundantly in mouse mandibular and skeletal morphogenesis.

cnp_protein.name: C-type natriuretic peptide
cnp_protein.summary:
CNP is encoded by NPPC, translated as proCNP and cleaved by furin at a tetrabasic site to CNP-53,
which is further processed to CNP-22 (Wu 2003). In the growth plate CNP is made by non-hypertrophic
chondrocytes and acts locally: cartilage-specific Nppc deletion in mouse reproduces essentially the
whole systemic-knockout dwarfism, so the autocrine/paracrine pool, not circulating CNP, is the
physiological driver (Nakao 2015). Nppc-null mice are severely dwarfed and die early (Chusho 2001).
The effect is zone-partitioned but GRADED, not exclusive: in cartilage-specific Nppc-null mice the
type X collagen-positive hypertrophic layer falls to 34.6% of control thickness whereas the
non-hypertrophic layer falls only to 76.7%, and the BrdU index merely trends lower - but in the
matched cartilage-specific Npr2-null the same index is SIGNIFICANTLY reduced, and the summary
given by the authors is that the proliferative layer and its proliferation are moderately reduced in both
(Nakao 2015, n=5 per group). In mouse tibia organ culture CNP acts largely by expanding the
hypertrophic zone and zonal microarray shows far more CNP-regulated genes in hypertrophic than in
the combined resting/proliferative compartment (Agoston 2007); the hypertrophic-zone expansion in
that system requires p38, while CNP simultaneously inhibits ERK. Downstream of NPR2 the effector
assignment is unsettled: the PKG-II zonal explanation has been retracted (CORR-003), and CNP-driven
bone growth in tibia explant is abolished by chondrocyte-specific Trpm7 ablation, placing a
PKG-BK channel-TRPM7-CaMKII arm alongside SOX9/GSK-3beta (Miyazaki 2022).
Human dosage evidence runs in both directions: heterozygous NPPC ring-domain mutations cause
autosomal dominant short stature with small hands (Hisado-Oliva 2018), while balanced translocations
clustering at 2q37.1 that overexpress NPPC cause a Marfanoid overgrowth syndrome with roughly doubled
plasma CNP (Bocciardi 2007; Moncla 2007).
cnp_protein.human_evidence_note: Human NPPC loss-of-function causes dominant short stature and human NPPC overexpression causes overgrowth with measured plasma CNP; a CNP analogue increases growth velocity in a randomised human trial.
cnp_protein.translation_risk_reason: Both directions of the human dosage series are documented and a human interventional trial of a CNP analogue reproduces the predicted direction and magnitude.
localization: mouse non-hypertrophic chondrocyte layers (RZ/PZ): confirmed by IHC and cartilage-specific KO (nakao2015). The CNP IHC in that paper demonstrates knock-down; it is not a quantitative zonal map
mouse HZ: CNP-regulated transcriptome strongly enriched, confirmed by zonal microarray (agoston2007)
human growth plate: zonal CNP protein distribution unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Nppc-null mice are dwarfed with severely shortened long bones and early death.
Cartilage-specific Nppc deletion reproduces systemic knockout dwarfism; hypertrophic layer falls to 34.6% of control while non-hypertrophic layer falls only to 76.7%.
CNP grows mouse tibia largely by expanding the hypertrophic zone; zonal microarray shows hypertrophic chondrocytes are the main CNP target.
CNP-facilitated bone growth in mouse tibia explant is abolished by chondrocyte-specific Trpm7 ablation, via PKG acting on the BK channel to drive TRPM7 Ca2+ entry and CaMKII.
Heterozygous NPPC ring-domain mutations cause autosomal dominant short stature with small hands.
A balanced t(2;7) near NPPC doubles plasma CNP and causes Marfanoid overgrowth.
Two further 2q37.1 translocations overexpress NPPC and reproduce the overgrowth phenotype.
Furin cleaves proCNP to CNP-53.
Vosoritide increased annualised growth velocity by 1.57 cm/yr versus placebo in achondroplasia.

Corin- and Nppa(ANP)-null mice have impaired chondrocyte differentiation and SHORTENED limb long bones with reduced adult bone density; ANP acts IN CHONDROCYTES via cGMP-dependent protein kinase G to inhibit MAPK phosphorylation and raise phospho-GSK-3beta and beta-catenin - a genetic requirement for the NPR1/GC-A ligand arm in the same cGMP-PKG readout the atlas attributes wholly to CNP/NPR2.

dkk1_antagonist.name: DKK1
dkk1_antagonist.summary: DKK1 is a secreted antagonist that binds LRP5/LRP6 (with Kremen) and removes them from the receptor complex, shutting down canonical WNT. Transgenic overexpression of Dkk1 in mouse bone causes osteopenia with reduced osteoblast number, and Dkk1 heterozygous-null mice have increased bone mass, giving a clean in vivo dose relation for the bone compartment (Li 2006). The human LRP5 G171V high-bone-mass allele acts by resisting DKK1 binding, which is independent human evidence that DKK1 tone is physiologically load-bearing (Boyden 2002). What is missing is the physeal half: no report establishes DKK1 protein in the human or mouse growth plate by zone, and no chondrocyte-restricted Dkk1 deletion growth plate phenotype has been published. DKK1 is thus a well-evidenced bone node and an assumed cartilage node.
dkk1_antagonist.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is the DKK1-resistant LRP5 allele; there is no direct human DKK1 growth plate measurement.
dkk1_antagonist.translation_risk_reason: Mouse transgenics for the mechanism; the human inference is via a receptor allele, not via DKK1 itself.
localization: mouse bone: confirmed by transgenic and heterozygous-null phenotypes (li2006)
growth plate zonal distribution: unconfirmed in mouse and human

key_refs.one_line_finding: Dkk1 overexpression causes mouse osteopenia and Dkk1 heterozygosity increases bone mass.
The human high-bone-mass LRP5 allele resists DKK1 inhibition.

evc_evc2_complex.name: EVC-EVC2 complex
evc_evc2_complex.summary: EVC and EVC2 form an obligate complex localised to a discrete compartment at the base of the primary cilium, the 'EvC zone'. Evc-null mice reproduce an Ellis-van Creveld-like syndrome with short ribs, short limbs and dental abnormalities; their growth plates show delayed bone collar formation and ADVANCED chondrocyte maturation, Ihh expression is normal but the Ihh target genes Ptch1 and Gli1 are markedly reduced, cilia are present and Gli3 processing is normal - so the lesion is downstream of SMO and independent of ciliogenesis itself (Ruiz-Perez 2007, mouse). Dorn 2012 supplies the biochemistry: Hedgehog agonists promote a SMO-EVC2 association restricted to the EvC zone, and EVC2 mutants that still enter cilia but are displaced from that zone act as dominant inhibitors, blocking signalling between SMO and PKA/SUFU before GLI activation. In human, EVC mutations cause recessive Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (short limbs, short ribs, postaxial polydactyly, dysplastic nails and teeth, congenital heart defect in about 60%) and heterozygous missense alleles cause dominant Weyers acrodental dysostosis, an allelic milder condition (Ruiz-Perez 2000). This node is the direct mechanical link between the cilium subsystem and the IHH subsystem.
evc_evc2_complex.human_evidence_note: EVC and EVC2 mutations cause human Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (recessive) and Weyers acrodental dysostosis (dominant).
evc_evc2_complex.translation_risk_reason: Human recessive and dominant allelic series, plus a concordant mouse null and cell-biological mechanism.
localization: mouse chondrocyte cilium base: confirmed by antibody staining (ruizperez2007)
EvC zone at ciliary base: confirmed biochemically (dorn2012)
human growth plate: inferred from Ellis-van Creveld phenotype

key_refs.one_line_finding: EVC mutations cause Ellis-van Creveld syndrome; heterozygous missense alleles cause allelic Weyers acrodental dysostosis.
Evc localises to the base of the chondrocyte cilium and is required for Ihh-dependent Ptch1/Gli1 induction downstream of Smo.
Hedgehog agonists drive a SMO-EVC2 complex confined to the EvC zone; EVC2 displaced from that zone is a dominant inhibitor.

fgf18_ligand.name: FGF18
fgf18_ligand.summary:
FGF18 is the principal physiological ligand for FGFR3 in the growth plate. Fgf18-null mice
phenocopy Fgfr3-null mice - expanded proliferative and hypertrophic zones with increased chondrocyte
proliferation and delayed terminal differentiation and ossification - which is the genetic argument
that FGF18 is the ligand acting on FGFR3 in this tissue (Liu 2002; Ohbayashi 2002). FGF18 is
expressed by perichondrium and adjacent mesenchyme rather than by chondrocytes themselves, so the
FGFR3 brake is applied from outside the cartilage. An allelic series combining Fgf9 and Fgf18
mutations shows unique and redundant roles, with Fgf18 dominant in the growth plate and Fgf9 dominant
in vascularisation (Hung 2016). FGF18 also drives the FGFR3-NPR2 antagonism: FGF18 reduces
CNP-dependent cGMP production in ATDC5 cells and counteracts CNP on longitudinal growth and on
hypertrophic chondrocyte size and number in organ-cultured fetal mouse tibia (Ozasa 2005). No human
FGF18 monogenic skeletal phenotype has been described.
fgf18_ligand.human_evidence_note: No human FGF18 variant with a skeletal phenotype has been reported and no human growth plate FGF18 localisation exists.
fgf18_ligand.translation_risk_reason: Ligand assignment rests entirely on mouse knockouts; the human growth plate ligand for FGFR3 has never been identified directly.
localization: mouse PERI and adjacent mesenchyme: confirmed by ISH (liu2002, ohbayashi2002)
human growth plate: FGF18 localisation unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Fgf18-null mice phenocopy Fgfr3-null mice with expanded proliferative and hypertrophic zones.
FGF18 is required for normal chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation during endochondral ossification.
Fgf9/Fgf18 allelic series separates unique and redundant roles, Fgf18 dominant in the growth plate.
FGF18 reduces CNP-dependent cGMP and counteracts CNP on hypertrophic chondrocyte size and number.

fgf2_ligand.name: FGF2
fgf2_ligand.summary:
FGF2 is the workhorse experimental ligand of this pathway rather than an established physiological
growth plate ligand. It is the agonist used to demonstrate FGFR3-dependent effects in chondrocyte
systems: FGF2 inhibits chondrocyte proliferation through STAT1 in rat chondrosarcoma cells and
primary murine chondrocytes (Sahni 1999), FGF2 markedly reduces CNP-dependent cGMP production in
ATDC5 cells in a MAPK-dependent manner (Ozasa 2005), and quantitative FRET studies of the
achondroplasia mutation used FGF1 and FGF2 as the ligands (Sarabipour 2016). In human thanatophoric
dysplasia type I fetal chondrocytes FGF2 produced a normal mitogenic response (Legeai-Mallet 1998).
Because FGF2 activates several FGFRs, effects attributed to FGF2 in cartilage cannot be assigned to
FGFR3 without genetic confirmation, and the physiological ligands in vivo are FGF18 and FGF9.
fgf2_ligand.human_evidence_note: FGF2 has been applied to cultured human fetal chondrocytes; there is no human genetic or tissue evidence for an endogenous FGF2 role in the growth plate.
fgf2_ligand.translation_risk_reason: Non-selective pharmacological tool ligand; receptor attribution requires genetic confirmation not available in human tissue.
localization: in vitro chondrocyte systems: applied exogenously; endogenous growth plate localization not the basis of its use
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: FGF2 inhibits chondrocyte proliferation through STAT-1 in rat and mouse chondrocytes.
FGF2 reduces CNP-dependent cGMP production in ATDC5 cells via MAPK.
FGF1 and FGF2 used as ligands in quantitative FRET analysis of the achondroplasia mutation.

fgf9_ligand.name: FGF9
fgf9_ligand.summary:
FGF9 is a second FGFR3 ligand in the developing skeleton whose principal, non-redundant function is
in the transition from cartilage to bone rather than in the proliferative column. Fgf9 loss delays
the onset of hypertrophic differentiation and impairs growth plate vascularisation and
vascular endothelial growth factor-dependent invasion in the mouse stylopod (Hung 2007), and the
combined Fgf9/Fgf18 allelic series confirms that Fgf9 contributes most to vascularisation while
Fgf18 dominates chondrocyte control (Hung 2016). In cultured human thanatophoric dysplasia type I
fetal chondrocytes FGF9 produced normal, not reduced, mitogenesis and accelerated ERK activation
relative to controls (Legeai-Mallet 1998), so the one place FGF9 has been applied to human growth
plate cells it did not reproduce the mouse proliferation-arrest phenotype. No human FGF9 skeletal
dysplasia has been reported.
fgf9_ligand.human_evidence_note: FGF9 has been applied to cultured human fetal chondrocytes but has no human genetic skeletal phenotype and no human tissue localisation.
fgf9_ligand.translation_risk_reason: Mouse-only genetics; the single human cell experiment gave a result opposite to the mouse expectation.
localization: mouse perichondrium and developing stylopod: confirmed (hung2007)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: FGF9 regulates onset of hypertrophic differentiation and skeletal vascularization in mouse stylopod.
Fgf9 contributes mainly to vascularization in the combined Fgf9/Fgf18 allelic series.
FGF9 gave normal mitogenic response in human TD I fetal chondrocytes.

fgfr1_receptor.name: FGFR1
fgfr1_receptor.summary:
In human embryo-fetal long bones FGFR1 transcripts are restricted to perichondrium and periosteum,
not to growth plate chondrocytes; the limb bud mesenchyme expresses FGFR1 early, and only in the
cranial vault do FGFR1-3 co-express in preosteoblasts and osteoblasts (Delezoide 1998). This human
expression map matters because it means the human growth plate is an FGFR3-dominant, not a
pan-FGFR, tissue. Mouse data place FGFR1 in the hypertrophic and osteoprogenitor compartments:
deletion of Fgfr1 in the osteo-chondrogenic lineage delays hypertrophic chondrocyte maturation and
alters sequential osteoblast differentiation (Jacob 2006), and loss of Fgfr1 with Fgfr2 in
Scleraxis-lineage cells enlarges bone eminences. FGFR1 is therefore best described as acting at the
chondro-osseous junction and perichondrium rather than within the proliferative column, but a
zone-resolved FGFR1 protein map of the human postnatal growth plate does not exist - the Delezoide
data are embryonic/fetal ISH.
fgfr1_receptor.human_evidence_note: FGFR1 expression was mapped directly in human embryo-fetal ossifying long bones by in situ hybridisation.
fgfr1_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Human data are expression only and embryonic/fetal; function is inferred from mouse conditional knockouts.
localization: human fetal long bone PERI and PERIOST: confirmed by ISH (delezoide1998)
human fetal growth plate chondrocytes: FGFR1 not detected (delezoide1998)
mouse HZ and osteoprogenitors: functionally confirmed by conditional deletion (jacob2006)

key_refs.one_line_finding: FGFR1 transcripts are perichondrial and periosteal, not chondrocytic, in human fetal long bone.
Fgfr1 deletion in the osteo-chondrogenic lineage delays hypertrophic chondrocyte maturation.

fgfr2_receptor.name: FGFR2
fgfr2_receptor.summary:
FGFR2 is the earliest marker of prechondrogenic condensations in the human embryo and is
subsequently restricted, like FGFR1, to perichondrium and periosteum, with marked additional
expression in periarticular cartilage (Delezoide 1998). It is not expressed in the columnar or
hypertrophic chondrocytes of the human fetal growth plate. Human FGFR2 mutations cause
craniosynostosis syndromes (Apert, Crouzon, Pfeiffer) dominated by membranous rather than
endochondral pathology, consistent with the expression map in which FGFR1-3 co-express in cranial
suture preosteoblasts. FGFR2 therefore contributes to the condensation and perichondrial phases of
endochondral skeletogenesis and to the periarticular compartment that supplies the growth plate,
rather than to zonal control within the plate itself.
fgfr2_receptor.human_evidence_note: Human embryo-fetal FGFR2 expression was mapped directly by in situ hybridisation and human FGFR2 mutations produce well-characterised craniosynostosis syndromes.
fgfr2_receptor.translation_risk_reason: The expression map is human and the disease phenotypes are human; risk is limited to inferring function from expression.
localization: human prechondrogenic condensation: earliest marker, confirmed by ISH (delezoide1998)
human fetal PERI, PERIOST and periarticular cartilage: confirmed by ISH (delezoide1998)
human growth plate columnar/hypertrophic chondrocytes: not detected (delezoide1998)

key_refs.one_line_finding: FGFR2 marks prechondrogenic condensations then perichondrium, periosteum and periarticular cartilage in human fetus.

fgfr3_mapk_branch.name: FGFR3-MAPK/ERK branch
fgfr3_mapk_branch.summary:
The RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK branch downstream of FGFR3 is the arm that suppresses chondrocyte hypertrophy.
Constitutively active MEK1 expressed in mouse chondrocytes produces achondroplasia-like dwarfism with
incomplete hypertrophy, reduced type X collagen, persistent Sox9 and a general delay in endochondral
ossification, while chondrocyte proliferation is unaffected; the same transgene suppresses the
overgrowth of Fgfr3-null mice, which the authors read as bone growth being regulated by FGFR3 "at
least in part" through MAPK (Murakami 2004). Note the logic: activating a downstream node and finding
it suppresses loss of the upstream node establishes SUFFICIENCY, not necessity, and the transgene is
a constitutively active MEK1 under a Col2a1 driver with mosaic expression, so the ERK amplitude tested
is supraphysiological and non-uniform rather than the amplitude FGFR3-G380R actually produces. The branch is also
the target of the CNP rescue: chondrocyte-targeted CNP overexpression rescues achondroplasia in
FGFR3-Ach mice through MAPK inhibition (Yasoda 2004), and CNP or 8-Br-cGMP dose-dependently blocks
FGF2- and FGF18-induced ERK phosphorylation at the level of RAF-1 without affecting STAT1
phosphorylation (Ozasa 2005). The MAPK branch additionally acts on NPR2 itself: FGF-driven, PPP-family
phosphatase-dependent dephosphorylation of NPR2 lowers growth plate cGMP (Shuhaibar 2017). Note also that "the MAPK branch" contains at least two
antagonistic arms, and only the ERK arm is in this node: in micro-dissected mouse tibia, CNP requires
p38 to achieve and maintain the expanded hypertrophic zone while simultaneously inhibiting ERK
(Agoston 2007), so p38 and ERK act in opposite directions on hypertrophy. The
branch weighting relative to STAT1 is contested - see fgfr3_stat1_branch and gap g_l3core_008.
fgfr3_mapk_branch.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is limited to accelerated ERK activation kinetics in cultured thanatophoric dysplasia chondrocytes; no in situ measurement of ERK activity in human growth plate zones.
fgfr3_mapk_branch.translation_risk_reason: Branch dissection is murine transgenic; human data are cultured fetal chondrocytes only.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: MEK1 transgene blocks hypertrophy, confirmed (murakami2004)
human growth plate: ERK activation state by zone unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Constitutively active MEK1 in chondrocytes blocks hypertrophy (reduced collagen X, persistent Sox9, BrdU-labelled cells stalling prehypertrophically) with an UNCHANGED BrdU index, and suppresses Fgfr3-null overgrowth; Stat1 loss restores proliferation in Fgfr3-ACH mice but rescues neither the hypertrophic zone nor the phenotype.
CNP overexpression rescues achondroplasia in FGFR3-Ach mice through a MAPK-dependent pathway.
CNP and 8-Br-cGMP inhibit FGF-induced ERK phosphorylation at RAF-1 without affecting STAT1.
FGF-driven phosphatase-dependent NPR2 dephosphorylation lowers growth plate cGMP in intact mouse tibia.

fgfr3_npr2_crosstalk.name: FGFR3-NPR2 crosstalk
fgfr3_npr2_crosstalk.summary:
This is the best-characterised convergence point in the layer, and the answer to whether FGFR3
reduces NPR2 output transcriptionally or post-translationally is: post-translationally, with no
demonstrated transcriptional component. Ozasa 2005 showed in mouse ATDC5 chondrogenic cells that
FGF2 and FGF18 markedly reduce CNP-dependent cGMP production and that MAPK inhibitors reverse this,
while Western blotting showed GC-B protein levels were unchanged - so the receptor is inactivated,
not removed. Robinson 2017 identified the mechanism in rat chondrosarcoma cells: FGF causes rapid,
potent and reversible dephosphorylation of the seven regulatory juxtamembrane serines and
threonines of GC-B, and a 7-glutamate phosphomimetic GC-B is completely FGF-resistant. Shuhaibar
2017 confirmed this in intact mouse tibia using an in vivo cGMP biosensor, showing FGF lowers growth
plate cGMP through a PPP-family phosphatase and that non-dephosphorylatable NPR2 increases bone
elongation. Wagner 2021 closed the genetic loop in mouse, but more narrowly than the
headline suggests: the cross is HOMOZYGOUS GC-B(7E/7E) into HOMOZYGOUS FGFR3-G380R (human
achondroplasia is heterozygous), it restores femur and tibia length and hypertrophic zone area to
wild-type values while leaving midface hypoplasia and macrocephaly entirely unrescued, and the
2-week effects are strongly sex-specific - G380R shortened bones and reduced hypertrophic zone area
in MALES only, GC-B(7E) lengthened bones in FEMALES only, and the hypertrophic-zone rescue was
therefore demonstrated in males. The interaction is genuine rather than merely additive, because the
femur gain from GC-B(7E) was 12.6% (male) and 7.9% (female) in the G380R background against 4.3% and
5.0% in wild-type FGFR3. Critically, NPR2 phosphorylation state has NEVER been measured in a G380R
growth plate: the chain FGFR3-G380R to phosphatase to NPR2-dephospho has not been observed
end-to-end in one system, and Wagner 2021 states it cannot rule out other FGFR3-activated pathways.
Nor is the phosphatase identified - Shuhaibar 2017 infers only a PPP-family phosphatase, unnamed, from
100 uM cantharidin, which inhibits PPP1, PPP2/PP2A, PPP4 and PPP5 together (g_l2d_004). Receptor
specificity is also weak in the mechanistic papers: Robinson 2017 applied FGF2 to rat chondrosarcoma
cells that express FGFR2 as well as FGFR3, with no receptor-specific manipulation, and Shuhaibar
2017 applied FGF rather than an FGFR3-selective perturbation to intact tibia. The reverse arm is also post-translational: CNP and
8-Br-cGMP inhibit FGF-induced ERK phosphorylation at RAF-1 without changing FGFR3 protein levels or
STAT1 phosphorylation (Ozasa 2005), which is why CNP overexpression rescues FGFR3-Ach mice (Yasoda
2004). Human confirmation is phenotypic rather than molecular: vosoritide, a CNP analogue, raises
annualised growth velocity by 1.57 cm/yr in children with achondroplasia (Savarirayan 2020). No
molecular measurement of NPR2 phosphorylation state has ever been made in human tissue.
fgfr3_npr2_crosstalk.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is the therapeutic epistasis - a CNP analogue partially rescues the growth phenotype of FGFR3 gain-of-function - not a molecular measurement of the interaction in human tissue.
fgfr3_npr2_crosstalk.translation_risk_reason: Molecular mechanism is entirely rodent, but the predicted therapeutic consequence was tested and confirmed in a randomised human trial, which constrains the translation risk substantially.
localization: mouse growth plate, in vivo cGMP biosensor: FGF-driven cGMP reduction confirmed (shuhaibar2017)
rat chondrosarcoma cells: GC-B dephosphorylation confirmed (robinson2017)
mouse ATDC5: GC-B protein unchanged by FGF, cGMP output reduced (ozasa2005)
human growth plate: NPR2 phosphorylation state never measured
FGFR3-G380R mouse growth plate: NPR2 phosphorylation state also never measured - the genetic rescue is epistasis, not a molecular observation of the proposed intermediate

key_refs.one_line_finding: FGF2/FGF18 reduce CNP-dependent cGMP via MAPK without changing GC-B protein level; CNP reciprocally blocks ERK at RAF-1 without affecting STAT1.

FGF2 causes rapid, potent, reversible dephosphorylation of GC-B in rat chondrosarcoma cells - which express FGFR2 as well as FGFR3, with no receptor-specific manipulation performed; a 7E phosphomimetic is FGF-resistant.

FGF lowers growth plate cGMP in intact newborn mouse tibia via NPR2 dephosphorylation blocked by 100 uM cantharidin, implicating an UNIDENTIFIED PPP-family phosphatase (PPP1/PPP2/PPP4/PPP5 are inhibited together at that dose); NPR2-7E is FGF-resistant and lengthens bone.

Homozygous GC-B(7E/7E) crossed into HOMOZYGOUS FGFR3-G380R restores femur/tibia length and hypertrophic zone area to wild-type, with strong sex-specificity at 2 weeks; midface hypoplasia and macrocephaly are NOT rescued; NPR2 phosphorylation state in the G380R growth plate was not measured.
CNP overexpression rescues achondroplasia in FGFR3-Ach mice via MAPK inhibition.
Vosoritide increases annualised growth velocity by 1.57 cm/yr in children with achondroplasia.

fgfr3_receptor.name: FGFR3
fgfr3_receptor.summary:
FGFR3 is the brake on the growth plate: Fgfr3-null mice show skeletal overgrowth with expanded
proliferative and hypertrophic zones (Colvin 1996; Deng 1996), and in human embryo-fetal long bones
FGFR3 is the only one of the three receptors expressed in growth plate chondrocytes, FGFR1 and FGFR2
being restricted to perichondrium and periosteum (Delezoide 1998). The achondroplasia allele G380R
sits in the transmembrane domain, and the mechanism is best described as both ligand-independent
activation and failed termination; which component dominates is NOT settled. Naski 1996 and Webster 1996
showed graded ligand-independent kinase activation with thanatophoric alleles stronger than
achondroplasia; Monsonego-Ornan 2000 showed that G380R dimerisation and activation are predominantly
ligand-dependent but that the mutant receptor is selectively resistant to ligand-mediated
internalisation and down-regulation, producing an expanded FGFR3 immunoreactive domain in transgenic
mouse growth plate; Cho 2004 attributed the defect to reduced c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitination
diverting active receptor from lysosome to recycling - but this is contested in SIGN, not merely in
detail: Monsonego-Ornan et al. 2004 report INCREASED ubiquitination of the same mutants, and Cho
2004 names the disparity, attributes it to Cos-7 versus HEK293, steady-state FGF2 versus pulsed
FGF9 and retroviral versus transient expression, and states it cannot exclude the alternative
(g_l2d_003). c-Cbl also does not bind FGFR3 directly: recruitment is via FRS2alpha and Grb2, and
FRS2alpha binds FGFR1 far more strongly than FGFR3, so the recruitment step for this receptor is
weakly established. Quantitative FRET adjudicates the DIMERISATION question only: G380R does not
change ligand-bound dimer configuration and increases unliganded dimerisation propensity by
-1.8 kcal/mol (Sarabipour 2016). That experiment cannot speak to the down-regulation model, because
the construct is FGFR3 extracellular + transmembrane domain with the ENTIRE INTRACELLULAR KINASE
DOMAIN REPLACED by a fluorescent protein, in CHO-derived vesicles - the machinery the competing
mechanism runs on is structurally absent from the assay. The same paper reports that chemical
cross-linking with Western blot did NOT detect increased G380R dimerisation, and that chemically
produced vesicles gave ~0.5 rather than 1.8 kcal/mol. The defensible reading is that G380R is a weak
constitutive activator that also fails to be switched off, with the relative weight of the two
contributions still unresolved.

claim_grades.claim: FGFR3 is a negative regulator of longitudinal bone growth: increasing its signalling shortens bone and reducing it lengthens bone.
claim_grades.basis: Human gain of function across four graded disorders (shiang1994, bellus1995, tavormina1995) and human partial loss of function giving tall stature in CATSHL syndrome (toydemir2006), concordant with Fgfr3-null mouse overgrowth (colvin1996, deng1996). Both directions are now human.

claim_grades.claim: The achondroplasia allele acts primarily by ligand-independent constitutive kinase activation.
claim_grades.basis: Contested. naski1996 and webster1996 report ligand-independent activation; monsonegoornan2000 reports G380R activation is predominantly ligand-DEPENDENT with failed down-regulation. Unresolved.

claim_grades.claim: The G380R receptor escapes degradation through reduced c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitination.
claim_grades.basis: Contradicted in SIGN: cho2004 reports reduced ubiquitination, Monsonego-Ornan et al. 2004 report increased ubiquitination of the same mutants. Logged as g_l2d_003. This is the claim that sets the node grade.

claim_grades.claim: FGFR3 is the only FGF receptor expressed in human growth plate chondrocytes.
claim_grades.basis: Single human fetal long-bone expression study (delezoide1998), abstract only, not replicated.

fgfr3_receptor.human_evidence_note: FGFR3 expression and pathology have been examined directly in human fetal growth plate and in thanatophoric dysplasia cartilage, and the achondroplasia allele is the commonest human skeletal dysplasia mutation.
fgfr3_receptor.translation_risk_reason: The receptor, its expression domain and the pathogenic allele are all documented in human tissue; mouse models reproduce the human phenotype.
localization: human fetal growth plate, mature chondrocytes: confirmed by ISH (delezoide1998)
human thanatophoric dysplasia cartilage: abundant perinuclear FGFR3 immunoreactivity (legeaimallet1998)
mouse growth plate: FGFR3 immunoreactive domain expanded in G380R transgenics (monsonegoornan2000)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Achondroplasia is caused by a recurrent G380R substitution in the FGFR3 transmembrane domain.
Achondroplasia and thanatophoric FGFR3 mutations give graded ligand-independent activation.
G380R constitutively activates FGFR3 kinase without ligand.
G380R activation is predominantly ligand-dependent; the mutation uncouples activation from down-regulation.

In Cos-7 and RCJ cells, ACH and TDII FGFR3 show REDUCED c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitination and diversion from lysosome to recycling endosome - the opposite sign to Monsonego-Ornan 2004, which Cho 2004 reports and cannot exclude. c-Cbl recruitment to FGFR is indirect, via FRS2alpha/Grb2.

Quantitative FRET on an FGFR3 EC+TM construct whose intracellular kinase domain is replaced by a fluorescent protein: G380R increases unliganded dimerisation by -1.8 kcal/mol and does not change ligand-bound Intrinsic FRET. Cross-linking/Western disagreed; chemical vesiculation gave ~0.5 kcal/mol.
Fgfr3-null mice show skeletal overgrowth with expanded proliferative and hypertrophic zones.
In human fetal long bone FGFR3 is expressed in growth plate chondrocytes while FGFR1/2 are perichondrial and periosteal.
Fgfr3-null mice show enhanced long bone growth, establishing FGFR3 as a negative regulator.
FGFR3 p.R621H causes partial loss of kinase function and CATSHL syndrome with tall stature, supplying the human loss-of-function arm that matches the Fgfr3-null mouse.

fgfr3_stat1_branch.name: FGFR3-STAT1 branch
fgfr3_stat1_branch.summary:
STAT1 is the arm of FGFR3 signalling that suppresses chondrocyte proliferation. FGF treatment of rat
chondrosarcoma cells and primary murine chondrocytes phosphorylates STAT1, drives it to the nucleus
and raises p21WAF1/CIP1; Stat1-null metatarsals do not arrest proliferation in response to FGF
(Sahni 1999). The thanatophoric dysplasia type II K650E mutant constitutively activates STAT1 (Su
1997), and in cultured human thanatophoric dysplasia type I fetal chondrocytes STAT1 is
ligand-independently activated with nuclear STAT1 detectable in hypertrophic chondrocytes
(Legeai-Mallet 1998). The weighting of this branch is genuinely contested. Murakami 2004 showed that
deleting Stat1 in achondroplasia-mutant mice restores chondrocyte proliferation but does not rescue
the reduced hypertrophic zone, the delayed secondary ossification centre or the dwarfism itself,
which places the phenotype-determining load on MAPK. Legeai-Mallet 1998 went further in the human
direction: in human TD I fetal chondrocytes the mitogenic response to FGF2 and FGF9 was not reduced
at all relative to controls, so the proliferation-arrest phenotype that STAT1 is supposed to mediate
was not reproduced in human cells; the observed human lesion was increased apoptosis with raised BAX
and reduced BCL-2. The disagreement is logged as gap g_l3core_008 and in audit/contradictions.md.
fgfr3_stat1_branch.human_evidence_note: STAT1 nuclear localisation was demonstrated in hypertrophic chondrocytes of human thanatophoric dysplasia fetuses, though the associated proliferation phenotype was not reproduced in human cells.
fgfr3_stat1_branch.translation_risk_reason: The core claim that FGFR3-STAT1 reduces chondrocyte proliferation holds in mouse and rat but was contradicted in human fetal thanatophoric dysplasia chondrocytes.
localization: human TD I hypertrophic chondrocytes: nuclear STAT1 confirmed by immunodetection (legeaimallet1998)
mouse PZ: STAT1-dependent proliferation arrest, functionally confirmed (sahni1999)

key_refs.one_line_finding: STAT-1 is required for FGF-mediated inhibition of chondrocyte proliferation in rat and mouse.
The TD II FGFR3 K650E mutant constitutively activates STAT1.
Human TD I fetal chondrocytes show normal FGF mitogenic response but ligand-independent STAT activation and increased apoptosis.
Stat1 loss restores proliferation in achondroplasia-mutant mice but does not rescue the hypertrophic zone or the dwarfism.

foxa_family_chondrocyte.name: FOXA family in chondrocytes (FOXA2/FOXA3)
foxa_family_chondrocyte.summary: FOXA factors are pioneer transcription factors induced during chondrogenesis that bind conserved sites in the collagen X enhancer and can drive a Col10a1 reporter in both chondrocytes and fibroblasts, i.e. they carry hypertrophy competence into a non-cartilage cell (Ionescu 2012). Mice lacking both FoxA2 and FoxA3 in chondrocytes have defective hypertrophy, reduced alkaline phosphatase and impaired sternebral mineralisation, and become postnatally dwarfed with significantly reduced collagen X and MMP13 in the growth plate; single mutants are unremarkable, so this is another redundant pair (Ionescu 2012, mouse). FOXA2 is separately of interest because a FoxA2-marked resting-zone population has been proposed in L2, which raises the unresolved question of whether the same factor acts at both ends of the differentiation trajectory. There is no human FOXA2/FOXA3 skeletal phenotype and no human growth plate FOXA measurement.
foxa_family_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human FOXA2/FOXA3 skeletal phenotype or growth plate data.
foxa_family_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Mouse compound conditional knockouts and reporter assays only.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: functionally required for the hypertrophic programme (ionescu2012)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: FoxA2/FoxA3 double-mutant chondrocytes fail to hypertrophy and the mice are postnatally dwarfed with reduced Col10a1 and Mmp13.

furin_cnp_processing.name: Furin processing of proCNP
furin_cnp_processing.summary:
NPPC is translated as a 126-residue preproprotein; after signal peptide removal, proCNP is cleaved
by the proprotein convertase furin at a tetrabasic RRRR site to release CNP-53, which can be further
trimmed to CNP-22. Furin cleavage was demonstrated directly by co-expression and by loss of
processing in furin-deficient cells (Wu 2003). Processing determines which CNP species reaches
NPR2 and how much amino-terminal proCNP (NTproCNP) is released; NTproCNP is the clinically used
circulating marker that tracks height velocity in children, so the processing step is the reason a
blood assay can report on growth plate activity at all (Olney 2012). No study has localised furin
activity or measured proCNP-to-CNP conversion efficiency by zone in growth plate cartilage of any
species, and the tissue site of the CNP-53 to CNP-22 conversion in cartilage is unresolved.
furin_cnp_processing.human_evidence_note: The processing product NTproCNP is measurable in human plasma and predicts height velocity, but furin cleavage itself was shown in cell systems, not human cartilage.
furin_cnp_processing.translation_risk_reason: Cleavage chemistry demonstrated in heterologous cells; cartilage-specific processing has never been measured.
localization: human plasma: NTproCNP measurable and correlated with height velocity (olney2012)
growth plate cartilage, any species: furin activity by zone unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Furin cleaves proCNP at the tetrabasic site to generate CNP-53.
Plasma NTproCNP predicts height velocity in healthy children.

gdf5_protein.name: GDF5
gdf5_protein.summary: GDF5 is a BMP-family ligand expressed at prospective joint interzones. Loss of function in mouse (brachypodism, bp) shortens and fuses limb segments and reduces digit number, and the bp locus was identified as Gdf5 by positional cloning (Storm 1994). The human orthologue produces the mirror phenotype: GDF5/CDMP1 mutations cause Grebe- and Hunter-Thompson-type acromesomelic chondrodysplasia with severe limb shortening (Thomas 1996), so this is one of the few BMP-arm nodes with direct human loss-of-function evidence. GDF5 is also a common-variant height locus: the GDF5-UQCC region carries SNPs associated with adult stature in general-population GWAS (Sanna 2008), which places the ligand on the normal-variation axis and not only in dysplasia. Guo 2009 proposes Gdf5/BMP signalling as a downstream, non-cell-autonomous effector of Wnt/beta-catenin control of hypertrophy in mouse, linking this node to the WNT subsystem.
gdf5_protein.human_evidence_note: Biallelic GDF5/CDMP1 mutations cause human acromesomelic chondrodysplasia, and common GDF5-region variants associate with adult height.
gdf5_protein.translation_risk_reason: Concordant loss-of-function phenotypes in mouse and human plus a human common-variant height association.
localization: mouse joint interzone: confirmed (storm1994)
human: inferred from skeletal phenotype of CDMP1 mutations (thomas1996)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mouse brachypodism is caused by mutations in Gdf5, a new TGF-beta superfamily member.
A human chondrodysplasia (Hunter-Thompson type) is caused by a CDMP1/GDF5 mutation.
Common variants at the GDF5-UQCC locus associate with adult human height.
Wnt/beta-catenin controls hypertrophy onset non-cell-autonomously, possibly via Gdf5/BMP.

gli1_tf.name: GLI1
gli1_tf.summary:
GLI1 is a Hedgehog-induced transcriptional activator and, because Gli1 transcription is itself
Hedgehog-dependent, it functions in the growth plate primarily as a pathway activity reporter rather
than an essential effector. Gli1 marks Hedgehog-responsive chondroprogenitors during postnatal mouse
chondrogenesis and Gli1-CreER lineage tracing is the standard tool for identifying Hh-responsive
cells around and within the growth plate (Li 2024). Genetic rescue experiments place the essential
transcriptional output of Ihh in relief of GLI3 repressor rather than in GLI1/GLI2 activator gain:
deleting Gli3 restores most of the Ihh-null cartilage phenotype (Hilton 2005; Koziel 2005). No human
GLI1 growth plate phenotype has been defined.
gli1_tf.human_evidence_note: No human GLI1 variant with a characterised growth plate phenotype.
gli1_tf.translation_risk_reason: Reporter-based mouse lineage data with no human counterpart.
localization: mouse PZ/PHZ and perichondrium: Gli1 reporter activity confirmed (li2024)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Gli1 labels Hedgehog-responsive chondroprogenitors in postnatal mice.
Gli3 removal, not Gli activator gain, rescues the Ihh-null cartilage phenotype.

gli2_tf.name: GLI2
gli2_tf.summary:
GLI2 is the principal Hedgehog-dependent transcriptional activator in the GLI family. In the growth
plate its activator role is largely dispensable relative to GLI3 repressor: the cartilage phenotype
of Ihh-null mice is rescued by removing Gli3 rather than by restoring GLI activator function,
indicating that the dominant Ihh output in chondrocytes is derepression (Hilton 2005; Koziel 2005).
GLI2 and GLI3 act together to mediate Hedgehog-TGF-beta crosstalk in mesenchymal progenitors that
feed the skeletal lineage (Zhou 2026). Human GLI2 loss causes Culler-Jones/holoprosencephaly-spectrum
disease dominated by pituitary and midline defects, so the human phenotype confounds a growth plate
readout with GH deficiency and cannot be used as a clean test of chondrocyte GLI2 function.
gli2_tf.human_evidence_note: Human GLI2 mutations cause pituitary/midline disease with short stature, but the growth defect is confounded by GH deficiency rather than being demonstrably chondrocyte-intrinsic.
gli2_tf.translation_risk_reason: Mouse epistasis only; the human GLI2 phenotype is endocrine-confounded.
localization: mouse PZ/PHZ: inferred from Gli reporter and genetic epistasis (hilton2005)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Gli3 deletion rescues Ihh-null cartilage, placing derepression above activator gain.
Gli3 acts downstream of Ihh at two separable steps of chondrocyte differentiation.
GLI2 and GLI3 synergistically mediate Hedgehog-TGF-beta crosstalk in skeletal mesenchymal progenitors.

gli3_repressor.name: GLI3R
gli3_repressor.summary:
In the absence of Hedgehog signalling, full-length GLI3 is proteolytically processed in the primary
cilium to a truncated repressor, GLI3R, which shuts down Hedgehog target transcription. GLI3R is the
dominant transducer of Ihh in growth plate cartilage: deleting Gli3 in Ihh-null mice restores
chondrocyte proliferation and the normal position of the hypertrophic transition, rescuing most of
the cartilage phenotype, although osteoblast and vascular defects persist and therefore require
additional Ihh effectors (Hilton 2005). Koziel 2005 separates two GLI3R-dependent steps - the onset
of hypertrophy and prehypertrophic maturation - showing that a single repressor gradient reads out at
more than one differentiation checkpoint. The practical consequence is that in this tissue Ihh works
mainly by derepression, so the amplitude of the Ihh signal is encoded as the local GLI3R
concentration; that concentration has never been measured across zones in any species.
gli3_repressor.human_evidence_note: Human GLI3 mutations cause Greig cephalopolysyndactyly and Pallister-Hall syndrome, which are limb-patterning phenotypes rather than characterised growth plate lesions.
