gli3_repressor.translation_risk_reason: Rescue genetics is murine; the human GLI3 phenotype reports limb patterning, not growth plate zonal control.
localization: mouse PZ (high GLI3R away from Ihh source, low near it): inferred from genetics, not directly measured
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Gli3 removal rescues most of the Ihh-null cartilage phenotype but not osteoblast/vascular defects.
Gli3 repressor acts at two distinct steps of chondrocyte differentiation downstream of Ihh.

gsk3b_kinase.name: GSK3B
gsk3b_kinase.summary: GSK3B is the destruction-complex kinase that phosphorylates beta-catenin on the N-terminal degron and targets it for beta-TrCP-mediated degradation; WNT-receptor engagement inhibits this activity and lets beta-catenin accumulate. In chondrocytes, pharmacological GSK3 inhibition with lithium chloride raises beta-catenin and drives terminal differentiation markers together with oxidative DNA damage and matrix remodelling in human OA chondrocytes in vitro (Guidotti 2015), which is a chemical-genetics mirror of the beta-catenin gain-of-function mouse phenotype. GSK3B is not chondrocyte-specific and sits downstream of many inputs, so any perturbation of it is a blunt instrument: it also regulates glycogen metabolism, mTOR-adjacent signalling and microtubule dynamics in the same cell. LiCl is also non-selective in a second, sharper sense: it does not distinguish GSK3B from its paralogue GSK3A at any concentration, and no ATP-competitive GSK3 inhibitor with meaningful GSK3A/B selectivity exists. The genetics say the distinction matters. A chondrocyte-restricted Gsk3b conditional knockout HAS been reported and is phenotypically NORMAL except for elevated GSK3A protein - the paralogue upregulates to compensate - whereas the tamoxifen-inducible cartilage-specific Gsk3a/Gsk3b DOUBLE knockout causes precocious growth plate remodelling with loss of cellular and proteoglycan components, decreased SOX9, increased osteoclast recruitment and apoptosis, shorter long bones and growth retardation (Bali 2021, mouse). Gsk3a-null alone and Gsk3b-heterozygous alone are likewise near-normal while the compound is dwarfed, and the redundant chondrocyte function runs through RelA Thr-254 phosphorylation INDEPENDENTLY of Wnt/beta-catenin (Itoh 2012, mouse). No chondrocyte phenotype is therefore assignable to GSK3B specifically: selective genetic removal of GSK3B does nothing, and non-selective chemical removal of both does something. No human growth plate GSK3B measurement exists (g_para_008).
gsk3b_kinase.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is in vitro pharmacology on cultured human articular chondrocytes, not growth plate tissue.
gsk3b_kinase.translation_risk_reason: Lithium is a promiscuous inhibitor, the cells were articular and diseased, and no in vivo physeal genetics exist.
localization: in_vitro_human_cell (OA chondrocytes): activity manipulated pharmacologically (guidotti2015)
human growth plate: unconfirmed
mouse growth plate zonal distribution: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: LiCl-dependent GSK3 inactivation in human chondrocytes links oxidative DNA damage to matrix remodelling and terminal differentiation.
Establishes that the level of beta-catenin - the GSK3B substrate - is what chondrocytes read.

Tamoxifen-inducible cartilage-specific Gsk3a/Gsk3b DOUBLE knockout causes precocious growth plate remodeling, loss of cellular and proteoglycan components, decreased SOX9, increased osteoclast recruitment and apoptosis, shorter long bones and growth retardation. States that cartilage-specific Gsk3b SINGLE knockout mice are NORMAL except for elevated GSK3A protein - the paralog compensates by upregulating.

GSK-3alpha and GSK-3beta act with functional redundancy in early chondrocyte differentiation via RelA Thr-254 phosphorylation, INDEPENDENTLY of Wnt/beta-catenin. Gsk3a(-/-) alone or Gsk3b(+/-) alone does not significantly affect skeletal development; the compound Gsk3a(-/-);Gsk3b(+/-) causes dwarfism with impaired chondrocyte differentiation.

hdac4_protein.name: HDAC4
hdac4_protein.summary: HDAC4 is a class IIa histone deacetylase with negligible intrinsic deacetylase activity that works as a signal-responsive corepressor. It is expressed in prehypertrophic chondrocytes and restrains hypertrophy by two routes: binding and inhibiting RUNX2 (Vega 2004) and binding and repressing MEF2 (Arnold 2007; Nishimori 2019). Hdac4-null mice show ectopic and premature chondrocyte hypertrophy with premature ossification, phenocopying constitutive RUNX2 expression, while HDAC4 overexpression in proliferating chondrocytes blocks hypertrophy and phenocopies RUNX2 loss (Vega 2004, mouse). Its activity is set by SUBCELLULAR LOCALISATION, not by abundance: phosphorylation at 14-3-3-binding sites holds it in the cytoplasm (inactive), and dephosphorylation lets it enter the nucleus (active as a repressor). PTHrP drives that dephosphorylation via PP2A (Kozhemyakina 2009) and via inhibition of SIK3 (Nishimori 2019, 2021). Human HDAC4 haploinsufficiency in 2q37 deletion syndrome causes brachydactyly type E, present in 48% of 103 reported individuals, plus developmental delay - direct human evidence that HDAC4 dose sets metacarpal/metatarsal growth plate output (Le 2019); a missense HDAC4 variant produces the same syndrome in a family (Takeyari 2023).
hdac4_protein.human_evidence_note: HDAC4 haploinsufficiency in humans (2q37 deletion, and a point mutation in one family) causes brachydactyly type E.
hdac4_protein.translation_risk_reason: Human haploinsufficiency produces a growth-plate-attributable digit phenotype concordant with the mouse premature-hypertrophy null.
localization: mouse PHZ: confirmed - HDAC4 expressed in prehypertrophic chondrocytes (vega2004)
human: inferred from 2q37 deletion phenotype (le2019)
human growth plate protein localisation: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: HDAC4 is expressed in prehypertrophic chondrocytes and inhibits RUNX2; Hdac4-null mice show ectopic premature hypertrophy.
HDAC4 and MEF2C are titrated against each other genetically in endochondral bone formation.
PTHrP/forskolin activates a PP2A-dependent HDAC4 phospho-S246 phosphatase, driving HDAC4 into the nucleus to repress MEF2.
In 103 individuals with 2q37 deletion, brachydactyly type E occurs in 48% and HDAC4 is the primary genetic contributor.
A missense HDAC4 variant causes brachydactyly-mental retardation syndrome in a family, without a deletion.

hedgehog_acyltransferase.name: HHAT
hedgehog_acyltransferase.summary:
HHAT is the membrane-bound O-acyltransferase that attaches palmitate to the N-terminus of Hedgehog
ligands including IHH; palmitoylation is required for full signalling potency and for correct
ligand release and range. Unpalmitoylated Hedgehog is secreted but signals weakly, so HHAT sets the
effective amplitude of the Ihh arm of the growth plate loop. Human biallelic HHAT variants cause
Nivelon-Nivelon-Mabille syndrome, a multiple congenital anomaly syndrome including skeletal dysplasia
and short stature (Ari 2025), and HHAT variants also cause 46,XY differences of sex development,
consistent with a shared requirement for Hedgehog lipidation across tissues. No study has measured
Ihh palmitoylation stoichiometry or HHAT expression by zone in growth plate cartilage of any species.
hedgehog_acyltransferase.human_evidence_note: Biallelic HHAT loss-of-function causes a human syndrome with skeletal dysplasia, but no growth plate tissue analysis has been reported.
hedgehog_acyltransferase.translation_risk_reason: Human genetic evidence exists but the growth plate mechanism is inferred from general Hedgehog lipidation biology, not measured in cartilage.
localization: human: HHAT loss produces skeletal dysplasia, tissue-level growth plate localization unconfirmed
mouse growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Four further patients confirm biallelic HHAT variants cause Nivelon-Nivelon-Mabille syndrome with skeletal dysplasia.
Lipid-modified Ihh acts as a long-range morphogen whose spread is matrix-regulated.

hes1_tf.name: HES1
hes1_tf.summary: HES1 is a basic helix-loop-helix repressor and canonical RBPJ target. In chondrocytes it is the effector through which Notch drives the terminal stage of endochondral ossification: NICD with RBPJ induces Hes1, and Hes1 induction is required for the ossification phenotype (Hosaka 2013, mouse). Genetic dissection of the Notch target repertoire shows HES1 and HES5 suppress chondrogenesis and promote the onset of hypertrophy, with partial overlap between them, whereas HEY1 and HEYL have no discernible role in either process - so the Notch output in cartilage is carried by the HES and not the HEY branch (Rutkowski 2016, mouse). Only HES5, not HES1, directly regulates Sox9 transcription in that analysis, which separates the two paralogues mechanistically. HES1 is heavily used in other tissues as a Notch activity reporter; in the growth plate it is a functional node in its own right. No human growth plate HES1 data exist.
hes1_tf.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate HES1 measurement or human HES1 skeletal phenotype.
hes1_tf.translation_risk_reason: Mouse genetics and mouse chondrogenic cell lines only.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: induced downstream of NICD-RBPJ (hosaka2013)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: NICD/RBPJ stimulates endochondral ossification through induction of Hes1 in chondrocytes.
HES1 and HES5 suppress chondrogenesis and promote hypertrophy onset; HEY1/HEYL do not, and only HES5 directly regulates Sox9.

hif1a_chondrocyte.name: HIF1A in chondrocytes
hif1a_chondrocyte.summary: HIF1A is the oxygen-labile subunit of HIF-1, hydroxylated by PHDs and destroyed by the VHL ubiquitin ligase when oxygen is available. Schipani 2001 provided the first evidence that the mammalian growth plate is developmentally hypoxic and, critically, that the hypoxia is in its INTERIOR rather than at its periphery; chondrocyte-restricted Hif1a deletion in mouse kills cells in that interior, lowers the CDK inhibitor p57 and raises BrdU incorporation, i.e. HIF1A enforces both survival and growth arrest. VEGF expression in the plate is only partly HIF1A-dependent: around dying cells VEGF rises HIF1A-independently and drives ectopic angiogenesis (Schipani 2001, mouse). Deleting the negative regulator Vhlh has the reciprocal effect - stabilised HIF1A, dwarfism, reduced proliferation, increased matrix - and the Vhlh;Hif1a double null resembles the Hif1a single null, placing HIF1A downstream (Pfander 2004, mouse). Human evidence is absent: there is no HIF1A staining series or oxygen measurement from human growth plate reported.
hif1a_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate HIF1A measurement; the human hypoxic-gradient claim is an extrapolation from mouse.
hif1a_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Human growth plates are far thicker than mouse and vascularised differently at the epiphyseal cartilage canal level, so the diffusion geometry that produces the mouse gradient may not scale.
localization: mouse growth plate interior: hypoxic and HIF1A-dependent for survival (schipani2001)
human growth plate: unconfirmed - no published HIF1A zonal staining series

key_refs.one_line_finding: The developing mouse growth plate is hypoxic in its interior; Hif1a-null interior chondrocytes die and lose p57-dependent growth arrest.
Vhlh deletion stabilises HIF1A and causes dwarfism; the Vhlh;Hif1a double null resembles the Hif1a null.
HIF1A-dependent suppression of mitochondrial oxygen consumption lowers intracellular hypoxia and is required for hypoxic chondrocyte survival.

hypoxic_gradient_signaling.name: Hypoxic gradient across the growth plate
hypoxic_gradient_signaling.summary: The standard model holds that oxygen falls from the vascularised epiphyseal and metaphyseal margins toward the avascular centre of the plate, and that this gradient patterns HIF1A activity, glycolytic metabolism and survival. The direct evidence for the gradient itself is thin and old: Brighton and Heppenstall 1971 measured oxygen tension with microelectrodes across zones of the epiphyseal plate, metaphysis and diaphysis in rats and rabbits, in vitro and in vivo. Every subsequent statement about a human growth plate oxygen gradient is inferred from HIF1A-dependent phenotypes, pimonidazole adduct staining or from that rodent measurement. Schipani 2001 established by HIF1A genetics that the mouse plate is hypoxic in its interior rather than its periphery, which is the correct topology but is a genetic inference, not an oxygen measurement. Chondrocytes also actively defend their own oxygenation: they synthesise haemoglobin into membraneless cytoplasmic condensates ('Hedy') under hypoxic control via KLF1 and independently of HIF1/2A, and deleting chondrocyte haemoglobin causes severe hypoxia, glycolytic shift and death in the cartilage centre (Zhang 2023, mouse) - so the tissue oxygen field is partly cell-autonomously buffered and cannot be predicted from diffusion geometry alone.
hypoxic_gradient_signaling.human_evidence_note: No direct measurement of oxygen tension in a human growth plate has been published; the human gradient is assumed.
hypoxic_gradient_signaling.translation_risk_reason: The only direct measurements are from rodent/lagomorph plates a fraction of the thickness of a human adolescent plate, so the diffusion distance - the key determinant - is not comparable.
localization: rat and rabbit epiphyseal plate: oxygen tension measured by microelectrode (brighton1971)
mouse growth plate interior: hypoxic by HIF1A-dependent genetics (schipani2001)
human growth plate: never measured directly

key_refs.one_line_finding: Oxygen tension was measured by microelectrode across epiphyseal plate zones, metaphysis and diaphysis in rats and rabbits.
The mouse growth plate is hypoxic in its interior, shown genetically rather than by oximetry.
Review by the group that defined growth plate hypoxia, stating the gradient claim and enumerating what remains unanswered.
Chondrocytes form haemoglobin condensates under KLF1 control, HIF-independently, and buffer their own oxygen supply.

ift80_protein.name: IFT80
ift80_protein.summary: IFT80 is an IFT-B subunit and the first intraflagellar transport protein linked to human disease: hypomorphic IFT80 mutations cause a subset of Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy, an autosomal recessive chondrodysplasia with a constricted thoracic cage, short ribs, and often polydactyly, retinal degeneration and cystic kidney disease; ift80 knockdown gives cystic kidneys in zebrafish and short or absent cilia in Tetrahymena (Beales 2007). IFT80 is predominantly expressed in growth plate chondrocytes, and silencing it in mouse stromal cells impairs cilium formation and chondrogenic differentiation with lower collagen II and aggrecan; the deficit is caused by simultaneously DOWN-regulated Hedgehog and UP-regulated WNT signalling, and is rescued by GLI2 overexpression (Wang 2013, mouse cells). Inducible Col2a1-CreER deletion of Ift80 shortens limbs when induced embryonically and, when induced postnatally, produces stunted growth with a shortened growth plate but THICKENED articular cartilage - opposite directions in the two cartilages of the same bone (Yuan 2015, mouse). IFT80 is therefore the best-anchored cilium node in this layer, with both human loss-of-function and mouse conditional genetics.
ift80_protein.human_evidence_note: Biallelic hypomorphic IFT80 mutations cause human Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy with short ribs and short limbs.
ift80_protein.translation_risk_reason: Human recessive chondrodysplasia and mouse conditional deletion agree on the direction of the growth defect.
localization: mouse growth plate chondrocytes: predominant expression site (wang2013)
human: inferred from Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (beales2007)

key_refs.one_line_finding: IFT80 mutations underlie a subset of human Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy.
IFT80 silencing impairs ciliogenesis and chondrogenesis by lowering Hedgehog and raising Wnt activity; GLI2 overexpression rescues it.
Inducible chondrocyte Ift80 deletion shortens the growth plate but thickens articular cartilage in postnatal mice.

ift88_protein.name: IFT88
ift88_protein.summary: IFT88 is a core IFT-B complex subunit required to build and maintain the ciliary axoneme; null alleles cause mid-gestation lethality, so limb function was established with a conditional allele. Disrupting cilia in limb MESENCHYME with conditional Ift88 deletion causes extensive polydactyly with loss of anteroposterior digit patterning (aberrant SHH pathway activity) and shortening of the proximodistal axis attributable to disrupted IHH signalling during endochondral bone formation; deleting cilia in limb ECTODERM has no overt patterning effect, localising the requirement to the mesenchymal lineage (Haycraft 2007, mouse). Ift88-mutant limbs also develop ectopic perichondrium-derived chondrocyte-like domains that are not seen in Ihh mutants, so cilium loss is not simply equivalent to Hedgehog loss. Human IFT88 variants have been reported in ciliopathy cohorts but IFT88 is not an established human chondrodysplasia gene, and no human growth plate IFT88 measurement exists.
ift88_protein.human_evidence_note: IFT88 is not an established human skeletal dysplasia gene; no human growth plate data.
ift88_protein.translation_risk_reason: Mouse conditional genetics only; the human ciliopathy anchor is IFT80/EVC, not IFT88.
localization: mouse limb mesenchyme/growth plate: functionally required (haycraft2007)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Conditional Ift88 deletion in limb mesenchyme, but not ectoderm, causes polydactyly and proximodistal shortening via Shh and Ihh disruption.

ihh_bmp_crosstalk.name: IHH-BMP crosstalk
ihh_bmp_crosstalk.summary: BMP and Indian hedgehog signalling in the growth plate are interdependent but not serial. In mouse limb explants, BMP2 beads raise Ihh expression, and Ihh signalling raises Bmp2/Bmp4 expression in the perichondrium, so each arm can amplify the other. The decisive experiment is that BMP2 still increases chondrocyte proliferation when Ihh signalling is blocked (and Ihh still acts when BMP signalling is blocked with Noggin), which places them as parallel proliferative inputs converging on the same columnar chondrocytes rather than as one linear cascade (Minina 2001, mouse). The two arms differ in what they control: Ihh/PTHrP sets the position of the hypertrophy boundary through the negative feedback loop, whereas BMP raises proliferation rate and delays hypertrophy largely independently of PTHrP. Minina 2002 adds the third input, showing FGF opposes BMP on both readouts in the same system. All of this is mouse explant work; there is no human tissue equivalent.
ihh_bmp_crosstalk.human_evidence_note: Crosstalk has never been tested in human tissue; no human explant or organoid experiment addresses it.
ihh_bmp_crosstalk.translation_risk_reason: Bead-implant explant pharmacology in embryonic mouse limbs; dose and diffusion are non-physiological.
localization: mouse PZ/PHZ and perichondrium: confirmed in limb explant culture (minina2001, minina2002)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: BMP and Ihh/PTHrP act as parallel, mutually reinforcing inputs on chondrocyte proliferation and hypertrophy timing.
FGF signalling antagonises BMP on proliferation and hypertrophy in mouse limb explants.
Ihh-null mice show reduced chondrocyte proliferation and failure of osteoblast development, defining the Ihh arm.

ihh_protein.name: Indian hedgehog
ihh_protein.summary:
IHH is secreted by prehypertrophic and early hypertrophic chondrocytes after cholesterol and
palmitate modification; release requires DISP1 and its spread through cartilage matrix is limited by
heparan sulfate proteoglycans (Koziel 2004; Tsiairis 2008). Ihh-null mice show severely reduced
chondrocyte proliferation - the BrdU-positive fraction is approximately half that of wild-type
littermates from as early as 12.5 dpc, alongside a shortened proliferative zone - plus ectopic
hypertrophic chondrocytes and complete failure of endochondral osteoblast development (St-Jacques
1999). That entire characterisation is EMBRYONIC (12.5-18.5 dpc; the null dies at birth), so it
constrains cartilage morphogenesis and says nothing directly about the postnatal growth plate. Ihh has at least three separable outputs in the growth
plate: it raises periarticular Pthlh (Vortkamp 1996; Karp 2000), it drives columnar proliferation
directly through Smo in chondrocytes (Long 2001), and it drives periarticular chondrocyte
differentiation into columnar chondrocytes and promotes hypertrophy independently of PTHrP
(Kobayashi 2005; Mak 2008) - noting that Mak 2008 raises Hh signalling largely with Shh protein and
Ptch1 inactivation rather than with Ihh itself, so the specificity rests on pathway identity, not
ligand identity. Most of the signal is transduced by relief of GLI3 repressor: removing
Gli3 rescues most of the Ihh-null cartilage phenotype (Hilton 2005; Koziel 2005). Human IHH
mutations give a dosage series - heterozygous missense causes brachydactyly type A1 (Gao 2001; Ma
2011), homozygous hypomorphs cause acrocapitofemoral dysplasia (Hellemans 2003), and a homozygous
variant has been reported causing an acromesomelic-Maroteaux-like dysplasia (Hanif 2025).

claim_grades.claim: Reduced IHH gene dosage reduces human stature, with incomplete penetrance.
claim_grades.basis: 16 heterozygous IHH probands including the first complete gene deletion show mild-to-moderate short stature with fifth-finger changes, cosegregating in 13 of 16 families, with 5 carriers of normal height (sentchordimont2020); IHH is the commonest finding on growth-plate gene panels in idiopathic short stature at 4/102 (andrade2022).

claim_grades.claim: IHH drives chondrocyte proliferation and raises periarticular PTHrP in the postnatal growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Established in mouse EMBRYO only (12.5-18.5 dpc; the Ihh null dies at birth) by stjacques1999, vortkamp1996 and kobayashi2005. No postnatal or human equivalent. This is the claim that sets the node grade.

claim_grades.claim: Most IHH signal is transduced by relief of GLI3 repressor.
claim_grades.basis: Mouse genetic rescue of the Ihh-null cartilage phenotype by Gli3 removal (hilton2005, koziel2005); replicated in mouse, no human data.

ihh_protein.human_evidence_note: A three-tier human IHH allelic series (BDA1, acrocapitofemoral dysplasia, acromesomelic dysplasia) establishes dosage-dependence, but no human growth plate ISH/IHC series has been mapped by zone.
ihh_protein.translation_risk_reason: Mechanistic dissection is entirely murine/avian; human data are genetic only.
localization: mouse PHZ and early HZ: confirmed by ISH (vortkamp1996, stjacques1999)
human fetal mandibular condyle: IHH protein confirmed by IHC (ohba2020 index)
human long-bone growth plate: zonal IHH protein map unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Ihh-null embryos have a BrdU-positive fraction ~half of wild type from 12.5 dpc with a shortened proliferative zone, ectopic hypertrophy and no endochondral osteoblasts; all data are embryonic (12.5-18.5 dpc).
Ihh raises periarticular PTHrP and blocks hypertrophy.
Ihh drives periarticular-to-columnar chondrocyte differentiation and sets column length independently of PTHrP; PTHrP heterozygosity had minimal effect on Ihh-driven column elongation.
Gli3 removal rescues most of the Ihh-null cartilage phenotype.
Heterozygous IHH missense mutations cause human brachydactyly type A1.
Homozygous IHH mutations cause human acrocapitofemoral dysplasia.
Heparan sulfate limits Ihh range; Ihh acts as a long-range morphogen.
16 probands with heterozygous IHH variants show mild-to-moderate short stature and fifth-finger middle-phalanx shortening; none had classical brachydactyly A-1 and five were of normal height.

kif3a_protein.name: KIF3A
kif3a_protein.summary: KIF3A is a subunit of heterotrimeric kinesin-II, the anterograde IFT motor; without it, cilia are not built. Cartilage-restricted Kif3a deletion in mouse produces cranial base growth retardation and progressive synchondrosis failure: by postnatal day 7 the mutant growth plate has lost identifiable proliferative and hypertrophic zones and is instead composed of cells with strong Col2a1 but barely detectable Ihh, Col10a1, Vegfa, Mmp13 and Sp7 (Koyama 2007). The informative part is the topology of the signalling defect: hedgehog readouts (Ptch1, Gli1, syndecan-3) are LOW inside the mutant plate but HIGHER and spatially spread throughout the adjacent perichondrium, and this is accompanied by excessive intramembranous ossification along the perichondrial border and ectopic cartilage masses - a combination that cartilage Ihh deletion does not reproduce. The cilium therefore restricts where Hedgehog acts, not only whether it acts. There is no human KIF3A skeletal dysplasia.
kif3a_protein.human_evidence_note: No human KIF3A skeletal phenotype; human KIF3A associations are with atopic disease.
kif3a_protein.translation_risk_reason: Mouse conditional genetics only, and the reported site is the cranial base synchondrosis rather than a long-bone physis.
localization: mouse growth plate and synchondrosis: functionally required (koyama2007)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Cartilage Kif3a deletion abolishes growth plate zonation and inverts the spatial distribution of hedgehog signalling between cartilage and perichondrium.
Independent IFT mutant confirming that cilium loss disrupts Ihh-dependent endochondral growth.

klotho_beta_cofactor.name: Beta-Klotho
klotho_beta_cofactor.summary: Beta-Klotho (KLB) is the single-pass transmembrane co-receptor that converts FGFR1 and FGFR3 from heparin-dependent paracrine receptors into receptors for the endocrine ligand FGF21; without KLB, FGF21 does not signal. It entered this atlas as the one demonstrated molecular entry point by which systemic caloric state reaches the growth plate outside the GH/IGF-1 axis. THAT DEMONSTRATION HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN (CORR-004). What stands is wu2012, which carries no retraction or correction notice: Fgf21, Fgfr1, Fgfr3 and Klb transcripts are detectable in fetal and 3-week-old MOUSE growth plate chondrocytes, and recombinant human FGF21 at 5-10 ug/ml suppressed thymidine incorporation and Col10a1 mRNA, abolished the GH-stimulated increase in both, and reduced 125I-GH binding; siRNA against FGFR1 or ERK1 prevented each of these effects in culture. What has fallen away is the in vivo circuit. Wu 2013 reported that four weeks of food restriction raised LEPROT and LEPROTL1 mRNA in liver and tibial growth plate, that Fgf21-knockout mice did not show the induction, and that rhFGF21 add-back restored it - the knockout-plus-rescue design that made this pathway causal rather than correlative. That paper was WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHORS in 2020 (notice PMID 32917830) on data-integrity grounds: duplicated lanes in the Fig 1C actin immunoblot, duplicated lanes in BOTH the LEPROT and LEPROTL1 immunoblots of Fig 2C, and a splice in the LEPROTL1 blot. Those blots ARE the LEPROT/LEPROTL1 measurement, so the observation does not survive independently of the interpretation and the disposition both_invalid is evidenced, not defaulted. The authors affirmed that the conclusions reflect work actually done in their laboratory; that affirmation is recorded and is not treated as restoring the data. Three limits are now load-bearing. The concentrations that inhibited chondrocytes (5-10 ug/ml) are far above physiological circulating FGF21. KLB has never been localised in human growth plate cartilage by any method. And there is no longer any in vivo evidence, in any species, that FGF21 mediates undernutrition-induced growth-plate GH insensitivity.

claim_grades.claim: Beta-Klotho is expressed in growth plate chondrocytes and permits FGF21 signalling there.
claim_grades.basis: Mouse mRNA detection at two ages plus siRNA epistasis in culture, from a single laboratory, in ONE paper. It was graded C on the strength of being replicated across wu2012 and wu2013; wu2013 is withdrawn, so the replication is gone and the grade falls one step to D. CORR-004.

claim_grades.claim: FGF21 acting through beta-Klotho/FGFR1 mediates growth-plate GH insensitivity during undernutrition.
claim_grades.basis: WITHDRAWN. This claim rested entirely on wu2013 (Fgf21-null loss of induction with rhFGF21 add-back rescue), withdrawn by J Biol Chem in 2020 with no retrievable reason. There is now no in vivo evidence in any species. Graded X - repeated in the literature but not traceable to standing primary data - and logged in audit/corrections.md as CORR-004 rather than deleted, because the claim continues to circulate.

claim_grades.claim: This pathway operates in the human growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Inference from mouse only; no human localization or functional data exist.

klotho_beta_cofactor.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate expression or functional data for beta-Klotho or FGF21 were retrieved; all data are murine or murine primary culture.
klotho_beta_cofactor.translation_risk_reason: The entire mechanism rests on two papers from one laboratory in mouse, at FGF21 concentrations well above physiological, and humans differ from mice in the FGF21 response to undernutrition. Restating this as a human pathway would be exactly the laundering this atlas exists to prevent.
localization: mouse growth plate chondrocyte: Klb, Fgfr1 and Fgfr3 mRNA confirmed at fetal and 3 weeks (wu2012)
human growth plate: not examined - no protein, mRNA or in situ localization retrieved (gap g_l0l9_001)

key_refs.one_line_finding: beta-Klotho, FGFR1 and FGFR3 are expressed in mouse growth plate chondrocytes; FGF21 blocks GH-stimulated proliferation and Col10a1 and reduces GH binding, via FGFR1-ERK1.

WITHDRAWN 2020 (J Biol Chem 295:13137). Formerly: FGF21 is required for the undernutrition-induced rise in LEPROT/LEPROTL1 in the mouse tibial growth plate. Kept in the reference list, flagged, so the withdrawal is visible to anyone who follows the citation rather than silently absent.

latent_tgfb_matrix_store.name: Latent TGF-beta matrix store (LAP/LTBP complex)
latent_tgfb_matrix_store.summary: TGF-beta is secreted as a small latent complex (mature dimer non-covalently held by its latency-associated peptide) covalently linked to a latent TGF-beta binding protein (LTBP1/3/4), which anchors it to fibrillin-containing microfibrils in the extracellular matrix. Cartilage matrix therefore holds a reservoir of pre-made ligand whose bioavailability is set by proteolytic, integrin-mediated and mechanical release rather than by transcription. Two human genetic experiments bracket the store: TGFB1 mutations in the LAP domain destabilise latency and cause Camurati-Engelmann disease with excess signalling (Kinoshita 2000), while biallelic LTBP3 loss of function causes brachyolmia with short stature and reduced growth (Huckert 2015). This makes the latent store one of the few L3 nodes with human bidirectional dose evidence. What has never been measured in any species is the absolute concentration of latent TGF-beta per unit volume of growth plate matrix, or how much of it is released per loading cycle.
latent_tgfb_matrix_store.human_evidence_note: Human LTBP3 and TGFB1 variant phenotypes imply a functional matrix latent store, but no direct measurement in human physeal matrix exists.
latent_tgfb_matrix_store.translation_risk_reason: Inference from germline human variants; the biochemistry itself is largely from non-skeletal tissue.
localization: human bone/cartilage matrix: inferred from LTBP3 and TGFB1 human phenotypes
growth plate zonal distribution of latent complex: unmeasured in any species

key_refs.one_line_finding: TGFB1 LAP-domain mutations cause Camurati-Engelmann disease, implying release of latent TGF-beta drives the phenotype.
Biallelic LTBP3 mutations cause human brachyolmia with short stature.

lrp5_coreceptor.name: LRP5
lrp5_coreceptor.summary: LRP5 is a single-pass WNT co-receptor that, with Frizzled, is required for canonical signal transduction. Human genetics supplies a rare two-sided dose experiment on one gene: biallelic loss-of-function causes osteoporosis-pseudoglioma syndrome with very low bone mass and fractures (Gong 2001), while the heterozygous G171V missense allele, which impairs binding of the antagonist DKK1, causes autosomal dominant high bone mass (Boyden 2002). Both phenotypes are dominated by bone mass rather than by stature, which is the important negative for this atlas: the human LRP5 read-out is osteoblastic, not clearly physeal. In mouse, Lrp5 and Lrp6 act redundantly in the embryo, and only the compound mutants reveal the full skeletal requirement (Joeng 2011). Whether LRP5 signalling in the growth plate chondrocyte itself contributes to human height has not been tested.
lrp5_coreceptor.human_evidence_note: Two independent human germline allele classes (null and DKK1-resistant missense) give opposite bone-mass phenotypes.
lrp5_coreceptor.translation_risk_reason: Human loss- and gain-of-function alleles are both characterised; the caveat is that the read-out is bone mass, not longitudinal growth.
localization: human bone: inferred from OPPG and HBM phenotypes (gong2001, boyden2002)
human growth plate chondrocyte: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: LRP5 loss of function causes human osteoporosis-pseudoglioma syndrome.
The LRP5 G171V allele causes autosomal dominant human high bone mass.
Lrp5 and Lrp6 act redundantly to control mouse embryonic skeletal development.

lrp6_coreceptor.name: LRP6
lrp6_coreceptor.summary: LRP6 is the paralogue of LRP5 and the dominant WNT co-receptor during mouse embryogenesis. Joeng 2011 shows that Lrp5 and Lrp6 are redundant in the embryonic skeleton: Lrp6 loss produces a markedly more severe skeletal phenotype than Lrp5 loss, and reducing Lrp5 dose on an Lrp6 mutant background worsens it further, so the two receptors provide a summed rather than a divided input. This gene-dose structure is the reason single-receptor knockouts underestimate the requirement for canonical WNT in cartilage and bone. Human LRP6 variants have been associated with low bone mass and with coronary disease, but there is no LRP6 skeletal dysplasia with a defined growth plate phenotype and no human physeal measurement.
lrp6_coreceptor.human_evidence_note: No human LRP6 growth plate phenotype; associations are with bone mass and cardiovascular traits.
lrp6_coreceptor.translation_risk_reason: Mouse embryonic genetics only; human LRP6 skeletal data are association-level.
localization: mouse embryonic skeleton: functionally required (joeng2011)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Lrp5 and Lrp6 redundantly control mouse embryonic skeletal development, with Lrp6 the more important of the two.

mef2c_tf.name: MEF2C
mef2c_tf.summary: MEF2C is the MADS-box transcription factor that activates the hypertrophy gene programme. Deleting Mef2c in endochondral cartilage, or expressing a dominant-negative MEF2C, impairs hypertrophy, cartilage angiogenesis, ossification and longitudinal bone growth in mouse; a superactivating MEF2C causes precocious hypertrophy, ossification of the growth plates and dwarfism (Arnold 2007). Both directions therefore shorten the bone, by opposite mechanisms - failure to hypertrophy and premature exhaustion of the plate - which is why MEF2C output must be described as a set point rather than as a 'growth-promoting' factor. The set point is enforced by HDAC4: the Mef2c-mutant bone deficiency is rescued by an Hdac4 mutation, and the ectopic ossification of Hdac4-null mice is reduced by Mef2c heterozygosity, i.e. the two are titrated against each other in vivo (Arnold 2007, mouse). MEF2C also acts with residual SOX9 protein to activate Col10a1 directly in upper hypertrophic chondrocytes (Dy 2012, mouse). Human MEF2C haploinsufficiency (5q14.3 deletion) is a neurodevelopmental syndrome without a defined physeal phenotype.
mef2c_tf.human_evidence_note: Human MEF2C haploinsufficiency presents as a neurodevelopmental disorder; no growth plate read-out is reported.
mef2c_tf.translation_risk_reason: Mouse conditional and transgenic alleles; the human haploinsufficiency phenotype does not include a described physeal defect.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: functionally required for hypertrophy (arnold2007)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: MEF2C is required for chondrocyte hypertrophy; superactive MEF2C causes precocious ossification and dwarfism, and MEF2C is titrated against HDAC4 in vivo.
MEF2C acts with residual SOX9 protein to directly activate Col10a1 in upper hypertrophic chondrocytes.

mek1_erk_chondrocyte.name: MEK1/ERK in chondrocytes
mek1_erk_chondrocyte.summary:
MEK1 and ERK1/2 form the terminal kinase module of the FGFR3 anti-hypertrophic branch in growth plate
chondrocytes. A constitutively active MEK1 transgene driven in chondrocytes is sufficient to
reproduce achondroplasia-like dwarfism in mice: hypertrophy is incomplete, type X collagen staining
is reduced, Sox9 persists in cells that should have exited, endochondral ossification is delayed, and
chondrocyte proliferation is unchanged (Murakami 2004). The same transgene abolishes the skeletal
overgrowth of Fgfr3-null mice, establishing epistasis. In the opposite direction, cGMP-dependent
signalling suppresses this module: CNP and 8-Br-cGMP inhibit FGF-stimulated ERK phosphorylation
dose-dependently at the level of RAF-1 in ATDC5 chondrogenic cells (Ozasa 2005), which is the
mechanistic basis for CNP analogues being used to treat achondroplasia. Because MEK1-ERK is the
convergence point of FGF, BMP and other RTK inputs on hypertrophy, its activity state is arguably the
single most informative missing measurement in human growth plate tissue.
mek1_erk_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No study reports phospho-ERK distribution across zones in human growth plate.
mek1_erk_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Sufficiency shown only by mouse transgenesis; no human tissue measurement of pathway activity exists.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: functionally confirmed by transgenic activation (murakami2004)
human growth plate: phospho-ERK zonal map unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Constitutively active MEK1 in chondrocytes is sufficient for achondroplasia-like dwarfism and epistatic to Fgfr3 loss.
CNP and 8-Br-cGMP inhibit FGF-induced ERK phosphorylation at RAF-1 in ATDC5 cells.

mtorc1_chondrocyte.name: mTORC1 signalling in chondrocytes
mtorc1_chondrocyte.summary: mTORC1 (mTOR-RAPTOR-mLST8) integrates amino acid, growth factor and energy availability and sets biosynthetic capacity through S6K1 and 4E-BP1. In mouse limb cartilage mTORC1 signalling is active during development, and Prx1-Cre deletion of either mTor or Raptor sharply reduces embryonic skeletal growth with delayed hypertrophy and bone formation. The mechanism is specifically translational: proliferation and survival are NOT changed, but chondrocyte cell size and cartilage matrix amount fall, and metabolic labelling shows a reduced protein synthesis rate in Raptor-deficient chondrocytes (Chen and Long 2014). This makes mTORC1 the node that converts nutrient supply into the cell-size component of longitudinal growth, distinct from the proliferation component set by IHH/PTHrP and FGFR3. mTORC1 also promotes limb bud cell growth and chondrogenesis at an earlier stage (Jiang 2017, mouse), and rapamycin blunts chondrocyte differentiation in vitro (Phornphutkul 2008). Zonally, mouse data show mTORC1 activity is LOW in resting and proliferating chondrocytes and that forcing it on there (chondrocyte Tsc1 deletion) expands the resting zone and gives its cells prehypertrophic character, reversibly with rapamycin (Hsieh 2021). No study has measured phospho-S6 or phospho-4E-BP1 zonally in HUMAN growth plate tissue, so the assumption that human hypertrophic chondrocytes are the high-mTORC1 compartment is untested.
mtorc1_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate mTORC1 activity measurement; the closest human data are systemic - growth retardation in children on mTOR inhibitors - which is not zone-resolved.
mtorc1_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Mouse conditional genetics plus rodent cell lines; no human tissue read-out at any zone.
localization: mouse RZ/PZ: mTORC1 activity low in wild type (hsieh2021)
mouse limb cartilage: mTORC1 activity confirmed during development (chen2014)
human growth plate, zonal phospho-S6/phospho-4E-BP1: unmeasured

key_refs.one_line_finding: mTOR or Raptor deletion in mouse limb cartilage reduces chondrocyte size and matrix via lower protein synthesis, not lower proliferation.
mTORC1 activity is normally suppressed in resting and proliferating zone chondrocytes; de-repressing it expands the resting zone.
mTORC1 signalling promotes limb bud cell growth and chondrogenesis in mouse.
mTOR signalling contributes to chondrocyte differentiation in vitro.
Synthesis of mTOR signalling in skeletal development, used here as an index to primaries.

aliases: mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, growth plate

noggin_antagonist.name: Noggin (NOG)
noggin_antagonist.summary: Noggin is a secreted BMP-binding antagonist. Mouse Nog-null embryos show grossly enlarged, fused cartilage elements with failure of joint formation, i.e. unopposed BMP signalling expands the chondrogenic field (Brunet 1998). Human heterozygous NOG loss-of-function causes proximal symphalangism and multiple synostoses syndrome - joint fusion rather than dwarfism - which is the clearest human demonstration that BMP dose, not BMP presence, is what the skeleton reads (Gong 1999). Noggin and Chordin are partially redundant: single nulls have distinct territories but the double mutant loses structures neither single mutant loses (Stottmann 2001, mouse). Noggin is widely used experimentally as the BMP-off reagent in growth plate explants, so a large fraction of 'BMP is required for X' claims in this subsystem are Noggin-inference rather than receptor genetics.
noggin_antagonist.human_evidence_note: Heterozygous NOG mutations cause human proximal symphalangism/multiple synostoses, a joint-fusion phenotype.
noggin_antagonist.translation_risk_reason: Human germline loss-of-function phenotype is concordant in direction with the mouse null.
localization: mouse joint interzone and perichondrium: confirmed (brunet1998)
human: inferred from NOG haploinsufficiency phenotype (gong1999)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Noggin-null mice have enlarged cartilage elements and fail to form joints.
Heterozygous NOG mutations cause human proximal symphalangism and multiple synostoses syndrome.
Chordin and Noggin have essential but partly redundant roles in mouse skeletal morphogenesis.

notch_signaling_chondrocyte.name: Notch signalling in chondrocytes
notch_signaling_chondrocyte.summary: Ligand binding releases the Notch intracellular domain (NICD) by gamma-secretase cleavage; NICD enters the nucleus and converts RBPJ from repressor to activator. In cartilage the pathway is required at two separable steps and its sign depends on which step is examined. Forced NICD expression in the mouse chondrocyte lineage reduces cartilage precursor proliferation and blocks hypertrophic differentiation, while chondrocyte-lineage Rbpj deletion increases proliferation and increases hypertrophic chondrocyte number (Mead 2009) - so Notch restrains both proliferation and, in the gain-of-function direction, hypertrophy. Kohn 2015 resolves the mechanism genetically: Notch controls the ONSET of maturation through SOX9 (the Rbpj-mutant phenotype is rescued by removing one Sox9 allele), whereas Notch control of TERMINAL maturation is SOX9-independent. Hosaka 2013 shows the terminal arm operates through HES1 and demonstrates NICD1/2 nuclear translocation in human osteoarthritic articular chondrocytes, the only human chondrocyte data in this subsystem. Notch activity has never been mapped by zone in a human growth plate.
notch_signaling_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: NICD nuclear translocation has been shown in human OA articular chondrocytes, and NOTCH2 gain-of-function causes human Hajdu-Cheney syndrome; neither is a growth plate measurement.
notch_signaling_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Mechanistic genetics are mouse; the human observations are in diseased articular, not physeal, cartilage.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: RBPJ-dependent activity required for onset and terminal maturation (mead2009, kohn2015)
human articular chondrocyte (OA): NICD1/NICD2 nuclear translocation confirmed (hosaka2013)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chondrocyte NICD gain of function blocks hypertrophy; Rbpj deletion increases proliferation and hypertrophic chondrocyte number.
Notch controls onset of chondrocyte maturation SOX9-dependently and terminal maturation SOX9-independently.
RBPJ-dependent Notch drives terminal endochondral ossification via HES1; NICD1/2 translocate in human OA chondrocytes.
Truncating NOTCH2 mutations that stabilise NICD cause human Hajdu-Cheney syndrome with acro-osteolysis and bone loss.

npr2_receptor.name: NPR2
npr2_receptor.summary:
NPR2 is a homodimeric transmembrane receptor guanylyl cyclase: CNP binding to the extracellular
domain activates the intracellular cyclase domain to make cGMP from GTP, and activity requires
phosphorylation of seven juxtamembrane serines and threonines plus ATP binding to the pseudokinase
domain. Cartilage-specific Npr2 deletion in mouse reproduces the systemic-knockout dwarfism and,
like CNP loss, partitions strongly onto the hypertrophic zone - type X collagen-positive layer
thickness falls to 23.0% of control while the non-hypertrophic layer falls only to 71.1%, with
femur at 45.3% and tibia at 54.6% of control length at 10 weeks (Nakao 2015). Human NPR2 is a
graded three-state dosage locus: biallelic loss causes acromesomelic dysplasia Maroteaux type with
adult heights around 120-134 cm; heterozygous loss causes proportionate to mildly disproportionate
short stature of roughly 1.4-1.7 SDS below non-carrier relatives that worsens with age; and
gain-of-function alleles in the kinase homology or submembrane regions cause tall stature with
macrodactyly (Bartels 2004; Olney 2006; Hanley 2020; Hannema 2013; Miura 2014; Lauffer 2020). The
receptor is inactivated post-translationally by FGF-driven dephosphorylation, which is the principal
molecular link between FGFR3 and this pathway (see fgfr3_npr2_crosstalk). What sets the zonal
partition of the CNP effect is NOT established. Npr2 mRNA is reported at similar levels across the
resting/proliferative (combined), hypertrophic and mineralized compartments of micro-dissected mouse
tibia - that study contains no resting-versus-proliferative comparison (Agoston 2007) - while the
prehypertrophic-restricted GC-B protein map attributed to the Kyoto group is a claim Nakao 2015
CITES to its own earlier work rather than data in that paper, whose GC-B immunohistochemistry serves
only to confirm knock-down (g_l2d_002). The downstream explanation previously carried here, that
PKG-I/II enrichment in hypertrophic cells accounts for the partition, does not survive the primary
data and has been retracted (see pkg2_kinase and CORR-003). A live alternative from the same
microarray is zone-specific ligand clearance: CNP induces Npr3 16-fold in the hypertrophic zone and
nowhere else (Agoston 2007). Note also that the zonal partition itself is graded rather than
exclusive - BrdU incorporation is significantly reduced in the cartilage-specific Npr2 knockout, not
merely trending down as in the Nppc knockout (Nakao 2015).
npr2_receptor.human_evidence_note: A complete human three-state dosage series (biallelic loss, heterozygous loss, gain of function) with measured heights in cm and SDS, plus in vitro cGMP assays on the patient alleles.
npr2_receptor.translation_risk_reason: The human allelic series is measured directly in humans and its direction and rank order match the mouse knockouts; residual risk is confined to zonal mechanism, which is murine.
localization: mouse PHZ: prehypertrophic GC-B protein is asserted by the Kyoto group but is NOT data in nakao2015 - that paper cites it to earlier work and uses GC-B IHC only to confirm knock-down. True primary unidentified (g_l2d_002)

mouse resting/proliferative (combined) vs hypertrophic vs mineralized: Npr2 transcript similar across these three compartments by zonal microarray (agoston2007). This study makes NO resting-versus-proliferative comparison; the atlas previously mis-stated its compartments as RZ/PZ/HZ
human growth plate: NPR2 zonal protein map unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Loss-of-function NPR2 mutations cause acromesomelic dysplasia Maroteaux type; obligate carriers are shorter than matched controls.
Heterozygous NPR2 carriers have height z -1.8 +/- 1.1 versus -0.4 +/- 0.8 in non-carrier relatives.
Heterozygous NPR2 short stature is progressive, z falling with age.
Dominant-negative heterozygous NPR2 mutations in 6% of an ISS cohort, height SDS -4.5 to -1.7.
NPR2 haploinsufficiency prevalence 0-1/26 in ISS; a gain-of-function allele found in tall individuals.
NPR2 p.Arg655Cys in the kinase homology domain raises cGMP output and causes extreme tall stature.
NPR2 p.Met482_Leu483del raises basal and stimulated cGMP; family heights +2.77, +1.96, +1.30 SDS.
Final heights 130.5 cm and 134 cm in two AMDM siblings after 8.5 y high-dose GH.
Cartilage-specific Npr2 deletion drops hypertrophic layer thickness to 23.0% of control.

Npr2/Nppc/Npr3 mRNA similar across resting-proliferative (combined), hypertrophic and mineralized compartments; Prkg1 5.9-fold and Prkg2 4.4-fold hypertrophic-enriched (mRNA only); CNP induces Npr3 16-fold in the hypertrophic zone alone.

Corin- and Nppa(ANP)-null mice have impaired chondrocyte differentiation and SHORTENED limb long bones with reduced adult bone density; ANP acts IN CHONDROCYTES via cGMP-dependent protein kinase G to inhibit MAPK phosphorylation and raise phospho-GSK-3beta and beta-catenin - a genetic requirement for the NPR1/GC-A ligand arm in the same cGMP-PKG readout the atlas attributes wholly to CNP/NPR2.

npr3_clearance_receptor.name: NPR3 clearance receptor
npr3_clearance_receptor.summary:
NPR3 binds all three natriuretic peptides without a guanylyl cyclase domain and removes them by
receptor-mediated internalisation and degradation, so it sets the local CNP concentration seen by
NPR2. NPR3 is a CNP-inducible gene in mouse growth plate, forming a negative feedback that limits
CNP signalling (Agoston 2007). Human biallelic NPR3 loss-of-function causes tall stature with
scoliosis and skeletal overgrowth, the phenotype predicted if CNP clearance is removed (Moffatt
2025; Lauffer 2022). NPR3 is therefore the pharmacological rationale for osteocrin/musclin-type
decoy strategies that raise local CNP by occupying the clearance receptor. What is not established
is the zonal distribution of NPR3 protein in human growth plate, or the fraction of CNP turnover
attributable to NPR3 versus neutral endopeptidase in cartilage.
npr3_clearance_receptor.human_evidence_note: Biallelic human NPR3 loss-of-function variants cause tall stature and scoliosis in more than one family.
npr3_clearance_receptor.translation_risk_reason: The human loss-of-function phenotype is the direction predicted from mouse clearance biology and has been replicated across independent families.
localization: mouse growth plate, CNP-inducible: confirmed by zonal microarray (agoston2007)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Homozygous loss-of-function NPR3 missense variant causes tall stature and scoliosis.
Additional biallelic NPR3 loss-of-function variants cause extreme tall stature.
CNP induces NPR3 in mouse growth plate, forming a negative feedback loop.

patched1.name: PTCH1
patched1.summary:
PTCH1 is the 12-pass receptor for IHH in growth plate chondrocytes and, in the unliganded state, the
inhibitor of SMO. Ptch1 is itself a direct Hedgehog target gene, so its transcript is the standard
readout of pathway activity in the growth plate and its expression domain maps the reach of Ihh from
the prehypertrophic source (Vortkamp 1996; Koziel 2004). Ihh binding to PTCH1 relieves SMO
inhibition, permitting GLI2 activator formation and blocking GLI3 processing to GLI3R (Hilton 2005;
Koziel 2005). Pharmacological Hedgehog pathway stimulation downstream of PTCH1 increases linear bone
growth in mice by acting on growth plate skeletal stem cells (Trompet 2024). Human PTCH1 germline
loss causes Gorlin syndrome, whose skeletal features are patterning anomalies rather than a defined
growth plate lesion, so PTCH1 has no clean human growth plate dosage phenotype comparable to IHH or
PTH1R.
patched1.human_evidence_note: Human PTCH1 mutations (Gorlin syndrome) produce skeletal anomalies but no characterised growth plate histology; growth plate role rests on mouse data.
patched1.translation_risk_reason: Entirely murine/avian growth plate evidence; the human PTCH1 phenotype does not read out growth plate function.
localization: mouse PZ/PHZ: Ptch1 transcript domain defines Ihh reach, confirmed by ISH (koziel2004)
human fetal mandibular condyle: PTCH1 protein detected by IHC (ohba2020 index)
human long-bone growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Ptch expression domain marks the Ihh-responsive field in chick and mouse cartilage.
Ptch1 domain expands when heparan sulfate synthesis is reduced, tracking Ihh range.
Downstream of PTCH1/SMO, GLI3R is the principal Ihh effector in cartilage.
Hedgehog pathway stimulation of growth plate stem cells increases linear bone growth in mice.

pathway_convergence_node.name: Pathway convergence in the growth plate signalling network
pathway_convergence_node.summary: Most L3 pathways are drawn as parallel cascades, but the genetics show they collapse onto a small number of shared targets, and it is the ratio at those targets - not the activity of any one pathway - that determines chondrocyte behaviour. Four convergence points are supported by primary data, each receiving three or more distinct upstream inputs. (1) SOX9 receives inputs from Notch (RBPJ-dependent suppression, genetically demonstrated by rescue of the Rbpj-mutant phenotype with Sox9 heterozygosity; Kohn 2015), from WNT (mutual antagonism with beta-catenin; Akiyama 2004, Topol 2009), from the cilium via Hedgehog (IFT80 loss lowers Hh and raises Wnt and thereby blocks chondrogenesis; Wang 2013), and from metabolism (SOX9 drives GLS1 and the resulting acetyl-CoA sustains its own regulon; Stegen 2020). (2) RUNX2 is the hypertrophy licence and is restrained by HDAC4 (Vega 2004), by ZFP521 downstream of PTHrP (Correa 2010) and by SOX9 (Dy 2012), while it is promoted by beta-catenin-dependent maturation (Dao 2012) and by MEF2C (Nishimori 2019); RUNX2 in turn transcribes Ihh directly (Yoshida 2004), feeding back into the loop that regulates it. (3) beta-catenin integrates canonical WNT, SOX9 antagonism, PTHrP (which it inhibits to initiate hypertrophy; Guo 2009) and cilium-dependent Hedgehog tone (Wang 2013). (4) HDAC4 nuclear localisation is the physical convergence of PTHrP-PKA-SIK3 phosphorylation control (Nishimori 2021), PP2A-dependent dephosphorylation (Kozhemyakina 2009) and MEF2C/RUNX2 availability (Arnold 2007) - one protein's address in the cell encodes the output of an entire endocrine loop. The practical consequence is that single-pathway therapeutic reasoning in the growth plate is unreliable: CNP/FGFR3 modulation, Hedgehog agonism and WNT modulation all terminate on these same four nodes.
pathway_convergence_node.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate study has measured multiple convergence-point activities in the same tissue; the convergence structure is assembled from separate mouse experiments.
pathway_convergence_node.translation_risk_reason: This node is a synthesis across mouse experiments performed in different genetic backgrounds, ages and skeletal sites; convergence demonstrated pairwise is not the same as convergence demonstrated jointly.
localization: mouse PZ/PHZ/HZ: all four convergence points demonstrated in mouse growth plate or chondrocytes
human growth plate: unconfirmed - no human tissue study has measured two or more of these nodes simultaneously

key_refs.one_line_finding: Genetic epistasis places SOX9 downstream of RBPJ-dependent Notch for the onset of chondrocyte maturation.
SOX9 and beta-catenin are reciprocal antagonists whose ratio determines the chondrocyte phenotype.
Loss of the ciliary protein IFT80 simultaneously lowers Hedgehog and raises Wnt output in chondrogenic cells.
SOX9 restrains both Runx2 expression and beta-catenin signalling in growth plate chondrocytes.
PTHrP-PKA-SIK3-HDAC4 phosphorylation converts an endocrine signal into the nuclear/cytoplasmic address of a single corepressor.
RUNX2 binds the Ihh promoter directly, closing a feedback loop from the hypertrophy licence back onto the IHH/PTHrP circuit.
SOX9 sets its own nutrient flux through GLS1, making metabolism part of the convergence rather than a downstream consequence.

pde1c.name: PDE1C
pde1c.summary:
PDE1C is a Ca2+/calmodulin-stimulated dual-specificity phosphodiesterase that hydrolyses cAMP and
cGMP with similar Km values, and is of theoretical interest in the growth plate because CNP/NPR2
signalling drives TRPM7-mediated Ca2+ entry into chondrocytes (Miyazaki 2022), which would allow
Ca2+ to feed back onto cyclic nucleotide degradation. No primary study reports PDE1C expression,
localisation or function in growth plate cartilage in any species. Among PDE1 family members it is
PDE1B, not PDE1C, that is reported in growth plate chondrocyte transcriptomes across human, mouse
and chicken, and PDE1 genes have never been functionally connected to the skeleton (Ursachi 2026).
The Ca2+-to-PDE1 feedback arm of the CNP pathway is therefore hypothesised but untested; it is
logged as gap g_l3core_007.
pde1c.human_evidence_note: No human PDE1C growth plate data of any kind.
pde1c.translation_risk_reason: No growth plate data in any species; nothing to translate.
localization: growth plate, any species: PDE1C not reported
human, mouse and chicken growth plate chondrocytes: PDE1B (not PDE1C) transcript reported (ursachi2026 index)

key_refs.one_line_finding: PDE1B rather than PDE1C is reported in growth plate chondrocytes; PDE1 genes have never been functionally linked to the skeleton.
CNP/NPR2 drives TRPM7-mediated Ca2+ entry in growth plate chondrocytes, providing the Ca2+ signal that a PDE1 isoform could read.

pde3a.name: PDE3A
pde3a.summary:
PDE3A is a dual-specificity phosphodiesterase with high affinity for both cAMP and cGMP, in which
cGMP binding competitively inhibits cAMP hydrolysis, making it a point of direct cross-inhibition
between the PTH1R/cAMP and NPR2/cGMP arms of growth plate control. Its human skeletal relevance is
established by a gain-of-function mechanism rather than by cartilage expression data: mutations that
potentiate PKA-mediated PDE3A activation cause autosomal dominant hypertension with brachydactyly
type E (Bilginturan syndrome), in which shortened metacarpals and short stature accompany the
cardiovascular phenotype and are attributed to accelerated chondrocyte maturation from blunted
PTH1R-cAMP signalling (Maass 2015; Reyes 2020). Direct evidence for PDE3A in the growth plate itself
is weak: it is reported at moderate to negligible levels in whole-bone and osteocyte transcriptomes
and the assignment of PDE3A to PTH1R-driven cAMP in chondrocytes is a review-level synthesis, not a
measurement (Ursachi 2026). No study localises PDE3A protein by growth plate zone in any species.
pde3a.human_evidence_note: Human PDE3A gain-of-function causes brachydactyly with short stature, but the skeletal mechanism is inferred and no human growth plate PDE3A measurement exists.
pde3a.translation_risk_reason: The human phenotype is real and dose-linked, but the cartilage mechanism is inferred from cAMP biology rather than measured in growth plate tissue.
localization: human: PDE3A gain-of-function produces brachydactyly and short stature, tissue localisation in growth plate unconfirmed
mouse whole bone/osteocyte: moderate to negligible transcript (ursachi2026 index)
human or rodent growth plate zone: no localisation reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Gain-of-function PDE3A mutations cause autosomal dominant hypertension with brachydactyly.
Assigns PDE3A to PTH1R-driven cAMP hydrolysis in growth plate chondrocytes as a synthesis of expression data.
Reviews non-GNAS causes of shortened fingers and toes including PDE3A gain-of-function.

pde3b.name: PDE3B
pde3b.summary:
PDE3B is the phosphodiesterase with the strongest functional evidence for degrading NPR2-derived
cGMP in the growth plate, and it was absent from the initial node inventory of this atlas. Pde3b-null
mice generated by the International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium have increased tibial length, the
direction predicted if PDE3B limits CNP output. Pharmacologically, the PDE3 inhibitors cilostazol
and milrinone raise cGMP in mouse growth plate chondrocytes, activate cell-surface K+ channels
through PKG-mediated phosphorylation, hyperpolarise the cell and thereby increase the driving force
for TRPM7-mediated Ca2+ entry; cilostazol elongated cultured bones and enlarged juvenile mice
(Kawabe 2025, building on Miyazaki 2022). In human and bovine articular cartilage PDE3B is enriched
in the superficial zone where chondroprogenitors reside (Grogan 2013), but no equivalent zonal
measurement exists for growth plate in any species and no human growth plate PDE3B data exist at all.
pde3b.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate PDE3B data; the only human PDE3B cartilage data are from articular, not growth plate, tissue.
pde3b.translation_risk_reason: Functional evidence is mouse pharmacology plus a mouse knockout; the human growth plate has never been examined and rat data assign the dominant cGMP PDE to PDE5 instead.
localization: mouse growth plate chondrocytes: functionally confirmed by PDE3 inhibitor pharmacology (kawabe2025)
human articular cartilage superficial zone: enriched (grogan2013)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: PDE3 inhibitors raise growth plate chondrocyte cGMP and elongate mouse bone; PDE3B identified as the target from expression data.
CNP/NPR2 signalling drives TRPM7-mediated autonomous Ca2+ entry required for mouse bone growth.
PDE3B is superficial-zone enriched in human and bovine articular cartilage.

PDE3A and PDE3B share 48% overall identity and >95% ACTIVE-SITE homology, described as a massive obstacle to active-site selectivity; every FDA-approved PDE3 inhibitor is family-selective only, not isoform-selective. Quantifies why cilostazol and milrinone cannot assign a cGMP effect to PDE3B over PDE3A.

pde5a.name: PDE5A
pde5a.summary:
PDE5A is a cGMP-specific phosphodiesterase and, in rat, the dominant cGMP-hydrolysing activity of
growth plate chondrocytes: transcript profiling of primary chondrocytes from newborn rat epiphyses
identified robust PDE5 expression, and the PDE5 inhibitor tadalafil raised the peak CNP-stimulated
intracellular cGMP by 37% and attenuated its decline (Wang 2018). The functional consequence,
however, was negative: three weeks of tadalafil at 10 mg/kg/day in one-month-old rats raised tissue
cGMP by 52% but produced no change in long bone length, cortical or trabecular bone properties, or
growth plate histology. This is a directly relevant negative result for the assumption that raising
bulk cGMP is sufficient to lengthen bone, and it stands against the positive mouse result obtained
with PDE3 inhibition (Kawabe 2025). PDE5A transcript is reported in human, mouse and chicken growth
plate chondrocytes in bulk profiling (Ursachi 2026), but no human growth plate PDE5A localisation or
pharmacology has been reported, despite children with pulmonary arterial hypertension being treated
chronically with PDE5 inhibitors.
pde5a.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate PDE5A measurement and no reported skeletal outcome data from paediatric PDE5-inhibitor exposure.
pde5a.translation_risk_reason: The one functional experiment is rat and negative; human children are chronically exposed to PDE5 inhibitors with no reported growth plate follow-up.
localization: rat epiphyseal chondrocytes: robust expression, confirmed by transcript profiling (wang2018)
human, mouse and chicken growth plate chondrocytes (bulk): PDE5A transcript reported (ursachi2026 index)
human growth plate zone: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: PDE5 is the major cGMP PDE in rat epiphyseal chondrocytes; tadalafil raised cGMP 37-52% but did not lengthen bone.
PDE5A transcript reported in human, mouse and chicken growth plate chondrocytes.

pde9a.name: PDE9A
pde9a.summary:
PDE9A is the highest-affinity cGMP-specific phosphodiesterase known and is therefore an a priori
candidate for setting basal cGMP tone in any cGMP-driven tissue, which is why it appears in this
atlas as a coastline node. The evidence does not support its inclusion as an active growth plate
component. Systematic searching of Europe PMC returns no primary study reporting PDE9A expression,
localisation or function in growth plate cartilage in any species, and the only comprehensive review
of PDE expression in skeletal tissue concludes that PDE6, PDE9 and PDE11 family genes are not
expressed in bone or cartilage (Ursachi 2026). This node is retained as an explicit negative: PDE9A
is a plausible but undocumented participant, and its absence is a finding rather than a hole. If a
zone-resolved human growth plate PDE map is ever produced (gap g_l3core_006) PDE9A is the isoform
whose status would change most informatively.
pde9a.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate PDE9A data exist; the only skeletal statement is a negative from a review of expression datasets.
pde9a.translation_risk_reason: No species has data on PDE9A in growth plate, so no translation judgement can be made.
localization: growth plate, any species: not reported
bone and cartilage transcriptomes: PDE9 family reported not expressed (ursachi2026)

key_refs.one_line_finding: PDE6, PDE9 and PDE11 family genes are reported not expressed in bone or cartilage.

pde_isoform_inventory.name: Phosphodiesterase isoform inventory in the growth plate
pde_isoform_inventory.summary:
Signal duration in the CNP/NPR2 arm is set by cGMP hydrolysis, so the phosphodiesterase complement is
a rate-limiting variable, yet it is one of the least mapped parts of this network. Transcript-level
profiling of growth plate chondrocytes across human, mouse and chicken reports concordant expression
of PDE1B, PDE3B, PDE4B, PDE4D, PDE5A, PDE7A, PDE8A and PDE10A, with PDE6, PDE9 and PDE11 family genes
reported absent from skeletal tissue (Ursachi 2026, indexing Takacs 2023 and Kawabe 2025). Functional
assignment conflicts by species: in newborn rat epiphyseal chondrocytes PDE5 was the dominant
cGMP-hydrolysing activity, but three weeks of tadalafil raised tissue cGMP 52% without lengthening
bone (Wang 2018), whereas in mouse PDE3B was the functional target and the PDE3 inhibitor cilostazol
elongated cultured bones and enlarged juvenile animals (Kawabe 2025). Zone-resolved PDE data exist
only for articular, not growth plate, cartilage: PDE3B is enriched in the superficial zone and PDE7A
in the deep zone of human and bovine articular cartilage (Grogan 2013). No study reports PDE isoform
localisation by growth plate zone in human tissue - established by systematic search, gap
g_l3core_006. The stub isoforms PDE9A and PDE1C in particular have no primary growth plate
literature at all.
pde_isoform_inventory.human_evidence_note: Human PDE data in cartilage come from bulk transcriptomes and from articular, not growth plate, zonal profiling; no human growth plate zonal PDE map exists.
pde_isoform_inventory.translation_risk_reason: Functional isoform assignment already disagrees between rat and mouse, and the human map is absent; extrapolating rodent PDE pharmacology to human growth plate is unsupported.
localization: mouse, human and chicken growth plate chondrocytes (bulk, not zonal): PDE1B, 3B, 4B, 4D, 5A, 7A, 8A, 10A transcripts reported (ursachi2026 index)
rat epiphyseal chondrocytes (bulk): PDE5 dominant cGMP hydrolysis, confirmed by expression and tadalafil pharmacology (wang2018)
human articular cartilage superficial zone: PDE3B enriched (grogan2013)
human articular cartilage deep zone: PDE7A enriched (grogan2013)
human growth plate RZ/PZ/PHZ/HZ: no PDE isoform localisation reported in any study

key_refs.one_line_finding: Growth plate chondrocytes of human, mouse and chicken express PDE1B, 3B, 4B, 4D, 5A, 7A, 8A and 10A; PDE6/9/11 family genes reported absent from skeletal tissue.
PDE5 is the major cGMP-hydrolysing PDE in newborn rat epiphyseal chondrocytes; tadalafil raised cGMP but not bone length.
PDE3B is the functional cGMP PDE in mouse growth plate; cilostazol elongates bone.
PDE3B is superficial-zone enriched and PDE7A deep-zone enriched in human and bovine articular cartilage.
Temporal transcriptomic atlas of chondrogenesis reporting PDE isoform expression across differentiation.

pkg2_kinase.name: PKG-II
pkg2_kinase.summary:
PKG-II is a membrane-anchored cGMP-dependent protein kinase required for the growth-promoting
output of the CNP/NPR2 pathway, but it is not a sufficient account of that pathway and its
canonical zonal story does not survive the primary data. Prkg2-null mice and the naturally mutant KMI
rat are dwarfed with an EXPANDED growth plate - 665 +/- 47 um versus 255 +/- 34 um in wild type,
n=8 - built from an accumulated intermediate layer of postmitotic but non-hypertrophic chondrocytes,
so PKG-II couples the cessation of proliferation to the START of hypertrophy, mechanistically by
blocking nuclear entry of SOX9 (Chikuda 2004) and by phosphorylating GSK-3beta at Ser9 (Kawasaki
2008). Two things follow that reviews do not carry. First, the direction is opposite to CNP/NPR2
loss: cartilage-specific Npr2 deletion REDUCES the hypertrophic layer to 23.0% of control and thins
the whole plate (Nakao 2015), whereas Prkg2 loss expands it 2.6-fold - a linear
CNP-GC-B-cGMP-PKG-II chain predicts these phenocopy and they do not. Chikuda 2004, Nakao 2015 and
Agoston 2007 each name this conflict in their own discussion. Second, PKG-II protein by IHC is
predominantly in LATE PROLIFERATIVE AND PREHYPERTROPHIC chondrocytes, not hypertrophic ones (Chikuda
2004, rat); the hypertrophic enrichment widely quoted is Prkg2 mRNA (4.4-fold) from micro-dissected
mouse tibia whose compartments are resting/proliferative combined, hypertrophic and mineralized
(Agoston 2007). The decisive alternative has never been removed: cGKI (Prkg1) is co-expressed at
HIGHER zonal enrichment (5.9-fold) and both Chikuda 2004 and Agoston 2007 independently name the
cGKI/cGKII double knockout as the experiment needed, which has still not been done (g_l2d_001).
PKG also has at least one substrate arm outside SOX9/GSK-3beta: CNP-driven bone growth in tibia
explant is abolished by chondrocyte-specific Trpm7 ablation, via PKG acting on the BK channel to
drive TRPM7 Ca2+ entry and CaMKII (Miyazaki 2022). Human biallelic PRKG2 loss-of-function variants
cause an acromesomelic dysplasia phenotypically overlapping the NPR2 form (Diaz-Gonzalez 2022),
which remains the strongest evidence that PKG-II is required for the pathway output in humans;
nonsense PRKG2 alleles also cause disproportionate dwarfism in dogs.
pkg2_kinase.human_evidence_note: Biallelic human PRKG2 loss-of-function causes acromesomelic dysplasia, but no human growth plate tissue has been examined for PKG-II.
pkg2_kinase.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism is rodent; the human evidence is a matching monogenic skeletal dysplasia without tissue-level confirmation.
localization: rat late PZ and PHZ: PKG-II PROTEIN by immunohistochemistry, predominant here and preceding the onset of hypertrophy (chikuda2004) - this is the only protein-level zonal map that exists
mouse HZ: Prkg1 (5.9-fold) and Prkg2 (4.4-fold) mRNA higher than in the combined resting/proliferative compartment (agoston2007) - mRNA only, and the compartments are not RZ/PZ/HZ
CONFLICT: protein (chikuda2004, rat, prehypertrophic) and mRNA (agoston2007, mouse, hypertrophic) disagree; see CORR-003
human growth plate: zonal PKG-II protein map unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: PKG-II protein is predominantly in LATE PROLIFERATIVE and PREHYPERTROPHIC chondrocytes; the Prkg2-mutant KMI rat growth plate is EXPANDED (665 +/- 47 vs 255 +/- 34 um, n=8) by a postmitotic non-hypertrophic intermediate layer; PKG-II acts by blocking SOX9 nuclear entry; cGKI involvement could not be excluded.
Prkg2-null mice are dwarfed with an expanded hypertrophic zone.
PKG-II phosphorylates GSK-3beta Ser9 to promote hypertrophic differentiation.

CNP-facilitated bone growth in mouse tibia explant is abolished by chondrocyte-specific Trpm7 ablation; the proposed chain is NPR2-cGMP-PKG-BK channel-TRPM7 Ca2+ entry-CaMKII, a PKG substrate arm outside SOX9 and GSK-3beta.
Cartilage-specific Npr2 deletion REDUCES the hypertrophic layer to 23.0% of control, the opposite direction to the expanded Prkg2-mutant plate; the authors flag this as an unresolved problem.
Biallelic PRKG2 variants cause a novel human acromesomelic dysplasia.

Prkg1 (5.9-fold) and Prkg2 (4.4-fold) mRNA are enriched in the hypertrophic versus the combined resting/proliferative compartment of micro-dissected mouse tibia; the authors state the cGKII and CNP knockout cartilage phenotypes are NOT identical and call for a cGKI/cGKII double knockout.

primary_cilium_chondrocyte.name: Primary cilium of the growth plate chondrocyte
primary_cilium_chondrocyte.summary: Growth plate chondrocytes carry a single non-motile primary cilium that acts as the compartment in which Hedgehog signal transduction occurs: PTCH1 leaves and SMO enters the ciliary membrane on ligand binding, and GLI processing depends on intraflagellar transport along the axoneme. Removing the cilium genetically therefore removes IHH responsiveness without removing IHH. Ift88 deletion in limb mesenchyme shortens the proximodistal axis and disrupts endochondral bone formation through loss of Ihh signalling, in addition to polydactyly from disturbed SHH patterning (Haycraft 2007, mouse). Cartilage Kif3a deletion abolishes the normal zonal organisation by postnatal day 7 - proliferative and hypertrophic zones are replaced by cells with strong Col2a1 but almost no Ihh, Col10a1, Vegfa, Mmp13 or Sp7 - while hedgehog signalling paradoxically INCREASES and spreads in the adjacent perichondrium, producing ectopic cartilage and excessive intramembranous ossification (Koyama 2007, mouse). The cilium's importance is thus topological: it does not merely amplify Hedgehog, it confines it. Human evidence is the ciliopathy skeletal dysplasias (Jeune, Ellis-van Creveld, short-rib polydactyly), which are among the strongest human anchors in this layer.
primary_cilium_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: Human ciliopathy genes (IFT80, EVC, EVC2) cause defined chondrodysplasias, but no human growth plate cilium morphometry was located.
primary_cilium_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism is mouse; human evidence is germline ciliopathy phenotypes without physeal tissue analysis.
localization: mouse growth plate, all zones: cilia present and required (haycraft2007, koyama2007)
human growth plate: inferred from ciliopathy dysplasias; direct ultrastructural zonal survey not identified

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mesenchymal Ift88 deletion shortens the proximodistal limb axis by disrupting Ihh signalling during endochondral bone formation.
Cartilage Kif3a deletion destroys zonal organisation and lowers hedgehog signalling inside the plate while raising it in the perichondrium.
IFT80 mutations cause human Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy, the first IFT protein linked to human disease.

pth1r_receptor.name: PTH1R
pth1r_receptor.summary:
PTH1R is a class B GPCR expressed most strongly in late proliferative and prehypertrophic
chondrocytes, coupling to Gs/cAMP/PKA and to Gq/11. Its activation by PTHrP maintains proliferation
and delays hypertrophy; targeted expression of the constitutively active Jansen mutant receptor in
mouse growth plate delays hypertrophic differentiation and mineralization and produces
chondrodysplasia; the same transgene CORRECTS the growth plate of PTHrP-null mice at birth and
rescues their survival, which is the epistasis result placing the receptor downstream of the ligand,
and the rescued animals show premature epiphyseal closure and absent tooth eruption (Schipani 1997)
- a rare instance of mouse epiphyseal closure, and directly relevant to L7 since mice do not
normally fuse,
and Pth1r ablation gives a phenotype distinct from Pthlh ablation, indicating PTHrP-independent
receptor functions (Lanske 1999). Both human directions of the dose-response are known: the
activating H223R substitution causes Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with retained hypertrophic
cartilage (Schipani 1995), and functional absence of the receptor causes Blomstrand lethal
chondrodysplasia with markedly advanced endochondral ossification (Jobert 1998). The genotype there
is more delicate than a plain statement of biallelic loss: the single reported patient was HETEROZYGOUS for a
splice-creating point mutation inherited from the mother, and the paternal allele was simply not
expressed by an unexplained mechanism, so the state is functionally but not genotypically biallelic,
n = 1. Chimeric mice carrying both wild-type and Pth1r-null cells show
the receptor acts CELL-AUTONOMOUSLY on proliferating chondrocytes, and that mineralization around
ectopic hypertrophic cells is non-cell-autonomous, requiring a critical mass of adjacent hypertrophic
cells (Chung 1998). Downstream of PTH1R in chondrocytes, cAMP is hydrolysed by PDE3A/PDE4 isoforms, and gain-of-function PDE3A variants
produce brachydactyly with short stature in humans, the mirror-image lesion (Maass 2015).
pth1r_receptor.human_evidence_note: Human gain-of-function (Jansen) and loss-of-function (Blomstrand) mutations give opposite, well-characterised growth plate histopathology in human tissue.
pth1r_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Both dosage directions are documented in human skeletal tissue and match the mouse genetic result.
localization: mouse late PZ/PHZ: confirmed by ISH (vortkamp1996)
human growth plate: expression inferred from disease phenotype, zonal protein map unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Constitutively active PTH1R H223R causes Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia.

Loss of functional PTH1R causes Blomstrand chondrodysplasia with advanced ossification; n=1 patient, heterozygous for a splice-creating point mutation with the paternal allele unexpressed by an unexplained mechanism - functionally, not genotypically, biallelic.

Targeted constitutively active PTH1R (HKrk-H223R) delays hypertrophic conversion and mineralization, corrects the PTHrP-null growth plate at birth and rescues survival; rescued animals show premature epiphyseal closure and no tooth eruption.
Pthlh-null and Pth1r-null mice differ, indicating PTHrP-independent receptor roles.

Gain-of-function PDE3A variants cause hypertension with brachydactyly and short stature, the mirror-image lesion downstream of PTH1R-cAMP. Cited in this node's prose since authoring but missing from key_refs until the phase 2d audit.
