In wild-type/Pth1r-null chimeras PTHrP signals directly to PTH1R on PROLIFERATING chondrocytes; matrix mineralization around ectopic hypertrophic cells is non-cell-autonomous and requires a critical mass of adjacent hypertrophic cells.

pthrp_cnp_crosstalk.name: PTHrP-CNP crosstalk
pthrp_cnp_crosstalk.summary:
The two dominant local control systems of the growth plate - PTHrP/PTH1R/cAMP and CNP/NPR2/cGMP -
have never been shown to interact directly, and the absence is established by systematic search
(gap g_l3core_005). A Europe PMC title/abstract query requiring both a PTHrP-pathway term and a
CNP-pathway term returns eight records, none of which reports a mechanistic interaction in growth
plate cartilage; the closest is a 2003 study of adrenomedullin, CNP and PTHrP effects on cultured
cells, in which the peptides were tested in parallel rather than in combination. Three indirect
convergence points are documented and are the reason to expect an interaction: PKG-II, the CNP
effector, blocks nuclear entry of SOX9 (Chikuda 2004) while PTHrP signalling maintains SOX9 and
represses hypertrophy through HDAC4/5-MEF2 (Nishimori 2019), so both pathways converge on the
hypertrophy switch from opposite directions; CNP acting through NPR2 also raises PKA activity in
hypertrophic chondrocytes (Hirota 2022), which is the same effector PTH1R uses; and PDE3A/PDE3B are
dual-specificity enzymes in which cGMP competitively inhibits cAMP hydrolysis, providing a
biochemical coupling that has never been tested in cartilage. This node is therefore a genuine
negative-space entry: the crosstalk is expected on mechanistic grounds and has not been looked for.
pthrp_cnp_crosstalk.human_evidence_note: No human study addresses PTHrP-CNP interaction; the human evidence for the two pathways is entirely separate monogenic series.
pthrp_cnp_crosstalk.translation_risk_reason: There is no established mechanism in any species, so translation risk cannot be graded.
localization: growth plate, any species: direct PTHrP-CNP interaction not reported
mouse HZ: PKA activation by CNP confirmed (hirota2022) - shared effector, not demonstrated crosstalk

key_refs.one_line_finding: PKG-II, the CNP effector, blocks SOX9 nuclear entry to permit hypertrophy.
PTHrP represses hypertrophy through HDAC4/HDAC5 acting on MEF2.
CNP raises PKA activity in hypertrophic chondrocytes, the effector shared with PTH1R.
PDE3 enzymes couple cAMP and cGMP hydrolysis, giving a candidate biochemical coupling between the two arms.

pthrp_ihh_feedback_loop.name: PTHrP/IHH negative feedback loop
pthrp_ihh_feedback_loop.summary:
PTHrP (PTHLH) is transcribed by periarticular and resting-zone chondrocytes and by perichondrium;
it diffuses toward the metaphysis and acts on PTH1R, which is most highly expressed in late
proliferative and prehypertrophic chondrocytes, to keep those cells cycling and to delay the switch
to hypertrophy (mouse and chick). Chondrocytes that leave the effective range of PTHrP exit the cell
cycle and switch on Ihh; Ihh then signals back through PTCH1/SMO, relieving GLI3 repressor, and
raises Pthlh transcription in the periarticular region, closing a negative feedback loop whose
geometry sets the length of the proliferative column - though whether the Ihh-to-Pthlh arm is direct
long-range action (Koziel 2004) or runs through a perichondrial signalling relay (raised by
St-Jacques 1999) has never been formally settled (Vortkamp 1996, chick and mouse; Lanske 1996;
St-Jacques 1999). The loop is not the whole of Ihh function: Ihh also drives columnar chondrocyte
proliferation cell-autonomously through Smo, and promotes both periarticular chondrocyte
differentiation and hypertrophy in a PTHrP-independent manner (Long 2001; Kobayashi 2002; Kobayashi
2005; Mak 2008). Ihh behaves as a long-range morphogen whose spread is limited by heparan sulfate
and requires DISP1: reducing Ext1 EXPANDS the Ihh signalling range, whereas Disp1 hypomorphs
establish the same loop over a shorter distance (Koziel 2004; Tsiairis 2008). Human genetics
supports each arm separately - PTHLH haploinsufficiency causes brachydactyly type E, IHH mutations
cause brachydactyly A1 and acrocapitofemoral dysplasia, PTH1R gain of function causes Jansen
metaphyseal chondrodysplasia and PTH1R loss causes Blomstrand chondrodysplasia - but the loop as a
closed control system has never been characterised quantitatively in any species: no measured
diffusion coefficient, decay length, transfer function or loop gain exists (gap g_l3core_001).
pthrp_ihh_feedback_loop.human_evidence_note: Each node of the loop has a human monogenic phenotype (PTHLH, IHH, PTH1R), but loop topology and gain have never been measured in human tissue.
pthrp_ihh_feedback_loop.translation_risk_reason: Loop wiring is inferred almost entirely from mouse and chick genetics; human evidence is genetic dose-effect only, and mice do not undergo epiphyseal fusion so late-stage loop behaviour may differ.
localization: mouse periarticular/RZ: Pthlh source, confirmed by ISH (vortkamp1996)
mouse PHZ: Ihh source, confirmed by ISH (vortkamp1996)
mouse PZ/PHZ: PTH1R highest, confirmed (vortkamp1996)
human RZ/PHZ: zonal PTHrP and IHH protein distribution unconfirmed in growth plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: Ihh from prehypertrophic chondrocytes raises periarticular PTHrP and blocks hypertrophy in chick limb.
PTHrP delays terminal chondrocyte differentiation in mouse endochondral bone.
Ihh-null mice lose chondrocyte proliferation and show ectopic hypertrophy.
Ihh sets the site of hypertrophy via PTHrP but controls proliferation independently.
PTHrP and Ihh act at multiple separable steps of chondrocyte differentiation.
Cell-autonomous Smo deletion reduces chondrocyte proliferation, showing direct Ihh action.
Ihh promotes hypertrophy even in a PTHrP-null background.
Heparan sulfate limits Ihh range; Ihh acts as a long-range morphogen directly activating Pthlh.
Disp1 hypomorphs establish the PTHrP-Ihh loop over a shorter distance.

pthrp_protein.name: PTHrP
pthrp_protein.summary:
PTHrP is encoded by PTHLH and secreted by periarticular/resting-zone chondrocytes and perichondrium.
Acting through PTH1R it holds chondrocytes in the proliferative pool and delays hypertrophy; mouse
Pthlh-null animals die at birth with markedly accelerated chondrocyte hypertrophy and premature
ossification (Lee 1996), and the same acceleration occurs cell-autonomously in PTH1R-null chondrocytes
transplanted into wild-type limbs (Chung 1998). Downstream, PTHrP-PTH1R signalling represses
hypertrophy by phosphorylation-dependent nuclear retention of HDAC4 and HDAC5 acting on MEF2
(Nishimori 2019), and by inducing ZFP521 and ECM1 (Correa 2010; Kong 2016). Human PTHLH deletions and
point mutations cause autosomal dominant brachydactyly type E with short stature, establishing that
human skeletal growth is PTHrP dose-sensitive (Klopocki 2010). A measured PTHrP protein gradient has
been demonstrated in mouse mandibular condylar cartilage (Tsutsumi-Arai 2024), but no equivalent
gradient measurement exists for the human long-bone growth plate.
pthrp_protein.human_evidence_note: Heterozygous PTHLH loss-of-function causes brachydactyly type E with short stature; no direct measurement of PTHrP in human growth plate zones.
pthrp_protein.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism is murine; human evidence is a dominant monogenic dosage phenotype without tissue-level confirmation.
localization: mouse periarticular chondrocytes and RZ: confirmed by ISH (vortkamp1996)
mouse PERI: confirmed (lee1996)
human RZ: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: PTHrP delays terminal differentiation; Pthlh-null mice show premature hypertrophy.
PTH1R-null chondrocytes hypertrophy prematurely cell-autonomously.
PTHrP represses hypertrophy through HDAC4 and HDAC5.
PTHLH deletions and point mutations cause human brachydactyly type E.
Zfp521 is a direct PTHrP target effector in growth plate chondrocytes.
A spatial PTHrP gradient drives condylar chondrogenesis via Runx2.

raptor_protein.name: RAPTOR (RPTOR)
raptor_protein.summary: RAPTOR is the defining scaffold subunit of mTORC1; it presents TOS-motif substrates such as S6K1 and 4E-BP1 to the mTOR kinase and is what distinguishes mTORC1 from RICTOR-containing mTORC2. Deleting Raptor in mouse limb mesenchyme phenocopies mTor deletion in cartilage - severe reduction of embryonic skeletal growth, delayed chondrocyte hypertrophy, smaller chondrocytes and less matrix - and metabolic labelling in Raptor-deficient chondrocytes shows the deficit is in the rate of protein synthesis (Chen and Long 2014). Because the mTor-null and Raptor-null cartilage phenotypes match, the skeletal growth requirement is attributable to mTORC1 rather than mTORC2. Upstream, RHEB1 is required for the same axis: Rheb1 loss impairs limb growth through chondrogenesis in mouse (Zhang 2024). No human growth plate RAPTOR data exist.
raptor_protein.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate RAPTOR measurement or human RPTOR skeletal phenotype.
localization: mouse limb cartilage: functionally required (chen2014)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Raptor deletion in mouse limb cartilage reduces protein synthesis rate, chondrocyte size and skeletal growth.
Rheb1, the mTORC1 activator, is required for mouse limb growth through chondrogenesis in the growth plate.

rbpj_tf.name: RBPJ
rbpj_tf.summary: RBPJ is the DNA-binding transcription factor through which all four Notch receptors signal; without NICD it recruits corepressors, with NICD it recruits MAML and activates transcription. Because it is a single obligatory node, Rbpj deletion is the cleanest available Notch-off experiment. Prx1-Cre and Sox9-Cre driven Rbpj deletion in mouse limb mesenchyme/chondroprogenitors impairs the terminal stage of endochondral ossification and raises SOX9 (Kohn 2015, Hosaka 2013), while Col2a1-CreERT-driven deletion in adult articular cartilage confers resistance to surgically induced osteoarthritis (Hosaka 2013). Deleting Rbpj in mesenchymal cells produces a rickets-like phenotype in mouse, indicating the requirement extends into mineralisation as well as differentiation (Gao 2022). RBPJ-independent Notch outputs exist in cartilage, so an Rbpj-null phenotype is a lower bound on Notch function, not a complete one. No human RBPJ growth plate data exist; human RBPJ haploinsufficiency causes Adams-Oliver syndrome, which is not primarily a physeal disorder.
rbpj_tf.human_evidence_note: Human RBPJ variants cause Adams-Oliver syndrome; no human growth plate RBPJ data.
rbpj_tf.translation_risk_reason: Conditional mouse genetics only; the human RBPJ phenotype is vascular/limb-terminal rather than physeal.
localization: mouse chondroprogenitor and growth plate: functionally required (kohn2015, hosaka2013)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Prx1Cre;Rbpj-null limb phenotype is rescued by Sox9 heterozygosity, placing SOX9 downstream of RBPJ for maturation onset.
Sox9-Cre Rbpj deletion impairs terminal endochondral ossification; adult deletion protects against osteoarthritis.
Deleting RBP-Jkappa in mesenchymal cells causes rickets-like changes in mouse.

runx2_tf.name: RUNX2
runx2_tf.summary: RUNX2 is the transcription factor that licenses chondrocyte hypertrophy and osteoblast differentiation. Human heterozygous RUNX2/CBFA1 loss of function causes cleidocranial dysplasia with clavicular hypoplasia, delayed fontanelle closure, supernumerary teeth and short stature (Mundlos 1997), giving this node direct human dose evidence. In mouse, chondrocyte maturation is delayed in Runx2-null animals but still occurs; only Runx2;Runx3 double nulls show a complete absence of maturation, and limb length falls in proportion to the combined Runx2 and Runx3 gene dose (Yoshida 2004). The same study shows RUNX2 binds the Ihh promoter directly and induces Ihh, so RUNX2 sits upstream of the IHH/PTHrP loop as well as downstream of it - a feedback the linear textbook cascade omits. RUNX2 activity is restrained post-translationally rather than only transcriptionally: HDAC4 binds and inhibits RUNX2 (Vega 2004), ZFP521 antagonises RUNX2 through an HDAC4-dependent mechanism downstream of PTHrP (Correa 2010), and SOX9 keeps Runx2 expression in check (Dy 2012).
runx2_tf.human_evidence_note: Human RUNX2 haploinsufficiency causes cleidocranial dysplasia including short stature.
runx2_tf.translation_risk_reason: Concordant human haploinsufficiency and mouse null phenotypes; both affect endochondral and intramembranous bone.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: confirmed (vega2004, yoshida2004)
human: inferred from cleidocranial dysplasia haploinsufficiency (mundlos1997)

key_refs.one_line_finding: CBFA1/RUNX2 mutations cause human cleidocranial dysplasia.
Runx2 and Runx3 are jointly essential for chondrocyte maturation and RUNX2 directly induces Ihh by binding its promoter.
HDAC4 binds and inhibits RUNX2 in prehypertrophic chondrocytes.
SOX9 keeps Runx2 expression in check to prevent premature prehypertrophy and osteoblastic conversion.

runx3_tf.name: RUNX3
runx3_tf.summary: RUNX3 is the RUNX paralogue that shares the hypertrophy-licensing function with RUNX2. Its importance is invisible in single mutants and appears only in combination: Runx2-null mice still complete chondrocyte maturation, whereas Runx2;Runx3 double nulls show a complete absence of maturation and shortened limbs, with the severity tracking total RUNX gene dose (Yoshida 2004, mouse). Runx3 transcripts rise at the onset of cartilage mineralisation, after Sox9 and concomitant with alkaline phosphatase, and gain/loss of function in limb-bud-derived chondrogenic cells shows RUNX3 regulates both early and late maturation markers while transcriptionally inhibiting Runx1 (Soung 2007, mouse cells). No human RUNX3 skeletal dysplasia is established, and RUNX3 is not a recognised human short stature gene, so the human contribution of this paralogue is unknown.
runx3_tf.human_evidence_note: No human RUNX3 skeletal phenotype or growth plate measurement.
runx3_tf.translation_risk_reason: Mouse compound genetics and mouse cell lines; no human anchor at all.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: RUNX3 protein detected by immunohistochemistry in embryos (soung2007)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Runx2;Runx3 double-null mice completely lack chondrocyte maturation; the defect is RUNX gene-dose-dependent.
Runx3 regulates early and late chondrocyte maturation markers and transcriptionally inhibits Runx1.

salt_inducible_kinase3.name: SIK3
salt_inducible_kinase3.summary: SIK3 is an AMPK-family kinase that sits directly above HDAC4 and controls where HDAC4 is. SIK3 phosphorylates HDAC4 at its 14-3-3-binding sites, anchoring HDAC4 in the cytoplasm and thereby releasing MEF2C to drive hypertrophy. Sik3-null mice are normal-sized as embryos and become dwarfed with age; hypertrophy is markedly delayed from E14.5 and blocked until E18.5, growth plates and articular cartilage are expanded, chondrocytes accumulate in sternum, ribs and spine, and HDAC4 remains NUCLEAR in Sik3-null chondrocytes where it is cytoplasmic in wild-type hypertrophic cells (Sasagawa 2012). The converse is also shown: chondrocyte-specific SIK3 overexpression closes growth plates in adult mice. PTHrP acts through this kinase: PTHrP-cAMP-PKA phosphorylates the PKA sites on SIK3, inhibiting SIK3 kinase activity, so HDAC4 loses its cytoplasmic anchor, enters the nucleus and blocks MEF2 and RUNX2 (Nishimori 2021, mouse). SIK1 and SIK2 substitute when SIK3 activity is low, and HDAC5 substitutes when HDAC4 is low, so the cascade is doubly redundant. No human SIK3 skeletal phenotype is established; human SIK3 variants are known for the short-sleep trait.
salt_inducible_kinase3.human_evidence_note: No human SIK3 skeletal phenotype; human SIK3 variants are associated with sleep duration, not stature.
salt_inducible_kinase3.translation_risk_reason: Mouse germline knockout and transgenic overexpression; the human orthologue has no described physeal role.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: SIK3 protein detected in cytoplasm of prehypertrophic and hypertrophic chondrocytes (sasagawa2012)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: SIK3 anchors HDAC4 in the cytoplasm; Sik3-null mice have blocked hypertrophy and nuclear HDAC4, and SIK3 overexpression closes growth plates.
PTHrP/cAMP/PKA phosphorylates and inhibits SIK3, lowering HDAC4 phosphorylation and allowing nuclear HDAC4 to block MEF2 and RUNX2.
HDAC4 is required for PTHrP effects on chondrocyte differentiation in vivo, with HDAC5 as a partially redundant mediator.

sclerostin_sost.name: Sclerostin (SOST)
sclerostin_sost.summary: Sclerostin is a secreted WNT antagonist that binds LRP5/LRP6 and blocks canonical signalling. Human loss of function is definitive and bidirectional in effect: SOST-null sclerosteosis produces massive bone overgrowth with gigantism-adjacent features including tall stature and cranial nerve compression (Balemans 2001), which is one of the very few human WNT-pathway phenotypes that includes increased linear growth rather than only increased bone mass. In normal human bone, sclerostin protein is a delayed product of embedded osteocytes and is not detectable in early osteoblasts, so it acts as a late, spatially restricted brake (Poole 2005). The critical unresolved point for this atlas is whether sclerostin reaches the growth plate chondrocyte at all: SOST expression in growth plate cartilage has not been demonstrated, and the tall stature of sclerosteosis could be an indirect consequence of cortical and endosteal overgrowth. The therapeutic antibody romosozumab is licensed in adults only, so no paediatric physeal read-out exists.
sclerostin_sost.human_evidence_note: SOST null (sclerosteosis) is a human loss-of-function phenotype including increased stature; osteocyte localisation is shown in human bone.
sclerostin_sost.translation_risk_reason: Primary evidence is human germline and human histology; the risk is mechanistic (site of action), not species.
localization: human osteocyte: confirmed by immunohistochemistry (poole2005)
human growth plate chondrocyte: unconfirmed - not demonstrated
mouse growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Sclerosteosis is caused by deficiency of the secreted protein SOST.
Sclerostin is a delayed secreted product of embedded osteocytes that inhibits bone formation.

smad1_5_8.name: SMAD1/5/8 (BMP-responsive R-SMADs)
smad1_5_8.summary: SMAD1, SMAD5 and SMAD9(SMAD8) are the receptor-regulated SMADs phosphorylated by BMPR1A/BMPR1B; phospho-SMAD1/5/8 partners SMAD4 and enters the nucleus. Chondrocyte-restricted removal of Smad1 and Smad5 together in mouse produces severe chondrodysplasia with disorganised proliferative columns and impaired hypertrophy, while Smad1 or Smad5 single mutants and Smad8-null mice are near-normal - the requirement is for combined dose, not for a particular paralogue (Retting 2009). SMAD1/5/8 is also the convergence point for the antagonist layer: Noggin, Chordin and SMAD7 all act by lowering pSMAD1/5/8 output. SMAD7 inhibits chondrocyte differentiation at several steps in mouse, including by interfering with BMP-SMAD signalling (Iwai 2008). In mouse the zonal activity profile has been measured: pSMAD1/5/8 immunostaining is highest in the proliferative and prehypertrophic zones and lower in the hypertrophic zone despite Bmp2/Bmp6 mRNA being highest there, an inversion attributed to hypertrophic-zone SMAD7 (Garrison 2017). No equivalent series has been published on human growth plate tissue, so the human activity gradient across RZ-PZ-PHZ-HZ is unmeasured.
smad1_5_8.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate pSMAD1/5/8 measurement; human evidence for the BMP arm is confined to ligand/antagonist genetics.
smad1_5_8.translation_risk_reason: Entirely mouse conditional genetics; the human zonal activity profile has never been measured.
localization: mouse PZ/PHZ: pSmad1/5/8 highest by immunohistochemistry (garrison2017)
mouse HZ: pSmad1/5/8 lower despite high ligand mRNA; Smad7 high (garrison2017)
human growth plate: unconfirmed - no published zonal pSMAD1/5/8 staining

key_refs.one_line_finding: pSmad1/5/8 activity peaks in mouse PZ/PHZ, not in the hypertrophic zone where BMP ligand mRNA is highest.
Combined chondrocyte Smad1/Smad5 loss, but not either alone, causes severe chondrodysplasia in mouse.
Smad7 inhibits chondrocyte differentiation at multiple steps of endochondral bone formation.

smad2_3.name: SMAD2/SMAD3 (TGF-beta-responsive R-SMADs)
smad2_3.summary: SMAD2 and SMAD3 are phosphorylated by TGFBR1 downstream of TGFBR2 and mediate the canonical TGF-beta response. Smad3-null mice develop normal-length skeletons at birth but show progressive expansion of the hypertrophic zone and accelerated terminal differentiation, with degeneration of articular cartilage - i.e. SMAD3 output is a brake on the hypertrophy transition, opposite in sign to the BMP-SMAD1/5/8 arm (Yang 2001, mouse). The same directionality is seen with dominant-negative TGFBR2 expression in mouse skeletal tissue, which produces terminal chondrocyte differentiation and osteoarthritis (Serra 1997). This BMP-versus-TGF-beta sign split inside one ligand superfamily is the reason 'TGF-beta superfamily signalling' is not a usable unit of analysis in this atlas. Human SMAD2/SMAD3 variants cause aneurysm-osteoarthritis/Loeys-Dietz-spectrum disease with skeletal features, but no human growth plate SMAD2/3 activity measurement exists.
smad2_3.human_evidence_note: Human SMAD3 variants cause connective tissue disease with skeletal manifestations, but no growth plate SMAD2/3 activity data exist.
smad2_3.translation_risk_reason: Growth plate causal data are mouse germline/dominant-negative only.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: inferred from Smad3-null zonal expansion (yang2001)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Smad3-null mice show expanded hypertrophic zones and accelerated terminal chondrocyte differentiation.
Dominant-negative TGF-beta type II receptor in mouse skeleton promotes terminal chondrocyte differentiation.

smoothened.name: SMO
smoothened.summary:
SMO is the class F GPCR that transduces Hedgehog signals after PTCH1 derepression, and in the growth
plate it acts in the primary cilium. Chondrocyte-specific Smo deletion reduces columnar chondrocyte
proliferation cell-autonomously, which established that Ihh acts directly on proliferating
chondrocytes and not solely through PTHrP (Long 2001). Constitutive Hedgehog activation achieved by
Smo pathway manipulation accelerates hypertrophy even without PTHrP (Mak 2008), and pharmacological
SMO agonism increases linear growth in mice (Trompet 2024). The canonical PTCH1-SMO-GLI chain is not
the whole story in this tissue: cartilage-to-bone transition has been reported to require Hedgehog
signalling but to proceed independently of Smoothened (Wang 2022), a result that is not reconciled
with the Smo conditional-knockout literature (contradiction c_l3core_smo).
smoothened.human_evidence_note: No human SMO growth plate phenotype; human SMO mutations (Curry-Jones syndrome) are mosaic patterning disorders.
smoothened.translation_risk_reason: Mouse conditional genetics only; no human tissue or genetic readout of SMO growth plate function.
localization: mouse PZ chondrocyte primary cilium: functionally confirmed by conditional deletion (long2001)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chondrocyte Smo deletion reduces proliferation, proving direct Ihh action.
Hedgehog activation accelerates hypertrophy in a PTHrP-null background.
Hedgehog drives cartilage-to-bone transition independently of Smoothened.
SMO agonism in growth plate stem cells promotes linear bone growth.

sox5_tf.name: SOX5 (L-SOX5)
sox5_tf.summary: SOX5 is a SoxD-family factor with no transactivation domain of its own; it binds DNA as a dimer and raises the efficiency with which SOX9 activates cartilage matrix genes. Sox5 single-null mice have only mild skeletal abnormalities, and the requirement is revealed only in combination with Sox6: Sox5;Sox6 double-null fetuses die with generalised chondrodysplasia in which chondroblasts express essentially no cartilage matrix genes, begin proliferating only after a long delay, and epiphyseal chondroblasts ectopically switch on hypertrophic markers (Smits 2001, mouse). SOX5 expression is itself SOX9-dependent (Akiyama 2002, mouse). In human, heterozygous SOX5 loss of function causes Lamb-Shaffer syndrome, whose core features are neurodevelopmental with variable skeletal findings, so the human phenotype does not recapitulate the murine cartilage-specific requirement - a species discordance that should be stated explicitly rather than smoothed over.
sox5_tf.human_evidence_note: Human SOX5 haploinsufficiency (Lamb-Shaffer syndrome) is primarily neurodevelopmental; no human growth plate data.
sox5_tf.translation_risk_reason: The mouse requirement is only visible in the Sox5;Sox6 double null; the human heterozygous phenotype is a different organ system.
localization: mouse cartilage, all zones: co-expressed with Sox6 and Sox9 (smits2001)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Sox5 and Sox6 are individually near-dispensable but jointly essential for cartilage matrix gene expression and growth plate formation.
Sox9 is required for expression of Sox5 and Sox6.

sox6_tf.name: SOX6
sox6_tf.summary: SOX6 is the near-identical paralogue of SOX5 and is functionally interchangeable with it in cartilage. Sox6 single nulls are born with mild skeletal abnormalities; Sox5;Sox6 double nulls have a severe generalised chondrodysplasia with matrix-deficient, rudimentary cartilages and disrupted growth plate formation, and epiphyseal chondroblasts inappropriately activate hypertrophic markers (Smits 2001, mouse). The redundancy means gene dose, not gene identity, is the variable, exactly as for BMP-SMAD1/5 and RUNX2/RUNX3 elsewhere in this layer. SOX6 expression requires SOX9 (Akiyama 2002, mouse). Human SOX6 variants have been reported with skeletal and haematological features, but no human growth plate SOX6 measurement or established SOX6 chondrodysplasia is available.
sox6_tf.human_evidence_note: No established human SOX6 chondrodysplasia and no human growth plate SOX6 data.
localization: mouse cartilage, all zones: co-expressed with Sox5 and Sox9 (smits2001)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Sox6 is redundant with Sox5; the double null has severe generalised chondrodysplasia.
Sox9 is required for Sox6 expression, placing SOX6 downstream of SOX9.

sox9_tf.name: SOX9
sox9_tf.summary: SOX9 is the master chondrogenic transcription factor and the only node in this layer with an unambiguous human loss-of-function phenotype. Heterozygous SOX9 mutations and translocations cause campomelic dysplasia with bowed long bones, hypoplastic scapulae and autosomal XY sex reversal (Foster 1994; Wagner 1994), so human haploinsufficiency alone is sufficient to derail skeletogenesis. In mouse, Sox9-null cells are excluded from cartilage condensations (Bi 1999), and staged inactivation shows successive requirements: for condensation, for overt chondrocyte differentiation, and for expression of Sox5 and Sox6 (Akiyama 2002). Later in the growth plate, SOX9 maintains columnar proliferation and is required to generate hypertrophy while simultaneously restraining Runx2 and beta-catenin, thereby blocking acquisition of an osteoblast phenotype; SOX9 protein outlives its mRNA into upper hypertrophic cells, where it acts with MEF2C to activate Col10a1 directly (Dy 2012, mouse). SOX9 is antagonised by and antagonises beta-catenin reciprocally (Akiyama 2004; Topol 2009), is suppressed by sustained Notch signalling (Kohn 2015), and drives its own nutrient supply via GLS1 (Stegen 2020) - making it the single most convergent node in L3.
sox9_tf.human_evidence_note: Heterozygous human SOX9 loss of function causes campomelic dysplasia, a defined skeletal phenotype.
sox9_tf.translation_risk_reason: Human haploinsufficiency phenotype and mouse conditional genetics agree in direction and in tissue.
localization: mouse RZ/PZ/PHZ and upper HZ (protein): confirmed (dy2012)
human: inferred from campomelic dysplasia haploinsufficiency (foster1994, wagner1994)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Campomelic dysplasia with autosomal sex reversal is caused by mutations in the SRY-related gene SOX9.
Independent confirmation that mutations in and around SOX9 cause campomelic dysplasia and sex reversal.
Sox9 is required at successive steps of chondrocyte differentiation and for Sox5/Sox6 expression in mouse.
Sox9 maintains columnar proliferation, generates hypertrophy, restrains Runx2 and beta-catenin, and activates Col10a1 with Mef2c.
Sox9-null cells are excluded from cartilage condensations in mouse chimaeras.

sox_trio.name: SOX trio (SOX9-SOX5-SOX6)
sox_trio.summary: The 'SOX trio' is the functional unit of SOX9 plus the two SoxD proteins SOX5 and SOX6. SOX9 provides the transactivation domain and is required for SOX5 and SOX6 expression (Akiyama 2002, mouse); SOX5 and SOX6 lack transactivation domains and act as potent, mutually redundant enhancers of SOX9-driven matrix gene transcription (Smits 2001, mouse). The trio's collective output is what defines the chondrocyte: loss of SOX9 removes the lineage, whereas loss of both SoxD factors leaves cells that are still nominal chondroblasts but produce almost no matrix and initiate proliferation only after a long delay. The asymmetry matters for the atlas: SOX9 is the identity switch, SOX5/SOX6 are the gain. The trio also sets metabolic state - SOX9 drives glutamine uptake and GLS1, and the resulting acetyl-CoA is needed for the histone acetylation that keeps chondrogenic genes on (Stegen 2020) - so this is a transcription-metabolism feedforward loop, not a linear regulon. Human data exist for SOX9 only.
sox_trio.human_evidence_note: Only the SOX9 member has direct human evidence (campomelic dysplasia); the trio as a unit has never been assayed in human tissue.
sox_trio.translation_risk_reason: Hierarchy is mouse-derived; human evidence covers one of the three members.
localization: mouse cartilage: co-expression and hierarchy established (akiyama2002, smits2001)
human growth plate: SOX9 inferred from campomelic dysplasia; SOX5/SOX6 unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Sox9 acts at successive differentiation steps and is required for Sox5 and Sox6 expression.
Sox5 and Sox6 are redundant potent enhancers of chondroblast function.
SOX9 raises glutamine consumption and GLS1, and the resulting acetyl-CoA maintains chondrogenic histone acetylation.

sprouty2.name: SPRY2
sprouty2.summary:
SPRY2 is an intracellular feedback antagonist induced by receptor tyrosine kinase signalling that
damps RAS-ERK output, and in the skeleton it therefore sets the gain of the FGF arm rather than
carrying signal. Sprouty2 loss in mice disturbs endochondral bone formation through combined
modulation of RTK and BMP signalling (Joo 2016), and combined Sprouty2/4 deficiency produces a
ciliopathic skeletal phenotype with upregulated Hedgehog signalling and disrupted early limb
signalling centres (Hruba 2021; Dalecka 2025). That Sprouty loss reads out as a Hedgehog phenotype is
the interesting part: it makes SPRY2 a node where the FGF and Hedgehog arms of this layer meet
through the primary cilium. No human SPRY2 skeletal dysplasia is known and no growth plate zonal
expression map exists in any species.
sprouty2.human_evidence_note: No human SPRY2 skeletal phenotype has been reported.
sprouty2.translation_risk_reason: Mouse knockout only; no human genetic or tissue evidence.
localization: mouse limb bud and growth plate: functionally confirmed by knockout (joo2016, hruba2021)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Sprouty2 regulates endochondral bone formation by modulating RTK and BMP signalling.
Sprouty2/4 loss produces a ciliopathic skeletal phenotype with upregulated Hedgehog signalling.
Sprouty2/4 deficiency disrupts early limb signalling centres and chondrogenesis.

sufu_protein.name: SUFU
sufu_protein.summary:
SUFU binds GLI proteins in the cytoplasm, restrains their activator function and is required for
efficient GLI3 processing to repressor. In cartilage SUFU is a brake on Hedgehog output:
chondrocyte-specific Sufu deletion in mice derepresses Hedgehog signalling and destroys the
epiphyseal growth plate and secondary ossification centre (Xiu 2022). This is the reciprocal of the
Ihh-null phenotype and shows that growth plate architecture requires Hedgehog activity to be held
within a band rather than simply present. Human SUFU germline mutations predispose to
medulloblastoma and basal cell carcinoma; no growth plate phenotype has been characterised in human
SUFU carriers.
sufu_protein.human_evidence_note: Human SUFU carriers are described for tumour predisposition; no growth plate histology reported.
sufu_protein.translation_risk_reason: Single-species conditional knockout evidence with no human skeletal readout.
localization: mouse growth plate chondrocytes: functionally confirmed by conditional deletion (xiu2022)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chondrocyte Sufu deletion derepresses Hedgehog and destroys the epiphyseal growth plate.

tgfb_signaling_chondrocyte.name: TGF-beta signalling in chondrocytes
tgfb_signaling_chondrocyte.summary: TGF-beta1/2/3 signal through TGFBR2-TGFBR1 to SMAD2/3 and, non-canonically, to TAK1-p38. In the growth plate the canonical arm restrains terminal differentiation: blocking it either at the receptor (dominant-negative TGFBR2, Serra 1997) or at the effector (Smad3-null, Yang 2001) accelerates hypertrophy and causes premature cartilage degeneration in mouse. This is the opposite sign to the BMP-SMAD1/5/8 arm, which promotes proliferation and, through beta-catenin/BMP2, maturation. Human evidence is indirect but unusually informative because it is dose-signed in both directions: gain-of-function TGFB1 mutations that release the latent complex cause Camurati-Engelmann disease with diaphyseal hyperostosis and limb pain (Kinoshita 2000), while LTBP3 loss of function - which impairs storage and presentation of latent TGF-beta - causes brachyolmia with short stature (Huckert 2015). The physiological ligand concentration seen by a human growth plate chondrocyte has never been measured.
tgfb_signaling_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: Human TGFB1 gain-of-function (Camurati-Engelmann) and LTBP3 loss-of-function (brachyolmia) phenotypes bracket the pathway in both directions, but neither is a growth-plate measurement.
tgfb_signaling_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism is mouse; human data are germline variants with systemic effects and no physeal read-out.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: inferred (yang2001, serra1997)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Truncated kinase-dead TGFBR2 in mouse skeleton promotes terminal chondrocyte differentiation and osteoarthritis.
TGF-beta/Smad3 signalling represses chondrocyte hypertrophic differentiation in mouse.
Domain-specific TGFB1 mutations that destabilise the latency complex cause human Camurati-Engelmann disease.
LTBP3 loss-of-function mutations cause human brachyolmia with short stature and amelogenesis imperfecta.

tgfbr2_receptor.name: TGFBR2
tgfbr2_receptor.summary: TGFBR2 is the ligand-binding serine/threonine kinase receptor that recruits and transphosphorylates TGFBR1, which then phosphorylates SMAD2/3. Expression of a truncated kinase-defective TGFBR2 in mouse skeletal tissue under the Col2a1 promoter produces progressive terminal chondrocyte differentiation, loss of the articular surface and osteoarthritis-like change, establishing TGFBR2 output as a brake on chondrocyte maturation (Serra 1997). In human, heterozygous TGFBR2 missense mutations cause Loeys-Dietz syndrome, whose skeletal features (arachnodactyly, scoliosis, joint laxity, craniosynostosis) are consistent with altered cartilage and connective tissue TGF-beta signalling, but the human phenotype is dominated by aortic disease and no growth plate specimen has been assayed. TGFBR2 activity in the physis is thus mouse-established and human-inferred.
tgfbr2_receptor.human_evidence_note: Human TGFBR2 variants cause Loeys-Dietz syndrome with skeletal features; no human growth plate receptor data.
tgfbr2_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype is systemic connective tissue disease; the physeal contribution is not separable.
localization: mouse growth plate cartilage: transgene-based inference (serra1997)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Dominant-negative TGFBR2 in mouse cartilage causes terminal chondrocyte differentiation and osteoarthritis.
The Smad3-null phenotype phenocopies receptor blockade, placing SMAD3 downstream of TGFBR2 in cartilage.

tsc1_tsc2.name: TSC1-TSC2 complex
tsc1_tsc2.summary: TSC1-TSC2 is the GTPase-activating complex that holds RHEB in its GDP-bound state and therefore keeps mTORC1 off; growth-factor signalling through AKT and ERK inactivates it. Chondrocyte-restricted Tsc1 deletion in mouse - the constitutive mTORC1-on experiment - gives a zone-specific result: the cranial base synchondroses EXPAND, and the expansion is entirely in the resting zone and is due to increased cell number and cell size with no change in proliferation rate. Critically, the same study shows that in wild-type mice mTORC1 activity is INHIBITED in resting and proliferating zone chondrocytes, and that Tsc1 deletion switches it on there; the resulting resting-zone cells acquire prehypertrophic characteristics (large size, high PTH1R and IHH), and rapamycin rescues the phenotype (Hsieh 2021, mouse). This makes TSC1-TSC2 the enforcer of the low-mTORC1 state that defines the resting zone, and identifies mTORC1 activation as one of the events that converts a resting chondrocyte into a prehypertrophic one. The converse loss-of-mTORC1 experiments (Raptor/mTor deletion) reduce chondrocyte size and matrix output (Chen and Long 2014). Human TSC1/TSC2 loss of function causes tuberous sclerosis complex with sclerotic bone lesions but no characteristic stature phenotype, and no human growth plate has been assayed for mTORC1 activity by zone.
tsc1_tsc2.human_evidence_note: Human TSC1/TSC2 loss causes tuberous sclerosis complex without an established growth plate phenotype; no physeal measurement exists.
tsc1_tsc2.translation_risk_reason: The decisive experiment is in mouse cranial base synchondroses, not a long-bone physis, and human TSC patients have no described growth plate phenotype.
localization: mouse RZ and PZ: mTORC1 activity normally low, i.e. TSC1-TSC2 active (hsieh2021)
mouse synchondrosis RZ: Tsc1 deletion activates mTORC1 and expands the zone (hsieh2021)
human growth plate: zonal mTORC1 activity unmeasured

key_refs.one_line_finding: mTORC1 is normally inhibited in resting/proliferating chondrocytes; chondrocyte Tsc1 deletion activates it, expands the resting zone and confers prehypertrophic features, rescued by rapamycin.
Loss of mTORC1 output in cartilage reduces chondrocyte size and matrix, the phenotype TSC1 loss inverts.
Rheb1, the direct target of TSC1-TSC2 GAP activity, is required for limb growth via growth plate chondrogenesis.

vangl2_pcp.name: VANGL2
vangl2_pcp.summary: VANGL2 is a four-pass transmembrane core PCP protein that becomes asymmetrically localised across a polarised cell. In the limb, WNT5A signalling through ROR2 phosphorylates VANGL2 at conserved N-terminal serine/threonine residues, and the amount of phosphorylation is proportional to WNT5A concentration; the Looptail (Vangl2 Lp) allele is phosphorylation-deficient and acts as a dominant negative (Gao 2011, mouse). This makes VANGL2 the molecular ruler that converts a diffusible WNT5A gradient into a directional instruction for chondrocyte stacking. Direct growth-plate-restricted conditional Vangl2 genetics with a columnar-organisation read-out are sparse, and no human VANGL2 skeletal dysplasia is established (human VANGL2 variants are associated with neural tube defects). This node is therefore mechanistically strong in mouse limb and empty in human physis.
vangl2_pcp.human_evidence_note: Human VANGL2 variants are linked to neural tube defects, not to a growth plate phenotype.
vangl2_pcp.translation_risk_reason: Mouse limb genetics only; no human skeletal phenotype anchors the node.
localization: mouse limb mesenchyme: confirmed, phosphorylation graded along the WNT5A axis (gao2011)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Graded ROR2-dependent VANGL2 phosphorylation encodes position within a WNT5A gradient in the mouse limb.
Non-canonical Frizzled signalling, the pathway VANGL2 serves, controls chondrocyte column formation.

vegfa_growth_plate.name: VEGFA in the growth plate
vegfa_growth_plate.summary: VEGFA couples the hypertrophic chondrocyte to the vasculature that will replace it. Sequestering VEGF with a soluble receptor chimera in growing mice suppresses blood vessel invasion of the hypertrophic cartilage, expands the hypertrophic zone, impairs trabecular bone formation and is reversible on withdrawal - a pharmacological, dose-reversible demonstration that vascular invasion is VEGF-gated (Gerber 1999, mouse). Genetically, Col2a1-Cre deletion of Vegfa delays vessel invasion of the primary ossification centre and delays removal of terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes, but it also causes massive death of epiphyseal and joint chondrocytes far from any vessel, indicating a direct chondrocyte-survival role and not only an angiogenic one (Zelzer 2004, mouse). The cell-death pattern closely resembles the Hif1a-null pattern and HIF1A-null epiphyseal chondrocytes make less VEGFA, placing HIF1A-VEGFA on one survival axis - though Schipani 2001 also documents HIF1A-independent VEGF induction around dying cells. Perichondrial Vegfa additionally controls perichondrial vascularity and osteoblast differentiation (Duan 2015, mouse). No human growth plate VEGFA measurement is available.
vegfa_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate VEGFA data; anti-VEGF therapeutics are not used in growing children in a way that yields physeal read-outs.
vegfa_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: Mouse pharmacology and conditional genetics; human physeal vascular biology is undescribed at this level.
localization: mouse HZ: confirmed - VEGFA from hypertrophic chondrocytes drives vessel invasion (gerber1999)
mouse epiphyseal/joint chondrocytes: VEGFA required for survival (zelzer2004)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: VEGF sequestration in growing mice blocks hypertrophic cartilage vascular invasion and expands the hypertrophic zone, reversibly.
Chondrocyte Vegfa deletion delays vascular invasion and causes massive epiphyseal chondrocyte death, phenocopying Hif1a loss.
Vegfa regulates perichondrial vascularity and osteoblast differentiation in mouse bone development.

vhl_protein.name: VHL
vhl_protein.summary: pVHL is the substrate-recognition component of the E3 ubiquitin ligase that destroys hydroxylated HIF alpha subunits; it is the oxygen-off switch of the pathway. Cartilage-wide conditional inactivation of Vhlh in mouse produces viable but severely dwarfed animals with a reduced chondrocyte proliferation rate, increased extracellular matrix and atypical enlarged cells in the resting zone, and HIF1A target genes are elevated as expected (Pfander 2004). The epistasis is explicit: newborns lacking both Vhlh and Hif1a in chondrocytes look essentially like Hif1a single nulls, so most of the Vhlh phenotype is accumulated HIF1A activity. This is the loss-of-brake counterpart to the Hif1a knockout and together they bracket the pathway in mouse. In human, germline VHL mutations cause von Hippel-Lindau disease (and the Chuvash R200W allele causes congenital polycythaemia) with no reported growth plate phenotype, so no human physeal evidence anchors this node.
vhl_protein.human_evidence_note: Human VHL disease has no described growth plate phenotype; no human physeal VHL measurement exists.
vhl_protein.translation_risk_reason: Mouse conditional genetics only; the human VHL phenotype is tumour-predisposition and erythropoietic.
localization: mouse growth plate, all zones (Col2-driven deletion): confirmed functionally (pfander2004)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Cartilage Vhlh deletion causes mouse dwarfism with reduced proliferation and increased matrix, epistatically upstream of HIF1A.
Defines the HIF1A-dependent survival/arrest programme that VHL loss constitutively activates.

wnt5a_ligand.name: WNT5A
wnt5a_ligand.summary: WNT5A is the principal non-canonical WNT ligand of the growth plate. In mouse it is expressed in a graded fashion across developing limb elements and acts through ROR2 to phosphorylate VANGL2, with the degree of phosphorylation reporting position in the gradient (Gao 2011). Functionally, Wnt5a and its paralogue Wnt5b have opposite effects on where the proliferative-to-hypertrophic transition occurs: Wnt5a delays and Wnt5b promotes the transition in mouse, so they are not interchangeable despite high sequence similarity (Yang 2003). In human, dominant and recessive WNT5A mutations cause Robinow syndrome, whose cardinal skeletal feature is mesomelic limb shortening with normal-length axial skeleton - a segment-selective growth failure consistent with a positional rather than a rate-limiting role. No human growth plate WNT5A protein gradient has been measured.
wnt5a_ligand.human_evidence_note: WNT5A mutations cause human Robinow syndrome with mesomelic shortening; no human growth plate expression or gradient data.
wnt5a_ligand.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism is mouse; the human phenotype is developmental patterning and cannot be assigned to a growth plate zone.
localization: mouse limb mesenchyme, graded: confirmed (gao2011)
mouse growth plate: reported (yang2003)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: WNT5A gradients establish planar cell polarity by inducing ROR2-dependent VANGL2 phosphorylation.
Wnt5a and Wnt5b exert distinct and partly opposing effects on the chondrocyte hypertrophy transition.

wnt_canonical_chondrocyte.name: Canonical WNT/beta-catenin signalling in chondrocytes
wnt_canonical_chondrocyte.summary: Canonical WNT signalling stabilises beta-catenin, which enters the nucleus and converts TCF/LEF from repressors into activators. In cartilage the pathway is dose-dependent with opposite phenotypes at the two extremes, and this is established by paired gain- and loss-of-function alleles in the same mouse genetic background. Too little: Col2a1-Cre inactivation of Ctnnb1 gives dwarfism with reduced chondrocyte proliferation and delayed hypertrophic differentiation (Akiyama 2004), and Col2a1-ICAT transgenic mice - normal size at birth, then progressively runted - have narrower proliferative and hypertrophic zones, more apoptosis and delayed secondary ossification centre formation (Chen 2008). Too much: chondrocyte-restricted beta-catenin stabilisation causes severe chondrodysplasia phenocopying Sox9 inactivation (Akiyama 2004), tamoxifen-induced stabilisation accelerates maturation and drives ectopic ossification centres (Dao 2012), and transient activation in young adult mice causes growth retardation with premature growth plate closure and articular cartilage thickening (Yuasa 2009). At the progenitor stage the sign flips again: beta-catenin is required for osteoblast fate, and osteoblast precursors lacking it become chondrocytes instead (Hill 2005, Day 2005). No dose-response curve has been measured in human chondrocytes.
wnt_canonical_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is confined to WNT co-receptor genetics (LRP5 OPPG and high-bone-mass alleles) and SOST; no human growth plate has been assayed for canonical WNT activity.
wnt_canonical_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Every dose statement comes from mouse conditional alleles; the human physiological range of chondrocyte beta-catenin activity is unknown, and mice do not undergo epiphyseal fusion.
localization: mouse PHZ/HZ: highest canonical activity inferred from reporter and genetic studies (dao2012, guo2009)
mouse PZ: lower activity; loss-of-function reduces proliferation (akiyama2004, chen2008)
human growth plate: unconfirmed - no zonal nuclear beta-catenin or TCF-reporter data

key_refs.one_line_finding: beta-catenin inactivation and Sox9 overexpression give the same dwarfism; beta-catenin stabilisation and Sox9 loss give the same chondrodysplasia.
Col2a1-ICAT mice (reduced chondrocyte beta-catenin) are progressively runted with narrowed PZ and HZ and delayed SOC.
Inducible cartilage-specific beta-catenin gain of function promotes maturation and primary/secondary ossification centre formation.
Transient Wnt/beta-catenin activation in young adult mouse cartilage causes growth retardation and abnormal growth plate closure.
Wnt/beta-catenin initiates hypertrophy by inhibiting PTHrP signalling activity, and controls final maturation PTHrP-independently.
Osteoblast precursors lacking beta-catenin become chondrocytes, so high canonical WNT blocks chondrogenesis at the progenitor stage.

wnt_noncanonical_pcp.name: Non-canonical WNT / planar cell polarity in the growth plate
wnt_noncanonical_pcp.summary: Column formation requires that daughter chondrocytes rotate and intercalate into a single file aligned with the long axis; this is a planar-cell-polarity process, not a proliferation process. In mouse, non-canonical Frizzled signalling controls chondrocyte polarity: manipulating Fzd/Wnt5a signalling disrupts the stereotyped rotation that follows division and produces disorganised, non-columnar clones without necessarily changing proliferation rate (Li and Dudley 2009). WNT5A acts as a graded cue: it induces ROR2-dependent phosphorylation of VANGL2, and the level of VANGL2 phosphorylation encodes the position of a cell within a WNT5A gradient, converting a diffusible signal into a vector (Gao 2011, mouse). Wnt5a and Wnt5b have distinct, non-interchangeable effects on the proliferation-to-hypertrophy transition (Yang 2003, mouse). This subsystem explains the columnar architecture that L1 describes, and it is the arm of WNT signalling least studied in human tissue - no human growth plate has been assayed for PCP protein asymmetry.
wnt_noncanonical_pcp.human_evidence_note: Human WNT5A and ROR2 mutations cause Robinow syndrome with limb shortening, but no human growth plate PCP measurement exists.
wnt_noncanonical_pcp.translation_risk_reason: Mouse genetics and explant imaging; the human columnar organisation is described morphologically but never mechanistically.
localization: mouse PZ: confirmed - polarity and rotation defects on Fzd/Wnt5a perturbation (li2009)
human PZ: unconfirmed - no PCP protein asymmetry data in human growth plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: Non-canonical Frizzled signalling controls the post-mitotic rotation that builds chondrocyte columns in mouse.
A WNT5A gradient induces graded ROR2-dependent VANGL2 phosphorylation, converting concentration into polarity.
Wnt5a and Wnt5b have distinct activities in coordinating chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation.

zfp521_protein.name: ZFP521 (ZNF521)
zfp521_protein.summary: ZFP521 is a zinc-finger transcriptional coregulator that PTHrP induces in prehypertrophic chondrocytes and that executes part of the PTHrP anti-hypertrophy programme. Chondrocyte-targeted Zfp521 deletion in mouse phenocopies PTHrP-null and chondrocyte PTH1R-null animals: reduced proliferation, early hypertrophic transition and a thinner growth plate. Mechanistically ZFP521 associates with RUNX2 and antagonises it by an HDAC4-dependent mechanism; without ZFP521, Runx2 and its target genes rise while cyclin D1 and BCL2 fall and caspase-3 activation and apoptosis increase, and PTHrP can no longer upregulate cyclin D1 or suppress Runx2, Ihh and Col10a1 (Correa 2010, mouse). ZFP521 therefore sits in the same RUNX2-restraining module as HDAC4 and provides an independent route by which PTHrP holds the hypertrophy switch off. No human ZNF521 skeletal phenotype has been established and there is no human growth plate measurement.
zfp521_protein.human_evidence_note: No human ZNF521 skeletal phenotype or growth plate data.
zfp521_protein.translation_risk_reason: Single-laboratory mouse conditional knockout with no human correlate.
localization: mouse PHZ: induced by PTHrP in prehypertrophic chondrocytes (correa2010)
human growth plate: unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Zfp521 is a PTHrP target that antagonises RUNX2 via an HDAC4-dependent mechanism; its deletion phenocopies PTHrP loss in mouse.

adrenarche.name: Adrenarche
adrenarche.summary: Adrenarche is the maturation of the adrenal zona reticularis from roughly age 6-8 years, producing a rise in DHEA, DHEAS and androstenedione that is independent of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and of gonadarche. It is a primate-restricted phenomenon - rodents have no zona reticularis and no adrenarche - which is the single most important constraint on animal modelling of this node. Its statural effect is a modest acceleration of growth and bone maturation. The clinically informative version is premature adrenarche, where advanced bone age might be expected to cost adult height but does not: in a cohort of children with premature adrenarche, predicted adult height remained normal despite advanced bone age (kanniainen2025). Adrenarche is therefore a case where growth acceleration and skeletal maturation advance together and largely cancel, unlike central precocious puberty where estrogen tips the balance toward early fusion.
adrenarche.human_evidence_note: Adrenarche is defined and quantified in human cohorts by serum DHEAS trajectories and bone age; premature adrenarche cohorts provide the growth outcome data.
adrenarche.translation_risk_reason: Adrenarche does not occur in rodents; only humans and some other primates have a zona reticularis that matures in this way, so there is nothing to translate.
localization: human SYS: adrenal zona reticularis -> serum DHEAS
growth plate: no established direct adrenal androgen action distinguishable from aromatisation

key_refs.one_line_finding: Predicted adult height remained normal in children with premature adrenarche despite advanced bone age.

als_igfals.name: Acid-labile subunit (ALS / IGFALS)
als_igfals.summary: ALS is an 85 kDa leucine-rich-repeat glycoprotein made by hepatocytes under GH-STAT5B control. It binds preformed IGF/IGFBP-3 or IGF/IGFBP-5 binary complexes to make the 150 kDa ternary complex, which cannot cross the capillary endothelium and so converts a paracrine growth factor into a long-lived circulating reservoir. Human IGFALS inactivation is the sharpest available test of whether the reservoir matters: it collapses circulating IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 to values seen in severe GH deficiency, yet the height deficit is comparatively modest and often only 1-2 SDS (domen2004, domen2009). This dissociation between circulating IGF-1 and stature is a direct human argument against the strong somatomedin hypothesis, and it is stronger evidence than the mouse LID experiment because it is a human null. Igfals-null mice likewise show only mild, sex-dependent reductions in body size and bone slenderness (courtland2010), but ALS knockout combined with liver Igf1 deletion does reduce growth plate height (yakar2002), locating the threshold below the single-gene nulls.
als_igfals.human_evidence_note: Homozygous human IGFALS inactivation has been characterised in multiple kindreds with near-absent circulating IGF-1/IGFBP-3 and disproportionately mild short stature.
als_igfals.translation_risk_reason: The key experiment is a human null allele; mouse data are concordant.
localization: human SYS: hepatocyte-secreted, serum
growth plate: ALS not present locally; its effect is on delivery, not on the plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: First human IGFALS inactivating mutation: near-absent circulating IGF-I and IGFBP-3 with only mild short stature.
Human ALS deficiency series: profound biochemical IGF-1 deficiency with modest height deficit.
Igfals-null mice show sex-specific reductions in body size and bone slenderness.
ALSKO alone reduces serum IGF-1 by 65% with near-normal growth; combined with LID it drops growth plate height.

androgen_receptor.name: Androgen receptor (AR)
androgen_receptor.summary: AR is the nuclear receptor for testosterone and DHT. It is present in the growth plate: AR protein was localised immunohistochemically in human bone including chondrocytes and osteoblasts (abu1997), and in rat tibial growth plate and metaphyseal bone with sex differences in abundance (van2002). The functional consequence at the plate, however, is unproven. In cultured fetal rat metatarsals - a system that reads out longitudinal growth directly - neither AR agonists nor antagonists changed growth (chagin2009). Human complete androgen insensitivity syndrome (46,XY with non-functional AR) is informative and cuts the same way: affected individuals are taller than average females, with growth and epiphyseal fusion tracking their aromatised estrogen exposure rather than their absent androgen signalling. AR is therefore best described as expressed but not demonstrated to be required for longitudinal growth, with androgen's growth effect running predominantly through aromatisation to estradiol.
androgen_receptor.human_evidence_note: Human complete androgen insensitivity provides a natural AR-null experiment in which stature and fusion are not androgen-dependent, but no human study measures AR function within the plate.
androgen_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Localisation exists in human tissue; the functional test is rat organ culture with a null result.
localization: human bone and growth plate: AR protein detected by immunohistochemistry (abu1997)
rat tibial growth plate: AR protein present, sex-different (van2002)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Androgen receptors localised in human bone including growth plate chondrocytes.
Sex differences in androgen receptor expression in rat tibial growth plate.
AR modulation did not change longitudinal growth in fetal rat metatarsal culture.

aromatase_cyp19a1.name: Aromatase (CYP19A1)
aromatase_cyp19a1.summary: Aromatase is the cytochrome P450 that converts androstenedione to estrone and testosterone to estradiol, the committed and rate-limiting step of estrogen synthesis. Its importance for the skeleton is that it makes estrogen a locally producible hormone: aromatase is expressed in adipose, bone and gonad, and in boys the great majority of circulating estradiol is aromatised from testosterone rather than secreted. This is why androgen and estrogen effects on the growth plate are hard to separate pharmacologically and why aromatase inhibitors are used clinically to delay fusion and increase predicted adult height. Aromatase activity has been reported in growth plate tissue and is regulated there - leptin stimulates aromatase in the growth plate, which has been proposed to limit the efficiency of catch-up growth. The human loss-of-function experiments (CYP19A1 deficiency with continued growth and unfused epiphyses) are covered in L7 and are not duplicated here; what belongs to L4 is that aromatase places the estrogen dose-response of estrogen_biphasic_dose_effect under partly local, partly adipose-mass-dependent control.
aromatase_cyp19a1.human_evidence_note: Human CYP19A1 loss of function and aromatase excess syndrome both alter epiphyseal fusion timing, and aromatase inhibitors change predicted adult height in randomised paediatric studies; the case series themselves are held in L7.
aromatase_cyp19a1.translation_risk_reason: The enzyme's role in human skeletal maturation is established by human genetics and human pharmacology; only the local physeal expression data are rodent.
localization: human SYS: adipose, gonad, bone, placenta
growth plate: aromatase expression reported in rodent physis; human physeal aromatase not quantified

key_refs.one_line_finding: In boys, growth velocity tracks aromatised estradiol at EC50 6.5 pmol/L alongside testosterone EC50 3.1 nmol/L.
Male serum estradiol - almost entirely aromatase-derived - rises from <4 to 32 pmol/L across puberty.

calcium_homeostasis.name: Calcium homeostasis
calcium_homeostasis.summary: Extracellular ionised calcium is held within a few percent by a fast loop (CASR on parathyroid cells sets PTH secretion within minutes) and a slow loop (PTH-driven renal CYP27B1 raises calcitriol and hence intestinal absorption over hours to days). For the growth plate, calcium matters chiefly as the cation of hydroxyapatite at the zone of provisional calcification, and severe hypocalcaemia produces rickets. Its role is however subordinate to phosphate in the specific mechanism of rachitic growth plate expansion: in mouse models that separate the variables, it is phosphate, not calcium or PTH, whose normalisation restores caspase-9-mediated hypertrophic chondrocyte apoptosis and prevents the expanded hypertrophic layer (sabbagh2005). Dietary calcium intake influences childhood growth in populations with low intake, but the effect size in well-nourished populations is small.
calcium_homeostasis.human_evidence_note: Human nutritional rickets, hypoparathyroidism and calcium supplementation trials give direct human evidence at the level of growth plate radiography and growth velocity.
calcium_homeostasis.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical data are primary; mouse work only apportions calcium versus phosphate.
localization: human SYS: serum ionised calcium
growth plate ZPC: calcium is the mineral cation deposited; local ionic activity not measured in human physis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Phosphate rather than calcium or PTH is the proximate determinant of hypertrophic chondrocyte apoptosis and rachitic change.

circadian_growth_regulation.name: Circadian regulation of growth
circadian_growth_regulation.summary: Longitudinal growth in humans has diurnal structure at two levels that are usually conflated. The first is systemic and well evidenced: the GH axis is strongly nycthemeral, with the dominant secretory burst after sleep onset and measurable 24-h rhythmicity in the deconvolved profile (van2016, calvert2022). Feeding pattern entrains this rhythm through ghrelin, and flattening the rhythm by continuous enteral feeding in humans produces continuously elevated GH with minimal ultradian structure (hornsby2025). The second level - a cell-autonomous circadian oscillator inside growth plate chondrocytes gating proliferation or matrix output - is asserted in reviews, but the primary cartilage-clock literature is dominated by articular and temporomandibular cartilage in osteoarthritis models, not by the physis. No study has demonstrated a functioning BMAL1/PER oscillator in human growth plate chondrocytes or shown that disrupting it changes longitudinal bone growth.
circadian_growth_regulation.human_evidence_note: Human evidence covers the systemic GH rhythm and the effect of feeding pattern on it; there is no human growth plate clock measurement.
circadian_growth_regulation.translation_risk_reason: The frequently repeated claim that a chondrocyte-intrinsic clock times growth rests on articular/TMJ cartilage rodent models - a different tissue in a disease context.
localization: human SYS: GH axis rhythm confirmed
human growth plate: intrinsic circadian oscillator unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: 24-h deconvolution establishes the nycthemeral structure of human GH secretion.
Feeding pattern entrains GH rhythmicity via ghrelin in rodents and humans.
GH bursts cluster with slow-wave sleep in pubertal children.

dheas_hormone.name: DHEAS (dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate)
dheas_hormone.summary: DHEAS is the sulfated, long-half-life circulating form of DHEA, produced by SULT2A1 in the adrenal zona reticularis. Because its half-life is hours rather than minutes and it lacks diurnal variation, DHEAS is the standard biochemical marker of adrenarche. DHEAS itself is essentially inactive at the androgen receptor; it is a reservoir that peripheral steroid sulfatase and 3beta-HSD convert to active androgens and, by aromatisation, to estrogens. Its growth relevance is as a quantitative index of the adrenarchal androgen supply rather than as a direct effector, and childhood DHEAS concentration prospectively predicts more advanced pubertal development several years later. Children with premature adrenarche have raised DHEAS and advanced bone age but preserved predicted adult height (kanniainen2025).
dheas_hormone.human_evidence_note: DHEAS is measured directly in human cohorts and prospectively associates with pubertal timing and bone age advance.
dheas_hormone.translation_risk_reason: Rodents do not produce adrenal DHEAS in the human pattern.
localization: human SYS: adrenal zona reticularis -> serum
growth plate: DHEAS not shown to act directly on chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Premature adrenarche with raised DHEAS advanced bone age without compromising predicted adult height.

dihydrotestosterone.name: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT)
dihydrotestosterone.summary: DHT is the 5alpha-reduced, non-aromatisable androgen with roughly 5-10 fold higher androgen receptor affinity than testosterone. Precisely because it cannot be aromatised, DHT is the reagent that tests whether androgens act on the growth plate directly. The evidence says largely not: androgen receptor modulation had no effect on longitudinal growth of cultured fetal rat metatarsal bones (chagin2009), and human 5alpha-reductase type 2 deficiency, in which DHT is absent from fetal life, is not characterised by short stature. What DHT does have is documented sex-specific, receptor-dependent effects on growth plate chondrocytes in vitro that require membrane-localised receptors, and an interaction with 1,25(OH)2D3 in epiphyseal chondrocyte cultures. The reasonable summary is that DHT modulates chondrocyte behaviour in culture without a demonstrated effect on longitudinal growth in vivo.
dihydrotestosterone.human_evidence_note: No human experiment isolates DHT's growth plate effect; 5alpha-reductase deficiency does not produce short stature, which is a weak human negative.
dihydrotestosterone.translation_risk_reason: All positive findings are in vitro rodent chondrocyte cultures.
localization: rat growth plate: androgen receptor expressed with sex differences in level (van2002)
human bone: androgen receptor localised immunohistochemically (abu1997)
human growth plate: DHT effect not tested

key_refs.one_line_finding: Androgen receptor modulation did not affect longitudinal growth of cultured fetal rat metatarsals.
Androgen receptor is expressed in rat tibial growth plate with sex differences in abundance.

dio2_deiodinase.name: Type 2 deiodinase (DIO2)
dio2_deiodinase.summary: DIO2 is an endoplasmic-reticulum selenoenzyme that removes an outer-ring iodine from T4 to generate T3, providing intracellular T3 locally rather than from the circulation. Its substrate-induced ubiquitination gives it a short half-life and makes local T3 production self-limiting when T4 rises. In the skeleton DIO2 is the enzyme that would allow a chondrocyte to set its own T3 exposure independently of serum T4, and DIO2 activity has been demonstrated in bone. Its developmental importance is inferred largely from the complementary observation that DIO3 inactivation dominates early fetal skeleton, minimising T3 signalling until the appropriate stage. The specific quantitative claim that most growth plate T3 is locally generated by DIO2 rather than imported is widely repeated but, as far as can be established, has not been measured with zonal resolution in any species and certainly not in human physis.
dio2_deiodinase.human_evidence_note: No human DIO2 loss-of-function growth phenotype; the common DIO2 Thr92Ala polymorphism has been studied for metabolic rather than statural endpoints.
dio2_deiodinase.translation_risk_reason: Local deiodinase control of skeletal T3 is a rodent-derived model with no human physeal measurement; the field states it more confidently than the data support.
localization: human growth plate: DIO2 protein/activity not measured by zone
rodent bone: iodothyronine deiodinase activity demonstrated in bone tissue

key_refs.one_line_finding: Establishes the receptor-bearing target zones on which any locally generated T3 would have to act.

The Hedgehog-inducible ubiquitin ligase subunit WSB-1 targets DIO2 for degradation in the developing growth plate, modulating local thyroid hormone activation and PTHrP secretion - primary evidence that DIO2 specifically is the locally regulated activating deiodinase in this tissue and is wired into the Ihh/PTHrP loop.

Iodothyronine deiodinase type 2 is differentially expressed in growth plates of chickens divergently selected for tibial dyschondroplasia - a species-limited but direct DIO2 growth plate expression measurement.

dio3_deiodinase.name: Type 3 deiodinase (DIO3)
dio3_deiodinase.summary: DIO3 is the inactivating selenodeiodinase: it removes an inner-ring iodine to convert T4 to reverse T3 and T3 to 3,3'-T2, both receptor-inactive. It is an imprinted, paternally expressed gene in the DLK1-DIO3 locus on chromosome 14q32 - the same imprinted domain that contains DLK1, whose paternal deletion causes central precocious puberty. DIO3 is highly expressed in fetal tissues and placenta, where its function is to shield developing tissue from premature T3 exposure; deiodinase-mediated inactivation has been shown to minimise thyroid hormone signalling in the early fetal skeleton. The growth plate consequence is a developmental gate: hypertrophic differentiation cannot be driven by T3 before DIO3 falls. Whether DIO3 is expressed with zonal specificity in the postnatal human growth plate has not been reported.
dio3_deiodinase.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is genomic - DIO3 sits in the imprinted 14q32 DLK1-DIO3 domain whose disruption (Temple syndrome, paternal DLK1 deletion) alters growth and pubertal timing - not direct enzyme measurement in human physis.
dio3_deiodinase.translation_risk_reason: Enzyme-level data are fetal rodent; the human link is genomic co-location and imprinting.
localization: fetal rodent skeleton: DIO3-mediated inactivation limits early T3 signalling
human growth plate: DIO3 expression not reported by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Paternally inherited deletion in the imprinted DLK1-DIO3 domain causes familial central precocious puberty.

dlk1_gene.name: DLK1
dlk1_gene.summary: DLK1 is a paternally expressed imprinted gene in the 14q32 DLK1-DIO3 domain encoding a transmembrane EGF-repeat protein that acts as a non-canonical NOTCH inhibitor and is shed as a soluble fragment. Paternally inherited DLK1 deletion causes familial central precocious puberty (dauber2017), making it the second imprinted puberty brake after MKRN3 and placing two independently imprinted loci in the same functional role. Loss of the whole 14q32 paternal contribution (Temple syndrome) combines precocious puberty with pre- and postnatal growth restriction, so DLK1 dosage affects growth as well as pubertal timing; DLK1 also links reproduction to metabolism, with affected individuals showing increased adiposity and insulin resistance. The same imprinted domain contains DIO3, the thyroid hormone-inactivating deiodinase, which means the L4 thyroid and puberty modules share a genomic control region.
dlk1_gene.human_evidence_note: Paternally inherited DLK1 deletions segregate with central precocious puberty in families, and Temple syndrome provides the broader imprinting phenotype.
dlk1_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human imprinted-locus genetics is the primary evidence.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamus, adrenal, adipose; soluble DLK1 measurable in serum
growth plate: DLK1 expression not established in human physis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Paternally inherited DLK1 deletion causes familial central precocious puberty.

dual_effector_hypothesis.name: Dual effector hypothesis
dual_effector_hypothesis.summary: The dual effector model holds that GH acts on the growth plate in two steps: it first recruits resting/germinal zone chondrocytes into the proliferative pool and simultaneously induces local IGF-1, which then drives clonal expansion of those cells. Its empirical basis is a specific set of rat experiments. Unilateral intra-arterial GH widened the growth plate only on the infused side (isaksson1982), excluding a purely systemic mechanism. GH increased the NUMBER of IGF-1-immunoreactive chondrocytes in the germinal zone (nilsson1986). A somatomedin antiserum abolished the local response to intra-arterial GH, showing the direct effect is IGF-1-mediated rather than IGF-1-independent (schlechter1986). GH multiplied the slowly cycling germinal cells specifically (ohlsson1992), and single-cell enzyme histochemistry confirmed GH raises the number of proliferating chondrocytes without raising the labelling index of cells already in cycle (gevers1996a). The model is therefore not an alternative to IGF-1 action but a relocation of it from liver to plate. Its status in humans is unresolved: no human experiment has separated locally produced from circulating IGF-1 at the plate.
dual_effector_hypothesis.human_evidence_note: The two-step model has never been tested in human tissue; the human GH-insensitivity syndromes cannot distinguish local from systemic IGF-1 because GHR loss removes both.
dual_effector_hypothesis.translation_risk_reason: Every load-bearing experiment is a hypophysectomised or dwarf rat; rat growth plates remain open for life and their GH profile is far more sharply pulsatile than the human one.
localization: rat RZ: GH-induced recruitment into proliferation confirmed (ohlsson1992, gevers1996a)
rat PZ: GH-induced IGF-1 immunoreactivity confirmed (nilsson1986)
human growth plate: local IGF-1 production not quantified

key_refs.one_line_finding: Local GH infusion widened only the ipsilateral growth plate in hypophysectomised rats.
GH raised the number of IGF-1-containing chondrocytes in the germinal zone.
Somatomedin antiserum abolished the local growth response to GH, implicating locally produced IGF-1.
GH increases the number of proliferating chondrocytes rather than their labelling index; pulsatile GH narrows the resting zone.

estradiol_hormone.name: 17beta-estradiol
estradiol_hormone.summary: 17beta-estradiol is the dominant estrogen of puberty in both sexes and the hormone that both drives the pubertal growth spurt and terminates growth. In boys almost all of it is produced by peripheral aromatisation of testosterone rather than by the gonad. Concentrations are extremely low relative to assay sensitivity: with an ultrasensitive extraction RIA (detection limit 4 pmol/L) the 24-h mean in boys rises from below 4 pmol/L prepubertally to 6 pmol/L in early puberty, 8 pmol/L in mid-puberty, 21 pmol/L in late puberty and 32 pmol/L once final height is reached (ankarberglindg2008), which is why routine immunoassays are inadequate for pediatric work. The growth-relevant dose-response has been fitted directly in humans: half-maximal pubertal growth acceleration occurs at a morning estradiol of 20 pmol/L in girls (95% CI 13-31; albin2012) and 6.5 pmol/L in boys (95% CI 3.2-13; albin2013). Above roughly the Tanner B2 range (10-51 pmol/L) less than 25% of potential pubertal growth remains - i.e. the stimulating and terminating actions are separated by well under one order of magnitude in concentration.
estradiol_hormone.human_evidence_note: Human dose-response has been fitted from frequently sampled 24-h estradiol profiles against individually modelled growth curves in both sexes; human aromatase deficiency and ESR1 resistance cases (covered in L7) supply the loss-of-function arm.
estradiol_hormone.translation_risk_reason: The quantitative dose-response cited here is human-only; mice do not fuse their epiphyses, so rodent estradiol dosing cannot be mapped onto this curve.
localization: human SYS: ovarian and peripheral aromatisation; serum
human growth plate: local estradiol concentration never measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: EC50 for half-maximal pubertal growth in girls is 20 pmol/L estradiol (95% CI 13-31).
EC50 for 50% growth velocity increase in boys is estradiol 6.5 pmol/L (95% CI 3.2-13) and testosterone 3.1 nmol/L (2.4-4.2).
Normative 24-h serum estradiol in boys by ultrasensitive extraction RIA: <4 pmol/L prepubertally to 32 pmol/L at final height.

estrogen_biphasic_dose_effect.name: Biphasic dose-dependent estrogen effect on growth
estrogen_biphasic_dose_effect.summary: Estrogen accelerates growth at low concentration and terminates it at high concentration, and the two limbs are separated by less than an order of magnitude. The only direct human dose-response experiment is small and old but decisive: five prepubertal or early pubertal boys received 4-day intravenous estradiol infusions at 4, 20 and 90 ug/day in double-blind randomised order, with three-week ulnar growth velocity measured before and after each and allowed to return to baseline between infusions. Growth velocity rose significantly ONLY at the lowest dose (0.45 +/- 0.11 to 1.38 +/- 0.51 mm/3 weeks, P<0.05, serum estradiol 10 +/- 2.3 pg/mL); the 20 ug/day and 90 ug/day infusions produced smaller, non-significant increments despite serum estradiol of 16 and 96 pg/mL, and somatomedin-C rose only at the two higher doses (carusonicolett1985). The same group had previously described a biphasic ethinyl estradiol dose-response in Turner syndrome. Physiologically, the ascending limb is quantified in healthy children: half-maximal growth acceleration at morning estradiol 20 pmol/L in girls (95% CI 13-31) and 6.5 pmol/L in boys (3.2-13), with under 25% of potential pubertal growth remaining above the Tanner B2 range of 10-51 pmol/L (albin2012, albin2013). Long-term pharmacology matches: in the 149-girl randomised Turner trial, childhood ultra-low-dose ethinyl estradiol (25 ng/kg/day ages 5-8, 50 ng/kg/day ages >8-12) added 0.32 SDS on top of GH but, given alone, produced an adult height WORSE than placebo (-3.39 vs -2.81 SDS) (ross2011, quigley2014). The descending limb's mechanism is senescence acceleration rather than direct ossification: estradiol cypionate 70 ug/kg/week in ovariectomised juvenile rabbits accelerated the decline in growth rate, proliferation, plate height and chondrocyte numbers, and fusion occurred abruptly once proliferation approached zero (weise2001). No single experiment has ever traced a complete dose-response curve spanning both limbs to a linear-growth endpoint in humans.
estrogen_biphasic_dose_effect.human_evidence_note: A double-blind randomised crossover of three intravenous estradiol doses with a direct linear-growth readout (knemometric ulnar growth) exists in humans, though n=5 and short-term; the physiological ascending limb is separately fitted from 24-h profiles and the long-term consequences from randomised Turner trials.
estrogen_biphasic_dose_effect.translation_risk_reason: Human data anchor both limbs but never in one experiment; the cellular mechanism of the descending limb comes from ovariectomised rabbits at a single supraphysiological dose.
localization: rabbit RZ: high-dose estrogen irreversibly depletes resting zone progenitor number (nilsson2014_2)
rabbit whole plate: fusion occurs abruptly when proliferation rate approaches zero (weise2001)
human growth plate: neither limb of the curve has been localised to a zone
