key_refs.one_line_finding: Only the lowest estradiol dose (4 ug/day) significantly accelerated ulnar growth in boys; 20 and 90 ug/day did not - the direct human biphasic demonstration.
EC50 20 pmol/L estradiol for half-maximal pubertal growth in girls; <25% of growth remains above the Tanner B2 range.
Ultra-low-dose childhood estrogen alone lowered adult height below placebo but added 0.32 SDS on top of GH in Turner syndrome.
Estradiol cypionate 70 ug/kg/week accelerated every senescence parameter in ovariectomised rabbits; fusion followed proliferative exhaustion.
Early very low-dose depot estradiol plus GH gave 3.5 cm more growth over 2 years than GH alone.

estrogen_gh_axis_amplification.name: Estrogen amplification of GH secretion
estrogen_gh_axis_amplification.summary: A substantial part of estrogen's effect on the pubertal growth spurt is not exerted at the plate at all but on the somatotroph axis, and the effect is on PULSATILE rather than basal GH. Under a GnRH-antagonist gonadal clamp in 74 older men, estradiol addback during aromatase inhibition raised basal, pulsatile and total overnight GH secretion by 60-70%, and log pulsatile GH correlated with concurrent estradiol; estradiol did not potentiate GHRH/ghrelin/somatostatin-withdrawal stimuli, so the site of action is likely hypothalamic rather than pituitary (roelfsema2018). A second mechanism is feedback disinhibition: in 25 postmenopausal women, recombinant IGF-I dose-dependently suppressed pulsatile GH by reducing burst mass and frequency, and 16 days of estradiol significantly blunted that suppression (veldhuis2008). Together these explain why oral versus transdermal estrogen route matters clinically (first-pass hepatic IGF-1 suppression) and why estrogen simultaneously raises GH and lowers hepatic IGF-1 output. This node is the reason the estrogen dose-response at the plate cannot be read off serum estradiol alone.
estrogen_gh_axis_amplification.human_evidence_note: Both experiments are randomised, clamped human interventional studies with 10-minute sampling and deconvolution analysis.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamic-pituitary; site inferred, not directly localised
growth plate: not applicable - this node acts entirely upstream

key_refs.one_line_finding: Estradiol addback under gonadal clamp raised nocturnal GH secretion 60-70% without potentiating secretagogues.
Estradiol blunted rhIGF-I negative feedback on pulsatile GH secretion in postmenopausal women.

aliases: sex steroid modulation of GH pulsatility

estrogen_receptor_alpha.name: Estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1 / ERalpha)
estrogen_receptor_alpha.summary:
ERalpha is the nuclear receptor that carries the growth-terminating action of estrogen. It transactivates through two activation functions, AF-1 (ligand-independent, N-terminal) and AF-2 (ligand-dependent). Mouse genetics dissociates them sharply: old female ERalpha-null mice continue growing, with tibiae 8.3% longer (P<0.01) and growth plate height 18% greater (P<0.05) than wild type, phenocopying human ESR1 and aromatase deficiency; whereas mice lacking only ERalphaAF-1 have SHORTER tibiae (-4.9%, P<0.01) and closed proximal tibial growth plates in every animal while all wild-type plates remained open (brjesson2012). AF-1 deletion therefore yields a HYPERactive ERalpha for the closure function, meaning growth plate closure is driven by ERalpha functions that do not require AF-1 and is actively opposed by AF-1. This is a rare instance where a mouse experiment makes a mechanistic prediction that the human experiments of nature (ESR1 inactivation, aromatase deficiency - covered in L7) then match phenotypically.

The human arm of that prediction is now attached rather than merely asserted. Smith 1994 described a
28-year-old man homozygous for a disruptive ESR1 mutation who reached 204 cm with radiographically
incomplete epiphyseal closure and a documented history of continued linear growth into adulthood,
despite elevated serum estradiol and estrone, normal testosterone, and normal masculinisation - so
the ligand was present, the androgen axis was intact, and only the receptor was missing. Lumbar
spine bone mineral density was 0.745 g/cm2, 3.1 SD below the young adult mean. Bernard 2017 adds
three homozygous ESR1 R394H siblings with delayed bone maturation. The mouse deletion and the human
null therefore make the same statement about the same proposition by different routes.

claim_grades.claim: ERalpha function is required for epiphyseal fusion, and losing it permits continued longitudinal growth past the normal age of closure.
claim_grades.basis: Mouse germline ERalpha-null females keep growing (tibia +8.3%, plate height +18%; brjesson2012) and a human ESR1-null male reached 204 cm with unfused epiphyses despite elevated estradiol (smith1994), with independent ESR1 loss-of-function families showing delayed bone maturation (bernard2017).

claim_grades.claim: Growth plate closure is driven by ERalpha functions that do not require AF-1 and is actively opposed by AF-1.
claim_grades.basis: Single mouse study dissociating AF-1 from AF-2 (brjesson2012); no human allele separates the activation functions.

estrogen_receptor_alpha.human_evidence_note: A human ESR1 loss-of-function male with measured adult height, radiographic epiphyseal status, gonadotropins and bone density, plus independent ESR1 loss-of-function families.
estrogen_receptor_alpha.translation_risk_reason: Unusually, the mouse loss-of-function phenotype matches the human experiment of nature; the AF-1/AF-2 dissection, however, is mouse-only.
localization: mouse growth plate: ERalpha required for closure; AF-1 opposes closure (brjesson2012)
human growth plate: ERalpha protein not quantified by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: ERalpha-null female mice keep growing (tibia +8.3%, plate height +18%) while ERalphaAF-1-null mice close their growth plates and have shorter tibiae (-4.9%).
A man homozygous for a disruptive ESR1 mutation reached 204 cm with incomplete epiphyseal closure and continued linear growth into adulthood, despite elevated estradiol and normal testosterone.
Two sisters and one brother homozygous for ESR1 R394H failed to enter puberty and had delayed bone maturation.

ERalpha-KO (ERKO), ERbeta-KO (BERKO) and DOUBLE ERalpha/beta-KO (DERKO) male mice compared head to head: ERKO and DERKO but NOT BERKO show decreased longitudinal and radial skeletal growth with decreased serum IGF-1. The estrogen receptor double perturbation has been done and removing ERbeta adds nothing over removing ERalpha alone.

estrogen_receptor_beta.name: Estrogen receptor beta (ESR2 / ERbeta)
estrogen_receptor_beta.summary: ERbeta is the second nuclear estrogen receptor. It is expressed in growth plate cartilage and can heterodimerise with ERalpha, where it generally damps ERalpha-driven transcription. Its role in longitudinal growth is secondary and, unlike ERalpha, is not supported by a human experiment of nature: no ESR2 inactivating mutation with continued growth and unfused epiphyses has been described, and Esr2-null mice have essentially normal longitudinal bone growth. Sex-specific in vitro work in rat costochondral chondrocytes shows 17beta-estradiol responses that require BOTH ERalpha and ERbeta and depend on receptor palmitoylation for membrane translocation, so ERbeta may matter more for rapid membrane-initiated signalling than for the nuclear closure programme. The practical consequence is that estrogen's growth-terminating action should be attributed to ERalpha; attributing it to 'estrogen receptors' generically overstates ERbeta's role.
estrogen_receptor_beta.human_evidence_note: No human ESR2 loss-of-function skeletal growth phenotype has been reported, in contrast to ESR1.
estrogen_receptor_beta.translation_risk_reason: Rodent in vitro data attribute part of the estradiol response to ERbeta, but there is no human phenotype to anchor this and no human physeal measurement.
localization: rodent growth plate: ERbeta expressed in chondrocytes
human growth plate: ERbeta protein not quantified by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Growth plate closure in female mice is driven by ERalpha, placing ERbeta outside the essential closure pathway.

ERalpha-KO (ERKO), ERbeta-KO (BERKO) and DOUBLE ERalpha/beta-KO (DERKO) male mice compared head to head: ERKO and DERKO but NOT BERKO show decreased longitudinal and radial skeletal growth with decreased serum IGF-1. The estrogen receptor double perturbation has been done and removing ERbeta adds nothing over removing ERalpha alone.

fgf23_hormone.name: FGF23
fgf23_hormone.summary: FGF23 is a 251-residue osteocyte- and osteoblast-derived hormone, the principal phosphaturic factor. It requires alpha-Klotho as an obligate co-receptor to signal through FGFR1c in the proximal renal tubule, where it internalises NaPi-2a/2c and suppresses CYP27B1 while inducing CYP24A1 - so it lowers both phosphate and calcitriol simultaneously. FGF23 excess (PHEX-mutant X-linked hypophosphataemia, autosomal dominant hypophosphataemic rickets, tumour-induced osteomalacia) causes rickets and disproportionate short stature; loss of FGF23 or Klotho causes hyperphosphataemic tumoural calcinosis. Chondrocytes are not merely downstream: VDR signalling in chondrocytes regulates osteoblast FGF23 production (masuyama2006). The therapeutic test in humans is burosumab, an anti-FGF23 monoclonal, which improved height velocity by 0.085-0.121 Z-score/year in 641 children and adolescents with XLH (fukumoto2026).
fgf23_hormone.human_evidence_note: Human FGF23 excess and deficiency syndromes have opposite mineral and skeletal phenotypes, and anti-FGF23 antibody treatment quantifiably improves growth in XLH.
fgf23_hormone.translation_risk_reason: Human genetic and therapeutic data are primary.
localization: human SYS: osteocyte/osteoblast-derived, acts on proximal renal tubule
growth plate: chondrocyte VDR modulates osteoblast FGF23 output (mouse); FGF23 protein not quantified in human physis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Anti-FGF23 antibody burosumab improved height velocity in XLH by 0.085-0.121 Z-score/year across 641 participants.
Chondrocyte VDR signalling regulates osteoblast FGF23 production.

gh_pulse_pattern_hypothesis.name: GH pulse pattern versus integrated exposure at the plate
gh_pulse_pattern_hypothesis.summary: The hypothesis is that the growth plate reads the SHAPE of the GH signal - burst amplitude, interburst trough depth and frequency - and not merely the 24-hour integral, and that pattern information is decoded at the chondrocyte via the kinetics of JAK2-STAT5B phosphorylation and SOCS2-mediated receptor turnover. The rat evidence is strong and quantitative: at matched total dose, adding a pulsatile component to a patterned infusion raised weight gain from 1.1 to 2.1 g/day while adding an equal continuous component did nothing, and pulsatile versus continuous dose-response curves were non-parallel; hepatic GHR and GHBP showed the mirror-image dependence on the trough component (gevers1996). At the tissue level, pulsatile but not continuous GH narrowed the resting zone while both widened proliferative and hypertrophic zones (gevers1996a) - the only existing zonal readout of pattern-dependence. Independently, meal-feeding versus grazing at matched intake tripled GH secretion, added two bursts per day and preserved tibial epiphyseal plate width in a ghrelin/GHS-R-dependent way (hornsby2025). No human experiment has varied GH pattern at matched exposure with a growth endpoint, and no measurement of the GH concentration-time profile in growth plate interstitium exists in any species.
gh_pulse_pattern_hypothesis.human_evidence_note: No human study manipulates GH pattern at matched integrated exposure with a linear growth endpoint; the human data are limited to showing that the endogenous pattern exists and is modulated.
gh_pulse_pattern_hypothesis.translation_risk_reason: Rat GH profiles are far more sharply pulsatile and more sexually dimorphic than human ones, so pattern-dependence magnitudes almost certainly differ; the long-acting human GH analogues now in use deliberately flatten the profile, which makes this an open clinical question, not an academic one.
localization: rat RZ: pattern-dependent narrowing demonstrated (gevers1996a)
human growth plate: GH concentration-time profile never measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Growth tracks the pulse component and hepatic GHR/GHBP the trough component of a patterned GH infusion at matched dose.
Pulsatile but not continuous GH narrowed the resting zone; both widened the proliferative and hypertrophic zones.
Feeding pattern changed GH burst number and height and preserved tibial epiphyseal plate width via ghrelin/GHS-R.

gh_receptor.name: Growth hormone receptor (GHR)
gh_receptor.summary: GHR is a single-pass class I cytokine receptor that exists as a preformed, ligand-independent dimer. Ligand binding does not dimerise the receptor; it rotates the two transmembrane helices from a parallel arrangement into a left-handed crossover, separating the juxtamembrane regions and pulling apart the two JAK2 pseudokinase domains that had been holding each other's kinase domains inhibited, which permits trans-activation (brooks2014). Proteolytic shedding of the ectodomain generates GH-binding protein (GHBP). GHR mRNA and protein are present across rat growth plate zones with the strongest signal in the germinal and proliferative zones (gevers2002), the anatomical basis for a direct plate action. Ghr-null mice show disproportionate skeletal shortening and markedly reduced bone mineral content (sjgren2000); in humans, biallelic GHR loss of function is Laron syndrome, with severely reduced untreated adult stature and only partial rescue by recombinant IGF-1 (laron2015, guevaraaguirre2025). Hepatic GHR abundance is set by the trough rather than the peak of the GH profile in rat (gevers1996); the equivalent regulation in chondrocytes has never been measured.
gh_receptor.human_evidence_note: Biallelic human GHR loss of function (Laron syndrome) causes severe GH-insensitive short stature with high GH and low IGF-1, establishing the receptor's necessity for human stature.
gh_receptor.translation_risk_reason: The requirement for GHR is human-proven; the activation mechanism comes from structural and biophysical work in cell systems and the zonal distribution is rat-only.
localization: rat RZ/PZ: GHR mRNA and protein confirmed, highest signal (gevers2002)
rat HZ: GHR present at lower level (gevers2002)
human growth plate: GHR protein not localised by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: GH rotates the preformed GHR dimer's transmembrane helices into a left-handed crossover, separating JAK2 pseudokinase domains.
GHR and GHBP localised across rat growth plate zones with highest germinal/proliferative signal.
Ghr-null mice show disproportionate skeletal growth and markedly decreased bone mineral content.
Fifty-year Laron syndrome cohort: untreated GHR-deficient adults reach markedly reduced stature.

gh_secretion_pulsatility.name: GH secretion pulsatility
gh_secretion_pulsatility.summary: GH is not released tonically; it is emitted in discrete secretory bursts superimposed on a low basal rate. The standard measurement is 10-minute venous sampling for 8-24 h followed by deconvolution analysis, which decomposes the concentration series into burst times, burst mass, a basal secretion rate and a monoexponential elimination term; pattern regularity is reported separately as approximate entropy (ApEn). In healthy middle-aged adults sampled for 24 h this yields 13.7-13.8 bursts/24 h with ~88% of total output attributable to bursts rather than basal secretion (van2016). Burst amplitude, not frequency, carries most of the physiological modulation: 24-h pulsatile secretion falls with age and, more steeply, with BMI, and the female excess disappears after age 50 (roelfsema2016, n=130). Pattern is mechanistically load-bearing and not merely descriptive: in GH-deficient dwarf rats given patterned infusions at matched total dose, body growth tracked the PULSE component while hepatic GHR and plasma GHBP tracked the TROUGH component, and pulsatile versus continuous dose-response curves were non-parallel (gevers1996). A single fasting GH measurement is uninformative about 24-h secretion (roelfsema2016).
gh_secretion_pulsatility.human_evidence_note: Deconvolution of frequently sampled human serum GH is a routine, validated human measurement; what is absent is any measurement of the GH profile actually seen by a chondrocyte.
gh_secretion_pulsatility.translation_risk_reason: Human data establish the systemic pattern; the demonstration that PATTERN rather than integrated exposure drives growth comes from rat infusion experiments, and rat GH profiles are more sharply pulsatile and more sexually dimorphic than human ones.
localization: human SYS: measured in peripheral venous blood only
human growth plate: local GH concentration-time profile never measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: 13.7-13.8 GH bursts/24 h with ~88% pulsatile output in healthy adults by deconvolution.
In 130 healthy adults pulsatile 24-h GH fell with age and BMI; a single fasting GH is uninformative.
Growth responds to the pulse component and hepatic GHR/GHBP to the trough component of a patterned GH infusion in dwarf rats.
Sparse deconvolution of 10-min overnight GH in 18 adolescents recovers burst timing, amplitude, basal rate and clearance.

ghrelin_hormone.name: Ghrelin
ghrelin_hormone.summary: Ghrelin is a 28-residue stomach-derived peptide, octanoylated on Ser3 by GOAT, that activates GHSR1a on somatotrophs and hypothalamic neurons and amplifies GH secretory bursts. Its role in skeletal growth was long argued mainly from pharmacology; it now has a direct mechanistic demonstration. In rodents fed identical total calories as discrete meals rather than by grazing, preprandial ghrelin surges tripled GH secretion, raised burst height and added two extra GH bursts per day, and this preserved body length and tibial epiphyseal plate width; the effect required ghrelin and GHS-R (hornsby2025). The same study showed the converse in humans: continuous nasogastric feeding failed to suppress circulating ghrelin and produced continuously elevated GH with minimal rhythmicity, whereas bolus enteral infusion restored postprandial ghrelin troughs and ultradian GH rhythm. Ghrelin is therefore the best-characterised link between feeding PATTERN, as distinct from total intake, and growth plate output.
ghrelin_hormone.human_evidence_note: In human volunteers, continuous versus bolus enteral feeding changed circulating ghrelin troughs and GH rhythmicity in the predicted directions; the skeletal endpoint was measured only in rodents.
ghrelin_hormone.translation_risk_reason: The GH-rhythm arm was replicated in humans, but the growth plate readout (epiphyseal plate width, body length) exists only in rodents.
localization: human SYS: gastric X/A-like cells -> circulation -> pituitary and hypothalamus
growth plate: no established direct ghrelin action on chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Meal-feeding tripled GH secretion via ghrelin/GHS-R and preserved tibial epiphyseal plate width; continuous enteral feeding flattened GH rhythm in humans.

ghrh_hormone.name: GHRH (growth hormone-releasing hormone)
ghrh_hormone.summary: GHRH is a 44-amino-acid hypothalamic peptide released from arcuate neurons into the hypophyseal portal circulation, where it binds the somatotroph GHRH receptor (a class B GPCR) and raises cAMP, driving both GH synthesis and secretory burst generation. Biallelic GHRHR loss of function causes isolated GH deficiency type IB with severe proportionate short stature; the Itabaianinha (Brazil) kindred provides a large human cohort homozygous for a GHRHR null allele followed from childhood into old age (aguiaroliveira2021). GH secretion in GHRHR-inactivated humans nonetheless remains pulsatile at minimal amplitude, which shows the pulse GENERATOR is not GHRH itself: somatostatin withdrawal and ghrelin provide non-GHRH inputs to burst timing. GHRH has no established action at the growth plate; its entire effect on stature is exerted through somatotroph output.
ghrh_hormone.human_evidence_note: Homozygous GHRHR null mutations in humans, including a large Brazilian kindred with lifelong follow-up, produce severe isolated GH deficiency and proportionate dwarfism.
ghrh_hormone.translation_risk_reason: Defining evidence is a human genetic cohort with lifelong follow-up.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamic arcuate nucleus -> portal blood -> pituitary somatotroph
growth plate: no established local action

key_refs.one_line_finding: Homozygous GHRHR null mutation in the Itabaianinha cohort causes lifelong isolated GH deficiency with proportionate dwarfism.

ghsr_receptor.name: GHS-R1a (ghrelin receptor)
ghsr_receptor.summary: GHSR1a is a Gq/11-coupled receptor with unusually high constitutive activity, expressed on pituitary somatotrophs and hypothalamic GHRH and NPY neurons. Acyl-ghrelin binding raises intracellular Ca2+ and augments GH burst mass; GHSR agonists (the GH secretagogue class) are used as pharmacological probes of somatotroph reserve. Genetic deletion of GHS-R in rodents abolished the skeletal benefit of meal-feeding - body length and tibial epiphyseal plate width were no longer preserved when the ghrelin signal could not be received (hornsby2025) - the strongest causal evidence that this receptor participates in setting growth plate output. In humans, rare GHSR variants have been reported in short stature and constitutional delay but penetrance is incomplete and GHSR is not an established monogenic growth gene.
ghsr_receptor.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is pharmacological (GH secretagogue responses) plus rare, incompletely penetrant GHSR variants; no definitive human loss-of-function growth syndrome.
ghsr_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Causal skeletal data are rodent; human data are pharmacological.
localization: human SYS: pituitary somatotroph, hypothalamic arcuate nucleus
growth plate: not established

key_refs.one_line_finding: GHS-R was required for meal-feeding to preserve body length and tibial epiphyseal plate width in rodents.

glucocorticoid_cortisol.name: Cortisol / glucocorticoid excess
glucocorticoid_cortisol.summary: Glucocorticoid excess is the most potent single suppressor of childhood linear growth, and the decisive experiments show the suppression is plate-INTRINSIC, not a systemic consequence of lowered GH or IGF-1. Infusing dexamethasone phosphate (80 ng/uL at 1 uL/h) into one proximal tibial growth plate of a 5-week-old rabbit reduced growth rate on that side by 77% relative to the vehicle-infused contralateral tibia, measured by serial radiographs of implanted pins with ~5% error (baron1992). The same unilateral model then showed that catch-up growth after the infusion stops is also confined to the affected plate (baron1994), which rules out a central 'sizostat' for this phenomenon and grounds the growth plate senescence model: glucocorticoid slows resting zone chondrocyte proliferation and slows the numerical depletion of those cells, conserving proliferative capacity (schrier2006). The counterweight is that inducible chondrocyte-specific GR deletion in mouse left growth plates, long bone length and bone microarchitecture normal (tu2014) - so ENDOGENOUS glucocorticoid tone is dispensable for normal growth even though PHARMACOLOGICAL excess acts locally.
glucocorticoid_cortisol.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is clinical and unambiguous at the whole-organism level (Cushing syndrome, glucocorticoid-treated chronic disease, inhaled corticosteroid effects on growth velocity) but there is no human experiment localising the effect to the plate or to a zone.
glucocorticoid_cortisol.translation_risk_reason: The plate-intrinsic conclusion rests on a rabbit unilateral-infusion model that cannot be performed in humans; the mouse GR-knockout null result shows the endogenous and pharmacological regimes are not interchangeable.
localization: rabbit RZ: dexamethasone slows resting zone chondrocyte proliferation and delays their numerical depletion (schrier2006)
rabbit whole plate: local infusion suppresses growth rate by 77% (baron1992)
human growth plate: zonal glucocorticoid receptor occupancy never measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Local intra-plate dexamethasone cut ipsilateral tibial growth rate by 77% versus the contralateral vehicle-infused plate in rabbits.
Catch-up growth after local glucocorticoid suppression is confined to the affected plate, so the mechanism is intrinsic, not neuroendocrine.
Dexamethasone slowed rabbit resting zone chondrocyte proliferation and their numerical depletion, conserving proliferative capacity.
Inducible chondrocyte-specific GR deletion left growth plates and long bone length normal in mice.

glucocorticoid_receptor.name: Glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1 / GR)
glucocorticoid_receptor.summary: GR is a cytoplasmic nuclear receptor that, on ligand binding, sheds HSP90, dimerises and either transactivates GRE-containing promoters or transrepresses AP-1 and NF-kB. It is the obligatory mediator of glucocorticoid action, so it is the natural test of whether glucocorticoid growth suppression is chondrocyte-autonomous. The genetic test in mouse gave a null result: tamoxifen-inducible chondrocyte-specific GR knockout mice, with deletion induced at several postnatal ages, had knee joint architecture, cartilage structure, growth plates, intervertebral discs, long bone length and bone microarchitecture indistinguishable from controls at all ages, although metaphyseal (not diaphyseal) fracture healing was impaired (tu2014). Endogenous glucocorticoid signalling in chondrocytes is therefore dispensable for normal longitudinal growth in mouse, which does not contradict the rabbit local-infusion result (a pharmacological excess) but does mean the two experiments answer different questions. No study has measured GR protein abundance, ligand occupancy or transcriptional output by zone in human growth plate tissue.
glucocorticoid_receptor.human_evidence_note: No human study localises GR expression or occupancy within the growth plate; human NR3C1 generalised glucocorticoid resistance presents with hyperandrogenism and hypertension rather than with a defined statural phenotype.
glucocorticoid_receptor.translation_risk_reason: The only clean genetic test is a mouse conditional knockout with a null skeletal result, which is hard to reconcile with the clinical potency of glucocorticoid growth suppression in children.
localization: mouse growth plate: GR deletion in chondrocytes has no structural effect (tu2014)
human growth plate: GR protein and occupancy not measured by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Chondrocyte-specific inducible GR knockout mice had normal cartilage and bone development but impaired metaphyseal fracture healing.
Pharmacological glucocorticoid acts locally on the plate, the effect GR would have to mediate.

gnrh_hormone.name: GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone)
gnrh_hormone.summary: GnRH is a decapeptide released in ~60-120 minute pulses from hypothalamic neurons into the hypophyseal portal circulation; the reactivation of that pulse generator is the first detectable event of puberty (abreu2013). Pulse FREQUENCY, not concentration, encodes the signal - continuous GnRH exposure downregulates the pituitary GnRH receptor, which is exactly why long-acting GnRH agonists suppress rather than stimulate the axis and are used to arrest precocious puberty and preserve adult height. GnRH has no established action at the growth plate; its entire statural effect is mediated by gonadal sex steroid output and therefore by the estrogen dose-response. Loss of the upstream kisspeptin input (KISS1R mutations) produces hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with absent pubertal growth spurt and delayed epiphyseal fusion (seminara2003, de2003).
gnrh_hormone.human_evidence_note: Human GnRH deficiency syndromes and the therapeutic use of GnRH analogues in central precocious puberty give bidirectional interventional human evidence.
gnrh_hormone.translation_risk_reason: Human genetic and pharmacological evidence dominates.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamic GnRH neurons -> portal circulation -> pituitary gonadotroph
growth plate: no established local action

key_refs.one_line_finding: Puberty onset is first detected as increased pulsatile GnRH secretion; MKRN3 deficiency releases this brake.
GPR54/KISS1R loss of function upstream of GnRH causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

gper1_receptor.name: GPER1 (G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1)
gper1_receptor.summary: GPER1 is a seven-transmembrane, Gs-coupled receptor that binds estradiol with nanomolar affinity and signals through cAMP-PKA-CREB and EGFR transactivation on a seconds-to-minutes timescale, distinct from the hours-timescale nuclear ERalpha programme. In the growth plate its documented role is on the ascending, growth-promoting limb rather than on fusion: GPER1 positively regulates chondrocyte proliferation in the pubertal female mouse growth plate (chou2021), and the effect is relayed through the PTHrP/Ihh feedback loop (chou2025). GPER1 is therefore a candidate mechanism for how the same ligand can be growth-promoting at low concentration and growth-terminating at high concentration - two receptors with different affinities, kinetics and downstream logic - but this two-receptor explanation of the biphasic effect has not been tested by manipulating GPER1 and ERalpha in the same animal across a dose range, and there is no human GPER1 growth phenotype.
gper1_receptor.human_evidence_note: No human GPER1 loss- or gain-of-function growth phenotype has been described.
gper1_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Entirely mouse, in a sex- and stage-restricted model, with no human counterpart; mice do not fuse, so the pubertal-proliferation result cannot be extended to the human fusion decision.
localization: mouse pubertal growth plate: GPER1 promotes chondrocyte proliferation via PTHrP/Ihh (chou2021, chou2025)
human growth plate: GPER1 protein not localised

key_refs.one_line_finding: GPER1 positively regulates growth plate chondrocyte proliferation in female pubertal mice.
GPER1 facilitates pubertal growth plate chondrocyte proliferation via PTHrP/Ihh regulation.

growth_hormone.name: Growth hormone (GH1 / somatotropin)
growth_hormone.summary: GH is a 191-residue, 22 kDa single-chain protein secreted in discrete bursts by anterior pituitary somatotrophs. It reaches the growth plate as a systemic ligand and also acts on the plate directly: unilateral intra-arterial infusion into hypophysectomised rats widened the tibial growth plate on the infused side only, with the contralateral limb as internal control (isaksson1982). That direct action is at least partly relayed by locally made IGF-1, because GH raised the number of IGF-1-immunoreactive chondrocytes in the germinal/proliferative zone (nilsson1986) and a somatomedin antiserum abolished the local growth response (schlechter1986). GH acts principally on the resting/germinal compartment: it increases the NUMBER of chondrocytes entering proliferation rather than the labelling index of cells already cycling (ohlsson1992, gevers1996a; rat). In humans the causal chain is established by loss-of-function at every node - GH1, GHRHR, GHR, STAT5B, IGF1, IGFALS, PAPPA2 - each producing short stature of characteristic severity. What GH does at the human growth plate has never been measured directly; all zonal data are rodent or rabbit.
growth_hormone.human_evidence_note: Human GH1, GHRHR and GHR loss-of-function each cause severe proportionate short stature and recombinant GH restores growth - interventional human evidence for the axis, though not for GH's zonal mechanism.
growth_hormone.translation_risk_reason: The systemic requirement for GH is proven in humans; the zonal mechanism (resting-zone recruitment, local IGF-1 relay) rests entirely on rat and rabbit work, and rodents do not fuse their epiphyses.
localization: rat RZ: GH receptor present and GH-responsive proliferation confirmed (gevers2002, ohlsson1992)
rat PZ: GH increases chondrocyte number, not labelling index (gevers1996a)
human growth plate: GH action not directly measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Unilateral intra-arterial GH infusion widened the growth plate only on the infused side of hypophysectomised rats.
GH increased the number of IGF-1-containing chondrocytes in the rat growth plate germinal zone.
Somatomedin antiserum blocked the local growth response to intra-arterial GH.
GH induces multiplication of the slowly cycling germinal cells of the rat tibial growth plate.
24-h deconvolution: 13.7-13.8 GH bursts/24 h, ~88% of output pulsatile, in healthy middle-aged humans.

hsd11b1_enzyme.name: 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (HSD11B1)
hsd11b1_enzyme.summary: HSD11B1 is an NADPH-dependent, predominantly reductase enzyme of the endoplasmic reticulum that regenerates active cortisol from inert cortisone, amplifying local glucocorticoid exposure independently of circulating cortisol. Its activity is the reason tissue glucocorticoid tone can diverge from serum cortisol, and it is a validated pharmacological target in metabolic disease. In bone, HSD11B1 activity in osteoblasts is established and rises with age and with inflammatory cytokine exposure. For the growth plate specifically, the pre-receptor amplification model is widely assumed but the primary evidence is essentially absent: a targeted search returns no study measuring HSD11B1 expression or activity in growth plate chondrocytes by zone, in any species. This is a mechanistically load-bearing hole, because it is the step that would determine whether a given systemic glucocorticoid dose is amplified or damped at the plate.
hsd11b1_enzyme.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate measurement; human HSD11B1 deficiency (cortisone reductase deficiency) is described for its androgen excess phenotype, not for stature.
hsd11b1_enzyme.translation_risk_reason: There is no growth plate data in any species to transfer, so the direction and magnitude of any species difference cannot be estimated.
localization: human growth plate: HSD11B1 expression/activity not reported
human/rodent bone: HSD11B1 activity demonstrated in osteoblasts, not in physeal chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Establishes that glucocorticoid acts locally at the plate, which is the action HSD11B1 would modulate.

hsd11b2_enzyme.name: 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (HSD11B2)
hsd11b2_enzyme.summary: HSD11B2 is an NAD+-dependent, unidirectional dehydrogenase that inactivates cortisol to cortisone. In kidney and colon it protects the mineralocorticoid receptor from cortisol; in the placenta it forms the barrier that shields the fetus from maternal cortisol, and reduced placental HSD11B2 is the leading mechanistic candidate linking maternal stress to fetal growth restriction. Human HSD11B2 loss of function causes apparent mineralocorticoid excess with hypertension and, notably, low birth weight and poor postnatal growth - the closest thing to a human experiment on glucocorticoid inactivation and stature. Within the growth plate itself, whether chondrocytes express HSD11B2 and thereby defend themselves against systemic cortisol has not been established; the only physeal-adjacent primary work found is in cartilage in a developmental-programming osteoarthritis model, not in the growth plate.
hsd11b2_enzyme.human_evidence_note: Human HSD11B2 mutations cause apparent mineralocorticoid excess with low birth weight and impaired growth, but the growth effect is not localised to the plate.
hsd11b2_enzyme.translation_risk_reason: No growth plate expression data exist in any species to transfer.
localization: human placenta, kidney, colon: HSD11B2 established
human growth plate: HSD11B2 expression not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Local glucocorticoid delivery suppresses plate growth, the effect any local inactivating enzyme would oppose.

igf1_local_growth_plate.name: Locally produced growth plate IGF-1
igf1_local_growth_plate.summary: Growth plate chondrocytes synthesise IGF-1 themselves, and this pool is GH-regulated: GH treatment of hypophysectomised rats increased the number of IGF-1-immunoreactive chondrocytes in the germinal and proliferative zones (nilsson1986), and blocking somatomedin with antiserum abolished the local growth response to intra-arterial GH (schlechter1986). The strongest argument for the local pool's importance is negative and comes from the liver-specific Igf1 knockouts: a 75% fall in circulating IGF-1 left mouse body and femoral length unchanged (yakar1999, sjgren1999), which is only interpretable if a non-hepatic IGF-1 source sustains growth. Local IGF-1 is also the node where thyroid hormone enters - T3-driven chondrocyte differentiation requires IGF-1 modulation of beta-catenin (wang2010). What is missing is quantity: no study reports the concentration of IGF-1 in growth plate interstitium, its gradient across zones, or the fraction of chondrocyte IGF1R occupancy attributable to local versus circulating ligand, in any species, and least of all in human tissue.
igf1_local_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: There is no human measurement of growth-plate-derived IGF-1; human inference is entirely by analogy from rodent conditional genetics.
igf1_local_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: The concept rests on rat immunohistochemistry and mouse liver knockouts. Human growth plate tissue is scarce and no equivalent measurement exists.
localization: rat RZ/PZ: IGF-1 immunoreactivity present and GH-inducible (nilsson1986)
human growth plate: IGF-1 protein concentration and zonal gradient not measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: GH increased the number of IGF-1-immunoreactive chondrocytes in the rat growth plate.
Somatomedin antiserum blocked the local cartilage response to GH.
Normal growth despite loss of hepatic IGF-1 implies a non-hepatic (local) IGF-1 source suffices in mouse.
T3-driven growth plate chondrocyte growth and differentiation requires IGF-1 modulation of beta-catenin signalling.

igf1_receptor.name: IGF-1 receptor (IGF1R)
igf1_receptor.summary: IGF1R is a disulfide-linked alpha2beta2 receptor tyrosine kinase closely homologous to the insulin receptor, with which it forms hybrid receptors. Ligand binding autophosphorylates the beta-subunit activation loop and recruits IRS-1/2 and Shc, driving PI3K-AKT (survival, cell size, protein synthesis) and RAS-ERK (proliferation). IGF1R binds IGF-1 with roughly 100-fold higher affinity than insulin, which is why insulin's growth effects are mostly indirect (alarid1992). At the growth plate IGF1R is the receptor through which both circulating and locally produced IGF-1 act, so it is the convergence point at which the somatomedin and dual-effector accounts become indistinguishable at the level of the chondrocyte. Human IGF1R haploinsufficiency causes intrauterine and postnatal growth restriction with elevated IGF-1 and relative GH resistance; biallelic loss is not viable. Zonal quantification of IGF1R protein or occupancy in human growth plate has not been reported.
igf1_receptor.human_evidence_note: IGF1R haploinsufficiency and heterozygous missense variants cause human pre- and postnatal growth restriction with raised circulating IGF-1, an unambiguous human loss-of-function phenotype.
igf1_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Human genetic evidence is direct and reproducible across unrelated patients.
localization: human growth plate: IGF1R protein not quantified by zone
rodent PZ: IGF1R expression reported but not quantified against local ligand concentration

key_refs.one_line_finding: Insulin's trophic effect on cartilage growth in vivo requires IGF-I, indicating signalling converges on the IGF1R axis.
Reduced free IGF-1 available to IGF1R, not total IGF-1, tracks stature in PAPP-A2 deficiency.

Cartilage-specific Igf1r knockout - embryonic and tamoxifen-inducible postnatal - is an IGF1R-selective cartilage perturbation that does not touch INSR: disorganised chondrocyte columns, delayed ossification and vascular invasion, reduced proliferation, increased apoptosis and increased Pthrp transcription in the growth plate.

igf1_systemic.name: Systemic (hepatic) IGF-1
igf1_systemic.summary: Circulating IGF-1 is a 70-residue single-chain peptide made predominantly by hepatocytes under GH-STAT5B control and carried in blood almost entirely in a 150 kDa ternary complex with IGFBP-3 (or IGFBP-5) and the acid-labile subunit ALS, which extends its half-life from minutes to hours. Free IGF-1 is under 1% of total. The liver is the dominant source: hepatocyte-specific Igf1 deletion cuts serum IGF-1 by 75% in mouse (sjgren1999). But source and function dissociate - that same 75% fall left postnatal body length unchanged (yakar1999). Circulating IGF-1 becomes growth-limiting only below a threshold, reached in LID+ALSKO double mutants, where growth plate total height and proliferative and hypertrophic zone heights all shrink and are restored by exogenous IGF-1 (yakar2002). In humans the assays that matter are total IGF-1 (routine) and free or bioactive IGF-1 (research-grade); PAPPA2 deficiency shows these can move in opposite directions and that height tracks the free fraction (dauber2016).
igf1_systemic.human_evidence_note: Human IGF1, IGFALS, STAT5B, GHR and PAPPA2 defects all alter circulating IGF-1 and stature concordantly, and recombinant IGF-1 (mecasermin) increases height velocity in severe primary IGF-1 deficiency.
igf1_systemic.translation_risk_reason: Human genetics anchor the endpoint, but the quantitative partition between systemic and local IGF-1 comes from mouse conditional knockouts with no human counterpart.
localization: human SYS: hepatocyte-derived, measured in serum
mouse growth plate: circulating IGF-1 becomes limiting for PZ and HZ height only below the LID+ALSKO threshold (yakar2002)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Liver is the principal source of blood IGF-I (75% fall on hepatocyte deletion) yet is not required for postnatal body growth in mice.
Liver-specific Igf1 deletion left body and femoral length normal.
Below a circulating IGF-1 threshold (LID+ALSKO) growth plate height, BMD and cortical thickness fall and are restored by IGF-1.
PAPP-A2 deficiency raises total IGF-1 several-fold while cutting the bioactive fraction to 0.09-0.32%, with short stature.

igf2_hormone.name: IGF-2
igf2_hormone.summary: IGF-2 is a paternally expressed imprinted growth factor that dominates fetal growth and is the most abundant IGF in adult human serum (roughly 3-5 fold higher than IGF-1 by mass), unlike in mouse where Igf2 is largely silenced postnatally - a species difference that undermines direct transfer of mouse IGF-2 data to humans. It signals through IGF1R and the insulin receptor A isoform; IGF2R (cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor) is a clearance receptor. Human dosage disorders make the growth role unambiguous: loss of IGF2 expression at 11p15 (or maternal uniparental disomy 7 / ICR1 hypomethylation) produces Silver-Russell syndrome with severe pre- and postnatal growth restriction, and IGF2 gain of dosage produces Beckwith-Wiedemann overgrowth. In PAPP-A2 deficiency circulating IGF-2 is elevated alongside IGF-1 because both are trapped in ternary complexes (dauber2016), which shows that IGF-2 shares the same bioavailability control layer.
igf2_hormone.human_evidence_note: Human imprinting disorders at 11p15 (Silver-Russell, Beckwith-Wiedemann) provide bidirectional dosage evidence that IGF2 sets human body size.
igf2_hormone.translation_risk_reason: Postnatal IGF-2 expression differs qualitatively between human (high) and mouse (largely silenced), so mouse Igf2 data cannot be read as human postnatal biology.
localization: human SYS: circulating, largely ternary-complex bound
human growth plate: IGF-2 protein not quantified by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Circulating IGF-2 as well as IGF-1 is elevated in PAPP-A2 deficiency, showing shared ternary-complex control.

igf_ternary_complex.name: IGF ternary complex and bioavailability layer
igf_ternary_complex.summary: Between 'how much IGF-1 is in the blood' and 'how much IGF-1 reaches a chondrocyte receptor' sits a control layer that most reviews skip. Over 99% of circulating IGF-1 is bound: mostly in a 150 kDa ternary complex of IGF-1, IGFBP-3 or IGFBP-5, and ALS, which cannot cross the capillary endothelium; the remainder is in binary IGFBP complexes. Release requires local proteolysis - PAPP-A2 cleaves IGFBP-3 and IGFBP-5, PAPP-A cleaves IGFBP-4 - and those proteases are themselves shut off by stanniocalcin-2, which covalently locks PAPP-A and excludes its substrate rather than blocking the catalytic site (kobber2022). Human genetics shows this layer is load-bearing and can invert the usual reading of an IGF-1 result: PAPPA2 loss of function raises total IGF-1 several fold while cutting the bioactive fraction to 0.09-0.32% of total against a healthy median of 1.23%, and produces heights of -2.16 to -3.81 SDS (dauber2016). IGFALS loss does the opposite, collapsing total IGF-1 with only mild short stature (domen2004). Total IGF-1 is therefore a poor proxy for IGF action, and the direction of the error depends on which node of this layer is disturbed.
igf_ternary_complex.human_evidence_note: Human PAPPA2 and IGFALS null alleles produce opposite dissociations between total IGF-1 and stature, which is the direct human evidence that bioavailability rather than concentration is the controlled variable.
igf_ternary_complex.translation_risk_reason: The two decisive experiments are human null alleles with measured free/bioactive IGF; mouse data are corroborative.
localization: human SYS: plasma; complexes sized by neutral size-exclusion chromatography
human growth plate: free IGF-1 concentration in physeal interstitium never measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: PAPP-A2 loss traps IGF-1 in ternary complex: total IGF-1 rises, bioactive fraction falls to 0.09-0.32%, height -2.16 to -3.81 SDS.
ALS loss collapses total circulating IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 with disproportionately mild short stature.
STC2 inhibits PAPP-A by disulfide locking and substrate exclusion, defining the top of the bioavailability layer.
PAPP-A2 and STC2 but not PAPP-A associate with circulating total IGF-1 in human adults.

igfbp1.name: IGFBP-1
igfbp1.summary: IGFBP-1 is a 25 kDa hepatic binding protein whose transcription is acutely suppressed by insulin and induced by fasting, hypoglycaemia and glucocorticoids; its serum concentration therefore swings several-fold within hours and inversely tracks portal insulin. Because it binds IGF-1 with affinity comparable to IGF1R and is not part of the ternary complex, IGFBP-1 acts as a rapid, nutrition-responsive brake on free IGF-1. This is the most plausible molecular route by which acute undernutrition and catabolic illness lower IGF bioactivity within hours rather than days, but no study has measured IGFBP-1 in growth plate interstitium or shown a chondrocyte-level effect in any species. This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation (IGFBP-3/-5 plus ALS), pericellular proteolysis (PAPP-A, PAPP-A2) and protease inhibition (STC1, STC2) - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1. Reviews typically stop at 'IGF-1 level'; the human PAPPA2 kindreds show that total and free IGF-1 can move in opposite directions and that stature tracks the free fraction.
igfbp1.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is limited to serum IGFBP-1 correlating inversely with insulin and nutritional status; no human IGFBP1 growth phenotype exists.
igfbp1.translation_risk_reason: Regulatory logic is established in human hepatocytes and serum; the growth plate link is inference.
localization: human growth plate: zonal protein localisation not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Population-level analysis of IGF axis regulators including binding proteins in human adults.

igfbp2.name: IGFBP-2
igfbp2.summary: IGFBP-2 is the second most abundant circulating IGFBP after IGFBP-3 and, unlike IGFBP-3, is not GH-dependent - it rises in GH deficiency and in catabolic states and falls with GH treatment, so its serum concentration moves opposite to IGFBP-3 across most of the growth disorders. It carries a heparin-binding domain and an RGD motif, giving it IGF-independent, integrin-mediated actions. It is a slow substrate for PAPP-A. Its specific contribution to growth plate IGF availability has not been isolated experimentally in any species. This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation (IGFBP-3/-5 plus ALS), pericellular proteolysis (PAPP-A, PAPP-A2) and protease inhibition (STC1, STC2) - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1. Reviews typically stop at 'IGF-1 level'; the human PAPPA2 kindreds show that total and free IGF-1 can move in opposite directions and that stature tracks the free fraction.
igfbp2.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is correlative serum biochemistry across GH-deficient and catabolic states.
igfbp2.translation_risk_reason: No zonal or mechanistic growth plate data in any species.
localization: human growth plate: zonal protein localisation not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Human population data on circulating IGF axis regulators.

igfbp3.name: IGFBP-3
igfbp3.summary: IGFBP-3 carries roughly 75-90% of circulating IGF-1 and is the principal partner, with ALS, in the 150 kDa ternary complex. Its synthesis is GH- and STAT5B-dependent, which is why serum IGFBP-3 falls in GH deficiency, GHR deficiency (Laron) and STAT5B deficiency and is used clinically as a GH-dependent analyte. IGFBP-3 is the main substrate through which PAPP-A2 releases IGF-1: in human PAPP-A2 deficiency IGFBP-3 rises to 4403-5912 ug/L against a Tanner I reference of 2206-4200 ug/L while free IGF-1 falls, and size-exclusion chromatography shows the IGF is retained in ternary complex (dauber2016). Human ALS deficiency collapses IGFBP-3 as well, because the ternary complex protects it from clearance (domen2004). This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation (IGFBP-3/-5 plus ALS), pericellular proteolysis (PAPP-A, PAPP-A2) and protease inhibition (STC1, STC2) - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1. Reviews typically stop at 'IGF-1 level'; the human PAPPA2 kindreds show that total and free IGF-1 can move in opposite directions and that stature tracks the free fraction.
igfbp3.human_evidence_note: Serum IGFBP-3 responds predictably to human GHR, STAT5B, IGFALS and PAPPA2 mutations and to rhGH treatment - direct, repeatedly replicated human biochemistry.
igfbp3.translation_risk_reason: The load-bearing measurements are human serum biochemistry in genetically defined patients.
localization: human growth plate: zonal protein localisation not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: IGFBP-3 accumulates and traps IGF-1 in ternary complex when PAPP-A2 proteolysis is lost.
IGFALS inactivation collapses circulating IGFBP-3 along with IGF-1.

igfbp4.name: IGFBP-4
igfbp4.summary: IGFBP-4 is a pure inhibitor of IGF action with no documented IGF-potentiating activity, and it is the specific, strictly IGF-dependent substrate of PAPP-A. The PAPP-A/IGFBP-4/STC2 module is therefore a self-contained local switch: IGF-1 bound to IGFBP-4 is inert until PAPP-A cleaves the complex, and STC2 shuts that off by covalently locking PAPP-A and excluding IGFBP-4 from binding (kobber2022). Igfbp4-null mice are modestly growth-retarded, which is counterintuitive for a pure inhibitor and is usually read as loss of a reservoir function. No human IGFBP4 growth disorder is known. This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation (IGFBP-3/-5 plus ALS), pericellular proteolysis (PAPP-A, PAPP-A2) and protease inhibition (STC1, STC2) - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1. Reviews typically stop at 'IGF-1 level'; the human PAPPA2 kindreds show that total and free IGF-1 can move in opposite directions and that stature tracks the free fraction.
igfbp4.human_evidence_note: No human IGFBP4 loss-of-function growth phenotype; human relevance is inferred from the structurally characterised PAPP-A/IGFBP-4/STC2 module.
igfbp4.translation_risk_reason: Growth data are mouse; structural data are human protein in vitro.
localization: human growth plate: zonal protein localisation not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: STC2 blocks PAPP-A's IGFBP-4 binding site, defining the local IGF release switch.

igfbp5.name: IGFBP-5
igfbp5.summary: IGFBP-5 is the most abundant IGFBP in bone matrix and the only IGFBP besides IGFBP-3 that forms a ternary complex with ALS. It binds hydroxyapatite and extracellular matrix, which converts it from a soluble carrier into a matrix-immobilised IGF reservoir - the property that makes it the most likely IGFBP to matter inside cartilage rather than in blood. It is a PAPP-A2 substrate: in human PAPP-A2 deficiency serum IGFBP-5 rises to 645-997 ug/L against a Tanner I reference of 211-707 ug/L (dauber2016). Whether matrix-bound IGFBP-5 in the growth plate sets a zonal gradient of free IGF-1 has not been measured in any species. This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation (IGFBP-3/-5 plus ALS), pericellular proteolysis (PAPP-A, PAPP-A2) and protease inhibition (STC1, STC2) - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1. Reviews typically stop at 'IGF-1 level'; the human PAPPA2 kindreds show that total and free IGF-1 can move in opposite directions and that stature tracks the free fraction.
igfbp5.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is serum IGFBP-5 elevation in PAPP-A2 deficiency; no human IGFBP5 mutation phenotype and no human physeal measurement.
igfbp5.translation_risk_reason: Matrix-reservoir concept is from bone biochemistry, not from physeal measurement.
localization: human growth plate: zonal protein localisation not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Serum IGFBP-5 rises when PAPP-A2 proteolysis is lost, confirming IGFBP-5 is a PAPP-A2 substrate in humans.

igfbp6.name: IGFBP-6
igfbp6.summary: IGFBP-6 is distinguished by an approximately 20-100 fold preference for IGF-2 over IGF-1, making it the only IGFBP that is functionally an IGF-2-selective inhibitor. Given that IGF-2 remains the quantitatively dominant IGF in adult human serum (unlike in mouse), IGFBP-6 is the binding protein whose human relevance is most likely to be underestimated from rodent work. It is O-glycosylated, does not form ternary complexes, and is a poor pappalysin substrate. No growth plate localisation, no human mutation phenotype and no chondrocyte functional data exist. This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation (IGFBP-3/-5 plus ALS), pericellular proteolysis (PAPP-A, PAPP-A2) and protease inhibition (STC1, STC2) - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1. Reviews typically stop at 'IGF-1 level'; the human PAPPA2 kindreds show that total and free IGF-1 can move in opposite directions and that stature tracks the free fraction.
igfbp6.human_evidence_note: No human IGFBP6 growth phenotype and no human physeal data; the IGF-2 selectivity is in vitro binding biochemistry.
igfbp6.translation_risk_reason: Rodent IGF-2 biology is not human IGF-2 biology; any inference about IGFBP-6's growth role from mouse would be misleading.
localization: human growth plate: zonal protein localisation not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Human PAPP-A2 deficiency raises total IGF-2 as well as IGF-1, showing IGF-2 shares the bioavailability layer that IGFBP-6 helps set.

insulin_hormone.name: Insulin
insulin_hormone.summary: Insulin contributes to linear growth in two distinct ways that are often conflated. First, it is the permissive nutritional signal for the GH axis: portal insulin maintains hepatic GHR expression and suppresses IGFBP-1, so insulinopenia (untreated type 1 diabetes, severe malnutrition) produces GH resistance with high GH and low IGF-1. Second, at supraphysiological concentrations insulin can cross-react with IGF1R. The direct cartilage action is largely IGF-mediated: insulin's trophic effect on cartilage growth in vivo required IGF-I (alarid1992). In humans the clearest evidence is clinical - Mauriac syndrome (growth failure in poorly controlled type 1 diabetes) reverses with insulin, and severe insulin receptor mutations (Donohue syndrome) cause profound growth failure. Prepubertal children with obesity, who are hyperinsulinaemic, have high free IGF-1 and accelerated growth despite REDUCED circulating pappalysins (martnrivada2025), which shows insulin acts on the bioavailability layer rather than on total IGF-1.
insulin_hormone.human_evidence_note: Insulin deficiency (Mauriac syndrome) and insulin receptor loss of function (Donohue syndrome) both cause human growth failure that responds to correcting the insulin signal where possible.
insulin_hormone.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical evidence is direct; rat data only refine the mechanism.
localization: human SYS: pancreatic beta cell -> portal and systemic circulation
growth plate: insulin receptor present but direct chondrocyte effect not isolated from IGF1R

key_refs.one_line_finding: Insulin's trophic effect on cartilage growth in vivo requires IGF-I.
Prepubertal children with obesity have high free IGF-1 and accelerated growth despite reduced pappalysin levels.

insulin_receptor.name: Insulin receptor (INSR)
insulin_receptor.summary: INSR is an alpha2beta2 receptor tyrosine kinase that heterodimerises with IGF1R to form hybrid receptors; the A isoform (exon 11 skipped) binds IGF-2 with near-insulin affinity, which matters in humans where IGF-2 remains abundant postnatally. Biallelic INSR loss of function causes Donohue syndrome (leprechaunism) with extreme intrauterine and postnatal growth failure that hyperinsulinaemia cannot rescue, establishing an insulin-receptor requirement for human growth that is separable from the IGF1R requirement. Hybrid INSR/IGF1R receptors mean that at the chondrocyte surface insulin and IGF signalling are not cleanly separable pharmacologically. INSR protein has not been quantified by zone in human growth plate.
insulin_receptor.human_evidence_note: Donohue and Rabson-Mendenhall syndromes are human biallelic INSR loss-of-function disorders with severe growth failure.
insulin_receptor.translation_risk_reason: The requirement is established by human null alleles.
localization: human SYS: ubiquitous
human growth plate: INSR and INSR/IGF1R hybrid abundance not quantified by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Insulin's cartilage growth effect in vivo is IGF-I-dependent, indicating signalling convergence at the IGF1R/INSR hybrid level.

jak2_kinase.name: JAK2 (Janus kinase 2)
jak2_kinase.summary: JAK2 is the tyrosine kinase constitutively bound to the Box1 motif of GHR and the proximal transducer of GH signal. In the resting GHR dimer the two JAK2 pseudokinase (JH2) domains hold each other's kinase (JH1) domains inhibited; GH-induced transmembrane helix rotation separates them and permits JH1 trans-phosphorylation (brooks2014). Activated JAK2 phosphorylates GHR cytoplasmic tyrosines, creating docking sites for STAT5B (the growth-relevant branch), STAT1/3, SHC-RAS-ERK and IRS-PI3K. The pathway is self-limiting: STAT5B transcribes SOCS2, which binds phosphorylated GHR and targets the complex for degradation. Human JAK2 loss-of-function causing isolated growth failure is far rarer than STAT5B or GHR defects, consistent with JAK2's non-redundant role in haematopoiesis; the growth-relevant human evidence is therefore indirect, inferred from the phenotypes of the receptor above and the transcription factor below.
jak2_kinase.human_evidence_note: There is no well-characterised isolated human JAK2 growth-failure syndrome; JAK2's requirement in GH action is inferred from GHR and STAT5B human phenotypes plus biophysical reconstitution.
jak2_kinase.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism established in reconstituted and cell systems; the human growth phenotype of JAK2 hypofunction is undefined because JAK2 is essential elsewhere.
localization: human SYS: ubiquitous
human growth plate: JAK2 phosphorylation not localised by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Receptor-driven separation of JAK2 pseudokinase domains is the activation step for GH signalling.
Human STAT5B loss of function downstream of JAK2 causes GH insensitivity, implicating the JAK2-STAT5B module in stature.

kiss1r_receptor.name: KISS1R (GPR54)
kiss1r_receptor.summary: KISS1R is a Gq/11-coupled receptor on GnRH neurons; kisspeptin binding raises intracellular Ca2+ and depolarises the neuron, generating the GnRH pulse. Its identification in 2003 by two independent groups studying consanguineous families with normosmic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (seminara2003, de2003) is one of the cleanest human forward-genetic results in reproductive endocrinology, and gain-of-function KISS1R variants have subsequently been reported in central precocious puberty, giving bidirectional human dosage evidence. For stature the consequence is indirect but large: absent KISS1R signalling means no pubertal sex steroid rise, hence no growth spurt but also no estrogen-driven epiphyseal fusion, so untreated patients continue growing into adulthood with eunuchoid proportions - a natural human demonstration that the spurt and the cessation are both downstream of this receptor.
kiss1r_receptor.human_evidence_note: Biallelic KISS1R loss of function causes human hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; activating variants have been reported in central precocious puberty.
kiss1r_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Human loss- and gain-of-function alleles both described.
localization: human SYS: GnRH neuron plasma membrane
growth plate: no established expression

key_refs.one_line_finding: GPR54 mutations cause hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in a consanguineous family.
Loss of function of the KiSS1-derived peptide receptor GPR54 causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

kisspeptin_kiss1.name: Kisspeptin (KISS1)
kisspeptin_kiss1.summary: Kisspeptin is the product of KISS1, processed to peptides of 54, 14, 13 and 10 residues sharing a C-terminal RF-amide motif, and is the principal excitatory drive onto GnRH neurons. Arcuate kisspeptin neurons co-express neurokinin B and dynorphin (KNDy neurons) and generate the GnRH pulse; they are also where sex steroid negative feedback is integrated. Kisspeptin's relevance to the growth plate is entirely upstream: it sets the timing of the sex steroid rise that produces the growth spurt and, later, epiphyseal fusion. The genetic proof came from loss of its receptor rather than the ligand - two independent 2003 reports of GPR54/KISS1R loss of function in consanguineous families with normosmic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (seminara2003, de2003) - and MKRN3 acts as a brake on puberty specifically through kisspeptin-expressing neurons (abreu2020).
kisspeptin_kiss1.human_evidence_note: Human KISS1R (and rarer KISS1) loss-of-function mutations cause absent puberty; kisspeptin administration to humans releases LH, a direct interventional confirmation.
kisspeptin_kiss1.translation_risk_reason: Human genetics plus human infusion pharmacology.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamic arcuate and AVPV kisspeptin neurons
growth plate: no established local action

key_refs.one_line_finding: GPR54 loss of function segregates with normosmic idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Independent identification of GPR54 loss of function as a cause of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
MKRN3 restrains the reproductive axis through actions in kisspeptin-expressing neurons.

klotho_alpha.name: alpha-Klotho
klotho_alpha.summary: alpha-Klotho is a single-pass transmembrane glycoprotein, expressed mainly in the distal renal tubule, parathyroid and choroid plexus, that is the obligate co-receptor converting FGFR1c into a high-affinity FGF23 receptor. Without alpha-Klotho, FGF23 cannot signal at physiological concentrations, which is why human alpha-Klotho loss of function phenocopies FGF23 deficiency (hyperphosphataemic tumoural calcinosis) and why Klotho-null mice show accelerated ageing with hyperphosphataemia. A shed ectodomain circulates as soluble Klotho with FGF23-independent activities. For the growth plate, alpha-Klotho's role is entirely through gating the FGF23-phosphate axis; there is no established Klotho expression in growth plate chondrocytes in human tissue, and the beta-Klotho paralogue relevant to FGF21/FGF15-19 signalling is a distinct protein (held separately in L3).
klotho_alpha.human_evidence_note: Human KL loss-of-function causes hyperphosphataemic tumoural calcinosis with FGF23 resistance, and a translocation causing Klotho overexpression caused hypophosphataemic rickets.
klotho_alpha.translation_risk_reason: Human loss- and gain-of-function alleles both described with concordant mouse data.
localization: human SYS: distal renal tubule, parathyroid, choroid plexus
human growth plate: alpha-Klotho expression not established

key_refs.one_line_finding: Blocking FGF23 - which requires alpha-Klotho to signal - improves growth in XLH, quantifying the axis's growth relevance.

leptin_hormone.name: Leptin
leptin_hormone.summary: Leptin is a 16 kDa adipocyte-derived cytokine whose circulating concentration is proportional to fat mass and which functions as the permissive energy-sufficiency signal for the reproductive and growth axes. Below a threshold of adiposity, leptin falls, hypothalamic kisspeptin output drops and puberty is delayed or arrested - the mechanism underlying pubertal delay in anorexia nervosa, athletic amenorrhoea and undernutrition. Human congenital leptin deficiency proves the necessity: in a 145-child cohort with LEP, LEPR or MC4R deficiency, LEP-deficient children had 26% mortality and LEPR-deficient 9%, mainly from infection, with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in survivors; recombinant leptin restores puberty (saeed2023). At the plate itself leptin has a reported local action - it stimulates aromatase in the growth plate, which has been proposed to limit catch-up growth efficiency - but that is rodent work and the direct chondrocyte effect has not been demonstrated in human tissue.
leptin_hormone.human_evidence_note: Congenital human leptin deficiency causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism reversed by recombinant leptin - an interventional human experiment.
leptin_hormone.translation_risk_reason: The energy-sufficiency gate is human-proven; the local growth plate aromatase action is rodent-only.
localization: human SYS: adipocyte -> serum -> hypothalamic arcuate nucleus
rodent growth plate: leptin stimulates local aromatase (not confirmed in human tissue)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Untreated congenital LEP (26% mortality) and LEPR (9%) deficiency in a 145-child cohort, with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in survivors.

leptin_receptor.name: Leptin receptor (LEPR)
leptin_receptor.summary: LEPR is a class I cytokine receptor; only the long ObRb isoform has the intracellular box motifs needed to activate JAK2-STAT3, and it is that isoform in hypothalamic arcuate POMC and AgRP neurons that transduces the energy-sufficiency signal to the kisspeptin-GnRH axis. LEPR therefore shares JAK2 with the GH receptor, one of several points where the growth and energy axes use the same kinase. Biallelic human LEPR mutations produce severe early-onset obesity, hyperphagia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, with 9% mortality in an untreated cohort (saeed2023); unlike LEP deficiency the phenotype is not rescuable with recombinant leptin, and MC4R agonism (setmelanotide) is the effective intervention, which localises the defect downstream of the receptor. Lepr is also the marker of the LepR+ bone marrow stromal population, so the same gene tags a skeletal progenitor lineage - a separate biology that should not be conflated with the endocrine role.
leptin_receptor.human_evidence_note: Biallelic human LEPR mutations cause obesity with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; setmelanotide trials provide the interventional arm.
leptin_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Human genetics and human pharmacology are both available.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamic arcuate neurons (ObRb), broad low-level expression elsewhere
bone marrow: LepR marks a stromal progenitor population (distinct from the endocrine role)
human growth plate: LEPR expression not established

key_refs.one_line_finding: LEPR-deficient children in a 145-child cohort had 9% mortality with severe obesity and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

lin28b_gene.name: LIN28B
lin28b_gene.summary: LIN28B encodes an RNA-binding protein that blocks maturation of the let-7 microRNA family, and it was the first locus shown by genome-wide association to set human pubertal timing. In 4,714 women with replication in 16,373, each major allele at rs314276 was associated with 0.12 years earlier menarche (95% CI 0.08-0.16; combined P=3.6x10-16), plus earlier breast development and voice breaking, faster tempo of height growth in both sexes, and SHORTER adult height in women and men - the expected consequence of earlier growth cessation (ong2009). A second, partially correlated variant tags effects that are distinct and sex-specific, influencing prepubertal growth in girls and final height in boys, so LIN28B affects the entire postnatal growth trajectory rather than only the timing of the spurt (widn2010). Lin28a transgenic mice reproduce both the increased body size and the delayed puberty predicted from the human association (zhu2010), a rare instance of successful reverse translation from a human GWAS signal.
lin28b_gene.human_evidence_note: Replicated genome-wide association with age at menarche, pubertal tempo and adult height across tens of thousands of individuals.
lin28b_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human population genetics is primary and the mouse transgenic reproduces the predicted phenotype.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamus and other tissues; effect is on developmental timing
growth plate: LIN28B expression in human physis not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: LIN28B rs314276 major allele associated with 0.12 y earlier menarche and shorter adult height.
Partially correlated LIN28B variants tag distinct, sex-specific effects across the whole postnatal growth trajectory.
Lin28a transgenic mice reproduce the increased size and delayed puberty predicted by the human association.

mct8_transporter.name: MCT8 (SLC16A2) thyroid hormone transporter
mct8_transporter.summary: MCT8 is a 12-transmembrane facilitative transporter that carries T4 and, preferentially, T3 across plasma membranes; thyroid hormone is not freely membrane-permeant, so transporter expression determines which cells can respond to a given serum concentration. Hemizygous SLC16A2 loss of function in males causes MCT8 deficiency (Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome): severe psychomotor disability from cerebral hypothyroidism combined with peripheral thyrotoxicosis, because tissues that do not require MCT8 are exposed to the high serum T3 that results. The characteristic biochemistry is high T3, low-normal T4, normal-to-mildly-raised TSH and a raised T3/T4 ratio. The growth-relevant consequence is being underweight and poor somatic growth; the T3 analogue Triac, which enters cells independently of MCT8, lowered serum T3 from 4.58 to 1.66 nmol/L over a median 2.2 years and improved body-weight-for-age by 0.72 SD versus untreated historical controls (van2022). Whether growth plate chondrocytes depend on MCT8 or on alternative transporters (OATP1C1, MCT10, LAT1/2) has not been established in any species.
mct8_transporter.human_evidence_note: MCT8 deficiency is a well-characterised human X-linked disorder with a multi-site treatment cohort and quantified biochemical and anthropometric endpoints.
mct8_transporter.translation_risk_reason: Human genetic and interventional data dominate; the mouse Mct8-null does not reproduce the human neurological phenotype, so mouse data are the weaker source here, not the stronger.
localization: human SYS: brain endothelium, neurons, thyroid, liver, kidney
human growth plate: MCT8 expression not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: Triac lowered serum T3 from 4.58 to 1.66 nmol/L and improved weight-for-age by 0.72 SD in 67 MCT8-deficient patients.

mkrn3_gene.name: MKRN3
mkrn3_gene.summary: MKRN3 is a paternally expressed imprinted gene in the Prader-Willi critical region at 15q11-q13 encoding a RING-finger E3 ubiquitin ligase. Whole-exome sequencing of 40 members of 15 families with central precocious puberty found four novel heterozygous MKRN3 mutations (three frameshift, one missense) in 5 of the 15 families, affecting both sexes, and in every case inherited from the father - perfect segregation with the imprinting mode (abreu2013). Mkrn3 mRNA is high in the arcuate nucleus of prepubertal mice, falls immediately before puberty and stays low afterwards, so MKRN3 is a brake whose release permits puberty rather than a trigger. It acts within kisspeptin-expressing neurons (abreu2020) and interacts with IGF2BP1 to remodel hypothalamic plasticity. For stature the consequence is the standard precocious-puberty trade: accelerated growth and bone maturation followed by early fusion and reduced adult height.
mkrn3_gene.human_evidence_note: Paternally inherited MKRN3 loss-of-function mutations cause human central precocious puberty in multiple independent families with perfect imprinting segregation.
mkrn3_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human genetics is the primary evidence; mouse expression only supplies the timing.
localization: mouse hypothalamic arcuate nucleus: Mkrn3 mRNA high prepubertally, falls before puberty (abreu2013)
growth plate: no established expression

key_refs.one_line_finding: Paternally inherited MKRN3 mutations cause central precocious puberty in 5 of 15 families.
MKRN3 acts in kisspeptin neurons to restrain the reproductive axis.

pappa2_protease.name: PAPP-A2 (pappalysin-2)
pappa2_protease.summary: PAPP-A2 is a secreted metzincin metalloproteinase that liberates IGF-1 from inhibitory binding proteins by cleaving IGFBP-3 and IGFBP-5, the two IGFBPs that form the 150 kDa ternary complex with ALS. Two unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous PAPPA2 mutations (p.D643fs25* and p.Ala1033Val, both abolishing proteolytic activity in vitro) define the human phenotype: progressive postnatal growth failure, moderate microcephaly, thin long bones and mildly reduced bone density, with a paradoxical biochemistry of ELEVATED total IGF-1, IGF-2, IGFBP-3, IGFBP-5 and ALS but REDUCED free and bioactive IGF-1 (dauber2016). Size-exclusion chromatography confirmed the IGF-1 is trapped in ternary complexes. Affected adults reached heights of -2.16 to -3.81 SDS. This is the cleanest human demonstration that IGF bioavailability, not IGF concentration, sets stature. This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation (IGFBP-3/-5 plus ALS), pericellular proteolysis (PAPP-A, PAPP-A2) and protease inhibition (STC1, STC2) - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1. Reviews typically stop at 'IGF-1 level'; the human PAPPA2 kindreds show that total and free IGF-1 can move in opposite directions and that stature tracks the free fraction.
pappa2_protease.human_evidence_note: Two unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous loss-of-function PAPPA2 mutations, biochemically and functionally characterised, plus a Pappa2-null mouse with reduced femur length.
pappa2_protease.translation_risk_reason: The defining experiment is human genetic with in vitro functional confirmation.
localization: human SYS: circulating; measured by ELISA in serum
human growth plate: PAPP-A2 protein not localised in physeal tissue

key_refs.one_line_finding: Homozygous PAPPA2 mutations cause short stature with elevated total but reduced free/bioactive IGF-1.
Pappa2 knockout alters IGF-1 bioavailability with sex-specific metabolic and skeletal consequences in mouse.
Pappa2-null mice show reduced body and femur length and sex-specific responses to rhGH, rhIGF1 and rhPAPP-A2.

pappa_protease.name: PAPP-A (pappalysin-1)
pappa_protease.summary: PAPP-A is the founding pappalysin, a homodimeric metzincin that cleaves IGFBP-4 (strictly IGF-dependently) and, more slowly, IGFBP-2 and IGFBP-5. Because IGFBP-4 is a pure inhibitor of IGF action, PAPP-A activity converts a locally sequestered IGF pool into free ligand at the cell surface - a paracrine amplifier rather than an endocrine one. It is inhibited stoichiometrically by stanniocalcin-2 (and STC1), which locks it by an intersubunit disulfide and excludes IGFBP-4 from binding without occluding the catalytic site (kobber2022). PAPP-A is required in cartilage specifically: Pappa-knockout mice have reduced femur length and disorganised chondrocyte columns, pappaa-null zebrafish show shortened Meckel's cartilage with disorganised chondrocytes and reduced sox9a, ihha and col10a1, the zebrafish phenotype is mimicked by pharmacological IGF-signalling inhibition and rescued by recombinant IGF-I (harboe2024). In human population data, however, PAPP-A concentration - unlike PAPP-A2 and STC2 - does NOT associate with circulating total IGF-1 (nimptsch2024), consistent with PAPP-A acting locally rather than on the circulating pool. No human PAPPA loss-of-function short-stature syndrome has been reported, a notable asymmetry with PAPPA2. This node belongs to the IGF bioavailability control layer - ternary complex formation, pericellular proteolysis and protease inhibition - which sets the free IGF-1 concentration seen by chondrocyte IGF1R independently of total IGF-1.
pappa_protease.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is correlative (population associations of circulating PAPP-A with IGF axis components); no human PAPPA null growth phenotype is described.
pappa_protease.translation_risk_reason: The dwarfism phenotype is mouse-only and the human population data actually dissociate PAPP-A from circulating IGF-1, so the mouse result should not be read as a human growth mechanism.
localization: mouse growth plate: Pappa-null mice show reduced femur length and disorganised chondrocyte columns (harboe2024)
zebrafish Meckel's cartilage: pappaa-null shortens cartilage and disrupts chondrocyte organisation, rescued by rhIGF-I (harboe2024)
human SYS: circulating (also the first-trimester screening analyte)
human growth plate: PAPP-A protein not localised in physeal tissue

key_refs.one_line_finding: PAPP-A is required for IGF-dependent chondrocyte differentiation and columnar organisation in mouse and zebrafish cartilage.
In a human adult population PAPP-A2 and STC2, but not PAPP-A, associated with circulating total IGF-1.
Cryo-EM structure of the 2:2 PAPP-A.STC2 complex reveals a disulfide-locked inhibition mechanism.

parathyroid_hormone.name: Parathyroid hormone (PTH)
parathyroid_hormone.summary: PTH is an 84-residue peptide from parathyroid chief cells, secreted in response to a fall in ionised calcium sensed by CASR.
