It raises serum calcium by mobilising bone mineral and increasing renal calcium reabsorption, and it lowers serum phosphate by internalising the renal NaPi-2a/2c cotransporters; it also induces renal CYP27B1, so its effect on the growth plate is largely exerted through calcitriol and phosphate. PTH shares PTH1R with PTHrP, which is the actual growth-plate ligand and belongs to L3, so systemic PTH and local PTHrP converge on one receptor - the reason chronic hyperparathyroidism and PTH1R activating mutations (Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia) both disturb the hypertrophic transition. In secondary hyperparathyroidism of chronic kidney disease, high PTH with low calcitriol and phosphate retention combine to produce the growth failure and metaphyseal disorganisation of renal osteodystrophy.
parathyroid_hormone.human_evidence_note: Human hypoparathyroidism, pseudohypoparathyroidism, primary and secondary hyperparathyroidism and PTH1R mutations all produce characteristic skeletal phenotypes measured in humans.
parathyroid_hormone.translation_risk_reason: Human endocrine disorders provide the phenotypes directly.
localization: human SYS: parathyroid chief cell -> serum; targets kidney and bone
growth plate: acts via PTH1R shared with PTHrP; direct systemic PTH action on the plate not separated from PTHrP in human tissue

key_refs.one_line_finding: Dissociates PTH, calcium and phosphate contributions to rachitic growth plate change using three mouse models.
Links chondrocyte vitamin D signalling to the FGF23-phosphate axis that PTH also regulates.

phosphate_homeostasis.name: Phosphate homeostasis
phosphate_homeostasis.summary: Serum phosphate is set by intestinal absorption (NaPi-2b, calcitriol-dependent), renal reabsorption (NaPi-2a/2c, suppressed by PTH and FGF23) and bone exchange. Its growth plate role is not merely structural: normal phosphate is required for caspase-9-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis of terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes, and hypophosphataemia blocks that apoptosis, producing the expanded late hypertrophic layer that is the histological definition of rickets. This was established by comparing three mouse models - VDR-null, diet-induced hypophosphataemia with hypercalcaemia and suppressed PTH, and Phex-mutant (Hyp) mice with normal calcium and PTH - which isolate phosphate as the common variable (sabbagh2005). In humans the therapeutic test is X-linked hypophosphataemia: burosumab, an anti-FGF23 antibody that restores phosphate, gave 0.085 Z-score/year additional height velocity in children and 0.121 Z-score/year in adolescents versus burosumab-naive comparators across 641 participants (fukumoto2026).
phosphate_homeostasis.human_evidence_note: Human XLH cohorts with and without burosumab give quantified height-velocity effects of correcting phosphate, and human nutritional and genetic hypophosphataemias produce radiographic rickets.
phosphate_homeostasis.translation_risk_reason: The mechanism is mouse but the human therapeutic experiment produces the predicted growth effect.
localization: mouse HZ: phosphate required for caspase-9-dependent apoptosis of terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes (sabbagh2005)
human growth plate: local phosphate activity not measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Hypophosphataemia causes rickets by blocking caspase-9-mediated hypertrophic chondrocyte apoptosis.
Burosumab added 0.085 (children) and 0.121 (adolescents) height Z-score/year in 641 XLH participants.

pubertal_growth_spurt.name: Pubertal growth spurt
pubertal_growth_spurt.summary: The pubertal growth spurt is the transient acceleration of height velocity produced by the simultaneous rise of sex steroids and of GH/IGF-1, the latter itself amplified by estrogen acting on the somatotroph. Its quantitative structure in humans has been fitted from 24-h hormone profiles against individually modelled growth curves: growth velocity reaches half its maximum increment at morning estradiol 20 pmol/L in girls (95% CI 13-31) and at testosterone 3.1 nmol/L (2.4-4.2) or estradiol 6.5 pmol/L (3.2-13) in boys, and less than 25% of the potential growth remains once estradiol exceeds the Tanner B2 range (albin2012, albin2013). The spurt and its termination are therefore driven by the same hormone across a narrow concentration band, which is why interventions that shift pubertal timing (GnRH analogues, aromatase inhibitors, precocious puberty) trade growth velocity against remaining growth time. LIN28B variants that advance menarche by 0.12 years per allele also produce shorter adult height, the population-scale version of the same trade (ong2009).
pubertal_growth_spurt.human_evidence_note: Directly measured in humans by serial stadiometry with concurrent ultrasensitive hormone profiling.
pubertal_growth_spurt.translation_risk_reason: Rodents have no comparable pubertal height spurt and do not fuse their plates; the spurt is a human/primate phenomenon.
localization: human SYS: measured as whole-body height velocity
human growth plate: the cellular correlate of the spurt has never been observed in human tissue

key_refs.one_line_finding: Fitted estradiol dose-response for pubertal growth in girls, EC50 20 pmol/L.
Fitted testosterone and estradiol dose-responses for pubertal growth in boys.
LIN28B alleles that advance menarche also shorten adult height, quantifying the timing-versus-height trade.

seasonality_growth_velocity.name: Seasonality of growth velocity
seasonality_growth_velocity.summary: Human linear growth velocity varies with season, and the effect replicates - but the phase and the proposed driver do not agree across studies, which is itself the informative finding. In 11,587 three-month intervals from 2,277 prepubertal GH-treated children, height velocity scaled with the average number of daylight hours in the interval: +0.146 cm/yr per daylight hour in the first treatment year and +0.121 cm/yr per hour thereafter, with the effect increasing with latitude and no independent effect of calendar month; total annual growth did not differ between latitudes (shulman2013). In 9,409 Japanese infants tracked by a phone application, the winter-to-summer difference in length z-velocity was 0.0026 z/day (95% CI 0.0015-0.0036), about 13% of mean linear growth velocity at 6 months, with a summer peak (narumi2020). In 760 Danish 8-11 year olds, however, height velocity peaked in January-April against a 6.10 cm/yr mean, and - unlike earlier reports of a spring height peak with an autumn weight peak - weight, BMI and fat-free mass index peaked coincidentally (dalskov2016). Daylight-hours, temperature and nutritional-availability explanations have not been discriminated.
seasonality_growth_velocity.human_evidence_note: Three independent large human cohorts (US GH-treated children, Japanese infants, Danish schoolchildren) all show a seasonal signal in linear growth measured by direct anthropometry.
localization: human SYS: whole-body height velocity
human growth plate: no seasonal tissue-level observation exists

key_refs.one_line_finding: Height velocity rose 0.146 cm/yr per daylight hour in GH-treated children, increasing with latitude, with no independent month effect.
Japanese infants showed a summer peak in length velocity worth ~13% of mean growth velocity.
Danish 8-11 year olds showed a January-April height velocity peak with coincident weight/BMI/FFMI peaks, unlike earlier reports.

sleep_dependent_gh_release.name: Sleep-dependent GH release
sleep_dependent_gh_release.summary: The largest GH secretory burst of the human 24-h cycle occurs shortly after sleep onset and is temporally coupled to slow-wave sleep (SWS). The coupling is real but weaker than the textbook account implies. In a within-subject randomised polysomnography experiment in 14 pubertal children, auditory disruption cut SWS by 40.0 +/- 7.8% and lowered the GH pulse rate during N2 sleep relative to SWS (incidence rate ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.32-0.97), yet did NOT reduce total pulsatile GH secretion across the night (calvert2022). The system therefore compensates: GH bursts redistribute rather than disappear when SWS is fragmented for one night. Whether chronic sleep restriction reduces integrated GH exposure at the growth plate and slows linear growth in children has not been tested with a growth endpoint.
sleep_dependent_gh_release.human_evidence_note: Interventional human experiment in children with polysomnography plus frequent GH sampling; the outcome measured was GH secretion, not growth.
sleep_dependent_gh_release.translation_risk_reason: Human-only phenomenon as measured; rodents do not share the human sleep-architecture-to-GH coupling.
localization: human SYS: pituitary output measured in peripheral blood during polysomnography

key_refs.one_line_finding: Acute SWS disruption lowered GH pulse rate in N2 vs SWS (IRR 0.56) but did not diminish total pulsatile GH in pubertal children.

socs2_protein.name: SOCS2
socs2_protein.summary: SOCS2 is a STAT5B-induced SH2-domain protein that binds phosphorylated GHR tyrosines and, via its SOCS box and an elongin-cullin-RING E3 complex, ubiquitinates the receptor - a delayed negative feedback loop on GH signalling. Its physiological weight is shown by the Socs2-null mouse, which is markedly larger than wild type across the skeleton despite normal circulating GH and IGF-1, and whose overgrowth is GH-dependent (metcalf2000). SOCS2 is therefore the clearest example in this axis of a gain of stature produced by removing a brake rather than adding a ligand, which implies whole-body growth is not saturated at physiological GH concentrations. No human SOCS2 loss-of-function overgrowth syndrome has been established, and SOCS2's zonal role inside the growth plate has not been mapped in any species.
socs2_protein.human_evidence_note: No confirmed human SOCS2 loss-of-function overgrowth phenotype; the case for SOCS2 in human stature rests on mouse genetics and on SOCS2's position as a direct STAT5B target.
socs2_protein.translation_risk_reason: A large size effect in mouse with no human counterpart is exactly the pattern that should not be assumed to transfer; the human GH axis has different pulse structure and feedback set points. The effect size itself is abstract-only (paywalled figures), so it is recorded value_unverified and the node's confidence is dropped one grade.
localization: mouse SYS: liver and other GH targets
growth plate: SOCS2 protein not localised by zone in any species

key_refs.one_line_finding: Socs2-null mice show gigantism with normal GH and IGF-1, identifying SOCS2 as a brake on GH-GHR signalling.

somatomedin_hypothesis.name: Somatomedin hypothesis
somatomedin_hypothesis.summary: The somatomedin hypothesis (Salmon and Daughaday, 1957) states that GH does not act on cartilage itself but stimulates the liver to release a circulating mediator - later identified as IGF-1 - which is the proximate growth stimulus at the plate. Two independent liver-specific Igf1 deletions in mouse falsified the strong form. Yakar 1999 deleted hepatic Igf1 by Cre/loxP and found body weight, body length and femoral length indistinguishable from littermates despite near-complete loss of hepatic Igf1 mRNA; Sjogren 1999 obtained the same result with a 75% fall in serum IGF-1 (sjgren1999). Both confirm the liver is the principal SOURCE of blood IGF-1 while denying that blood IGF-1 is the principal DRIVER of postnatal growth. A weaker, threshold form survives: LID plus ALS-knockout double mutants, in which serum IGF-1 falls further, do show reduced linear growth with a shorter total growth plate and shorter proliferative and hypertrophic zones, 10% lower bone mineral density and >35% lower periosteal circumference, all partly restored by 4 weeks of IGF-1 (yakar2002). These are mouse data. The equivalent partition has never been made in humans.
somatomedin_hypothesis.human_evidence_note: Human IGF1, IGFALS, PAPPA2 and GHR mutations show that IGF-1 availability sets stature, but no human experiment separates hepatic from locally produced IGF-1.
somatomedin_hypothesis.translation_risk_reason: The falsification and the surviving threshold form are both mouse-only; mice reach adult size without epiphyseal fusion and their IGF-1 ternary complex biology differs quantitatively from human. Reviews routinely state the LID result as if it were a general fact about mammals.
localization: mouse SYS: hepatocyte-derived circulating IGF-1
mouse growth plate: total, proliferative and hypertrophic zone heights reduced only when serum IGF-1 falls below the LID/ALSKO double-mutant threshold (yakar2002)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Liver-specific Igf1 deletion left body weight, body length and femoral length unchanged despite loss of hepatic Igf1.
Hepatocyte Igf1 inactivation cut serum IGF-1 by 75% with no discernible effect on postnatal body growth.
LID+ALSKO double mutants fall below a circulating IGF-1 threshold and show shorter growth plates, lower BMD and thinner cortices, partly rescued by IGF-1.

somatostatin_hormone.name: Somatostatin (SST)
somatostatin_hormone.summary: Somatostatin is a cyclic peptide (SST-14 and SST-28) released from periventricular hypothalamic neurons that inhibits somatotroph GH release through Gi-coupled SSTR2 and SSTR5. Its role in growth is to sculpt the TROUGHS between GH bursts: burst timing in vivo is generated largely by episodic somatostatin withdrawal rather than by GHRH pulses alone, which is why GH remains pulsatile in humans carrying an inactivating GHRHR mutation. Pharmacological blockade separates pituitary from cartilage action cleanly - the somatostatin analogue octreotide abolished GH-stimulated tibial growth in hypophysectomised rats but had no effect on IGF-1-stimulated growth in the same model (zapf2002), placing somatostatin's growth effect entirely upstream of the plate. Trough depth also matters for the receptor: hepatic GHR and GHBP levels in rat track the continuous (trough) component of the GH pattern (gevers1996).
somatostatin_hormone.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is pharmacological and inferential (octreotide lowers GH and IGF-1 and is used to treat acromegaly); there is no human somatostatin loss-of-function growth phenotype.
somatostatin_hormone.translation_risk_reason: The dissection of pituitary versus cartilage action is rat pharmacology; human data are limited to acromegaly treatment responses.
localization: human SYS: hypothalamic periventricular nucleus; also gut and pancreatic delta cells
growth plate: no established local somatostatin action

key_refs.one_line_finding: Octreotide blocked GH-stimulated but not IGF-I-stimulated tibial growth in hypophysectomised rats.
Hepatic GHR/GHBP track the trough component of a patterned GH infusion, the component somatostatin sets.

stanniocalcin2.name: Stanniocalcin-2 (STC2)
stanniocalcin2.summary: STC2 is a secreted glycoprotein that is the endogenous inhibitor of PAPP-A and PAPP-A2, and therefore the top of the IGF bioavailability control layer. Cryo-EM of the 500 kDa 2:2 PAPP-A.STC2 complex shows an unusual mechanism: a specific intersubunit disulfide bond covalently locks STC2 onto PAPP-A so the complex cannot dissociate, and STC2 contacts a module at the extreme C-terminus of PAPP-A that is required for IGFBP-4 binding. The catalytic site itself remains accessible - the inhibited complex still hydrolyses a short synthetic IGFBP-4 peptide - so inhibition is by substrate exclusion, not active-site blockade (kobber2022). Common human STC2 variants are among the replicated coding-variant associations with adult height, and circulating STC2 associates with total IGF-1 in human adults (nimptsch2024). STC2 is thus a rare case where the structural mechanism, the human genetics and the human biomarker association all point the same way, yet its zonal role in the growth plate has never been examined.
stanniocalcin2.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is genetic association with adult height plus population-level correlation of circulating STC2 with total IGF-1; no human monogenic STC2 growth disorder is described.
stanniocalcin2.translation_risk_reason: The inhibitory mechanism was solved on human proteins and the height association is human genetic.
localization: human SYS: circulating
human growth plate: STC2 protein not localised

key_refs.one_line_finding: STC2 inhibits PAPP-A by covalent disulfide locking and substrate exclusion, leaving the active site accessible.
Circulating STC2 and PAPP-A2, but not PAPP-A, associate with total IGF-1 in human adults.
Pappalysin and stanniocalcin concentrations track IGF-I bioavailability in children with type 1 diabetes.

stat5b_tf.name: STAT5B
stat5b_tf.summary: STAT5B is the transcription factor carrying the growth-relevant arm of GH signalling. JAK2 phosphorylates STAT5B on Y699; phospho-STAT5B dimerises, enters the nucleus and transactivates IGF1, IGFALS and SOCS2 among others. Homozygous human STAT5B mutations produce GH insensitivity biochemically indistinguishable from GHR deficiency - high GH, very low IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 - but with an additional immune phenotype (lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis, eczema, autoimmunity), because STAT5B also transduces IL-2 receptor signalling in T cells (kofoed2003, hwa2005). This dual phenotype is the cleanest evidence that GH's effect on human stature runs through STAT5B specifically rather than through the ERK or PI3K branches of GHR signalling. Because circulating IGF-1 and ALS are both STAT5B targets, STAT5B loss collapses the ternary complex as well as IGF-1 production, so the biochemical picture is a compound one.
stat5b_tf.human_evidence_note: Homozygous STAT5B loss of function has been characterised in multiple unrelated humans with severe GH insensitivity plus immune disease; total absence of STAT5B protein was documented in at least one patient.
stat5b_tf.translation_risk_reason: The defining evidence is human genetic and biochemical.
localization: human SYS: hepatocyte nucleus (IGF1/IGFALS transcription); T lymphocytes
human growth plate: STAT5B phosphorylation status by zone not reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: A homozygous STAT5B mutation causes GH insensitivity with severe IGF-1 deficiency and immune dysfunction in a human.
Complete absence of STAT5B protein in a human produced severe GH insensitivity with pulmonary and immune disease.

aliases: signal transducer and activator of transcription 5B

testosterone_hormone.name: Testosterone
testosterone_hormone.summary: Testosterone drives the male pubertal growth spurt, but the fitted human dose-response shows it does so at concentrations at which its aromatised product is also rising. In 26 healthy boys, a 50% increase in growth velocity from prepubertal baseline to peak height velocity occurred at a morning testosterone of 3.1 nmol/L (95% CI 2.4-4.2), and boys within 4% of PHV had testosterone above 10 nmol/L and estradiol above 9 pmol/L (albin2013). Because these two curves are superimposed, human observational data cannot by themselves separate direct androgen action from aromatisation. Where the separation has been attempted, the answer favours aromatisation: in cultured fetal rat metatarsals neither androgen receptor agonists nor antagonists changed longitudinal growth (chagin2009). Clinically, non-aromatisable androgens such as oxandrolone increase growth velocity but with limited effect on adult height, consistent with a mainly aromatisation-dependent mechanism for the spurt itself.
testosterone_hormone.human_evidence_note: A fitted human dose-response between 24-h testosterone profiles and individually modelled growth velocity exists; it cannot separate direct from aromatised action.
testosterone_hormone.translation_risk_reason: The quantitative relationship is human; the mechanistic separation attempt is rat organ culture.
localization: human SYS: Leydig cell -> serum
growth plate: androgen receptor present but direct androgen effect on longitudinal growth not demonstrated

key_refs.one_line_finding: Testosterone EC50 3.1 nmol/L (95% CI 2.4-4.2) for a 50% growth velocity increase in healthy boys.
Androgen receptor agonists and antagonists did not change longitudinal growth of cultured fetal rat metatarsals.

thra_receptor.name: Thyroid hormone receptor alpha (THRA / TRalpha)
thra_receptor.summary: THRA encodes TRalpha1 (T3-binding) and TRalpha2 (non-T3-binding, dominant-negative-like), nuclear receptors that heterodimerise with RXR on thyroid hormone response elements and switch from corepressor to coactivator occupancy on T3 binding. TRalpha1 and TRalpha2 protein are present in reserve and proliferating zone chondrocytes of the rat tibial growth plate but are absent from hypertrophic cells (robson2000). In humans, heterozygous dominant-negative THRA variants (resistance to thyroid hormone alpha) cause growth retardation, delayed bone age and disharmonious short stature with low free T4, normal or mildly raised TSH and constipation; the endocrine picture is subtle enough to be mistaken for central hypothyroidism, and these children respond strikingly to rhGH (up to 2.5 SDS height gain in one patient) as well as to levothyroxine (jorge2025). THRA is therefore the isoform whose HUMAN loss produces a skeletal phenotype - which sits awkwardly against mouse chondrocyte data assigning the differentiation response to TRbeta.
thra_receptor.human_evidence_note: Heterozygous dominant-negative THRA variants in unrelated humans produce short stature with delayed bone age, established by exome sequencing plus functional characterisation.
thra_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Human genetics implicate THRA in stature while rodent chondrocyte experiments implicate TRbeta; the isoform assignment does not transfer cleanly between species.
localization: rat RZ and PZ: TRalpha1 and TRalpha2 protein confirmed by immunohistochemistry (robson2000)
rat HZ: TRalpha protein not detected (robson2000)
human growth plate: TRalpha protein not localised

key_refs.one_line_finding: Three unrelated children with heterozygous THRA variants had short stature, low free T4 and marked response to levothyroxine plus rhGH.
TRalpha1 and TRalpha2 are expressed in reserve and proliferating but not hypertrophic rat growth plate chondrocytes.

TRalpha1(-/-)beta(-/-) double-null mice show retarded growth and bone maturation NOT found in either single receptor-deficient mouse; deletion of TRalpha1 or TRbeta individually reveals only a small proportion of hypothyroid phenotypes, so the two isoforms cooperate with or substitute for each other on common pathways.

thrb_receptor.name: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRB / TRbeta)
thrb_receptor.summary: THRB encodes TRbeta1 and TRbeta2 and dominates T3 feedback on TSH in the pituitary and hypothalamus; heterozygous dominant-negative THRB mutations cause resistance to thyroid hormone beta, characterised by raised free T4 with non-suppressed TSH and, importantly, largely NORMAL adult stature. TRbeta1 protein is present in reserve and proliferating zone rat chondrocytes and absent from hypertrophic cells (robson2000). In cultured primary neonatal rib chondrocytes from TRalpha- and TRbeta-deficient mice, T3 reduced proliferation and accelerated differentiation normally in TRalpha-deficient cells but ALL T3 responses were abolished in TRbeta-deficient cells, and T3 upregulated TRbeta1 itself (rabier2006). The direct conflict between this mouse result and the human observation that THRA, not THRB, mutations cause short stature is unresolved and is logged as a contradiction; possible explanations include rib versus long-bone chondrocyte differences, compensation in the germline knockouts, or a genuine species difference in isoform deployment.
thrb_receptor.human_evidence_note: Human RTHbeta (dominant-negative THRB) is well characterised and, in contrast to RTHalpha, does not typically cause short stature - a human negative result that constrains TRbeta's role in stature.
thrb_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Mouse chondrocyte data make TRbeta necessary for T3 action while the human phenotype makes THRA the stature-relevant isoform; transferring the mouse conclusion to human growth plate would be unsupported.
localization: rat RZ and PZ: TRbeta1 protein confirmed (robson2000)
rat HZ: TRbeta1 not detected (robson2000)
mouse rib chondrocyte: TRbeta required for all T3 responses in vitro (rabier2006)
human growth plate: TRbeta protein not localised

key_refs.one_line_finding: T3 responses were abolished in TRbeta-deficient but preserved in TRalpha-deficient mouse rib chondrocytes.
TRbeta1 protein is present in reserve and proliferating but not hypertrophic rat growth plate chondrocytes.

TRalpha1(-/-)beta(-/-) double-null mice show retarded growth and bone maturation NOT found in either single receptor-deficient mouse; deletion of TRalpha1 or TRbeta individually reveals only a small proportion of hypothyroid phenotypes, so the two isoforms cooperate with or substitute for each other on common pathways.

thyroid_hormone_t3.name: Triiodothyronine (T3)
thyroid_hormone_t3.summary: T3 is the receptor-active thyroid hormone and the switch that moves growth plate chondrocytes out of the resting/proliferative programme into hypertrophy. Its action is reciprocal, not simply stimulatory: in rat growth plate chondrocytes in agarose suspension T3 INHIBITED clonal expansion and proliferation while simultaneously INDUCING alkaline phosphatase activity, collagen X mRNA and alcian-blue-positive matrix within 7 days (robson2000). This explains the paradoxical growth plate in juvenile hypothyroidism, where the plate is disorganised and chondrocytes fail to hypertrophy even though proliferation is not the limiting step. Downstream, T3 acts through IGF-1-dependent modulation of beta-catenin (wang2010) and regulates PTHrP and its receptor during hypertrophic differentiation (stevens2000), placing it upstream of the PTHrP-Ihh loop rather than parallel to it. Human relevance is established by the growth arrest of untreated juvenile hypothyroidism and its reversal on levothyroxine; in the neonatal screening era final height in congenital hypothyroidism is normal and actually exceeds target height (delvecchio2015).
thyroid_hormone_t3.human_evidence_note: Untreated juvenile hypothyroidism arrests human linear growth and levothyroxine restores it; screened and early-treated congenital hypothyroidism reaches normal final height.
thyroid_hormone_t3.translation_risk_reason: The clinical requirement is human-proven, but the zonal mechanism (RZ/PZ receptor localisation, reciprocal proliferation/differentiation effect) is rat and mouse in vitro.
localization: rat RZ/PZ: TRalpha1, TRalpha2 and TRbeta1 protein present (robson2000)
rat HZ: thyroid hormone receptors NOT detected - hypertrophic cells are not the direct T3 target (robson2000)
human growth plate: T3 concentration and receptor occupancy by zone not measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: T3 inhibits clonal expansion and proliferation while inducing hypertrophic markers; TRs are in reserve/proliferating but not hypertrophic chondrocytes.
Thyroid hormones regulate hypertrophic differentiation and PTHrP/PPR expression during endochondral bone formation.
T3-mediated chondrocyte growth and differentiation requires IGF-1 modulation of beta-catenin signalling.
Final height in 215 screened congenital hypothyroid patients was -0.1 SDS, above target height -0.8 SDS.

thyroxine_t4.name: Thyroxine (T4)
thyroxine_t4.summary: T4 is the quantitatively dominant secretory product of the thyroid and is essentially a prohormone: it has low affinity for thyroid hormone receptors and must be 5'-deiodinated to T3 by DIO1 or DIO2 to act. Because DIO2 and DIO3 are expressed locally in skeletal tissue, T4 sets a systemic supply while local deiodinase balance sets the T3 concentration each tissue actually sees - the reason serum T4 and tissue thyroid status can dissociate. Clinically T4 (levothyroxine) is the replacement given in congenital hypothyroidism, and in the neonatal-screening era it restores final height to normal, exceeding target height in a 215-patient 20-year cohort (delvecchio2015). Notably in that cohort neither age at diagnosis nor starting levothyroxine dose predicted final height, which argues the growth endpoint saturates once replacement is adequate. In THRA-mutant children free T4 is characteristically low with normal or only mildly raised TSH (jorge2025), an unusual pattern that is easily misread as central hypothyroidism.
thyroxine_t4.human_evidence_note: Levothyroxine replacement in human congenital and acquired hypothyroidism restores linear growth and final height - interventional human evidence.
thyroxine_t4.translation_risk_reason: Human interventional and cohort data are the primary evidence.
localization: human SYS: thyroid follicular cell -> serum, largely protein-bound
growth plate: local conversion to T3 by DIO2 presumed but not quantified in human physis

key_refs.one_line_finding: Final height was normal (-0.1 SDS) and independent of age at diagnosis or starting LT4 dose in 215 screened patients.
THRA-mutant children have low free T4 with variable TSH, short stature, and respond well to levothyroxine plus rhGH.

vitamin_d_calcitriol.name: 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol)
vitamin_d_calcitriol.summary: Calcitriol is the VDR ligand generated by renal CYP27B1 1alpha-hydroxylation of 25(OH)D, under PTH stimulation and FGF23 inhibition. Its dominant action on the growth plate is indirect: it raises intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption, and it is the resulting mineral ion supply, not VDR signalling in cartilage, that determines whether the plate mineralises normally. The decisive experiment is that normalising mineral ion homeostasis with a rescue diet prevents rachitic growth plate changes in VDR-null mice, showing rickets is secondary to hypophosphataemia (and hypocalcaemia/hyperparathyroidism) rather than to loss of VDR action in chondrocytes (sabbagh2005). A residual direct component exists - receptor-dependent 1,25(OH)2D action was required for normal growth plate maturation in Npt2a-null mice (miedlich2010), and VDR in chondrocytes drives osteoclastogenesis and regulates osteoblast FGF23 production (masuyama2006) - so the plate both responds to and feeds back on the mineral axis.
vitamin_d_calcitriol.human_evidence_note: Nutritional rickets and its reversal with vitamin D, and hereditary 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D-resistant rickets, are direct human evidence at the tissue level (radiographic growth plate changes).
vitamin_d_calcitriol.translation_risk_reason: Human rickets provides the phenotype and its treatment response; mouse genetics only resolves whether the mechanism is direct or mineral-mediated.
localization: mouse growth plate: VDR-dependent effects on hypertrophic zone maturation demonstrated (miedlich2010)
human growth plate: calcitriol concentration and VDR occupancy not measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Rickets in VDR-null mice is secondary to hypophosphataemia, which blocks caspase-9-mediated hypertrophic chondrocyte apoptosis.
Receptor-dependent 1,25(OH)2D actions are required for normal growth plate maturation in Npt2a-null mice.
VDR in chondrocytes promotes osteoclastogenesis and regulates osteoblast FGF23 production.

vitamin_d_receptor.name: Vitamin D receptor (VDR)
vitamin_d_receptor.summary: VDR is a nuclear receptor that heterodimerises with RXR on vitamin D response elements. Its growth plate role has been dissected more cleanly than most: VDR-null mice develop rickets with an expanded late hypertrophic layer caused by impaired chondrocyte apoptosis, but a calcium/phosphate/lactose rescue diet that normalises mineral ion homeostasis prevents the rachitic changes, showing that most of the phenotype is mineral-mediated rather than a direct cartilage VDR requirement (sabbagh2005). A residual chondrocyte-autonomous role remains: VDR in chondrocytes promotes osteoclastogenesis at the chondro-osseous junction and regulates osteoblast FGF23 production (masuyama2006), making the hypertrophic chondrocyte an endocrine participant in phosphate homeostasis rather than only a target of it. Human hereditary 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin-D-resistant rickets (VDR loss of function, often with alopecia) reproduces the phenotype and responds to high-dose calcium, consistent with the mineral-mediated model.
vitamin_d_receptor.human_evidence_note: Human VDR loss-of-function (hereditary vitamin D-resistant rickets) produces radiographic rickets that responds to high-dose calcium, matching the mouse mineral-rescue result.
vitamin_d_receptor.translation_risk_reason: Human and mouse loss-of-function phenotypes and their calcium rescue agree.
localization: mouse growth plate: VDR present in hypertrophic chondrocytes; regulates osteoclastogenesis and osteoblast FGF23 (masuyama2006)
human growth plate: VDR protein not quantified by zone

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mineral ion normalisation prevents rachitic growth plate change in VDR-null mice.
Chondrocyte VDR regulates osteoclastogenesis and osteoblast FGF23 production.

adamts4.name: ADAMTS4 (aggrecanase-1)
adamts4.summary: ADAMTS4 is a secreted aggrecanase that cleaves aggrecan at the Glu373-Ala374 bond in the interglobular domain and at further sites in the chondroitin sulphate region, generating the ARGS neoepitope fragments found in human synovial fluid. In mouse it is dispensable: Adamts4-null mice are not protected from surgical osteoarthritis whereas Adamts5-null mice are, and Adamts4/Adamts5 double-null mice are physiologically normal, which means neither aggrecanase is required for skeletal growth or for growth plate development in mouse. In human cartilage explants the division of labour is different - both ADAMTS-4 and ADAMTS-5 contribute to aggrecan degradation - so the murine ADAMTS5 dominance should not be assumed for humans. ADAMTS4 is inhibited potently and selectively by TIMP-3 (sub-nanomolar Ki for the N-terminal domain) while TIMP-1, -2 and -4 are weak or inactive.
adamts4.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is cartilage explant pharmacology and neoepitope detection in synovial fluid; there is no human ADAMTS4 loss-of-function phenotype.
adamts4.translation_risk_reason: Mouse assigns dominance to ADAMTS5 whereas human explants implicate both, so the species differ in exactly the parameter of interest.
localization: human articular cartilage explants: ADAMTS-4 contributes to aggrecan degradation alongside ADAMTS-5 (song2007)
human growth plate zonal ADAMTS4: not established

key_refs.one_line_finding: Adamts4/Adamts5 double knockout mice are physiologically normal and protected from surgical osteoarthritis
The N-terminal domain of TIMP-3 inhibits ADAMTS4 and ADAMTS5 with sub-nanomolar Ki
TIMP-3 inhibits ADAMTS4 while TIMP-1, -2 and -4 are weak or inactive
Aggrecan degradation in human articular cartilage explants is mediated by both ADAMTS-4 and ADAMTS-5

adamts5.name: ADAMTS5 (aggrecanase-2)
adamts5.summary: ADAMTS5 is the dominant murine aggrecanase. Deletion of catalytically active ADAMTS5, but not of ADAMTS4, prevents aggrecan loss and cartilage degradation in surgically induced murine osteoarthritis, and the double Adamts4/Adamts5 knockout is physiologically normal. This second result is the growth-plate-relevant one: aggrecan is normally cleared from the hypertrophic zone before mineralization, yet mice lacking both aggrecanases and mice carrying MMP-cleavage-resistant aggrecan both develop normal skeletons and do not accumulate aggrecan. The mechanism of aggrecan removal from the growth plate is therefore not established by any of the obvious candidates, and remains one of the real holes in this layer. ADAMTS5 is inhibited by TIMP-3 with sub-nanomolar Ki and by no other TIMP appreciably. In human cartilage explants ADAMTS-4 and ADAMTS-5 both contribute, so the murine hierarchy does not transfer cleanly.
adamts5.human_evidence_note: No human ADAMTS5 loss-of-function phenotype; human data are cartilage explant studies implicating both ADAMTS-4 and -5.
adamts5.translation_risk_reason: Species disagree on which aggrecanase dominates, and the mouse null gives no skeletal phenotype at all.
localization: mouse cartilage: ADAMTS5 is the operative aggrecanase in surgical OA (glasson2005)
human growth plate zonal ADAMTS5: not established

key_refs.one_line_finding: Deletion of catalytically active ADAMTS5 prevents cartilage aggrecan loss in murine surgical osteoarthritis
Adamts4/Adamts5 double knockout mice are physiologically normal and protected from surgical osteoarthritis
The N-terminal domain of TIMP-3 inhibits ADAMTS4 and ADAMTS5 with sub-nanomolar Ki
Aggrecan made resistant to MMP cleavage at N341-F342 does not accumulate and the mice develop normally, excluding MMP aggrecanolysis in the growth plate

aggrecan_acan.name: Aggrecan (ACAN)
aggrecan_acan.summary: Aggrecan is the large chondroitin-sulphate/keratan-sulphate proteoglycan that carries essentially all of the fixed negative charge of cartilage and therefore all of its osmotic swelling pressure. Its N-terminal G1 domain binds hyaluronan, the interaction is stabilised by link protein (HAPLN1), and up to a hundred monomers decorate a single hyaluronan filament to form the aggregate that is immobilised inside the collagen network. In the growth plate aggrecan is synthesised across all zones but with a strong zonal gradient of metabolism: in bovine distal tibial growth plate explants both synthesis and breakdown rates are highest in the resting/proliferative third and lowest in the lower hypertrophic third, and about 90% of newly synthesised proteoglycan is aggregation-competent. Aggrecan is removed from the hypertrophic zone before mineralization, but not by MMPs: mice engineered with aggrecan resistant to MMP cleavage at the N341-F342 interglobular-domain site grow normally and do not accumulate aggrecan, which excludes MMP aggrecanolysis as the removal mechanism and leaves ADAMTS cleavage at Glu373-Ala374 and simple dilution as the surviving candidates. Human ACAN haploinsufficiency is one of the commonest monogenic causes of idiopathic short stature.
aggrecan_acan.human_evidence_note: Heterozygous ACAN loss-of-function is a directly measured human short-stature syndrome with height SDS data in >100 individuals; the zonal biochemistry is bovine.
aggrecan_acan.translation_risk_reason: The human genetics is direct, but every quantitative statement about zonal aggrecan metabolism comes from bovine explants and every turnover half-life from adult human articular cartilage rather than physis.
localization: bovine growth plate RZ/PZ: highest aggrecan synthesis and turnover (shapses1994)
bovine growth plate lower HZ: reduced aggrecan gene expression adjacent to the calcification zone (shapses1994)
human growth plate: aggrecan present in all zones; zonal turnover rates not measured

key_refs.one_line_finding: Aggrecan synthesis and breakdown are both fastest in the resting/proliferative zone of bovine growth plate
MMP-resistant aggrecan mice grow normally and do not accumulate aggrecan, excluding MMP aggrecanolysis
Aggrecan monomer half-life 3.4 years, free G1 half-life 25 years in adult human articular cartilage
ACAN heterozygotes reach median adult height -2.8 SDS with advanced bone age

ankh_transporter.name: ANKH / ANK (progressive ankylosis protein)
ankh_transporter.summary: ANKH is a multipass plasma membrane protein of hypertrophic and terminally differentiating growth plate chondrocytes that was for two decades described as a PPi transporter carrying intracellular PPi to the extracellular space. That description is wrong in its mechanism. In HEK293 cells engineered to lack ENPP1 entirely, introducing ANKH produces robust ATP release with NO increase in extracellular PPi, and Enpp1-/- mouse bone contains under 2.5% of wild-type PPi despite intact Ank. ANKH therefore exports nucleoside triphosphates, predominantly ATP, which ENPP1 then converts extracellularly to PPi and AMP; the same is true of ABCC6, so both transporters that maintain plasma PPi do so by extruding NTPs. ANKH supplies about 25% of plasma PPi and ABCC6 60-70%. This matters for the growth plate because the older chondrocyte literature - blocking Ank raises intra- and extracellular PPi and blocks mineralization, overexpressing Ank in hypertrophic cells lowers PPi and induces alkaline phosphatase, collagen I, osteocalcin and mineralization - was interpreted as direct PPi transport and must be reread as ATP export plus local ENPP1 activity. ANK expression in growth plate chondrocytes is oxygen-dependent and HIF-1 regulated, tying the hypoxic gradient across the plate to PPi handling. In humans ANKH gain-of-function causes craniometaphyseal dysplasia and chondrocalcinosis; loss causes a distinct skeletal phenotype.
ankh_transporter.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is genetic (ANKH gain-of-function craniometaphyseal dysplasia and chondrocalcinosis); the transport mechanism is established in human cell lines but not in human cartilage.
ankh_transporter.translation_risk_reason: Mechanism established in HEK293 overexpression and mouse bone; whether ANKH-derived ATP is the dominant PPi source in the human hypertrophic zone specifically is untested.
localization: mouse/rat growth plate HZ and terminal HZ: Ank expressed, highest in terminally differentiated mineralizing chondrocytes (wang2005)
mouse matrix vesicles: ANK absent, unlike NPP1 (harmey2004)
human growth plate: ANKH zonal protein localisation unconfirmed

key_refs.one_line_finding: ANKH exports ATP, not PPi; Enpp1-/- mouse bone contains <2.5% of wild-type PPi, so ENPP1 is required for all ANK-attributable PPi, i.e. PPi arising downstream of ANKH ATP export
Blocking Ank in terminal growth plate chondrocytes raises PPi and blocks mineralization; Ank overexpression lowers PPi and induces mineralization
TNAP, NPP1 and ANK coordinately set extracellular PPi and osteopontin; Enpp1 or ank loss genetically rescues Akp2-/- hypomineralization
ANK expression in growth plate chondrocytes is oxygen-tension dependent and HIF-1 mediated

biglycan_protein.name: Biglycan (BGN)
biglycan_protein.summary: Biglycan is the class I SLRP most closely related to decorin, differing in carrying two rather than one glycosaminoglycan chain, and it is the more important of the two for bone. Biglycan-null mice have reduced bone mass and shortened long bones with an osteoporosis-like phenotype that worsens with age, attributed to defective marrow stromal cell function. Direct comparison of single and double knockouts shows the hierarchy: Bgn deletion but not Dcn deletion reduces trabecular bone mass, with the double knockout worst; both genotypes lose NMR-measured bound water and fracture toughness, with the largest losses in Bgn-null and double-null; and AFM shows decreased in situ permanent energy dissipation with INCREASED elastic modulus in the extrafibrillar matrix, an effect abolished by dehydration. So the SLRPs make bone tougher, not stiffer, by holding water. Decorin is markedly upregulated in Bgn-null mice while biglycan is only modestly upregulated in Dcn-null mice, confirming biglycan is the dominant partner. Biglycan is X-linked in humans, and BGN variants cause Meester-Loeys syndrome (an X-linked aortopathy), but no human biglycan short-stature syndrome is established.
biglycan_protein.human_evidence_note: No human BGN loss-of-function growth plate phenotype was located; the described human BGN disease is aortic.
biglycan_protein.translation_risk_reason: Entirely murine; the human X-linked BGN phenotype does not primarily involve longitudinal growth.
localization: mouse bone extrafibrillar matrix: biglycan-dependent water retention demonstrated by AFM and NMR (hua2025)
human growth plate zonal biglycan: not established

key_refs.one_line_finding: Biglycan-null mice have reduced bone mass and shortened long bones, an osteoporosis-like phenotype
Bgn but not Dcn deletion lowers trabecular bone mass; both lower NMR bound water and fracture toughness, and raise extrafibrillar modulus in a hydration-dependent way
Decorin-null mice have coarse irregular collagen fibrils and fragile skin

cartilage_osmotic_swelling.name: Cartilage osmotic swelling pressure
cartilage_osmotic_swelling.summary: The compressive stiffness of cartilage is largely osmotic. Aggrecan's sulphate and carboxylate groups are immobilised in the collagen network at a fixed charge density of order 0.2-0.3 mol/L, counterions accumulate to preserve electroneutrality, and the resulting Donnan imbalance draws water in until the collagen network's tension balances it. The size of that pressure has been measured directly rather than inferred: confined compression stress-relaxation of immature bovine (n=18) and mature human (n=6) cartilage in baths of varying osmolarity shows that the real swelling pressure is only about ONE THIRD of the ideal Donnan prediction, i.e. the tissue is markedly non-ideal, and that material properties themselves are salt-concentration dependent: the aggregate modulus rises roughly threefold as the bath goes from hypertonic 2 M to hypotonic 0.001 M NaCl (bovine 0.420 +/- 0.109 to 1.266 +/- 0.438 MPa; human 0.499 +/- 0.208 to 1.597 +/- 0.455 MPa). Donnan osmotic and Poisson-Boltzmann electrostatic interactions coexist in the same tissue, which is why single-parameter Donnan models overestimate. All of these measurements are articular cartilage. No equivalent direct swelling-pressure measurement exists for growth plate, although epiphyseal cartilage fixed charge density has been measured by sodium NMR and lies in the same range.
cartilage_osmotic_swelling.human_evidence_note: Mature human articular cartilage was measured directly alongside bovine tissue in the same apparatus; growth plate was not.
cartilage_osmotic_swelling.translation_risk_reason: Human articular cartilage behaves like bovine here, but growth plate matrix has different aggrecan and collagen composition, so extrapolating the number to the physis is not justified.
localization: articular cartilage: direct measurement (zimmerman2021)
growth plate: swelling pressure never measured directly

key_refs.one_line_finding: Direct in situ cartilage osmotic pressure is ~1/3 of the ideal Donnan prediction; aggregate modulus rises threefold from 2 M to 0.001 M NaCl in both bovine and human cartilage
Sodium NMR gives FCD -0.28 +/- 0.03 M in calf articular cartilage and -0.19 to -0.35 M in calf epiphyseal cartilage

chondron.name: Chondron
chondron.summary: A chondron is the chondrocyte together with its pericellular matrix and capsule, treated as the mechanical unit of cartilage. In the growth plate the geometry differs fundamentally from articular cartilage: resting zone chondrocytes sit singly or in pairs with no preferred arrangement, while proliferative and hypertrophic chondrocytes are stacked inside long tubular chondrons that are the columns. This makes the chondron the load-transmitting element of the physis. Direct measurement of chondron deformation under compression shows that the apparently random strain fields reported in the compressed growth plate are not random at all: the chondron tubes undergo large bending deformations, kinking preferentially at the reserve/proliferative zone interface at 20%, 30% and 40% applied compression. The authors propose that this bending is itself the cue that aligns dividing cells longitudinally to maintain the column. Chondrons are also the failure interface: in bovine physeal tensile testing, fracture propagates leaving bundles of intact chondrons on the metaphyseal side, torn away from an interterritorial matrix that stays on the epiphyseal side.
chondron.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate chondron mechanics were located; the human physeal tensile specimens tested to date came from two cerebral palsy patients and were not analysed at chondron level.
chondron.translation_risk_reason: Chondron mechanics in the physis are bovine only.
localization: growth plate PZ and HZ: chondrocytes arranged inside tubular chondrons; RZ cells singly or in pairs (vendra2018)
bovine physis tensile failure plane: chondrons remain intact on the metaphyseal side (williams2001)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Growth plate chondrons bend and kink at the reserve/proliferative interface under 20-40% compression, explaining nonuniform strain fields
Chondron pericellular matrix morphology varies by zone and deforms under compression
In situ AFM stiffness mapping gives PCM:ECM modulus ratio ~0.35 in human, porcine and murine articular cartilage
Physeal tensile fracture leaves intact chondron bundles on the metaphyseal side torn from interterritorial matrix on the epiphyseal side

collagen_crosslinking.name: Collagen crosslinking in cartilage
collagen_crosslinking.summary: Cartilage collagen owes its tensile strength to covalent crosslinks formed by lysyl oxidase, which oxidatively deaminates specific telopeptide lysine and hydroxylysine residues to aldehydes that then condense with helical residues on neighbouring molecules. In cartilage the pathway is the hydroxylysine route, so divalent ketoimines mature into the trivalent 3-hydroxypyridinium crosslinks hydroxylysyl pyridinoline (HP) and lysyl pyridinoline (LP); collagen II is bonded head-to-tail at the two telopeptide-to-helix sites, and collagen IX is covalently attached to the collagen II fibril surface and to other collagen IX molecules at at least six identified sites, all of which are occupied in matrix-resident collagen IX. This makes the fibril a single covalent polymer that cannot be reassembled if broken, which is why cartilage collagen turnover is essentially nil in adults and why damaged collagen architecture is not recapitulated. Crosslink chemistry is a readout of mineralization status as well: Phospho1-/- bone shows altered DHLNL/HLNL and pyridinoline/deoxypyridinoline ratios alongside its hypomineralization. Lysyl oxidase itself is essential - Lox-null mice die perinatally - but no zone-resolved crosslink density measurement of any growth plate was located in this sweep, and the human cartilage crosslink data are articular, not physeal.
collagen_crosslinking.human_evidence_note: Human articular cartilage pyridinoline content has been measured across age, but no human physeal crosslink data were located and no human LOX deficiency skeletal phenotype is described here.
collagen_crosslinking.translation_risk_reason: The chemistry is conserved and human articular data exist, but the growth plate specifically has not been measured in any species.
localization: cartilage collagen fibril: HP/LP crosslinks at telopeptide-to-helix sites (eyre2002)
growth plate zones: crosslink density by zone not measured in any species located here

key_refs.one_line_finding: Cartilage collagen II is crosslinked head-to-tail by hydroxylysyl pyridinoline at two telopeptide-to-helix sites; collagen IX carries at least six crosslink sites all occupied in the matrix pool
Hydroxypyridinium crosslink content of human articular cartilage collagen rises with age on a different trajectory from bone
Lox-null mice die perinatally with aortic aneurysm and diaphragmatic defects from failed collagen and elastin crosslinking
Phospho1-/- bone shows altered DHLNL/HLNL and pyridinoline/deoxypyridinoline crosslink ratios alongside hypomineralization

collagen_fibril_stoichiometry.name: Cartilage collagen fibril stoichiometry (II:IX:XI)
collagen_fibril_stoichiometry.summary: Cartilage fibrils are not pure collagen II. They are heterotypic copolymers in which collagen XI forms the nucleating core, collagen II supplies the bulk of the 4D-staggered lattice, and collagen IX decorates the fibril surface covalently crosslinked to collagen II. The stoichiometry is developmental, not fixed: in young growth cartilage the mass proportions are approximately 80% collagen II, >=10% collagen IX and >=10% collagen XI, which shifts on maturation to >=90% II, ~3% XI and ~1% IX in adult articular cartilage. The functional consequence is fibril diameter: reconstitution of purified collagens shows that a mixture of II and XI produces uniform ~20 nm fibrils only while the molar excess of II over XI is below eight-fold, above which control is lost and irregular tactoids form; collagen IX is not required for diameter control but sharply increases assembly efficiency. So the '8:1:1' figure quoted in reviews is a mass proportion of young growth cartilage that coincides numerically with the II:XI molar ceiling for diameter control, and the two are frequently conflated. The values above were determined in chick embryonic sternum and bovine/foetal cartilage by CNBr peptide and antibody quantitation; no equivalent quantitation exists for human physeal cartilage specifically, and mammalian fibrils are additionally heterogeneous, with decorin-bearing and collagen IX-bearing fibril subpopulations occupying different territories of the same tissue. Human physeal tissue has however been examined ultrastructurally: in human juvenile rib growth plate collagen XI is confined to fibrils under 25 nm and is absent from thick fibrils even after chaotropic disruption, while collagens II and IX decorate fibrils of all diameters - and the thin fibrils are concentrated in the HYPERTROPHIC zone, the thick ones in the resting zone, with a mixture in the proliferative zone. So the II:XI ratio in the human growth plate is zonally graded, lowest (most XI-rich) where mineralization is about to occur.
collagen_fibril_stoichiometry.human_evidence_note: Collagen XI, IX and II have been localised ultrastructurally in human juvenile rib growth plate by immuno-EM, establishing the zonal fibril-diameter pattern; the mass stoichiometry has still not been quantified in human physeal tissue.

collagen_type_ii.name: Collagen type II (COL2A1)
collagen_type_ii.summary: Collagen II is the fibril-forming backbone of all hyaline cartilage including every zone of the growth plate, supplying roughly two-thirds of the dry mass of cartilage collagen and forming a 4D-staggered polymer heavily crosslinked head-to-tail by hydroxylysyl pyridinoline at the two telopeptide-to-helix sites. Two splice forms exist: IIA retains the cysteine-rich N-propeptide and is made by prechondrocytes and perichondrium, IIB lacks it and is the form made by differentiated chondrocytes; the alpha3(XI) chain of collagen XI is in fact an alternatively glycosylated alpha1(II)B product, so collagen II and XI are not genetically independent. Collagen II is not the diameter-determining component: fibril width is set by the collagen XI content and the II:XI ratio. Its mechanical role is to resist the swelling pressure of the aggrecan gel, so tensile stiffness of cartilage depends on collagen network integrity while compressive stiffness depends on proteoglycan charge. In the growth plate the collagen II network is progressively lost from the lower hypertrophic zone as MMP-13 cleaves it, and the type II C-propeptide accumulates there. Human COL2A1 mutations produce a graded series from lethal achondrogenesis II/hypochondrogenesis through spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita to Stickler syndrome and Kniest dysplasia, which is the human proof that collagen II dosage and structure set long-bone length.
collagen_type_ii.human_evidence_note: COL2A1 mutations cause a well-characterised human allelic series (achondrogenesis II, SEDC, Kniest, Stickler) with directly measured height deficits; the biochemistry is largely bovine/human articular cartilage.
collagen_type_ii.translation_risk_reason: The gene, the splice forms and the disease series are established directly in humans.

collagen_type_ix.name: Collagen type IX (COL9A1/2/3)
collagen_type_ix.summary: Collagen IX is a FACIT collagen that sits on the surface of the collagen II/XI fibril, covalently attached by lysyl-oxidase-derived pyridinoline and divalent crosslinks at at least six identified sites distributed across the alpha1(IX), alpha2(IX) and alpha3(IX) chains, all of which are occupied in matrix-resident collagen IX. Its NC4 globular domain and COL3 domain project away from the fibril surface, so collagen IX acts as a covalently anchored molecular projection from the fibril rather than as a load-bearing lattice element. It is enriched on the thinnest fibrils of the pericellular basket. Functionally it is not required for fibril formation: Col9a1-null mice have grossly normal skeletal development and only develop non-inflammatory degenerative joint disease from about four months. It is required for correct assembly of the fibril surface, since matrilin-3 fails to integrate normally into cartilage matrix in collagen IX-null mice. In humans, COL9A1/2/3 mutations cause multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (mild short stature and early osteoarthritis) rather than a lethal chondrodysplasia, which matches the mouse: collagen IX is a fibril-surface organiser rather than a load-bearing element.
collagen_type_ix.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is genetic: COL9A1/2/3 mutations cause multiple epiphyseal dysplasia; no direct human growth plate biochemistry.
collagen_type_ix.translation_risk_reason: Mouse null phenotype (late osteoarthritis, normal growth) and human MED (mild short stature plus early OA) agree in kind, but the human quantitative growth deficit is not explained by any mouse measurement.

collagen_type_x.name: Collagen type X (COL10A1)
collagen_type_x.summary: Collagen X is a short-chain non-fibrillar network collagen expressed by hypertrophic chondrocytes and by essentially nothing else in the skeleton, which makes COL10A1 the canonical marker of the hypertrophic zone and of the thin calcified cartilage layer under articular cartilage. Its C-terminal NC1 domain trimerises and drives assembly into a hexagonal lattice concentrated in the pericellular matrix of hypertrophic cells. Its loss is the most instructive loss-of-function result in this layer, and it does not point where the field says it does. Col10a1-null mice were originally reported to have entirely normal long bone growth and development; re-analysis of the same null line found the growth plate width reduced by about 14% at day 21 with the PROLIFERATIVE zone more compressed than the hypertrophic - explicitly the opposite of the collagen X dominant-interference transgenic - together with about 10.8% perinatal lethality at week three, about 14% total lethality by 12 weeks, marrow aplasia and lymphatic organs at about 80% of control (Gress 2000). A collagen expressed in hypertrophic chondrocytes and nowhere else therefore produces its clearest histological effect one zone upstream, which is a non-cell-autonomous action through an unidentified intermediate. Human COL10A1 haploinsufficiency causes Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, which is mild: short stature, coxa vara, genu varum and a waddling gait, with normal intelligence and normal life expectancy. Most Schmid alleles are nonsense or frameshift alleles degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, so the disease is true haploinsufficiency, although at least one frameshift allele (p.W651fsX666) blocks trimerisation of the wild-type chain and acts dominant-negatively. The decisive human experiment is CRISPR deletion in human iPSC-derived chondrocytes: COL10A1-/- cells undergo normal hypertrophic differentiation in vitro, but the transplanted bone-area fraction was significantly larger in one of two iPSC backgrounds and the hypertrophic transcriptome shifted away from proliferating-phase and toward calcification-phase genes, which the authors read as accelerated differentiation (Kamakura 2023). Collagen X is therefore a marker of hypertrophy that is dispensable for hypertrophy itself, and any model that makes collagen X the structural prerequisite for cartilage mineralization is contradicted by three independent systems - but it is not phenotypically silent: both loss-of-function systems shift the proliferation/ossification balance toward ossification.
collagen_type_x.human_evidence_note: Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is a directly characterised human COL10A1 haploinsufficiency syndrome, and COL10A1 knockout has been performed in human iPSC-derived chondrocytes.
collagen_type_x.translation_risk_reason: Mouse null, human haploinsufficiency and human iPSC knockout all converge on a mild phenotype; the species agree.

collagen_type_xi.name: Collagen type XI (COL11A1/COL11A2)
collagen_type_xi.summary: Collagen XI is the minor fibrillar collagen that nucleates the cartilage fibril and sets its diameter. The molecule is a heterotrimer of alpha1(XI), alpha2(XI) and alpha3(XI), the last of which is the COL2A1 gene product alpha1(II)B differing only in post-translational glycosylation. It is buried inside the fibril and antigenically masked, becoming accessible to antibodies only where fibril packing is disrupted. Reconstitution experiments show the causal role directly: purified collagen II alone forms tapered tactoids of uncontrolled width, whereas II plus XI forms uniform ~20 nm fibrils provided the molar excess of II over XI stays below eight-fold. In the chondrodysplasia (cho/cho) mouse, a Col11a1 null, alpha1(XI) is absent and alpha1(V) substitutes in the fibril, giving abnormally thick cartilage collagen fibrils and severe chondrodysplasia; heterozygotes have hearing loss, showing dosage sensitivity. In humans COL11A1 mutations cause Marshall and Stickler type II syndromes and fibrochondrogenesis, COL11A2 causes otospondylomegaepiphyseal dysplasia and non-syndromic deafness, and COL11A2 variants have been reported in autosomal dominant familial short stature. In adult articular cartilage the isolated collagen XI fraction contains roughly equal amounts of alpha1(V) and alpha1(XI), so what is called collagen XI in mature tissue is a V/XI hybrid, not the embryonic molecule.
collagen_type_xi.human_evidence_note: Collagen XI has been immunolocalised ultrastructurally in human juvenile rib growth plate, in addition to the human COL11A1/2 disease genetics.

comp_protein.name: Cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP)
comp_protein.summary: COMP is a pentameric extracellular glycoprotein of the thrombospondin family, assembled through a five-stranded parallel coiled coil that encloses an axial channel, with each of the five arms ending in a C-terminal globular domain; native molecules appear by electron microscopy as five-armed bouquets. The arms contain calcium-binding thrombospondin type 3 repeats, and essentially all pseudoachondroplasia and many multiple epiphyseal dysplasia mutations fall in these repeats or in the C-terminal domain and abolish calcium binding. The consequence is not loss of an extracellular function but a proteinopathy: misfolded COMP is retained in the chondrocyte endoplasmic reticulum, and PSACH is a disease of ER stress and chondrocyte death rather than of matrix deficiency. This is why COMP mutations cause severe disproportionate short stature whereas Comp-null mice have no skeletal phenotype - a dominant-negative/gain-of-toxicity mechanism that is the opposite of the aggrecan and collagen X haploinsufficiency logic elsewhere in this layer. COMP also participates in matrix assembly, binding collagen IX and cooperating with it in fibril organisation.
comp_protein.human_evidence_note: COMP mutations are a directly characterised human dominant skeletal dysplasia series (pseudoachondroplasia and MED) with defined molecular mechanism.
comp_protein.translation_risk_reason: The disease mechanism was defined in human patients and human chondrocytes; the mouse null is uninformative precisely because the mechanism is dominant-negative.

decorin_protein.name: Decorin (DCN)
decorin_protein.summary: Decorin is a class I small leucine-rich proteoglycan carrying a single chondroitin/dermatan sulphate chain whose horseshoe-shaped leucine-rich repeat core binds the collagen fibril surface and limits lateral fibril growth. Decorin-null mice have abnormally coarse and irregular collagen fibrils with skin fragility, the founding demonstration that a SLRP sets fibril diameter in vivo. In cartilage decorin is not distributed uniformly over fibrils: decorin-bearing and collagen IX-bearing fibrils are biochemically distinct subpopulations within the same mammalian cartilage, so the fibril network is compositionally heterogeneous at the level of individual fibrils. Decorin also sequesters TGF-beta. Mechanically its contribution is second to biglycan's in bone: in single and double knockouts, Bgn deletion but not Dcn deletion reduces trabecular bone mass, but both reduce NMR-measured bound water and fracture toughness and raise extrafibrillar matrix modulus - and that modulus effect disappears on dehydration, showing the SLRPs act mechanically through retained water. Decorin is upregulated in biglycan-null mice, indicating partial compensation. No human decorin-deficiency growth phenotype is established.
decorin_protein.human_evidence_note: No human DCN loss-of-function growth phenotype was located in this sweep.
decorin_protein.translation_risk_reason: All functional data are murine knockouts; human decorin biology in the physis is untested.

enpp1_enzyme.name: ENPP1 (ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase 1)
enpp1_enzyme.summary: ENPP1 is the ectoenzyme that generates extracellular PPi by hydrolysing ATP to AMP plus PPi. It is the opposing arm to TNAP, and the two act on the same pool. The 2022 revision of the model made ENPP1 more central, not less: since ANKH exports ATP rather than PPi, ENPP1 is downstream of every known cellular PPi source, and Enpp1-/- mouse bone contains under 2.5% of wild-type PPi. Enpp1-/- mice and the ttw mouse are hypermineralized, and deleting Enpp1 genetically rescues the hypomineralization of Akp2(Alpl)-/- mice, the cleanest demonstration that the phenotype of TNAP loss is caused by PPi excess rather than Pi deficiency. In humans, biallelic ENPP1 loss of function causes generalized arterial calcification of infancy, and the SAME alleles cause autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 - so ENPP1 deficiency simultaneously produces ectopic calcification (from PPi deficiency) and defective growth plate mineralization (from FGF23-driven phosphate wasting). ENPP1 protein has been detected at the mineralization-promoting growth plate-metaphysis interface in human tissue.
enpp1_enzyme.human_evidence_note: Biallelic human ENPP1 loss-of-function is directly characterised as GACI and as ARHR2, both with skeletal phenotypes.

fetuin_a_ahsg.name: Fetuin-A (AHSG)
fetuin_a_ahsg.summary: Fetuin-A is a liver-derived serum glycoprotein that reaches bone and cartilage from the circulation and acts as a systemic mineralization inhibitor with a mechanism unlike osteopontin's. Rather than adsorbing to a growing crystal face, it sequesters calcium and phosphate into soluble colloidal calciprotein particles, keeping supersaturated fluid metastable. Ahsg-null mice develop widespread ectopic calcification, particularly on a calcification-prone genetic background, establishing the function in vivo. Its relevance to the growth plate was established directly in human tissue: spatial proteomics of human growth plate identifies AHSG together with SPP1 as the proteins concentrated at the growth plate-epiphysis interface, which behaves as a mineralization inhibition zone, while the metaphyseal interface carries the same inhibitors PLUS ENPP1 and ALPL and behaves as a promotion zone. A size-exclusion mechanism may make this spatially precise: fetuin is excluded from the interior of the collagen fibril, so intrafibrillar mineral can form by inhibitor exclusion while extrafibrillar mineral is suppressed.
fetuin_a_ahsg.human_evidence_note: AHSG protein has been localised directly in human paediatric growth plate tissue at a defined mineralization boundary.
fetuin_a_ahsg.translation_risk_reason: Mouse loss-of-function and human tissue localisation agree, and the biophysical mechanism is defined on the purified human protein.

fibronectin_cartilage.name: Fibronectin in cartilage and growth plate
fibronectin_cartilage.summary: Fibronectin is the adhesive glycoprotein through which chondrocytes engage their own matrix, principally via alpha5beta1 integrin, and it is a node in the matrix-matrix network, binding COMP directly. Its relevance to this layer rests on one strong human observation and a set of weaker cell-biological ones. The human observation is that heterozygous FN1 mutations cause a subtype of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with corner fractures - a metaphyseal, growth-plate-adjacent phenotype - so fibronectin dosage does affect the human physis. The cell biology is that alpha5beta1-fibronectin engagement modulates chondrocyte proliferation and matrix interaction, and that fibronectin fragments generated by matrix degradation are catabolic, inducing collagenase-3 and inflammatory mediators in chondrocytes, which makes fibronectin fragmentation an amplifier of matrix loss rather than a structural role. Zonal fibronectin distribution across the human growth plate was not established in this sweep, and this node is the thinnest in the layer for that reason.
fibronectin_cartilage.human_evidence_note: Heterozygous FN1 mutations cause a directly characterised human spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with metaphyseal corner fractures.

fixed_charge_density.name: Fixed charge density (FCD)
fixed_charge_density.summary: Fixed charge density is the molar concentration of immobilised negative charge, almost all of it chondroitin-sulphate and keratan-sulphate carboxylate and sulphate groups on aggrecan, held inside the collagen network. It is the physical parameter that converts proteoglycan content into mechanical function. Measured non-destructively by sodium NMR combined with ideal Donnan theory, calf articular cartilage near physiological conditions has an FCD of -0.28 +/- 0.03 M (n=10), and calf EPIPHYSEAL cartilage - the closest available proxy for growth plate - has an FCD of -0.19 to -0.35 M that varies with position within the joint in proportion to glycosaminoglycan content. Sodium NMR visibility in cartilage is essentially complete: the NMR:ICP sodium ratio is 1.02 +/- 0.04 in calf and 1.04 +/- 0.11 in adult bovine tissue, so the measurement is not missing a bound pool. FCD falls with decreasing bath ionic strength, and the FCD-derived swelling pressure is markedly non-ideal, so FCD calculated by ideal Donnan theory is an upper bound on the mechanically effective charge. Depletion of glycosaminoglycan raises permeability and restoring synthetic polyanion charge restores it, confirming the causal chain from charge to fluid transport to stiffness. No zone-resolved FCD measurement of a growth plate exists.
fixed_charge_density.human_evidence_note: No human cartilage or growth plate FCD measurement was located in this sweep; the technique is applicable in vivo but has been applied to bovine tissue.
fixed_charge_density.translation_risk_reason: All values are bovine; human physeal proteoglycan content and hence FCD are unmeasured.

hyaluronan_matrix.name: Hyaluronan in growth plate matrix
hyaluronan_matrix.summary: Hyaluronan is the unsulphated, unbranched glycosaminoglycan that forms the central filament of the proteoglycan aggregate: aggrecan G1 domains bind it non-covalently, link protein stabilises each interaction, and the resulting aggregate is too large to diffuse out of the collagen network. It is also the ligand of CD44 and thus the anchor of the chondrocyte pericellular coat. Its necessity is shown by conditional Has2 deletion in limb bud mesenchyme with Prx1-Cre: all limb skeletal elements are severely shortened, growth plates are disorganised with loss of columnar architecture and reduced aggrecan deposition in the matrix, the number of hypertrophic chondrocytes and the expression domains of hypertrophic markers are strikingly reduced, secondary ossification centres fail to form centrally, and proximal phalanges are duplicated. So hyaluronan is required not just to immobilise aggrecan but for chondrocyte maturation itself. The synthesis and degradation rates of hyaluronan in the growth plate, and its concentration by zone, were not located in this sweep.

hydroxyapatite_nucleation.name: Hydroxyapatite nucleation and mineral maturation
hydroxyapatite_nucleation.summary: Growth plate mineral does not appear as hydroxyapatite. It appears as amorphous calcium phosphate that is transiently stabilised by inhibitory proteins and then converted to oriented apatite platelets on a collagen template. Cryo-TEM and cryo-tomography of collagen mineralised in the presence of nucleation inhibitors show the mechanism: the positive net charge near the collagen C-terminus draws ACP into the fibril, and clusters of charged residues in the 40 nm gap zone and the overlap zone act as nucleation sites that convert ACP into a parallel array of oriented crystals within the 67 nm D-period. In human growth plate the same sequence has been imaged directly at the growth plate-metaphysis interface, where extrafibrillar spherical mineral particles fuse across the interfibrillar space and permeate the fibrils, and where immature spherical mineral gives way to crystal platelets with distance from the front. The chemistry that permits this is set by the Pi:PPi ratio and by protein inhibitors: in porcine growth plate the extracellular Ca and P concentrations are already several-fold above the ion product needed for in vitro mineralization in ALL zones, so the tissue is chronically supersaturated and mineralization is controlled by inhibition, not by supply.
hydroxyapatite_nucleation.human_evidence_note: ACP-to-apatite transformation and mineral platelet maturation have been imaged directly in human growth plate tissue from paediatric donors.
hydroxyapatite_nucleation.translation_risk_reason: The key structural observations have now been made in human growth plate rather than inferred from animals.

inorganic_pyrophosphate.name: Inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi)
inorganic_pyrophosphate.summary: PPi is the master physiological inhibitor of hydroxyapatite deposition. It adsorbs to nascent apatite crystal faces and blocks crystal proliferation and growth, so mineralization occurs where PPi is locally destroyed and is prevented everywhere else. Human plasma PPi is about 3.5 umol/L (99% range 1.19-5.65 umol/L in 73 healthy adults by isotope dilution), slightly higher in 0-15 year olds, and urinary PPi exceeds 10 umol/L. Against a serum phosphate of roughly 1-2 mmol/L this makes the circulating Pi:PPi ratio of order 300-600:1, and the local ratio in the extracellular fluid of the hypertrophic zone is the actual control variable. The two ends of the human dose response are known experiments: loss of TNAP (hypophosphatasia) raises PPi and produces rickets and osteomalacia with an unmineralized hypertrophic zone, while loss of ENPP1 (generalized arterial calcification of infancy) lowers PPi and produces catastrophic ectopic calcification, and the same ENPP1 alleles also produce autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2, so PPi deficiency and PPi excess both damage the growth plate. In growth plate chondrocytes PPi is not merely a physicochemical inhibitor: extracellular PPi suppresses and extracellular Pi stimulates terminal differentiation and apoptosis, so PPi/Pi is a differentiation signal as well as a crystal poison.
inorganic_pyrophosphate.human_evidence_note: Plasma PPi has been measured directly in healthy humans and in hypophosphatasia, and both PPi-raising (ALPL) and PPi-lowering (ENPP1) human loss-of-function syndromes are characterised.
inorganic_pyrophosphate.translation_risk_reason: Both directions of the PPi axis are established by human loss-of-function genetics with matching mouse models.

link_protein_hapln1.name: Link protein (HAPLN1)
link_protein_hapln1.summary: Link protein is the small glycoprotein that clamps the aggrecan G1 domain onto hyaluronan, converting a reversible interaction into a stable ternary complex. Hapln1-null mice are dwarfed with craniofacial abnormalities, so link protein is required for normal longitudinal growth in vivo. Its stoichiometry is not one-to-one and it changes with age in a way that destabilises the aggregate: in human articular cartilage from individuals over 13 years, the molar concentration of link protein is LOWER than that of the aggrecan G1 domain in every sequential extract, and particularly so in the 1 M guanidinium fraction, so a substantial fraction of aggregates in adult human cartilage are link-protein-deficient and therefore unstable. Link protein also fragments with age, but fragmentation does not change its extractability. The consequence, stated bluntly by the authors, is that the textbook model of the proteoglycan aggregate - derived from immature animal cartilage where a single PBS extraction recovers most components - does not describe adult human cartilage, which contains a heterogeneous population of complexes with varying stability. Quantitative electron microscopy agrees: monomers per aggregate and the proportion of aggregating monomers both fall with age.
link_protein_hapln1.human_evidence_note: Link protein and aggrecan G1 molar concentrations were measured directly in human articular cartilage across a newborn-to-63-year age range.
link_protein_hapln1.translation_risk_reason: Human biochemistry is direct but articular; the growth phenotype is murine.
localization: human articular cartilage: link protein present but substoichiometric to aggrecan G1 after age 13 (wells2003)
mouse growth plate: link protein required for normal growth (watanabe1999)
human growth plate zonal link protein: unmeasured

lysyl_oxidase.name: Lysyl oxidase (LOX)
lysyl_oxidase.summary: Lysyl oxidase is the copper- and lysine-tyrosylquinone-dependent amine oxidase that initiates all covalent collagen and elastin crosslinking by converting telopeptide lysine and hydroxylysine to allysine. It is the single enzymatic step on which the entire mechanical competence of the cartilage collagen network depends, and it is irreversibly inhibited by beta-aminopropionitrile, the lathyrogen. Lox-null mice die perinatally with aortic aneurysm, cardiovascular dysfunction and diaphragmatic defects; the paralogue Loxl3 null has cleft palate and spinal deformity, so the family has partially distinct skeletal roles. Beyond crosslinking, LOX is hypoxia-induced and the growth plate is a steep oxygen gradient, which makes zonal LOX activity a plausible but untested regulator of the zonal stiffness gradient. This node is deliberately thin because the evidence is thin: no zone-resolved LOX expression, activity or crosslink-density measurement in growth plate cartilage of any species was located in this sweep, and there is no human LOX-deficiency chondrodysplasia. Everything specific to the physis here is inference from vascular and tendon biology.
lysyl_oxidase.human_evidence_note: No human LOX loss-of-function growth plate phenotype was located; human LOX variants are associated with thoracic aortic aneurysm.
lysyl_oxidase.translation_risk_reason: The only in vivo loss-of-function data are murine and vascular, and the growth plate role is inferred from the general chemistry of collagen crosslinking.
localization: growth plate zones: LOX expression and activity not localised in any species located in this sweep

key_refs.one_line_finding: Lox-null mice die perinatally with aortic aneurysm and diaphragmatic defects from failed collagen and elastin crosslinking
