matrilin3.name: Matrilin-3 (MATN3)
matrilin3.summary: Matrilin-3 is a cartilage-specific oligomeric adaptor protein built around a single von Willebrand factor A domain plus EGF repeats and a coiled-coil oligomerisation module. It sits on the surface of the collagen fibril and bridges fibrils to other matrix components. Its position in the assembly hierarchy is established genetically: matrilin-3 fails to integrate normally into cartilage matrix in collagen IX-null mice, so matrilin-3 incorporation is downstream of collagen IX; and matrilin-1/matrilin-3 double-deficient mice have abnormally thick and irregular cartilage collagen fibrils, so the matrilins constrain fibril growth even though single nulls are near-normal through redundancy. In humans, missense mutations in the beta strands of the single A domain cause autosomal dominant multiple epiphyseal dysplasia, and a homozygous MATN3 mutation causes a distinct spondylo-epi-metaphyseal dysplasia. As with COMP, the dominant mechanism is misfolding: MED mutations cause A-domain misfolding and prevent secretion of mutant matrilin-3, retaining it in the ER, so the disease is again a proteinopathy rather than simple loss of matrix protein.
matrilin3.human_evidence_note: MATN3 mutations cause directly characterised human autosomal dominant MED and a recessive SEMD; mechanism confirmed in human mutant protein studies.
matrilin3.translation_risk_reason: Human disease genetics and mouse matrix biology agree; the dominant human mechanism is a misfolding effect demonstrated on the human protein.
localization: cartilage collagen fibril surface: matrilin-3 integration requires collagen IX (budde2005)
human growth plate zonal matrilin-3: not established in this sweep

matrix_gla_protein.name: Matrix Gla protein (MGP)
matrix_gla_protein.summary: MGP is a small vitamin-K-dependent, gamma-carboxyglutamate-containing matrix protein made by chondrocytes and vascular smooth muscle cells whose function is to keep soft tissue and non-hypertrophic cartilage unmineralized. Mgp-null mice develop to term and then die within about two months from arterial rupture caused by spontaneous arterial calcification, and - the point for this layer - they inappropriately calcify their growth plate cartilage, which leads to short stature, osteopenia and fractures. This is the cleanest demonstration in the literature that cartilage mineralization is actively suppressed rather than passively absent: withdraw one inhibitor and the proliferative cartilage mineralizes even though nothing about the mineral supply has changed. The gamma-carboxylation is functionally required, which is why warfarin causes cartilage and arterial calcification in rats and why the undercarboxylated form is used as a circulating biomarker. In humans, MGP loss of function causes Keutel syndrome with abnormal cartilage calcification. Ex vivo, MGP is one of the genes expressed more highly by the calcification-suppressing superficial cartilage layer in bovine osteochondral explants.
matrix_gla_protein.human_evidence_note: Human MGP loss of function causes Keutel syndrome with abnormal cartilage calcification, but no quantitative human growth plate data were located.
matrix_gla_protein.translation_risk_reason: The mouse null phenotype is dramatic and the human syndrome is qualitatively concordant, but no human growth plate measurement supports it.

matrix_vesicle.name: Matrix vesicle
matrix_vesicle.summary: Matrix vesicles are 30-200 nm membrane-bounded structures budded from the plasma membrane of hypertrophic chondrocytes into the longitudinal septa of the lower hypertrophic zone, and they are where the first apatite crystal in the growth plate forms. They are functionally defined by their cargo: PHOSPHO1 inside, generating Pi from phosphocholine and phosphoethanolamine; TNAP and NPP1 GPI-anchored or bound on the outer leaflet; PiT-1 phosphate transporters to import extravesicularly generated Pi; annexins and ion channels to admit Ca; and a nucleational core of calcium-acidic-phospholipid-phosphate complexes on the inner leaflet. Mineralization is therefore a two-stage process with genetically separable steps. Stage one is intravesicular crystal initiation, which requires PHOSPHO1 and Pi influx and which still occurs normally in Alpl-/- mice. Stage two is rupture of the vesicle membrane and propagation of mineral onto the collagen scaffold, which requires TNAP to hold extravesicular PPi low and which is exactly the step that fails in Alpl-/- growth plate by high-resolution TEM. This is why Phospho1/Alpl double nulls have no skeletal mineral at all while each single null retains some. NPP1 localises to matrix vesicles but ANK does not, which explains why ANK deficiency cannot rescue the Alpl-/- phenotype even though it lowers systemic PPi.
matrix_vesicle.human_evidence_note: Matrix vesicle biology is animal and in vitro; the human link is that hypophosphatasia shows the same failure of perivesicular mineral propagation described in Alpl-/- mice.
matrix_vesicle.translation_risk_reason: The genetic dissection is entirely murine, but the human hypophosphatasia histology is consistent with the same two-stage model.
localization: mouse/chick/rat lower HZ longitudinal septa: matrix vesicles concentrated here (wuthier1992, anderson2004)
human growth plate matrix vesicles: not quantified in this sweep

matrix_water_content_zonal.name: Zonal matrix water content of the growth plate
matrix_water_content_zonal.summary: Water is the majority phase of growth plate matrix and the medium through which every solute, including Pi and PPi, reaches the mineralization front, yet its zonal distribution is one of the least quantified variables in this layer. The best available figure is indirect: X-ray microprobe analysis of pig growth plate normalises elemental concentrations assuming 66% tissue fluid, and derives extracellular Ca of about 58 mmol/kg wet weight from 0.7% Ca per dry mass on that assumption. A validated non-invasive method exists - MR T1 mapping calculates cartilage and physeal water content with 97.3% accuracy against freeze-drying, with a coefficient of variance of 2.73 (SD 1.3) in vivo in 30 kg pigs and interobserver CV 0.053 - but it has not been applied to produce a zone-resolved human dataset. Indirectly, water content is mechanically load-bearing: knocking out biglycan and decorin in mouse reduces NMR-measured bound water and fracture toughness and raises extrafibrillar matrix modulus, and the modulus effect disappears on dehydration, showing the small proteoglycans act mechanically through the water they retain. Zonal water content of the human growth plate, and its change across the mineralization front, remain unmeasured.
matrix_water_content_zonal.human_evidence_note: No zone-resolved water content measurement of human growth plate was located; the validated MR method has only been demonstrated in pigs.
matrix_water_content_zonal.translation_risk_reason: The single quantitative anchor is a normalisation assumption inside a 1982 porcine microprobe study, not a measurement.
localization: porcine growth plate: whole-plate fluid fraction assumed at 66% (althoff1982)
human growth plate zones: water content unmeasured

mineralization_front.name: Mineralization front / zone of provisional calcification
mineralization_front.summary: The mineralization front is the sharp boundary in the lower hypertrophic zone where the longitudinal septa between chondrocyte columns become mineralized while the transverse septa do not, converting cartilage into the scaffold that osteoblasts subsequently coat. Human data now show that the growth plate is mineralization-polarised, not merely mineralization-terminated: the growth plate-epiphysis interface shows a sharp step in tissue modulus and is an active mineralization INHIBITION zone enriched in SPP1 (osteopontin) and AHSG (fetuin-A), whereas the growth plate-metaphysis interface shows a gradual modulus rise and is a mineralization PROMOTION zone enriched in ENPP1 and ALPL alongside the same inhibitors. Both boundaries therefore carry inhibitors; what differs is whether TNAP and ENPP1 are present to override them. The same polarity has been reproduced ex vivo in bovine osteochondral explants, where the superficial cartilage layer actively suppresses calcification of the deep layer while expressing higher FGF18, PTHLH and MGP, and the deep layer expresses ALPL, COL10A1 and IHH. Compositionally the front is marked by loss of matrix sulphur, a proxy for sulphated proteoglycan, from about 3.5% to 0.3% of dry mass on mineralization in pig growth plate.
mineralization_front.human_evidence_note: Modulus, elemental and spatial proteomic mapping of both growth plate-bone interfaces has been performed on human paediatric growth plate tissue.
mineralization_front.translation_risk_reason: The defining observations are human; animal data are corroborative.

human GP-epiphysis interface: mineralization inhibition zone, SPP1 and AHSG enriched (xie2025)
bovine osteochondral explants: superficial layer suppresses deep-layer calcification (xu2026)

mmp13_protease.name: MMP-13 (collagenase-3)
mmp13_protease.summary: MMP-13 is the chondrocyte-intrinsic collagenase of the hypertrophic zone and is the enzyme that cleaves the triple helix of collagen II in the lower growth plate. Its expression rises steeply from epiphysis to metaphysis in parallel with the loss of type II collagen and the appearance of type X collagen and the type II C-propeptide. Mmp13-null mice have profound growth plate defects: markedly increased hypertrophic domains, delayed endochondral ossification, delayed formation and vascularisation of the primary ossification centre, and significant interstitial collagen accumulation attributable to the missing collagenase cleavage. Unlike the Mmp9-null, these growth plate abnormalities persist into adult life and phenocopy human hereditary chondrodysplasias. There is a human anchor: MMP13 variants cause metaphyseal anadysplasia and, more recently, a frameshift variant causing short stature via a gain-of-function interaction with HSPA5 and ER stress. MMP-13 is also active inside matrix vesicles, where it can activate latent TGF-beta, so it is not solely a bulk collagenase.
mmp13_protease.human_evidence_note: Human MMP13 variants cause metaphyseal anadysplasia and short stature, but no direct human growth plate MMP-13 zonal quantification was located.
mmp13_protease.translation_risk_reason: Mouse null and human MMP13 skeletal dysplasia agree in kind; the human zonal expression pattern is inferred.

mmp14_mt1mmp.name: MT1-MMP (MMP14)
mmp14_mt1mmp.summary: MT1-MMP is the membrane-anchored collagenase whose loss produces the most severe skeletal phenotype of any single matrix metalloproteinase: Mmp14-null mice develop dwarfism, osteopenia, generalised arthritis and connective tissue disease attributed directly to inadequate collagen turnover, with defective secondary ossification and soft tissue fibrosis. That contrast is the informative part of this layer's protease section. Deleting the secreted collagenase MMP-13 gives an expanded hypertrophic zone; deleting the vascular-invasion gelatinase MMP-9 gives a transient eight-fold plate; deleting the two aggrecanases together gives a physiologically normal mouse; but deleting the membrane-tethered collagenase gives frank dwarfism. Pericellular, membrane-localised proteolysis is therefore the non-redundant activity. MT1-MMP also has substrates beyond collagen relevant to growth: it cleaves PTH1R in the chondrocyte-derived osteoblast lineage, curbing PTH signalling intensity, and chondrocyte-specific deletion in adult mice does NOT reproduce the inflammatory arthritis of the global null, so much of the phenotype is non-chondrocytic.
mmp14_mt1mmp.human_evidence_note: Human MMP14 biallelic loss causes Winchester syndrome/multicentric osteolysis with skeletal dysplasia, but no human growth plate data were retrieved here.
mmp14_mt1mmp.translation_risk_reason: All quantitative statements are murine and the tissue of origin of the dwarfism has not been resolved even in the mouse.

mmp9_protease.name: MMP-9 (gelatinase B)
mmp9_protease.summary: MMP-9 is not made by chondrocytes. It is supplied by invading cells of bone marrow origin - the chondroclasts/septoclasts at the chondro-osseous junction - and it acts at the last septum of the hypertrophic zone to release matrix-bound angiogenic activity and permit vascular invasion. The Mmp9-null mouse is the cleanest demonstration: hypertrophic chondrocytes still differentiate normally, but apoptosis, vascularisation and ossification are all delayed and the growth plate lengthens progressively to about EIGHT TIMES normal. The phenotype is transient - after three weeks postnatal, compensatory apoptosis and vascularisation remodel the enlarged plate and adult skeletal appearance is normal - so MMP-9 controls the timing of cartilage removal, not whether it happens. That the defect is cell-extrinsic to cartilage is shown directly by rescue with wild-type bone marrow transplantation, and Mmp9-null growth plates in culture show delayed release of an angiogenic activator. No human MMP9 deficiency syndrome is known, so this is a mouse-only mechanism with no human genetic anchor.
mmp9_protease.human_evidence_note: No human MMP9 loss-of-function skeletal phenotype is known and no zonal MMP-9 localisation in human growth plate was located in this sweep.
mmp9_protease.translation_risk_reason: Entirely murine; the eight-fold phenotype is dramatic but the mouse growth plate never fuses, so the compensation observed may not have a human analogue.

osteopontin_spp1.name: Osteopontin (SPP1)
osteopontin_spp1.summary: Osteopontin is a highly phosphorylated acidic glycoprotein that inhibits hydroxyapatite formation and growth by adsorbing to crystal faces through polyaspartate and phosphoserine motifs; its inhibitory activity is phosphorylation-dependent and is largely lost when the covalently bound phosphate is removed. It is a second, PPi-independent brake on mineralization and it is transcriptionally coupled to the PPi system: Alpl-/- mice have raised osteopontin, ank/ank mice have reduced osteopontin, and both are normalised in the corresponding double mutants, so the hypomineralization of TNAP loss is the combined effect of PPi excess AND osteopontin excess rather than PPi alone. In vivo the inhibitory role is shown by epistasis with matrix Gla protein: Opn-/-;Mgp-/- double nulls calcify far worse than Mgp-/- alone. In human growth plate, SPP1 protein is one of the two proteins concentrated at the mineralization-inhibiting growth plate-epiphysis interface, alongside AHSG. Osteopontin is therefore an inducible inhibitor whose expression rises when mineralization is dysregulated, which makes it a sensor as well as an effector.
osteopontin_spp1.human_evidence_note: SPP1 protein has been localised in human growth plate tissue, but no human osteopontin loss-of-function phenotype is known.
osteopontin_spp1.translation_risk_reason: Function is defined by mouse knockouts and in vitro crystal assays; the human data are localisation only.

pericellular_matrix.name: Pericellular matrix (PCM)
pericellular_matrix.summary: The pericellular matrix is the 2-4 um shell immediately surrounding each chondrocyte, distinguished from the interterritorial matrix by containing collagen VI, perlecan, hyaluronan-CD44 coats, high collagen IX and XI on thin fibrils, and little or no collagen II fibril bulk. It is mechanically distinct and SOFTER than the surrounding matrix: in situ AFM stiffness mapping gives a PCM:ECM modulus ratio of about 0.35 in human, porcine and murine articular cartilage, consistent with earlier measurements on mechanically isolated chondrons. That compliance is functional - it converts tissue-level strain into a cell-level strain and fluid-flow signal - and the PCM is also a signalling reservoir, with FGF-2 stored bound to perlecan heparan sulphate and released on mechanical loading. In the growth plate the PCM is additionally the structural unit of the column: chondrons are tubular rather than spherical, and under compression they bend and kink preferentially at the reserve/proliferative interface. The PCM:ECM modulus ratio of the growth plate specifically, as distinct from articular cartilage, has not been measured.
pericellular_matrix.human_evidence_note: Human articular cartilage PCM modulus was measured directly in the same study as porcine and murine; human growth plate PCM has not been.
pericellular_matrix.translation_risk_reason: Human articular data exist, but transferring an articular PCM:ECM ratio to the physis is unvalidated.

perlecan_hspg2.name: Perlecan (HSPG2)
perlecan_hspg2.summary: Perlecan is a very large modular heparan sulphate proteoglycan that is a core component of the cartilage pericellular matrix as well as of basement membranes. In cartilage it does two things. Structurally it maintains cartilage integrity: perlecan-null mice die perinatally with severe chondrodysplasia, disorganised growth plate columns and defective cartilage matrix. Functionally it is a growth-factor reservoir: FGF-2 is stored bound to perlecan heparan sulphate in the articular pericellular matrix and released on mechanical loading, making perlecan a mechanotransducer rather than a passive scaffold. The human allelic series is unusually informative because it is a dose series: complete functional null HSPG2 mutations cause dyssegmental dysplasia Silverman-Handmaker type, which is perinatal lethal, while hypomorphic mutations that reduce but do not abolish perlecan cause Schwartz-Jampel syndrome (chondrodystrophic myotonia) with short stature and myotonia compatible with survival. Perlecan is therefore dosage-sensitive in humans across the full range from lethal to viable.
perlecan_hspg2.human_evidence_note: Two distinct human HSPG2 loss-of-function syndromes (DDSH and Schwartz-Jampel) define a genotype-dose-phenotype relationship directly in humans.
perlecan_hspg2.translation_risk_reason: Human null and hypomorph phenotypes mirror the mouse null, so mouse and human agree.
localization: cartilage pericellular matrix: perlecan present and FGF-2 bound to its heparan sulphate (vincent2007)
mouse growth plate: perlecan required for columnar organisation (costell1999)

phospho1_enzyme.name: PHOSPHO1
phospho1_enzyme.summary: PHOSPHO1 is a cytosolic, matrix-vesicle-enclosed phosphatase specific for phosphoethanolamine and phosphocholine. It supplies the intravesicular Pi that seeds the first apatite crystals inside matrix vesicles, which is a different step from TNAP's job of destroying extravesicular PPi. The division of labour is proved by epistasis: Phospho1-/- mice have growth plate abnormalities, bowed long bones, spontaneous fractures, osteomalacia and scoliosis, with reduced-mineralizing chondrocytes and matrix vesicles and elevated plasma PPi; transgenic overexpression of TNAP normalises their plasma PPi but does NOT correct their bone phenotype; and Phospho1/Alpl double-null mice show complete absence of skeletal mineralization with perinatal lethality. Mechanically, Phospho1-/- tibiae deform plastically rather than fracturing in three-point bending and have significantly lower elastic modulus and hardness by nanoindentation with lower Raman mineral:matrix ratio. Spatial lipidomics confirms the substrate logic: PHOSPHO1 ablation shifts the growth plate lipidome with accumulation of phosphatidylcholine, lysophosphatidylcholine, sphingomyelin and phosphatidylethanolamine species across resting, proliferative and hypertrophic zones. Independent chick work reproduces the mineralization defect on pharmacological inhibition.
phospho1_enzyme.human_evidence_note: No human PHOSPHO1 loss-of-function syndrome is established; human relevance rests on proton pump inhibitors inhibiting PHOSPHO1 at micromolar concentrations and on epidemiological PPI fracture risk.
phospho1_enzyme.translation_risk_reason: Every skeletal phenotype is murine or avian; there is no human genetic proof that PHOSPHO1 is required for human skeletal mineralization.
localization: mouse growth plate: PHOSPHO1 highly expressed at sites of mineralization in cartilage and bone (huesa2011)
matrix vesicle lumen: PHOSPHO1 present (roberts2007)
mouse RZ, PZ and HZ: lipidome altered in all three zones on PHOSPHO1 ablation (tzvetkov2023)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Phospho1/Alpl double-null mice show complete absence of skeletal mineralization and perinatal lethality
Phospho1-/- tibiae have reduced elastic modulus and hardness by nanoindentation and lower Raman mineral:matrix ratio
PHOSPHO1 is functionally involved in matrix-vesicle-mediated mineralization
PHOSPHO1 ablation significantly alters the growth plate lipidome in all three zones by MALDI imaging

PHOSPHO1 inhibition impairs skeletal mineralization in chick limb development

pi_ppi_ratio.name: Extracellular Pi/PPi ratio as the mineralization control variable
pi_ppi_ratio.summary: Mineralization in the growth plate is not controlled by mineral supply. Electron microprobe analysis of pig growth plate shows the extracellular Ca x P ion product is far above the ~2 mM^2 needed for mineralization in vitro in EVERY zone, including the resting and proliferative zones that never mineralize, so the tissue is chronically supersaturated and the operative variable is inhibition. The dominant inhibitor is PPi and the dominant permissive signal is Pi, so the ratio of the two is the control variable. Human circulating values bracket the scale: plasma PPi is 3.50 +/- 0.11 umol/L (99% range 1.19-5.65) against a serum phosphate of order 1-2 mmol/L, i.e. a circulating Pi:PPi ratio of roughly 300-600:1. The ratio is not merely physicochemical. In growth plate chondrocytes extracellular Pi stimulates and extracellular PPi inhibits terminal differentiation marker expression, mineralization and apoptosis, with different Pi thresholds for the two - lower Pi favours differentiation, higher Pi is required for apoptosis - all dependent on Pit-1/Pit-2 type III Na/Pi cotransporter expression and actual Pi uptake. Every genetic manipulation of the axis (TNAP loss, ENPP1 loss, ANK loss, PHOSPHO1 loss) moves the phenotype in the direction predicted by the ratio, and opposing mutations cancel. What is missing is the number: no measurement of Pi or PPi concentration, or of their ratio, in the extracellular fluid of any growth plate zone in situ was located in this sweep.
pi_ppi_ratio.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is the plasma PPi range plus the two opposing human loss-of-function syndromes (ALPL and ENPP1); the local ratio in the growth plate has never been measured in humans or animals.
pi_ppi_ratio.translation_risk_reason: The systemic numbers are human but the tissue-level ratio, which is the actual control variable, is unmeasured in every species.
localization: porcine growth plate all zones: supersaturated Ca x P product (althoff1982)
growth plate zone-resolved Pi and PPi concentrations: never measured in situ in any species

proteoglycan_turnover.name: Proteoglycan turnover in cartilage and growth plate
proteoglycan_turnover.summary: Proteoglycan turnover in cartilage is measured either by radiosulphate pulse-chase in explants or by aspartate racemization, which reads the molecular age of a protein pool directly. In ADULT HUMAN ARTICULAR cartilage the numbers are unambiguous: the aggrecan large monomer has a turnover constant of 0.206/year, a half-life of 3.4 years, whereas the free G1 hyaluronan-binding region has a constant of 0.027/year and a half-life of 25 years. The G1 fragments therefore accumulate for decades and progressively occupy hyaluronan binding sites, which is a mechanistic explanation for the age-related decline in aggregation seen by quantitative electron microscopy. In the GROWTH PLATE the picture is zonal and much faster but has never been converted into a half-life: in bovine distal tibial explants, rates of both aggrecan synthesis and breakdown are highest in the resting/proliferative third and lowest in the lower hypertrophic third, and are higher in calf than fetal tissue. How aggrecan is actually removed before mineralization is unresolved: mice with MMP-cleavage-resistant aggrecan grow normally without accumulating aggrecan, and Adamts4/Adamts5 double-null mice are physiologically normal, so neither protease family is required.
proteoglycan_turnover.human_evidence_note: Human turnover data are from adult articular cartilage; no human growth plate proteoglycan turnover measurement was located.
proteoglycan_turnover.translation_risk_reason: A 3.4-year aggrecan half-life measured in adult articular cartilage cannot be transferred to a tissue that is entirely replaced every few weeks; the physeal rate is unknown.
localization: bovine growth plate RZ/PZ: fastest aggrecan turnover (shapses1994)
human growth plate: no turnover measurement exists

key_refs.one_line_finding: Aggrecan monomer half-life 3.4 years and free G1 half-life 25 years in adult human articular cartilage by aspartate racemization
Aggrecan synthesis and breakdown are both fastest in the resting/proliferative third of the bovine growth plate

Adamts4/Adamts5 double-null mice are physiologically normal

timp_family.name: TIMPs (tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases)
timp_family.summary: The four TIMPs are the endogenous stoichiometric inhibitors that set net proteolysis in cartilage. They are not interchangeable. TIMP-3 is the only member that inhibits the aggrecanases: its N-terminal inhibitory domain blocks ADAMTS4 and ADAMTS5 with sub-nanomolar Ki, whereas TIMP-1, TIMP-2 and TIMP-4 are weak or inactive against ADAMTS4. TIMP-3 is also unique in binding to the extracellular matrix through its C-terminal domain rather than circulating freely, so it is retained where it is made. Because TIMP-3 is the only aggrecanase inhibitor and aggrecanase activity is not required for normal murine skeletal development, the physiological role of TIMP-3 in the growth plate specifically is unresolved. Human TIMP3 mutations cause Sorsby fundus dystrophy, a retinal not skeletal disease, so there is no human genetic evidence linking TIMPs to longitudinal growth.
timp_family.human_evidence_note: Human TIMP3 mutations cause Sorsby fundus dystrophy with no skeletal phenotype; no human growth plate TIMP data were located.
timp_family.translation_risk_reason: All quantitative data are recombinant enzyme kinetics; no in vivo growth plate role has been demonstrated in any species.
localization: human growth plate: TIMP-1 present in all zones plus osteoblasts and osteoclasts; TIMP-2 in hypertrophic chondrocytes and osteoblasts (haeusler2005)
cartilage extracellular matrix: TIMP-3 is matrix-bound via its C-terminal domain (kashiwagi2001)
human growth plate zonal TIMP expression: not established

key_refs.one_line_finding: The N-terminal domain of TIMP-3 inhibits ADAMTS4 and ADAMTS5 with sub-nanomolar Ki
TIMP-3 inhibits ADAMTS4 while TIMP-1, -2 and -4 are weak or inactive

Human child and adolescent growth plate: MMP-14 most prominent and present in all zones; MMP-1/9/10/11/13 and VEGF in hypertrophic chondrocytes; TIMP-1 in all zones, TIMP-2 in hypertrophic chondrocytes

tnap_alpl.name: Tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP/ALPL)
tnap_alpl.summary: TNAP is the GPI-anchored ectophosphatase on the outer membrane of matrix vesicles and of hypertrophic chondrocytes and osteoblasts whose job is to destroy extracellular PPi so that hydroxyapatite can propagate. It is a homodimer with three catalytic metal sites (Zn at M1/M2, Mg at M3) plus a structural M4 site; the rising extracellular Ca gradient during mineralization first activates TNAP by replacing Mg with Ca at M3 and then deactivates it as Ca displaces Zn from M1/M2, which is a built-in shut-off at the completion of mineralization. Its activity in growth cartilage is restricted to the hypertrophic and calcifying zones by immunohistochemistry and by X-ray microprobe, which finds maximal alkaline phosphatase activity coincident with maximal extractable organically bound phosphorus in the hypertrophic zone of the pig growth plate. Alpl-/- mice have under 1% of wild-type plasma activity, accumulate PPi, phosphoethanolamine and pyridoxal-5-phosphate, and show developmental arrest of chondrocyte differentiation with diminished or absent hypertrophic zones. High-resolution TEM in these mice places the defect precisely: mineral crystals still initiate normally INSIDE matrix vesicles but fail to proliferate beyond the vesicle membrane, so TNAP is required for the extravesicular, not the intravesicular, step. In humans this is hypophosphatasia, and bone-targeted enzyme replacement with asfotase alfa raised one-year survival in perinatal and infantile disease from 42% to 95%, which is the interventional human proof that TNAP activity is rate-limiting.
tnap_alpl.human_evidence_note: Human ALPL loss-of-function (hypophosphatasia) and its reversal by enzyme replacement provide both observational and interventional human evidence, and ALPL protein has been detected at the human growth plate-metaphysis interface.
tnap_alpl.translation_risk_reason: Mouse null recapitulates infantile hypophosphatasia and the human therapeutic response confirms the mechanism in humans.
localization: chicken epiphyseal growth cartilage: alkaline phosphatase confined to hypertrophic and calcifying zones (vnnen1980)
porcine growth plate HZ: maximal alkaline phosphatase activity coincident with maximal extractable organic phosphorus (althoff1982)
human growth plate metaphyseal boundary: ALPL protein detected at the mineralization-promoting GP-metaphysis interface (xie2025)
matrix vesicle outer membrane: TNAP is GPI-anchored there (anderson2004)

zonal_stiffness_gradient.name: Zonal mechanical properties of the growth plate
zonal_stiffness_gradient.summary: There is no single number for growth plate stiffness, and the published values span three orders of magnitude because the methods measure different things at different length scales on differently prepared tissue. Tissue-scale hydrated measurements give hundreds of kilopascals to low megapascals: microindentation of 9-week rabbit proximal tibial physis gives a Hertz reduced modulus of 380-690 kPa; AFM microindentation of rabbit cranial base growth plate gives 0.57 +/- 0.05 MPa in the reserve zone rising to 1.41 +/- 0.19 MPa in the mineralizing zone. Nanoscale sharp-tip AFM on human growth plate cryosections gives 130.7 +/- 36.6 MPa in the resting zone and 416.2 +/- 107.2 MPa in the hypertrophic zone - two to three orders of magnitude higher, because a 9 nm tip loaded to 6 uN probes the local mineralised/fibrillar matrix rather than the poroelastic tissue, and because the interstitial fluid cannot redistribute at that scale. Worse, the DIRECTION of the gradient is not agreed. Porcine unconfined compression makes the reserve zone the stiffest zone, with proliferative and hypertrophic zones half as stiff axially. Rabbit microindentation puts the peak in the upper hypertrophic zone. Rabbit cranial base AFM has modulus increasing monotonically from reserve to mineralizing zone. Species, site, age, hydration, loading rate and constitutive model all differ between these, and none of them is a human weight-bearing physis measured hydrated at tissue scale. The growth plate is also mechanically anisotropic - longitudinal indentation of the rabbit reserve zone gives 0.77 +/- 0.12 MPa versus 0.57 MPa transversely - and permeability differs threefold between zones, so a scalar modulus is an incomplete description in any case.
zonal_stiffness_gradient.human_evidence_note: One study measures modulus directly in human growth plate tissue, but at nanoscale with a sharp tip; no hydrated tissue-scale modulus of a human weight-bearing physis exists.
zonal_stiffness_gradient.translation_risk_reason: The only human numbers were obtained by a method whose values are 200-1000 fold above every animal tissue-scale measurement, so human and animal data cannot currently be reconciled or pooled.

rabbit cranial base: modulus increases monotonically RZ -> mineralizing zone (radhakrishnan2004)
porcine distal ulna: reserve zone stiffest (sergerie2009)
human phalangeal and tibial growth plate: RZ softer than HZ at nanoscale (xie2025)

bed_rest_growth_human.name: Bed rest as a human unloading experiment
bed_rest_growth_human.summary: Head-down-tilt bed rest is the standard terrestrial analogue of microgravity and produces a well-characterised musculoskeletal deconditioning syndrome, but as an experiment on the growth plate it is essentially empty. All established bed rest protocols - 14, 30 and 60 day campaigns with artificial gravity, exercise and pharmacological countermeasures - are conducted in adults, whose physes are closed, so they measure bone loss and muscle atrophy rather than growth modulation. What bed rest does reliably show in adults is spinal lengthening: recumbency removes the axial load that compresses intervertebral discs, and stature rises, which is the same mechanism as overnight recovery of diurnal height loss. Bed rest in children is never elective and long-term recumbency in paediatric populations occurs only alongside serious illness, so no controlled paediatric bed-rest study with a height-velocity endpoint has been located. This node therefore exists mainly to mark a gap: the mechanically cleanest human unloading protocol has never been applied to a growing skeleton, and the entire human unloading evidence base for the physis rests on disease cohorts and on spaceflight anthropometry in adults.
bed_rest_growth_human.human_evidence_note: No controlled bed rest study in children with a longitudinal growth endpoint was located; adult bed rest measures bone density and disc height, not physeal growth.
bed_rest_growth_human.translation_risk_reason: Human protocol, but performed exclusively in skeletally mature adults.
localization: human intervertebral discs and spine: lengthening under recumbency
human physis: no data

key_refs.one_line_finding: Quantifies the recumbency-driven recovery of stature that underlies the bed-rest spinal lengthening effect: ~70% of diurnal loss regained in the first half of the night
Provides the closest true unloading anthropometry in humans, from spaceflight rather than bed rest

blount_disease.name: Blount disease (tibia vara)
blount_disease.summary: Blount disease is progressive varus of the proximal tibia caused by growth suppression of the posteromedial proximal tibial physis, and it is the standard human illustration of the Hueter-Volkmann law running away with itself: varus alignment shifts load medially, medial compression suppresses medial growth, and the resulting deformity increases the medial load - a mechanical positive feedback identical in form to the scoliosis vicious cycle. Its epidemiology fits the mechanical account: obesity is the dominant risk factor and early walking is a recognised association, both of which raise medial compartment compressive stress in a child whose physis is still soft. Treatment is itself a mechanical experiment in the opposite direction - lateral tension band plating or transphyseal screw hemiepiphysiodesis restores growth symmetry - but Blount is the setting in which guided growth performs worst, with lower correction rates and more failures than idiopathic genu varum, and late-onset disease in heavy adolescents frequently requires osteotomy instead. That failure is informative: it implies the compressive stress in a heavy varus knee exceeds the range in which the physis remains modulable, or that the medial physis is already partly bridged. No study has measured the medial physeal stress in a child with Blount disease.
blount_disease.human_evidence_note: Human clinical entity with radiographic natural history and surgical outcome data; the mechanical cause is inferred from risk factors and response to unloading, never measured.
localization: human posteromedial proximal tibial physis: the site of suppressed growth

key_refs.one_line_finding: Guided growth outcomes in juvenile and adolescent Blount disease, showing lower success than in idiopathic deformity
Non-idiopathic aetiologies including varus deformity correct more slowly and less completely than idiopathic ones
Supplies the stress-growth coefficient on which the mechanical account of tibia vara depends

cytoskeletal_tension_chondrocyte.name: Chondrocyte cytoskeletal tension
cytoskeletal_tension_chondrocyte.summary: Cytoskeletal tension is the proximate variable that most mechanotransduction models assume the chondrocyte actually reads. In the growth plate there is one hard structural result: the actin- and adhesion-dependent 90-degree rotation of daughter chondrocytes that builds a column is driven by integrin beta-1 and antagonised by N-cadherin, so cytoskeletal force generation is directly responsible for growth plate architecture rather than merely reporting on it. The complementary measurement is deformation rather than force: hypertrophic chondrocytes in stress-controlled explant compression accumulate lateral and volumetric strain under static but not dynamic loading at the same mean stress and the same axial strain, showing that the cell's mechanical state is set by the viscoelastic history of the matrix, not by instantaneous load. The chondron pericellular matrix that mediates this is itself built mechanoresponsively. Beyond this, the F-actin/RhoA/ROCK evidence in cartilage comes from articular chondrocytes and dedifferentiation studies, and no measurement of actual cytoskeletal tension (traction force, FRET tension sensor) has been made in a growth plate chondrocyte in any species.
cytoskeletal_tension_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate cytoskeletal or cell-strain measurement located.
cytoskeletal_tension_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Explant and conditional-knockout data only; no human tissue is available for live cell-mechanics measurement.
localization: mouse growth plate proliferative zone: adhesion-dependent rotation confirmed (greer2024)
rat hypertrophic zone: cell strain measured (zimmermann2017)
human growth plate: no data

key_refs.one_line_finding: Adhesion-driven chondrocyte rotation, an actively force-generating process, builds growth plate columns
Hypertrophic chondrocyte lateral and volumetric strain depends on loading waveform, not mean stress
The chondron pericellular matrix transmitting load to the chondrocyte is mechanoresponsively assembled

distraction_osteogenesis.name: Distraction osteogenesis
distraction_osteogenesis.summary: Distraction osteogenesis is the deliberate creation of a de novo growth zone: a bone is osteotomised, allowed a latency period, then the fragments are separated slowly, and new bone forms in the gap. Ilizarov's canine experiments established that the resulting tissue is not a growth plate but a distinct structure - new bone forms in parallel columns extending in both directions from a central fibrous growth zone, with features of both physeal and intramembranous ossification and belonging to neither. Three variables were shown to determine success: stability of external fixation, preservation of periosteum, bone marrow and medullary blood supply at osteotomy, and the rate and rhythm of distraction. The same experiments showed the tension vector, not the bone's mechanical axis, sets the direction of new bone: canine tibiae widened by lateral distraction formed bone parallel to the applied tension even when perpendicular to the mechanical axis. Distraction osteogenesis is therefore the cleanest demonstration in any species that sustained tensile strain is an instructive, direction-setting stimulus for skeletal tissue formation - the tension arm of Hueter-Volkmann operating outside a physis. It is routine human surgery, so its efficacy in humans is not in doubt; what is absent is any human measurement of the strain or stress in the regenerate.
distraction_osteogenesis.human_evidence_note: Distraction osteogenesis is performed in humans daily with radiographically measured regenerate formation; only the mechanical dose at tissue level is unmeasured.
distraction_osteogenesis.translation_risk_reason: The canine-derived rate and rhythm parameters were adopted into human practice and have held for four decades.
localization: canine tibial diaphysis (experimental): confirmed (ilizarov1989, ilizarov1989a)
human long bones: routine clinical practice

key_refs.one_line_finding: Defined the rate and rhythm dose-response and showed the regenerate is a physis-like but distinct structure with a central growth zone
Fixation stability and soft-tissue/marrow preservation determine osteogenesis; new bone aligns with the tension vector, not the mechanical axis

distraction_rate_dose_response.name: Distraction rate and rhythm dose-response
distraction_rate_dose_response.summary: The canonical prescription - 1 mm per day in four increments - traces to a single primary source, Ilizarov's canine tibial series, and the primary source supports it. Three rates were compared at fixed frequency: 0.5 mm/day often caused premature consolidation of the lengthening bone, 2.0 mm/day often caused undesirable changes in the elongating soft tissues (fascia, muscle, vessels, nerve, skin), and 1.0 mm/day gave the best result. Frequency was varied independently at 1, 4 and 60 steps per day and the finding was monotonic: the greater the frequency, the better the outcome, so 4 steps/day is a practical compromise rather than an optimum - continuous distraction would be predicted to be better still. The reported endpoints are histomorphological and biochemical grading of the regenerate and of the elongating soft tissues, not a numeric growth rate, so no sensitivity coefficient (mm of regenerate per mm/day of distraction) exists. The upper and lower failure modes are mechanistically distinct - premature consolidation below the optimum is a bone problem, soft-tissue injury above it is a nerve/muscle/vessel problem - which means the therapeutic window is set by two different tissues and should be expected to differ by segment, age and species. Human practice inherited the 1 mm/day figure without an equivalent human dose-finding study.
distraction_rate_dose_response.human_evidence_note: Human limb lengthening uses ~1 mm/day in 3-4 increments by inheritance from the canine data; no human study has randomised rate or rhythm against a regenerate-quality endpoint.
distraction_rate_dose_response.translation_risk_reason: A single canine series with qualitative endpoints underwrites a universal human prescription; segment, age and pathology are known in clinical practice to shift the tolerable rate, but that shift has not been quantified.

key_refs.one_line_finding: 0.5 mm/day premature consolidation, 2.0 mm/day soft-tissue damage, 1.0 mm/day optimal; higher frequency always better
Establishes the fixation-stability and tissue-preservation conditions under which the rate/rhythm optimum holds

disuse_growth_effect.name: Disuse and longitudinal growth
disuse_growth_effect.summary: Removing load does not simply reverse the Hueter-Volkmann effect. Two observations bound the question. In the growth plate itself, limb immobilisation abolished the abnormal peripheral ossification phenotype of cartilage-specific Ift88-null mice, showing that the disruptive stimulus in the adolescent plate is physiological load and that unloading is protective rather than growth-promoting for that phenotype. In humans, chronic disuse produces smaller and thinner long bones: children and adolescents with cerebral palsy and other neuromotor impairments have reduced bone size and cortical thickness, and even ambulatory children with spastic cerebral palsy already show smaller bone area and trabecular deficits. Whether the length deficit in these children is a physeal effect or is dominated by nutrition, muscle traction and the underlying neurological disorder is unresolved and is the reason human disuse cannot be read as a clean unloading experiment. Perpendicular evidence comes from prenatal akinesia, where absent fetal movement impairs joint and bone development and maternal exercise rescues it. The consistent pattern is that loading is required for normal skeletal form and cross-section, while its effect on longitudinal growth rate is smaller and its sign depends on the waveform.
disuse_growth_effect.human_evidence_note: Human disuse data come from cerebral palsy and neuromotor impairment cohorts in which disuse is confounded with nutrition, spasticity and the primary neurological lesion.
disuse_growth_effect.translation_risk_reason: The controlled unloading experiments are murine limb immobilisation; the human comparisons are uncontrolled disease cohorts.

human long bones in cerebral palsy: reduced size and cortical thickness (hodgson2025)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Limb immobilisation abolished the growth plate phenotype of Ift88 deletion, proving the phenotype is load-driven

diurnal_stature_variation.name: Diurnal stature variation
diurnal_stature_variation.summary: Human stature falls measurably over a waking day and recovers overnight, and the effect is large enough to corrupt growth monitoring. In eight young adults measured to 1 mm precision, mean circadian variation was 19.3 mm, 1.1% of stature; 54% of the loss occurred within the first hour after rising and about 70% was regained during the first half of the night. The loss is load-dependent: static shoulder loads from 2.5 to 40 kg increased the rate of shrinkage nonlinearly, and repetitive lifting produced more shrinkage than the equivalent static load, so the disc creeps faster under cyclic than sustained loading - the opposite ordering to what static compression does to the growth plate. In children the effect is smaller but not negligible: 12-14 year old boys lost 2.0 mm from 09:30 to 14:00 and 4.6 mm from 10:00 to 17:00 with sitting height falling 2.0 and 2.8 mm, against a measurement standard error of 1.8 mm, and children with idiopathic scoliosis lost a mean 7 mm standing (0.43%) and 7 mm sitting (0.79%) between early morning and evening. The mechanism is intervertebral disc fluid exudation and unloading of the spinal curves, not physeal growth; the practical consequence is that a single unrecorded measurement time can hide or fabricate a centimetre of apparent annual growth.
diurnal_stature_variation.human_evidence_note: Directly measured in adults and children with stadiometry accurate to 1-2 mm, replicated across several independent groups since 1974.
localization: human intervertebral discs and spinal curvature: the source of the variation
human physis: not involved

epiphysiodesis.name: Epiphysiodesis
epiphysiodesis.summary: Epiphysiodesis is the deliberate, permanent destruction or mechanical bridging of a physis to stop growth at that site, used to equalise leg lengths or to limit final height. As an experiment it is the mechanical converse of guided growth: instead of modulating growth by asymmetric compression, it abolishes it by continuity of bone across the plate. Its outcomes establish two facts relevant to this layer. First, surgically induced physeal arrest in humans is permanent - 28 to 40 year follow-up after epiphysiodesis for leg length discrepancy shows the correction is maintained into middle age, with no evidence of late intra-articular knee deformity after temporary epiphysiodesis. Second, the effect is quantitatively predictable enough to be planned: remaining growth prediction methods are accurate enough to time the operation, which means human physeal output is forecastable from age and skeletal maturity even though it is not forecastable from load. Bilateral epiphysiodesis is also used deliberately to reduce final height in extremely tall adolescents, which is the only human procedure that directly trades measured growth for a mechanical intervention on the physis.
epiphysiodesis.human_evidence_note: Long-term human follow-up series with radiographic and clinical endpoints.
localization: human distal femoral, proximal tibial and distal radial/ulnar physes: routine clinical targets

key_refs.one_line_finding: 28-40 year follow-up shows permanent epiphysiodesis for leg length discrepancy maintains correction into middle age
Bilateral epiphysiodesis safely reduces final height in extremely tall adolescents

focal_adhesion_kinase.name: Focal adhesion kinase (FAK/PTK2)
focal_adhesion_kinase.summary: FAK is the obligatory kinase downstream of integrin engagement and is therefore the assumed transducer converting growth plate matrix strain into intracellular signalling. The assumption is not backed by a growth-plate experiment. The direct skeletal mechanotransduction evidence for FAK is in osteocytes, where mechanosensitive FAK together with phosphodiesterase 8A sets intracellular cAMP in response to load. In cartilage, cyclic tensile stress restores chondrocyte homeostasis through an integrin-FAK-RhoA/ROCK2 axis, but that work is in articular chondrocytes, and integrin-beta1/FAK/Akt signalling supports chondrogenic activity in human chondrocyte culture rather than in a physis. No conditional Ptk2 deletion in a chondrocyte Cre line with a longitudinal growth readout has been located, and there is no zonal FAK localisation in human or animal growth plate. FAK is included here as a mechanistically necessary but experimentally unvalidated node, and its confidence reflects that: the inference runs from integrin beta-1's demonstrated growth plate role, not from FAK data.
focal_adhesion_kinase.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate FAK data; human evidence is limited to cultured chondrocytes.
focal_adhesion_kinase.translation_risk_reason: The node is an inference from integrin biology; without a growth plate experiment in any species the translation question cannot yet be posed properly.
localization: osteocytes: functional mechanotransduction evidence

gravity_posture_spinal_loading.name: Gravity, posture and spinal loading
gravity_posture_spinal_loading.summary: Gravity acting through posture is the largest sustained mechanical variable acting on the growing human axial skeleton, and it can be titrated without surgery. Upright posture compresses the intervertebral discs and vertebral endplate physes; recumbency releases them, producing the overnight recovery of ~70% of the day's stature loss; and true weightlessness releases them completely, producing a stature gain of up to 3% that fully reverses on return to Earth. Added axial load scales the effect: static shoulder loads of 2.5-40 kg increased the shrinkage rate nonlinearly, and repetitive lifting exceeded equivalent static loading. This makes posture and gravity the natural experiment that most closely mirrors the animal compression studies - except that everything that has actually been measured in humans concerns the disc, not the physis. The vertebral endplate physis sits in series with the disc and must experience some fraction of the same load, but the partition between disc deformation and physeal stress has never been measured in a living human, which is precisely why the human vertebral stress-growth relation is unquantified. Finite element models of the growth plate show that plate morphology itself adapts to the local mechanical environment, so the geometry through which gravity acts is not fixed.
gravity_posture_spinal_loading.human_evidence_note: Postural and gravitational effects on stature are directly measured in humans; the share of that load borne by the physis is not.
gravity_posture_spinal_loading.translation_risk_reason: Human measurement, though the physeal component is inferred.
localization: human intervertebral disc: directly measured
human vertebral endplate physis: load share never measured

guided_growth_tension_band.name: Guided growth (tension band plating)
guided_growth_tension_band.summary: Guided growth is the therapeutic application of Hueter-Volkmann: a two-hole plate with divergent screws is placed extraperiosteally across one side of a physis, tethering that side while the other continues to grow, so the bone angulates. It is the largest human dataset on mechanically modulated physeal growth. In 654 growth modulations in 313 children the mean correction rate was 0.67 +/- 0.55 degrees/month for the distal femur (mLDFA) and 0.43 +/- 0.38 degrees/month for the proximal tibia (mMPTA); a neutral mechanical axis was achieved in 68.7% overall, 78.2% in idiopathic and 66.3% in non-idiopathic aetiologies, and older age at surgery and varus deformity predicted slower correction. The very wide standard deviations - roughly 80-90% of the mean - are the important number: the human response to a nominally identical mechanical intervention is far more variable than the tight animal stress-growth relation would predict. The mechanical dose is unknown: the only estimate comes from personalised finite element models of four human distal femoral epiphyses under gait loads, which show the implant locally imposes static stress and removes cyclic loading at the insertion site while raising tensile stress on the contralateral side, so the plate acts through both arms of the static/dynamic distinction, not by compression alone. Correction is not always permanent; rebound after implant removal is recognised.
guided_growth_tension_band.human_evidence_note: Thousands of human physes have been mechanically modulated with radiographically measured angular outcomes; only the applied stress is unmeasured.
localization: human distal femoral and proximal tibial physes: direct clinical measurement (tolk2026)

gymnastics_stature_effect.name: Gymnastics and stature
gymnastics_stature_effect.summary: Female artistic gymnasts are short, mature late and have a blunted pubertal spurt; whether training causes this is the longest-running controversy in human growth mechanobiology. The pro-causal case rests on prospective cohorts: 22 gymnasts training >18 h/wk had peak height velocity 5.48 cm/yr against 8.0 cm/yr in age-matched swimmers, a height SDS that fell significantly over 2.35 years while the swimmers' did not, selective stunting of leg length (sitting height/leg length ratio 1.054 vs 1.100), and falling predicted adult height - and, critically, no change in the chronological-age/bone-age ratio, which weakens the pure maturational-delay explanation. A dose gradient exists within gymnasts: advanced (20-27 h/wk) versus intermediate (7.5-22 h/wk) trainees had lower peripubertal sitting-height velocity (2.3 vs 3.1 cm/yr) and over 35% of pre- and peripubertal gymnasts had height velocity below 4.5 cm/yr. The selection case is equally concrete: gymnasts' growth curves are indistinguishable from short, late-maturing girls with short parents, the spurt is present and about one year late rather than absent, and adult height is normal in retired gymnasts. The FIG Scientific Commission review concluded that available data cannot establish causality because training volume is confounded with selection, energy availability and family size, and epidemiological criteria for causation are not met. Adjudication: the attenuation during training is real and dose-related; the claim that it removes adult height is not established, and no study has separated mechanical loading of the physis from energy deficit and hypothalamic suppression, which is the mechanistically decisive question for this layer.
gymnastics_stature_effect.human_evidence_note: All data are human prospective anthropometric cohorts; the dispute is about confounding and causal inference, not about whether the association exists.

hueter_volkmann_law.name: Hueter-Volkmann law
hueter_volkmann_law.summary: Stated qualitatively in the 1860s-1870s, the law asserts that sustained compression across a physis slows longitudinal growth and sustained tension accelerates it. Its quantitative form comes from one experimental programme (Stokes, Aronsson and colleagues), which applied calibrated external loading apparatus across caudal vertebral and proximal tibial growth plates in rats, rabbits and calves for 8 days and measured growth as the separation of fluorochrome labels given 24 and 48 h before euthanasia. Over roughly -0.2 to +0.1 MPa the stress-growth relation was apparently linear, with a growth-rate sensitivity of 17.1% per 0.1 MPa averaged across all plates (range 9.2-23.9% per 0.1 MPa), 15.0%/0.1 MPa for vertebrae and 18.6%/0.1 MPa for proximal tibia, despite baseline growth rates spanning 30 um/day (rat vertebra) to 366 um/day (rabbit proximal tibia). Cellularly the modulation is not a single mechanism: about half the growth change under sustained compression is accounted for by reduced hypertrophic chondrocyte enlargement and the remainder by fewer proliferative-zone chondrocytes per column, and in multiple regression the hypertrophic enlargement term carries the larger coefficient (1.39 vs 0.72). The response is asymmetric: compression suppresses more than an equal tension accelerates (52% vs 113% of control at ~60% body weight in rat tail vertebrae over 4 weeks). No equivalent sensitivity coefficient has ever been measured in a human physis; every human application - guided growth, vertebral body tethering, the scoliosis vicious cycle - extrapolates the animal coefficient.
hueter_volkmann_law.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is entirely inferential: guided growth, epiphysiodesis, vertebral body tethering and the progression of Blount disease and scoliosis behave as the law predicts, but no human study has applied a known stress across a physis and measured the resulting growth rate, so no human sensitivity coefficient exists.
hueter_volkmann_law.translation_risk_reason: The coefficient is extrapolated to humans from three quadrupedal species at two skeletal sites over 8-28 day loading windows; human physes differ in thickness, baseline growth rate, loading history and duration of exposure, and the human in vivo physeal stress is itself unmeasured.

integrin_beta1_chondrocyte.name: Integrin beta-1 (ITGB1) in growth plate chondrocytes
integrin_beta1_chondrocyte.summary: Integrin beta-1 is the growth plate's principal cell-matrix adhesion receptor and, unusually for this layer, its growth-plate function has been tested directly rather than borrowed from articular cartilage. Live time-lapse confocal imaging of mouse cranial base explants with conditional Itgb1 deletion shows that column formation fails: the 90-degree rotation by which a daughter chondrocyte aligns with the long axis of the bone is integrin beta-1-driven. Conditional deletion of the cell-cell adhesion molecule Cdh2 (N-cadherin) also disrupts column formation, but the compound mutant resolves the hierarchy - defective rotation in the N-cadherin mutant is rescued by heterozygous loss of Itgb1, so N-cadherin acts as a negative regulator of integrin beta-1 rather than as a parallel driver. Because a column is the structural unit of longitudinal growth, this places integrin beta-1 upstream of growth plate architecture itself. Integrin beta-1 is also a load-transducing receptor: mechanical loading of chondrocytes activates beta-1 integrins and FGFR, and the two target distinct, non-overlapping mechano-response gene sets. The integrin's ligand environment is itself mechanically tuned, since the chondron pericellular matrix through which load reaches the cell surface is built and remodelled in a mechanoresponsive way. No human growth plate integrin beta-1 perturbation data exist.
integrin_beta1_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: All functional data are mouse conditional knockouts and cell culture; no human physeal integrin beta-1 study located.
integrin_beta1_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: Conditional deletion in mouse cartilage cannot be replicated in humans and the column-rotation assay has no human counterpart.

loading_effect_plate_height.name: Loading effect on growth plate height and zonal structure
loading_effect_plate_height.summary: Sustained compression thins the growth plate and the thinning is zonally specific. In rat caudal vertebrae under 0.2 MPa for two weeks, static loading significantly reduced total plate thickness, the number of proliferative chondrocytes per column and hypertrophic chondrocyte height, whereas dynamic loading at the same mean stress produced the same growth-rate reduction with none of these histological changes. Under four weeks of ~60% body weight compression, hypertrophic zone height fell to 87% of control, mean hypertrophic cell height to 85%, and the increment in cell height along the growth direction to 78%; distraction changed none of these significantly, which is why compression and tension are not mirror images. Across species, altered plate height correlates with altered growth rate but explains it only partly: proliferative cell number per unit width and maximum hypertrophic cell height together account for the growth change with correlation coefficients of 0.38 and 0.56. Plate thinning is reversible - height returned to sham within 10 days of unloading. Plate thickness is also the single most influential parameter in finite-element models of how the plate adapts its shape to the local mechanical environment.
loading_effect_plate_height.human_evidence_note: Human growth plate height under known load has not been measured; paediatric MRI physeal thickness studies do not control applied stress.
loading_effect_plate_height.translation_risk_reason: Histomorphometry requires sacrifice, so all zonal data are animal; human physeal thickness data are cross-sectional imaging without a load variable.

mechanical_modulation_growth.name: Mechanical modulation of longitudinal growth
mechanical_modulation_growth.summary: Mechanical modulation is the change in endochondral growth rate produced by an externally imposed stress across a physis, over and above the growth the plate would have produced unloaded. Its measured magnitude in animals is large: 8 days of sustained loading changes growth rate by up to 53%, and the response is approximately linear in stress at 17.1% per 0.1 MPa. Two cell-level levers carry the effect - the number of proliferative chondrocytes generated per column and the final height reached by hypertrophic chondrocytes - and both are altered in the same direction as growth. Modulation is reversible: after 15 days of 0.2 MPa compression on rat caudal vertebrae, both growth rate and plate height returned to sham values within 10 days of unloading. Duration matters independently of magnitude, since halving the daily loading time from 24 h to 12 h roughly halves the growth suppression, and the response saturates or reverses with time under a fixed displacement, as posterior vertebral tethering in kyphotic swine shows a 53% growth-modulation advantage of high over low tether tension at 2 weeks that has vanished by 4 weeks. In humans the process is only observed through its surgical exploitation, never measured against a known applied stress.
mechanical_modulation_growth.human_evidence_note: Guided growth, epiphysiodesis and vertebral tethering demonstrate that human physes are mechanically modulable, but the applied stress is never measured, so the human dose-response is unknown.
mechanical_modulation_growth.translation_risk_reason: All dose-response data are from quadruped tail vertebrae and proximal tibiae under externally applied apparatus over days to weeks.

key_refs.one_line_finding: Growth changes of up to 53% track proliferative cell number and hypertrophic cell height

physeal_bar_formation.name: Physeal bar formation
physeal_bar_formation.summary: A physeal bar is a bridge of bone spanning the growth plate that tethers one region while the rest continues to grow, producing angular deformity, or that arrests growth entirely if extensive. It is the pathological limit case of mechanical tethering: the bar imposes an internal, self-generated tension band. Human incidence after physeal fracture is uncertain and probably higher than textbooks state - a prospective cohort of 332 children found growth arrest in 30.1% overall, against up to 5.5% in the prior literature, with 86% after distal femoral physeal fractures, older age and initial displacement associated with arrest; the authors caution that diagnostic criteria for arrest vary and the true figure may be lower. Physeal fractures themselves account for 18-30% of all paediatric fractures. Mechanistically, a reproducible mouse distal femoral drill-hole model shows bone tissue accumulating in the defect over 42 days and identifies the cellular source: Pdgfra- and Pdgfrb-lineage cells, absent from the plate before injury, migrate into the defect and contribute to the bar. This makes the bar a repair response by perivascular/mesenchymal populations rather than transdifferentiation of resident chondrocytes.
physeal_bar_formation.human_evidence_note: Human incidence and risk factors are measured prospectively; the cellular mechanism is mouse only.
physeal_bar_formation.translation_risk_reason: Incidence data are human; the Pdgfra/Pdgfrb lineage attribution rests on mouse reporter lines with no human counterpart.

physeal_stress_in_vivo.name: In vivo physeal stress
physeal_stress_in_vivo.summary: Every quantitative claim in this layer is expressed per MPa of applied stress, and the value of that stress in a living human has never been measured. The animal stress-growth experiments impose known stress with an external apparatus, over a range of roughly 0.02-0.2 MPa, chosen for instrument convenience rather than because it matches physiological loading. The only human-facing numbers come from modelling: personalised finite element models of four human distal femoral epiphyses driven by instrumented gait analysis show that stress across the physis is markedly heterogeneous and geometry-dependent, that a tension-band plate imposes local static stress and abolishes cyclic loading at its insertion, and that tensile stress rises on the opposite side - but the authors are explicit that their models are not fully participant-specific in geometry and loading, so absolute values should not be quoted as measurements. Related FE work shows growth plate shape itself adapts to the local mechanical environment, so the geometry that determines stress is not a fixed input. Direct measurement is method-blocked: an implanted pressure transducer across a healthy child's physis is not ethically available, and the alternatives (MRI-based strain mapping, dual-fluoroscopy kinematics driving subject-specific models validated against cadaveric measurement) have not been applied to a paediatric physis. This is the single largest missing number in the layer, because without it the animal sensitivity coefficient cannot be converted into a human prediction.
physeal_stress_in_vivo.human_evidence_note: No in vivo human physeal stress measurement exists; the only human values are finite-element estimates whose authors caution against treating them as measurements.
physeal_stress_in_vivo.translation_risk_reason: The entire clinical use of the Hueter-Volkmann coefficient depends on assuming that human physeal stress falls in the range the animal experiments probed, an assumption that has never been checked.

piezo1_channel.name: PIEZO1
piezo1_channel.summary: PIEZO1 is the only mechanosensitive channel with loss-of-function evidence obtained inside the growth plate rather than in articular cartilage. Col2a1-Cre inactivation in mice produces near-absence of trabecular bone beneath the growth plate postnatally and multiple rib fractures adjacent to the physes by day 7, while linear skeletal growth is only mildly affected - so the channel is required for the bone that the plate produces more than for the plate's own output. Col10a1-Cre deletion restricted to hypertrophic chondrocytes gives an osteopenic phenotype with increased osteoclast number in the primary spongiosa, mediated by RANKL repression and OPG induction, without altering hypertrophic apoptosis or chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transdifferentiation. Under applied compression, PIEZO1 is upregulated in vertebral growth plate chondrocytes and drives GPX4 loss and ferroptosis; Col2a1-CreERT;Piezo1fl/fl deletion or local pharmacological blockade slowed scoliosis progression in mice. PIEZO1 colocalises with the primary cilium in mouse growth plate chondrocytes and its stress response requires IFT88. Human data are thin: increased PIEZO1 protein has been shown in cartilaginous zones of human osteophytes, but no study has localised PIEZO1 in human growth plate tissue.
piezo1_channel.human_evidence_note: The only human PIEZO1 protein data in cartilage come from osteophytes in osteoarthritis; PIEZO1 has not been localised or functionally tested in human physeal tissue.
piezo1_channel.translation_risk_reason: Entirely conditional-knockout mouse biology; human physeal expression is unestablished and mice do not undergo epiphyseal fusion.

piezo2_channel.name: PIEZO2
piezo2_channel.summary: PIEZO2 is repeatedly listed as a growth plate mechanotransducer but the supporting experiments were done elsewhere. Chondrocyte-specific Piezo2 inactivation with Col2a1-Cre produced no growth plate or endochondral ossification phenotype and did not protect against surgically induced osteoarthritis, in the same study in which Piezo1 deletion did both. In inducible Aggrecan-Cre mice, Piezo2 deletion reduced pain behaviour and preserved activity after destabilisation of the medial meniscus but failed to protect cartilage, and separately reduced trabecular bone volume, thickness and density independent of injury - a bone rather than physis effect. The best-characterised PIEZO2 mechanism in skeletal tissue is neuronal: in dorsal root ganglion neurons, PIEZO2 activation by abnormal mechanical stress releases CGRP, which acts through RAMP1 on cartilage endplate cells to drive IL-6 and IL-1beta, degrading the endplate. No experiment has localised or deleted PIEZO2 in a growth plate with a growth-rate readout, and there is no human growth plate PIEZO2 data at all. Human PIEZO2 loss-of-function causes distal arthrogryposis and proprioceptive loss, with skeletal consequences that are plausibly secondary to absent fetal movement rather than to a chondrocyte-autonomous defect.
piezo2_channel.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate PIEZO2 expression or function data exist; human PIEZO2 phenotypes are neuromuscular and arthrogrypotic.

primary_cilium_mechanosensing.name: Primary cilium mechanosensing in the growth plate
primary_cilium_mechanosensing.summary: The primary cilium is the one mechanosensory organelle with a clean, loading-controlled growth plate experiment. Cartilage-specific inducible deletion of Ift88 (AggrecanCreERT2;Ift88fl/fl) in juvenile and adolescent mice reduced ciliation and disrupted chondrocyte differentiation, cartilage resorption and mineralisation - but only in the peripheral tibial regions beneath the load-bearing compartments of the knee, which accumulated enlarged hypertrophic populations. Hedgehog signalling was preserved, so the defect is not the usual ciliary Hh phenotype; instead hypertrophic VEGF expression fell, with downstream loss of vascular recruitment, osteoclastic activity and cartilage-to-bone replacement. Two controls make the mechanical interpretation strong: raising physiological loading in control mice reproduced the impaired peripheral ossification, and limb immobilisation abolished the Ift88-null phenotype. Separately, PIEZO1 colocalises with the cilium in mouse growth plate chondrocytes and chloral hydrate cilia disruption (cilia-positive cells 97.2% to 16.6%) or IFT88 knockdown reversed compression-induced cartilage degeneration, placing the cilium downstream of or in a feedback loop with PIEZO1. All of this is mouse; no human physeal cilium mechanics data exist.
primary_cilium_mechanosensing.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate ciliary mechanosensing data; human ciliopathies affect the skeleton but through Hedgehog patterning rather than a demonstrated load pathway.
primary_cilium_mechanosensing.translation_risk_reason: Requires inducible cartilage-specific gene deletion plus controlled limb loading and immobilisation, none of which is possible in humans.

scoliosis_vertebral_growth.name: Scoliosis and vertebral growth modulation
scoliosis_vertebral_growth.summary: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is the largest natural human experiment in physeal mechanobiology, through the 'vicious cycle' hypothesis: a pre-existing lateral curve makes muscular and gravitational loading asymmetric across vertebral endplate physes, asymmetric loading modulates vertebral growth by Hueter-Volkmann, the vertebra wedges, and the curve worsens. The hypothesis has been tested quantitatively rather than merely asserted - a frontal-plane mathematical simulation using the measured animal stress-growth sensitivity reproduced observed rates of curve progression, giving quantitative data consistent with the cycle. The animal counterpart is direct: sustained compression and distraction across rat and calf tail vertebrae produce wedging and altered growth exactly as required. Two caveats sit on the human side. Vertebral wedging in the animal model arises from both asymmetric growth and remodelling, not growth alone. And clinical growth modulation shows the relation is not a simple monotone function of applied load: in kyphotic swine, high tether tension gave 53% growth modulation versus -1% for low tension at 2 weeks, but by 2-4 weeks the two were indistinguishable (14% vs 10%), so the tension benefit is transient and modulation becomes load-independent. Human vertebral body tethering works, but no human study has measured the stress across a vertebral endplate physis.
scoliosis_vertebral_growth.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is the observed correlation between curve magnitude, remaining growth and progression, plus the success of tethering; the mechanical step is modelled from animal coefficients.
scoliosis_vertebral_growth.translation_risk_reason: The phenomenon is human and the treatment works in humans, but the quantitative mechanism is imported wholesale from quadruped tail vertebrae.

spaceflight_microgravity_growth.name: Spaceflight, microgravity and growth
spaceflight_microgravity_growth.summary: Astronauts get taller in orbit, but the gain is spinal unloading, not endochondral growth. Photogrammetric and tape anthropometry on nine ISS crew members showed a biphasic change: stature rose by up to 3% in the early flight phase, then plateaued for the remainder of the mission, and returned to preflight values after landing. Acromion height followed the same pattern, while chest, hip, thigh and calf circumferences fell by up to 11%. A 3% gain in an adult of 1.75 m is roughly 5 cm, several times the ~19 mm diurnal stature loss on Earth, consistent with removal of axial compression from the whole spine plus loss of the standing postural curves. Full reversibility on return, and the fact that these are adults with closed physes, rule out a growth plate contribution in this dataset. There is no human paediatric spaceflight, so the effect of microgravity on a growing physis is unmeasured in humans. The rodent literature provides the only direct evidence, showing spaceflight alters skeletal tissue including the spinal column, and simulated microgravity has been used experimentally to reverse PIEZO1-driven growth plate ossification in mice - which is a mechanistic argument that unloading acts on the physis, not a measurement of growth rate in flight.
spaceflight_microgravity_growth.human_evidence_note: Direct human in-flight anthropometry exists, but only in adults with closed physes, so it says nothing about physeal growth.
spaceflight_microgravity_growth.translation_risk_reason: The human measurement is real but concerns disc and posture, not growth plate output.

sport_specific_loading_human.name: Sport-specific mechanical loading effects on the human skeleton
sport_specific_loading_human.summary: Sport gives the only human experiments in which a physis is loaded far outside the normal range for years, and the results split by site. Where loading is compressive, repetitive and applied through a small joint, local growth is suppressed: in gymnasts the wrist bears body weight, and imaging shows distal radial physeal stress injury with acquired positive ulnar variance, i.e. the radius is shortened relative to the ulna in the same limb - an internally controlled demonstration of load-suppressed physeal output in humans. Wrist pain and physeal injury are common enough in adolescent artistic gymnasts to have their own systematic review and meta-analysis. Where loading is impact-type, intermittent and axial, growth is preserved or promoted: a 24-week supervised jumping protocol (3 sessions/week, 50 min) in 47 prepubertal short-stature children gave 4.20 cm of height gain against 2.48 cm in controls (p=0.001) alongside a femoral neck BMD Z-score gain of 1.075. The two findings are consistent with the static-versus-dynamic distinction seen in animals rather than with a single monotonic load-growth relation. Neither the gymnast wrist nor the jumping trial measures the stress at the physis, so the human dose axis remains empty; the jumping trial is also small, single-centre and not blinded, and its mediation analysis (via femoral neck BMD, beta=-0.442) is fragile.
sport_specific_loading_human.human_evidence_note: Both the gymnast wrist series and the jumping trial are human, but neither measures physeal stress and neither is randomised with adult height as the endpoint.
localization: human distal radial physis in gymnasts: stress injury and positive ulnar variance (difiori2006)
human lower limb physes under impact loading: growth promotion inferred, not localised

key_refs.one_line_finding: Repetitive weight-bearing wrist loading in gymnasts causes distal radial physeal injury and acquired positive ulnar variance
Quantifies the epidemiology and risk factors of wrist pain and injury in adolescent artistic gymnasts
24 weeks of jumping exercise gave 4.20 cm height gain vs 2.48 cm in controls in prepubertal short-stature children

static_vs_dynamic_loading.name: Static versus dynamic loading of the growth plate
static_vs_dynamic_loading.summary: The clinically important claim is that dynamic loading is growth-preserving where static compression is suppressive. The evidence supports a weaker and more specific statement. Duty cycle matters: cutting sustained 0.1 MPa compression from 24 h/day to 12 h/day raised rat vertebral growth from 82% to 90-93% of control and tibial growth from 70% to 84-86%, with no difference between day and night loading. But oscillation about a non-zero mean does not spare growth: sinusoidal 0.2 MPa +/- 30% at 0.1 Hz reduced rat caudal vertebral growth by exactly the same 19% as sustained 0.2 MPa, while sparing plate histology - only the static group lost plate thickness, proliferative cells per column and hypertrophic cell height. In swine explants at matched compressive strain (10% static vs 7-13% at 0.1 Hz for 48 h) the static group lost aggrecan, collagen II and collagen X while the dynamic group maintained the proliferative:hypertrophic ratio and matrix synthesis but lost columnar alignment. The mechanical explanation is viscoelastic: under stress control, static compression permits continued time-dependent creep, so hypertrophic chondrocytes accumulate significantly greater lateral and volumetric strain than under dynamic loading at the same mean stress and the same axial strain, and higher frequency reduces volumetric strain further. So mean stress sets growth rate; the waveform sets tissue damage.
