static_vs_dynamic_loading.human_evidence_note: No human study compares static with dynamic physeal loading; the tension-band plate is the closest analogue and it is modelled, not measured.
static_vs_dynamic_loading.translation_risk_reason: All comparisons are rodent tail vertebrae or swine explants; loading waveforms used are far simpler than human gait.

key_refs.one_line_finding: Halving daily loading duration roughly halved growth suppression at both vertebral and tibial sites
Static and dynamic loading at equal mean stress reduced growth equally (19%) but only static damaged plate histomorphometry
At matched strain, static compression destroyed matrix protein expression while dynamic preserved it but disordered columns
Static stress-controlled loading produces greater lateral and volumetric hypertrophic cell strain than dynamic at equal mean stress
Dynamic compression reduced growth rate without histomorphometric change unless both magnitude and frequency were raised together
Static compression reduced growth plate chondrocyte viability more than dynamic at comparable loading

strain_frequency_dependence.name: Strain frequency dependence
strain_frequency_dependence.summary: Frequency has been varied over a narrow band (0.1-1.0 Hz) in in vivo growth plate loading and it changes both growth and tissue response. In rat caudal vertebrae held at 0.2 MPa mean, sinusoidal loading at 0.1 Hz (+/-0.2 MPa) and at 1.0 Hz (+/-0.06 MPa) each reduced growth rate below sham without measurable histomorphometric change, whereas 1.0 Hz combined with +/-0.14 MPa produced repeated inflammation and loss of plate integrity - so frequency and amplitude are not independent. At the cell level frequency acts through viscoelasticity: in stress-controlled explant compression, higher-frequency dynamic loading produced significantly lower hypertrophic chondrocyte volumetric strain than lower-frequency loading (p=0.002), because each cycle is too short for full creep. Distraction osteogenesis provides the only frequency dose-response with a clinical endpoint: at a fixed 1.0 mm/day, increasing the number of increments from 1 to 4 to 60 per day monotonically improved regenerate quality in the canine tibia. No physiological frequency spectrum of human physeal loading (gait at ~1-2 Hz, running higher) has been mapped onto a growth response.
strain_frequency_dependence.human_evidence_note: The only human-facing frequency evidence is distraction rhythm in limb lengthening, where higher increment frequency at fixed rate is preferred; physiological gait-frequency effects on the physis are unmeasured.
strain_frequency_dependence.translation_risk_reason: Frequencies tested (0.1-1.0 Hz) barely overlap human locomotor loading, and the canine distraction data concern regenerate bone, not a native physis.

key_refs.one_line_finding: Frequency and amplitude interact; each alone reduced growth without histological change, together they destroyed the plate
Higher-frequency dynamic compression gave lower hypertrophic cell volumetric strain
At fixed 1.0 mm/day, greater distraction frequency (up to 60 steps/day) gave better osteogenesis

strain_magnitude_dependence.name: Strain magnitude dependence of growth modulation
strain_magnitude_dependence.summary: Within the range tested experimentally the growth response is linear in applied stress rather than threshold-like: across rat, rabbit and calf plates the percentage growth change was proportional to stress with a slope of 17.1% per 0.1 MPa and no evidence of a dead band around zero. The range actually probed is narrow, roughly 0.02-0.2 MPa in compression and a comparable magnitude in distraction, so linearity outside it is an assumption. In explant work strain rather than stress is the controlled variable and the magnitudes used are an order of magnitude larger than physiological: 10% static compressive strain for 48 h in swine ulnar plates suppressed every histomorphological parameter measured and abolished aggrecan and collagen II/X expression, and compressive modulation reduces chondrocyte viability in a magnitude-dependent way. Magnitude also interacts non-additively with frequency: raising either alone reduced growth without histological change in rat caudal vertebrae, but raising both together (1.0 Hz at 0.2 +/- 0.14 MPa) caused repeated inflammation and destroyed the tissue. There is no measured strain-magnitude dose-response curve for any human physis.
strain_magnitude_dependence.human_evidence_note: No human physeal strain-magnitude dose-response exists; human physeal strain in vivo has not been measured.
strain_magnitude_dependence.translation_risk_reason: Linearity is asserted over a narrow, non-physiological stress window in quadrupeds; explant strains used are far above in vivo values.

key_refs.one_line_finding: Growth change was apparently linear in stress with a 17.1%/0.1 MPa slope
10% static compressive strain for 48 h abolished aggrecan and collagen II/X expression in swine explants
Magnitude and frequency interact: raising both together destroyed the plate
Chondrocyte viability falls with compressive modulation magnitude

strain_rate_dependence.name: Strain rate dependence
strain_rate_dependence.summary: Growth plate cartilage is strongly viscoelastic and poroelastic, so its mechanical response depends on how fast strain is applied, not only on how much. This is the mechanistic root of the static/dynamic distinction: under stress control, a slowly or indefinitely applied load allows fluid exudation and continued creep, and hypertrophic chondrocytes accumulate lateral and volumetric strain over time, whereas a rapidly cycling load of the same mean magnitude truncates creep and leaves cells with the same axial but lower lateral and volumetric deformation. Digital image correlation in porcine explants likewise shows qualitatively different internal strain fields under static versus dynamic modulation rather than a simple scaling. Because the tissue's apparent modulus rises with loading rate, the stress transmitted to chondrocytes during a fast heel strike is not predictable from the quasi-static modulus, which is one reason in vivo human physeal stress cannot be inferred from joint contact force alone. No experiment has yet varied strain rate as the sole independent variable in an in vivo growth plate and measured growth rate.
strain_rate_dependence.human_evidence_note: No human physeal strain-rate measurement exists.
strain_rate_dependence.translation_risk_reason: Inference rests on explant rheology in two species; the in vivo human loading rate spectrum is unknown.

key_refs.one_line_finding: Time-dependent creep under static stress control is what raises lateral and volumetric chondrocyte strain
Internal strain fields in growth plate cartilage differ qualitatively between static and dynamic modulation

trpv4_channel.name: TRPV4
trpv4_channel.summary: TRPV4 has the strongest human evidence of any candidate physeal mechanotransducer, but that evidence is genetic rather than mechanical. Gain-of-function TRPV4 variants cause a graded series of human skeletal dysplasias - metatropic dysplasia, spondylometaphyseal dysplasia Kozlowski type, brachyolmia - all of which are growth plate diseases with severe short stature and metaphyseal disorganisation, and loss-of-function variants also produce SMD Kozlowski, so the dose-response is non-monotonic. Small-molecule TRPV4 inhibition rescues the skeletal phenotype of Trpv4 mutant mice, establishing that the channel's activity level, not merely its presence, sets growth plate output. The direct mechanotransduction experiments, however, are prenatal or articular: in mechanically stimulated mouse embryonic hindlimb explants TRPV4 localises to regions of high biophysical stimulus and is required for loading-driven cartilage growth and joint morphogenesis via proliferation and matrix synthesis, while the classic osmotic and compressive TRPV4 work is in articular chondrocytes. No study has applied a defined mechanical stimulus to a postnatal growth plate and shown a TRPV4-dependent change in longitudinal growth rate, and TRPV4 has not been localised zonally in human physeal tissue.
trpv4_channel.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is Mendelian: gain- and loss-of-function TRPV4 variants cause metatropic dysplasia and spondylometaphyseal dysplasia Kozlowski, both growth plate disorders, but no human mechanical experiment exists.
trpv4_channel.translation_risk_reason: The human genetic link to growth plate disease is solid; the mechanotransduction step is demonstrated only in mouse embryonic explants and articular chondrocytes.
localization: mouse embryonic hindlimb cartilage, regions of high biophysical stimulus: confirmed (khatib2023)
mouse growth plate (postnatal), zonal: not established mechanically
human growth plate: inferred from dysplasia phenotypes, no zonal localisation study located

key_refs.one_line_finding: Loading-driven cartilage growth and joint morphogenesis in mouse embryonic hindlimb explants require TRPV4 activity
Small-molecule TRPV4 inhibition rescues the skeletal dysplasia phenotype of Trpv4 mutant mice
Documents the clinical spectrum of human TRPV4 metatropic dysplasia
A loss-of-function TRPV4 variant also causes human spondylometaphyseal dysplasia Kozlowski type

wolff_law.name: Wolff's law (as applied to the physis)
wolff_law.summary: Wolff's law is a statement about bone: trabecular architecture and cortical mass adapt to the direction and magnitude of habitual loading. Frost's mechanostat recast it as a set-point controller in which modelling is switched on above roughly 1000-1500 microstrain of peak strain and remodelling removes bone below a lower threshold, so bone responds to peak intermittent strain rather than to mean stress. Frost's chondral modeling theory extended the same logic to cartilage and explicitly predicted the opposite dependence to Hueter-Volkmann: intermittent, dynamic loading drives cartilage growth, while static compression is the suppressive stimulus. The two laws are therefore not variants of each other and are distinguished experimentally by the loading waveform, not the tissue. Where Hueter-Volkmann is measured with mean stress held constant for days, Frost's prediction concerns the peak-to-trough excursion and the number of loading cycles; the static/dynamic experiments in the growth plate are the direct test, and they partly support Frost (dynamic loading preserves growth plate histology at stresses that static loading damages) while partly contradicting him (at matched mean stress, dynamic loading in rat caudal vertebrae suppressed growth just as much as static). Frost's writings are narrative theory, not primary data; the numerical thresholds he quotes are for bone strain, and no equivalent threshold has been measured for physeal cartilage in any species.
wolff_law.human_evidence_note: Human evidence for the bone form of the law is abundant (loading asymmetry in racquet-sport athletes, disuse osteopenia); for the cartilage/physis form there is no human strain-threshold measurement at all.
wolff_law.translation_risk_reason: The bone statement generalises well across species; the cartilage extension is a theoretical proposal by one author and its numerical thresholds have never been measured in physeal cartilage.
localization: bone cortex and trabeculae: the domain of the original law
growth plate cartilage: extension by analogy only (frost1979, frost2001)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Proposed the chondral modeling theory: intermittent rather than static loading governs cartilage growth and modelling
Applies the Utah paradigm to longitudinal growth, treating the physis as a load-bearing organ tuned to peak intermittent strain
Restates Wolff's law as the mechanostat with strain-defined modelling and remodelling thresholds in bone
At matched mean stress, dynamic loading suppressed rat caudal vertebral growth as much as static loading, contradicting a pure Frost prediction
Dynamic compression preserved matrix synthesis and zonal proportions in swine growth plate explants where static compression destroyed them

yap_taz_chondrocyte.name: YAP/TAZ in growth plate chondrocytes
yap_taz_chondrocyte.summary: YAP and TAZ are the canonical stiffness- and tension-responsive transcriptional co-activators, shuttling to the nucleus when cytoskeletal tension is high. In skeletal tissue their best-documented in vivo mechanoregulatory role is not in the chondrocyte: YAP and TAZ in osteoblast precursors couple precursor mobilisation to angiogenesis and mechanoregulation during murine bone development. Within the endochondral lineage, Yap/Taz orchestrate chondrocyte differentiation fate in fibrocartilage, and substrate stiffness modulates hypertrophic chondrocyte reversion in culture, but neither establishes a load-dependent YAP/TAZ function in a growth plate. The one mechanically explicit endochondral result is from distraction osteogenesis, where cyclic distraction-compression promotes bone regeneration through a Piezo1-YAP-beta-catenin axis - a regenerate, not a physis. There is no chondrocyte-specific Yap1/Wwtr1 deletion with a physeal loading challenge and a growth-rate readout, and no human growth plate YAP/TAZ localisation. This node is therefore held at low confidence deliberately: the pathway is highly plausible and widely asserted for the growth plate, and the specific experiment has not been done.
yap_taz_chondrocyte.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate YAP/TAZ data located.
yap_taz_chondrocyte.translation_risk_reason: The growth plate role is extrapolated from osteoblast, fibrocartilage and regenerate biology; the enabling experiment has not been performed in any species.
localization: mouse osteoblast precursors: functional mechanoregulatory evidence
mouse fibrocartilage chondrocytes: differentiation-fate evidence
growth plate zones, any species: no load-dependent localisation located
human growth plate: no data located

key_refs.one_line_finding: Provides the closest growth plate mechanotransduction cascade (PIEZO1-GPX4) into which YAP/TAZ is usually inserted without direct evidence
Shows the pericellular matrix stiffness environment through which YAP/TAZ would be expected to act in the growth plate

adult_height_attainment.name: Adult height attainment
adult_height_attainment.summary:
Adult height is attained when the last contributing growth plate closes, and because fusion is
site-asynchronous the endpoint is a distribution rather than a date. MRI of 958 healthy subjects
bounds it directly: by age 17 in females, 97-98% of ankle plates and 85% of distal femoral
plates but only 75% of distal radial plates were completely fused; by age 19 in males the
distal radius had reached 90% and the other sites 95-98% (kvist2021). Complete fusion of the
last long-bone sites therefore falls around 16-18 years in females and 18-20 years in males,
approximately two years later, with the distal radius consistently last among the sites
examined. Because appendicular fusion precedes vertebral maturation, small further stature
gain continues after the long bones are closed. The estrogen dependence of the endpoint is
demonstrated by its failure: untreated men with aromatase deficiency continue slow linear growth
into their third decade and reach heights of 188-204 cm despite severely impaired GH secretion
and normal or low IGF-I, because delayed bone maturation extends the growth period
(rochira2010, morishima1995, singhania2022). In clinical cohorts, the reference values against
which final height is judged are population- and era-specific: adult height in a German cohort
of untreated constitutional delay was 170.4 cm (SD 5.4) in boys and 157.8 cm (SD 4.2) in girls
(brmswig1990), which is itself lower than contemporary population means because of the secular
trend.
adult_height_attainment.human_evidence_note: Direct imaging of fusion completion in 958 healthy subjects plus measured adult heights in clinical cohorts and in estrogen-deficient men.
adult_height_attainment.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype measured directly in humans.
localization: human distal radius: last of the imaged sites to complete fusion (kvist2021)
human spine: continues to contribute after appendicular fusion

key_refs.one_line_finding: Site-specific completion percentages by age and sex place last-site fusion around 17-19 years with the distal radius latest.
Aromatase-deficient men reach tall stature despite severe GH deficiency because delayed bone maturation prolongs the growth period.
A 188 cm man with two novel CYP19A1 variants had open wrist and knee epiphyses at age 24 and a history of continued growth after 18 years.
Untreated constitutional delay reached adult heights of 170.4 (SD 5.4) cm in boys and 157.8 (SD 4.2) cm in girls.

apoptosis_at_fusion.name: Apoptosis at fusion
apoptosis_at_fusion.summary:
Mechanism 4 of 6, and the only one that has been tested in human fusing tissue and failed.
Claim: the terminal chondrocytes of the growth plate die by classical apoptosis, clearing the
cartilage for bony replacement. Direct human test: growth plate tissues were collected across
pubertal stages including one late-pubertal plate that was about to fuse. In the unfused
plates only a few chondrocytes were TUNEL-positive. In the fusing plate there was not a single
TUNEL-positive cell. Anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL and pro-apoptotic Bax, Bad and cleaved
caspase-3 were detectable in all growth plate zones with no change in intensity across pubertal
progression; in the fusing plate the anti-apoptotic proteins were present but of the
pro-apoptotic proteins only Bad was detected. Electron microscopy found no typical signs of
apoptosis or autophagy in any plate, but did show morphological signs of hypoxia and necrosis
(emons2009, human). The authors concluded that classical apoptosis is not likely to be involved
in human growth plate fusion. This is a negative result on n=1 fusing specimen and has not been
replicated, because no second human fusing plate has been reported. It nonetheless directly
contradicts the apoptosis-centred account that dominates the rodent hypertrophic-chondrocyte
literature, and it is why this node is retained as a competing hypothesis with negative human
evidence rather than as an established process. Discriminating experiment: cleaved-caspase-3
and TUNEL plus RIPK3/MLKL (necroptosis) and LC3/p62 (autophagy) staining on a series of human
physeal specimens obtained at epiphysiodesis and at fusion. Under this hypothesis apoptotic
cells concentrate at the bridging front; under the hypoxia/necrosis alternative necroptotic or
necrotic markers dominate and caspase-3 stays uncleaved.
apoptosis_at_fusion.human_evidence_note: Directly tested in human growth plate tissue including one fusing plate; the human result is negative for classical apoptosis.
apoptosis_at_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The decisive evidence here is human. The limitation is sample size, not species.
localization: human growth plate all zones: Bcl-2, Bcl-XL, Bax, Bad and cleaved caspase-3 present without pubertal change (emons2009)
human fusing plate: no TUNEL-positive cells, only Bad among pro-apoptotic proteins (emons2009)

key_refs.one_line_finding: No TUNEL-positive cells and no ultrastructural apoptosis or autophagy in a human fusing growth plate; hypoxia and necrosis were seen instead.
Estrogen-accelerated loss of rabbit resting zone chondrocytes did not appear to be due to apoptosis.
Lists apoptosis as one of four candidate final steps in fusion, alongside autophagy, transdifferentiation and hypoxia.

automated_bone_age_ai.name: Automated/AI bone age assessment
automated_bone_age_ai.summary:
Automated bone age determination now outperforms human readers on precision, which changes
where the residual error in remaining-growth prediction comes from. BoneXpert reconstructs the
borders of fifteen hand-wrist bones from a radiograph using an active appearance model,
computes intrinsic bone ages for thirteen of them (radius, ulna and eleven short bones), and
transforms these into Greulich-Pyle or Tanner-Whitehouse bone age; it rejects images with
abnormal morphology or poor quality rather than guessing. Developed on 1559 images, it
reproduced the Greulich-Pyle atlas over ages 2-17 with SD 0.42 years (95% CI 0.37-0.47) and
clinical TW ratings on 84 images with SD 0.80 years (95% CI 0.68-0.93). Critically, its
precision - the ability to return the same result on a repeat radiograph - was SD 0.17 years
(95% CI 0.13-0.21), roughly a fifth of the human interobserver spread of 0.74-0.96 years
(thodberg2009; compare king1994). Deep learning has since matched but not clearly beaten this:
in the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge, using 14,236 hand radiographs
(12,611 train, 1,425 validation, 200 test), the best five submissions achieved mean absolute
deviations from the reference standard of 4.2, 4.4, 4.4, 4.5 and 4.5 months (halabi2019). Head
to head in 292 Turkish children, BoneXpert and the deep-learning system VUNO Med-Bone Age were
indistinguishable from each other and from manual reading (ICC 0.994-0.995 in both sexes)
(zmen2025). A systematic review of 26 machine-learning bone age studies found the field almost
entirely confined to hand-wrist radiographs, with samples predominantly from the United States
and Western Europe and few studies exploring ethnic differences (dallora2019).
automated_bone_age_ai.human_evidence_note: Validated on human radiograph collections with human expert reference standards.
automated_bone_age_ai.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical method with no animal analogue.
localization: human left hand and wrist radiograph: 15 bones segmented, 13 scored

key_refs.one_line_finding: BoneXpert reproduces GP bone age with SD 0.42 y and has a repeat-radiograph precision of SD 0.17 y, far tighter than human readers.
Best deep-learning entries in the RSNA challenge achieved mean absolute deviations of 4.2-4.5 months on a 200-image test set.
BoneXpert and VUNO Med-Bone Age agreed with manual GP reading at ICC 0.994-0.995 in 292 Turkish children with no superiority of either.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 machine-learning bone age studies; samples were predominantly US and West European and few explored ethnic differences.

bidirectional_vascular_invasion.name: Bidirectional vascular invasion at fusion
bidirectional_vascular_invasion.summary:
Mechanism 3 of 6. Claim: fusion is executed by blood vessels and their accompanying
osteoprogenitors invading the plate from BOTH sides - epiphyseal and metaphyseal - rather than
by the unidirectional metaphyseal invasion that drives ordinary endochondral growth; where the
two fronts meet, a bony bridge forms and the plate is perforated. The morphological basis is
classical human and canine histology: as union approaches, mineralisation demarcated by tide
lines spreads inward from both plate surfaces, engulfing the cartilage columns; first union is
by that mineralised cartilage, and only afterwards is a restricted region perforated and
replaced by new bone and marrow, the perforation then enlarging until all cartilage is
destroyed (haines1975, human and dog). The molecular link to estrogen is only partly built:
VEGF protein was down-regulated by ovariectomy and restored by estradiol in rat growth plates,
estradiol dose-dependently stimulated VEGF-121 and VEGF-189 (but not VEGF-164) in the rat
chondrocyte line RCJ3.1C5.18, and VEGF mRNA and protein were present in human growth plate
specimens with protein levels rising across pubertal development (emons2010, rat and human).
Nobody has imaged the vasculature of a human growth plate at fusion. Discriminating experiment:
contrast-enhanced or synchrotron phase-contrast 3D vascular imaging of human physeal specimens
or of rabbit plates at defined stages, scoring the direction of vessel ingrowth relative to the
first bridge. Under this hypothesis bridges initiate where epiphyseal and metaphyseal canals
meet and precede chondrocyte loss; under the exhaustion and senescence hypotheses chondrocyte
loss precedes and permits vascular ingrowth; under the apoptosis hypothesis dying chondrocytes
are found ahead of, not behind, the vascular front.
bidirectional_vascular_invasion.human_evidence_note: Human histology shows bidirectional mineralisation and perforation at union (haines1975) and VEGF protein rising through puberty (emons2010), but no human study has visualised vessels crossing the plate at fusion.
bidirectional_vascular_invasion.translation_risk_reason: The morphological claim is human; the mechanistic (VEGF/estrogen) claim is rat and rat cell line with only a human protein-abundance correlate. Rodents do not fuse, so the rat VEGF data cannot address the fusion step itself.
localization: human growth plate: mineralisation front advances from both epiphyseal and metaphyseal surfaces before union (haines1975)
human growth plate: VEGF protein present and increasing with pubertal development (emons2010)
rat growth plate: VEGF protein estrogen-dependent (emons2010)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mineralisation spreads from both plate surfaces before union in human and dog epiphyses; union is completed by perforation and enlargement of the perforation.
Growth plate VEGF is estrogen-regulated in rat and increases at protein level across human pubertal development.
The one human fusing growth plate showed morphological signs of hypoxia and necrosis, consistent with a perfusion change at fusion.

bone_age.name: Bone age
bone_age.summary:
Bone age is the developmental age of the skeleton inferred from the radiographic appearance of
maturity indicators, conventionally in the left hand and wrist. It is the only routinely
available clinical proxy for how much growth plate is left, and it is the variable on which
every remaining-growth prediction is built. Two families of method dominate: atlas matching
(Greulich-Pyle) and bone-by-bone point scoring (Tanner-Whitehouse, of which the RUS subset is
the most used), with Fels, Sanders staging, Risser sign and automated methods filling
specific niches (satoh2015). Bone age is not chronological age with noise: it is systematically
displaced by sex, adiposity and estrogen exposure. Skeletal maturation is faster in girls and
tracks the pubertal estradiol trajectory; obese boys at genital Tanner stage 5 had a mean bone
age around 18 years with fused epiphyses while lean boys at the same stage had a mean bone age
around 16 years with unfused epiphyses (rochira2015). The clean demonstration that bone age is
an estrogen readout rather than a time readout is the aromatase-deficient man whose bone age
was 14 years at a chronological age of 24 years 3 months (morishima1995), and the
ER-alpha-null man whose bone age advanced only from 15 to 17.5 years over 3.5 years of follow
up (smith2008). Bone age is therefore best read as an integrated estrogen-exposure dosimeter
for the skeleton, with a measurement error of roughly plus or minus one year (bone_age_measurement_error).
bone_age.human_evidence_note: Bone age is defined only in humans and measured only in humans; all reference standards are human population data.
bone_age.translation_risk_reason: A human measurement with no animal counterpart; mice have no maturity indicators of this kind because their epiphyses do not complete union.
localization: human left hand and wrist: conventional site for all major methods
human knee, ankle, pelvis: alternative sites (MRI staging, Risser sign)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Surveys Greulich-Pyle, Tanner-Whitehouse, ultrasonographic, MRI and BoneXpert bone age methods and their clinical uses.
Bone age of 14 years at chronological age 24 years 3 months in an untreated aromatase deficient man.
Bone age advanced only 2.5 years over 3.5 years of follow up in a man with homozygous ER-alpha loss of function.
Bone age at the end of male puberty separates by adiposity and by serum estradiol, with fused epiphyses above and unfused below roughly 20 pg/mL.

bone_age_measurement_error.name: Bone age measurement error
bone_age_measurement_error.summary:
The measurement error of manual bone age is close to one year and is large relative to the
clinical decisions it supports. Interobserver: mean spread of results across three readers was
0.96 years for Greulich-Pyle and 0.74 years for Tanner-Whitehouse 2 on the same 50 films, a
difference not significant at the 5% level (king1994). Intra-observer: mean 0.33 years for TW2
but with 95% confidence limits of -0.87 to +1.53 years (king1994); on 362 consecutive clinical
radiographs the 95% limits of agreement were -1.41 to +1.43 years for TW2 and -2.46 to +2.18
years for GP (bull1999). Between-method: the 95% confidence interval for the GP-minus-TW2
difference spanned -1.52 to +2.28 years, so the two methods cannot be interchanged within a
patient's serial record (bull1999). Modern trained-reader studies look better on correlation
metrics without contradicting these limits: ICC exceeded 0.9 for both GP and TW3-RUS across
1725 radiographs and 12 readers, with mean absolute GP-versus-TW3-RUS differences of 2.5-3.3
months in most age bands but larger discrepancies above 180 months of age, i.e. in the fusion
window (tewattanarat2026). Automation collapses the reproducibility component: BoneXpert
returns the same value on a repeat radiograph with SD 0.17 years (95% CI 0.13-0.21), about a
fifth of the human interobserver spread (thodberg2009). What remains uneliminated is the
systematic component - the displacement of the reference standard relative to the population
being measured - which is 2.9 months in one modern US cohort with 95% limits of agreement of
about 2 years (guevel2026) and -2.2 months in an Australian one (paxton2013). No pooled
meta-analytic estimate of manual bone age error with a confidence interval was located in this
sweep (g_l7fuse_008).
bone_age_measurement_error.human_evidence_note: All error estimates come from human reader studies on human radiographs; the numbers are directly measured, not modelled.
localization: SYS: applies to every clinical use of bone age, including growth prediction and forensic age estimation

key_refs.one_line_finding: Interobserver spread 0.96 y (GP) versus 0.74 y (TW2); TW2 intra-observer 0.33 y with 95% limits -0.87 to +1.53 y.
GP and TW2 differ with a 95% CI of -1.52 to +2.28 years and GP has the wider intra-observer limits.
Automated determination reduces the repeat-measurement SD to 0.17 years.
ICC exceeded 0.9 for both GP and TW3-RUS among 12 trained readers, with the largest method disagreement above 180 months of age.
Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement between GP bone age and chronological age were about 2 years in a modern US cohort.

bony_bridge_formation.name: Bony bridge formation
bony_bridge_formation.summary:
A bony bridge is a discrete column of bone crossing the growth plate and mechanically tethering
epiphysis to metaphysis. Bridges are the physical substrate of fusion: in humans, union begins
with mineralised cartilage uniting the two surfaces, then a restricted region is perforated and
replaced by bone and marrow, and the perforation enlarges - one perforation in small,
early-uniting epiphyses, multiple perforations in large, late-uniting ones (haines1975, human
and dog). Bridging can now be quantified non-destructively in three dimensions: synchrotron
X-ray computed microtomography resolves individual bridges and supports micron-scale finite
element modelling of the local stress they generate, and the method transfers to benchtop
micro-CT (staines2018). Bridging is not a human-specific event and is not by itself sufficient
for fusion: wild-type mice carry hundreds of bridges per tibial growth plate (495, SD 45, in
sham-operated wild types) at a bridge density of 1.2 (SD 0.5), while Socs2-/- mice with
de-repressed GH signalling had fewer but far denser bridges (187, SD 56; density 14.4, SD 0.7),
described by the authors as accelerated growth plate fusion (samvelyan2022, mouse) - yet the
mouse plate still persists as calcified cartilage at 55 weeks (yu2025). Pathological bridging
after physeal injury produces the clinical physeal bar, with growth arrest and angular
deformity, and transphyseal vascular communication after Salter-Harris injury is the recognised
risk factor. The unresolved question is whether physiological fusion bridges and traumatic
physeal bars share a cellular origin.
bony_bridge_formation.human_evidence_note: Human bridging and perforation at union are described histologically (haines1975); no quantitative 3D bridge counts have been published for human physes.
bony_bridge_formation.translation_risk_reason: Bridge counting is well developed in mouse, where bridges never complete fusion; the human quantitative equivalent does not exist, so bridge number cannot currently be used as a cross-species surrogate for progress toward fusion.
localization: human plate at union: single or multiple perforations depending on epiphysis size (haines1975)
mouse tibial plate: hundreds of discrete bridges detectable by micro-CT (samvelyan2022)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Union proceeds through mineralised-cartilage bridging then perforation of the plate, with single perforations in small epiphyses and multiple in large ones.
Synchrotron micro-CT resolves individual growth plate bridges in 3D and enables micron-scale finite element modelling of their mechanical effect.
Bridge number and density differ markedly between wild-type and Socs2-/- mouse tibiae, interpreted as accelerated growth plate fusion with de-repressed GH signalling.

comparative_fusion_across_species.name: Comparative epiphyseal fusion across species
comparative_fusion_across_species.summary:
Species sort into three groups by terminal growth plate fate, and the sorting is the single
most load-bearing fact in this atlas. (1) Complete fusion, cartilage destroyed and epiphysis
united with metaphysis: human and dog, described histologically as mineralisation advancing
from both plate surfaces followed by perforation and destruction of residual cartilage
(haines1975); rabbit, in which fusion is observed as an abrupt event with all remaining
chondrocytes rapidly replaced by bone elements (weise2001); goat, in which epiphyseal
synostosis of the autopod is a documented postnatal event (panebianco2026). (2) Growth
cessation without fusion: rat, whose plates persist to 62-80 weeks with a sealed metaphyseal
edge and acellular regions (roach2003); mouse, whose plate persists as calcified cartilage
at 55 weeks with loss of type X collagen and MMP-13 (yu2025) despite forming countable bony
bridges (samvelyan2022). (3) Site- and age-specific persistence in a non-human primate:
unclosed vertebral growth plate cartilage was found in every lumbar endplate of 11 normal
cynomolgus monkeys aged approximately 9-15 years, in explicit contrast with complete
epiphyseal closure in adult humans (iwata2018). The rabbit is therefore the only species in
which the whole causal chain from estrogen exposure to fusion has been demonstrated
experimentally, and it is not a genetically tractable model; the two genetically tractable
models cannot express the endpoint at all.
comparative_fusion_across_species.human_evidence_note: Human union histology is directly described in autopsy/surgical material by haines1975 and in one fusing pubertal plate by emons2009; the comparative claims about other species come from those species' own primaries.
comparative_fusion_across_species.translation_risk_reason: This node is the comparative statement itself; it is the input to translation risk grading elsewhere rather than a claim being transferred.
localization: human: complete union, residual cartilage destroyed (haines1975)
dog: complete union (haines1975)
rabbit: abrupt fusion when proliferation approaches zero (weise2001)
goat autopod: epiphyseal synostosis (panebianco2026)
rat: plate persists, growth ceases (roach2003)
mouse: plate persists as calcified cartilage (yu2025)
cynomolgus monkey lumbar endplate: unclosed at 9-15 y (iwata2018)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Human and dog epiphyseal union described stage by stage; mineralisation spreads from both surfaces, union first by metaplastic bone, then perforation, then loss of all cartilage.
In rabbits, epiphyseal fusion is an abrupt event in which all remaining chondrocytes are rapidly replaced by bone, occurring when proliferation rate approaches zero.
Unclosed vertebral growth plate cartilage in all lumbar endplates of 11 cynomolgus monkeys aged approximately 9-15 years, unlike adult humans.
Characterises postnatal bone development and epiphyseal synostosis in the caprine autopod.
Mouse growth plate remains calcified cartilage at 55 weeks and is not replaced by bone.
Aged rat growth plates persist while longitudinal growth ceases.

ecm_remodeling_at_fusion.name: ECM change at fusion
ecm_remodeling_at_fusion.summary:
Mechanism 5 of 6. Claim: the plate ends because its matrix stops being cartilage - proteoglycan
and collagen II are lost, mineral accumulates, and the residue is either resorbed or converted
to metaplastic bone. The best characterised matrix trajectory is murine and is, importantly,
the opposite of what a matrix-degradation model would predict: in mice the hypertrophic zone
mineral content (Ca, P) rose and the mineralised area expanded between 10 and 55 weeks, while
the degradative and hypertrophic machinery was lost - type X collagen and MMP-13 were present
in the hypertrophic zone at 10 weeks and absent at 55 weeks - and aggrecan and type II collagen
protein became sparse; the plate remained calcified cartilage rather than being replaced by
bone (yu2025, mouse). In humans, the equivalent step is Haines's observation that mineralisation
advances from both surfaces, engulfing intact cartilage columns, and that the first bony union
is by that mineralised cartilage as a form of metaplastic bone (haines1975, human and dog).
There is no human immunohistochemical or biochemical characterisation of matrix composition at
fusion - no collagen typing, no proteoglycan quantification, no MMP or ADAMTS profiling of a
fusing human plate. Discriminating experiment: matrix proteomics plus collagen II/X and
aggrecan-neoepitope immunohistochemistry on graded human physeal specimens. Under this
hypothesis matrix conversion precedes chondrocyte loss and MMP-13 or ADAMTS activity rises at
the bridging front; under the mouse-like pattern the degradative enzymes fall and mineral simply
accumulates, which would predict that human fusion needs an additional, non-matrix trigger.
ecm_remodeling_at_fusion.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is limited to classical histology of mineralisation and metaplastic bone at union (haines1975); no human matrix composition data at fusion exist.
ecm_remodeling_at_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The only quantitative matrix data come from a species that does not complete fusion, and the murine trajectory (loss of MMP-13 and Col X) is not obviously the trajectory of a plate that is about to be replaced by bone.
localization: mouse HZ: mineral-rich bright zone expands with age while Col X and MMP-13 are lost (yu2025)
human plate at union: mineralisation engulfs intact cartilage columns; union first by metaplastic bone (haines1975)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Aged mouse growth plate calcifies while losing type X collagen, MMP-13, aggrecan and type II collagen, and persists as calcified cartilage.
First union of a human epiphysis is by mineralised cartilage, a form of metaplastic bone, with tide lines advancing from both surfaces.
Reviews growth plate maturation including matrix change, and notes that the final steps of fusion remain unestablished.

epigenetic_drift_fusion.name: Epigenetic drift model of fusion
epigenetic_drift_fusion.summary:
Mechanism 6 of 6, and the one with the least evidence in any species and none at all in
humans. Claim: growth plate senescence and hence fusion are driven by progressive, largely
cell-autonomous epigenetic change in chondrocytes - a drift in DNA methylation and chromatin
state accumulated with each replication - which silences the growth-promoting expression
programme. The strongest indirect support is that growth plate senescence is a coordinated
transcriptional programme rather than a passive failure: in rodents, functional, structural and
molecular senescent changes occur earlier in the growth plates of small bones (metacarpals,
phalanges) than of large bones (femur, tibia), with modulation of IGF, BMP and WNT paracrine
pathways, and this differential timing helps set skeletal proportions (lui2018, mouse and rat).
A replication-counting clock is also implied by the rabbit dexamethasone experiment, in which
suppressing proliferation delayed both senescence and fusion (gafni2001, rabbit). Neither
establishes an epigenetic mechanism. A search of Europe PMC for DNA methylation or methylome
studies of human growth plate or physeal cartilage in relation to puberty, bone age or
epiphyseal fusion returned no qualifying primary study (see g_l7fuse_005): the human growth
plate methylome at any age is, as far as this sweep could establish, unpublished.
Discriminating experiment: whole-genome bisulfite or EM-seq of FACS-sorted resting-zone and
proliferative-zone chondrocytes from human physeal specimens spanning Tanner 2 to fusion, with
an epigenetic-clock readout. Under this hypothesis methylation age of resting-zone cells
advances faster than chronological age and faster in early-fusing sites; under the
progenitor-exhaustion hypothesis the surviving cells are epigenetically young but few.
epigenetic_drift_fusion.human_evidence_note: No study has measured DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility or histone modification in human growth plate cartilage as a function of pubertal stage or at fusion; the search establishing this null is logged under g_l7fuse_005.
epigenetic_drift_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The supporting data are rodent transcriptomic and rabbit physiological, from species that either do not fuse or are not genetically tractable, and the epigenetic step itself is inferred rather than measured in any species.
localization: rodent growth plate: senescence programme timing differs between small and large bones (lui2018)
human growth plate: no methylation or chromatin data at any age

key_refs.one_line_finding: Growth plate senescence is a coordinated molecular programme whose timing differs between small and large bones and involves IGF, BMP and WNT pathway modulation.
Delaying chondrocyte proliferation delayed growth plate senescence and epiphyseal fusion in rabbits, consistent with a replication-counted rather than time-counted clock.
Surveys the hypotheses for growth plate maturation and fusion; no epigenetic mechanism is established.

aliases: methylation drift model of growth plate senescence

epiphyseal_fusion.name: Epiphyseal fusion
epiphyseal_fusion.summary:
Epiphyseal fusion is the terminal, irreversible replacement of the cartilaginous growth
plate by bone, after which the epiphysis and metaphysis are in bony continuity and
longitudinal growth at that site is permanently over. The human histological sequence,
described from human and dog material, is: new cartilage is added to the epiphyseal surface
of the plate by chondrification of epiphyseal marrow as union approaches; column architecture
is preserved into early union; mineralisation then spreads inward from BOTH the epiphyseal
and metaphyseal surfaces, demarcated by tide lines, engulfing the cartilage columns; first
union is by this mineralised cartilage, a form of metaplastic bone; a restricted area of the
plate is then perforated and replaced by new bone and marrow, and the perforation enlarges
(single perforation in small, early-uniting epiphyses; multiple perforations in large,
late-uniting ones) until all cartilage is destroyed (haines1975, human and dog). The one
reported human growth plate caught in the act of fusing showed disorganised large chondrocytes
surrounded by a border of dense cortical-like bone, with no TUNEL-positive cells anywhere and
electron-microscopic signs of hypoxia and necrosis rather than apoptosis or autophagy
(emons2009, human, n=1 fusing plate). Fusion is estrogen-dependent in both sexes: it fails in
men with inactivating CYP19A1 or ESR1 mutations and is induced by estradiol replacement in the
CYP19A1 cases (estrogen_driven_fusion). What is not known is which cellular event is the
trigger; six mechanisms are still live and none has been discriminated in human tissue.
epiphyseal_fusion.human_evidence_note: Directly described in human autopsy/surgical material (haines1975) and in one human fusing growth plate with immunohistochemistry and electron microscopy (emons2009); radiographic and MRI timing data exist in cohorts of hundreds (kvist2021).
epiphyseal_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The endpoint as defined here is a human (and rabbit, dog, goat) phenotype; the risk attaches to mechanism nodes, not to the existence of the process.
localization: human growth plate: mineralisation advances from both epiphyseal and metaphyseal surfaces before union (haines1975)
human fusing plate: disorganised large chondrocytes bounded by dense cortical-like bone (emons2009)
human late-uniting epiphyses: multiple perforations, remnants persist as physeal scar (haines1975)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Stage-by-stage histology of human and dog epiphyseal union: bidirectional mineralisation, metaplastic-bone union, perforation, then destruction of all residual cartilage.
A single human fusing growth plate contained no TUNEL-positive cells and showed hypoxia and necrosis but no apoptosis or autophagy on electron microscopy.
Sets out four candidate final steps in fusion - apoptosis, autophagy, transdifferentiation and hypoxia - none of which is established.
MRI staging of wrist, knee and ankle in 958 healthy 14-21.5 year olds gives site-specific completion percentages and an ascending foot-to-wrist order.

estradiol_threshold_fusion.name: Serum estradiol threshold for epiphyseal closure
estradiol_threshold_fusion.summary:
Fusion in humans appears to be threshold-gated rather than dose-graded. The observation comes
from an accidental human dose-response: a 26-year-old man with compound heterozygous CYP19A1
mutations (23 bp deletion in exon IV and a point mutation at the first nucleotide of intron
IX) was followed for five years on transdermal estradiol with poor compliance, so serum
estradiol remained low but detectable for long periods. During that time neither bone age nor
the radiographic appearance of the growth plate changed. Closure of the epiphyseal cartilage,
normalisation of BMD and of bone turnover markers, and improvement in fasting insulin were all
achieved only once serum estradiol rose above 73 pmol/L (approximately 20 pg/mL) on the correct
transdermal dose (lanfranco2008, human, n=1). The same threshold shows up in an independent
and non-pathological setting: at genital Tanner stage 5, obese boys with median serum estradiol
34.8 pg/mL (range 25.6-41.1) had a mean bone age of about 18 years consistent with fused
epiphyses, while lean boys with median estradiol 15.7 pg/mL (range 13.2-21.0) had a mean bone
age of about 16 years with epiphyses still unfused (as summarised in rochira2015). The threshold
is clinically important because it defines the estradiol exposure that a growth-sparing therapy
must stay below, and because it is the only quantitative human dose parameter in this layer.
It rests on one case and one cross-sectional comparison, and it has never been estimated with a
confidence interval.
estradiol_threshold_fusion.human_evidence_note: Within-subject longitudinal human data from an aromatase-deficient man on variable estradiol replacement, supported by a cross-sectional obese-versus-lean comparison at Tanner G5.
estradiol_threshold_fusion.translation_risk_reason: Human-only data. The risk is n=1 for the interventional element and the assay dependence of low estradiol measurements, which differ substantially between immunoassay and LC-MS/MS.
localization: SYS: circulating estradiol; the effective concentration at the growth plate has never been measured in humans

key_refs.one_line_finding: Epiphyseal closure, BMD normalisation and turnover-marker normalisation occurred only when serum estradiol exceeded 73 pmol/L in an aromatase-deficient man on transdermal estradiol.
Argues from human models that a serum estradiol threshold of roughly 20 pg/mL separates unfused from fused epiphyses at the end of male puberty.
A 25-year-old man with two novel compound heterozygous CYP19A1 mutations had undetectable serum estradiol with continuing linear growth and eunuchoid habitus.

estrogen_accelerated_senescence.name: Estrogen acceleration of growth plate senescence
estrogen_accelerated_senescence.summary:
Mechanism 1 of 6. Claim: estrogen does not ossify the growth plate directly; it accelerates a
pre-existing developmental programme of growth plate senescence, so the plate reaches its
intrinsic terminus earlier. Evidence: in juvenile ovariectomised rabbits given 70 ug/kg
estradiol cypionate i.m. weekly and examined at 2, 4, 6 and 8 weeks, vehicle-treated animals
showed a gradual senescent decline in tibial growth rate, chondrocyte proliferation rate,
growth plate height, proliferative and hypertrophic cell number, terminal hypertrophic cell
size and column density; estradiol accelerated the decline in every one of these parameters,
and fusion occurred earlier and only once proliferation rate approached zero (weise2001,
rabbit). The reciprocal experiment supports a proliferation-counting clock rather than a
chronological one: dexamethasone-induced growth suppression in rabbits delayed the senescent
decline in growth rate and in proliferative, hypertrophic and total plate heights, and also
delayed epiphyseal fusion, after which catch-up growth occurred (gafni2001, rabbit).
Human evidence: none direct. The only human-side support is indirect and endocrine - fusion
fails without estrogen (estrogen_driven_fusion) - which is equally compatible with every other
mechanism in this list. Discriminating experiment: in a fusing species, block proliferation
pharmacologically without estrogen and ask whether fusion still occurs on schedule. Under this
hypothesis fusion follows proliferative exhaustion regardless of estrogen status; under the
direct-ossification alternative estrogen is required even when proliferation is already zero.
estrogen_accelerated_senescence.human_evidence_note: No human growth plate has been examined for accelerated senescence under estrogen; the human link is the clinical observation that estrogen deficiency prevents fusion and estrogen replacement produces it.
estrogen_accelerated_senescence.translation_risk_reason: The rabbit does express the fusion endpoint, so this is the strongest available non-human evidence; but rabbit estrogen pharmacology, growth plate geometry and pubertal timing are not validated against human, and no human tissue replication exists.
localization: rabbit RZ/PZ/HZ: senescent decline in all zonal parameters, accelerated by estradiol (weise2001)
human growth plate: not examined

key_refs.one_line_finding: Estradiol accelerated the senescent decline in every structural and functional growth plate parameter in ovariectomised rabbits and brought fusion forward; fusion occurred when proliferation approached zero.
Dexamethasone-induced growth suppression in rabbits delayed growth plate senescence and delayed epiphyseal fusion, supporting a replication-count clock.
Senescent functional, structural and molecular changes occur earlier in growth plates of small bones than of large bones, and this differential aging shapes skeletal proportions.

estrogen_driven_fusion.name: Estrogen-driven fusion
estrogen_driven_fusion.summary:
That estrogen, not androgen, terminates the human growth plate is the only fusion mechanism
with direct human interventional evidence, and it rests on a handful of individuals. A
28-year-old man homozygous for a C-to-T transition at codon 157 of ESR1 (premature stop in
exon 2) was 204 cm tall, had incomplete epiphyseal closure and a history of continued linear
growth into adulthood despite normal pubertal development, with elevated serum estradiol and
estrone, normal testosterone, raised FSH and LH, and lumbar spine BMD 0.745 g/cm2 (3.1 SD
below age-matched normal women); six months of transdermal estrogen producing a 10-fold rise
in free estradiol had no detectable effect (smith1994, human, n=1). On longitudinal follow-up
his bone age advanced only from 15 to 17.5 years over 3.5 years while spine aBMD fell to
0.684 g/cm2 (Z -3.85) (smith2008, human, n=1). The mirror-image experiment is aromatase
deficiency, where the receptor is intact and the ligand absent: a 24 3/12-year-old man with a
novel CYP19A1 mutation was 204 cm (+3.7 SD) with eunuchoid proportions, testosterone 2015
ng/dL, estradiol and estrone below 7 pg/mL, and a bone age of 14 years at a chronological age
of 24.25 years (morishima1995, human, n=1 male sib; his 46,XX sister reached 177.6 cm, +2.5
SD). In these patients estradiol replacement closes the plates: transdermal estradiol produced
complete epiphyseal closure, final skeletal maturation and arrest of growth in height
(carani1997), whereas six months of high-dose testosterone given before diagnosis to the same
patient had no effect on bone age. The dissociation - receptor-defective man does not respond
to estrogen, ligand-deficient man does - is what makes the inference causal rather than
correlative, and it is the strongest single argument in this atlas that a rodent-derived
mechanism can be human-relevant. The denominator is small and must not be inflated: 15
CYP19A1 mutation reports in males had been published by 2022 (singhania2022), and homozygous
ESR1 loss of function is known in one man with adult data (smith1994), one woman (quaynor2013),
and one consanguineous Algerian family of two sisters and one brother carrying R394H, all still
prepubertal with delayed bone maturation at report (bernard2017). Estradiol replacement in
aromatase deficiency also raises bone mass (bilezikian1998).
estrogen_driven_fusion.human_evidence_note: Two complementary human loss-of-function experiments of nature with interventional follow-up: ESR1 nonsense mutation (estrogen-unresponsive, plates stay open) and CYP19A1 mutations (estrogen-deficient, plates close on estradiol replacement).
estrogen_driven_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The evidence is human genetic and human interventional. The residual risk is not species but sample size and publication bias: single cases, no untreated control course, and treatment responses reported without blinding.
localization: SYS: circulating estradiol acting on ER-alpha; no human growth plate ER-alpha localisation at fusion has been reported

key_refs.one_line_finding: A 204 cm man homozygous for an ESR1 codon 157 stop mutation had incomplete epiphyseal closure and no response to six months of transdermal estrogen.
Longitudinal follow-up of the same propositus: bone age advanced 15 to 17.5 y over 3.5 y and spine aBMD fell to Z -3.85; heterozygous carriers had normal spine aBMD.
CYP19A1 mutation in a brother-sister pair; the man was 204 cm with a bone age of 14 years at chronological age 24.25 years and osteoporosis.
Showed that transdermal estradiol, but not testosterone, produced epiphyseal closure and growth arrest in a man with aromatase deficiency.
A 188 cm 24-year-old man with two novel CYP19A1 variants and open epiphyses; tabulates 15 published male aromatase deficiency reports.
All reported men with aromatase deficiency present with tall stature, delayed bone maturation, unfused epiphyses, osteopenia or osteoporosis and eunuchoid proportions.
An 18-year-old woman homozygous for an ESR1 loss-of-function variant had no breast development, markedly elevated estrogens and bilateral multicystic ovaries.
Two sisters and one brother homozygous for ESR1 R394H failed to enter puberty and had delayed bone maturation, with plasma estradiol above 50-fold the normal range.
Reported increased bone mass following estrogen therapy in a man with aromatase deficiency.

fels_method.name: Fels method
fels_method.summary:
The Fels method assesses skeletal maturity from graded indicators and ratios of hand-wrist
bones and, unlike Greulich-Pyle and Tanner-Whitehouse, returns a standard error alongside each
skeletal age estimate - the only widely used manual method that quantifies its own uncertainty
per case. It was developed on the Fels Longitudinal Study, a serially radiographed cohort of
residents of southwest Ohio, and the same cohort underpins the Roche-Wainer-Thissen and
Khamis-Roche adult stature prediction models (khamis1994). Its practical footprint has always
been small: a 1996 methodological survey judged Greulich-Pyle assessments often very
inaccurate, TW2 the method of choice at the time, and experience with Fels still very limited.
In this sweep no primary study reporting Fels inter-rater or intra-rater error in years with a
confidence interval was located, and the per-case standard error remains the method's
advertised rather than independently validated property; this is logged as part of the
quantitative gap on bone age error (g_l7fuse_008). Fels remains important chiefly because it is
the maturity scale on which the best-characterised adult height prediction equations were
calibrated, and because the Khamis-Roche variant of those equations - which omits skeletal age
entirely - provides the sharpest available test of how much bone age actually contributes to
remaining-growth prediction (remaining_growth_prediction).
fels_method.human_evidence_note: Built and validated on a human longitudinal radiographic cohort.
fels_method.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical method with no animal analogue.
localization: human left hand and wrist: graded maturity indicators plus bone-ratio measurements

key_refs.one_line_finding: Built on the Fels Longitudinal Study, a stature prediction model omitting skeletal age had errors only slightly larger than the Roche-Wainer-Thissen model that uses it.
The RWT method predicts adult stature from recumbent length, weight, midparent stature and hand-wrist skeletal age, with smaller errors than Bayley-Pinneau.
Reviews bone age methods and their clinical applications, including the position of Fels relative to GP and TW.

fusion_timing_order.name: Site-by-site fusion order
fusion_timing_order.summary:
Human epiphyses do not close together; they close in a reproducible ascending order. MRI of
wrist, knee and ankle in 958 healthy subjects aged 14.0-21.5 years established that fusion
proceeds from the foot upward to the wrist, with the calcaneus and distal tibia closing before
the femur and the radius last (kvist2021, human). The site-specific completion percentages at
fixed ages quantify the spread: in 17-year-old females complete fusion was present in 75%
(radius), 85% (femur), 97% (proximal tibia), 98% (distal tibia) and 98% (calcaneus); in
19-year-old males the corresponding figures were 90%, 97%, 95%, 97% and 98% (kvist2021).
Skeletal-collection data extend the sequence to the whole skeleton: in 258 Bosniak males aged
14-30 years the fusion status of 21 epiphyses was compared pairwise to derive separate
sequences for beginning and for complete union, and although substantial variation existed in
the order of both initiation and completion, most pairwise relationships showed no variant
ordering at all (schaefer2007, human). The sacrum runs on its own schedule: partial union of
primary ossification centres occurs from 1 to 8 years and of secondary centres from 15 to 21
years, with the S5 neural arch-centrum junction first and the S1 costal element-centrum
junction last (cardoso2014, human). The invariant pairwise relationships are the forensically
useful ones and are also the ones that constrain any mechanistic model: whatever ends the plate
must be tunable per site, since different plates in the same individual, in the same endocrine
environment, close years apart.
fusion_timing_order.human_evidence_note: Direct human imaging (n=958) and direct human skeletal observation (n=258 and n=191) with published stage-by-age distributions.
fusion_timing_order.translation_risk_reason: A human phenotype measured directly in humans.
localization: human: ascending order calcaneus and distal tibia, then knee, then distal radius (kvist2021)
human sacrum: S5 neural arch-centrum first, S1 costal element-centrum last (cardoso2014)

key_refs.one_line_finding: MRI in 958 healthy 14-21.5 year olds shows fusion in an ascending foot-to-wrist order with site-specific completion percentages by age and sex.
Pairwise sequencing of 21 epiphyses in 258 Bosniak males yields separate beginning-union and complete-union orders, with most pairwise relationships invariant.
Sacral primary centres fuse between 1 and 8 years and secondary centres between 15 and 21 years in a documented Portuguese collection.

greulich_pyle_method.name: Greulich-Pyle atlas method
greulich_pyle_method.summary:
Greulich-Pyle assigns bone age by matching a left hand-wrist radiograph to the closest
standard plate in a printed atlas. What it measures is therefore a global gestalt of hand and
wrist maturity, not a per-bone score. Its reference population is narrow and historical: the
standards derive from healthy Caucasian children of high socioeconomic status in Cleveland,
Ohio, radiographed in the 1920s to 1940s (guevel2026); the discrete atlas intervals mean the
method cannot resolve maturity differences finer than the gap between adjacent plates. Speed is
its advantage - 1.4 minutes per assessment versus 7.9 minutes for TW2 in a head-to-head audit
(king1994). Reproducibility is comparable to or slightly worse than point scoring: mean spread
of results across three registrars was 0.96 years for GP versus 0.74 years for TW2, a
difference not significant at the 5% level (king1994); intra-observer 95% limits of agreement
were -2.46 to +2.18 years for GP versus -1.41 to +1.43 years for TW2 (bull1999). GP and TW2 do
not give equivalent estimates - the 95% confidence interval for their difference spanned -1.52
to +2.28 years - so the two must not be mixed in serial follow-up of one patient (bull1999).
Applied to modern populations, GP performs better than its provenance suggests but with wide
limits: in 472 modern US paediatric patients bone age exceeded chronological age by 2.9 months
(SD 12.8) with no systematic bias across race, ethnicity or deprivation, but with 95% limits of
agreement of about 2 years (guevel2026); in 406 Australian children bone age was 2.2 months
below chronological age (paxton2013).
greulich_pyle_method.human_evidence_note: Method built on, and validated in, human radiographic cohorts only.
greulich_pyle_method.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical method with no animal analogue.
localization: human left hand and wrist: 28 hand-wrist bones assessed as a whole-image match

key_refs.one_line_finding: GP interobserver spread 0.96 years versus TW2 0.74 years, with GP more than five times faster (1.4 versus 7.9 minutes).
GP and TW2 are not equivalent (95% CI of difference -1.52 to +2.28 y) and GP has wider intra-observer limits (-2.46 to +2.18 y).
In modern diverse US patients GP shows a 2.9-month systematic bias and about 2-year limits of agreement, with no differences by race, ethnicity or deprivation.
GP bone age was 2.2 months below chronological age in 406 Australian children, with no significant intra- or inter-observer difference.

growth_cessation.name: Growth cessation
growth_cessation.summary:
Growth cessation and epiphyseal fusion are related but not identical, and conflating them is a
recurring error. In humans they are effectively simultaneous: fusion destroys the plate, so
growth at that site is over. In the rat they are dissociated: longitudinal growth ceases while
a histologically recognisable plate persists, sealed at the metaphyseal edge by a bone band,
with acellular regions and sporadic residual chondrocyte proliferation that cannot produce net
elongation (roach2003, rat). In the rabbit, cessation and fusion are coupled as in humans, and
fusion occurs precisely when the chondrocyte proliferation rate approaches zero (weise2001,
rabbit). This dissociation defines the correct endpoint hierarchy for the atlas: an intervention
that changes growth rate has not been shown to change fusion, and an intervention that changes
plate height has been shown to change neither. In humans, cessation is site-asynchronous - the
foot fuses before the knee, the knee before the wrist (kvist2021) - so whole-body stature stops
increasing only when the last major contributing plate closes, and the residual vertebral
contribution continues after long-bone fusion. Cessation is estrogen-gated: aromatase-deficient
men continue to grow slowly into adulthood despite severe GH deficiency, and stop when
estradiol replacement is adequate (rochira2010, lanfranco2008).
growth_cessation.human_evidence_note: Human cessation timing is measured directly by serial imaging of fusion status in cohorts of hundreds (kvist2021) and by the continued growth of estrogen-deficient men until replacement.
growth_cessation.translation_risk_reason: The human process is well described phenomenologically; the mechanistic account depends on rabbit and rat data in which cessation and fusion are coupled differently.
localization: human: site-asynchronous, ascending foot to wrist (kvist2021)
rat: cessation without plate destruction (roach2003)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Rats cease longitudinal growth while retaining a histologically present growth plate.
In rabbits, fusion occurs when the chondrocyte proliferation rate approaches zero, coupling cessation to fusion.
Human growth plate fusion is site-asynchronous and occurs in an ascending order from foot to wrist.
Four aromatase-deficient men reached tall stature despite severely impaired GH secretion, because delayed bone maturation prolonged the growth period.

hypoxia_necrosis_at_fusion.name: Hypoxia and necrosis at fusion
hypoxia_necrosis_at_fusion.summary:
Mechanism 4b of 6, promoted from footnote status because it is what the single human fusing
specimen actually showed. Claim: terminal growth plate chondrocytes are removed by hypoxic,
non-apoptotic death as the plate is sealed off by the dense cortical-like bone that surrounds
it, rather than by a programmed cell-autonomous death pathway. Evidence: electron microscopy
of human growth plates across pubertal stages, including the fusing plate, found no typical
signs of apoptosis or autophagy but did find morphological signs of hypoxia and necrosis; the
fusing plate itself consisted of disorganised large chondrocytes surrounded by a border of
dense, cortical-like bone (emons2009, human, n=1 fusing plate). The rat terminal picture is
compatible: aged rat plates develop a bone band that seals the metaphyseal edge and extensive
acellular areas resistant to resorption (roach2003, rat). Hypoxia is listed as one of the four
candidate final steps in the standard review of the field (emons2011_2). What is missing is any
molecular corroboration in human tissue - no HIF1A, no lactate, no necroptosis marker has been
measured in a fusing human plate. Discriminating experiment: HIF1A stabilisation, pimonidazole
adduct or equivalent hypoxia readout plus RIPK3/MLKL staining on human physeal specimens at
successive MRI-defined fusion stages. Under this hypothesis hypoxia markers rise before
chondrocyte loss and track the encircling bone border; under the vascular-invasion hypothesis
the plate becomes better, not worse, perfused as bridges form.
hypoxia_necrosis_at_fusion.human_evidence_note: Ultrastructural observation in human tissue including one fusing plate; entirely descriptive, with no molecular hypoxia readout.
hypoxia_necrosis_at_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The observation is human; the limitation is that it is one specimen and purely morphological.
localization: human fusing plate: disorganised large chondrocytes bounded by dense cortical-like bone, with hypoxic/necrotic ultrastructure (emons2009)
rat aged plate: metaphyseal edge sealed by a bone band, acellular regions (roach2003)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Human growth plates including the fusing plate showed morphological signs of hypoxia and necrosis on electron microscopy, and none of apoptosis or autophagy.
Aged rat growth plates are sealed at the metaphyseal edge by a bone band and contain extensive acellular regions resistant to resorption.
Lists hypoxia among the four candidate final steps in epiphyseal fusion.

menarche_growth_remaining.name: Menarche and remaining growth
menarche_growth_remaining.summary:
The clinical rule of thumb that a girl grows about 5-7 cm after menarche is both approximately
right on average and dangerously wrong as a prediction for an individual. In 793 healthy
term-born Swedish girls from the GrowUp 1990 Gothenburg cohort, mean age at menarche was 13.0
years (SD 1.3, range 8.2-17.2) and postmenarcheal growth averaged 8.0 cm (SD 4.9) - but ranged
from 0.2 cm to 31.1 cm, and decreased with later menarche (grdstedtbergho2024). A standard
deviation of 4.9 cm on a mean of 8.0 cm means the between-individual variance is comparable in
magnitude to the quantity being predicted; the tail extends to more than 30 cm of remaining
growth in the earliest-maturing girls. Menarche occurred at 71.6% (SD 18.8) of the specific
pubertal growth function in the QEPS model, so menarche is a fixed fraction of the spurt on
average but with a wide individual spread. Data available at the start of puberty explained
44% of the variance in menarcheal age, on average 3.2 years before it occurred
(grdstedtbergho2024). Postmenarcheal growth decreased with later menarche in the same
cohort, so the same chronological menarcheal age carries different residual growth depending on
how far skeletal maturation has already advanced (grdstedtbergho2024). For prediction, menarcheal status is worth including: Tanner-Whitehouse Mark I intervals narrow
from plus or minus 5-6 cm premenarcheal to plus or minus 3-4 cm postmenarcheal at the same ages
(tanner1975).
menarche_growth_remaining.human_evidence_note: Longitudinal community-based measurement in 793 girls with model-derived and observed postmenarcheal increments.
menarche_growth_remaining.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype measured directly; menarche has no growth plate analogue in mice.
localization: SYS: whole-body stature; the residual contribution after menarche is dominated by spine and remaining open long-bone plates

key_refs.one_line_finding: Postmenarcheal growth averaged 8.0 cm (SD 4.9) but ranged from 0.2 to 31.1 cm in 793 healthy Swedish girls, decreasing with later menarche.
Adult height prediction is substantially more accurate in postmenarcheal than premenarcheal girls at the same chronological age.
Menarche is one of six pubertal markers whose ages at peak velocity correlate 0.8-0.92 in girls, indicating a coherent tempo trait.

mouse_does_not_fuse.name: Mice do not undergo epiphyseal fusion
mouse_does_not_fuse.summary:
The mouse growth plate is never replaced by bone. In mice examined by SEM/energy-dispersive
X-ray spectroscopy and immunohistochemistry, the growth plate at 55 weeks of age was still a
discrete cartilaginous band: mineral (Ca, P) content of the hypertrophic zone had risen and
the mineralised area had expanded relative to 10 weeks, but the plate remained calcified
cartilage rather than bone, and aggrecan glycosaminoglycan was still detectable across it
(yu2025, mouse). The differentiation machinery required to complete endochondral replacement
was switched off rather than up: type X collagen and MMP-13 were present in the hypertrophic
zone at 10 weeks but absent at 55 weeks, and type II collagen and aggrecan protein were only
sparsely detectable at 55 weeks (yu2025, mouse). This is not "nothing happens": mice do form
discrete transphyseal bony bridges countable by micro-CT, and their number and density are
genotype-sensitive (wild-type sham tibiae 495 bridges at density 1.2; Socs2-/- 187 bridges at
density 14.4) (samvelyan2022, mouse). Murine bridging is therefore a real, quantifiable,
partial process that never proceeds to the complete cartilage-to-bone replacement and loss of
a continuous cartilaginous plate that defines human epiphyseal fusion; a 2026 human growth
plate study states the contrast directly (chu2026). The consequence is structural: no murine
experiment can report the endpoint "epiphyseal fusion", so every murine claim about fusion
mechanism is an inference from a surrogate (plate height, bridge count, proliferation rate),
and the surrogate-to-endpoint step has never been validated in any species.
mouse_does_not_fuse.human_evidence_note: This node is a statement about mice. The human side of the contrast rests on human histology showing complete cartilage-to-bone replacement (haines1975) and on direct assertion within a human growth plate study (chu2026); no study has processed human and mouse fusing plates in the same assay.
mouse_does_not_fuse.translation_risk_reason: Reverse-direction risk: this node is what makes every murine node in the atlas high-risk. Because the mouse cannot express the endpoint, murine mechanism data can only be transferred to humans by assuming that the sub-fusion processes mice do show (plate thinning, bridging, senescent decline) are the processes that terminate the human plate. That assumption is untested.
localization: mouse growth plate: persists as calcified cartilage to at least 55 weeks (yu2025)
mouse HZ: type X collagen and MMP-13 lost by 55 weeks (yu2025)
mouse growth plate: discrete transphyseal bony bridges quantifiable by micro-CT (staines2018, samvelyan2022)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mouse growth plate calcifies with age but remains calcified cartilage at 55 weeks, losing type X collagen and MMP-13, and is never replaced by bone.
Micro-CT quantification of growth plate bony bridges in wild-type and Socs2-/- mouse tibiae; bridge density differs ~12-fold by genotype.
Synchrotron X-ray microtomography method for non-destructive 3D quantification of growth plate bone bridging with micron-scale finite element modelling.
States as premise of a human growth plate single-cell study that the plate closes after puberty in humans but remains open throughout life in mice.

aliases: absence of physeal closure in Mus musculus

mri_physeal_closure_staging.name: MRI staging of physeal closure
mri_physeal_closure_staging.summary:
MRI grades the growth plate itself rather than inferring maturity from surrounding bone shape,
and it does so without ionising radiation, which is what makes it usable in healthy volunteer
cohorts. A prospective cross-sectional study imaged the wrist, knee and ankle of 958 healthy
subjects aged 14.0-21.5 years, graded each plate on an ordinal fusion scale by two radiologists,
and reported inter-observer kappa of 0.87-0.94 (kvist2021). Sequence choice matters more than
reader seniority for the knee: in 395 subjects, cartilage-weighted sequences gave inter- and
intra-observer agreement of 93% (kappa 0.86) and 89% (kappa 0.79) for the femur and 95% (kappa
0.90) and 91% (kappa 0.81) for the tibia, against T1-weighted agreement of 82% (kappa 0.73) and
77% (kappa 0.65) for the femur and 90% (kappa 0.82) and 87% (kappa 0.75) for the tibia among
paediatric radiologists; general radiologists reading T1-weighted images fell to 69% (kappa
0.56) for the femur and 56% (kappa 0.34) for the tibia (kvist2020). The practical implications
are that MRI physeal staging is at least as reproducible as hand radiograph bone age, that
cartilage sequences should be specified, and that paediatric radiology experience is required.
It is the only method in this layer that observes the fusion process directly rather than a
correlate of it, and it is therefore the natural stratifier for any future study that seeks
human physeal tissue at defined fusion stages.
mri_physeal_closure_staging.human_evidence_note: Prospective human volunteer cohorts of 395 and 958 subjects with published reader agreement.
mri_physeal_closure_staging.translation_risk_reason: Human imaging method applied to the human endpoint directly.
localization: human distal femur, proximal and distal tibia, calcaneus, distal radius: ordinal fusion staging

key_refs.one_line_finding: MRI fusion staging of wrist, knee and ankle in 958 healthy subjects with inter-observer kappa 0.87-0.94, establishing site-specific and sex-specific fusion timing.
Cartilage-weighted sequences give higher reader agreement than T1-weighted for knee growth plate staging, and paediatric radiology experience substantially improves agreement.

peak_height_velocity.name: Peak height velocity
peak_height_velocity.summary:
Peak height velocity is the maximum rate of statural growth during the pubertal spurt, and its
timing (age at PHV) is the standard objective marker of pubertal tempo because it needs no
physical examination or self-report. Modelled with SITAR and a matched mixed-effects model for
Tanner stages in the Edinburgh Longitudinal Growth Study (103 boys, 74 girls), mean age at peak
velocity across six pubertal markers was 13.0-14.0 years in boys and 12.0-13.1 years in girls,
with a between-subject standard deviation of about 1 year; peak height velocity itself was 8-9
cm/year in both sexes (cole2014). The correlation of age at peak velocity across different
pubertal markers was 0.6-0.8 in boys and 0.8-0.92 in girls, significantly higher in girls
(p=0.005), whereas the correlations for peak velocity magnitude were much lower (-0.2 to 0.6) -
i.e. pubertal timing is a coherent individual trait but pubertal intensity is not (cole2014).
In a Chilean cohort of 549 girls followed twice yearly from age 6, mean age at PHV was 10.6
years (SD 1.1) with a peak velocity of 8 cm/year, considerably earlier than the Edinburgh
figures, which places population and secular differences on the same order as the
between-individual SD. SITAR-derived age at PHV is now the standard exposure variable in
large birth cohorts (frysz2018). PHV precedes fusion by roughly 3-6 years and is the last
point at which growth-modifying intervention has substantial leverage.
peak_height_velocity.human_evidence_note: Derived from serial human anthropometry in longitudinal cohorts.
localization: SYS: whole-body stature velocity, integrating all open growth plates

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mean age at peak velocity was 13.0-14.0 y in boys and 12.0-13.1 y in girls with between-subject SD about 1 year and peak height velocity 8-9 cm/year.
Describes SITAR-based derivation of age at peak height velocity as an objective pubertal timing measure in the ALSPAC birth cohort.

physeal_scar.name: Physeal scar
physeal_scar.summary:
The physeal scar is the transverse radiodense line that remains at the site of a fused growth
plate. Its histological origin is specified in the classical description of human union: in the
smaller, earlier-uniting epiphyses the mineralised cartilage and the lamellar bone sheets
covering it are removed in one restricted area and replaced by new bone and marrow, the
perforation enlarges until all cartilage is destroyed, and union leaves no scar; in the larger,
later-uniting epiphyses there are multiple perforations and remnants of epiphyseal bone often
persist as an epiphyseal scar (haines1975, human and dog). In both types, peripheral remnants
of the plate may persist for a time with cartilage columns set at right angles to the long axis
of the bone, an orientation Haines flagged as unexplained; at full union all such residual
