cartilage is destroyed. The practical importance is that the scar is a permanent radiographic
record of the fusion event and is the anatomical basis for judging complete fusion on plain
film and MRI; its persistence explains why late-uniting sites (distal femur, proximal tibia)
retain a visible line into adulthood while early-uniting small bones do not.
physeal_scar.human_evidence_note: Described directly in human epiphyses at successive stages of union; also visible in the MRI fusion staging used in living cohorts (kvist2021, kvist2020).
physeal_scar.translation_risk_reason: A human anatomical structure; the mouse has no equivalent because the plate is never destroyed.
localization: human large late-uniting epiphyses: epiphyseal scar persists (haines1975)
human small early-uniting epiphyses: union leaves no scar (haines1975)
human plate periphery: residual cartilage columns transverse to the long axis, destroyed at full union (haines1975)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Remnants of epiphyseal bone persist as an epiphyseal scar in large, late-uniting epiphyses but not in small early-uniting ones.
MRI staging of knee growth plate closure is more reliable on cartilage-weighted than on T1-weighted sequences, which is how residual physeal signal is graded.

population_variation_fusion.name: Population variation in fusion timing
population_variation_fusion.summary:
Fusion timing varies substantially between populations while the fusion order appears largely
conserved, and the two facts have different consequences. Timing: of ten epiphyses compared
between young Bosnian males and the McKern and Stewart North American Korean War sample, every
element was at least two years advanced in the Bosnian material; standards built on the
American sample therefore produce upper age limits two or more years older than the true
chronological age when applied in the Balkans (schaefer2005, human). Bone age standards inherit
the same problem in reverse: the Greulich-Pyle atlas was built on healthy Caucasian children of
high socioeconomic status in Cleveland, Ohio in the 1920s to 1940s, and its applicability to
modern diverse populations is an empirical question rather than an assumption (guevel2026). The
empirical answer is mixed rather than catastrophic - in 472 modern US paediatric patients,
Greulich-Pyle bone age exceeded chronological age by only 2.9 months (SD 12.8) with no
systematic bias across race, ethnicity or area deprivation index, but with 95% limits of
agreement of about 2 years and a 15.9-month underestimate in underweight patients
(guevel2026); in 406 Australian children mean bone age was 2.2 months below chronological age
overall, and 3.7 months below in girls (paxton2013). Order: no study located in this sweep has
formally compared the sequence of epiphyseal union between populations, so the widespread
assumption that fusion order is conserved is an untested extrapolation from single-population
sequences (g_l7fuse_010).
population_variation_fusion.human_evidence_note: Direct cross-population comparisons of epiphyseal union ages and of bone age versus chronological age in three separate national cohorts.
population_variation_fusion.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype measured directly in humans.
localization: SYS: applies to all radiographic and skeletal age standards used across populations

key_refs.one_line_finding: All ten epiphyses examined united at least two years earlier in young Bosnian males than in the North American reference sample.
In a modern diverse US cohort the Greulich-Pyle atlas showed no systematic bias by race, ethnicity or deprivation index but 95% limits of agreement of about 2 years.
In 406 Australian children Greulich-Pyle bone age was on average 2.2 months below chronological age, with a larger deficit in girls.

rat_growth_cessation_without_fusion.name: Rat growth cessation without epiphyseal fusion
rat_growth_cessation_without_fusion.summary:
The rat is the intermediate case that is most often stated loosely. Rats stop growing but do
not fuse. In Wistar rats aged 62-80 weeks compared with rats aged 2-16 weeks, femoral and
tibial growth plates were still histologically present although longitudinal growth had
ceased (roach2003, rat). Four morphologies absent from young plates appeared in old plates:
a bone band running parallel to the metaphyseal edge that effectively sealed that edge;
extensive acellular areas resistant to resorption and remodelling; extensive remodelling and
bone formation within still-cellular regions of the plate; and direct bone formation by
former growth plate chondrocytes (roach2003, rat). Chondrocyte proliferation continued
sporadically, but loss of synchrony across the plate plus the sealed metaphyseal edge
prevented any net longitudinal expansion. This is a mechanistically distinct endpoint from
human fusion: in the rat the cartilage is walled off and functionally silenced while
remaining a recognisable plate, whereas in humans the cartilage is destroyed and the
epiphyseal and metaphyseal bone become continuous (haines1975, human). Statements that
"rodents do not fuse" (emons2011_2) are correct at the level of the endpoint but conceal that
the rat has its own terminal programme, whose relationship to human fusion has never been
tested.
rat_growth_cessation_without_fusion.human_evidence_note: No human counterpart of the rat's sealed-edge/acellular terminal morphology has been sought in human physes; the only human fusing-plate histology series describes a different picture (disorganised large chondrocytes bounded by dense cortical-like bone) (emons2009).
rat_growth_cessation_without_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The rat terminal phenotype is a different endpoint from human fusion, so rat mechanism data about growth cessation cannot be read as data about fusion. Rat is also the source species for much endocrine growth plate pharmacology.
localization: rat metaphyseal edge of growth plate: bone band sealing the edge in old animals (roach2003)
rat growth plate: acellular areas resistant to resorption in old animals (roach2003)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Aged rat growth plates persist but growth ceases, via a metaphyseal bone band, acellular zones, intraplate bone formation and direct chondrocyte-to-bone formation.
States that experimental study of fusion is complicated by humans and rabbits fusing their growth plates while rodents do not.
In humans and dogs, union proceeds by mineralisation spreading from both plate surfaces, then perforation, then complete destruction of residual cartilage.

remaining_growth_prediction.name: Remaining growth prediction
remaining_growth_prediction.summary:
Predicting how much growth is left is the clinical purpose of this entire layer, and it is
accurate to roughly plus or minus 4-8 cm at 95% confidence - error large enough to swallow the
effect size of most growth-promoting interventions. Tanner-Whitehouse Mark I equations,
built on RUS bone age plus height in 116 boys and 95 girls, predicted within plus or minus 7 cm
in 95% of boys aged 4-12 and plus or minus 6 cm at 13-14; within plus or minus 6 cm for girls
aged 4-11; and improved to plus or minus 4 cm and plus or minus 3 cm for postmenarcheal girls
aged 12 and 13 (tanner1975). Mark II, refitted on a sample deliberately including very tall,
very short and very growth-delayed children, gave 95% intervals of plus or minus 8 cm at age 10
in boys, narrowing to plus or minus 6 cm at 15, or plus or minus 4 cm if the previous year's
height increment was known (tanner1983). The decisive observation for this atlas is how little
of that accuracy comes from bone age: the Khamis-Roche model predicts adult stature from
height, weight and midparent stature with no skeletal age at all, and its errors are only
slightly larger than the Roche-Wainer-Thissen model that uses skeletal age (khamis1994).
Method choice also introduces systematic error that dwarfs reader error: in 37 boys and 32
girls with constitutional delay, mean prediction errors ranged from -0.6 cm (RWT, boys) to
-7.3 cm (TW Mark I, boys), with different methods biased in opposite directions in the two
sexes (brmswig1990). The formal variance decomposition - how much of prediction error is bone
age reading error, how much is reference-standard displacement, how much is irreducible
biological variance in remaining growth at a given maturity - has not been published
(g_l7fuse_007).
remaining_growth_prediction.human_evidence_note: All prediction equations were built and validated on human longitudinal cohorts with observed adult heights as the outcome.
remaining_growth_prediction.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical prediction problem with no animal analogue.
localization: SYS: clinical prediction from height, bone age, midparent height and menarcheal status

key_refs.one_line_finding: TW Mark I equations predict adult height within plus or minus 7 cm in 95% of boys aged 4-12 and plus or minus 3 cm in postmenarcheal girls aged 13.
TW Mark II gives 95% intervals of plus or minus 8 cm at boys aged 10, improving to plus or minus 4 cm when the previous height increment is known.
Adult stature prediction without any skeletal age has errors only slightly larger than the RWT model that uses skeletal age.
Five height prediction methods gave mean errors from -7.3 to +3.1 cm in boys and -2.1 to +2.3 cm in girls with constitutional delay, biased in opposite directions by sex.
The RWT method, using recumbent length, weight, midparent stature and skeletal age, had smaller prediction errors than Bayley-Pinneau.

risser_sign.name: Risser sign
risser_sign.summary:
The Risser sign grades skeletal maturity from the extent of ossification and subsequent fusion
of the iliac apophysis on an anteroposterior pelvic or spine radiograph, and was introduced as
a practical maturity indicator for scoliosis management because the iliac crest is already in
the field of view of a scoliosis film (risser1958). It measures a single, late-maturing
apophysis, which is both its convenience and its limitation: it is uninformative before the
apophysis begins to ossify, it saturates once fusion is complete, and two incompatible grading
conventions are in use (the US system dividing the crest into quarters of excursion, and the
French system dividing it into thirds), so a stated Risser grade is ambiguous without the
convention. Its clinical performance against a growth endpoint is worse than hand-based
maturity scoring: in the development study of Sanders staging, the simplified hand-based system
correlated more strongly with the scoliosis curve acceleration phase than either the Risser sign
or Greulich-Pyle skeletal age (sanders2008). The Risser sign nonetheless remains the most widely
recorded maturity index in spinal deformity practice, so a large body of clinical decision
thresholds is expressed in its units.
risser_sign.human_evidence_note: Human radiographic sign, developed and used only in humans.
risser_sign.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical method with no animal analogue.
localization: human iliac crest apophysis: ossification excursion then fusion, on AP pelvis or spine radiograph

key_refs.one_line_finding: Original description of the iliac apophysis as a maturity sign for the management of scoliosis.
A hand-based simplified maturity staging system correlated more strongly with scoliosis behaviour than the Risser sign or Greulich-Pyle skeletal age.

rus_score.name: RUS score
rus_score.summary:
RUS is the Tanner-Whitehouse subset that scores the radius, ulna and eleven short bones of the
first, third and fifth rays, deliberately excluding the carpals. The exclusion is
methodological rather than cosmetic: carpal maturity saturates early and adds noise in the
peripubertal range where clinical decisions are actually made, so RUS carries most of the
discriminating information near fusion. The Tanner-Whitehouse adult height prediction equations
were built on RUS rather than 20-bone bone age for exactly this reason (tanner1975). RUS is the
scoring backbone of downstream simplified systems: Sanders staging was developed from
Tanner-Whitehouse-III RUS descriptors and reduces them to a small number of clinically
recognisable stages (sanders2008). It is also the intermediate representation of automated
systems: BoneXpert computes intrinsic bone ages for thirteen bones - radius, ulna and eleven
short bones - and only then transforms them into Greulich-Pyle or Tanner-Whitehouse bone age
(thodberg2009). Direct comparison with atlas matching in 1725 radiographs read by twelve
experts showed mean absolute differences of 2.5-3.3 months in most age bands, widening above
180 months, and slightly greater between-specialty variation for RUS than for GP
(tewattanarat2026).
rus_score.human_evidence_note: Human radiographic scoring system validated only in human cohorts.
rus_score.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical method with no animal analogue.
localization: human left hand and wrist: radius, ulna, metacarpals and phalanges of rays 1, 3 and 5; carpals excluded

key_refs.one_line_finding: Adult height prediction equations were built on RUS bone age, omitting the carpal score, from 116 boys and 95 girls of the Harpenden and London longitudinal studies.
BoneXpert computes intrinsic bone ages for the radius, ulna and eleven short bones before transforming to GP or TW bone age.
TW3-RUS and GP differ by 2.5-3.3 months in most age bands with excellent reliability for both.
A simplified staging system derived from Tanner-Whitehouse-III RUS descriptors correlates 0.91 with the scoliosis curve acceleration phase.

sanders_staging.name: Sanders skeletal maturity staging
sanders_staging.summary:
Sanders staging reduces Tanner-Whitehouse-III RUS descriptors to a small ordinal set of stages
recognisable from the digital epiphyses on a hand radiograph, designed for use in a busy clinic
without an atlas or scoring sheet. It was developed and tested by six raters on thirty skeletal
age radiographs: average intra-observer unweighted kappa 0.88 and weighted kappa 0.96, with 89%
exact agreement on repeat reading and 100% of differences within one stage; average
inter-observer unweighted kappa 0.71 and weighted kappa 0.89, with 71% exact agreement between
two reviewers and 97% of differences within one stage or matching. Agreement was highest between
the most experienced raters and was not improved by supplying a classification-specific atlas
(sanders2008). Its clinical claim is that it tracks the growth event that matters better than
its competitors: correlation with the scoliosis curve acceleration phase in 22 girls with
idiopathic scoliosis was 0.91, and the authors report it correlating more strongly with
scoliosis behaviour than either the Risser sign or Greulich-Pyle skeletal age (sanders2008).
The validation sample is small (30 radiographs for reliability, 22 girls for the growth
correlation) and single-centre, and the system is defined only over the peripubertal range where
the digital epiphyses are changing, so it carries no information before capping begins or after
the distal radius fuses.
sanders_staging.human_evidence_note: Developed, tested for reliability and validated against growth behaviour in human cohorts.
sanders_staging.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical method with no animal analogue.
localization: human hand radiograph: digital epiphyses of the phalanges, plus distal radius

key_refs.one_line_finding: A simplified TW3-RUS-derived staging system achieved inter-observer weighted kappa 0.89 and correlated 0.91 with the scoliosis curve acceleration phase.
Original description of the iliac apophysis sign as a maturity indicator in scoliosis management, the comparator Sanders staging was designed to replace.

sex_difference_fusion_timing.name: Sex difference in fusion timing
sex_difference_fusion_timing.summary:
Girls fuse approximately two years before boys, and the gap is site-consistent. In MRI of 958
healthy subjects aged 14.0-21.5 years, complete fusion occurred about 2 years earlier in
females than males across wrist, knee and ankle; the percentages already quoted for 17-year-old
females (75-98% complete by site) are matched by 19-year-old males (90-98%) (kvist2021, human).
Fusion status correlated with pubertal development (Spearman rho 0.514-0.598 across sites) far
more strongly than with any other measured covariate, which locates the sex difference in
pubertal timing and estrogen exposure rather than in a sex-intrinsic property of cartilage
(kvist2021). The endocrine account is consistent: skeletal maturation advances more rapidly in
girls than boys and parallels the sex difference in the trajectory of serum estradiol through
puberty (rochira2015). Body composition modulates the same axis in both sexes - overweight and
obese subjects had higher odds of complete fusion (OR 2.65-8.71 in females, 1.71-4.03 in males)
- whereas regular physical activity did not correlate with fusion at all (kvist2021). Bone age
reading also carries a sex-dependent bias that must not be mistaken for biology: Greulich-Pyle
bone age exceeded chronological age by 3.9 months more in females than in males in a US
multicentre cohort (guevel2026).
sex_difference_fusion_timing.human_evidence_note: Direct imaging comparison within a single healthy cohort of 958 subjects.
sex_difference_fusion_timing.translation_risk_reason: Human phenotype measured directly in humans.
localization: human wrist, knee, ankle: female fusion approximately 2 years ahead of male (kvist2021)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Complete growth plate fusion occurs about 2 years earlier in girls than boys and correlates with pubertal development and BMI but not physical activity.
Greulich-Pyle bone age exceeded chronological age by 2.9 months on average with a 3.9-month greater bias in females, and 95% limits of agreement of about 2 years.
Attributes the more rapid skeletal maturation of girls to the sex difference in the pubertal rise of serum estradiol.

species_transfer_risk_fusion.name: Species-transfer risk in fusion biology
species_transfer_risk_fusion.summary:
This node defines how translation_risk is graded for any claim about growth plate
termination in this atlas, and why the default grade is high. The rule follows from the
comparative facts: the endpoint "epiphyseal fusion" is expressible in human, dog, rabbit and
goat, and is not expressible in mouse or rat (comparative_fusion_across_species). A murine
or rat result therefore cannot be a result about fusion; it is at best a result about a
surrogate. Grading rule used here: (a) low - human tissue or human interventional data
measuring fusion or its imaging proxy directly; (b) moderate - rabbit data on the fusion
endpoint itself, or human genetic experiments of nature with radiographic fusion endpoints;
(c) high - mouse or rat data on any surrogate, or human correlative data whose mechanistic
interpretation rests on rodent work; (d) unknown - no data in any fusing species. Applying
this rule, the three best-evidenced human facts about fusion are all endocrine and none is
cellular: estrogen is required (smith1994, morishima1995, carani1997), a serum estradiol
threshold near 73 pmol/L is needed for closure (lanfranco2008), and fusion order and timing
are reproducible across imaging cohorts (kvist2021). Every cellular mechanism on offer -
senescence, progenitor exhaustion, vascular invasion, apoptosis, ECM change, epigenetic
drift - is graded moderate at best, and only two of the six have ever been examined in
human tissue at all (apoptosis, emons2009; VEGF, emons2010).
species_transfer_risk_fusion.human_evidence_note: The rubric itself is a methodological convention; its inputs are the comparative species data and the human case and imaging literature cited here.
species_transfer_risk_fusion.translation_risk_reason: This node defines the grading scheme rather than carrying a transferred claim.
localization: SYS: applies to all L7 nodes and to any node whose evidence base is rodent growth plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: Names the species barrier explicitly as the reason experimental study of fusion is complicated, and lists apoptosis, autophagy, transdifferentiation and hypoxia as the four competing hypotheses for the final step.
States and demonstrates that the mouse and rat growth plates do not fuse completely even after sexual maturity, making fusion mechanism hard to study in these models.
In an aromatase-deficient man with poor compliance, epiphyseal closure occurred only once serum estradiol exceeded 73 pmol/L.
MRI in 958 healthy subjects aged 14.0-21.5 y establishes site-specific fusion percentages and an ascending foot-to-wrist order.

stem_cell_exhaustion_fusion.name: Stem cell exhaustion model of fusion
stem_cell_exhaustion_fusion.summary:
Mechanism 2 of 6, and the sharpest competitor to generic senescence. Claim: the growth plate
ends because the resting-zone progenitor pool that feeds the proliferative columns is
irreversibly depleted; estrogen acts by accelerating that depletion, not by acting on the
differentiated chondrocytes. Evidence: juvenile ovariectomised rabbits given estradiol
cypionate for 5 weeks and then left untreated for 5 weeks separate two effects. Structural
parameters (growth plate height, number of proliferative and hypertrophic chondrocytes)
remained advanced 5 weeks after estrogen withdrawal, i.e. irreversibly aged, and transient
estrogen exposure hastened fusion. Functional parameters (growth rate, proliferation rate,
hypertrophic cell size) all normalised after withdrawal, i.e. estrogen also exerts a separable
reversible suppression. Estrogen accelerated the normal age-related loss of resting-zone
chondrocytes, and this loss was maintained after withdrawal and did not appear to be apoptotic
(nilsson2014_2, rabbit). Human evidence: none for depletion. What now exists is a description of
the human resting zone in early puberty - single-cell and spatial profiling of surgical growth
plate specimens identified two stem-like resting-zone populations, including PTHrP-negative
"root" stem cells in a WNT- and TGF-beta-low niche, conserved with mouse (chu2026, human,
early pubertal). Nobody has counted those cells as a function of pubertal stage, so the central
quantity of this hypothesis has never been measured in a human. Discriminating experiment:
serial quantification of resting-zone stem cells (by the chu2026 markers) in human growth plate
specimens spanning Tanner 2 to fusion. Under this hypothesis root-cell number falls
monotonically to near zero before column collapse; under the senescence-of-differentiated-cells
hypothesis root-cell number is preserved while proliferative output falls; under the vascular
and apoptosis hypotheses root-cell loss is a late consequence, not an antecedent.
stem_cell_exhaustion_fusion.human_evidence_note: Human resting-zone stem cells have now been identified and profiled in early pubertal specimens (chu2026), but no human study has measured their number or exhaustion as a function of pubertal stage or at fusion.
stem_cell_exhaustion_fusion.translation_risk_reason: The depletion data are rabbit, in a species that does fuse; the human data establish that an analogous progenitor compartment exists but say nothing about its fate. The bridging assumption - that human root cells deplete the way rabbit resting-zone cells do - is untested.
localization: rabbit RZ: chondrocyte number falls with age and estrogen accelerates the loss, non-apoptotically (nilsson2014_2)
human RZ: two stem-like populations, one PTHrP-negative root population in a WNT/TGF-beta-low niche (chu2026)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Transient estrogen in ovariectomised rabbits irreversibly advanced structural senescence and resting-zone cell loss and hastened fusion, while reversibly suppressing growth plate function.
Single-cell and spatial profiling of human early-pubertal growth plate identifies two resting-zone stem-like populations, including PTHrP-negative Prrx1-marked root stem cells.
Fusion in rabbits occurred when the chondrocyte proliferation rate approached zero, consistent with proliferative exhaustion as the trigger.
Suppressing proliferation with dexamethasone delayed both senescence and fusion in rabbits.

tanner_whitehouse_tw3.name: Tanner-Whitehouse 3
tanner_whitehouse_tw3.summary:
Tanner-Whitehouse scores each of a defined set of hand-wrist bones against illustrated stage
criteria, sums weighted stage scores to a maturity score, and converts that score to a bone
age against a reference population. Because it is a per-bone ordinal score, it resolves
maturity more finely than atlas matching and yields a continuous maturity score usable
independently of the age conversion. The reference sample is a British cohort of the 1950s-60s
(TW2), revised for secular change in TW3; the height-prediction equations were built on the
Harpenden Growth Study and the London International Children's Centre longitudinal series
(tanner1975, tanner1983). Reproducibility is somewhat better than atlas matching: interobserver
spread 0.74 years versus 0.96 for GP, intra-observer mean 0.33 years but with 95% confidence
limits of -0.87 to +1.53 years (king1994); intra-observer 95% limits of -1.41 to +1.43 years
versus -2.46 to +2.18 for GP (bull1999). The cost is time: 7.9 minutes per assessment versus
1.4 for GP (king1994). In a modern 1725-radiograph comparison by twelve trained readers, both
GP and TW3-RUS achieved excellent inter- and intra-observer reliability (ICC > 0.9), with mean
absolute differences between GP and TW3-RUS of approximately 2.5-3.3 months in most age bands
and larger discrepancies above 180 months of age, i.e. exactly where fusion decisions are made
(tewattanarat2026). TW3 and GP are not interchangeable within a patient's serial record
(bull1999).
tanner_whitehouse_tw3.human_evidence_note: Human radiographic method, validated only in human cohorts.
tanner_whitehouse_tw3.translation_risk_reason: Human clinical method with no animal analogue.
localization: human left hand and wrist: 20 bones (TW2 20-bone) or 13 bones (RUS subset)

key_refs.one_line_finding: TW2 interobserver spread 0.74 y and intra-observer 0.33 y (95% limits -0.87 to +1.53 y), at 5.6 times the reading time of GP.
TW2 has tighter intra-observer limits than GP and gives non-equivalent estimates, so methods should not be mixed in serial measurement.
In 1725 radiographs read by 12 experts, GP and TW3-RUS both reached ICC > 0.9 with mean absolute differences of 2.5-3.3 months, widening above 180 months of age.
TW Mark II height prediction equations built on a sample including very tall, very short and very growth-delayed children.

acan_gene.name: ACAN
acan_gene.summary:
Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in ACAN, which encodes the growth-plate proteoglycan
aggrecan, produce autosomal dominant short stature with advanced rather than delayed bone age -
an unusual combination that inverts the normal clinical heuristic for short stature. Nilsson 2014
identified novel heterozygous ACAN variants by whole-exome sequencing in three families with
dominant short stature, advanced bone age and premature growth cessation; affected adults reached
-2.3 to -4.2 SDS and affected children measured -1.9 to -3.5 SDS. Gkourogianni 2017 extended this
to 103 individuals from 20 families, with perfect cosegregation of variant and phenotype: adult
median height -2.8 SDS (range -5.9 to -0.9), childhood median -2.0 SDS (range -4.2 to -0.6), and
frequent early-onset osteoarthritis (12 of 20 families) and intervertebral disc disease (9 of 20).
The direction of the bone-age effect is the mechanistically informative part: aggrecan
haploinsufficiency does not simply slow the plate, it accelerates its maturation and shortens the
total growth window. No genotype-phenotype correlation was found between mutation class and joint
involvement, so within this gene the dominant-negative/haploinsufficiency distinction does not
appear to stratify outcome the way it does for COL10A1. The childhood-to-adult widening of the
deficit (-2.0 to -2.8 SDS median) is itself a quantitative statement that the loss accrues across
puberty rather than being set prenatally.
acan_gene.human_evidence_note: Two independent human cohorts with measured adult and childhood stature and cosegregation testing.
acan_gene.translation_risk_reason: Claims here are restricted to human allele-dose and measured stature; the murine cmd/nanomelia aggrecan literature is not invoked.
localization: human: germline; effector tissue is growth plate and articular cartilage extracellular matrix

key_refs.one_line_finding: Heterozygous ACAN variants in three families cause short stature (adult -2.3 to -4.2 SDS) with advanced bone age and early growth cessation.
103 individuals from 20 ACAN families: adult median height -2.8 SDS, childhood -2.0 SDS, with early osteoarthritis in 12/20 families.
ACAN variants in 2 of 102 children classified as idiopathic short stature.

assortative_mating_height.name: Assortative mating for height
assortative_mating_height.summary:
Height is one of the traits for which assortative mating is genetically detectable, and it matters
for this atlas because it inflates every quantitative-genetic parameter derived from relatives.
Sunde 2024 showed theoretically and empirically that assortative mating raises trait-specific
genetic variance and genetic similarity between relatives, and that distant relatives are more
affected than close ones - a signature that lets the history of assortment be read from
present-day data. Correlating polygenic indices in 47,135 co-parents from the Norwegian Mother,
Father and Child Cohort Study gave genetic evidence of assortative mating in nine of sixteen traits
examined, and the same traits showed elevated similarity between relatives, especially distant
ones. For six of the nine traits the offspring generation showed greater genetic variance than
stable long-run assortment would produce, implying assortment is recent or intensifying rather than
at equilibrium. Three consequences follow for L8. Twin heritability estimates are biased upward
because assortment increases dizygotic but not monozygotic genetic correlation. Polygenic score
weights trained in an assorting population absorb the induced gametic-phase disequilibrium between
causal alleles. And Mendelian randomization using height instruments inherits the same bias unless
family-based designs are used. The magnitude of the height-specific inflation is not quantified in
the sources reached here, which is the main quantitative gap on this node.

claim_grades.claim: Assortative mating is genetically detectable and raises genetic variance and relative similarity for assorted traits.
claim_grades.basis: Path-analytic prediction plus empirical confirmation in 47,135 co-parents with the predicted distant-versus-close relative gradient (sunde2024).

claim_grades.claim: Assortative mating for height specifically inflates height heritability estimates by a quantified amount.
claim_grades.basis: No height-specific inflation magnitude was located; the effect is established in principle and for the trait class but not measured for stature. See gap g_l8gen_011.

assortative_mating_height.human_evidence_note: Polygenic indices measured in 47,135 human co-parents plus relative-similarity patterns across a national cohort.
localization: human: population mating structure, not tissue-localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: Genetic evidence of assortative mating in 9 of 16 traits among 47,135 MoBa co-parents, with elevated similarity between distant relatives and offspring genetic variance inconsistent with equilibrium assortment.
Sibling IBD heritability design chosen partly because it is less exposed to assortative-mating inflation than pedigree correlations.

col10a1_gene.name: COL10A1
col10a1_gene.summary:
COL10A1 encodes the short-chain collagen made exclusively by hypertrophic chondrocytes, and it is
the one human locus in this atlas where dominant-negative and haploinsufficiency alleles of the
same gene have been compared quantitatively in the same cohort. Warman 1993 mapped autosomal
dominant Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia to a 13 bp COL10A1 deletion segregating in a large
kindred (lod 18.2 at theta=0), producing a frameshift that shortens the alpha-1(X) chain by nine
residues in the conserved C-terminal NC1 domain. Meng 2025 assembled 4 new cases plus 124 published
ones and found the discriminating result: patients carrying missense variants had height Z
-3.62 +/- 1.95 versus -1.99 +/- 1.28 for truncating variants (P = 0.013), and had more metaphyseal
irregularity of the distal radius and ulna (P = 0.019). Because truncating COL10A1 alleles are
degraded by nonsense-mediated decay - leaving the wild-type allele to make half the normal amount
of collagen X - while missense alleles produce a stable chain that disrupts trimerisation of the
wild-type product, this is a direct human measurement that dominant-negative interference costs
about 1.6 SDS more stature than losing one copy outright. NC1-domain variants also present earlier
than non-NC1 variants (median 12 versus 72 months, P = 0.0014). The mechanistic reading is
corroborated in vitro: Xu 2025 showed a frameshift allele disrupts trimerisation of normal collagen
X, exerting a dominant-negative effect on the wild-type chain.

claim_grades.claim: COL10A1 mutations cause metaphyseal chondrodysplasia Schmid.
claim_grades.basis: Original linkage kindred at lod 18.2 (warman1993) plus a 128-case genotype-phenotype series (meng2025).

claim_grades.claim: Missense (dominant-negative) COL10A1 alleles reduce stature more than truncating (haploinsufficient) alleles.
claim_grades.basis: Single pooled cohort of 128 cases with P=0.013 (meng2025); the comparison is within one literature aggregation rather than two independent cohorts.

col10a1_gene.human_evidence_note: Height Z-scores measured in 128 human COL10A1 cases and stratified by mutation class.
col10a1_gene.translation_risk_reason: The Col10a1-null mouse has a mild or absent phenotype and is deliberately not used to support any claim here.
localization: human: germline; product restricted to hypertrophic zone chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: A 13 bp COL10A1 deletion segregates with autosomal dominant Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia at lod 18.2, truncating the NC1 domain.
In 128 COL10A1 cases, missense variants gave height Z -3.62 +/- 1.95 versus -1.99 +/- 1.28 for truncating variants (P=0.013).

col2a1_gene.name: COL2A1
col2a1_gene.summary:
COL2A1 encodes the alpha-1 chain of type II collagen, the principal fibrillar collagen of growth
plate and articular cartilage, and its human allelic series is the textbook case of
dominant-negative dosage rather than haploinsufficiency. The recurrent pathogenic class is glycine
substitution within the Gly-X-Y repeat of the triple-helical domain: Zhan 2025 found six such
substitutions (Gly1110Ser, Gly1107Glu, Gly873Arg, Gly456Ala, Gly1062Ser, Gly1182Arg) plus one
intronic variant across seven unrelated Chinese SEDC families, all presenting with disproportionate
short stature and skeletal abnormality. Because collagen II is a homotrimer, a single mutant chain
poisons the assembly of trimers containing any wild-type chains, which is why heterozygous missense
alleles give a phenotype far more severe than the expected 50% reduction and why true whole-gene
deletions instead give the mild Stickler spectrum. The severity gradient across type II
collagenopathies - achondrogenesis type II (lethal), SEDC, Kniest, Stickler - tracks the position
and steric bulk of the substituting residue rather than the amount of protein made. ClinGen's
skeletal disorders expert panel classifies COL2A1 as definitively associated with at least one
skeletal disorder among the 26 gene-disease relationships it curated. The quantitative weakness of
this node is that no published series gives a mean adult height SDS by mutation class for COL2A1
the way Meng 2025 does for COL10A1; the reported growth data are single-arm GH-treatment responses
(+0.76 and +0.27 height SDS over 3.5 and 3 years in two SEDC children).

claim_grades.claim: Heterozygous glycine substitutions in the COL2A1 triple-helical domain cause spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita.
claim_grades.basis: Seven unrelated families (zhan2025) plus ClinGen definitive gene-disease classification (webb2026); a very large independent literature exists.

claim_grades.claim: The mechanism is dominant-negative incorporation into the collagen II homotrimer rather than haploinsufficiency.
claim_grades.basis: Consistent with the severity gradient and with the mild phenotype of whole-gene deletions, but no allele-matched human trimer-assembly experiment was reached in this sweep. See gap g_l8gen_005.

col2a1_gene.human_evidence_note: Human genotype-phenotype series with cosegregation; no animal data are used for any claim on this node.
localization: human: germline; product is the dominant fibrillar collagen of growth plate and articular cartilage

key_refs.one_line_finding: Six COL2A1 glycine substitutions plus one intronic variant across seven unrelated SEDC families; GH gave +0.76 and +0.27 height SDS in two patients.
ClinGen skeletal disorders expert panel classifies COL2A1 as definitively associated with skeletal disease across curated gene-disease relationships.
COL2A1 variant found in 1 of 102 children classified as idiopathic short stature.

common_vs_rare_pathway_divergence.name: Divergence between common-variant and rare-disease pathway rankings for height
common_vs_rare_pathway_divergence.summary:
Ranking growth-plate pathways by common-variant height signal and by monogenic skeletal-dysplasia
burden produces two different orders, and the divergence is systematic rather than random. The
common-variant ranking, read from the three primary pathway-enrichment analyses, is dominated by
paracrine growth-plate signalling and matrix synthesis: Weedon 2008 reported Hedgehog (IHH, HHIP,
PTCH1), extracellular matrix (EFEMP1, ADAMTSL3, ACAN) and cell-cycle/chromatin genes (CDK6, HMGA2,
DLEU7); Lango Allen 2010 reported 180 loci enriched for genes connected in biological pathways and
for genes underlying skeletal growth defects; Wood 2014 reported FGF signalling, WNT/beta-catenin,
chondroitin-sulfate-related genes, mTOR, osteoglycin and hyaluronic acid binding. The rare-disease
ranking, read from the 2023 nosology's 771 entries across 552 genes and from ClinGen's curated
panel, is dominated by structural collagens and matrix assembly (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL2A1, COL10A1,
COMP, MATN3), sulfate transport (SLC26A2), mineralisation (ALPL), ion channels (TRPV4) and - the
largest single stature effects in medicine - the GH-IGF endocrine axis (GHR at -4 to -10 SDS,
STAT5B at -7.8 SDS, IGFALS, IGF1, IGF1R, PAPPA2). The GH-IGF axis appears in no published height
GWAS pathway-enrichment list retrieved in this sweep. Three pathway families are shared: Hedgehog
(IHH is both the commonest ISS panel finding and a top GWAS locus), CNP/NPR2, and
proteoglycan/glycosaminoglycan synthesis, which Marouli 2017 identifies specifically at the rare
coding tier. The reading offered here is that a gene contributes common-variant height variance
only if its dose is both continuously variable in the population and non-lethal at the margin;
endocrine-axis genes are buffered by feedback so that common variation produces little phenotype
while total loss is catastrophic, whereas paracrine and matrix genes act locally and dose-linearly
in the plate. That is a hypothesis, and it is graded as one.

claim_grades.claim: Published height GWAS pathway-enrichment analyses list paracrine signalling and matrix genes, not the GH-IGF endocrine axis.
claim_grades.basis: Direct reading of the enrichment results in weedon2008, lango2010 and wood2014, plus a reproducible null search (g_l8gen_001).

claim_grades.claim: Monogenic short stature is dominated by GH-IGF axis and structural collagen genes.
claim_grades.basis: The 2023 nosology (unger2023) and ClinGen curation (webb2026), together with the measured stature effects in ghr_gene, stat5b_gene, igfals_gene, col2a1_gene, col10a1_gene and comp_gene.

claim_grades.claim: Hedgehog, CNP/NPR2 and proteoglycan synthesis are the pathway families where the two rankings converge.
claim_grades.basis: IHH and ACAN appear in weedon2008 and in monogenic ISS panels (andrade2022); proteoglycan/GAG synthesis is named at the rare coding tier by marouli2017. Convergence is by inspection rather than by a formal overlap statistic.

claim_grades.claim: The divergence arises because feedback-buffered endocrine genes tolerate common variation while dose-linear local genes do not.
claim_grades.basis: Explanatory hypothesis, not tested. The discriminating test is stated in gap g_l8gen_001.

common_vs_rare_pathway_divergence.human_evidence_note: Both rankings are compiled from human data - GWAS pathway enrichment on measured stature and curated human monogenic disorder catalogues.
common_vs_rare_pathway_divergence.translation_risk_reason: A comparison of two human evidence bases.
localization: human: genome-wide comparison of two ranking procedures, not tissue-localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: 697 height variants implicate FGF signalling, WNT/beta-catenin, chondroitin-sulfate genes, mTOR, osteoglycin and hyaluronic acid binding - no endocrine axis.
The first 20 height loci implicate Hedgehog (IHH, HHIP, PTCH1), extracellular matrix (EFEMP1, ADAMTSL3, ACAN) and cell-cycle genes.
180 height loci are enriched for genes connected in biological pathways and for genes underlying monogenic skeletal growth defects.
Rare coding height variants implicate proteoglycan and glycosaminoglycan synthesis and overlap monogenic growth-disorder genes.
771 genetic skeletal disorder entries across 552 genes define the rare-disease gene ranking.
ClinGen curation identifies COL1A1, COL1A2, COL2A1, FGFR3, SLC26A2, TRPV4, COMP, ALPL and SOX9 as the genes behind the commonest skeletal dysplasias.
Homozygous GHR loss gives -4 to -10 SDS, the largest monogenic stature effect, at a locus absent from height GWAS enrichment lists.

aliases: GWAS versus skeletal dysplasia gene rankings

comp_gene.name: COMP
comp_gene.summary:
COMP mutations cause pseudoachondroplasia and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 1, and the human
allelic data show that these are not two diseases but two ends of one continuum produced by
mutations in a single structural domain. Briggs 1995 localised both to chromosome 19p13.1 and found
COMP mutations in three patients within the region encoding a calcium-binding motif, establishing
allelism. Ni 2026 aggregated 830 genetically diagnosed PSACH/EDM1 patients (471 probands, 224
distinct COMP variants) from 106 publications: 80.8% of variants are missense, 87.7% of probands
carry a variant in the type-3 calcium-binding repeat domain, 38.9% in exon 13 alone, and
c.1417_1419del (p.Asp473del) is the single commonest allele. PSACH patients had significantly
earlier onset and significantly shorter stature than EDM1 patients (both P < 0.001). The mechanism
is not dosage: COMP is a pentamer, mutant subunits misfold, accumulate in the chondrocyte rough
endoplasmic reticulum and trigger a stress response, so heterozygous missense alleles are
cytotoxic-dominant while true null alleles are far milder. The consequence for this atlas is that
COMP is a counterexample to the assumption that a matrix gene's stature effect scales with how much
functional protein is left. What is missing is a published mean adult height in centimetres or SDS
for genotype-defined PSACH cohorts; the 830-case aggregation reports stature only as a
between-group comparison.

claim_grades.claim: COMP mutations cause both pseudoachondroplasia and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 1 as one allelic continuum.
claim_grades.basis: Original allelism demonstration (briggs1995) plus 830-case aggregation with domain mapping (ni2026); ClinGen definitive (webb2026).

claim_grades.claim: PSACH is significantly shorter than EDM1 at the same locus.
claim_grades.basis: One systematic aggregation of published cases (ni2026, P<0.001); vulnerable to ascertainment because diagnosis labels are partly assigned on stature.

comp_gene.human_evidence_note: 830 genotyped human patients with clinical stature comparison between PSACH and EDM1.
localization: human: germline; product is a pentameric extracellular matrix glycoprotein of growth plate and articular cartilage

key_refs.one_line_finding: PSACH and MED are allelic, both caused by COMP mutations in a calcium-binding motif on chromosome 19p13.1.
830 PSACH/EDM1 patients: 80.8% missense variants, 87.7% in the type-3 repeat domain; PSACH significantly shorter and earlier-onset than EDM1.
ClinGen curation places COMP among genes definitively associated with skeletal disorders.

cyp19a1_gene.name: CYP19A1
cyp19a1_gene.summary:
CYP19A1 encodes aromatase, the single enzyme converting androgens to estrogens, and its human
loss-of-function phenotype is the ligand-side control for the ESR1 receptor-side experiment.
Morishima 1995 reported a novel CYP19 mutation in an XX proband and her brother: the 28-year-old
sister had non-adrenal female pseudohermaphroditism at birth, progressive virilisation at the age
of puberty, pubertal failure with no signs of estrogen action, hypergonadotropic hypogonadism,
polycystic ovaries and tall stature, with elevated plasma testosterone, androstenedione and
17-hydroxyprogesterone and low estradiol. Carani 1997 then performed the intervention that closes
the loop, treating an aromatase-deficient man with testosterone and then estradiol and showing that
only estradiol produced the skeletal response. Rochira 2010 characterised four aromatase-deficient
men and found a paradox that constrains any simple model: their GH response to GHRH plus arginine
was severely impaired compared with 12 normal subjects and basal IGF-1 was low, yet they were tall.
Tall stature in aromatase deficiency therefore occurs despite, not because of, growth hormone -
the plate stays open long enough that a subnormal growth rate accumulates more total height than a
normal rate applied for a normal number of years. Aromatase deficiency and ESR1 disruption together
form the ligand/receptor pair that makes the estrogen-fusion claim in this atlas an A-grade human
result rather than an extrapolation.

claim_grades.claim: Loss of aromatase activity prevents epiphyseal fusion and produces tall stature in humans of both sexes.
claim_grades.basis: Sibling pair with the enzyme defect (morishima1995), an intervention showing estradiol but not testosterone restores the skeletal response (carani1997), and four further adult men (rochira2010).

claim_grades.claim: Tall stature in aromatase deficiency occurs despite an impaired GH-IGF-1 axis.
claim_grades.basis: Case-control GH stimulation testing in 4 patients versus 12 controls (rochira2010); single study, small n.

cyp19a1_gene.human_evidence_note: Human enzyme-deficient patients of both sexes, with an intervention arm (testosterone versus estradiol) in an affected man.
cyp19a1_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human enzyme deficiency with human hormone-replacement intervention.
localization: human: germline; aromatase expressed in ovary, testis, placenta, brain and adipose tissue under alternative tissue-specific promoters

key_refs.one_line_finding: A novel CYP19 mutation in XX and XY siblings gives absent estrogen action, hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and tall stature.
In an aromatase-deficient man, estradiol but not testosterone produced the skeletal response.
Four aromatase-deficient men had severely impaired GH response to GHRH-arginine and low IGF-1 yet were tall.

de_novo_variant_growth.name: De novo variation and growth
de_novo_variant_growth.summary:
Several of the largest-effect growth-plate mutations in humans are not inherited but arise de novo
in the paternal germline, and they are enriched far above the background mutation rate by positive
selection acting on spermatogonial stem cells. Neville 2025 sequenced 81 bulk sperm samples from
men aged 24-75 with duplex NanoSeq and measured a linear accumulation of 1.67 mutations per year
per haploid genome (95% CI 1.41-1.92), identified more than 35,000 germline coding mutations, and
found 40 genes under significant positive selection in the male germline, most of them associated
with developmental or cancer-predisposition disorders; selection drives a 2-3 fold increased risk
of known disease-causing mutations, so 3-5% of sperm from middle-aged and older men carry a
pathogenic exome mutation. FGFR3, the achondroplasia gene, is the archetype. Moura 2024 assayed 10
FGFR3 missense substitutions by digital PCR across a dissected postmortem human testis and showed
that 9 raise ligand-independent receptor signalling, with two distinct expansion behaviours: some
variants form larger subclonal expansions whose frequency correlates positively with donor age,
while others show elevated frequency independent of age, consistent with accumulation before sexual
maturity. That is the mechanistic explanation for why achondroplasia is overwhelmingly de novo,
paternal in origin, and associated with advanced paternal age - the mutation is not merely
tolerated in the germline, it is selected for.

claim_grades.claim: Positive selection in the male germline enriches pathogenic de novo mutations above the neutral rate.
claim_grades.basis: Genome-wide duplex sequencing of 81 sperm samples identifying 40 positively selected genes (neville2025) plus locus-resolved subclonal expansion mapping in testis for FGFR3 (moura2024).

claim_grades.claim: This mechanism explains the paternal-age association of achondroplasia specifically.
claim_grades.basis: Age-correlated FGFR3 subclonal expansions measured directly in human testis (moura2024); the epidemiological link to achondroplasia incidence is inferred rather than jointly measured in the same study.

de_novo_variant_growth.human_evidence_note: Direct sequencing and locus-specific quantification in human sperm and dissected human testis.
localization: human: male germline, spermatogonial stem cell compartment

key_refs.one_line_finding: Duplex sperm sequencing of 81 men: 1.67 mutations/year/haploid genome and 40 positively selected genes, driving 2-3 fold enrichment of disease-causing mutations.
Nine of ten FGFR3 missense substitutions raise ligand-independent signalling; several form age-correlated subclonal expansions in human testis.
Achondroplasia arises from recurrent FGFR3 Gly380 substitutions, predominantly de novo.

dna_methylation_growth_plate.name: DNA methylation in the growth plate
dna_methylation_growth_plate.summary:
DNA methylation in developing human cartilage has now been mapped directly, which converts a
previously animal-only claim into a human one. McDonnell 2024 quantified methylation at
approximately 700,000 CpGs in developing human chondrocytes from 72 samples spanning 7 to 21
post-conception weeks, found significant change at 3% of all CpGs, and defined more than 8,200
developmental differentially methylated regions. Integrating with genetic data identified 24 loci
where osteoarthritis risk variants colocalise with methylation quantitative trait loci, and
comparison with mature chondrocyte datasets separated effects exerted only during development from
those operating throughout the life course. The developmental-only class is the important one for
this atlas: it means a regulatory variant can act on cartilage before birth and leave a permanent
skeletal consequence with no detectable effect in adult tissue, which is a specific mechanism by
which height-associated non-coding variants could be invisible to any adult-tissue eQTL catalogue.
The complementary claim from animal work - Nilsson 2005 showed growth plate senescence in rabbit is
accompanied by loss of DNA methylation - remains species-restricted and is not asserted here as
human fact. The gap between the two is that no human dataset yet spans postnatal growth plate
through fusion, so the human methylome is characterised in fetal cartilage and in adult articular
cartilage but not across the growing physis itself.

claim_grades.claim: DNA methylation changes substantially across human cartilage development and colocalises with skeletal disease risk variants.
claim_grades.basis: 72-sample human developmental methylome with 8,200 DMRs and 24 mQTL-GWAS colocalisations (mcdonnell2024).

claim_grades.claim: Growth plate senescence is accompanied by loss of DNA methylation in humans.
claim_grades.basis: Demonstrated in rabbit (nilsson2005); no human postnatal growth plate methylome exists. Recorded as a species gap, not as human fact. See gap g_l8gen_013.

dna_methylation_growth_plate.human_evidence_note: Epigenome-wide methylation measured in 72 human developing cartilage samples with colocalisation against human genetic association data.
dna_methylation_growth_plate.translation_risk_reason: The methylome claim is measured in human tissue. The senescence-associated demethylation claim is rabbit-only and is explicitly not extended to humans here.
localization: human: developing chondrocytes 7-21 post-conception weeks; postnatal growth plate not covered

key_refs.one_line_finding: 700,000-CpG methylome of 72 human developing chondrocyte samples (7-21 PCW): 3% of CpGs change, >8,200 developmental DMRs, 24 OA loci colocalise with mQTLs.
Growth plate senescence in rabbit is associated with loss of DNA methylation - animal evidence only.
Human skeletal developmental functional genomics intersecting chondrocyte regulatory maps with height heritability.

dominant_negative_vs_haploinsufficiency.name: Dominant-negative versus haploinsufficiency dose effects
dominant_negative_vs_haploinsufficiency.summary:
Two heterozygous alleles of the same gene can produce very different phenotypes depending on whether
the mutant product is absent or present-but-defective, and the growth plate provides the cleanest
human measurement of that difference anywhere in medicine. In COL10A1 metaphyseal chondrodysplasia
Schmid, Meng 2025 pooled 4 new and 124 published cases and found height Z of -3.62 +/- 1.95 for
missense variants versus -1.99 +/- 1.28 for truncating variants (P = 0.013), with more metaphyseal
irregularity in the missense group (P = 0.019). Truncating COL10A1 transcripts are degraded by
nonsense-mediated decay, leaving one functional allele; missense alleles make a stable chain that
disrupts trimerisation of the wild-type product, as Yang 2025 demonstrated directly for the
p.W651fsX666 allele. Dominant-negative interference therefore costs about 1.6 SDS more stature than
losing one copy outright, at the same locus, in the same disease. The same logic explains why
COL2A1 glycine substitutions give lethal-to-severe type II collagenopathies while whole-gene
deletions give the mild Stickler spectrum, and why COMP missense variants concentrated in the
type-3 calcium-binding repeat (87.7% of 471 probands) are cytotoxic through ER retention rather
than dosage-limiting. The generalisation has a documented exception within this layer: in ACAN,
Gkourogianni 2017 found no genotype-phenotype correlation between mutation class and joint
involvement across 20 families, so the dominant-negative premium is locus-specific and must be
demonstrated rather than assumed.

claim_grades.claim: At COL10A1, dominant-negative missense alleles reduce stature more than haploinsufficient truncating alleles.
claim_grades.basis: One pooled 128-case cohort with P=0.013 (meng2025), mechanistically corroborated by an independent trimerisation assay (yang2025); the height comparison itself has not been repeated in a second cohort.

claim_grades.claim: The dominant-negative premium generalises across matrix-protein loci.
claim_grades.basis: Consistent with the COL2A1 and COMP genotype-phenotype patterns but explicitly absent in ACAN (gkourogianni2017), so the generalisation has a documented counterexample.

dominant_negative_vs_haploinsufficiency.human_evidence_note: Direct human height comparison between mutation classes at a single locus, with an in vitro trimerisation assay establishing the mechanism.
dominant_negative_vs_haploinsufficiency.translation_risk_reason: Human genotype-phenotype comparison with human-protein biochemistry.
localization: human: applies at any locus whose product is a multimer or matrix assembly

key_refs.one_line_finding: COL10A1 missense variants give height Z -3.62 +/- 1.95 versus -1.99 +/- 1.28 for truncating variants (P=0.013) in 128 cases.
COL10A1 p.W651fsX666 impairs trimerisation of normal collagen X, demonstrating a dominant-negative effect on the wild-type allele.
80.8% of COMP variants are missense and 87.7% of probands carry one in the type-3 repeat domain, the domain whose misfolding drives ER retention.
No genotype-phenotype correlation between ACAN mutation class and joint involvement across 20 families - the documented counterexample.

epigenetic_clock_growth.name: Epigenetic clocks and growth
epigenetic_clock_growth.summary:
Epigenetic clocks estimate biological age from DNA methylation and are accurate enough in children
to be a candidate maturational readout, but they have not been validated against skeletal
maturation, which is what this atlas would need them for. McEwen 2020 built the Pediatric-Buccal-
Epigenetic clock from 1,721 genome-wide methylation profiles across 11 cohorts of typically
developing individuals aged 0-20, selecting 94 CpG sites by elastic-net regression in a
1,032-sample training set and achieving a median absolute error of 0.35 years in a separate
689-sample test set. That is finer resolution than bone age scoring, non-invasive, and continuous.

Two longitudinal cohorts have in fact tested epigenetic age against growth, and both found the
association to be real but weak. Simpkin 2017 measured methylation at birth, 7 and 17 years in
1,018 ALSPAC children and found that age acceleration at 7 years was associated with higher average
height across development (0.23 cm per year of age acceleration, 95% CI 0.04-0.41), while also
reporting conflicting directions - positive associations with change in weight, BMI and Tanner
stage but negative with change in height. Kim 2024 examined 135 children and found epigenetic age
acceleration at about 10 years associated with higher peak height velocity (beta 0.018, P = 0.0008)
but not with age at peak height velocity (beta -0.0022, P = 0.067), and concluded the associations
were statistically significant but not strong. What remains genuinely absent, established by
explicit search, is any study relating an epigenetic clock to radiographic bone age or to
epiphyseal fusion status - the two skeletal-maturation endpoints this atlas would need. Until that
exists an epigenetic clock is a validated chronological-age estimator in children with a weak
association to growth velocity, and not a substitute for bone age.

claim_grades.claim: DNA methylation predicts chronological age in children to within about 0.4 years.
claim_grades.basis: Training and independent test sets totalling 1,721 profiles across 11 cohorts (mcewen2020).

claim_grades.claim: Epigenetic age acceleration is associated with growth in children, weakly.
claim_grades.basis: Two independent longitudinal cohorts: ALSPAC n=1,018 (simpkin2017, 0.23 cm per year of AA) and n=135 (kim2024, PHV beta 0.018, P=0.0008). Directions are partly conflicting within simpkin2017 and both papers describe the effect as small.

claim_grades.claim: Epigenetic age acceleration indexes skeletal maturation, i.e. tracks bone age or predicts epiphyseal fusion.
claim_grades.basis: No study relating any epigenetic clock to radiographic bone age or fusion status exists; established by explicit search (g_l8gen_014, 33 hits, none qualifying). Downgraded from an initial grade-X assessment after the search returned two genuine growth-endpoint primaries.

epigenetic_clock_growth.human_evidence_note: Human paediatric cohorts with measured chronological age; no skeletal maturation endpoint has been tested.
localization: human: buccal epithelium and blood; no cartilage or growth plate clock exists

key_refs.one_line_finding: The PedBE clock predicts chronological age from 94 buccal CpGs with median absolute error 0.35 years in children aged 0-20.
Human developmental cartilage methylome, the substrate a cartilage-specific clock would have to be built on.
ALSPAC n=1,018: epigenetic age acceleration at 7 years associated with higher average height (0.23 cm per year of AA, 95% CI 0.04-0.41), with conflicting directions for change measures.
n=135 children: epigenetic age acceleration associated with higher peak height velocity (beta 0.018, P=0.0008) but not with age at peak height velocity.

contradicts: simpkin2017 reports epigenetic age acceleration positively associated with AVERAGE height but negatively associated with CHANGE in height within the same cohort; the two directions are not reconciled in the paper.

esr1_gene.name: ESR1
esr1_gene.summary:
ESR1 supplies the single most decisive human experiment in the fusion literature. Smith 1994
described a 28-year-old man homozygous for a disruptive ESR1 mutation who was 204 cm tall with
incomplete epiphyseal closure and a history of continued linear growth into adulthood despite
otherwise normal pubertal development; serum estradiol and estrone were elevated, testosterone was
normal, FSH and LH were increased, and lumbar spine bone mineral density was 0.745 g/cm2, 3.1 SD
below the young adult mean. He was normally masculinised, so androgen action was intact. The
inference is unavoidable and does not require a mouse: in humans it is estrogen acting through
ESR1, not androgen and not estrogen concentration per se, that closes the growth plate and
mineralises bone, in both sexes. Quaynor 2013 supplied the female counterpart, a woman with an ESR1
variant, delayed puberty and estrogen resistance. Because oestrogen was high and the receptor was
absent, the experiment separates ligand from receptor in a way no pharmacological study can. The
node is graded on a single index male plus one female case, which is thin by cohort standards but
epistemically strong because the phenotype is a natural knockout with an unambiguous readout.

claim_grades.claim: Estrogen acting through ESR1 is required for epiphyseal fusion in humans of both sexes.
claim_grades.basis: Male ESR1-null with unfused plates and continued growth despite high estradiol (smith1994) plus independent female estrogen-resistance case (quaynor2013), and the concordant aromatase-deficiency series which removes ligand rather than receptor.

claim_grades.claim: The adult-height effect of ESR1 loss is about +204 cm / continued growth.
claim_grades.basis: Single male patient; no cohort exists because the genotype is exceptionally rare.

esr1_gene.human_evidence_note: Two human loss-of-function patients (one male, one female) with measured stature, bone density and gonadotropins.
esr1_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human receptor-null phenotype; the mouse ERKO literature is not needed and is not invoked.
localization: human: germline; receptor acts in growth plate chondrocytes, bone and the hypothalamic-pituitary axis

key_refs.one_line_finding: A man homozygous for a disruptive ESR1 mutation reached 204 cm with unfused epiphyses, elevated estradiol, normal testosterone and lumbar BMD 3.1 SD below the young adult mean.
A woman with an ESR1 alpha variant showed delayed puberty and estrogen resistance.

fgfr3_gene.name: FGFR3
fgfr3_gene.summary:
FGFR3 is the clearest bidirectional dose experiment in human skeletal genetics because activating
and inactivating alleles of the same receptor move stature in opposite directions, and because the
activating series is graded rather than binary. Shiang 1994 and Rousseau 1994 independently showed
that achondroplasia is caused by heterozygous transmembrane-domain substitutions at Gly380, found
on essentially all achondroplasia chromosomes; Tavormina 1995 showed that thanatophoric dysplasia
types I and II arise from distinct, more strongly activating FGFR3 domains; Bellus 1995 showed
hypochondroplasia arises from the weaker tyrosine-kinase-domain N540K. FGFR3 is thus a negative
regulator of bone growth in which the degree of constitutive activation predicts the degree of
shortening across four clinically distinct disorders. The loss-of-function arm was found last:
Toydemir 2006 mapped CATSHL syndrome - camptodactyly, tall stature, scoliosis, hearing loss - to
FGFR3 p.R621H, a partial loss of kinase function that recapitulates the Fgfr3-knockout mouse
phenotype and therefore establishes in humans that reducing FGFR3 signalling lengthens bone. A
second, independent CATSHL family with p.R621C at the same residue has since been reported.
Separately, FGFR3 is a paternal-age-effect gene: Moura 2024 measured 10 FGFR3 missense
substitutions in postmortem human testis by digital PCR and found 9 raised ligand-independent
signalling, several forming age-correlated subclonal expansions - the germline selection mechanism
that makes achondroplasia predominantly a de novo, paternally derived mutation.
fgfr3_gene.human_evidence_note: Gain- and loss-of-function alleles both defined in humans with measured stature and independently replicated across four disorders.
fgfr3_gene.translation_risk_reason: All allele-to-stature claims are human; the mouse Fgfr3 knockout is cited only as concordant background for the CATSHL direction.
localization: human: germline; receptor acts in proliferative and prehypertrophic growth plate chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Achondroplasia is caused by heterozygous FGFR3 transmembrane Gly380 substitutions present on all 16 achondroplasia chromosomes examined.
Independent identification of FGFR3 mutations as the cause of achondroplasia.
Thanatophoric dysplasia types I and II are caused by distinct FGFR3 mutations more strongly activating than the achondroplasia allele.
Hypochondroplasia is caused by the weaker tyrosine-kinase-domain FGFR3 N540K substitution.
FGFR3 p.R621H causes partial loss of function and CATSHL syndrome with tall stature, establishing that reduced FGFR3 signalling lengthens human bone.
Nine of ten FGFR3 missense substitutions assayed in human testis raise ligand-independent signalling; several form age-correlated subclonal germline expansions.

gdf5_height_locus.name: GDF5 height locus
gdf5_height_locus.summary:
The GDF5-UQCC region is the height locus that ties normal stature variation to osteoarthritis risk.
Sanna 2008 performed genome-wide association analyses in 6,669 individuals from Finland and
Sardinia with follow-up in 28,801 more and showed that common variants in this osteoarthritis-
associated locus contribute to height with an estimated additive effect of 0.44 cm per allele
(overall P < 1e-15). GDF5 (growth/differentiation factor 5, BMP-14) is a genuine skeletal
developmental gene - it specifies the joint interzone and is mutated in brachydactyly and in
Grebe/Hunter-Thompson chondrodysplasia - so unlike ZBTB38 this locus has a plausible and
independently established route to the growth plate and joint. The per-allele effect, 0.44 cm, is
statistically indistinguishable in magnitude from HMGA2's 0.4 cm, which is the useful comparison:
a locus with clear skeletal developmental function and a locus with none contribute the same
fraction of a centimetre. That equality is a direct observation against the intuition that
common-variant effect size tracks biological centrality, and it is one of the empirical footings of
the omnigenic argument. Sanna's authors explicitly proposed the link between height genetics and
osteoarthritis is mediated through bone growth and development.
gdf5_height_locus.human_evidence_note: Human GWAS with replication and a measured per-allele centimetre effect.
gdf5_height_locus.translation_risk_reason: Human association data; murine Gdf5 (brachypodism) work sits in gdf5_protein and gdf5_gene (L0).
localization: human: germline 20q11.22; GDF5 protein acts at the joint interzone and in growth plate cartilage

key_refs.one_line_finding: Common variants in the GDF5-UQCC region alter adult height by an estimated 0.44 cm per allele (P < 1e-15) in 35,470 individuals.
Independent first-generation height GWAS establishing the scale of common-variant effects against which the GDF5 effect is compared.

gene_environment_interaction_height.name: Gene-environment interaction in height
gene_environment_interaction_height.summary:
The default expectation - that height heritability should be low in deprived populations because
environmental variance dominates, and should rise as living standards improve - has been tested at
large scale and is not supported. Jelenkovic 2016 pooled 40 twin cohorts with 143,390 complete twin
pairs born between 1886 and 1994 and found adult heritability of 0.69-0.84 in men and 0.53-0.78 in
women with no clear secular pattern across birth-year cohorts; genetic variance did trend upward,
but so did total variance, leaving the ratio flat. Comparing Europe, North America and Australia,
and East Asia, total height variance was greatest in North America and Australia and lowest in East
Asia, yet the heritability proportion was similar across all three. The companion developmental
analysis of 45 twin cohorts (180,520 paired measurements, ages 1-19) locates the environmental
signal where it actually is: shared-environment variance is greatest in early childhood and
persists until early adulthood, while the relative genetic contribution rises with age. A
purpose-built test of the socioeconomic hypothesis reached the same negative conclusion: pooling 29
cohorts and 65,978 twin pairs with parental education data, parental education was positively
associated with offspring height from mid-childhood onward but the genetic and environmental
variance components showed no consistent relation to it, with only a weak meta-regression trend
toward greater shared-environmental variance in low-education families. So the environment shifts
the mean of height strongly and reproducibly, while leaving the variance decomposition close to
unchanged - which is a different statement from 'no gene-environment interaction' but is the one
the data support.

claim_grades.claim: Height heritability does not increase with improving living standards or higher parental education.
claim_grades.basis: 143,390 twin pairs across birth years 1886-1994 and three regions (jelenkovic2016a) plus a purpose-designed 65,978-pair parental-education test (jelenkovic2020), by overlapping but independently analysed designs.

claim_grades.claim: Shared environment contributes most to height variance in early childhood and declines thereafter.
claim_grades.basis: 45-cohort developmental decomposition with 180,520 paired measurements (jelenkovic2016).

gene_environment_interaction_height.human_evidence_note: Three pooled twin analyses covering over 200,000 twin pairs across 20+ countries and a century of birth years.
localization: human: population-level variance decomposition

key_refs.one_line_finding: 143,390 twin pairs born 1886-1994: no secular change in height heritability despite rising genetic variance; heritability proportion similar across three world regions.
Shared-environment variance in height is greatest in early childhood; heritability rises with age to 0.83 (boys) and 0.76 (girls) in adolescence.
29 twin cohorts, 65,978 pairs: parental education raises mean offspring height but the genetic and environmental variance components of height show no consistent relation to it.

genomic_imprinting_growth.name: Genomic imprinting and growth
genomic_imprinting_growth.summary:
A small number of human loci are expressed from only one parental allele, and they are
disproportionately growth-regulating - which is what the parental-conflict hypothesis predicts, and
which gives human genetics a set of natural single-dose experiments no other mechanism supplies.
The two best-characterised clusters both cause reciprocal growth phenotypes. At 11p15.5, loss of
paternal ICR1 methylation reduces IGF2 and causes Silver-Russell syndrome with severe intrauterine
and postnatal growth retardation, while gain of maternal ICR1 methylation causes Beckwith-Wiedemann
overgrowth; disruption of the same region therefore moves growth in opposite directions depending
on which parental allele is affected. At 14q32.2, hypomethylation of the paternal MEG3/DLK1 region
gives Temple syndrome with pre- and postnatal growth failure, while the reciprocal defect gives
Kagami-Ogata syndrome with prenatal overgrowth. Abi Habib 2019 supplied the finding that links the
two clusters mechanistically: 14q32.2 hypomethylation alters expression not only at that locus but
across other imprinted genes, and specifically lowers IGF2 at 11p15.5, producing a shared
transcriptional signature that explains the long-noted clinical overlap between Temple and
Silver-Russell syndromes. Imprinted growth regulation is therefore not a set of independent loci
but a network with IGF2 as a convergence point - a claim made from patient-derived expression
profiling rather than from mouse.

Uniparental disomy is the cleanest arm of this mechanism because total gene dose stays normal and
only parental provenance changes. Ogawa 2025 reported 60 genetically confirmed Temple syndrome
patients - 31 with maternal UPD(14), 22 with an epimutation, 5 with a deletion and 2 undetermined -
and found small for gestational age in 88.3%, postnatal short stature by about age 2 in 87.0% and
central precocious puberty in 86.0%. The growth phenotype is therefore double: a prenatal and early
postnatal deficit followed by a shortened growth window from precocious puberty, so untreated adult
stature is worse than the childhood deficit alone predicts. Growth hormone in 32 patients raised
median height SDS from -3.4 to -2.4 and GnRH analogue therapy in 32 ameliorated the precocious
puberty. Uniparental isodisomy carries a second consequence unrelated to imprinting: it makes any
recessive founder variant on the duplicated chromosome homozygous, producing blended phenotypes
that can be misread as atypical presentations of the imprinting disorder.

claim_grades.claim: Reciprocal methylation defects at imprinted growth loci produce reciprocal growth phenotypes.
claim_grades.basis: Two independent clusters (11p15.5 SRS/BWS, 14q32.2 Temple/Kagami-Ogata) each with reciprocal patient groups and molecular confirmation.

claim_grades.claim: 14q32.2 hypomethylation acts partly by lowering IGF2 at 11p15.5, explaining Temple/Silver-Russell overlap.
claim_grades.basis: Single transcriptional profiling study (abi2019); not independently replicated.

claim_grades.claim: Maternal UPD14 causes pre- and postnatal growth failure plus central precocious puberty in the great majority of patients.
claim_grades.basis: 60 genetically confirmed patients across three distinct molecular mechanisms with concordant phenotypes (ogawa2025).

genomic_imprinting_growth.human_evidence_note: Human patient cohorts with molecularly defined methylation defects and patient-derived expression profiling.
genomic_imprinting_growth.translation_risk_reason: Human imprinting disorders; mouse distal chromosome 7 models are not used to support these claims because parental-transmission phenotypes are known to differ between the species.
localization: human: 11p15.5 (IGF2/H19, CDKN1C/KCNQ1OT1) and 14q32.2 (DLK1/MEG3) imprinted clusters

key_refs.one_line_finding: 14q32.2 hypomethylation deregulates other imprinted genes and lowers IGF2 at 11p15.5, giving Temple and Silver-Russell syndromes a shared transcriptional signature.
60 genetically confirmed Temple syndrome patients: postnatal short stature in 87.0% and central precocious puberty in 86.0%.

ghr_gene.name: GHR
ghr_gene.summary:
GHR is the human experiment that separates growth hormone secretion from growth hormone action.
Godowski 1989 determined the nine-exon coding structure of the receptor gene on chromosome 5 and
showed that two of nine Laron-type dwarfism patients carried a deletion removing a large,
non-consecutive part of the extracellular hormone-binding domain. Amselem 1989 independently
demonstrated linkage of the disease trait to intragenic GHR markers in two consanguineous
Mediterranean families and identified a thymidine-to-cytosine substitution replacing phenylalanine
96 with serine in the extracellular domain, absent from seven unrelated Laron patients of other
population groups - so the disorder is genetically heterogeneous but locus-specific. The
phenotypic consequence of biallelic GHR loss is the largest monogenic stature effect in this
atlas: Laron syndrome patients in the 69-patient Israeli cohort span -4 to -10 height SDS, with
high circulating GH and low IGF-1, retarded bone age and delayed sexual development. Only
homozygotes express the disease. The mechanistic value of GHR is that it fixes the causal
direction of the somatomedin hypothesis in humans: abolishing the receptor while leaving the
ligand elevated produces near-complete growth failure, which no amount of GH can rescue and which
IGF-1 replacement partially does.
ghr_gene.human_evidence_note: Biallelic loss-of-function humans with measured height SDS across a 69-patient cohort followed for over 50 years, plus two independent 1989 gene-level identifications.
ghr_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human genotype-to-stature data; the Ghr-knockout mouse is not used to support any claim here.
localization: human: germline; receptor expressed in liver and in growth plate chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: The human GHR gene has nine coding exons over at least 87 kb of chromosome 5; two of nine Laron patients carry a deletion of the extracellular hormone-binding domain.
Laron dwarfism segregates with intragenic GHR markers and a p.Phe96Ser substitution in the extracellular domain in consanguineous Mediterranean families.
69-patient Laron syndrome cohort followed for over 50 years spans -4 to -10 height SDS with high GH and low IGF-1; only homozygotes express the disease.

hdac4_gene.name: HDAC4
hdac4_gene.summary:
HDAC4 encodes the class IIa histone deacetylase that restrains RUNX2-driven and MEF2C-driven
chondrocyte hypertrophy, and human haploinsufficiency of it defines the skeletal component of 2q37
deletion syndrome. Williams 2010 analysed six individuals with overlapping 2q37.3 deletions to
reduce the critical region from more than 20 candidate genes to HDAC4 alone, then found HDAC4
point lesions - an intragenic deletion disrupting splicing and an intragenic insertion causing a
frameshift and premature stop - in individuals with the same clinical picture but no 2q37 deletion.
That two-step argument (interval narrowing followed by intragenic mutation in deletion-negative
cases) is what establishes HDAC4 as the causal gene rather than a positional bystander. The
skeletal phenotype is brachydactyly type E - shortened metacarpals and metatarsals - together with
short stature, alongside developmental delay, behavioural abnormalities and craniofacial
dysmorphism. Penetrance is markedly incomplete: in 103 individuals with 2q37 deletion the
supposedly cardinal features were present in only a fraction, with brachydactyly type E in 48% and
overweight/obesity in 34%. The mechanistic significance for the growth plate is the direction of
effect: losing a repressor of hypertrophy shortens the digits, which is the phenotype expected if
premature or excessive hypertrophic differentiation exhausts the plate rather than extends it.

claim_grades.claim: HDAC4 haploinsufficiency causes brachydactyly mental retardation syndrome including brachydactyly type E and short stature.
