claim_grades.basis: Critical-region narrowing plus de novo intragenic mutations in deletion-negative cases (williams2010), with a 103-individual genotype-phenotype series (le2019).

claim_grades.claim: HDAC4 dosage sets adult stature quantitatively.
claim_grades.basis: No published mean height SDS for HDAC4-mutation carriers as distinct from whole-2q37-deletion carriers. See gap g_l8gen_008.

hdac4_gene.human_evidence_note: Human deletion mapping plus intragenic mutations in deletion-negative patients, with penetrance quantified in 103 individuals.
hdac4_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human genotype-phenotype only; the Hdac4-null mouse (premature ossification) is cited in hdac4_protein, not here.
localization: human: germline 2q37.3; the deacetylase acts in prehypertrophic chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Six overlapping 2q37.3 deletions narrow the critical region to HDAC4 alone; de novo intragenic HDAC4 mutations are found in deletion-negative patients with the same phenotype.
103 individuals with 2q37 deletion: brachydactyly type E in 48%, obesity 34%, craniofacial dysmorphism 86%; HDAC4 supported as primary contributor with incomplete penetrance.

height_gwas.name: Height GWAS
height_gwas.summary:
Adult height is the canonical polygenic human trait and the first for which
common-variant discovery reached saturation. The largest analysis to date
(Yengo 2022) meta-analysed 5.4 million individuals of diverse ancestries and
resolved 12,111 statistically independent genome-wide-significant SNPs, which
together account for nearly all of the common-SNP-based heritability of height,
meaning further common-variant discovery in this design yields diminishing
returns. Those SNPs are not scattered uniformly: they cluster into 7,209
non-overlapping genomic segments of mean size ~90 kb covering ~21% of the
genome, and association density is elevated near genes with skeletal growth
function. Saturation is ancestry-specific, not universal: the same 12,111 SNPs
explain 40% of phenotypic variance in European-ancestry populations but only
~10-20% in populations of other ancestries, despite similar per-allele effect
sizes and similar prioritized genes. That gap is therefore attributed to
differences in linkage disequilibrium and allele frequency rather than to
different underlying biology, which matters because it makes the
transferability failure a study-design artefact rather than evidence that
height genetics differs between ancestries. This node also carries the two
entities previously stubbed separately as `giant_consortium` and
`polygenic_architecture_height`, which were not distinct objects. GIANT is the
meta-analysis structure that produced this dataset rather than an independent
actor: Yengo 2022 is a GIANT analysis, as was the first-generation 20-locus scan
(Weedon 2008, n=30,147), so the trajectory 20 loci explaining ~3% of variance to
12,111 SNPs explaining ~40% is one consortium's sample-size curve, not the
convergence of independent groups. The "architecture" is the same object measured
here from the other side: extreme polygenicity (7,209 segments over 21% of the
genome), small per-allele effects, and an ancestry-dependent ceiling on prediction.

claim_grades.claim: These 12,111 independent SNPs associate with adult height at the reported effect sizes.
claim_grades.basis: Yengo 2022, n=5.4M. NOT independently replicated by another GWAS - Wood 2014 and Wainschtein 2026 are NESTED inside the same 5.4M sample, so GWAS cannot replicate its own flagship estimate. The legitimate independent test is a DIFFERENT evidence type: out-of-sample polygenic prediction in a non-overlapping cohort. Wang X 2026 supplies one (HCHS/SOL admixed Latinos, European-derived weights, R2 improving ~0.05 with ancestry PCs), which corroborates that the variant effects carry real predictive signal outside the discovery sample.

claim_grades.claim: Height is highly heritable.
claim_grades.basis: Independently corroborated by twin and pedigree designs, which share NO inferential route with GWAS. Dewau 2025 meta-analysis (162,293 twin pairs, 380,195 parent-offspring pairs). This is a genuinely independent replication in the propositional sense - a different study design testing the same proposition.

claim_grades.claim: SNP-based and family-based heritability estimates agree in magnitude.
claim_grades.basis: THEY DO NOT. GREML-LDMS gives 56% (SE 2.3%), inferred true 60-70%; twin designs give ~0.80 in adults and 0.57 (95% CI 0.52-0.61) under age 5. That disagreement IS the missing-heritability problem and is recorded as a contradiction, not resolved into a single number.

claim_grades.claim: The pathways enriched in height GWAS signal are the pathways that mechanistically build the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: Weakest claim on the node and graded lowest. Enrichment is demonstrated (Richard 2025, Darbellay 2024); the variance PARTITION across tissues has never been computed (g_l8gwas_001). And per common_vs_rare_pathway_divergence, 0 of 3 GWAS enrichment lists names the somatotropic axis despite it carrying the largest monogenic stature effects - so GWAS enrichment is NOT a readout of mechanistic importance.

height_gwas.human_evidence_note: Entirely human by construction - a meta-analysis of measured stature in 5.4 million people.
height_gwas.translation_risk_reason: Human observational genetics; no cross-species inference involved. The transferability limit is between human ancestry groups, not between species.
localization: human: germline variation, not tissue-localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: The first-generation GIANT height GWAS found 20 loci explaining ~3% of height variance, implicating hedgehog (IHH, HHIP, PTCH1) and matrix (ACAN, EFEMP1, ADAMTSL3) genes.
12,111 independent SNPs from 5.4M individuals capture nearly all common-SNP heritability of height; variance explained drops from 40% in European to 10-20% in other ancestries.
Out-of-sample height PGS prediction in a non-overlapping admixed Latino cohort - an independent evidence TYPE, not another GWAS.

contradicts: yengo2022 internal discrepancy: the peer-reviewed Nature version states the 7,209 segments have a MEAN size of ~90 kb, whereas the bioRxiv preprint of the same analysis states a MEDIAN of ~90 kb. For a right-skewed size distribution these cannot both be ~90 kb. Logged in audit/contradictions.md; the published value is used here and the discrepancy is flagged rather than silently resolved.

SNP-based (56%, SE 2.3%) versus twin/pedigree (~0.80 adult) heritability estimates disagree in magnitude. This is the missing-heritability problem and is recorded as an open contradiction, not collapsed into a single figure.
aliases: genome-wide association study of adult height

height_heritability.name: Heritability of adult height
height_heritability.summary:
Height is among the most heritable continuous human traits, but the headline
figure of "~80% heritable" conceals real structure in age, ancestry and study
design. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 twin and 26 family studies
(162,293 twin pairs, 380,195 parent-offspring pairs, 19,965 sibling pairs,
birth years 1929-2004) found that twin-based heritability of childhood height
RISES from birth to age 17 rather than being constant, which is consistent with
the progressive expression of growth-regulating alleles across development and
with the diminishing relative weight of intrauterine and early-nutritional
effects. Under age 5 the estimate is 0.57 (95% CI 0.52-0.61) in European-ancestry
samples, 0.48 (0.39-0.57) in Asian-ancestry samples and 0.46 (0.40-0.51) in
multi-ancestry samples, so the commonly quoted adult figure should not be
applied to young children. Molecular estimates converge from below: GREML-LDMS
applied to ~17 million imputed variants in 44,126 unrelated individuals gives
56% (SE 2.3%), and after accounting for imperfect imputation tagging the authors
place true heritability at 60-70%. Twin designs absorb shared-environment and
non-additive variance into the additive term, biasing h2 upward relative to
molecular estimates - the direction of the discrepancy seen between the twin
estimate here (0.57 under age 5) and the molecular one (0.56 tagged).

Two later designs sharpen this. Jelenkovic 2016 pooled 40 twin cohorts and 143,390 complete twin
pairs born 1886-1994 and found adult heritability of 0.69-0.84 in men and 0.53-0.78 in women with
no clear secular pattern: genetic variance trended upward across birth years but heritability did
not, and although total height variance was greatest in North America and Australia and lowest in
East Asia, the heritability proportion was similar across all three regions. That is a direct
refutation, on 143,390 pairs, of the frequently repeated claim that height heritability is lower in
populations with poor living standards and rises as conditions improve. Sidorenko 2024 provides the
non-twin cross-check that the equal-environments assumption cannot contaminate: recombination-rate-
stratified identity-by-descent sharing between 119,000 sibling pairs gives 0.76 +/- 0.05, which
sits inside the twin range and above the GREML-LDMS tagged estimate, exactly as expected if the
molecular estimate is limited by imputation of rare variants.

claim_grades.claim: The narrow-sense heritability of adult height is approximately 0.7-0.8.
claim_grades.basis: Twin pooling across 143,390 pairs (jelenkovic2016a) and an independent sibling IBD estimate 0.76 +/- 0.05 that does not use the equal-environments assumption (sidorenko2024).

claim_grades.claim: Height heritability rises from birth through adolescence rather than being constant.
claim_grades.basis: Meta-analysis of 28 twin and 26 family studies (dewau2025) and pooled analysis of 45 twin cohorts with 180,520 paired measurements (jelenkovic2016), by independent groups and designs.

claim_grades.claim: Height heritability does not increase as living standards improve.
claim_grades.basis: 143,390 twin pairs across birth years 1886-1994 and three geographic-cultural regions show no secular pattern (jelenkovic2016a).

height_heritability.human_evidence_note: Twin, family and molecular-genetic variance decomposition in humans; over 560,000 relative pairs in the meta-analysis alone.
height_heritability.translation_risk_reason: Heritability is a population-specific human parameter by definition.
localization: human: population-level variance decomposition, not tissue-localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: Heritability of childhood height rises from birth to 17 years and differs by ancestry; under-5 h2 is 0.57 (European), 0.48 (Asian), 0.46 (multi-ancestry).
GREML-LDMS on ~17M imputed variants explains 56% (SE 2.3%) of height variance; true h2 likely 60-70%, so missing heritability is small.
Pooled 45 twin cohorts: shared-environment variance is greatest in early childhood and heritability peaks in adolescence at 0.83 (boys) and 0.76 (girls).
143,390 twin pairs born 1886-1994 show adult height heritability 0.69-0.84 (men) and 0.53-0.78 (women) with no secular trend across birth cohorts or regions.
Recombination-stratified sibling IBD gives an unbiased height heritability of 0.76 +/- 0.05.

height_polygenic_score.name: Height polygenic score
height_polygenic_score.summary:
A height polygenic score sums allele dosages weighted by GWAS effect sizes and is the best-performing
polygenic predictor of any human quantitative trait, which makes it the ceiling case for what
polygenic prediction can do. Yengo 2022 reported that the 12,111 genome-wide-significant SNPs
account for 40% of phenotypic variance in European-ancestry out-of-sample prediction, rising to 45%
using all HapMap 3 SNPs, and falling to about 10-20% (14-24% with all HapMap 3 SNPs) in populations
of other ancestries. Depope 2026 reached a comparable ceiling by a different route, jointly
modelling tens of millions of UK Biobank whole-genome-sequence variants with approximate message
passing and obtaining about 46% prediction accuracy for height. Against a narrow-sense heritability
of about 0.76, a 40-46% predictor captures roughly 55-60% of the genetic variance and essentially
all of the common-variant component - the residual is the rare and non-coding tier that
Wainschtein 2026 quantifies at 20% of pedigree heritability. Two limits are structural rather than
technical. First, prediction accuracy is not transferable across ancestries because it depends on
linkage disequilibrium and allele frequency in the training population, not because the biology
differs. Second, a score trained in a population with assortative mating carries inflated effect
estimates, since assortment raises the genetic variance of the trait and induces correlations
between causal alleles.

The transferability limit deserves its own statement because the same paper that measures the loss
also tests the two candidate explanations. Yengo 2022 found that per-allele effect sizes, associated
regions and prioritised genes were similar across ancestries even as prediction accuracy fell,
which excludes the interpretation that height has a different genetic basis in different
populations and localises the failure to linkage disequilibrium and allele frequency differences
within associated regions - a property of the marker panel, not of the biology. Graff 2021 supports
this from the other direction: in an African-ancestry meta-analysis of 52,764 individuals, 643 of
802 known European height signals were directionally consistent and 205 were nominally significant,
and only 2 of 20 newly identified secondary signals had minor allele frequency below 5%. The
consequence for the rest of the atlas is that any claim of the form 'this locus explains X% of
height' is a claim about a population and a marker panel, and none of the growth-plate mechanism
nodes inherits an ancestry qualifier from it.

claim_grades.claim: A height polygenic score explains about 40-46% of phenotypic variance in the population it was trained in.
claim_grades.basis: Out-of-sample prediction in yengo2022 (40%, 12,111 SNPs) and an independent method on WGS data (depope2026, ~46%).

claim_grades.claim: Height PGS accuracy falls by roughly half to three quarters outside the training ancestry.
claim_grades.basis: Measured out of sample in yengo2022 and corroborated by partial signal transfer in graff2021.

claim_grades.claim: The transferability loss is caused by linkage disequilibrium and allele frequency differences rather than different underlying biology.
claim_grades.basis: Supported by similar per-allele effect sizes and gene prioritisation across ancestries within yengo2022 and 643/802 directional concordance in graff2021, but not established by a purpose-designed decomposition.

height_polygenic_score.human_evidence_note: Out-of-sample prediction accuracy measured against observed stature in independent human cohorts.
localization: human: germline genome-wide; a statistical construct, not tissue-localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: Height PGS explains 40% of variance in European-ancestry and 10-20% in other-ancestry populations out of sample.
Joint WGS modelling by approximate message passing reaches ~46% prediction accuracy for height.
Height heritability 0.76 +/- 0.05 provides the benchmark against which PGS accuracy is judged.
Assortative mating raises trait genetic variance and similarity between relatives, biasing PGS-derived estimates trained in assorting populations.
643 of 802 European height signals are directionally consistent in 52,764 African-ancestry individuals; 205 nominally significant.

hmga2_gene.name: HMGA2
hmga2_gene.summary: HMGA2 was the first common variant reproducibly associated with normal human height and remains the cleanest example of the effect size the common-variant regime actually delivers. Weedon 2007 found rs1042725 in 4,921 individuals, replicated it in 19,064 adults from four further studies (overall P = 4e-16), and confirmed it in 6,827 children and a tall/short case-control sample: the C allele adds approximately 0.4 cm of adult height and the variant explains about 0.3% of population height variance. That is the scale at which the polygenic architecture operates - about 1/25th of the effect of a rare coding variant of the kind catalogued in this layer, and it took ~30,000 individuals to establish. HMGA2 is also a strong biological candidate rather than a statistical accident, because severe rare lesions in the gene alter body size in both mouse and human, and rare aggregate variation proximal to the related HMGA1 locus is worth ~5 cm in whole-genome sequencing. The gene reappears in the rare-disease direction as a cause of Silver-Russell syndrome, so HMGA2 spans the full allelic spectrum from a 0.4 cm common variant to a syndromic growth disorder - which is the argument that the common/rare divide in height genetics is one of allele frequency, not of biology. What HMGA2 does not yet have in this atlas is a growth plate mechanism: no human growth-plate localization or chondrocyte-level function was retrieved.

claim_grades.claim: rs1042725 near HMGA2 raises adult height by ~0.4 cm per allele.
claim_grades.basis: Discovery plus four independent replications and a childhood sample (weedon2007).

claim_grades.claim: HMGA2 exerts this effect through the growth plate chondrocyte.
claim_grades.basis: No growth-plate expression, eQTL or functional data for HMGA2 were retrieved.

hmga2_gene.human_evidence_note: Discovery and replication in ~31,000 humans with measured adult height plus 6,827 children.
hmga2_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human association genetics; the mouse body-size data are cited only as candidate-gene support.
localization: human: germline; no growth plate expression or chondrocyte function data retrieved

key_refs.one_line_finding: rs1042725 near HMGA2 is the first reproducibly replicated common height variant, worth ~0.4 cm per allele and ~0.3% of height variance.
Rare aggregate non-coding variation proximal to the related HMGA1 locus is associated with 5 cm taller height, showing the same gene family spans the frequency spectrum.

igf1_gene.name: IGF1
igf1_gene.summary:
IGF1 supplies the human null experiment that the GH receptor cannot: Woods 1996 described a patient
with a homozygous partial deletion of the IGF1 gene presenting with intrauterine growth
retardation followed by continued postnatal growth failure, together with sensorineural deafness
and mental retardation. The combination is what makes the locus informative. Growth hormone
deficiency and GH receptor deficiency both spare prenatal growth, because fetal growth is largely
GH-independent, whereas IGF1 deletion impairs growth from before birth - so the IGF1 gene sits
downstream of the point at which the somatotropic axis becomes GH-dependent, and IGF-1 itself is
required in both epochs. The extra-skeletal features (deafness, cognitive impairment) establish
that IGF-1 action is not confined to the growth plate, which is a constraint on any therapeutic
strategy that raises systemic IGF-1 to gain stature. On the common-variation side of the same
locus, Mendelian randomisation now shows the relationship is continuous rather than confined to
null alleles: instrumenting serum IGF-1 with UK Biobank variants and testing against GIANT height
gives 0.09 SD taller adult height per 1 SD higher IGF-1, an effect that persists after adjustment
for childhood BMI and is reproduced by an IGF-1 genetic risk score against measured heights at ages
7-17 in ALSPAC. The gap between a catastrophic null phenotype and a 0.09 SD per SD population slope
is the quantitative statement of how strongly buffered this axis is.

claim_grades.claim: Homozygous IGF1 deletion causes combined pre- and postnatal growth failure with deafness and cognitive impairment.
claim_grades.basis: Single patient (woods1996); later IGF1 point-mutation patients exist but were not independently verified in this sweep.

claim_grades.claim: Higher circulating IGF-1 causally increases adult height by about 0.09 SD per SD.
claim_grades.basis: Two-sample MR in >1.1M individuals with an independent longitudinal replication in ALSPAC (de2026).

igf1_gene.human_evidence_note: One homozygous human deletion patient plus a large-scale Mendelian randomization estimate of the continuous IGF-1 to height slope.
igf1_gene.translation_risk_reason: Both the null phenotype and the population slope are measured in humans.
localization: human: germline; IGF-1 produced systemically by liver and locally within the growth plate

key_refs.one_line_finding: Homozygous partial deletion of IGF1 causes intrauterine growth retardation with postnatal growth failure, deafness and mental retardation.
Mendelian randomization gives 0.09 SD taller adult height per 1 SD higher serum IGF-1, replicated against measured heights at ages 7-17 in ALSPAC.

igf1r_gene.name: IGF1R
igf1r_gene.summary:
IGF1R is the receptor-side counterpart to IGF1 and is the locus that explains a specific clinical
puzzle: children born small for gestational age who fail to catch up and whose serum IGF-1 is
normal or high rather than low. Abuzzahab 2003 screened 42 patients with unexplained intrauterine
growth retardation and persistent short stature plus a second cohort of 50 short children with
elevated circulating IGF-1, and found a girl who was a compound heterozygote for two exon-2 point
mutations (Arg108Gln and Lys115Asn) whose fibroblasts showed decreased IGF-I binding, establishing
partial IGF1R loss of function as a cause of combined prenatal and postnatal growth failure. The
receptor is haploinsufficiency-sensitive: heterozygous nonsense and deletion alleles are now
recurrently reported in severe short stature with poor growth hormone response, because the defect
is downstream of the ligand that GH raises. The signature - low birth size, no catch-up, normal or
raised IGF-1, blunted rhGH response - is the mirror image of the GHR/Laron signature (normal birth
size, high GH, low IGF-1). Together IGF1, IGF1R and GHR partition the somatotropic axis into
prenatal-competent and prenatal-independent segments using nothing but human alleles. The
quantitative weakness is that no adequately powered genotype-defined IGF1R cohort with mean adult
height SDS was reached in this sweep.
igf1r_gene.human_evidence_note: Human compound-heterozygote patient with fibroblast binding assay; the phenotype has been recurrently reported since.
igf1r_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human alleles with patient-derived fibroblast assays.
localization: human: germline; receptor expressed in growth plate chondrocytes and near-ubiquitously

key_refs.one_line_finding: IGF1R compound-heterozygous exon-2 mutations reduce IGF-I binding in patient fibroblasts and cause intrauterine plus postnatal growth retardation.
Mendelian randomization of the IGF-1 axis gives 0.09 SD taller adult height per 1 SD higher serum IGF-1.

igf2_h19_imprinting.name: IGF2/H19 imprinted locus
igf2_h19_imprinting.summary:
The IGF2/H19 domain at 11p15.5 is controlled by imprinting control region 1, which is methylated on
the paternal allele and unmethylated on the maternal one, and its disruption produces the two
reciprocal human growth syndromes that bracket normal stature. Paternal ICR1 loss of methylation
silences IGF2 and accounts for roughly 60% of Silver-Russell syndrome, characterised by severe
intrauterine and postnatal growth retardation. Maternal ICR1 hypermethylation activates IGF2 on
both alleles and causes about 10% of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, characterised by overgrowth. The
lesions are structurally reciprocal at the same 1.5 kb element, so the locus behaves as a
continuous human IGF2 dose rheostat rather than a binary disease gene. Two mechanistic details are
established in patient material rather than inferred. First, microdeletions of the CTCF-binding
repeats within ICR1 and point mutations in an OCT-binding motif can each cause the hypermethylated
BWS state in a maternally inherited, familial pattern, which localises the control to specific
transcription-factor footprints. Second, Abi Habib 2019 showed that IGF2 at this locus is
downregulated by hypomethylation at an entirely different imprinted domain on chromosome 14,
placing IGF2 downstream of a wider imprinting network. Because IGF2 acts principally on prenatal
growth, the postnatal stature deficit in Silver-Russell is not fully explained by IGF2 dose alone.

claim_grades.claim: Reciprocal ICR1 methylation defects cause reciprocal growth phenotypes through IGF2 dosage.
claim_grades.basis: Two large reciprocal patient groups (SRS and BWS) with allele-specific methylation and IGF2 expression data; established across many independent diagnostic series.

claim_grades.claim: IGF2 dosage at this locus is regulated in trans by imprinting status at 14q32.2.
claim_grades.basis: Single expression-profiling study (abi2019).

igf2_h19_imprinting.human_evidence_note: Human imprinting disorder cohorts with allele-specific methylation analysis and patient-derived expression profiling.
igf2_h19_imprinting.translation_risk_reason: Human imprinting; the mouse distal-7 orthologue shows contradictory parental-transmission phenotypes for some models and is deliberately not invoked.
localization: human: 11p15.5; IGF2 expressed from the paternal allele, H19 from the maternal allele

key_refs.one_line_finding: 14q32.2 hypomethylation lowers IGF2 expression at the 11p15.5 domain, and paternal ICR1 loss of methylation accounts for ~60% of Silver-Russell syndrome.
Temple syndrome (the 14q32.2 counterpart) causes postnatal short stature in 87.0% of 60 genetically confirmed patients.

igfals_gene.name: IGFALS
igfals_gene.summary:
IGFALS encodes the acid-labile subunit that, with IGFBP-3 or IGFBP-5, forms the 150 kDa ternary
complex holding IGF-1 and IGF-2 in circulation. Domene 2004 identified the first inactivating
IGFALS mutation and showed that it collapses the whole circulating IGF system. The subsequent
14-mutation, 17-patient review (Domene 2009) gives the number that matters for this atlas: despite
extraordinarily low serum IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 that fail to rise on GH stimulation, prepubertal height
SDS was typically only between -2 and -3, about 1.4 SD below midparental height SDS. That is a
remarkably mild stature phenotype for a near-total loss of circulating IGF-1 carriage, and it is
the strongest human argument in the atlas that the growth plate is driven principally by locally
produced or locally bioavailable IGF-1 rather than by the size of the circulating reservoir.
Pubertal delay occurred in half of patients and insulin insensitivity was common, so the complex is
not functionally inert. IGFALS therefore functions as a dosage control that dissociates circulating
IGF-1 concentration from linear growth - the same dissociation PAPPA2 makes from the opposite
direction, by trapping IGF-1 in an intact complex.

claim_grades.claim: IGFALS inactivation collapses the circulating IGF ternary complex.
claim_grades.basis: Original inactivating mutation with biochemistry (domen2004) and 17 patients with concordant IGF-1/IGFBP-3/ALS profiles (domen2009).

claim_grades.claim: The stature cost of that collapse is only about -1.4 SDS relative to midparental height.
claim_grades.basis: One aggregated patient series (domen2009); the estimate has not been reproduced in an independent cohort.

igfals_gene.human_evidence_note: 17 human patients with 14 distinct mutations, measured heights and full IGF-axis biochemistry.
localization: human: germline; ALS protein is hepatically produced and circulates

key_refs.one_line_finding: Inactivation of the IGFALS gene produces a deficiency of the entire circulating insulin-like growth factor system.
17 ALS-deficient patients with 14 mutations: prepubertal height SDS -2 to -3, about 1.4 SD below midparental height, with pubertal delay in 50%.

ihh_gene.name: IHH
ihh_gene.summary:
IHH gives a three-level human dose series with an unusually informative middle. Gao 2001 showed
that heterozygous missense mutations in the amino-terminal signalling domain cause brachydactyly
type A-1, shortening or loss of the middle phalanges, with three mutations in three large families
all altering residues predicted to lie adjacent on the IHH surface - a gain-of-abnormal-function or
altered-ligand-range mechanism rather than simple dosage reduction. Hellemans 2003 showed that
homozygous IHH mutations cause acrocapitofemoral dysplasia, an autosomal recessive disorder with
cone-shaped epiphyses in hands and hips - biallelic loss gives a generalised, not digit-restricted,
epiphyseal disorder. Sentchordi-Montane 2020 then characterised 16 probands with heterozygous IHH
variants including the first complete IHH deletion and found that none showed classical
brachydactyly A-1; the commonest presentation was mild-to-moderate short stature with shortening of
the fifth-finger middle phalanx, and two short probands had no radiological hand anomaly at all
while five carriers of normal height did. Heterozygous IHH loss is therefore a
variably-penetrant short-stature allele rather than a brachydactyly allele, and the BDA-1 missense
class must be mechanistically distinct from haploinsufficiency. In unselected idiopathic short
stature IHH is the commonest single finding on growth-plate gene panels: 4 of 102 in Andrade 2022,
ahead of SHOX.

claim_grades.claim: Heterozygous IHH loss of function causes mild-to-moderate short stature with incomplete penetrance.
claim_grades.basis: 16-proband cosegregating series (sentchordimont2020) plus independent panel yield in an unselected ISS cohort (andrade2022).

claim_grades.claim: BDA-1 missense alleles act by a mechanism other than reduced IHH dosage.
claim_grades.basis: Inferred from the phenotypic non-overlap between gao2001 missense families and haploinsufficient carriers; not directly tested by an allele-matched functional comparison.

ihh_gene.human_evidence_note: Heterozygous, homozygous and null alleles all characterised in humans with measured stature and hand radiology.
ihh_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human allelic series only; the extensive murine Ihh literature is held in ihh_protein.
localization: human: germline; ligand produced by prehypertrophic chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: Three heterozygous missense mutations in the IHH N-terminal signalling domain cause brachydactyly type A-1 in three large families.
Homozygous IHH mutations cause acrocapitofemoral dysplasia with cone-shaped epiphyses of hands and hips.
16 heterozygous IHH probands show mild-moderate short stature and fifth-finger changes but no classical brachydactyly A-1; five carriers of normal height.
IHH is the commonest gene found (4/102) on a growth-plate panel in children classified as idiopathic short stature.

mendelian_randomization_height.name: Mendelian randomization using height
mendelian_randomization_height.summary:
Height is the workhorse exposure and outcome for Mendelian randomization because it has thousands of
strong instruments, is measured without error, and cannot be reverse-caused by most outcomes of
interest. Two uses matter for this atlas. Used as an outcome, MR converts endocrine correlations
into causal slopes: De La Barrera 2026 instrumented serum IGF-1 with UK Biobank variants and tested
against GIANT height excluding UK Biobank (non-Hispanic White n=1,176,465, plus African descent
168,191, South Asian 49,032, East Asian 361,369 and Hispanic 58,709), obtaining 0.09 SD taller
adult height per 1 SD higher IGF-1 by inverse-variance weighting, persisting after adjustment for
childhood BMI and replicated longitudinally against measured heights at ages 7-17 in ALSPAC. That
number puts a hard ceiling on how much of normal stature variation the IGF-1 axis explains, and it
sits alongside the Laron and IGFALS phenotypes as the population-scale version of the same axis.
Used as an exposure, height MR consistently estimates effects on cardiovascular and other outcomes,
but those analyses are outside this atlas's scope. The methodological caveat that matters here is
that assortative mating for height induces correlations between causal alleles and inflates genetic
variance, which biases MR estimates that use height instruments unless family-based designs are
used - a caveat that applies specifically and strongly to this trait.

claim_grades.claim: Higher circulating IGF-1 causally increases adult height by about 0.09 SD per SD.
claim_grades.basis: Two-sample MR in >1.8M individuals with an independent ALSPAC longitudinal replication using both measured IGF-1 and an IGF-1 genetic risk score (de2026).

claim_grades.claim: Height MR estimates are unbiased in populations with assortative mating.
claim_grades.basis: Not supported. Assortative mating induces gametic-phase correlations between causal alleles (sunde2024), which biases population-based MR using height instruments; family-based designs are required.

mendelian_randomization_height.human_evidence_note: Human genetic instruments against measured human stature, with a longitudinal cohort replication.
localization: human: population-level instrumental-variable analysis

key_refs.one_line_finding: MR gives 0.09 SD taller adult height per 1 SD higher serum IGF-1, replicated against repeated height measurements at ages 7-17 in ALSPAC.
Assortative mating increases trait-specific genetic variance and genetic similarity between relatives, a source of bias for height-instrument designs.
Supplies the instrument set: 12,111 conditionally independent height SNPs from 5.4M individuals.

missing_heritability_height.name: Missing heritability of height
missing_heritability_height.summary:
"Missing heritability" named the early-GWAS gap between family-based
heritability estimates (~80%) and the variance captured by genome-wide
significant SNPs (a few percent in the first height GWAS). For height the gap
has since largely closed, and it closed for methodological rather than
biological reasons. Yang 2015 showed with GREML-LDMS on ~17 million imputed
variants in 44,126 unrelated individuals that 56% (SE 2.3%) of height variance
is tagged once variants are stratified by linkage-disequilibrium and minor
allele frequency, and argued true heritability is 60-70% - so the residual gap
against family estimates is small and is plausibly explained by imperfect
imputation of rare variants plus overestimation in family designs. Yengo 2022
closed the discovery side by resolving 12,111 independent SNPs capturing nearly
all common-SNP heritability. Height is therefore the trait where the missing
heritability problem was effectively solved, which makes it the reference case
against which other traits are judged. The residuum that remains is
concentrated in rare and structural variation and in the fact that
heritability estimated in one population does not transfer to another.

Wainschtein 2026 closed the remaining accounting. Whole-genome sequencing of 347,630
European-ancestry UK Biobank participants, covering 40 million single-nucleotide and short indel
variants with MAF above 0.01%, captures on average about 88% of pedigree-based narrow-sense
heritability across 34 complex traits: 68% from common variants (MAF >= 1%) and 20% from rare
variants, with 79% of the rare-variant component sitting in non-coding rather than coding sequence.
Fifteen of the 34 traits showed no significant difference between WGS-based and pedigree-based
estimates at all. The gap that motivated a decade of theorising about epistasis and gene-environment
interaction was therefore mostly rare, mostly regulatory variation that genotyping arrays never
assayed - not a failure of the additive model. One residual is now well characterised rather than
merely absent: Sidorenko 2024 shows sibling linkage signals colocalise with GWAS loci and that the
heritability still unaccounted for by GWAS-identified variants is polygenic and enriched near those
same loci, implying allelic heterogeneity at known loci rather than undiscovered biology.

claim_grades.claim: The missing heritability of height is largely accounted for by rare and non-coding variation not assayed on genotyping arrays.
claim_grades.basis: One very large WGS variance partition (wainschtein2026) plus concordant discovery of large-effect rare non-coding signals (hawkes2024); the 88% figure is a cross-trait average not independently replicated at that precision.

claim_grades.claim: Common SNP discovery for height is saturated.
claim_grades.basis: 12,111 independent SNPs capture nearly all common-SNP heritability in 5.4M individuals (yengo2022), consistent with the 68% common-variant share measured by WGS (wainschtein2026).

missing_heritability_height.human_evidence_note: Human molecular and family-based variance decomposition; the entire question is a human-population one.
missing_heritability_height.translation_risk_reason: Population-genetic parameter specific to human cohorts.
localization: human: population-level, not tissue-localized

key_refs.one_line_finding: Stratifying imputed variants by LD and MAF recovers 56% of height variance, leaving negligible missing heritability.
12,111 independent SNPs account for nearly all common-SNP heritability, closing the discovery side of the gap.
WGS in 347,630 individuals captures ~88% of pedigree heritability across 34 traits: 68% common, 20% rare, with 79% of the rare component non-coding.
Residual heritability not captured by GWAS-identified loci is polygenic and enriched near those same loci, indicating allelic heterogeneity rather than unknown biology.
29 independent rare non-coding height signals with effects from -7 cm to +4.7 cm demonstrate that the missing component is reachable by sequencing.

nppc_gene.name: NPPC
nppc_gene.summary:
NPPC encodes the CNP precursor and is the ligand-side member of the CNP/NPR2 dose axis, so its
human allelic series is the mirror image of NPR2's. Overexpression comes first historically:
Bocciardi 2007 characterised a de novo balanced t(2;7)(q37.1;q21.3) in a girl with Marfanoid
habitus and skeletal overgrowth, with the chromosome 2 breakpoint near NPPC, plasma CNP doubled
relative to five controls, and NPPC substantially overexpressed in her fibroblasts. Moncla 2007
then found two further patients with balanced translocations breaking in the same 2q37.1 band
(involving chromosomes 8 and 13), the same overgrowth phenotype and the same NPPC overexpression,
and proposed that the breakpoints separate NPPC from a negative regulatory element on chromosome 2
- a mutational mechanism defined by three independent chromosomal partners converging on one gene.
Loss of function was found much later: Hisado-Oliva 2018 screened 668 patients (357 with
disproportionate short stature, 311 with autosomal dominant idiopathic short stature) plus 29 ISS
families and identified two heterozygous NPPC mutations, both in the highly conserved CNP ring,
both giving significant reductions in cGMP synthesis, cosegregating with short stature and small
hands. One of the two alleles corresponds to the spontaneous mouse lbab long-bone-abnormality
mutation. The gene is therefore bidirectionally validated in humans, but the loss-of-function arm
rests on two families and yields no published effect size in SDS, which is the main quantitative
hole on this node.

claim_grades.claim: Increased NPPC expression causes human skeletal overgrowth.
claim_grades.basis: Three independent patients with different translocation partners, each with measured NPPC overexpression (bocciardi2007, moncla2007).

claim_grades.claim: Heterozygous NPPC loss of function causes autosomal dominant short stature.
claim_grades.basis: Two mutations in one screening study with in vitro cGMP confirmation and cosegregation; no independent replication cohort and no reported SDS effect size.

nppc_gene.human_evidence_note: Overgrowth from NPPC overexpression is documented in three independent translocation patients; loss of function is documented in two families with functional cGMP assays.
nppc_gene.translation_risk_reason: Stature claims rest entirely on measured human phenotypes; the mouse lbab allele is cited only as convergent support for pathogenicity of one variant.
localization: human: germline; ligand acts on NPR2 in growth plate cartilage

key_refs.one_line_finding: Balanced t(2;7) near NPPC gives skeletal overgrowth with plasma CNP doubled versus five controls and NPPC overexpressed in fibroblasts.
Two further 2q37.1 translocation patients (partners chr8, chr13) show the same NPPC overexpression and overgrowth phenotype.
Two heterozygous NPPC CNP-ring mutations reduce cGMP synthesis and cause autosomal dominant short stature with small hands.

npr2_gene.name: NPR2
npr2_gene.summary:
NPR2 encodes the transmembrane guanylyl cyclase that converts GTP to cGMP on binding C-type
natriuretic peptide, and it is the best human dosage series in the whole growth-plate atlas
because both directions of the dose axis have been measured. Bartels 2004 sequenced 21 families
with acromesomelic dysplasia type Maroteaux and found 21 NPR2 mutations (4 nonsense, 4 frameshift,
2 splice-site, 11 missense), with three tested missense alleles showing markedly deficient
guanylyl cyclase activity - biallelic loss gives severe acromesomelic dwarfism. The same paper
noted that obligate heterozygous carriers were below the matched-control mean. Olney 2006
quantified that: in a 39-member AMDM family the 16 NPR2 mutation carriers had height z-score
-1.8 +/- 1.1 versus -0.4 +/- 0.8 in 23 non-carriers (P < 0.0005), with no difference in body
proportion. Vasques 2013 found three novel heterozygous NPR2 mutations in 47 idiopathic
short-stature probands, all three failing to produce cGMP on CNP stimulation and showing a
dominant-negative reduction when co-transfected 1:1 with wild type. Hisado-Oliva 2015 screened 173
suspected Leri-Weill and 95 ISS cases negative for SHOX and found pathogenic NPR2 alleles in ~3% of
the dyschondrosteosis referral group. Gain of function runs the other way: Miura 2012 reported
p.Val883Met producing ligand-independent cGMP and tall stature with macrodactyly across three
generations, and Hannema 2013 reported p.Arg655Cys in the kinase homology domain giving extreme
tall stature with no skeletal deformity. Loss and gain of the same cyclase therefore move human
stature in opposite directions, which is as close to a controlled human dose experiment as this
field gets.

claim_grades.claim: Reduced NPR2 gene dosage lowers human adult stature and increased signalling raises it.
claim_grades.basis: Loss-of-function height z-scores measured in a controlled family design (olney2006) plus independent gain-of-function pedigrees (miura2012, hannema2013).

claim_grades.claim: The heterozygous effect size is about -1.4 SDS relative to non-carriers.
claim_grades.basis: Single family (olney2006, 16 vs 23); not replicated at that precision in an independent cohort.

npr2_gene.human_evidence_note: Human genotype-stature data at three dose levels (biallelic LoF, monoallelic LoF, GoF), each with an independent cohort and in vitro cyclase confirmation.
npr2_gene.translation_risk_reason: All stature claims rest on measured human height; the mouse Npr2 literature is cited only in the protein node npr2_receptor.
localization: human: germline; effector receptor localizes to growth plate chondrocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: 21 NPR2 mutations across 21 AMDM families; tested missense alleles show markedly deficient guanylyl cyclase activity and obligate carriers are below control mean height.
16 heterozygous NPR2 carriers had height z -1.8 +/- 1.1 versus -0.4 +/- 0.8 in 23 non-carriers within one family (P < 0.0005).
Three novel heterozygous NPR2 mutations in 47 ISS probands, all abolishing CNP-stimulated cGMP and reducing wild-type activity when co-expressed.
Pathogenic NPR2 alleles in ~3% of SHOX-negative Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis referrals (n=173).
NPR2 p.Val883Met is constitutively active, raises blood cGMP and causes three-generation tall stature with macrodactyly.
NPR2 p.Arg655Cys in the kinase homology domain markedly increases CNP-stimulated cGMP and causes extreme tall stature without skeletal deformity.

omnigenic_model.name: Omnigenic model
omnigenic_model.summary:
Boyle 2017 proposed that for complex traits, association signal is spread across most of the genome
- including near many genes with no obvious connection to the trait - because gene regulatory
networks are sufficiently interconnected that any gene expressed in a trait-relevant cell can
affect the function of core trait genes, and that most heritability is explained by effects on
genes outside core pathways. Height is the trait the argument was built on and the trait where it
is most testable. The supporting observations from this atlas are quantitative and independent of
the model's authors: Yengo 2022 found 12,111 independent height SNPs clustered in 7,209 segments
covering about 21% of the genome; the per-allele effect of GDF5-UQCC, a bona fide skeletal
developmental locus, is 0.44 cm, statistically indistinguishable from the 0.4 cm of HMGA2 and no
larger than that of loci with no known skeletal function; and Wood 2014 needed 697 variants to
reach one fifth of heritability while all common variants together captured 60%. Against a strict
core-gene reading, Marouli 2017's 83 rare coding variants of up to 2 cm are concentrated in genes
that are also mutated in monogenic growth disorders, so the effect-size tail does respect a core
gene set even while the common-variant bulk does not. The model is a hypothesis node in this atlas
and is graded as one: the observation that signal is diffuse is A-grade, the mechanistic claim that
diffuseness arises through regulatory-network propagation to core genes has not been directly
tested in any growth-plate system.

claim_grades.claim: Height association signal is spread across a large fraction of the genome rather than confined to skeletal pathways.
claim_grades.basis: 12,111 independent SNPs across 21% of the genome in 5.4M people (yengo2022) and the 697-variant/60% split (wood2014).

claim_grades.claim: Peripheral genes affect height by propagating through regulatory networks onto core growth-plate genes.
claim_grades.basis: The mechanistic core of the model; not tested in chondrocytes or any growth-plate system. Flagged as inference.

claim_grades.claim: Large-effect variants are concentrated in a core gene set even though common-variant signal is not.
claim_grades.basis: 83 rare coding variants of up to 2 cm overlap monogenic growth-disorder genes (marouli2017); a single analysis, but internally consistent with the monogenic literature in this layer.

omnigenic_model.human_evidence_note: The model is an interpretation of human GWAS architecture; the diffuseness observation is direct human data, the network-propagation mechanism is not directly measured.
omnigenic_model.translation_risk_reason: A statement about human genetic architecture; no animal inference.
localization: human: genome-wide; no tissue localization is claimed

key_refs.one_line_finding: Proposes that interconnected regulatory networks let all genes expressed in trait-relevant cells affect core genes, so most heritability lies outside core pathways.
12,111 independent height SNPs cluster in 7,209 segments covering ~21% of the genome.
697 variants explain one fifth of height heritability while all common variants capture 60%.
Rare coding variants of up to 2 cm per allele overlap genes mutated in monogenic growth disorders.

pappa2_gene.name: PAPPA2
pappa2_gene.summary:
PAPPA2 encodes the metalloproteinase that liberates IGF-1 from IGFBP-3 and IGFBP-5, and its human
loss-of-function phenotype is the cleanest available demonstration that free rather than total
IGF-1 drives growth. Dauber 2016 found two different homozygous PAPPA2 mutations, p.D643fs25* and
p.Ala1033Val, in multiple members of two unrelated families with progressive growth failure,
moderate microcephaly, thin long bones and mildly decreased bone density. The biochemical signature
is inverted relative to every other short-stature endocrinopathy: circulating total IGF-1, IGFBP-3,
IGFBP-5, acid-labile subunit and IGF-II were all elevated, not reduced. In vitro both mutations
abolished PAPP-A2 proteolytic activity entirely, size-exclusion chromatography showed a significant
increase in IGF-1 held within the ternary complex, and free IGF-1 concentrations were decreased.
The gene therefore separates two quantities that are normally measured as one: total IGF-1 goes up
while the growth-relevant fraction goes down, and the child gets shorter. Any clinical inference
that reads total serum IGF-1 as a proxy for IGF-1 action is falsified by this locus. Its
therapeutic corollary - that recombinant IGF-1 bypasses the block - has been tested in these
patients, and PAPPA2 deficiency now sits in the growth-plate basket of the vosoritide RASopathy
trial programme alongside ACAN and NPR2.

claim_grades.claim: Loss of PAPP-A2 proteolytic activity causes short stature despite elevated total IGF-1.
claim_grades.basis: Two unrelated families with independent mutations and concordant inverted biochemistry (dauber2016).

claim_grades.claim: The proximate cause of the growth failure is reduced free IGF-1 rather than another PAPP-A2 substrate.
claim_grades.basis: Supported by the chromatography and free-IGF-1 measurements in dauber2016 but not tested against an alternative-substrate hypothesis; single study.

pappa2_gene.human_evidence_note: Two unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous mutations, full IGF-axis biochemistry and matched in vitro proteolysis assays.
pappa2_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human loss-of-function families with human-protein enzymology.
localization: human: germline; protease acts in the circulation and in the pericellular space

key_refs.one_line_finding: Two homozygous PAPPA2 mutations abolish IGFBP proteolysis, raising total but lowering free IGF-1 and causing progressive growth failure in two unrelated families.
Vosoritide basket trial enrolling children with ACAN and NPR2 deficiency and RASopathies, the therapeutic context in which these growth-plate genotypes are now grouped.

pth1r_gene.name: PTH1R
pth1r_gene.summary:
PTH1R is a bidirectional human dose experiment on the PTHrP-IHH feedback loop that sets the pace of
chondrocyte hypertrophy. Schipani 1995 identified a heterozygous His223Arg substitution in the
first intracellular loop in Jansen-type metaphyseal chondrodysplasia and showed it produces
constitutive, ligand-independent cAMP accumulation in COS-7 cells - a gain-of-function receptor
that delays hypertrophic differentiation and gives short-limbed dwarfism with ligand-independent
hypercalcaemia and hypophosphataemia. Jobert 1998 supplied the opposite pole: in Blomstrand
chondrodysplasia the patient was heterozygous for a maternally inherited point mutation creating a
novel splice site that deletes 11 amino acids of the fifth transmembrane domain; the mutant
receptor was well expressed but bound neither PTH nor PTHrP and produced no cAMP or inositol
phosphate response, and critically the paternal allele was not expressed, so the chondrocytes had
functionally zero receptor. Blomstrand chondrodysplasia is lethal with advanced endochondral bone
maturation. The two disorders therefore bracket the receptor: constitutive activation delays
hypertrophy and shortens limbs; total absence accelerates ossification and is lethal. Because the
Blomstrand case achieved nullizygosity through allele-specific silencing rather than biallelic
mutation, the human evidence for the null state is a single carefully dissected patient, and that
is the weak link on this node.

claim_grades.claim: Constitutive PTH1R activation causes Jansen metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with short limbs and hypercalcaemia.
claim_grades.basis: Human mutation plus matched in vitro constitutive-activity assay (schipani1995), phenotype replicated in later Jansen kindreds.

claim_grades.claim: Complete absence of functional PTH1R accelerates endochondral maturation and is lethal.
claim_grades.basis: Single patient (jobert1998); the null state arose from allele-specific non-expression rather than biallelic mutation and has not been replicated by that route.

pth1r_gene.human_evidence_note: Gain- and loss-of-function human patients with matched in vitro receptor assays.
pth1r_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human mutations with human-cell functional assays; no rodent inference.
localization: human: germline; receptor acts on proliferative/prehypertrophic chondrocytes and on kidney and bone

key_refs.one_line_finding: A heterozygous PTH1R His223Arg substitution causes constitutive ligand-independent cAMP accumulation and Jansen-type metaphyseal chondrodysplasia.
In Blomstrand chondrodysplasia a splice-altering PTH1R mutation gives a receptor that binds neither PTH nor PTHrP, with the paternal allele unexpressed.

rare_variant_height.name: Rare variant contribution to height
rare_variant_height.summary:
Rare variation contributes to height in a way that is quantitatively bounded and mechanistically
distinct from common variation. Marouli 2017 reported 83 height-associated coding variants with
minor allele frequencies of 0.1-4.8% and effects up to 2 cm per allele - more than ten times the
average common-variant effect - in genes including IHH, STC2, AR and CRISPLD2, and showed
functionally that rare height-increasing STC2 alleles compromise proteolytic inhibition of PAPP-A
and increase IGFBP-4 cleavage, raising IGF bioavailability. Those 83 variants overlap genes mutated
in monogenic growth disorders, so the rare-coding tier is partly the same gene set as the Mendelian
tier at lower allelic severity. Hawkes 2024 extended the search to non-coding regulatory regions
using whole-genome sequencing in 333,100 individuals across UK Biobank, TOPMed and All of Us, and
found 29 independent rare associations at P < 6e-10 after conditioning on known signals, with
effects from -7 cm to +4.7 cm, plus a replicated aggregate signal near HMGA1 worth about 5 cm.
Wainschtein 2026 then bounded the whole tier: across 34 traits in 347,630 UK Biobank whole genomes,
rare variants (MAF < 1%) account for about 20% of pedigree heritability and common variants about
68%, and of the rare-variant component 21% is coding and 79% non-coding. The rare tier is
therefore real, contains the largest individual effects outside Mendelian disease, and is mostly
regulatory rather than protein-altering.
rare_variant_height.human_evidence_note: Three independent large human sequencing analyses with measured stature and explicit variance partitions.
localization: human: germline, genome-wide

key_refs.one_line_finding: 83 low-frequency coding variants alter height by up to 2 cm per allele; rare STC2 alleles act by compromising PAPP-A inhibition and raising IGF bioavailability.
29 independent rare non-coding height associations with effects from -7 cm to +4.7 cm in 333,100 whole genomes, plus a replicated ~5 cm aggregate signal near HMGA1.
Rare variants account for ~20% and common variants ~68% of pedigree heritability across 34 traits; 79% of the rare-variant component is non-coding.
Joint WGS modelling identifies 59 rare variants and gene burden scores for height and achieves ~46% polygenic prediction accuracy.

shox_gene.name: SHOX
shox_gene.summary:
SHOX sits in the pseudoautosomal region PAR1 of Xp22/Yp11.3 and escapes X-inactivation, so it is
one of the very few human genes that is genuinely dosage-sensitive in a diploid-versus-monosomic
sense. Rao 1997 defined a 170 kb PAR1 interval deleted in 36 short-statured individuals with Xp22
or Yp11.3 rearrangements and absent from normal-height relatives and from 30 rearrangement
carriers of normal height, then isolated SHOX inside it and found one functional SHOX mutation by
screening 91 idiopathic-short-stature patients. Shears 1998 showed the same gene is deleted or
truncated in Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis and that Langer mesomelic dysplasia is its homozygous
form, establishing a strict allelic dose series: two functional copies = normal stature, one copy =
mesomelic short stature with Madelung deformity, zero copies = severe mesomelic dwarfism. That
series has been measured: in 41 patients from 23 families the median height SDS was -6.3 for
Langer (nullizygous), -2.4 for Leri-Weill (haploinsufficient) and -2.1 for the SHOX-positive
idiopathic short stature referrals. SHOX is a homeodomain transcription factor; the human
mechanistic work localizing its product in growth plate cartilage is far thinner than the genetic
dose data, which is why the gene node and any protein-level claim must be graded separately.
SHOX has no mouse orthologue (the gene is absent from the rodent genome), so there is no
knockout mouse and essentially no murine mechanism to launder - an unusual and welcome situation
for this atlas.

claim_grades.claim: SHOX gene dosage sets human stature in a monotonic 0/1/2-copy series.
claim_grades.basis: Three independent human cohorts (rao1997 discovery, shears1998 LWD/LMD allelism, doan2026 quantified SDS by dose).

claim_grades.claim: SHOX acts as a transcription factor within growth plate chondrocytes to produce this effect.
claim_grades.basis: Asserted in reviews; no human growth-plate localization primary was reached in this sweep. See gap g_l8gen_004.

shox_gene.human_evidence_note: The entire allelic series - nullizygous, haploinsufficient, and heterozygous-mild - is defined in humans with measured stature; there is no mouse orthologue of SHOX.
shox_gene.translation_risk_reason: SHOX is absent from the rodent genome, so no cross-species inference is possible or attempted.
localization: human: germline PAR1 (Xp22.33/Yp11.32), escapes X-inactivation

key_refs.one_line_finding: A 170 kb PAR1 interval containing the novel homeobox gene SHOX is deleted in 36 short-statured individuals and in no normal-height relative.
SHOX deletions and a premature stop segregate with Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis; Langer mesomelic dysplasia is the homozygous form.
Median height SDS by SHOX dose in 41 patients: -6.3 nullizygous, -2.4 Leri-Weill, -2.1 idiopathic short stature.
SHOX variants in 3 of 102 children classified as idiopathic short stature.

shox_haploinsufficiency.name: SHOX haploinsufficiency
shox_haploinsufficiency.summary:
SHOX haploinsufficiency is the single-copy state of the PAR1 SHOX locus, produced by whole-gene
deletion, enhancer deletion, nonsense or missense variants, or by loss of one sex chromosome as in
Turner syndrome. It is the commonest identified monogenic cause of disproportionate short stature
in children referred as idiopathic. The measured penetrance on stature is incomplete but the
central tendency is reproducible: median height -2.4 SDS in molecularly confirmed Leri-Weill
dyschondrosteosis and -2.1 SDS where the same lesion presents without Madelung deformity. Two
features distinguish it from a generic short-stature gene. First, the deficit is mesomelic - the
forearm and lower leg are disproportionately shortened and the radius bows into a Madelung
deformity - so it is a limb-segment-specific rather than uniform growth defect. Second, expression
is consistently more severe in females than in males at the same genotype, and the penetrance gap
is wide enough that obligate carriers of normal height are routinely observed within affected
pedigrees. In molecular screening of unselected idiopathic short stature, MLPA plus sequencing
detects SHOX lesions in roughly one in six children, with two-thirds of the lesions falling in
enhancer rather than coding regions - a distribution that matters because coding-only sequencing
misses the majority.
shox_haploinsufficiency.human_evidence_note: Human genotype-phenotype series only; the gene has no rodent orthologue.
shox_haploinsufficiency.translation_risk_reason: No animal model of SHOX exists, so no cross-species claim is made.
localization: human: germline PAR1, systemic; limb effect is mesomelic (zeugopod-predominant)

key_refs.one_line_finding: SHOX deletions/nonsense segregate with Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis; homozygous state gives Langer mesomelic dysplasia.
41 SHOX-deficiency patients: median height SDS -2.4 (LWD) and -2.1 (ISS); GH raised mean height SDS from -2.5 to -2.0 in 15 treated.
PAR1 deletions encompassing SHOX cause growth failure in idiopathic short stature and Turner syndrome.

stat5b_gene.name: STAT5B
stat5b_gene.summary:
STAT5B is the transcription factor through which the growth hormone receptor drives IGF1
transcription, and human STAT5B deficiency is the experiment that places the defect below the
receptor while keeping the receptor intact. Kofoed 2003 reported the first patient: severe growth
hormone insensitivity with normal-to-elevated GH and GH-binding protein but very low IGF-1, caused
by a homozygous STAT5B mutation, and accompanied by immune dysfunction - because STAT5B also
transduces interleukin-2 receptor signalling, so the same allele produces growth failure and
lymphoid disease together. Hwa 2005 characterised a second patient from a consanguineous pedigree
with a novel homozygous insertion causing total absence of STAT5B protein; she measured 114 cm at
16.4 years, a height SDS of -7.8, with IGF-1 at 7.2 ng/ml against a normal range of 242-600,
IGFBP-3 at 543 against 2500-4800, and acid-labile subunit at 1.22 microg/ml against 5.6-16, none of
which rose during an IGF-1 generation test. The severity is the point: STAT5B nullizygosity gives a
larger stature deficit than IGFALS deficiency by roughly 5 SDS despite both collapsing circulating
IGF-1, because STAT5B loss also removes locally transcribed IGF-1 and the immune phenotype adds
morbidity. The combination of near-absent IGF-1 and a failed generation test with a structurally
normal GH receptor is the diagnostic fingerprint that distinguishes it from Laron syndrome.

claim_grades.claim: Homozygous STAT5B loss causes severe growth hormone insensitivity with normal GH receptor.
claim_grades.basis: Two independent patients from unrelated pedigrees with concordant biochemistry (kofoed2003, hwa2005).

claim_grades.claim: The stature deficit of STAT5B nullizygosity is about -7.8 SDS.
claim_grades.basis: Single measured patient (hwa2005); no genotype-defined cohort mean exists.

stat5b_gene.human_evidence_note: Two independent homozygous human patients with full GH-IGF axis biochemistry and an IGF-1 generation test.
localization: human: germline; STAT5B transduces GH receptor signalling in liver and growth plate and IL-2 receptor signalling in lymphocytes

key_refs.one_line_finding: A homozygous STAT5B mutation causes growth hormone insensitivity with normal GH and GH-binding protein but low IGF-1, plus immune dysfunction.
Total absence of STAT5B protein gives height -7.8 SDS with IGF-1 7.2 ng/ml (normal 242-600) and no response to an IGF-1 generation test.

aliases: signal transducer and activator of transcription 5B gene

zbtb38_gene.name: ZBTB38
zbtb38_gene.summary:
ZBTB38 is one of the 20 loci in the first-generation height GWAS (Weedon 2008) and is retained in this layer for a specific reason: it is a methyl-CpG-binding zinc-finger transcription factor, so it is the one top height locus whose annotated molecular function is the reading of DNA methylation - the same mark that tracks growth plate senescence in rabbit and that is required for normal bone length in mouse. That makes ZBTB38 the natural place to test whether the height-associated methylation biology and the height-associated genetic biology are the same system, and no retrieved study has done so. The association itself is solid and has been replicated outside the discovery ancestry: rs724016 is associated with height in individuals of African ancestry with sickle cell anaemia, in a sample where it is also associated with fetal haemoglobin. What is missing is everything downstream. No human growth-plate expression, no chondrocyte eQTL, and no functional experiment linking ZBTB38 genotype to any growth plate parameter was retrieved, so the node stands as a well-replicated association with an unexploited mechanistic handle rather than as a characterised growth gene.

Direct functional work on the locus does exist, and it moved this node's grade. Parsons 2022
genotyped rs6764769 and rs724016 in 261 idiopathic-short-stature patients, showed the two SNPs are
in linkage disequilibrium, and found the rs724016 GG genotype associated with lower birth length
(P = 0.01) and with a smaller height SDS gain over the first year of recombinant human growth
hormone in 93 treated patients (P = 0.02); ZBTB38 expression rose with age across 87 normal
children and young adults, and siRNA knockdown in SiHA cells increased proliferation without
altering MCM10 expression. So ZBTB38 genotype tracks a prenatal growth measure and a treatment
response, not only adult stature. What is still missing is a per-allele centimetre effect for
ZBTB38 in a general population and any demonstration that the gene acts in chondrocytes.

claim_grades.claim: Common variation at ZBTB38 is associated with adult height at genome-wide significance.
claim_grades.basis: weedon2008 discovery plus follow-up genotyping; the locus persists in yengo2022.

claim_grades.claim: ZBTB38 genotype also tracks birth length and growth hormone treatment response.
claim_grades.basis: Single cohort of 261 ISS patients with 93 treated (parsons2022); not replicated.

claim_grades.claim: ZBTB38 influences height through the growth plate.
claim_grades.basis: No chondrocyte expression or perturbation evidence; the only functional work is siRNA knockdown in a cervical carcinoma line. Flagged as inference. See gap g_l8gen_009.

zbtb38_gene.human_evidence_note: Association established in ~30,000 humans with measured height and replicated in an African-ancestry sample.
zbtb38_gene.translation_risk_reason: Human association genetics only; no animal claim is made.
localization: human: germline; no growth plate expression data retrieved (gap g_l0l9_005)

key_refs.one_line_finding: ZBTB38 is among 20 loci associated with adult height in the first-generation GWAS, which together explain ~3% of height variance.
rs724016 at ZBTB38 is associated with height in an African-ancestry sickle cell anaemia cohort, replicating the locus outside the discovery ancestry.
rs724016 GG in 261 ISS patients is associated with lower birth length (P=0.01) and smaller first-year height SDS gain on rhGH (P=0.02); ZBTB38 expression rises with age in normal children.

aliases: zinc finger and BTB domain containing 38

activin_receptor_2b.name: ActRIIB
activin_receptor_2b.summary: ActRIIB is the type II serine-threonine kinase receptor through which myostatin, activins and several GDFs signal in skeletal muscle. It is the druggable node of that axis: bimagrumab, a human monoclonal antibody that blocks ActRIIB, increased thigh muscle volume in adult men recovering from casting-induced atrophy in a randomised study (rooks2017). Its inclusion in an organism-growth layer is justified by a negative result rather than a positive one - receptor blockade produces a large, measurable change in one organ system's mass in adults, at an age when no change in stature is possible, which makes the muscle and skeletal growth programmes separately addressable in the same individual. Whether ActRIIB signalling has any role in the growth plate itself is not addressed by these human data; ligand traps against the receptor alter bone geometry in a mouse model of osteogenesis imperfecta, but that is mouse and disease-specific and is not carried forward as a human claim here.
activin_receptor_2b.human_evidence_note: A randomised human pharmacological study of receptor blockade with imaging endpoints.
activin_receptor_2b.translation_risk_reason: The retained claim is from a human randomised study; no murine claim is asserted.
localization: human skeletal muscle: receptor for myostatin and activins

key_refs.one_line_finding: ActRIIB blockade with bimagrumab increases thigh muscle volume after casting-induced atrophy in men.
Human loss of the principal ActRIIB ligand produces muscle hypertrophy.

allometry_organ_scaling.name: Allometry and organ scaling
allometry_organ_scaling.summary: Allometry is the statement that organ size scales with body size as a power law rather than proportionally, and its relevance here is that different organs have different exponents, so shape necessarily changes as size changes. The oldest quantitative human dataset on this is the regression of brain weight on body height and on body weight across 23 age groups from birth to the ninth decade, which shows clearly differential rates of change: the brain-to-height and brain-to-weight ratios fall steeply through childhood because the body continues to grow long after the brain has stopped (dekaban1978). The MRI charts give the same relation with modern precision - grey matter volume peaks at 5.9 years while stature is still six years from its peak velocity (bethlehem2022). This atlas records allometry as a constraint rather than a mechanism: any model that reproduces cm/yr at the growth plate must not simultaneously predict isometric growth of the organism, because the human body demonstrably does not grow isometrically. No modern human dataset of organ-specific scaling exponents across postnatal development was located in this sweep and this is logged as a quantitative gap.

claim_grades.claim: Human postnatal growth is not isometric and organ-to-body ratios change systematically with age
claim_grades.basis: Directly measured brain-to-height and brain-to-weight ratios across 23 age groups plus modern MRI milestones.

claim_grades.claim: Organ-specific allometric exponents for human postnatal growth are established
claim_grades.basis: Not traceable: no source reporting fitted human postnatal organ scaling exponents was found in this sweep. Logged as gap g_l9organism_017.

allometry_organ_scaling.human_evidence_note: Both retained sources are direct human measurements, though neither reports fitted scaling exponents.
localization: human whole organism: organ weight or volume against body height and weight

key_refs.one_line_finding: Regressions of brain weight on body height and weight across 23 age groups show differential rates of change.
Brain tissue volume milestones fall years before the skeletal pubertal spurt.

articular_cartilage.name: Articular cartilage
articular_cartilage.summary: Articular cartilage is the permanent cartilage at the epiphyseal surface, and during growth it behaves as the growth plate's opposite number: it thins while the plate is running and stabilises once the plate closes. In 240 knee MRI scans of children aged 7-18 without chondral pathology, femoral articular cartilage was significantly thicker in patients with open distal femoral physes than in those with closing or closed physes at the medial condyle, lateral condyle and lateral trochlea (all p<0.001), and linear regression showed an inverse association between femoral cartilage thickness and age. Patellar cartilage, by contrast, was the thickest of all sites and did not vary with age or skeletal maturity, so the thinning is site-specific rather than a whole-joint phenomenon. This node is retained in L9 because it supplies a quantitative organism-level dissociation the mechanistic layers must reproduce: the same ciliary perturbation that shortens the mouse growth plate thickens articular cartilage (yuan2015, the target of an existing L3 edge from ift80_protein), so plate output and articular thickness are not two readouts of one chondrocyte programme. The human numbers are cross-sectional MRI, not histology, and no human study has measured plate output and articular thickness in the same joint over time.

claim_grades.claim: Femoral articular cartilage is thicker while the distal femoral physis is open and thins with age and skeletal maturity
claim_grades.basis: Directly measured in 240 knee MRIs with physeal status scored on the same images, significant at three femoral sites (p<0.001) and on linear regression against age.

claim_grades.claim: Articular cartilage thickness and growth plate output are separately controlled
claim_grades.basis: Supported by the opposite-direction response of the two cartilages to Ift80 deletion in mouse (yuan2015) and by the site-specific human pattern (patella invariant, femur age-dependent); no human within-joint longitudinal test exists.

articular_cartilage.human_evidence_note: Normative articular cartilage thickness measured by MRI in 240 children and adolescents with physeal status recorded on the same scans.
articular_cartilage.translation_risk_reason: The human data are thickness on MRI with no cellular content; the dissociation between articular and physeal responses to a single perturbation is established only in mouse.
localization: human knee: patellar, femoral condylar, trochlear and tibial plateau cartilage on MRI (sidharthan2021)
mouse epiphysis: articular and growth plate cartilage under Ift80 deletion (yuan2015)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Femoral articular cartilage is thicker with open distal femoral physes and thins with age, while patellar cartilage does not vary with age or maturity.
Ift80 deletion impairs both epiphyseal and articular cartilage formation, thickening articular cartilage while shortening the growth plate.

body_proportion_development.name: Body proportion development
body_proportion_development.summary: Body proportions are not fixed and rescaled during growth; they change systematically and in opposite directions at different ages, which is the organism-level signature of site-specific physeal velocity. The head is proportionally largest at birth and the legs proportionally shortest; through infancy and childhood leg length grows fastest so the sitting height ratio falls; during and after the pubertal spurt vertebral growth persists after the lower-limb plates decelerate, so the ratio rises again. The Dutch and Japanese national references quantify these trajectories in sitting height, leg length, arm span and their ratios (fredriks2005, hirano2025), and the ICP decomposition attributes the childhood limb-favouring phase to a stronger childhood growth component in the legs than in the trunk (karlberg1989). Two independent constraints on mechanism follow. First, disproportion in disease is site-selective rather than global: short children born small for gestational age show a short anterior cranial base (-1.8 SDS), a small retropositioned mandible (<= -1.7 SDS) and a small maxilla (-1.5 SDS) with an increased lower anterior face height (+1.7 SDS) - a specific pattern, not uniform miniaturisation (van1998). Second, the ratio a child ends with is population-specific at every age, so any single systemic growth signal must be read differently by different plates in a way that itself varies between populations.

claim_grades.claim: Body proportions change in opposite directions before and after the pubertal spurt
claim_grades.basis: Directly measured in national reference cohorts of 14500 (Dutch) and 11059 (Japanese) children.

claim_grades.claim: Growth restriction produces a site-selective, not uniform, pattern of skeletal shortfall
claim_grades.basis: Directly measured cephalometric SDS pattern in 48 short SGA subjects (van1998); single centre, wide age range, no untreated control series.

claim_grades.claim: The childhood growth phase acts preferentially on the legs
claim_grades.basis: Model-derived from the ICP decomposition only (karlberg1989).

body_proportion_development.human_evidence_note: All measurements are human anthropometry and cephalometry; the SGA disproportion series is a directly measured clinical cohort.
localization: human whole organism: sitting height, leg length, arm span, lateral cephalometry

key_refs.one_line_finding: Age references for sitting height, leg length and their ratio across 0-21 years.
Arm span/height ratio trajectories differ between Japanese, Dutch and Turkish children at every age.
Short children born SGA show a specific craniofacial disproportion pattern with normal dental age.
Attributes the infancy-to-childhood change in body proportions to a leg-biased childhood growth component.

brain_growth_trajectory.name: Brain growth trajectory
brain_growth_trajectory.summary: The brain and the skeleton run on different clocks, and the size of the mismatch is now measured precisely. In the largest normative MRI resource assembled - 123984 scans from 101457 people spanning 115 days post-conception to 100 years - grey matter volume peaks at 5.9 years (95% CI 5.8-6.1), total cerebrum volume at 12.5 years (12.14-12.89), cortical surface area at 10.97 years, subcortical grey matter at 14.4 years and white matter volume at 28.7 years, while mean cortical thickness peaks at 1.7 years and its velocity peaks prenatally at about -0.38 years relative to birth (bethlehem2022). The velocity peaks are earlier still: grey matter volume velocity peaks at 5.08 months and white matter volume velocity at 2.4 years. Critically, none of these trajectories shows an adolescent volume spurt corresponding to peak height velocity - only grey matter peaks before puberty at all, and the remaining tissue classes peak during or long after it. Autopsy weights give the same picture with a different method: brain weight quadruples over birth weight in the first 3 years and rises only marginally further over the next 15 years, reaching maximum near 19 years, with male brains 9.8% heavier than female across 4736 pathology-free brains (dekaban1978). Any theory that a single systemic maturational signal drives organ growth must explain why the brain's peak precedes the pubertal skeletal spurt by six years and the white matter's by fifteen.

claim_grades.claim: Human brain tissue volumes peak at ages between 1.7 and 28.7 years depending on tissue class
claim_grades.basis: Normative GAMLSS model on 123984 scans with bootstrap CIs on each milestone.

claim_grades.claim: There is no adolescent brain volume spurt corresponding to the height spurt
claim_grades.basis: No pubertal velocity peak appears in any charted tissue class (bethlehem2022); MRI cohorts are unevenly sampled in adolescence, which limits the strength of a negative result.

brain_growth_trajectory.human_evidence_note: Both sources are human: a 123984-scan MRI normative model and a 4736-brain autopsy series.
localization: human brain: structural MRI volumes and fresh autopsy weights

key_refs.one_line_finding: Lifespan brain charts place peak grey matter volume at 5.9 y, total cerebrum at 12.5 y and white matter at 28.7 y, with no adolescent volume spurt.
Brain weight quadruples by 3 years, peaks near 19 years, and is 9.8% greater in males across 4736 autopsy brains.

canalization_growth.name: Canalization of human growth
canalization_growth.summary: Canalization is the observation that a growing child perturbed off its height trajectory returns to it, implying that the organism stores a target and can compute a deviation from it. Prader, Tanner and von Harnack coined the term catch-up growth for the return phase and framed it explicitly as developmental canalization in man (prader1963); Tanner generalised the target-seeking description to mammals (tanner1963). The empirical content of the model is a trajectory, not just an endpoint: when height SDS minus target height SDS is followed through recovery in adequately treated children it is well fitted by a monomolecular (single-exponential approach-to-asymptote) function, which means catch-up has a rate constant k and therefore a time constant 1/k (wit2021).
