The rate constant differs by disease - coeliac disease recovers faster than juvenile hypothyroidism and GH deficiency (p=0.02 and p=0.004 respectively), while the asymptote reached is the same - so the deficit and the recovery rate are separately controlled. Two mechanistic accounts compete and are not resolved: a systemic neuroendocrine comparator, and a growth plate-intrinsic model in which suppression delays the consumption of a finite proliferative capacity so the plate is younger than its chronological age when the suppression lifts (delayed_senescence_hypothesis, L2). The monomolecular fit failed in 10-17% of children because height SDS fell again after several measurements, violating the assumption that catch-up is an irreversible one-way process (wit2021) - the clearest published evidence that the target is not perfectly held.

claim_grades.claim: Human catch-up growth follows a single-exponential approach to an asymptote and therefore has a definable time constant
claim_grades.basis: Monomolecular fits succeed in 83-90% of episodes across three diseases (wit2021), but total n is 38 children in the hypothyroid/GHD analysis and the model was developed on coeliac disease.

claim_grades.claim: The rate of catch-up and the size of the deficit are separately controlled
claim_grades.basis: Different k with equal asymptote between coeliac disease and hypothyroidism in one modelling study; not independently replicated.

claim_grades.claim: Growth is target-seeking, i.e. the organism stores a set point
claim_grades.basis: Inference from the reproducibility of return to a prior centile (prader1963, tanner1963); no comparator, signal or set-point has ever been identified, and 10-17% of episodes reverse.

canalization_growth.human_evidence_note: The canalization phenomenon and its kinetics are described directly from serial human height measurement in clinical cohorts.
canalization_growth.translation_risk_reason: The phenomenon as quantified here is measured in humans.
localization: human whole organism: height SDS relative to target height SDS through a recovery episode

key_refs.one_line_finding: Names catch-up growth after illness or starvation and frames it as developmental canalization in man.
States the target-seeking model of size regulation in mammals.
Catch-up growth in juvenile hypothyroidism and GHD fits a monomolecular function with a slower rate constant than coeliac disease but the same endpoint.
Sets out the competing neuroendocrine and growth-plate-intrinsic models of catch-up growth.
Tests the delayed growth plate senescence hypothesis of catch-up growth in humans; abstract not available, full text queued.

catch_down_growth.name: Catch-down growth
catch_down_growth.summary: Catch-down is the mirror image of catch-up: an infant born larger than its genetic channel decelerates and crosses height centiles downward until it reaches that channel. Smith and colleagues documented both directions in the same series and drew the mechanistic conclusion that birth length reflects the intrauterine environment while the postnatal trajectory reflects the child's own genotype, so the first two postnatal years are a period of realignment onto the genetic channel rather than of continuous growth along it (smith1976). The realignment is essentially complete by about 2 years, which is why the correlation between length and adult height rises steeply over that interval and why height-for-age becomes a stable trait thereafter. This matters to a mechanistic atlas for a specific reason: it means the postnatal growth plate does not simply inherit the size it was born with and scale it, and any model that treats birth length as the initial condition of a monotone growth process will mispredict roughly the same fraction of infants in each direction. Quantitative centile-crossing rates with modern denominators were not extracted in this sweep and are logged as a gap.

claim_grades.claim: Infants shift height centiles in both directions during the first two years to reach a parentally determined channel
claim_grades.basis: Directly observed in serial human data with parental heights (smith1976) and consistent with the 0.75-0.78 parent-offspring regression slope; the original series is small and pre-dates modern references.

claim_grades.claim: Birth length reflects the intrauterine environment rather than the child's genotype
claim_grades.basis: Inference from the direction and completeness of the shift; not tested against measured genotype or a polygenic score in the primary.

catch_down_growth.human_evidence_note: Described from serial human infant length measurements related to parental heights.
catch_down_growth.translation_risk_reason: Human infant phenomenon; no animal model reproduces the two-year realignment window.
localization: human whole organism: serial recumbent length from birth to 2 years

key_refs.one_line_finding: Infants shift linear growth channels in both directions during infancy, illustrating genetic control of growth from fetal life onward.
Supplies the parent-offspring regression slope that defines the channel an infant realigns to.

cdc_growth_reference.name: CDC 2000 growth reference
cdc_growth_reference.summary: The 2000 CDC growth charts are a descriptive reference: they summarise how US children actually grew in five national survey cycles, without prescriptive inclusion criteria, and they were smoothed with the LMS method so each chart carries explicit L, M and S parameters that permit exact SDS computation (kuczmarski2002). They matter to this atlas for two reasons. They supply the adult-height distribution used to convert clinical target-height bands into centimetres - the +/-1.64 SDS band recommended for idiopathic short stature becomes +/-10.6 cm for girls and +/-11.7 cm for boys under these charts (zeevi2024) - and they supply the matched-percentile male and female heights that expose the additive 13 cm sex correction as wrong at the extremes. Because the reference is descriptive it embeds the secular trend and the body composition of the US survey population, so an SDS computed against CDC is not interchangeable with one computed against WHO, and the two diverge most in infancy and at the tails (de2011).
cdc_growth_reference.human_evidence_note: Constructed from measured heights and weights in national probability samples of US children.
localization: human whole organism: US national survey anthropometry, birth to 20 years

key_refs.one_line_finding: Methods and construction of the 2000 CDC growth charts, published with LMS parameters.
Uses CDC matched-percentile heights to show the male-female difference is multiplicative, not additive.
Quantifies the divergence between US reference increments and the WHO velocity standards.

cranial_base_synchondrosis.name: Cranial base synchondrosis
cranial_base_synchondrosis.summary: The synchondroses of the cranial base are bidirectional growth plates: a mirror-image pair of hypertrophic zones flanking a central resting zone, elongating in both directions at once, in contrast to the unidirectional physis of a long bone. The spheno-occipital synchondrosis is the last to close and is the principal contributor to postnatal cranial base lengthening. Its closure is a staged process resolvable on 3D CT, and in 630 Korean subjects aged 6-18 the intermediate stages 3 and 4 fell at 12.7-13.9 years in males and 11.0-12.5 years in females, with females significantly more advanced than males at the same age (odds ratio 1.972, 95% CI 1.063-3.658) (kim2024). Fusion stage correlated with cervical vertebral maturation stage at Spearman 0.955 in males and 0.964 in females, so the cranial base and the vertebral column mature almost in lockstep - a much tighter coupling than that between skeletal and dental maturation. That contrast is the mechanistic point: two endochondral sites in different embryological lineages track each other closely, while an adjacent non-endochondral maturation process in the same head does not.

claim_grades.claim: Spheno-occipital synchondrosis fusion stages 3-4 mark the pubertal growth peak and occur 1.4-1.7 years earlier in females
claim_grades.basis: Direct 3D CT staging in 630 subjects with sex-stratified age groups and formal ordinal regression.

claim_grades.claim: Cranial base and cervical vertebral maturation are almost perfectly coupled
claim_grades.basis: Spearman 0.955-0.964 in one cross-sectional series; correlation across a wide age range is inflated by shared chronological age.

cranial_base_synchondrosis.human_evidence_note: Cross-sectional 3D CT staging in 630 human subjects with paired cervical vertebral maturation staging.
cranial_base_synchondrosis.translation_risk_reason: Human imaging series; the murine synchondrosis does not close on a comparable schedule.
localization: human cranial base: spheno-occipital synchondrosis on 3D CT

key_refs.one_line_finding: Spheno-occipital synchondrosis fusion staged on 3D CT in 630 subjects correlates 0.955-0.964 with cervical vertebral maturation and marks the pubertal growth peak.

craniofacial_growth.name: Craniofacial growth
craniofacial_growth.summary: The craniofacial skeleton grows by three mechanically and developmentally distinct mechanisms operating simultaneously: sutural growth at the calvarial and facial sutures, endochondral growth at the cranial base synchondroses, and surface remodelling with condylar growth at the mandible. Because these mechanisms are separable, growth restriction produces a patterned rather than a uniform shortfall. In 48 short subjects born small for gestational age the anterior cranial base was -1.8 SDS, the mandible at or below -1.7 SDS and the maxilla -1.5 SDS, while the mandibular plane angle was +1.9 SDS, the cranial base angle +1.0 SDS and lower anterior face height +1.7 SDS - a small retrognathic face with a relatively increased lower face height, not a scaled-down normal face (van1998). In the same subjects skeletal maturation was delayed but dental age was not, which is why craniofacial growth cannot be predicted from bone age alone. The timing anchor for the whole complex is the cranial base: spheno-occipital synchondrosis fusion stages 3 and 4 fall at 12.7-13.9 years in males and 11.0-12.5 years in females, i.e. close to peak height velocity in each sex (kim2024), so the endochondral component of the skull ceases on the same schedule as the appendicular skeleton while the sutural component does not.

claim_grades.claim: Growth restriction produces a patterned, site-selective craniofacial shortfall
claim_grades.basis: Directly measured cephalometric SDS pattern in 48 short SGA subjects; single centre, wide age range, no matched short-non-SGA control group.

claim_grades.claim: The endochondral cranial base ceases growing on the same schedule as the appendicular skeleton
claim_grades.basis: Spheno-occipital fusion stages 3-4 coincide with the sex-specific pubertal growth peak in 630 CT subjects (kim2024); a cross-sectional staging study, so individual synchrony is inferred not observed.

craniofacial_growth.human_evidence_note: Both sources are direct human radiographic measurement series.
localization: human skull: lateral cephalometry and 3D CT of the cranial base

key_refs.one_line_finding: Short subjects born SGA show a specific pattern of craniofacial hypoplasia with delayed skeletal but normal dental maturation.
Spheno-occipital synchondrosis fusion stages 3-4 fall at 12.7-13.9 y in males and 11.0-12.5 y in females on 3D CT.

dental_development_clock.name: Dental development as an independent maturity clock
dental_development_clock.summary: Dental development is the only widely used maturity indicator that runs independently of skeletal maturation, and that independence is a hard constraint on any theory that a single systemic signal drives maturation. Demirjian and colleagues measured five maturity indicators in 50 French-Canadian girls - menarche, peak height velocity, 75% skeletal maturity, appearance of the ulnar sesamoid and 90% dental maturity - and found that ages at peak height velocity, menarche and 75% skeletal maturity were significantly intercorrelated, while age at 90% dental maturity showed no significant relationship with any of them; they concluded that the mechanisms controlling dental development are independent of somatic and sexual maturation (demirjian1985). The dissociation is largest exactly where a single systemic signal would predict coupling. In isolated GH deficiency, bone age is delayed by 1.99 years before treatment while dental age is delayed by only 0.31 years, and critically the two delays are uncorrelated within individuals (torliskawalkow2026, 48 GHD children versus 48 controls). Children born small for gestational age with persistent short stature show delayed skeletal maturation and specific craniofacial hypoplasia but no dental delay (van1998). Stunting in a Peruvian school population shifted neither dental nor skeletal maturity stage (floresmir2005). Correlations between dental and skeletal stage in unselected populations are nonetheless moderate to high (r = 0.85 in Peruvian schoolchildren; Spearman 0.78-0.79 against cervical vertebral maturation in Iranian orthodontic patients), so dental and skeletal clocks share chronological age as a common driver but not the endocrine perturbations that move one of them.

claim_grades.claim: Dental maturation dissociates from skeletal maturation under endocrine perturbation, by about 1.7 years in untreated GH deficiency
claim_grades.basis: Direct within-individual measurement of both clocks in 48 GHD children against 48 controls, with the delays explicitly uncorrelated (torliskawalkow2026); corroborated in an independent SGA cohort (van1998).

claim_grades.claim: Dental maturity is uncorrelated with somatic and sexual maturity indicators in healthy girls
claim_grades.basis: A single longitudinal cohort of 50 girls with five indicators measured in the same individuals (demirjian1985); not replicated in a comparable design, and unselected cross-sectional samples show moderate-to-high dental-skeletal correlation driven by shared chronological age.

claim_grades.claim: Neither dental nor skeletal maturation is shifted by chronic undernutrition sufficient to cause stunting
claim_grades.basis: One cross-sectional Peruvian school study with 140 stunted children; null results, no power calculation reported.

dental_development_clock.human_evidence_note: All comparisons are direct within-individual measurements of dental and skeletal maturity in human children.
dental_development_clock.translation_risk_reason: Human maturity indicators; rodent molars erupt on a fixed schedule not comparable to the human dentition.
localization: human whole organism: panoramic radiography or clinical dental examination compared with hand-wrist or cervical-vertebral skeletal staging

key_refs.one_line_finding: Age at 90% dental maturity is uncorrelated with peak height velocity, menarche and 75% skeletal maturity in the same 50 girls.
In GH deficiency bone age is delayed 1.99 y but dental age only 0.31 y, and the two delays do not correlate.
Short children born SGA have delayed skeletal maturation and craniofacial hypoplasia with normal dental age.
Dental and skeletal maturity stages correlate at r=0.85 and neither differs by stunting status in 280 Peruvian schoolchildren.

growth_velocity_curve.name: Human height velocity curve
growth_velocity_curve.summary: The human height velocity curve is triphasic: a steep monotonic decline through infancy, a slowly decelerating childhood plateau interrupted in some children by a small mid-growth spurt at 6-8 years, and an adolescent spurt that reverses the deceleration for the only time postnatally before velocity falls to zero at fusion. The pubertal peak is reached about two years earlier in girls than boys and is smaller. Three independent longitudinal cohorts modelled with the same shape-invariant method give peak height velocity 9.5-9.6 cm/yr in boys and 8.3-8.4 cm/yr in girls (chun2024 Korea, galvo2025 Brazil). Between-individual variance is dominated by timing rather than amplitude: in ALSPAC the SD of age at peak height velocity is 0.8 years in females around a mean of 11.8 years, with a male mean of 13.5 years (elhakeem2024, n=8518). Timing and amplitude are not independent - earlier pubertal onset raises peak velocity by 1.82 cm/yr per year in boys and 1.39 cm/yr per year in girls (chun2024), and age at onset correlates -0.48 with peak velocity in a separate biannually sampled male cohort (srensen2026). Mechanistically the constraint is severe: one physis must change its output roughly two-fold between the childhood trough and the pubertal peak and then to zero, with no change in the cell types present. Standing height is also a serial sum over the two lower-limb plates, the vertebral plates and the skull base, each running at its own velocity (site_specific_growth_rate, L1), so no plate-level model reaches cm/yr without an explicit summation step.

claim_grades.claim: Peak height velocity is 9.5-9.6 cm/yr in boys and 8.3-8.4 cm/yr in girls
claim_grades.basis: Three independent longitudinal cohorts on two continents fitted with the same shape-invariant model agree to within 0.1 cm/yr.

claim_grades.claim: Between-individual variance in the pubertal curve is dominated by timing rather than amplitude
claim_grades.basis: ALSPAC SD of age at PHV 0.8 y in females plus the SITAR variance decomposition in Christ's Hospital (tempo SD 0.97 y, velocity SD 15%); never tested as a formal variance partition within one cohort.

claim_grades.claim: Earlier pubertal onset produces a higher and shorter spurt
claim_grades.basis: Consistent in sign and magnitude across a Korean SITAR cohort, a Brazilian SITAR cohort and a Danish biannually sampled male cohort.

claim_grades.claim: A mid-growth spurt occurs at 6-8 years in a substantial minority of children
claim_grades.basis: Detected by kernel regression and shape-invariant modelling of Fels and Zurich serial data (guo1992, sttzle1980) but invisible to Preece-Baines; prevalence is model-dependent.

growth_velocity_curve.human_evidence_note: Every number is measured in humans by serial stadiometry in longitudinal cohorts; there is no animal component.
growth_velocity_curve.translation_risk_reason: The phenotype is defined only in humans and all data are human.
localization: human whole organism: standing height by stadiometer; velocity derived from serial measurement

key_refs.one_line_finding: SITAR fit to 3339 Korean heights gives PHV 9.61 cm/yr at 12.46 y in boys and 8.32 cm/yr at 10.99 y in girls.
Bayesian SITAR in 398 Brazilian children gives PHV 9.52 cm/yr at 13.55 y in boys and 8.38 cm/yr at 11.30 y in girls.
ALSPAC age at PHV is 11.8 y in females (SD 0.8) and 13.5 y in males, correlating r=0.76 with menarche.
Age at pubertal onset correlates -0.48 with PHV across 105 longitudinally studied boys.
Original British longitudinal height-velocity centiles from birth to maturity.
US height velocity centiles ages 7-18 from 6532 children, presented separately for early, average and late maturers.
Preece-Baines cannot describe the midgrowth spurt and shifts pubertal-spurt onset earlier than kernel regression on the same Fels data.

head_circumference_growth.name: Head circumference growth
head_circumference_growth.summary: Head circumference is the clinical proxy for brain growth and it tracks brain volume closely in infancy, which is why it is the only anthropometric measure with a WHO velocity standard alongside length and weight (who_velocity_2009). Its trajectory is unlike stature: the increment is largest in the first months and then decays rapidly, mirroring the peak grey matter volume velocity at 5.08 months and the four-fold rise in brain weight by 3 years (bethlehem2022, dekaban1978), and there is no pubertal head-circumference spurt. This is the clearest organism-level demonstration that the calvaria and the long bones are not driven by a common growth signal: cranial vault expansion is essentially complete when the long bones still have more than a decade of elongation ahead, and the sutures that permit vault expansion begin closing in a substantial minority of children before adolescence (han2025). Numerical increment centiles for head circumference by month are published in the WHO velocity standards and are flagged for hand verification because the source is a manual rather than an indexed article.

claim_grades.claim: Head circumference velocity peaks in early infancy and there is no pubertal spurt
claim_grades.basis: Directly standardised in infancy (who_velocity_2009) and consistent with the brain volume velocity peaks; the absence of a pubertal spurt is inferred from brain charts rather than measured as head circumference in this sweep.

head_circumference_growth.human_evidence_note: WHO velocity standards are constructed from measured human infant head circumference; the brain correlates are human MRI and autopsy data.
localization: human head: occipitofrontal circumference by tape

key_refs.first_author: WHO Multicentre Growth Reference Study Group
key_refs.one_line_finding: Publishes head circumference increment standards from birth to 24 months.
Grey matter volume velocity peaks at 5.08 months with no adolescent volume spurt.
Brain weight quadruples in the first three years.

height_sds_z_score.name: Height standard deviation score
height_sds_z_score.summary: Height SDS expresses a measurement as the number of reference SDs from the age- and sex-specific median, and it is the currency in which every organism-level growth claim in this atlas is denominated. Because childhood height is not normally distributed at every age, SDS is computed by the LMS method, which fits three smooth age-varying curves - the Box-Cox power L, the median M and the coefficient of variation S - and normalises through a Box-Cox transform (cole1992). Two properties matter mechanistically. First, an SDS is a rank statement about a reference population, not a physical quantity: the same SDS corresponds to a different number of centimetres at each age because S varies with age, so an unchanged SDS during treatment does not mean an unchanged centimetre deficit. Second, SDS is reference-dependent: a child scored against the WHO prescriptive standard and against the CDC descriptive reference receives different values, and the two disagree most at the tails and in infancy (de2011). Any conversion of a plate-level model output into SDS therefore requires the reference to be named, and any target number recorded in SDS in this atlas carries the reference with it.
height_sds_z_score.human_evidence_note: A statistical method developed on and applied only to human reference data.
localization: human whole organism: any anthropometric measurement expressed against an age- and sex-specific reference

key_refs.one_line_finding: Defines the LMS method: reference centiles as three smooth age-varying curves fitted by penalized likelihood.
WHO and US velocity references disagree systematically, most at the lower percentiles.

icp_growth_model.name: ICP (infancy-childhood-puberty) growth model
icp_growth_model.summary: The ICP model decomposes an individual height curve into three additive, partly overlapping components: an infancy component (a sharply decelerating exponential present from mid-gestation), a childhood component (a slowly decelerating polynomial) and a puberty component (a logistic) (karlberg1987, karlberg1989). Its claim is biological rather than statistical: each component is asserted to map onto a different dominant endocrine driver - nutrition and insulin for infancy, growth hormone for childhood, sex steroids superimposed on GH for puberty. Its one hard testable prediction is the infancy-childhood transition: the childhood component switches on between 6 and 12 months, producing a measurable acceleration (the IC spurt) that is absent in untreated GH deficiency, complete by about 3 years, and delayed in 30-50% of children with growth disorders or living in a deprived environment (karlberg1990). A second structural prediction is that the puberty component is invariant in size, so the inverse relation between age at pubertal onset and peak velocity must be generated by the shape of the childhood component alone (karlberg1989) - a claim the later QEPS decomposition contradicts by finding P-function pubertal gain independent of onset age while total pubertal gain is not (holmgren2017). No ICP component has ever been mapped onto a measured change in growth plate cell kinetics; the model is a hypothesis about control, not about tissue.

claim_grades.claim: Human height growth can be fitted by three additive components with small residuals
claim_grades.basis: Direct fits to large human longitudinal series, replicated in many cohorts.

claim_grades.claim: The infancy-childhood transition at 6-12 months marks the onset of significant GH control of growth
claim_grades.basis: Inferred from the absence of the IC spurt in untreated GH deficiency (karlberg1990); no direct measurement of GH-dependence of growth plate output across the transition in any species.

claim_grades.claim: The puberty component is time-invariant in size
claim_grades.basis: Asserted in karlberg1989; the QEPS decomposition of 2280 Swedish children separates P-function from QES-function pubertal gain and finds sex-different contributions (holmgren2017), so the invariance is model-dependent.

icp_growth_model.human_evidence_note: The model was constructed from, and is only ever fitted to, human longitudinal length and height series.
icp_growth_model.translation_risk_reason: Human curve-fitting method with no animal counterpart.
localization: human whole organism: fitted to serial supine length and standing height

key_refs.one_line_finding: First statement of the additive infancy/childhood/puberty decomposition of the human growth curve.
Full ICP formulation asserting a time-invariant puberty component superimposed on a decelerating childhood component.
The infancy-childhood spurt starts at 6-12 months, ends near 3 years, is delayed in 30-50% of growth-disordered children and absent in untreated GHD.
QEPS separation in 2280 children shows pubertal gain from the P-function is independent of onset age, contradicting the ICP account of the onset-amplitude relation.

infancy_growth_nutrition_dependence.name: Nutrition dependence of infant growth
infancy_growth_nutrition_dependence.summary: Infant linear growth is the fastest and the least hormonally buffered phase of postnatal life. In the ICP framework the infancy component is driven by nutrition and insulin rather than by growth hormone, and growth hormone only becomes a significant regulator when the childhood component switches on between 6 and 12 months (karlberg1987, karlberg1990). The strongest evidence for that boundary is negative and human: untreated GH-deficient infants show no infancy-childhood spurt at all, whereas their infancy-component growth is intact, and a delayed spurt occurs in 30-50% of infants in a deprived environment as well as in 30-50% of children with growth disorders (karlberg1990). The corollary for a mechanistic atlas is that the postnatal growth plate operates under two different control regimes within its first three years, and a model calibrated on the childhood or pubertal plate cannot be assumed to apply to the infant plate. The WHO multicentre data set the ceiling on how much of infant growth variation is environmental at the population level: under growth-permitting conditions, site explains only about 3% of variance in length while individuals within sites explain about 70% (who2006), so nutrition dominates the difference between deprived and non-deprived populations but not the difference between healthy individuals.

claim_grades.claim: Growth hormone becomes a significant regulator of linear growth only from 6-12 months
claim_grades.basis: Inferred from the absence of the infancy-childhood spurt in untreated GH deficiency and its delay in deprived infants (karlberg1990); no direct measurement of GH action on the infant growth plate exists in any species.

claim_grades.claim: Under growth-permitting conditions, population of origin explains almost none of the variance in infant length
claim_grades.basis: Formal variance decomposition in a six-country prospective study (who2006).

infancy_growth_nutrition_dependence.human_evidence_note: Human longitudinal length data from clinical cohorts and from a six-country prospective study with prescriptive inclusion criteria.
infancy_growth_nutrition_dependence.translation_risk_reason: All quantities are measured in human infants.
localization: human whole organism: recumbent length, birth to 3 years

key_refs.one_line_finding: The infancy-childhood spurt is absent in untreated GHD and delayed in 30-50% of deprived or growth-disordered infants.
Assigns nutrition/insulin control to the infancy component and GH control to the childhood component.

key_refs.first_author: WHO Multicentre Growth Reference Study Group
key_refs.one_line_finding: Site explains about 3% and individuals about 70% of variance in early linear growth.
Prospective birth cohort quantifying infant growth velocity and its hormonal determinants.

jpa2_model.name: JPA-2 asymptotic growth model
jpa2_model.summary: JPA-2 is an asymptotic parametric model of human stature defined from birth rather than from age 2, so it spans infancy and puberty in a single function (jolicoeur1992). It descends from JPA-1, a lifetime asymptotic curve fitted to French longitudinal data (jolicoeur1988). Its value to this atlas is coverage rather than accuracy: because it reaches back to birth it supplies one continuous velocity function across the infancy-childhood transition, which Preece-Baines cannot reach at all and which the ICP model reaches only by summing components across a switch-on discontinuity. No head-to-head residual comparison of JPA-2 against Preece-Baines or against a nonparametric fit on the same individuals was located in this sweep, so the frequently repeated claim that JPA-2 fits better over the overlapping age range is at present untraceable to a primary and is graded X.

claim_grades.claim: JPA-2 models human stature from birth to adulthood with an asymptotic parametric form
claim_grades.basis: The published derivations (jolicoeur1992, jolicoeur1988).

claim_grades.claim: JPA-2 fits human stature better than Preece-Baines over the overlapping age range
claim_grades.basis: Repeated in review literature; no head-to-head residual comparison on the same individuals located. Logged as gap g_l9organism_002.

jpa2_model.human_evidence_note: Fitted only to human longitudinal stature series.
localization: human whole organism: serial recumbent length and standing height from birth

key_refs.one_line_finding: Presents asymptotic models (JPA family) for longitudinal human stature spanning birth to maturity.
JPA-1 lifetime asymptotic growth curve for human height fitted to French longitudinal data.

limb_segment_proportion.name: Limb segment proportions
limb_segment_proportion.summary: Arm span minus height, and the arm span/height ratio, index the relative output of the upper- and lower-limb growth plates and of the vertebral plates against each other. In Japanese national anthropometry of 6089 boys and 4970 girls aged 5.5-18.5 years, arm span rises throughout childhood with a marked acceleration at puberty and the arm span/height ratio rises slowly throughout childhood before plateauing (hirano2025). Two population facts fall out of the same analysis and constrain any universal mechanistic model: the Japanese ratio is lower than the Dutch and Turkish ratio at every age between 5.5 and 18.5 years, and it reaches its plateau earlier. Population differences in limb proportion are therefore not a simple consequence of differences in adult stature or in pubertal timing alone, since the plateau age and the ratio differ independently. Because arm span is dominated by the proximal humeral and distal radial physes while height is dominated by the distal femoral and proximal tibial physes (proximal_humerus_plate, distal_radius_plate, distal_femur_plate, proximal_tibia_plate in L1), the ratio is the cheapest organism-level readout of differential physeal velocity that exists, and a mechanistic model that predicts a single systemic growth signal must explain why these four plates respond to it in fixed but population-specific proportions.

claim_grades.claim: Arm span/height ratio rises through childhood and plateaus in adolescence
claim_grades.basis: LMS-smoothed reference curves from 11059 children.

claim_grades.claim: Population differences in limb proportion are independent of differences in the timing of the plateau
claim_grades.basis: Both differences observed in the same three-population comparison but not formally decomposed; the comparison is cross-sectional and the reference cohorts differ in decade of collection.

limb_segment_proportion.human_evidence_note: Two large national anthropometric surveys compared against two further published national references.
localization: human whole organism: arm span and standing height by standardised anthropometry

key_refs.one_line_finding: Japanese arm span and arm span/height references from 11059 children; the ratio is lower and plateaus earlier than in Dutch and Turkish children.
Dutch leg length and sitting height references providing the complementary lower-body proportion measures.

mandibular_condylar_cartilage.name: Mandibular condylar cartilage
mandibular_condylar_cartilage.summary: The mandibular condyle grows by a secondary cartilage that is structurally and lineally unlike a growth plate. It has no resting-proliferative-hypertrophic columnar organisation; instead a fibrous surface layer overlies a polymorphic progenitor layer whose cells express early osteoblast markers - alkaline phosphatase and Runx2 - and can be labelled by an osteoblast progenitor reporter (the 3.6 kb collagen type I fragment in rat), yet differentiate into chondrocytes when appropriately mechanically loaded (robinson2015). So the same progenitor can become bone or cartilage depending on load, whereas the growth plate's resting zone produces only chondrocytes. The consequence at the organism level is that mandibular length is load-responsive in a way that femoral length is not, which is the mechanistic basis for functional orthopaedic appliances and for the mandibular retrognathia seen in growth restriction (craniofacial_growth). All cellular evidence for the progenitor identity is rodent; no human condylar progenitor has been characterised, and the potency and regenerative capacity of these cells remain explicitly open even in rodent.

claim_grades.claim: Mandibular condylar cartilage is a secondary cartilage without growth-plate columnar zonation
claim_grades.basis: Consistent histological description across species including human autopsy material, though not quantified here.

claim_grades.claim: Condylar progenitors are osteoblast-lineage cells that become chondrogenic under mechanical load
claim_grades.basis: Rodent reporter data summarised in a review (robinson2015); the review itself states the potency of these cells remains in question.

mandibular_condylar_cartilage.human_evidence_note: No human mandibular condylar progenitor has been isolated or characterised; all cellular claims are rodent.
mandibular_condylar_cartilage.translation_risk_reason: The defining claim - that an osteoblast-lineage progenitor becomes chondrogenic under load - rests entirely on rodent reporters, and rodent mandibular growth differs in duration and loading regime from human.
localization: rat mandibular condyle: fibrous, polymorphic/progenitor, and chondrogenic layers
human mandibular condyle: uncharacterised at the cellular level

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mandibular condylar cartilage derives from ALP- and Runx2-expressing osteoblast-lineage progenitors that become chondrogenic under mechanical loading.
Mandibular size is disproportionately reduced (<= -1.7 SDS) in short subjects born SGA.

mid_parental_target_height.name: Mid-parental target height
mid_parental_target_height.summary: Target height is a child's mid-parental height corrected for sex, conventionally by adding 6.5 cm for a son or subtracting 6.5 cm for a daughter (equivalently, adding 13 cm to the mother's height before averaging), a procedure introduced by Tanner, Goldstein and Whitehouse (tanner1970) and still the recommended method. Three of its assumptions are demonstrably wrong. First, the sex correction is additive and constant, but in the CDC reference the male-female height difference at matched percentiles rises from 12.2 cm at the 3rd percentile to 14.7 cm at the 97th, and a multiplicative factor of 1.08 fits with R-squared = 1 (zeevi2024). Second, parental height is measured after adult height loss has begun, biasing target height downward: in a cohort with parents aged 62 +/- 5 years the children were 2.7 cm taller than predicted, and a nonlinear age correction reduced that bias to 0.06 cm (zeevi2024). Third, regression to the mean is ignored: the regression of standardised child height on standardised mid-parental height has a slope of about 0.79 (zeevi2024) and 0.75-0.78 in a population-based Swedish sample (luo1998), so the uncorrected method systematically underestimates the adult height of children of short parents - Luo found up to a 6 cm error by the Tanner method at mid-parental height below -2 SDS. Wright and Cheetham showed the practical consequence: of 13 children below the 2nd height centile, 8 appeared to be within the mid-parental 90% range, but only 3 remained so once regression to the mean was applied (wright1999).

claim_grades.claim: Mid-parental height explains only about 36-40% of the variance in adult child height
claim_grades.basis: Directly measured in 303 adult children of 23 large families with both parents measured (zeevi2024); consistent with the 0.75-0.78 parent-offspring regression slopes in a population sample of 2402 (luo1998).

claim_grades.claim: The additive 13 cm sex correction is wrong at the height extremes and a multiplicative 1.08 factor is correct
claim_grades.basis: Demonstrated arithmetically against CDC matched-percentile heights and validated by improved variance explained in one family cohort; not replicated in a second population.

claim_grades.claim: Ignoring regression to the mean systematically misclassifies short children
claim_grades.basis: Direct demonstration in a representative survey sample: 8 of 13 children below the 2nd centile appeared within the mid-parental 90% range, falling to 3 of 13 after correction (wright1999).

mid_parental_target_height.human_evidence_note: All data are measured adult heights of parents and their adult children in population-based and family-based human cohorts.
mid_parental_target_height.translation_risk_reason: A human clinical calculation with no animal counterpart.
localization: human whole organism: adult standing height of parents and offspring

key_refs.one_line_finding: Introduces parent-adjusted height standards and the corrected mid-parental target height method still in clinical use.
In 23 large nuclear families, uncorrected mid-parental height explains 36% of child height variance with a 2.7 cm downward bias; corrections raise this to 40% and remove the bias.
Population-based regression of adult height on mid-parental height with slopes 0.78 (boys) and 0.75 (girls) and a 95% prediction interval of about +/-10 cm.
Mid-parental height misclassifies short children unless regression to the mean is applied.
Reconsiders the arithmetic of target-height calculation; full text not retrieved in this sweep.

mini_puberty_infancy.name: Mini-puberty of infancy
mini_puberty_infancy.summary: Mini-puberty is the transient postnatal activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis that produces adult-range sex steroid concentrations in the first months of life. Its relevance to skeletal growth was until recently assumed rather than measured. In the Copenhagen Minipuberty Study, 189 healthy term appropriate-for-gestational-age infants (101 boys, 88 girls) were followed with repeated anthropometry and hormone measurement to 12 months: growth velocity declined in both sexes after birth but boys grew faster than girls for the first three months before the trajectories converged, and free testosterone was positively associated with growth velocity, most strongly in boys - shifting free testosterone from the 25th to the 75th percentile corresponded to a growth velocity 8.3 cm/yr higher (95% CI 3.5-15.3), of which 32.6% (95% CI 15.3-...) was mediated by IGF-I (pridik2026). This is an organism-level number with a direct mechanistic consequence: sex steroids act on the human growth plate to accelerate it months before any secondary sexual characteristic appears, and they do so partly through the somatotropic axis and partly not. It also establishes an initial condition, since the infant plate is exposed to androgen and estrogen concentrations it will not see again until puberty.

claim_grades.claim: Free testosterone during mini-puberty is associated with faster infant linear growth in boys
claim_grades.basis: Prospective cohort with repeated measures and a stated effect size with CI; observational, single cohort, no interventional confirmation.

claim_grades.claim: About one third of the association is mediated by IGF-I
claim_grades.basis: Mediation analysis in one observational cohort; mediation estimates are model-dependent and the reported CI is wide.

mini_puberty_infancy.human_evidence_note: Prospective population-based human birth cohort with repeated hormone and anthropometric measurement (NCT02784184).
mini_puberty_infancy.translation_risk_reason: Directly measured in human infants; rodents have a mini-puberty but not a comparable postnatal length trajectory.
localization: human whole organism: recumbent length velocity, 0-12 months, related to serum free testosterone and IGF-I

key_refs.one_line_finding: A 25th-to-75th percentile shift in free testosterone corresponds to an 8.3 cm/yr higher infant growth velocity in boys, 32.6% mediated by IGF-I.
Places the infancy-to-childhood control switch at 6-12 months, overlapping the end of mini-puberty.

muscle_bone_mechanical_coupling.name: Muscle-bone mechanical coupling
muscle_bone_mechanical_coupling.summary: The mechanostat predicts that bone strength is a consequence of the loads muscle imposes, so muscle growth should lead bone growth in time. Rauch and colleagues tested the prediction directly with longitudinal DXA in 70 boys and 68 girls through puberty. Peak whole-body lean mass accrual preceded peak bone mineral content accrual by 0.36 years in boys and 0.51 years in girls; in the arms the interval was 0.63 and 0.71 years and in the legs 0.48 and 0.22 years (rauch2004). The temporal ordering therefore holds at every site but with a site-specific lag - the arm lag is roughly three times the girls' leg lag - which a single systemic driver does not predict. The stronger result is the regression: peak lean mass velocity, but not peak height velocity and not sex, was independently associated with peak bone mineral content velocity, explaining 50% of the variance for the total body, 61% for the arms and 41% for the legs. Longitudinal bone growth is thus statistically dissociable from bone mineral accrual: whatever sets peak height velocity is not what sets peak bone mineral accrual. The authors are explicit that the data cannot exclude the alternative that muscle and bone development are independently determined genetically and merely correlated.

claim_grades.claim: Peak lean mass accrual precedes peak bone mineral accrual at every site measured
claim_grades.basis: Directly measured intervals at three anatomical levels in 138 children.

claim_grades.claim: Muscle growth causes bone mineral accrual
claim_grades.basis: The temporal precedence and the regression are compatible with causation but the authors state explicitly that independent genetic determination of both is not excluded; no interventional human data.

claim_grades.claim: Longitudinal growth and bone mineral accrual are driven by different variables
claim_grades.basis: Peak height velocity had no independent association with peak BMC velocity once lean mass velocity was in the model (rauch2004); one cohort.

muscle_bone_mechanical_coupling.human_evidence_note: Longitudinal DXA in 138 healthy children measured through the pubertal spurt.
localization: human whole body, arms and legs: DXA lean mass and bone mineral content

key_refs.one_line_finding: Peak lean mass velocity precedes and predicts peak bone mineral content velocity while peak height velocity does not.

muscle_hypertrophy_vs_hyperplasia.name: Muscle hypertrophy versus hyperplasia
muscle_hypertrophy_vs_hyperplasia.summary: The question of whether postnatal muscle grows by adding fibres or by enlarging them is settled in mouse and unsettled in human. In mouse EDL there is no net gain in myofibre number between P7 and adulthood while fibre volume rises 14.1-fold, so growth is essentially pure hypertrophy (white2010). This is the exact opposite of the growth plate, where elongation is generated by producing new cells that then enlarge and are removed, so the tissue turns over its cell population continuously; muscle keeps the same fibres for life and only adds nuclei to them, and only until P21 in mouse. The distinction has a direct consequence for how the two tissues can be perturbed: a muscle can be enlarged in adulthood by hypertrophic signalling because the hypertrophic mechanism is still available - ActRIIB blockade increases thigh muscle volume in adult men after casting-induced atrophy (rooks2017) - whereas the growth plate cannot be restarted after fusion because the cell-producing mechanism has been destroyed. Human fibre-number data across development are absent, and the claim that human muscle also fixes fibre number early rests on extrapolation from rodent.
muscle_hypertrophy_vs_hyperplasia.human_evidence_note: Human data show that adult muscle retains hypertrophic capacity but say nothing about fibre number during development.
muscle_hypertrophy_vs_hyperplasia.translation_risk_reason: Fibre-number constancy is established only in one mouse muscle; human developmental fibre counts do not exist.
localization: mouse EDL (white2010)
human thigh, MRI volume (rooks2017)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Mouse postnatal muscle growth is hypertrophic with no net change in fibre number.
ActRIIB blockade increases thigh muscle volume in adult men after casting-induced atrophy.

myostatin_mstn.name: Myostatin (MSTN, GDF8)
myostatin_mstn.summary: Myostatin is a TGF-beta superfamily ligand secreted by skeletal muscle that signals through ActRIIB and restrains muscle mass. The human evidence is a single reported case: a child with a loss-of-function MSTN mutation and gross muscle hypertrophy (schuelke2004). The organism-level significance for this atlas is what did not happen in that child - the phenotype reported is muscular, not skeletal, so a pathway that doubles muscle mass does not correspondingly change stature. That dissociates the myostatin axis from the growth plate and constrains the mechanostat account of longitudinal growth: if increased muscle force drove bone elongation, myostatin loss should lengthen bones, and no such report exists. Pharmacological confirmation runs the same way in adults: blocking the receptor with bimagrumab increases thigh muscle volume in men recovering from casting-induced atrophy (rooks2017) without any claim on bone length. The full text of the index human case was not retrieved in this sweep, so no genotype detail or muscle-mass quantity is asserted here.

claim_grades.claim: Human MSTN loss of function causes gross muscle hypertrophy
claim_grades.basis: One published case (schuelke2004); no abstract retrievable and the full text was not obtained in this sweep.

claim_grades.claim: Myostatin-axis manipulation increases muscle mass without a reported effect on stature
claim_grades.basis: An argument from absence: no skeletal-length phenotype is reported in the human case or the blockade trial. Absence of report is not absence of effect, and the point is flagged as inference.

myostatin_mstn.human_evidence_note: A single human loss-of-function case plus a randomised human pharmacological blockade study of the receptor.
myostatin_mstn.translation_risk_reason: The claims recorded here are human; murine myostatin biology is extensive but not relied on for these statements.
localization: human skeletal muscle: secreted ligand
human serum

key_refs.one_line_finding: Reports a myostatin mutation associated with gross muscle hypertrophy in a child.
Bimagrumab, an ActRIIB blocker, increases thigh muscle volume in adult men after casting-induced atrophy.

preece_baines_model.name: Preece-Baines growth model
preece_baines_model.summary: Preece and Baines derived a family of growth functions from the differential equation dh/dt = s(t)(h1 - h), where h1 is adult size and s(t) a time-varying rate function; different choices of s(t) generate different family members (preece1978). Model 1, with five parameters, is the version in universal use for pubertal height; it fits an individual curve from age 2 to maturity with a residual SD of 6-7 mm, the benchmark against which later models are judged (cole2010, which independently reproduces 0.79 cm in 3245 boys). Derived quantities - peak height velocity, age at peak height velocity, age at take-off - are read off the fitted curve rather than from raw increments, which makes them far more stable than difference-based estimates, and a published erratum supplies the direct algebraic expressions for them (sayers2013). Two documented failures constrain use: the function contains no term capable of representing the mid-growth spurt, and fitted to Fels serial data it places pubertal-spurt onset earlier, the spurt longer and the velocity rise slower than kernel regression or a triple-logistic model on the same children (guo1992). The residual SD of 6-7 mm is the operative number for this atlas: it is comparable to diurnal stature variation, so a plate-level model that claims to reproduce individual height to better than about 7 mm is fitting measurement structure rather than biology.

claim_grades.claim: PB model 1 fits individual pubertal height with residual SD 6-7 mm
claim_grades.basis: Stated in the original derivation and independently reproduced as 0.79 cm in 3245 boys with 129508 measurements (cole2010).

claim_grades.claim: PB cannot represent the mid-growth spurt and biases pubertal spurt parameters relative to nonparametric fits
claim_grades.basis: Direct comparison of PB, triple logistic and kernel regression on 227 Fels participants (guo1992); one cohort only.

preece_baines_model.human_evidence_note: Constructed and validated on human longitudinal stature series only.
localization: human whole organism: serial standing height

key_refs.one_line_finding: Derives the PB family; model 1 with five parameters fits stature from age 2 to maturity better than earlier models.
Erratum giving direct algebraic calculation of peak height velocity, age at take-off and related quantities from PB parameters.
Quotes and reproduces the PB residual SD of 6-7 mm as the benchmark that SITAR matches.
PB places pubertal spurt onset earlier and the velocity rise slower than kernel regression on the same Fels children and cannot describe the midgrowth spurt.

satellite_cell.name: Muscle satellite cell
satellite_cell.summary: Satellite cells are the Pax7-positive resident stem cells of skeletal muscle, lying between the myofibre plasma membrane and the basal lamina, and they are the only source of new myonuclei during postnatal muscle growth. Their behaviour during growth is phasic and, in mouse, well quantified: satellite cell number per EDL myofibre is about 14 at postnatal day 7 and falls to the adult level of about 5 by P21, exactly the point at which myonuclear addition to the growing fibre stops (white2010). Muscle continues to enlarge after P21 without further nuclear accretion, so the satellite cell pool is not rate-limiting for late hypertrophy in normal growth. The parallel with the growth plate resting zone is structural rather than demonstrated: both are quiescent stem pools that contract as growth proceeds, but no experiment has tested whether the two pools deplete on a shared schedule or respond to a shared signal. In humans, satellite cell density has been counted mainly in pathology - contractured muscle in cerebral palsy has reduced satellite cell number in situ (dayanidhi2015) - and no normal human developmental series exists.
satellite_cell.human_evidence_note: Human satellite cell counts exist only in pathological muscle; there is no normal human developmental series.
satellite_cell.translation_risk_reason: The entire developmental trajectory of the satellite cell pool is murine and compressed into three weeks; the human equivalent spans nearly two decades and is unmeasured.
localization: mouse EDL: sublaminar satellite cells counted on isolated fibres
human contractured muscle: in situ counts (dayanidhi2015)

key_refs.one_line_finding: Satellite cells per mouse EDL fibre fall from about 14 at P7 to about 5 by P21, coincident with the end of myonuclear addition.
Satellite cell number is reduced in situ in muscular contractures from children with cerebral palsy.

sitar_model.name: SITAR shape-invariant growth model
sitar_model.summary: SITAR fits one mean spline curve to all subjects and gives each individual three random effects: size (vertical shift, cm), tempo (horizontal shift, years) and velocity (age-scale stretch, fractional) (cole2010). Its importance here is that it partitions between-individual variance into interpretable pieces, and the partition is lopsided. In 3245 Christ's Hospital boys with 129508 heights, adjusting for size alone cut the residual SD from 6.6 cm to 2.3 cm, adding tempo cut it to 1.2 cm, and adding velocity cut it to 0.8 cm - a 98.9% variance reduction from three numbers per child. The final residual SD of 0.79 cm matches the median residual of individually fitted five-parameter Preece-Baines curves, so three population-level parameters buy the same fit as five individual ones. The random-effect SDs are the organism-level dispersion numbers a mechanistic model must reproduce: size SD 6.1 cm, tempo SD 0.97 years, velocity SD 0.15, that is a 15% between-child spread in how fast the pubertal clock runs. The three axes correlate with each other only at about +0.3 in healthy boys, so growing tall, growing late and growing fast are largely separable; in Turner syndrome the tempo-velocity correlation reverses to -0.46, showing the correlation structure is not a property of the method.

claim_grades.claim: Three random effects explain 98.9% of the between-child variance in pubertal height
claim_grades.basis: Direct fit to 129508 heights in 3245 boys with the stepwise residual reduction reported.

claim_grades.claim: Size, tempo and velocity are largely independent axes of variation
claim_grades.basis: Pairwise correlations near +0.3 in one large male cohort; the tempo-velocity correlation reverses sign in Turner syndrome, so independence is cohort-specific.

sitar_model.human_evidence_note: Fitted directly to two human longitudinal height datasets totalling 130829 measurements.
localization: human whole organism: serial standing height, ages 9-19 in both example cohorts

key_refs.one_line_finding: SITAR reduces residual SD from 6.6 cm to 0.79 cm with three random effects per child, matching individually fitted Preece-Baines curves.
Applies SITAR to Korean children to derive pubertal onset, PHV magnitude and PHV timing.
Bayesian SITAR in Brazilian children stratified by maturity group.

sitting_height_ratio.name: Sitting height ratio
sitting_height_ratio.summary: Sitting height divided by standing height measures the trunk's share of stature and therefore reports directly on the difference in output between vertebral and lower-limb growth plates in the same child. The ratio falls steeply through infancy and childhood as the legs outgrow the trunk, then rises again during and after the pubertal spurt as vertebral growth continues after the lower-limb plates have decelerated - which is why disproportion is detectable at some ages and not others. Dutch nationwide references from 14500 children aged 0-21 years give age- and sex-specific LMS-smoothed centiles (fredriks2005). The clinically decisive finding in that reference is that SH/H SDS is not independent of height SDS: they are negatively correlated, so in a child with height SDS below -2 the conventional +2 SD cut-off generates too many false positives and must be shifted to +2.5 SD, while in exceptionally tall children the lower cut-off must be shifted to -2.2 SDS. Sensitivity of the height-corrected cut-off is 80% for hypochondroplasia but only 30% for Marfan syndrome, so a normal ratio does not exclude disproportionate growth. The ICP decomposition attributes the childhood fall in the ratio to a greater influence of the childhood growth component on the legs than on the trunk (karlberg1989), which if correct predicts that the growth-hormone-dependent phase acts preferentially on the lower-limb physes - a site-specific prediction that has never been tested at the level of the plate.

claim_grades.claim: Age- and sex-specific SH/H reference centiles exist and SH/H SDS depends on height SDS
claim_grades.basis: Direct measurement in 14500 children with the dependency quantified across three age strata (fredriks2005).

claim_grades.claim: The childhood growth component acts preferentially on the legs relative to the trunk
claim_grades.basis: A model-derived inference from the ICP decomposition (karlberg1989), never tested against site-specific plate measurements.

sitting_height_ratio.human_evidence_note: Nationwide cross-sectional anthropometry in 14500 children plus two disease comparison groups.
sitting_height_ratio.translation_risk_reason: A human anthropometric ratio; quadrupeds have no comparable trunk/limb partition of stature.
localization: human whole organism: sitting height and standing height by stadiometer and sitting-height table

key_refs.one_line_finding: Dutch nationwide SH, leg length and SH/H references from 14500 children, with height-corrected cut-offs and disease sensitivities.
Attributes the childhood change in body proportions to a stronger childhood-component effect on legs than on trunk.

skeletal_muscle_growth.name: Skeletal muscle growth
skeletal_muscle_growth.summary: Postnatal skeletal muscle grows almost entirely by enlarging existing fibres, not by making new ones, and this is the structural difference between muscle growth and bone elongation. In mouse extensor digitorum longus there is no net change in myofibre number between postnatal day 7 and adulthood, while myofibre cross-sectional area increases 7.6-fold and length 1.9-fold, giving a 14.1-fold increase in fibre volume (white2010). Because muscle is a syncytium, that hypertrophy requires nuclei: myonuclear number per fibre rises about 5-fold between P3 and P21 and then stops, so all subsequent volume growth expands the myonuclear domain, which doubles to 9.2 x 10^3 um3 by P21 and then triples again to 26.5 x 10^3 um3 by P56 (white2010, mouse). Satellite cell number per fibre falls from about 14 at P7 to the adult level of about 5 by P21, i.e. the progenitor pool contracts as the nuclear-accretion phase ends. The organism-level coupling to the skeleton is temporal and measurable in humans: peak lean-mass accrual velocity precedes peak bone mineral content accrual by 0.36 years in boys and 0.51 years in girls (rauch2004). No equivalent human measurement of myofibre number, myonuclear accretion or satellite cell density across postnatal growth exists, so the phase structure above is mouse and must not be stated as human fact.

claim_grades.claim: Postnatal muscle growth is hypertrophic with fibre number fixed early
claim_grades.basis: Directly counted in mouse EDL across the full postnatal period (white2010); no human counterpart.

claim_grades.claim: Peak lean mass velocity precedes peak bone mineral accrual in humans
claim_grades.basis: Longitudinal DXA in 138 children with the interval measured at three anatomical levels (rauch2004).

skeletal_muscle_growth.human_evidence_note: Human evidence is limited to DXA-derived whole-body lean mass velocity; the cellular growth mode is entirely murine.

suture_fusion_timing.name: Cranial suture fusion timing
suture_fusion_timing.summary: Cranial sutures are the intramembranous growth sites of the calvaria and their patency is what allows the vault to expand with the brain. The textbook statement that the major sutures close during the third decade is wrong for a substantial minority of children. In 1119 healthy children aged 0-18 imaged by high-resolution head CT for unrelated reasons, with craniofacial disorders, syndromes, fractures and intracranial pathology excluded, complete or partial sagittal suture closure was present in 11.1%, coronal closure in 2.8% and lambdoid closure in 1.6%; up to 17% had some asymptomatic calvarial suture closure before adulthood (han2025). Sagittal patency fell from 99.3% under age three to 83% by age nine. The metopic suture behaved as the textbooks describe, with over 75% closed by 21 months. Closure was not morphologically silent - sagittal closure was associated with a lower cephalic index (beta -0.8, p=0.026) and 86.4% of children with a cephalic index below 70 had partial or complete sagittal closure - but 83.1% of children with sagittal closure remained normocephalic. The organism-level significance is that the calvarial growth sites finish long before the long bones, and they do so on a schedule that tracks brain growth rather than the pubertal spurt.

claim_grades.claim: Up to 17% of healthy children have asymptomatic calvarial suture closure before adulthood
claim_grades.basis: Direct CT assessment of 1119 children by three neuroradiologists with explicit exclusion criteria.

claim_grades.claim: The classical teaching that the major sutures close in the third decade is wrong
claim_grades.basis: Directly contradicted by the same measurement: sagittal patency falls from 99.3% under age 3 to 83% by age 9.

target_height_predictive_sd.name: Predictive SD of mid-parental target height
target_height_predictive_sd.summary: The number a clinician needs from target height is not the point estimate but its predictive SD, because that SD defines what counts as an abnormal deviation. The value in routine use, 'mid-parental height plus or minus 8.5 cm', was not measured: Tanner and colleagues derived it from theoretical considerations as the 3rd-to-97th centile band (tanner1970, as documented by zeevi2024), later revised it to +/-9 cm for girls and +/-10 cm for boys, and other authorities recommend +/-1.64 SDS, which under CDC standards is +/-10.6 cm for girls and +/-11.7 cm for boys. These three bands imply predictive SDs of about 4.5, 4.8-5.3 and 6.5-7.1 cm respectively for the same quantity. The direct empirical measurement, made only in 2024, gives the residual SD of adult child height about the fully corrected target height as 4.7 cm for sons and 4.4 cm for daughters pooled across families, and 4.5 +/- 0.9 cm and 4.2 +/- 0.8 cm within families (zeevi2024, n=303 adult children from 23 families with 7-16 children each). The independent population-based estimate is wider: Luo and colleagues report a 95% prediction interval of about +/-10 cm around the regression estimate in 2402 Swedes, implying a predictive SD near 5.1 cm (luo1998). So the honest number is a predictive SD of 4.4-5.1 cm, and the widely quoted +/-8.5 cm is best read as a theoretically derived ~1.9 SD band, not the 2 SD band it is usually assumed to be. The residual dispersion is not larger for taller parents (zeevi2024, r=0.38, p=0.08), consistent with the population-based finding, so a single SD can be used across the height range once the mean is corrected.

tooth_mineralization_stages.name: Tooth mineralization staging
tooth_mineralization_stages.summary: Demirjian, Goldstein and Tanner defined dental maturity as an eight-stage ordinal score of crown and root mineralization applied to the seven left mandibular permanent teeth on a panoramic radiograph, converted to a 0-100 maturity score and then to a dental age (demirjian1973). The method's design choices are what make it useful as an independent clock: stages are defined by shape changes rather than by absolute length, so they are invariant to radiographic magnification and to body size, and the scoring is confined to one side of one jaw, so it does not average across skeletal sites the way bone-age scoring does. Its known limitation is that the original standard is French-Canadian and systematically overestimates dental age in other populations; a recent Iranian orthodontic series found the Demirjian method overestimated dental age while still correlating with chronological age at r = 0.894 in males and 0.876 in females and with cervical-vertebral skeletal stage at Spearman 0.779 and 0.785 (mohammadianras2026). The mineralization sequence itself, unlike the growth plate, is not a rate process that can be transiently suppressed and resumed: each stage is a one-way morphological transition, which is the structural reason the dental clock is robust to systemic perturbation.

claim_grades.claim: Dental maturity can be scored as an eight-stage shape-based ordinal system with a population conversion to dental age
claim_grades.basis: The original derivation (demirjian1973) and universal subsequent use.

claim_grades.claim: The original standard overestimates dental age outside its source population
claim_grades.basis: Reported in one 194-patient Iranian series (mohammadianras2026) and widely observed elsewhere; magnitude is population-specific and not pooled here.

visceral_organ_growth.name: Visceral organ growth
visceral_organ_growth.summary: Internal organs do not grow on the skeletal schedule, and organ weight references are the quantitative record of that. The largest contemporary single-centre reference derives LMS-smoothed 5th to 95th centile weight charts for heart, lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, pancreas, thymus and adrenals from 1190 of 1525 consecutive infant autopsies over 14 years (pryce2014). Two of those organs are the strongest counterexamples to a common growth clock: the thymus is largest in absolute terms in early childhood and involutes from puberty onward, and the adrenal cortex loses its fetal zone in the first postnatal months and regrows a functionally distinct zona reticularis at adrenarche. So within a single individual, at the moment the growth plate is accelerating toward peak height velocity, at least one organ is regressing. This is an organism-level constraint rather than a plate mechanism, but it bounds what a systemic signal can be: no circulating factor whose concentration rises through puberty can be the sole driver of organ size, because organ responses at that time have opposite signs. Postnatal organ weight references beyond infancy were not located in this sweep and are logged as a gap.

claim_grades.basis: Direct measurement in 1190 modelled cases from 1525 consecutive autopsies.

who_growth_standard.name: WHO Child Growth Standards
who_growth_standard.summary: The WHO Child Growth Standards are prescriptive rather than descriptive: they were built from children raised under conditions defined a priori as growth-permitting (breastfeeding, non-smoking mothers, adequate nutrition, no major morbidity) in six sites on five continents, so they describe how children should grow rather than how a given population does grow. The decisive empirical result underpinning that design is that between-site variance in linear growth was small: site differences accounted for only about 3% of the variance in length, while individual differences within sites accounted for about 70% (who2006). This is the strongest single piece of evidence that under permissive conditions the human linear-growth trajectory is close to species-universal in the first five years, which in turn is what licenses the atlas to treat early growth-velocity targets as a property of the organism rather than of a population. The companion velocity standards give 1-, 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-month length increments with percentiles from birth to 24 months (who_velocity_2009), and these differ systematically from US reference increments, most at the lower percentiles (de2011) - so the choice of reference changes what counts as growth faltering more than it changes the median.

claim_grades.claim: Under growth-permitting conditions, site of origin explains only about 3% of variance in early linear growth
claim_grades.basis: Prospective multicentre design with prescriptive inclusion criteria and formal variance decomposition (who2006).

claim_grades.claim: The WHO velocity standards are the appropriate tool for detecting growth faltering in infancy
claim_grades.basis: Argued by de2011 from the divergence between WHO and US increments; this is an inference about clinical utility rather than a measured outcome.

edges.magnitude: one lost allele costs approximately 1.4 SDS of height: 16 heterozygous carriers -1.8 +/- 1.1 SDS versus 23 non-carrier relatives -0.4 +/- 0.8 SDS in the same family (P<0.0005); 7 heterozygous variants in 192 short-stature patients versus 0 in 192 height-normal controls; ~3% yield in SHOX-negative Leri-Weill referrals
edges.context: human, heterozygous, both sexes; within-family design controls for shared environment and background; zone unknown (not reported), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: lifelong; the deficit is present through childhood and worsens with age

edges.magnitude: three mechanistically distinct activating classes: V883M (cyclase domain) generates cGMP with no CNP present; R655C (kinase homology domain) amplifies the CNP response and its ATP stabilisation and heterodimerises dominantly with wild-type receptor; plus an activating submembrane deletion
edges.context: human, heterozygous, three-generation family for V883M; single probands for the others; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 4 sources), childhood, pubertal, adult (15-year-old/18 week-old/8-week-old; 37-year-old/5 years old)
edges.notes: V883M (tall WITH scoliosis and macrodactyly) and R655C (tall WITHOUT skeletal deformity) show that ligand-independent basal signalling and amplified ligand-dependent signalling are not interchangeable in the growth plate. No pooled effect size in cm or SDS exists for NPR2 gain of function.

edges.magnitude: blood cGMP elevated in affected members of the V883M family; mutant receptor generated cGMP in HEK293A cells in the complete absence of CNP where wild type did not. In the R655C proband plasma NT-proCNP was REDUCED, i.e. augmented receptor activity feeds back onto ligand production.
edges.context: human blood (not growth plate) plus transfected human cell line; the only setting in which the transducer and the stature phenotype have been measured in the same people; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), pubertal (15-year-old/18 week-old/8-week-old)

edges.magnitude: plasma CNP 2-fold above five controls in the de novo t(2;7)(q37.1;q21.3) proband with a breakpoint adjacent to NPPC, with substantially raised NPPC expression in the proband's fibroblasts; an independent t(1;2)(q41;q37.1) with a breakpoint 200,365 bp downstream of NPPC raised serum NT-proCNP
edges.context: human, two independent de novo balanced translocations at the same locus, same phenotype, same biomarker; zone unknown (not reported), female only (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: not quantified - ligand concentration was measured, receptor output was not
edges.context: human; inferred from ligand dosage. Supported independently from the clearance side: biallelic NPR3 loss of function, which raises local CNP without changing NPPC, causes tall stature with skeletal overgrowth; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), pubertal (14-year-old)
edges.notes: Written at C rather than A because no receptor-level or cGMP measurement exists in NPPC-duplication patients; the ligand-to-receptor step is inferred from the dose-response of the series as a whole.

edges.magnitude: ligand-independent cAMP accumulation from heterozygous activating alleles; H223R in 18/24 patients in the natural-history series, plus T410P, T410R (father and two sons), I458R and I458K
edges.context: human, heterozygous, both sexes; cAMP measured in COS-7 cells expressing the mutant receptor. The growth plate itself remains undescribed in living patients; bone histomorphometry exists in 2 children; zone unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: HALF 1 OF 2 of the matched human PTH1R pair. Partner edge e00020 carries the opposite sign.

edges.magnitude: homozygous P132L abolishes both PTH- and PTHrP-stimulated cAMP accumulation and radioligand binding while the mutant protein still reaches the cell surface of the affected infant's OWN growth plate chondrocytes - so the defect is binding, not trafficking; an independent exon-M5 splice allele abolished PTH-induced inositol phosphate accumulation as well as cAMP
edges.context: human, biallelic, perinatally lethal; receptor pharmacology in COS-1/COS-7 cells plus direct immunolocalisation in patient growth plate chondrocytes; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: constitutive from fetal life; lethal in the perinatal period
edges.notes: HALF 2 OF 2 of the matched human PTH1R pair. Jansen and Blomstrand are the same receptor perturbed in opposite directions in humans, and together they establish the direction of the timing control without requiring any animal model.

edges.magnitude: constitutive PTH1R signalling holds chondrocytes in the proliferative state and DELAYS exit into hypertrophy, giving markedly delayed and disorganised metaphyseal mineralisation with severe short stature
edges.context: human, heterozygous; the mouse counterpart (targeted expression of the Jansen H223R receptor in growth plate) reproduces delayed hypertrophic differentiation; sex unknown (not reported in source), neonatal, adult
edges.timescale: years - the phenotype is the integral of a per-cycle timing shift over childhood

edges.magnitude: extremely ADVANCED endochondral bone maturation - the exact phenotypic mirror of Jansen - lethal in the perinatal period
edges.context: human, biallelic; matches the mouse Pthlh-null and Pth1r-null acceleration of hypertrophy; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: fetal; the whole phenotype is expressed before birth
edges.notes: Read against e00021, the pair establishes in humans what the mouse knockouts establish in mice: PTH1R signalling sets the timing of the proliferative-to-hypertrophic transition, more signal delays it and less signal advances it, and stature is the integral of that timing decision.

edges.magnitude: brachydactyly, most characteristically of the fourth and fifth metacarpals, produced by PREMATURE closure of the affected growth plates, with only mild overall short stature
edges.context: human; the lesion is in GNAS (Gs-alpha) or its imprinting, one step DISTAL to an intact PTH1R, so this edge represents loss of pathway output rather than loss of receptor. Partial and tissue-restricted by imprinting, which is why the phenotype is site-selective rather than lethal; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), infant, childhood, pubertal, adult (1-year-old/12-year-old/18-year-old)
edges.timescale: childhood - selective plates close early while others continue
edges.notes: The third member of the human PTH1R series: reduced PTHrP-PTH1R-cAMP signalling accelerates exit of proliferative chondrocytes into hypertrophy, the exact opposite of Jansen.

edges.magnitude: germline gain-of-function PTPN11 (commonest), SOS1, RAF1 and RIT1 raise RAS/MAPK flux. In the genotyped 101-patient cohort birth length was ALREADY REDUCED at -1.23 SDS [-1.74; -0.57], so growth failure is not purely postnatal; adult height approaches the lower limit of normal rather than falling into the skeletal dysplasia range.
edges.context: human, heterozygous germline, both sexes; MAPK flux has been measured in patient-derived non-cartilage cells only, never in human growth plate. Family-based cohorts carry a polygenic confounder - in a 101-patient genotyped cohort the fathers were themselves -0.33 SDS; zone unknown (not reported), neonatal, juvenile, pubertal (mean age 11 year)
edges.notes: Mechanistically adjacent to achondroplasia - the same cascade - and it bounds how much of the achondroplasia phenotype scalar MAPK activation alone can explain: raising RAS/MAPK flux germline costs roughly 1-2 SDS, not the 6 SDS of achondroplasia. FRAGILITY-VERIFY 2026-08-05 (audit/fragility.md): The magnitude statement previously read "birth length is usually normal and growth failure is postnatal". Its own primary, jirova2026, reports birth length -1.23 SDS in the same cohort the edge cites. Corrected to the measured value. This is the one defect in the verified set where the edge contradicted the paper it cited rather than merely overreaching beyond it.

edges.magnitude: tall stature with dolichostenomelia - reduced upper:lower segment ratio and arm span exceeding height, i.e. the long-bone plates overgrow relative to the vertebral plates
edges.context: human, heterozygous FBN1; the increased-free-TGF-beta model rests on the microfibril-sequestration role of fibrillin-1 and has NOT been demonstrated in human cartilage or growth plate tissue; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), pubertal (mean age 13 year)
edges.notes: Sign is opposite to every other structural-matrix disorder in L11. Consistent in direction with the mouse result that the canonical TGF-beta arm restrains terminal differentiation, so more signal should delay hypertrophy and lengthen the growth period - but that chain is inferred, not measured.

edges.magnitude: heterozygous TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD3, TGFB2 or TGFB3 mutations giving marfanoid habitus with skeletal overgrowth, arachnodactyly and scoliosis
edges.context: human, heterozygous; no growth plate specimen from a Loeys-Dietz patient has been assayed, and the human phenotype is dominated by aortic rather than skeletal disease; zone unknown (not reported), female only (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The receptor-level control for Marfan, and it exposes an unresolved paradox: receptor loss-of-function produces an overgrowth phenotype resembling ligand excess. One human double perturbation is on record - the t(1;2)(q41;q37.1) patient carried both an NPPC gain and TGFB2 haploinsufficiency, so that individual's overgrowth cannot be attributed to either lesion alone.

edges.magnitude: heterozygous loss by point mutation, whole-gene deletion, or a 4.2 kb deletion of the 3' untranslated region; intramembranous bone (clavicle, cranial vault) severely affected while endochondral long bones are comparatively spared and stature is only mildly to moderately reduced
