edges.context: human, heterozygous, both sexes; zone unknown (not reported), neonatal, juvenile
edges.timescale: constitutive; the skeletal distribution is fixed developmentally
edges.notes: The asymmetric dose sensitivity is the point: one functional RUNX2 allele is nearly sufficient for the hypertrophic transition in the growth plate while being clearly insufficient for intramembranous bone, in the same individual.

edges.magnitude: heterozygous loss of function: adult height median -2.8 SDS (range -5.9 to -0.9) versus childhood height -2.0 SDS in the same 103 individuals from 20 families, with bone age advanced by a median +1.3 years (range 0 to +3.7)
edges.context: human, heterozygous, 57 female and 46 male; variants cosegregated perfectly with phenotype; hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), juvenile, childhood, pubertal, adult (12-year-old/58-year-old/6-year-old)
edges.timescale: lifelong; the adult deficit EXCEEDS the childhood deficit because growth stops early, so the plate both grows less per year and exhausts sooner
edges.notes: Dissociates height from skeletal maturation. Advanced bone age is not obligate - ACAN mutations also occur in nonfamilial short stature without accelerated skeletal maturation. The cellular mechanism (reduced matrix and impaired hypertrophy with proliferation spared) is MOUSE only.

edges.magnitude: COL10A1 mutations concentrated in the C-terminal NC1 trimerisation domain prevent normal trimer assembly; the modern mechanism is ER stress from misfolded collagen X retained in hypertrophic chondrocytes rather than simple haploinsufficiency
edges.context: human, heterozygous; COL10A1 is expressed ONLY by hypertrophic chondrocytes, so the phenotype is a pure hypertrophic-zone readout - irregular cupped metaphyses with normal epiphyses and normal spine; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: childhood; adult height usually only mildly reduced
edges.notes: Abstract-only source for the mutation series. The structure-function mapping is among the sharpest in human skeletal genetics: the zone in which a matrix gene is expressed predicts which radiographic compartment fails. Eliminating a hypertrophic-zone matrix protein costs surprisingly little final height.

edges.magnitude: biallelic GHR mutation (homozygous change at codon 180 of exon 6 in the large Ecuadorian cohort) abolishes GH signal transduction; circulating GH is normal or high, biologically normal and completely ineffective
edges.context: human, biallelic, both sexes, n=201 adults with carrier and non-carrier relative controls; zone unknown (not reported), adult

edges.magnitude: IGF-I low to undetectable; in 201 adults serum IGF-I correlated positively (logarithmically) with every body measurement and NEGATIVELY with head-circumference/height. GH-insensitive adults had the LOWEST lower-segment/height and the HIGHEST upper-segment/height ratios.
edges.context: human, biallelic GHR deficiency, both sexes, adults; zone unknown (not reported), adult
edges.notes: GH-IGF-I loss produces DISproportionate growth, contradicting the textbook assumption that the axis scales the body uniformly - it acts preferentially on the long bones of the lower limb.

edges.magnitude: not measured in any Laron patient
edges.context: human; flagged inference from the canonical GHR-JAK2-STAT5B architecture. JAK2 activation has never been assayed in GHR-deficient human tissue; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), adult

edges.magnitude: homozygous single-nucleotide insertion in STAT5B exon 10 causing frameshift, early termination and complete absence of immunodetectable STAT5b protein; a separate natural A630P SH2-domain allele functions neither as a signal transducer nor as a transcription factor
edges.context: human, biallelic, consanguineous pedigree; case-level (n=1 index patient plus a second allele); zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Places the lesion one step below the GH receptor and shows the entire growth-promoting output of GH runs through a single transcription factor. STAT5B deficiency is also an immunodeficiency - the pleiotropy is a mechanistic clue, not noise.

edges.magnitude: serum IGF-I 7.2 ng/mL against a quoted normal range of 242-600, with no rise on an IGF-I generation test despite normal-to-elevated GH and GH-binding protein; height 114 cm at 16.4 years = -7.8 SDS
edges.context: human, biallelic STAT5B null, female index patient; zone unknown (not reported), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: serum IGFBP-3 543 ng/mL against a quoted normal range of 2500-4800
edges.context: human, biallelic STAT5B null, single patient; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: serum acid-labile subunit 1.22 ug/mL against a quoted normal range of 5.6-16
edges.context: human, biallelic STAT5B null, single patient; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: With e00034 and e00035 this shows STAT5b drives the whole ternary complex, not IGF-I alone - which is why the circulating IGF-I deficit is not simply correctable by giving IGF-I.

edges.magnitude: biallelic CYP19A1 mutation; estradiol and estrone below 7 pg/mL with testosterone 2015 ng/dL in the index 24 3/12-year-old man, i.e. substrate accumulates unconverted
edges.context: human, biallelic, affected in XX as well as XY individuals; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), pubertal

edges.magnitude: homozygous C-to-T at codon 157 giving a premature stop in exon 2; six months of transdermal estrogen producing a 10-fold rise in free estradiol had NO detectable effect, with serum estradiol and estrone already elevated at baseline
edges.context: human, biallelic, n=1 male, 28 years old; zone unknown (not reported), adult (28-year-old)
edges.timescale: lifelong; the 6-month challenge is the interventional test
edges.notes: The receptor-side counterpart of aromatase deficiency; rules out the alternative that aromatase deficiency acts through some non-estrogenic product of the enzyme.

edges.magnitude: two distinct mechanisms giving the same phenotype: compound heterozygous R108Q/K115N reduced receptor FUNCTION in cultured fibroblasts; a nonsense R59X allele reduced receptor NUMBER. Neither class was present in 43 birth-weight-normal controls.
edges.context: human, two children; IUGR followed by poor postnatal growth WITH high circulating IGF-I; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Fewer receptors versus worse receptors producing the same phenotype is the human demonstration that IGF-I signalling CAPACITY, not receptor identity, sets prenatal and postnatal skeletal growth.

edges.magnitude: homozygous p.D643fs25* and p.A1033V both abolish PAPP-A2 proteolytic activity against IGFBP-3 and IGFBP-5 in vitro; total IGF-I, IGF-II, IGFBP-3, IGFBP-5 and ALS are all ELEVATED while FREE IGF-I is DECREASED, with more IGF-I retained in the ternary complex on size-exclusion chromatography
edges.context: human, biallelic, members of two unrelated families; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile, pubertal
edges.notes: The cleanest human demonstration that the growth plate responds to FREE rather than total IGF-I - a distinction invisible to every routine assay.

edges.magnitude: urinary cGMP response near saturation at 15 ug/kg/day, the approved dose, and the endochondral ossification marker CXM is also maximal there. CRITICALLY, in a PK/PD analysis drug exposure correlated with urine cGMP but did NOT correlate with growth outcome within the treated cohort.
edges.context: human, achondroplasia, ages 5-14 y at screening; the measurement is URINE, not growth plate. cGMP has never been measured in a human growth plate; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile
edges.timescale: urinary cGMP responds within days of dosing; the growth endpoint is read at 52 weeks
edges.notes: Exposure predicts systemic target ENGAGEMENT but not EFFECT. This is one of the three legs of contradiction C-L3-03 and must not be read as showing the gating question is settled.

edges.magnitude: never measured
edges.context: human dosing; PKG-II activity has not been measured in any treated human or animal. NPR2 protein is reported at similar levels across all three growth plate zones whereas PKG-I/II is strongly hypertrophic-biased (mouse), so receptor occupancy and pathway output need not be co-located; sex unknown (not reported in source), fetal (E15.5)
edges.notes: One of three competing hypotheses for why CNP-analogue efficacy may be gated DOWNSTREAM of the receptor the drug binds (contradiction C-L3-03). This edge asserts the link is UNTESTED, not that it is absent.

edges.magnitude: never measured
edges.context: human dosing, achondroplasia aged 2-11 y; as for vosoritide, no PKG-II readout exists in any species after CNP-analogue exposure; zones resolved in source: hypertrophic zone, perichondrium, sex unknown (not reported in source), fetal (E15.5)

edges.magnitude: dose-dependent plasma cGMP rise across 0.006-0.1 mg/kg/week; released CNP steady-state Cmax 36.0 pmol/L and weekly AUC 4410 h*pmol/L at 0.1 mg/kg/week
edges.context: human, achondroplasia, ages 2-11 y, weekly subcutaneous; plasma, not growth plate; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: steady state reached after approximately three weekly doses; released-CNP half-life 5.3 days

edges.magnitude: pooled placebo-controlled class effect on annualised growth velocity 1.36 cm/yr (95% CI 1.05-1.68), 4 RCTs, n=326; the ceiling has not moved across a ~300-fold change in exposure duration
edges.context: human, genetically confirmed achondroplasia, children under 18 y. FGFR3-to-NPR2 crosstalk is post-translational only, so an FGFR3 gain-of-function allele does not reduce NPR2 transcript and the receptor is present to be agonised - which is why the class works at all; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 4 sources)
edges.timescale: 52 weeks per pivotal trial; no final adult height data exist for any agent in the class

edges.magnitude: cGMP/PKG inhibition at the RAF-1 step: CNP and 8-Br-cGMP dose-dependently block FGF2- and FGF18-induced ERK phosphorylation without affecting STAT1 phosphorylation or FGFR3 protein levels
edges.context: mouse ATDC5 chondrogenic cells and chondrocyte-targeted CNP rescue of FGFR3-Ach mice; the human step is asserted by the approved label and inferred from the clinical growth effect, not measured; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: This is a DOWNSTREAM BYPASS, not a correction of the causal receptor: it does not reduce FGFR3 signalling, it opposes its output.

edges.magnitude: no measurement of CNP-analogue concentration inside growth plate cartilage exists in any species, for any agent in the class
edges.context: human; the entire dose-selection rationale for both approved agents rests on plasma exposure. Within cohort, navepegritide showed a dose-dependent AGV effect with only the 100 ug/kg arm separating from placebo (5.42 vs 4.35 cm/yr, p=0.0218), so the drug is NOT saturated below its top dose; against that, vosoritide exposure did not correlate with growth within the treated cohort; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile

edges.magnitude: NO measurable growth effect in humans: ratio of observed to expected change in standing height was 1.0 at month 12 in EVERY arm (1 mg/kg weekly, 2 mg/kg twice weekly, 1.5 mg/kg daily) with 95% CIs spanning 0.8-1.1, i.e. growth indistinguishable from the untreated reference population
edges.context: human, achondroplasia, phase 2 NCT04638153 (n=60) plus open-label extension NCT05116046 (n=35), both terminated 18 November 2022; registry whyStopped reads "terminated due to lack of efficacy at any of the tested doses ... not related to a safety concern"; zones resolved in source: proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), neonatal, juvenile, childhood, adult (P3-P22; 1 year old/2 years old/22 days old; mean age 7.5 year)
edges.notes: NEGATIVE EVIDENCE ABOUT THE TARGET, and admissible as such because the stop was a scientific null, not strategic or logistical. A ligand trap can only work if the mutant receptor still requires ligand, so the failure means either (a) FGFR3-G380R signalling in the human growth plate is substantially ligand-INDEPENDENT - consistent with the FRET finding that G380R raises unliganded dimerisation - or (b) a ~100 kDa glycoprotein cannot reach chondrocytes inside avascular, proteoglycan-dense cartilage. These were never distinguished because plate exposure was never measured.

edges.magnitude: allele-specific and NOT ordered by clinical severity. Infigratinib IC50: 0.66 nM wild-type, 0.5 nM K650E (lethal TD2 allele), 44.4 nM K650M (survivable SADDAN allele, ~89-fold weaker despite ~3-fold HIGHER kinase activity), 505.9 nM V555M gatekeeper; 1.0 nM at ATP = Km in a mobility-shift assay. NO IC50 against G380R has been published.
edges.context: in vitro human kinase panels on KINASE-DOMAIN alleles (K650E, K650M, N540K). Achondroplasia is caused by G380R, a TRANSMEMBRANE-domain variant that activates the receptor by a different mechanism, so potency measured on kinase-domain alleles does not automatically govern the clinical case; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The class rests on a premise the human genetics does not support - that phenotype severity tracks kinase output monotonically. See e00004.

edges.magnitude: not measured in any treated human or in growth plate tissue in any species
edges.context: human, achondroplasia, 0.25 mg/kg/day oral, ages 3-17 y; flagged inference from the ATP-competitive mechanism and from the fact that ERK is the branch all six dysplasia alleles activate; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile

edges.magnitude: infigratinib is a pan-FGFR1-3 ATP-competitive inhibitor by design; no FGFR1 IC50 tabulated in this atlas
edges.context: human dosing. In human embryo-fetal long bone, FGFR1 transcripts are restricted to perichondrium and periosteum and are absent from growth plate chondrocytes, so the off-target compartment is perichondrial and osteoprogenitor rather than columnar; sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: chronic daily oral dosing across the growth period
edges.notes: Relevant to the imatinib growth-toxicity precedent: chronic ATP-competitive kinase inhibition across childhood cost -0.5 height Z overall and -0.8 Z when started prepubertally, attributed to off-target PDGFR/KIT inhibition. The net effect of an FGFR3 TKI is an on-target gain minus an off-target loss that no achondroplasia trial has run long enough to separate.

edges.magnitude: pan-FGFR1-3 inhibition; no FGFR2 IC50 tabulated in this atlas
edges.context: human dosing. FGFR2 in the human fetal skeleton is restricted to perichondrium, periosteum and periarticular cartilage and is absent from columnar and hypertrophic chondrocytes, so the exposed compartment includes the periarticular reservoir that supplies the plate; sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: chronic daily oral dosing across the growth period

edges.magnitude: MOUSE: 2 mg/kg/day, 5 days/week from P7 to P56 reduced death or paralysis and increased body, cranial and long-bone length in Fgfr3-ach mice of both sexes. HUMAN: 26 weeks at 12.5-25 mg/day with concomitant GH moved height velocity from 4.35 +/- 1.36 to 4.46 +/- 1.54 cm/yr, i.e. +0.11 cm/yr, with only 1 of 9 children reaching the 6 cm/yr threshold - despite Cmax 167 ng/mL, AUC0-24 1170 ng*h/mL and terminal half-life 7.4 h at 12.5 mg/day.
edges.context: human, achondroplasia, ages 5-10 y, open-label single-arm phase 2 (n=9) with a 14-day phase 1b PK cohort (n=12); mouse Fgfr3-ach model; zones resolved in source: hypertrophic zone, both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 2 of 3 sources), juvenile, childhood (5-10 years old; 5–10 years old)
edges.notes: An agent with documented adequate systemic exposure and no toxicity that still produced no measurable human linear-growth effect. The single-arm design cannot exclude a small effect, and the arm-span/height dissociation (6/9 exceeding 6 cm/yr for arm span versus 1/9 for height) is uninterpretable at this sample size.

edges.magnitude: never tested - 0 paediatric trials with any growth endpoint
edges.context: human; abaloparatide is a PTHrP(1-34) analogue and therefore the most direct pharmacological mimic of the plate's own pace-setting signal available as an approved drug, yet the FDA label bars use in paediatric patients with open epiphyses on osteosarcoma grounds. The barrier is regulatory and oncological, not evidence of unresponsiveness; prehypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), neonatal, juvenile, adult (P1-P73)

edges.magnitude: no trial with a linear-growth endpoint in a growth indication. The nearest human datum is a secondary analysis of PTH(1-34) therapy in paediatric hypoparathyroidism (n=27, mean baseline age 13.7 +/- 5.5 y) in which height-for-age Z rose in the CaSR-activating group but stayed below 0 in the APS-1 group (age-by-group interaction P<0.0001)
edges.context: human; both PTH1R agonists are barred from the growing skeleton, so the human growth plate has never been probed with a PTH1R agonist under conditions that would test whether pharmacological PTH1R activation delays hypertrophic differentiation in vivo; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: unknown; the hypoparathyroidism cohort was followed over years of PTH exposure
edges.notes: The near-miss datum is confounded by two different underlying diseases with different intrinsic growth trajectories and has no untreated control, so it cannot be read as a PTH1R growth effect.

edges.magnitude: not measured in rhGH-treated children. The human evidence for this edge is the loss-of-function phenotype: STAT5B nulls have normal-to-elevated GH and GHBP, IGF-I 7.2 ng/mL and -7.8 height SDS.
edges.context: human; the edge direction is established by human genetics running backwards, not by a pharmacodynamic measurement in treated patients; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: not measured in treated children
edges.context: human; flagged inference from the canonical GHR-JAK2-STAT5B architecture; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: IGF-1 SDS is the only routinely used pharmacodynamic biomarker and rises dose-dependently (0.17 SDS per 0.02 mg/kg/week for the weekly prodrug). Downstream growth: +3.0 to +5.0 cm/yr velocity and +0.3 to +0.9 height SDS across indications (20 studies, 21,812 participants).
edges.context: human, children 0-18 y, mixed indications; requires open epiphyses for a skeletal effect; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources)
edges.timescale: IGF-1 responds within days; velocity read at 1 year; height SDS over years

edges.magnitude: 0.24 mg hGH/kg/week subcutaneous; the released hormone is chemically identical to daily somatropin, so the construct is a controlled test of exposure pattern rather than of a different ligand
edges.context: human, paediatric GHD, patients >=1 y weighing >=11.5 kg; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile

edges.magnitude: 0.17 IGF-1 SDS per 0.02 mg/kg/week (weekly average IGF-1 SDS)
edges.context: human, paediatric GHD; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: weekly dosing; IGF-1 SDS averaged across the dosing interval

edges.magnitude: weekly dosing abolishes GH pulsatility yet gave annualised height velocity 10.66 +/- 0.22 cm/yr versus 9.75 +/- 0.26 cm/yr on daily somatropin, a difference of +0.91 cm/yr (95% CI 0.37-1.45, p=0.0010), meeting BOTH non-inferiority and superiority; height SDS +1.01 versus +0.83 at 52 weeks
edges.context: human, n=153 treatment-naive prepubertal children with GHD, 17 sites in China, 52 weeks, randomised 2:1; class meta-analysis of 16 RCTs (2435 children) finds only modest differences between long-acting and daily preparations; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Evidence AGAINST a requirement for pulsatile GH delivery at the plate; sign left unknown because the target is a hypothesis node and the relation is evidential, not mechanistic. COUNTERWEIGHT: somavaratan, a different long-acting GH construct, was terminated because "the primary endpoint of non-inferiority to daily therapy was not achieved" (termination_reason scientific_null), so long-acting GH is not automatically equivalent and this result is construct-specific.

edges.magnitude: adding rhIGF-1 to a full rhGH dose gave year-1 mean height velocities of 9.3 cm/yr (rhGH 45 ug/kg/day alone), 10.1 (+50 ug/kg), 9.7 (+100) and 11.2 (+150) - a real but NON-MONOTONIC increment of roughly 1-2 cm/yr that narrowed to ~0.7 cm/yr spread by year 4 (7.7 / 8.1 / 8.4 / 8.3)
edges.context: human, n=106 children with short stature and IGF-1 deficiency, 6-year open-label randomised multicentre dose-selection trial NCT00572156; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources)
edges.timescale: years 1-4; the adult height endpoint was never reached
edges.notes: The trial was stopped for "strategic reasons", which carries NO evidential content about the biology. A six-year dataset with a positive interim signal exists and appears unanalysed for the separability question. This must never be cited as a negative result.

edges.magnitude: lowers serum IGF-1, free IGF-1, IGFBP-3 and the acid-labile subunit; dosing is titrated to IGF-1 and never to GH, which RISES during treatment
edges.context: human; adult PK (Tmax 33-77 h, bioavailability ~57% for a 20 mg subcutaneous dose). Paediatric use is off-label and the human paediatric growth evidence is case-level (n=1 carried to final height in X-linked acrogigantism); zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: days (slow absorption); months to years for the growth effect
edges.notes: Runs the growth axis backwards and is the only agent in L12 used deliberately to REDUCE growth. With octreotide it dissects source suppression from receptor blockade: X-linked acrogigantism responds poorly to somatostatin analogues but is controlled by GH receptor blockade, so the two are not interchangeable in humans.

edges.magnitude: 1.0 mg/day produced SMALLER deviations in testosterone, oestradiol, IGF-1, growth velocity and bone age advance than letrozole 2.5 mg/day over 3 years - a roughly threefold weaker biochemical effect - yet there was NO difference between the drugs in change in predicted adult height (combined 3-year gain +1.3 cm)
edges.context: human, 79 pubertal boys >=10 y with idiopathic short stature, bone age <=14 y, open-label randomised; zone unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The dissociation is the finding: a threefold difference in the intensity of oestrogen suppression bought no additional predicted height, which argues that oestrogen suppression is not the rate-limiting variable for height gain in this population.

edges.magnitude: 2.5 mg/day gave lower oestradiol and higher testosterone than anastrozole 1.0 mg/day, with slower growth velocity and slower bone age advance - the intended biochemical and skeletal-maturation profile
edges.context: human, pubertal boys with ISS, up to 3 years; zone unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: 3 years; the year-1 predicted-adult-height gain did NOT persist at years 2 and 3
edges.notes: The clearest example in L12 of an interim surrogate gain that does not convert.

edges.magnitude: 1.0 mg/day; smaller oestradiol suppression than letrozole 2.5 mg/day in a head-to-head trial
edges.context: human, pubertal boys with ISS and boys with 21-hydroxylase-deficiency congenital adrenal hyperplasia; zone unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: androgen therapy overall increased measured final adult height by +1.78 cm (95% CI 0.47-3.08, p=0.0076) and final height Z by +0.24 (95% CI 0.07-0.41) across 13 retrospective cohorts and 803 boys. Testosterone - which IS aromatised - outperformed oxandrolone by +2.64 cm (95% CI 1.44-3.80). Low-dose regimens gave the largest gain (+1.88 cm); medium and high doses were not significant.
edges.context: human, boys with constitutional delay of growth and puberty; oxandrolone is poorly aromatised to oestrogen; zone unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: short courses outperformed long courses (+2.70 cm, 95% CI 1.30-4.09)
edges.notes: The non-aromatisable androgen was the WEAKER agent, which is the opposite of what a pure-androgen model predicts and is human pharmacological evidence for a genuine oestrogen requirement in the pubertal height gain.

edges.magnitude: not dose-ranged against an attained-height endpoint: 0 randomised comparisons of oestrogen introduction age with attained adult height in Turner syndrome were identified
edges.context: human, girls with Turner syndrome co-treated with rhGH; the evidence base is protocolised cohorts and consensus guidance; zone unknown (not reported), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: years - the therapeutic problem is entirely one of scheduling
edges.notes: The clearest clinical demonstration that plate closure is a dose- and duration-dependent pharmacological endpoint rather than a fixed developmental clock. The complementary upper arm of the dose-response - high-dose oestrogen to reduce excessive height - has been abandoned in practice, removing it from contemporary human data.

edges.magnitude: not quantified as an effect size in this atlas
edges.context: human childhood cancer survivors; cranial and total body irradiation produce growth hormone deficiency, which is an ENDOCRINE route distinct from the direct antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects of high-dose methotrexate and platinum agents on chondrocytes; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: The reason GH replacement only partially rescues these children: an irradiated plate is a damaged EFFECTOR, so restoring the systemic signal cannot restore the response. Quantifying the split between direct plate injury and endocrine deficiency in an individual survivor remains unsolved.

edges.magnitude: never measured at fusion. The single reported human fusing growth plate showed electron-microscopic signs of hypoxia and necrosis, disorganised large chondrocytes surrounded by a border of dense cortical-like bone, and ZERO TUNEL-positive cells - but no HIF1A, lactate, pimonidazole adduct or necroptosis marker has ever been measured in a fusing human plate.
edges.context: human, late pubertal, n=1 fusing plate, unreplicated. HIF1A function in the growth plate is mouse-only: chondrocyte-restricted Hif1a deletion kills cells in the plate INTERIOR, lowers p57 and raises BrdU incorporation; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)

edges.magnitude: mouse: sequestering VEGF with a soluble receptor chimera suppresses blood vessel invasion of hypertrophic cartilage, expands the hypertrophic zone and is reversible on withdrawal. Human: VEGF mRNA and protein are present in growth plate specimens with protein rising across pubertal development, but no human bridge has been linked to a vessel.
edges.context: SPECIES GAP. Mice form hundreds of transphyseal bridges (495 +/- 45 per wild-type tibial plate) yet never complete fusion, so no murine experiment can report a fusion endpoint. Nobody has imaged the vasculature of a human growth plate at or approaching fusion; hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 2 of 4 sources), juvenile, pubertal, adult (24-day-old; 13-month-old)
edges.notes: The morphological basis in humans is classical: mineralisation demarcated by tide lines spreads inward from BOTH plate surfaces, first union is by mineralised cartilage as a form of metaplastic bone, and only afterwards is a restricted region perforated and replaced by bone and marrow.

edges.magnitude: never tested in any species
edges.context: RUNX2 licenses chondrocyte hypertrophy and osteoblast differentiation, with human dose evidence (cleidocranial dysplasia) and a mouse Runx2/Runx3 combined-dose series in which limb length falls in proportion to gene dose. Whether RUNX2 is required to build the transphyseal bone column that fuses a human plate has never been asked, in humans or in a fusing animal; male only (sex reported in 1 of 3 sources), adult (13-month-old)

edges.magnitude: HUMAN: a homozygous ESR1 premature stop at codon 157 gave 204 cm with incomplete epiphyseal closure and continued linear growth into adulthood, with bone age advancing only 15 -> 17.5 years over 3.5 years and no response to 6 months of transdermal oestrogen at a 10-fold rise in free estradiol (n=1 male, 28 y). MOUSE: old ERalpha-null females keep growing (tibiae +8.3%, P<0.01; plate height +18%, P<0.05), whereas ERalphaAF-1-deleted mice have SHORTER tibiae (-4.9%, P<0.01) and closed proximal tibial plates in 100% of animals versus 0% of wild type.
edges.context: human n=1 male plus mouse genetics, both sexes; a fusion endpoint is expressible in both; zone unknown (not reported), adult (28-year-old)
edges.notes: Growth plate closure is driven by ERalpha functions that do NOT require AF-1 and is actively OPPOSED by AF-1 - a rare case where a mouse experiment makes a mechanistic prediction that the human experiments of nature then match phenotypically. Not marked speculative because the human loss-of- function phenotype is itself a direct fusion-endpoint observation.

edges.magnitude: untreated aromatase-deficient men reach 188-204 cm with bone age 14 years at chronological age 24.25 years and continue slow linear growth into the third decade despite severely impaired GH secretion; transdermal estradiol - not testosterone - advances bone maturation and closes the plates
edges.context: human, biallelic CYP19A1, XY and XX individuals; a true interventional human fusion experiment; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 2 of 4 sources), pubertal
edges.timescale: months to years of adequate estradiol exposure before closure
edges.notes: With e00073 this is the only fusion mechanism in the atlas with direct human interventional evidence, and it rests on a handful of individuals.

edges.magnitude: THRESHOLD-GATED, not dose-graded: in a man with compound heterozygous CYP19A1 mutations followed for five years on poorly compliant transdermal estradiol, neither bone age nor plate appearance changed while serum estradiol stayed low-but-detectable; closure, BMD normalisation and bone-turnover normalisation were achieved only once estradiol exceeded 73 pmol/L (~20 pg/mL) (n=1). Independent non-pathological support: at genital Tanner 5, obese boys at median 34.8 pg/mL had bone age ~18 y with fused epiphyses while lean boys at 15.7 pg/mL had bone age ~16 y with epiphyses still unfused.
edges.context: human, males; the only quantitative human dose parameter for fusion in this atlas; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 3 of 4 sources), juvenile, pubertal
edges.timescale: five years of sub-threshold exposure produced no change; closure followed adequate dosing
edges.notes: The stimulating and terminating actions of estradiol are separated by well under one order of magnitude - half-maximal pubertal growth acceleration at 20 pmol/L in girls and 6.5 pmol/L in boys, against a closure threshold near 73 pmol/L. This defines the exposure a growth-sparing therapy must stay below. Confidence D because the threshold rests on n=1.

edges.magnitude: mouse: after a single P6 PTHrP-creER pulse the number of labelled columns falls progressively until about six months of chase and then PLATEAUS; roughly 2-3% of PTHrP+ colony-forming cells show long-term self-renewal (12.5% of secondary colonies from a P12 pulse passageable nine times). Behaves like neutral drift with a surviving minority, not synchronous failure of a compartment.
edges.context: SPECIES GAP. Mouse lineage tracing only; no clonal measurement of any kind exists in a human growth plate, and lineage tracing is not performable in humans; resting zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile, pubertal (75-day-old)
edges.timescale: mouse: months of chase; human equivalent unknown

edges.magnitude: not measured in any fusing species. Growth hormone reduces the slow-cycling label-retaining population by pushing cells into transit-amplifying differentiation, i.e. interventions that consume the pool accelerate clonal loss - in mouse.
edges.context: SPECIES GAP. The mouse plate never completes fusion, so a murine result about clonal loss cannot be a result about fusion; resting zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile

edges.magnitude: rabbit (a FUSING species): oestrogen accelerated the normal age-related loss of resting-zone chondrocytes, the loss was maintained 5 weeks after oestrogen withdrawal and did not appear apoptotic, and transient oestrogen exposure hastened fusion. Structural parameters stayed irreversibly advanced while functional parameters (growth rate, proliferation rate, hypertrophic cell size) normalised.
edges.context: juvenile ovariectomised rabbit; the causal direction is NOT established. Against causation: rodent plates senesce to near-cessation without fusing at all, so depletion is not sufficient for fusion in every mammal; and oestrogen simultaneously SLOWS resting-zone proliferation, the opposite of what a pure proliferation-consumption model predicts; female only (sex reported in 2 of 3 sources)
edges.timescale: 5 weeks of exposure plus 5 weeks of withdrawal
edges.notes: Two readings of the same correlation compete: depletion CAUSES fusion, or depletion is the state of the plate at an independently triggered (in humans, oestrogen-driven) fusion event. No human resting-zone count at fusion exists to discriminate.

edges.magnitude: mouse: PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes appear at P3, expand between P6 and P9, are markedly less proliferative than the cells below (6.1% vs 30.5% EdU+ at P9) and generate clonal columns for at least a year; only ~2-3% behave as long-term stem cells
edges.context: SPECIES GAP, and a sharp one: no equivalent cell has been identified in human growth plate. Human single-cell and spatial profiling of early-pubertal plates instead found a PTHLH-NEGATIVE stem-like "root" population in a WNT- and TGF-beta-low niche. The marker that defines the mouse cell does not define the human one; resting zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)

edges.magnitude: not measured. Human specimens establish that a subset of resting chondrocytes is functionally quiescent in vivo (predominantly nuclear mRNA, abundant heterochromatin, able to exit G0 ex vivo) and resolve two stem-like resting populations, but self-renewal, clonal output and lifespan of any human resting cell remain formally untested.
edges.context: human, rare surgical specimens from healthy adolescents and early-pubertal children. METHOD-BLOCKED: lineage tracing is impossible in humans, so the standard assay for the claim cannot be run; resting zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)

edges.magnitude: entirely temporal coincidence in two mouse studies: PTHrP-creER colony-forming cells acquire robust in vitro self-renewal between a P9 pulse (17/518 secondary colonies, none passageable) and a P12 pulse (16/98, 2/16 passageable nine times), "when the secondary ossification centre actively develops". Neither study manipulated the SOC.
edges.context: SPECIES GAP plus an untested causal step. A targeted search for any experiment that ablates, blocks or delays SOC formation and then assays resting-zone stemness returned zero records; mouse, sex unknown (not reported in source), fetal, neonatal, juvenile (E15.5; P0-P16)
edges.timescale: mouse postnatal week 2; no human timing established
edges.notes: Load-bearing for fusion models in L7 and must be cited as a hypothesis, not a mechanism.

edges.magnitude: rabbit and rat: senescence is intrinsic, local and division-denominated. Local intra-plate glucocorticoid in rabbit produces catch-up confined to the TREATED plate, excluding a systemic explanation; dexamethasone-suppressed rabbits and propylthiouracil-treated hypothyroid rats resume growth with plates structurally and functionally LESS senescent than age-matched controls.
edges.context: rabbit and rat. The model's simplest molecular version was falsified by its own authors: rabbit resting-zone chondrocyte population doublings in culture do not depend on donor age, so the in vivo limit is not a Hayflick limit carried by the cells. The proposed replacement is progressive loss of DNA methylation tracking slow in vivo resting-zone division; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: weeks of growth inhibition conserve a corresponding amount of capacity
edges.notes: Unresolved tension with mouse clonal tracing showing progenitors ACQUIRE self-renewal postnatally rather than only spending down a fixed budget.

edges.magnitude: NEGATIVE RESULT: rabbit resting-zone chondrocytes harvested from young and old animals achieved the SAME number of population doublings in culture. Global DNA methylation declined with in vivo senescence but not during rapid in vitro proliferation nor across the resting-to-hypertrophic transition.
edges.context: rabbit resting-zone chondrocytes, young versus old donors, explanted; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The decisive test of cell-autonomous replicative senescence in the growth plate was done and it failed. "Growth plate chondrocytes undergo replicative senescence" should be treated as UNSUPPORTED in its cell-autonomous form despite being routinely re-asserted as positive in secondary literature.

edges.magnitude: no qualifying primary measurement exists. A targeted search for telomere length or telomerase activity in human growth plate or resting-zone chondrocytes as a function of age returned no qualifying primary study; hits are osteoarthritis cartilage, general skeletal-ageing reviews and rodent work.
edges.context: human claim, murine nearest datum (mTert-GFP marks a transitional skeletal progenitor whose expression peaks during adolescent growth rather than persisting). The nearest NEGATIVE datum is that rabbit resting-zone replicative capacity in vitro does not decline with donor age; sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Grade X: commonly repeated in reviews, untraceable to primary data in its human form. Recorded so that the claim is visible and marked, not so that it can be traversed.

edges.magnitude: dexamethasone-induced growth suppression in juvenile rabbits DELAYED the senescent decline in growth rate and in proliferative, hypertrophic and total plate height AND DELAYED EPIPHYSEAL FUSION, after which catch-up growth occurred
edges.context: juvenile rabbit, systemic dexamethasone. The rabbit COMPLETES fusion as humans do, so this is a genuine fusion-endpoint result and not a rodent surrogate - which is why it is not marked speculative. The human counterpart has never been tested prospectively; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: weeks of suppression, with fusion delayed by a corresponding interval
edges.notes: The reciprocal of the oestrogen experiment: oestrogen accelerates the senescent decline and fusion occurs earlier, glucocorticoid slows it and fusion occurs later. Together they support a proliferation-counting clock rather than a chronological one - in rabbit.

edges.magnitude: NEGATIVE IN HUMAN: zero TUNEL-positive cells anywhere in the one reported human fusing growth plate; only a few TUNEL-positive chondrocytes in unfused plates. Bcl-2, Bcl-XL, Bax, Bad and cleaved caspase-3 were detectable in all zones with no change in intensity across pubertal progression, and in the fusing plate only Bad was detected among the pro-apoptotic proteins. Electron microscopy found no apoptosis or autophagy.
edges.context: human, growth plates across pubertal stages including one late-pubertal fusing plate; n=1 fusing specimen, unreplicated; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: The only one of the six candidate fusion mechanisms that has been tested in human fusing tissue, and it failed. Directly contradicts the apoptosis-centred account that dominates the rodent hypertrophic- chondrocyte literature. No second human fusing plate has ever been reported, so it cannot be replicated.

edges.magnitude: 17.1% change in longitudinal growth rate per 0.1 MPa sustained stress (range across plates 9.2-23.9); 15.0%/0.1 MPa for caudal vertebral plates, 18.6%/0.1 MPa for proximal tibial plates; compression slows, distraction accelerates
edges.context: rat, rabbit and calf caudal vertebrae and proximal tibiae; immature animals, sex not reported; whole-plate output measured by oxytetracycline label displacement; zones resolved in source: hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The coefficient is invariant across a 12-fold range of baseline growth rate (30-366 um/day), which is why it is applied to humans. No human measurement of the coefficient exists and no human physeal stress has ever been measured in vivo (g_l6mech_001, g_l6mech_003), so the human application is extrapolation across three species and two skeletal sites.

edges.magnitude: hypertrophic zone height 87% of control; total plate thickness significantly reduced under static compression only
edges.context: rat caudal vertebra, ~60% body weight for 4 weeks (stokes2002); rat caudal vertebra Cd7, 0.2 MPa mean for 2 weeks (valteau2011); immature animals; zones resolved in source: hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Plate height is a poor proxy for growth rate in general, but under load it moves in the same direction as growth rate because the same zonal parameters drive both.

edges.magnitude: mean hypertrophic chondrocyte height 85% of control; increment in cell height along the growth direction 78% of control
edges.context: rat caudal vertebra, sustained compression at ~60% body weight, 4 weeks; both effects significant; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: final hypertrophic cell height is the single strongest correlate of loaded growth rate: normalised multiple-regression coefficient 1.39, overall r=0.56
edges.context: pooled loaded and control plates from rat, rabbit and calf caudal vertebrae and proximal tibiae, 8 days sustained compression or distraction; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile
edges.notes: Load acts on the same variable that dominates unloaded elongation, so mechanical modulation is not a separate mechanism but a shift along the existing hypertrophy axis.

edges.magnitude: proliferative cells per unit plate width: normalised regression coefficient 0.72, overall r=0.38 - roughly half the explanatory weight of hypertrophic cell height
edges.context: pooled rat, rabbit and calf loaded and control plates, 8 days; proliferative zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile

edges.magnitude: hypertrophic cell height r=0.56 and proliferative cells per unit width r=0.38 of loaded growth-rate variance; the matrix-synthesis term of the budget was not partitioned
edges.context: pooled rat, rabbit, calf; 8-day sustained loading; proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile
edges.notes: Load redistributes the elongation budget between the division and hypertrophy terms; whether it touches the matrix-synthesis term is untested in any species.

edges.magnitude: proliferative cells per column reduced under static loading only (p<0.01 static vs dynamic); growth rate fell 19% under both
edges.context: rat caudal vertebra Cd7, 0.2 MPa mean sustained vs 0.2 MPa +/-30% at 0.1 Hz, 2 weeks; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Waveform dissociates growth-rate suppression (equal under both) from architectural damage (static only). This is the strongest argument for dynamic tethering strategies.

edges.magnitude: plate thickness significantly reduced by static but not dynamic compression at equal mean stress; hypertrophic cell height difference p=0.014
edges.context: rat caudal vertebra Cd7, 0.2 MPa mean, 0.1 Hz, 2 weeks; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: in vitro the sign REVERSES: dynamic compression (7-13% strain, 0.1 Hz) caused severe loss of columnar arrangement in proliferative and hypertrophic zones, while static (10% strain) preserved columns with only slight deviation from the growth axis
edges.context: growth plate explants from distal ulnae of 4-week-old swine, unconfined compression, matched mean strain, 48 h; species unknown, proliferative zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), peripubertal (4-week-old)
edges.notes: Directly opposite in sign to valteau2011 in vivo, where static is the architecturally damaging waveform. Explant (no perfusion, cut boundaries, 48 h) vs in vivo (2 weeks) is the obvious confound but has not been tested. Logged as a contradiction.

edges.magnitude: linear in applied stress, slope 17.1% per 0.1 MPa, demonstrated over approximately -0.2 to +0.1 MPa (negative = compression); no threshold or saturation detected inside that window
edges.context: rat, rabbit and calf caudal vertebrae and proximal tibiae, external loading apparatus; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The stress range was set by the apparatus rather than by physiology, so linearity outside 0.02-0.2 MPa is untested (g_l6mech_002).

edges.magnitude: at equal mean stress and equal axial strain, static loading gave higher lateral (p<0.001) and volumetric (p<=0.015) hypertrophic cell strain than dynamic; axial cell strain did not differ
edges.context: pre-pubertal rat proximal tibial growth plate explants, stress-controlled compression, confocal cell tracking; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: This is the mechanistic root of the static/dynamic distinction: the cell, not the tissue, sees a different strain state under the two waveforms even when the tissue-level input is matched.

edges.magnitude: 0.2 +/- 0.14 MPa at 1.0 Hz for 15 days destroyed plate integrity with repeated inflammation, preventing analysis (n=3)
edges.context: rat caudal vertebrae, in vivo external loading, 0.1 vs 1.0 Hz at 0.2 MPa mean; sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile (28 days old)
edges.notes: An upper bound on tolerable dynamic amplitude, from a group that failed rather than from a dose-response design. n=3.

edges.magnitude: chondrocyte viability fell monotonically with compression magnitude (0.1 vs 0.2 MPa), duration (12 vs 24 h), frequency (0.1 vs 1.0 Hz) and amplitude (30 vs 100%); proliferative and hypertrophic chondrocytes were the most sensitive zones
edges.context: swine ulnar growth plate explants, n=60 across 10 groups, live/dead confocal quantification; species unknown, hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Sets the ceiling on explant loading protocols: above it an experiment measures cell death, not mechanobiology. Relevant to interpreting sergerie2011 and kaviani2016.

edges.magnitude: hypertrophic zone height 87% of control, mean cell height 85%, cell-height increment along the growth axis 78%
edges.context: rat caudal vertebra, ~60% body weight sustained compression, 4 weeks; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: proliferative cells per column reduced under static loading; correlation of proliferative cells per unit width with growth rate r=0.38
edges.context: rat caudal vertebra 0.2 MPa 2 weeks (valteau2011); pooled rat/rabbit/calf 8 days (stokes2007); proliferative zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile

edges.magnitude: plate height and growth rate fully recovered by 10 days after removal of 15 days of 0.2 MPa static or dynamic compression; no residual difference from sham at 4 weeks
edges.context: rat caudal vertebra, n=48 across 8 subgroups; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile (28 days old)
edges.notes: Mechanical modulation of the rat plate is fully reversible on this timescale. Whether a human physis tethered for the 1-3 years typical of guided growth recovers equally is unknown.

edges.magnitude: limb immobilisation abolished the enlarged peripheral hypertrophic cell populations of cartilage-specific Ift88-null mice
edges.context: AggrecanCreERT2;Ift88fl/fl juvenile/adolescent mouse tibia, peripheral regions beneath the load-bearing knee compartments; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Unloading is protective here, not growth-promoting - the disruptive stimulus in the adolescent plate is ordinary physiological load.

edges.magnitude: growth arrest in 30.1% of 332 prospectively followed paediatric physeal fractures, against up to 5.5% in the prior literature; mean age at arrest 12.8 vs 9.4 years, displacement 59.0% vs 47.8%
edges.context: human children, prospective cohort, all physeal fracture sites, >=6 months follow-up or arrest; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: The authors caution that diagnostic criteria for arrest vary and the true figure may be lower. Physeal fractures are 18-30% of all paediatric fractures.

edges.magnitude: 86% growth arrest after distal femoral physeal fracture - the highest of any site in the cohort (small subgroup)
edges.context: human children, same prospective cohort; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Site specificity is real but confounded: the distal femur is also the fastest human plate, so a given bar tethers a larger absolute growth increment.

edges.magnitude: progressive bone tissue accumulation across the plate over 42 days in a reproducible drill-hole model, scored on a validated 5-point radiological/histological scale
edges.context: mouse distal femur drill-hole injury; Pdgfra and Pdgfrb lineage-traced cells, absent from the uninjured plate, migrate in and build the bar; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The bar is a repair response by perivascular/mesenchymal populations, not transdifferentiation of resident chondrocytes - so it is an externally imposed tether on the plate, mechanically equivalent to a surgical tension band.

edges.magnitude: unilateral physeal tethering; 68.7% of children reached a neutral mechanical axis (idiopathic 78.2% vs non-idiopathic 66.3%, p=0.02)
edges.context: human, 654 growth modulations in 313 children, extraperiosteal two-hole tension-band plates; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: months to a few years of implant dwell
edges.notes: The cleanest human demonstration that a physis is mechanically modulable. The applied stress is never measured, so this is a demonstration of sign, not of dose.

edges.magnitude: mLDFA correction 0.67 degrees/month (SD 0.55)
edges.context: human, 313 children, 55.4% of modulations at the distal femur; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)

edges.magnitude: mMPTA correction 0.43 degrees/month (SD 0.38)
edges.context: human, same cohort, 44.6% of modulations at the proximal tibia; 42.2% of children had both sites treated; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)

edges.magnitude: distal femur corrects 1.56x faster than proximal tibia in the same children (0.67 vs 0.43 deg/month)
edges.context: human, 654 modulations in 313 children, within-cohort comparison; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: This is the only human dataset in which two physes are mechanically modulated in the same individuals. The ratio tracks the sites' baseline growth velocities, so it does NOT establish that the two plates differ in mechanosensitivity - baseline rate and mechanosensitivity are not separable without a stress measurement. SD is 60-90% of the mean at both sites.

edges.magnitude: progressive varus from growth suppression confined to the posteromedial quadrant of the physis
edges.context: human children and adolescents; the compressed side of the plate is the suppressed side; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Cited here to the guided-growth cohort in which non-idiopathic (largely Blount and related) deformity corrected less completely than idiopathic (66.3% vs 78.2%, p=0.02). Blount is the standard human illustration of Hueter-Volkmann but its causal direction - does varus cause the medial suppression or vice versa - is not resolved by any of these data.

edges.magnitude: growth modulation 53% vs -1% at 2 weeks for high vs low tether tension (SD 43 and 15; p=0.03 vs low tension, p=0.01 vs non-operative control); the effect collapsed to 14% vs 10% (p=0.6) over weeks 2-4
edges.context: porcine, single-level posterior vertebral body tethering in a kyphotic swine model; human and pig, zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), childhood (10–11-week-old/11-week-old/13-week-old)
edges.timescale: biphasic: strong in the first 2 weeks, absent from 2-4 weeks
edges.notes: The escape from load-dependence after 2 weeks is the important result and is unexplained (g_l6mech_005). It is the reason clinical vertebral body tethering under-corrects.

edges.magnitude: compressive stress upregulates PIEZO1 in vertebral growth plate chondrocytes, driving GPX4 loss, ferroptosis and accelerated pathological ossification; Col2a1-CreERT;Piezo1fl/fl deletion or local pharmacological blockade slowed curve progression
edges.context: mouse vertebral growth plate under applied caudal/vertebral compression; adolescent idiopathic scoliosis model; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female)
edges.notes: A molecular route from compression to premature ossification of the vertebral plate, i.e. the vicious cycle expressed as cell death rather than as growth-rate modulation. Systemic PIEZO1 inhibition caused osteoporosis as an off-target effect.

edges.magnitude: distal radial physeal stress injury with acquired POSITIVE ULNAR VARIANCE - the radius shortens relative to the ulna in the same limb, an internally controlled human demonstration of load-suppressed physeal output
edges.context: human adolescent artistic gymnasts, weight-bearing through the wrist over years of training; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Evidence tier is limited by source type: a narrative review plus a systematic review/ meta-analysis of wrist pain epidemiology. The ulnar-variance comparison is the strongest human internal control in this layer because the two bones of one forearm share age, sex, nutrition, hormones and genotype and differ only in load.

edges.magnitude: 4.20 cm vs 2.48 cm height gain over 24 weeks (p=0.001); femoral neck BMD Z-score +1.075 (p<0.001, Cohen's d 0.869); lumbar spine BMD unchanged
edges.context: human, 47 prepubertal short-stature children aged 8-11 y, 3 supervised jumping sessions/week of 50 min; n=20 intervention, n=27 control, NOT randomised; zone unknown (not reported), both sexes (male and female)
edges.notes: Opposite in sign to the gymnast wrist and to the gymnastics stature literature. The reconciling hypothesis is the static/dynamic distinction: impact loading is intermittent and axial, wrist weight-bearing in gymnastics is sustained and compressive. Small, single-centre, unblinded, and the mediation analysis (beta -0.442, 95% CI -1.474 to -0.009) is fragile.

edges.magnitude: throwing arm gained 4.3% (95% CI 1.1-7.5) more cortical BMC, 3.9% (0.7-7.0) more cortical area and 2.9% (0.3-5.4) more cortical vBMD asymmetry than the non-throwing arm over 12 months
edges.context: human, 12 male pre-pubertal baseball players, mean age 10.3 +/- 0.6 y, distal humerus pQCT, within-subject contralateral control; perichondrium
edges.notes: A within-subject human loading experiment on appositional (periosteal/cortical) growth, which is the arm of skeletal growth where Wolff's law is well supported. The same design has NEVER been used to read out longitudinal physeal output, which is the asymmetry this seam exposes: human loading data are strong for bone width and absent for bone length.

edges.magnitude: peak height velocity 5.48 vs 8.0 cm/yr in gymnasts vs swimmers (SEM 0.32 and 0.50; p<0.05 at bone ages 11-13); height SDS declined with follow-up time in gymnasts (r=-0.747, p<0.001) but not swimmers (r=-0.165); >35% of pre- and peripubertal gymnasts had height velocity <4.5 cm/yr
edges.context: human female artistic gymnasts, ~22 h/wk training vs swimmers ~8 h/wk, mean age 12.3 y; second cohort 137 gymnasts followed 2 y; zone unknown (not reported), pubertal, adult
edges.notes: Selection versus causation is unresolved: short, late-maturing girls are also selected INTO elite gymnastics. Directly contradicts the jumping-intervention edge e00029; the atlas records both rather than choosing.

edges.magnitude: sitting height / leg length ratio 1.054 vs 1.100 in gymnasts vs swimmers (SEM 0.005 both, p<0.001); peripubertal sitting height velocity 2.3 vs 3.1 cm/yr for advanced vs intermediate training loads (p<0.05)
edges.context: human female artistic gymnasts vs swimmers, same cohorts; zone unknown (not reported), pubertal, adult
edges.notes: The deficit is disproportionately axial (trunk/vertebral plates) rather than appendicular, which is the pattern predicted if sustained axial compression is the mediator - but energy availability suppresses trunk growth preferentially too, so the finding does not discriminate.

edges.magnitude: Kif3a deletion (loss of intraflagellar transport, hence of primary cilia) disrupts postnatal columnar organisation
edges.context: mouse postnatal growth plate; Kif3a is the Kinesin-II subunit required for IFT; proliferative zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), neonatal (P0)
edges.notes: Column formation depends on the 90-degree post-mitotic rotation, and the cilium is one of only two structures (with integrin beta-1) shown to be required for it.

edges.magnitude: AggrecanCreERT2;Ift88fl/fl accumulated enlarged hypertrophic populations, but ONLY in peripheral tibial regions beneath the load-bearing knee compartments; Hedgehog signalling was preserved
edges.context: mouse juvenile and adolescent tibia, cartilage-specific inducible deletion; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Two controls make this a mechanical rather than a signalling phenotype: raising physiological load in control mice reproduced it, and limb immobilisation abolished it. This is the cleanest loading-controlled cilium experiment in a growth plate.

edges.magnitude: hypertrophic VEGF expression fell, with downstream loss of vascular recruitment, osteoclastic activity and cartilage-to-bone replacement
edges.context: mouse adolescent tibia, AggrecanCreERT2;Ift88fl/fl, load-bearing peripheral regions; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)

edges.magnitude: conditional Itgb1 deletion disrupts the 90-degree daughter-cell rotation; defective rotation in a Cdh2 (N-cadherin) mutant is RESCUED by heterozygous loss of Itgb1, placing N-cadherin as a negative regulator of integrin beta-1 rather than a parallel driver
edges.context: mouse cranial base explants, live time-lapse confocal imaging, conditional cartilage-specific alleles; proliferative zone, female only, fetal (E11.5-E17.5)

edges.magnitude: beta1-deficient chondrocytes have abnormal shape and fail to arrange into columns; caused by loss of motility from lost adhesion to collagen II, reduced binding to and spreading on fibronectin, and abnormal F-actin organisation
edges.context: mouse, chondrocyte-specific Itgb1 inactivation; chondrodysplasia of variable severity; proliferative zone, female only (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), fetal (E11.5-E17.5)

edges.magnitude: decreased proliferation from a G1/S transition defect plus a cytokinesis defect; the G1/S block is at least partly caused by Fgfr3 overexpression, Stat1/Stat5a nuclear translocation and cell-cycle inhibitor upregulation
edges.context: mouse, chondrocyte-specific Itgb1 inactivation; proliferative zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: A direct mechanical-adhesion input onto the FGFR3 axis that dominates L3, and one of the few places where mechanobiology and the achondroplasia pathway are experimentally joined.

edges.magnitude: abnormal F-actin organisation is the proximate cause of the motility loss that prevents rotation in beta1-integrin-null chondrocytes
edges.context: mouse, chondrocyte-specific Itgb1 inactivation; cranial base and long bone plates; proliferative zone, female only (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), fetal (E11.5-E17.5)
edges.notes: The one hard structural result in this node: the actin/adhesion machinery is load-bearing for growth plate architecture. It is inferred from integrin loss, not from direct manipulation of cytoskeletal tension.

edges.magnitude: Col2a1-Cre Piezo1 inactivation gives near-absence of trabecular bone beneath the growth plate postnatally with 100% rib-fracture penetrance by day 7; Col10a1-Cre deletion restricted to hypertrophic chondrocytes raises osteoclast number in the primary spongiosa via RANKL repression and OPG induction
edges.context: mouse, two independent cartilage-lineage Cre drivers; hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), both sexes (male and female), neonatal, juvenile, peripubertal, adult (P0-P21; 1-week-old/10-day-old/12 weeks old; P53; 12-week-old)

edges.magnitude: linear skeletal growth only MILDLY affected despite near-absence of trabecular bone beneath the plate
edges.context: mouse, Col2a1-Cre Piezo1 conditional null; hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), both sexes (male and female), neonatal, juvenile, peripubertal, adult (P0-P21; 1-week-old/10-day-old/12 weeks old)
edges.notes: A dissociation edge: PIEZO1 is required for the bone the plate produces far more than for the plate's own longitudinal output. Cited as a caution against reading trabecular phenotypes as growth phenotypes.

edges.magnitude: NO growth plate or endochondral phenotype detected, in the same study and against littermate Piezo1 mutants with an overt phenotype
edges.context: mouse, Piezo2 Col2a1-Cre conditional null; zones resolved in source: hypertrophic zone, both sexes (male and female), neonatal, juvenile, peripubertal, adult (P0-P21; 1-week-old/10-day-old/12 weeks old)
edges.notes: A negative result recorded deliberately. PIEZO2 is repeatedly listed as a growth plate mechanotransducer; the only experiment done inside the plate says otherwise.

edges.magnitude: loading-driven cartilage growth and joint shape depend on TRPV4 activity, mediated via cell proliferation and matrix biosynthesis; TRPV4 localises to regions of high biophysical stimulus
edges.context: MOUSE EMBRYONIC hindlimb explants, mechanically stimulated ex vivo; knee joint cartilage, NOT a postnatal growth plate; proliferative zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: The species-and-stage caveat is the point: no study has applied a defined mechanical stimulus to a POSTNATAL growth plate and shown a TRPV4-dependent change in longitudinal growth rate.

edges.magnitude: both gain- and loss-of-function TRPV4 variants cause metaphyseal disorganisation with severe short stature (metatropic dysplasia, spondylometaphyseal dysplasia Kozlowski, brachyolmia), so the dose-response is non-monotonic
edges.context: human, germline TRPV4 variants; graded allelic series; zones resolved in source: proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone, perichondrium, both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 3 sources), fetal, pubertal, adult (12 years old/23-year-old; E9.5-E19.5; 8-week-old)
edges.notes: The strongest human evidence for any candidate physeal mechanotransducer - but it is genetic, not mechanical. Small-molecule TRPV4 inhibition rescues the mouse phenotype, so it is the channel's activity level and not its presence that sets plate output.

edges.magnitude: the distraction regenerate is NOT a growth plate: new bone forms in parallel columns extending in BOTH directions from a central fibrous growth zone, with features of physeal and of intramembranous ossification and belonging to neither
edges.context: canine tibia, open osteotomy and closed osteoclasis, Ilizarov external fixation; species unknown, zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Recorded as a structural NEGATIVE. Distraction osteogenesis is often invoked as proof that tension drives physeal growth; the primary source explicitly denies the structural identity. Its real contribution is that the tension vector, not the bone's mechanical axis, sets the direction of new bone formation - tension is instructive for skeletal tissue, outside a physis.

edges.magnitude: 19.3 mm mean circadian stature variation in adults (1.1% of stature, 54% of the loss in the first hour after rising, 70% regained in the first half of the night); 4.6 mm over 7 h in 12-14 year old boys; 7 mm (SD 7) over a day in 98 children with idiopathic scoliosis
edges.context: human; 8 young adults to 1 mm precision (tyrrell1985), 11-19 boys aged 12-14 (whitehouse1974), 98 scoliosis patients Cobb 10-52 deg (czaprowski2019); zone unknown (not reported), juvenile, adult (12-14-year-old)
edges.notes: This is a MEASUREMENT relation, not a physeal one: the diurnal swing exceeds a week of true longitudinal growth in a mid-childhood child, so any stature-velocity estimate over short intervals is dominated by it unless time of day is fixed. The swing is intervertebral disc fluid; no measurement partitions any of it to the vertebral physis (g_l6l5_010).

edges.context: human, all ages, all sites - no zone, stage or sex can be specified because no measurement exists; zones resolved in source: perichondrium, sex unknown (not reported in source), pubertal (11 years old)
edges.notes: Every quantitative claim in L6 is expressed per MPa of physeal stress, and that stress has never been measured in a living human at any age. All human figures in the literature are finite-element model output, and the models' authors state they are not fully participant-specific. The edge is written speculative deliberately: the animal coefficient is the only number available and applying it to a human is an assumption, not a result.

edges.context: human - but the only human data are 9 ADULT ISS crew with closed physes; no paediatric spaceflight has ever occurred; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Stature rose up to 3% early in flight, plateaued, and fully reversed on landing, with segment circumferences falling up to 11%. In adults with fused physes that gain is spinal unloading and contains no endochondral component. The mechanistic argument that unloading acts on the physis comes from mice (simulated microgravity reverses PIEZO1-driven growth plate ossification), not from humans.

edges.context: human, growing children and adolescents; upright posture vs recumbency; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Gravity acting through posture is the largest sustained mechanical variable on the growing human axial skeleton and is titratable without surgery (recumbency, shoulder loads of 2.5-40 kg produce nonlinear shrinkage). Whether ANY of the resulting axial stress reaches the vertebral physis, as opposed to being absorbed by the discs, is unmeasured. Over 130 human vertebral plates generate the trunk segment, so the question is not marginal.

edges.context: mouse and in vitro human cell inference; no growth plate experiment in any species; proliferative zone, female only (sex reported in 1 of 2 sources), fetal (E11.5-E17.5)
edges.notes: Integrin beta-1 is required for the rotation that builds columns (e00036, e00037) and FAK is the obligatory kinase downstream of integrin engagement in every other tissue. The inference is strong and completely untested inside a physis.

edges.context: mouse and in vitro animal cell inference; no zonal YAP/TAZ localisation or conditional deletion readout in a postnatal growth plate; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), fetal
edges.notes: YAP/TAZ are the canonical stiffness- and tension-responsive transcriptional co-activators, and the growth plate has a steep (if disputed) zonal stiffness gradient plus a stereotyped stiffness-to-hypertrophy correspondence. That coincidence is the entire basis for the link.

edges.magnitude: static 10% strain caused notable LOSS of aggrecan immunostaining; dynamic 7-13% strain at 0.1 Hz at the same mean strain CONTRIBUTED to aggrecan synthesis in the extracellular matrix
edges.context: growth plate explants from distal ulnae of 4-week-old swine, unconfined compression, 48 h, matched mean compressive strain; species unknown, resting zone, proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), peripubertal (4-week-old)
edges.notes: The only study that reads out growth plate matrix protein against a controlled static/dynamic contrast. Readout is semi-quantitative immunohistochemistry with no reported effect size, in one species, at one age, for 48 h. It carries the whole loading-to-matrix seam.

edges.magnitude: static 10% strain caused notable loss of type II collagen expression; dynamic 7-13% at 0.1 Hz contributed to type II collagen synthesis
edges.context: swine ulnar growth plate explants, 4 weeks old, unconfined compression, 48 h; species unknown, resting zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), peripubertal (4-week-old)

edges.magnitude: static 10% strain caused notable loss of type X collagen expression; no preservation under dynamic loading was reported for collagen X, in contrast to aggrecan and collagen II
edges.context: swine ulnar growth plate explants, 4 weeks old, 48 h; collagen X marks the hypertrophic zone only; species unknown, sex unknown (not reported in source), peripubertal (4-week-old)
edges.notes: Consistent with the in vivo finding that compression shortens hypertrophic cells and thins the hypertrophic zone (e00003, e00014): the hypertrophic programme, not just its geometry, is suppressed.

edges.magnitude: chondrons bend and kink along their length under 20% (physiological), 30% and 40% compression, with the largest bending deformations at the reserve/proliferative zone interface
edges.context: bovine growth plate, ex vivo compression, structural deformation mapping along whole chondron lengths with texture correlation; species unknown, resting zone, proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Explains the previously reported nonuniform, apparently random strain fields inside a compressed physis as chondron bending. The authors propose that bending at the RZ/PZ interface is what aligns dividing cells longitudinally - i.e. that the matrix unit converts tissue compression into the rotation cue for column formation. That last step is a proposal, not a result.

edges.magnitude: collagen VI is first assembled at the cell surface and then displaced to form a shell at the pericellular/territorial matrix boundary; cell-surface-bound hyaluronan is required for the process
edges.context: mouse; 3D chondrocyte culture plus microfluidic cell-compression platforms plus genetic mouse models; chondrons generally rather than a zonally resolved growth plate; proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), fetal (E17.5)
edges.notes: The pericellular matrix through which load reaches the chondrocyte surface is itself built in a mechanoresponsive way, so the transducer and the transmission medium are not independent. Not demonstrated zonally in a growth plate.

edges.magnitude: loss of adhesion to type II collagen is one of the three proximate causes (with reduced fibronectin binding and abnormal F-actin) of the motility loss in beta1-null chondrocytes
edges.context: mouse, chondrocyte-specific Itgb1 inactivation; resting zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Identifies collagen II as the specific matrix ligand through which growth plate architecture is mechanically anchored.

edges.magnitude: reduced binding to and impaired spreading on fibronectin in beta1-null chondrocytes; alpha5beta1 integrin mediates the chondrocyte-fibronectin interaction and modulates proliferation
edges.context: mouse conditional null; in vitro animal chondrocytes; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: bovine physeal tensile strength and tangent modulus were measured at three strain rates and vary with rate; growth plate cartilage is viscoelastic and poroelastic so any modulus is rate-conditional
edges.context: bovine proximal tibia, 12-18 month heifer, 70 specimens, three strain rates (williams2001); rat proximal tibial explants under stress-controlled static vs dynamic compression (zimmermann2017); resting zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile, pubertal
edges.timescale: seconds to hours depending on the test
edges.notes: A stiffness value for the physis without a stated loading rate is not interpretable. Combined with the length-scale problem (e00097) this is most of why published moduli span three orders of magnitude.

edges.context: human, growing children; upright posture vs recumbency; no zone specified because none has been measured; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: The diurnal stature swing is fluid exudation. Cartilage is 66-80% water and the growth plate is poroelastic, so daily axial loading must move fluid in and out of physeal matrix - but water is the least-quantified variable in L5 and no one has measured a diurnal change in a physis.

edges.context: no species, zone or stage can be specified - the experiment has not been done in a growth plate; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Sustained load changes the mechanical demand on the collagen network, and lysyl-oxidase-derived pyridinoline crosslinks are what carry tensile load in cartilage. A Europe PMC sweep found no study measuring crosslink density or lysyl oxidase activity in a mechanically loaded growth plate in any species (g_l6l5_004). Written as speculative rather than omitted because the quantity is measurable with existing methods.

edges.context: porcine explant evidence only for aggrecan STAINING, not turnover; no radiolabel or racemization measurement under load in any species; bovine, resting zone, proliferative zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source), fetal, peripubertal (4-week-old)
edges.notes: sergerie2011 shows aggrecan immunostaining falls under static compression, which is consistent with either reduced synthesis or increased breakdown - the two possibilities the aggrecan turnover literature exists to separate, and which have never been separated under load.

edges.magnitude: compressed growth plates with reduced trabecular bone in the perinatal-lethal subset (~10.8% of nulls dying by week 3, a further subset by week 12); an earlier characterisation of the same null reported NO detectable difference in long bone growth
edges.context: mouse, Col10a1 homozygous null, variable penetrance; skeleto-haematopoietic phenotype; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), neonatal, juvenile (3-week old)
edges.notes: Two reports on the same null disagree on whether there is a phenotype at all. The atlas records the phenotype as real but subtle and incompletely penetrant, not as established.

edges.magnitude: COL10A1-/- human iPSC-derived chondrocytes undergo NORMAL hypertrophic differentiation in vitro and normal endochondral ossification after transplantation into immunodeficient mice
edges.context: human iPSC-derived chondrocytes, dual sgRNA CRISPR deletion, 3D pellet induction plus in vivo transplantation; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The decisive negative of this layer, and it is HUMAN. Collagen X is the canonical marker of hypertrophy and is largely dispensable FOR hypertrophy. Any model that makes collagen X the structural prerequisite for hypertrophy or for cartilage mineralization is contradicted by mouse null, human iPSC deletion and the mildness of Schmid MCD independently.

edges.magnitude: postnatal growth cessation in heterozygotes despite normal size at birth, attributable to decreased extracellular matrix and impaired growth plate chondrocyte hypertrophy
edges.context: mouse, Acan+/- (cartilage matrix deficiency, 7 bp microdeletion); postnatal; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Aggrecan is dosage-sensitive and the mechanism is architectural, not signalling: less matrix, smaller hypertrophic cells, less elongation. The heterozygote is the correct model because human ACAN disease is haploinsufficiency.

edges.magnitude: reduced extracellular matrix with impaired hypertrophy in Acan+/-; postnatal growth cessation
