edges.magnitude: >8,200 developmental differentially methylated regions; 24 loci where skeletal disease risk variants colocalise with methylation QTLs
edges.context: human, 72 developing chondrocyte samples 7-21 post-conception weeks, ~700,000 CpGs; zone unknown (organism-level readout, no zonal resolution), sex unknown (not reported in source), fetal, adult
edges.notes: Identifies a developmental-only regulatory class that would be invisible in adult-tissue eQTL catalogues - a specific route by which height-associated non-coding variants could act.

edges.magnitude: temporal coincidence only: PTHrP-creER resting chondrocytes go from 3.3% secondary colony-forming (17/518, none passageable) at a P9 pulse to robust self-renewal at a P12 pulse, spanning the days in which the murine SOC forms. No experiment has advanced, delayed or ablated SOC formation and measured the clonal consequence
edges.context: mouse proximal tibia and distal femur, P9-P12, sex not stated; resting zone. The human SOC of the distal femur is already present in 100% of fetuses after 35 weeks gestation, so the mouse temporal window has no human counterpart and the coincidence argument does not transfer; sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: days (mouse P9 to P12); prenatal in humans
edges.notes: Written as hypothesized_link deliberately. This is the load-bearing claim of the L2 stem-cell story and it currently rests on two mouse studies that report a correlation in time and nothing else. The species mismatch makes it worse rather than better: in humans the SOC forms before birth while the resting zone continues to function for another fifteen years.

edges.magnitude: Osterix-expressing osteoprogenitors migrate INTO the cartilage template along the invading vessels and become trabecular osteoblasts, whereas mature osteoblasts do not migrate; type H (CD31-high, endomucin-high) capillaries in the metaphysis are surrounded by osteoprogenitors and decline with age in parallel with bone formation
edges.context: mouse embryonic and postnatal long bone, both sexes; primary ossification centre and metaphysis. Not demonstrated in human tissue; zones resolved in source: perichondrium
edges.timescale: hours to days for progenitor co-migration with the vascular front
edges.notes: The first vascular invasion event is what installs the progenitor-carrying vasculature the later niche depends on; the coupling node itself is metaphyseal and postnatal, so this edge is the developmental antecedent rather than a restatement of it.

edges.magnitude: Col10a1- and Aggrecan-creER lineage tracing shows hypertrophic chondrocytes survive the chondro-osseous junction and become osteoblasts and osteocytes in the primary spongiosa during development, postnatal growth and fracture repair, so a fraction of trabecular bone is chondrocyte-derived rather than derived from perichondrial osteoprogenitors
edges.context: mouse long bone, embryonic through postnatal, both sexes; hypertrophic zone and primary spongiosa
edges.timescale: days (label appears in metaphyseal osteoblasts within ~3-7 days of a hypertrophic-zone pulse)
edges.notes: Two independent groups reaching the same conclusion with different Cre drivers in the same year. Still mouse-only: no human lineage tracing exists (see lineage_tracing_limitations), so the human fraction of chondrocyte-derived osteoblasts is unknown.

edges.magnitude: unmeasured. Fgfr3-creER pulsed at the condensation stage marks descendants that stay dorsally restricted in the resting and proliferative zones for the life of the plate, establishing that condensation-stage partitioning IS inherited; whether founder NUMBER sets the total division budget has never been measured in any species
edges.context: mouse limb bud condensation to postnatal growth plate, both sexes; whole element. The quantitative link asserted here has no measurement in mouse or human; zones resolved in source: resting zone, proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone, fetal, neonatal, juvenile, peripubertal (E17.5; 1-week-old/3 weeks old/4-week-old)
edges.timescale: the full growth period - embryonic condensation to fusion, i.e. weeks in mouse and ~15-18 years in human
edges.notes: This is the embryonic initial condition the finite-proliferative-capacity model needs and does not have. Recorded as hypothesized_link rather than omitted because the two halves of the claim are each demonstrated separately and only their product is missing.

edges.magnitude: the arithmetic that must close and never has: organism peak height velocity is 9.61 cm/yr at 12.46 y in boys and 8.32 cm/yr at 10.99 y in girls, and under the Hunziker formulation plate elongation equals chondrocyte production rate multiplied by terminal hypertrophic cell height. No published calculation multiplies HUMAN column density by HUMAN production rate by HUMAN terminal cell height and compares the product to measured human height velocity
edges.context: human, both sexes, puberty (organism side) versus rat and pig hypertrophic zone (cellular side); the species and the scale both change across this edge
edges.timescale: cm/yr at the organism against um/day at the cell - a 10^4 gap in the time unit, which is why the join has never been made
edges.notes: Distinct from e00001 in the canonical set (growth_velocity_curve -> growth_velocity_longitudinal), which is the summation across plates. This edge is the cell-kinetic decomposition WITHIN a plate, and it is the one the atlas exists to test.

edges.magnitude: a null that discriminates: 83-90% of catch-up episodes are fitted by a monomolecular function, the rate constant k differs by diagnosis (higher in coeliac disease than in either juvenile hypothyroidism or GH deficiency), but GH DOSE has no significant effect on k. The deficit, not the systemic drive, sets the catch-up rate
edges.context: human, prepubertal, both sexes, treated coeliac disease vs juvenile hypothyroidism vs GH deficiency; zone unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: k is expressed in reciprocal years; catch-up episodes run over 1-3 years and infant realignment onto the parental channel completes by about 2 years
edges.notes: The existing canonical edge canalization_growth -> delayed_senescence_hypothesis records the hypothesis this result SUPPORTS; this edge records the one it constrains. A neuroendocrine sizostat that senses the deficit and drives the endocrine axis harder predicts that raising GH dose raises k. It does not.

edges.magnitude: unmeasured in either direction. Catch-up in rabbit is accompanied by DELAYED growth plate senescence (capacity apparently conserved), while the finite-capacity model as usually stated implies catch-up spends capacity. No cohort has been followed from a resolved growth insult to attained adult height and physeal closure with both endpoints measured
edges.context: human prepubertal catch-up (wit2021, smith1976) against rabbit growth-restriction catch-up (gafni2001); no human plate-level capacity readout exists at any age; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: catch-up over 1-3 years; the cost, if any, would be paid 5-15 years later at fusion
edges.notes: This is the edge that decides whether L12's growth-promoting endpoints are honest. Every near-adult-height trial assumes catch-up is free.

edges.magnitude: a dissociation of 1.68 years: in untreated isolated GH deficiency, bone age is delayed by 1.99 years but dental age by only 0.31 years, and the extent of dental delay does not correlate with the extent of bone age delay. Independently, age at 90% dental maturity shows no significant correlation with peak height velocity
edges.context: human children with untreated isolated GH deficiency, both sexes (torliskawalkow2026); human mixed-sex maturity series (demirjian1985); zone unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: years - both clocks are read in years of maturational age, which is what makes the 1.68-year dissociation interpretable
edges.notes: An organism-level readout that bounds where GH acts. Dental development is a maturational clock that runs largely independently of the GH axis, so any model in which GH sets a global somatic maturation rate is falsified. It also supplies the control the bone-age literature lacks: a second, GH-insensitive maturity clock in the same child.

edges.magnitude: zero of the brain tissue classes show an adolescent volume spurt. Peak grey matter volume occurs at 5.9 years and peak white matter volume at 28.7 years, with peak total cerebrum volume at 12.5 years, against peak height velocity at 12.46 years (boys) and 10.99 years (girls). The organ that consumes the largest share of childhood energy does not participate in the pubertal spurt
edges.context: human, both sexes, birth to old age; brain MRI normative modelling of >100,000 scans (bethlehem2022) against SITAR height velocity cohorts (chun2024); zone unknown (not reported), fetal, neonatal, juvenile, pubertal
edges.timescale: years; the brain trajectory peaks are separated from peak height velocity by 6.6 years (grey matter) and 16 years (white matter)
edges.notes: Constrains L4: whatever produces the pubertal height spurt is a skeletal-tissue-specific signal, not a general anabolic or maturational drive, because the brain sees the same hormonal environment and does not spurt. Total cerebrum volume peaking at 12.5 y is a passive consequence of white matter still accruing, not a spurt.

edges.magnitude: peak lean mass velocity leads peak total-body bone mineral content velocity by 0.36 years in girls and 0.51 years in boys (0.71/0.63 y at the arms, 0.22/0.48 y at the legs), and peak lean mass velocity explains 50% of the variance in peak BMC velocity; peak HEIGHT velocity shows no independent association with peak BMC velocity once lean mass is accounted for
edges.context: human adolescents, both sexes, pubertal growth spurt; whole body and limb-segment DXA; perichondrium
edges.timescale: months to years - the lead time is 0.22-0.71 years depending on site and sex
edges.notes: Directs the muscle-bone coupling to the periosteal/appositional compartment rather than to the physis: bone MASS accrual follows muscle force with a measurable lag, while longitudinal growth velocity contributes nothing independent. This is an organism-level argument that mechanical loading acts on the bone envelope, not on plate elongation.

edges.magnitude: WITHDRAWN EVIDENCE (CORR-004). The in vivo demonstration - four weeks of food restriction raising tibial LEPROT/LEPROTL1, absent in Fgf21-knockout mice and restored by rhFGF21 add-back - came entirely from wu2013, which J Biol Chem withdrew in 2020. What survives is wu2012 alone: Klb, Fgfr1 and Fgfr3 mRNA are detectable in fetal and 3-week-old mouse growth plate chondrocytes, and rhFGF21 at 5-10 ug/ml suppresses thymidine incorporation, Col10a1 and 125I-GH binding in culture. In vitro presence at supraphysiological ligand does not establish that systemic energy state acts on the plate through this route in a living animal.
edges.context: mouse, 3 weeks to adult, sex not stated; tibial growth plate and primary growth plate chondrocyte culture. Not shown in human tissue; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: weeks - the in vivo induction requires 4 weeks of restriction
edges.notes: Was graded C as "the only DEMONSTRATED molecular entry point from the environment layer that does not route through GH/IGF-1 systemically". The demonstration was the knockout-plus-rescue design in the withdrawn paper. Converted to hypothesized_link rather than regraded, because without an in vivo result there is no demonstration left to grade. The consequence is that the L10-to-L3 seam this edge carried is now open, and that is the true state.

edges.magnitude: siRNA epistasis places the effect on FGFR1: knocking down FGFR1 (or ERK1) in cultured mouse growth plate chondrocytes abolishes the FGF21 actions measured in vitro - the fall in thymidine incorporation and Col10a1, the block on GH-stimulated proliferation, and the reduction in 125I-GH binding. The LEPROT/LEPROTL1 induction formerly listed here has been REMOVED: it came from wu2013, withdrawn in 2020 (CORR-004).
edges.context: cultured mouse growth plate chondrocytes, fetal and 3-week-old; rhFGF21 5-10 ug/ml; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Names the receptor arm rather than restating e00011. Graded D and not higher because the concentrations required (5-10 ug/ml) are orders of magnitude above human circulating FGF21 even in starvation, so the receptor assignment is secure but its physiological relevance is not. CORR-004: wu2013 removed from refs; the in vivo LEPROT arm of this claim is withdrawn. The in vitro receptor assignment rests on wu2012 and is unaffected, but see paralog_risk on klotho_beta_cofactor - FGFR3 was co-detected and never knocked down.

edges.magnitude: untested in humans. The mouse mechanism requires FGF21 at 5-10 ug/ml to inhibit chondrocytes, which is far above human circulating FGF21 even in starvation, and KLB has never been detected in human physeal cartilage. No study has measured FGF21 alongside height velocity in undernourished children CORR-004: the murine in vivo result that motivated this hypothesis is withdrawn (wu2013), which weakens the hypothesis further rather than removing it - the exposure question in humans was never answered either way.
edges.context: human stunted children (the exposure) against mouse growth plate chondrocytes (the only place the mechanism has been shown); no human physeal tissue has been examined; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: stunting accumulates over months to years; the murine mechanism operates over 4 weeks of restriction
edges.notes: Recorded as hypothesized_link, not as an edge with a sign one could act on. The human stunting literature attributes growth failure entirely to the GH/IGF-1 axis; this is the competing route and it has never been looked for in a child.

edges.magnitude: exactly TWO human growth plates have ever been examined histologically while physiological fusion was in progress - one distal tibia undergoing physiological epiphysiodesis studied by stereological histomorphometry (white2008, n=1) and one fusing plate within an apoptosis and electron-microscopy series (emons2009, n=1) - out of 30 catalogued human growth-plate studies
edges.context: human, adolescent, at physeal closure; whole plate. Provenance is surgical waste and autopsy, with no biobank; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: the fusion process itself takes months to a few years per site, and the two available specimens are single time points within it
edges.notes: Hard ceiling on the whole of L7. Every mechanistic statement about how the human growth plate closes - bony bridge formation, apoptosis at fusion, hypoxia and necrosis, ECM remodelling - is downstream of n=2. This is a supply constraint, not a knowledge gap that more analysis can close.

edges.magnitude: no human growth plate spatial transcriptomics exists. Every human zonal molecular assignment in this atlas derives either from laser-capture microdissection of n=2 donors (gse9160, distal femur, 11y10m female and 13y3m male, five zones) or from mouse spatial data, so any claim that a particular PDE isoform is zonally restricted in the human plate is an inference across both method and species
edges.context: human distal femur, peripubertal; RZ/PZ/PHZ/HZ/PERI. Mouse spatial data exist; human do not; sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: not applicable - a static expression-map constraint
edges.notes: Chosen as the target because the PDE inventory is where the atlas most wants zonal resolution (it determines which phosphodiesterase inhibitor could raise cGMP in the right zone) and where it has least.

edges.magnitude: no genetic fate mapping is possible in humans, so every human skeletal stem cell claim rests on prospective marker-based isolation followed by xenotransplantation, or on inference from single-cell and spatial profiling of static tissue - never on watching a labelled cell and its progeny in situ
edges.context: human, fetal and paediatric skeletal tissue; whole plate. The mouse hierarchy that defines the concept is built entirely on Cre-lox tracing that cannot be repeated in human; resting zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: the unobservable quantity is precisely the long one - clone lifetime and self-renewal over months to years
edges.notes: The asymmetry is the point: the mouse skeletal stem cell hierarchy is a lineage claim, the human one is a marker-and-transplant claim, and they are not the same kind of evidence. Any edge running from mouse SSC biology to human SSC biology inherits this.

edges.magnitude: the monoclonality of the human chondrocyte column has never been demonstrated. In mouse it is established by multicolour clonal reporters; in human it is inferred from column morphology and from static single-cell and spatial profiling of four donors aged 11-14 years
edges.context: human growth plate, peripubertal; proliferative zone columns; sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: a column represents days to weeks of clonal output; that history is exactly what static human data cannot recover
edges.notes: Marked as a method constraint on an L1 structural claim, because the word "clonal" in clonal_column is doing mouse work inside a human node.

edges.magnitude: hypertrophic chondrocytes are the cells most severely under-recovered by enzymatic dissociation - they are large, fragile and embedded in mineralising matrix - so the question of whether they survive the chondro-osseous junction or die there is the question that dissociation-based single-cell RNA-seq is structurally least able to answer
edges.context: multiple species, dissociation-based scRNA-seq of growth plate; hypertrophic zone and chondro-osseous junction; human, both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 3 sources), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: the transit through the hypertrophic zone takes hours to a few days, so the cells in question are a small and short-lived fraction even before dissociation loss
edges.notes: Distinct from the existing canonical edge chondrocyte_dissociation_bias -> hypertrophic_chondrocyte, which records the cell-recovery bias itself. This edge records what that bias does to a specific contested L2 claim: the survival-versus-apoptosis question at the junction cannot be settled by the method most often used to argue it.

edges.magnitude: the saltation-and-stasis claim asserts that growth occurs in discrete increments separated by days to weeks of stasis, and the increments asserted are of the same order as the measurement error of the instruments used to detect them; diurnal variation in standing height alone is several millimetres
edges.context: human infants and children, both sexes; whole-organism stature by stadiometry and knemometry. The dispute is entirely about measurement, not about biology; zone unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: the contested unit is exactly the sampling interval - daily to weekly measurement produces saltation, less frequent measurement does not
edges.notes: One of the few places in this atlas where a whole L1 hypothesis node is downstream of an instrument's noise floor rather than of a biological uncertainty. Recorded so the hypothesis is not read as settled biology.

edges.magnitude: the entire human zonal map of oestrogen receptor expression in the growth plate rests on immunohistochemistry in 32 donors across three studies (n=24 Tanner 1-5 proximal tibia; n=4 pubertal tibia and femur; n=4, two prepubertal girls and two adolescent boys), with no orthogonal confirmation by in situ hybridization or zonal transcriptomics
edges.context: human proximal tibia and distal femur, Tanner 1-5, both sexes; all zones; zones resolved in source: proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone, juvenile, pubertal
edges.timescale: not applicable - a static localization constraint
edges.notes: Oestrogen action on the human plate is the mechanism on which the whole of L7 fusion and much of L12 aromatase-inhibitor pharmacology depends, and its zonal anatomy is an IHC result in 32 children. Cartilage IHC has specific artefact modes (endogenous biotin, matrix trapping, fixation-dependent epitope loss) that this node catalogues.

edges.magnitude: a seasonal amplitude in height velocity can only be resolved if the measurement interval is shorter than the season being claimed; annualised velocities are mathematically incapable of showing it, and sub-annual intervals inflate apparent velocity variance because measurement error is divided by a shorter time base
edges.context: human children, both sexes, longitudinal auxology; whole organism; zone unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: the constraint IS a timescale - seasonal claims require intervals well under 3 months
edges.notes: L13 -> L4 was empty before this edge. Seasonality of growth velocity is a real and repeatedly reported phenomenon whose effect size is not separable from the sampling design used to measure it.

edges.magnitude: the prehypertrophic restriction of Ihh expression - the spatial fact on which the entire PTHrP/IHH negative feedback loop is built - is an in situ hybridization result. The human counterpart rests on IHC in a pubertal series with donor number not stated, plus the two-donor laser-capture zonal array
edges.context: mouse embryonic and postnatal long bone (stjacques1999, long2001) with human pubertal confirmation of uncertain n (kindblom2002); prehypertrophic zone; sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.timescale: not applicable - a static expression-domain constraint
edges.notes: L13 -> L3 was empty. The feedback loop is usually drawn as though the expression domains were measured directly in human; they were not.

edges.magnitude: the zonal modulus gradient of the human plate is an AFM nanoindentation result on hydrated cryosections: resting-zone cartilage 130.70 MPa (SD 36.56) stepping to 11920 MPa (SD 6.60 GPa) at epiphyseal bone, n=3 per interface with 4 areas each across 10 donors. Tip geometry, section thickness and hydration state each move the absolute values substantially
edges.context: human phalangeal and tibial growth plates, paediatric, both sexes; all zones and both interfaces; resting zone, hypertrophic zone (zonal localization of the interacting nodes, per their localization records), infant, childhood (0–5 years old/6–14 years old)
edges.timescale: indentation rate dependence matters - cartilage is poroviscoelastic, so the modulus reported depends on the loading timescale of the measurement
edges.notes: L13 -> L5 was empty. Every finite-element model of the physis takes its material properties from measurements of this kind, so the modelling layer inherits the method's assumptions without restating them.

edges.magnitude: the muscle-bone unit argument at puberty is a DXA result: peak lean mass velocity leading peak bone mineral content velocity by 0.22-0.71 years depending on site and sex, with 50% of peak BMC velocity variance explained. DXA measures areal rather than volumetric density and conflates size with density in growing children, which biases exactly the growth-phase comparison being made
edges.context: human adolescents, both sexes, pubertal spurt; whole body, arms and legs; zone unknown (organism-level readout, no zonal resolution)
edges.timescale: the lead time being measured (0.22-0.71 y) is of the same order as the spacing of annual DXA scans, so it is near the design's resolution
edges.notes: L13 -> L9 was empty. This edge and e00010 are deliberately paired: the organism-level conclusion and the instrument that produced it should not be separated.

edges.magnitude: the fetal metatarsal explant is the assay in which CNP and its analogues were shown to lengthen cartilage directly, and it is the bridge every NPR2 agonist programme crossed between receptor pharmacology and animal growth. It is a fetal, rodent, avascular, unloaded explant with no secondary ossification centre and no resting zone niche of the kind the postnatal human plate has
edges.context: fetal mouse and rat metatarsal, embryonic; whole rudiment. Applied to a class of drugs given to human children aged 2-15 with an intact postnatal physis; zones resolved in source: resting zone, proliferative zone, prehypertrophic zone, hypertrophic zone, perichondrium, both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 3 sources)
edges.timescale: explant assays run over days; the clinical endpoint they are used to predict is annualised growth velocity over years
edges.notes: L13 -> L12 was empty. The mismatch matters for the atlas's own CNP-analogue puzzle: an assay with no resting zone cannot report on resting-zone-mediated effects, which is one of the candidate explanations for why plasma exposure and growth response decouple in the clinic.

edges.magnitude: the niche is defined by position within the zone: PTHrP-expressing chondrocytes occupy the resting zone specifically, and the zone provides the WNT-inhibitory microenvironment in which those cells stay undifferentiated. Removing the zone removes the niche by construction, and resting zone transplantation experiments show the zone induces columnar organisation in the tissue beneath it
edges.context: mouse distal femur and proximal tibia, postnatal, both sexes; resting zone; neonatal, juvenile, adult (P4-P56)
edges.timescale: the niche property is a standing state maintained over the whole growth period, not an event
edges.notes: L1 -> L2 had zero edges before this. The architectural zone and the stem-cell niche are deliberately separate nodes - one is a histological compartment, the other a functional claim about the cells in it - and the dependency between them was never written down.

edges.magnitude: the epiphyseal vessels reaching the plate through cartilage canals are the delivery route for the vascular signals the niche depends on; type H capillaries are surrounded by osteoprogenitors and their decline with age parallels the decline in bone formation
edges.context: mouse metaphysis and epiphysis, postnatal to aged, both sexes; type H vessel compartment. The human cartilage canal is described anatomically but the coupling is not demonstrated in human; zone unknown (not reported), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.timescale: the type H decline runs over the animal's lifespan (months in mouse), so this is a slow structural variable, not a signalling event
edges.notes: Complements e00002, which is the developmental installation of the same coupling. This edge is its postnatal maintenance.

edges.magnitude: a defined fraction of hypertrophic chondrocytes escape apoptosis at the chondro-osseous junction and become osteoblasts and osteocytes in the primary spongiosa, demonstrated independently with Col10a1-creER and with Aggrecan-creER lineage tracing
edges.context: mouse long bone, embryonic through postnatal growth and fracture repair, both sexes; hypertrophic zone
edges.timescale: days - labelled progeny appear in metaphyseal bone within roughly one week of a pulse
edges.notes: The cell-type-to-process edge that L1 and L2 both needed and neither carried. Mouse only; the human fraction is unknown because no human lineage tracing is possible (see e00016, e00017).

edges.magnitude: PTHrP-creER-marked resting chondrocytes generate the columnar clones of the proliferative zone after the secondary ossification centre forms; before it, the same pulse produces short-lived clones that are not maintained. The switch is sharp between a P9 and a P12 pulse
edges.context: mouse distal femur and proximal tibia, P9 onward, both sexes; resting to proliferative zone
edges.timescale: clones become detectable as columns over days and are maintained for weeks to months in mouse
edges.notes: L2 -> L1 had zero edges before this. This is the single most consequential cross-layer claim in the stem-cell story - it is what makes the resting zone a source rather than a reserve - and it was previously implicit.

edges.magnitude: senescence is a coordinated programme, not a passive failure: functional, structural and molecular senescent changes occur EARLIER in the plates of small bones (metacarpals, phalanges) than of large bones (femur, tibia), with corresponding modulation of IGF, BMP and WNT paracrine signalling, and this differential timing helps set skeletal proportions. Suppressing proliferation with dexamethasone in rabbit DELAYS both senescence and fusion, showing the decline is indexed to divisions rather than to elapsed time
edges.context: mouse and rat, postnatal, small versus large bones (lui2018); rabbit, growth-restricted and control (gafni2001); all zones; proliferative zone, both sexes (male and female) (sex reported in 1 of 3 sources), fetal, neonatal, juvenile, peripubertal (E17.5; 1-week-old/3 weeks old/4-week-old)
edges.timescale: weeks to months in rodent and rabbit; the equivalent human process runs over years and has never been measured directly
edges.notes: The direction matters: senescence is written here as acting ON proliferation rate, which is what the replication-counting model requires, rather than as a synonym for slow growth.

edges.magnitude: the architectural process of column formation - post-mitotic rotation and stacking of daughter cells into a single file - is downstream of the clonal process: a column is the physical trace of one progenitor's output, so the clonality result constrains what column-forming mechanisms are admissible
edges.context: mouse postnatal growth plate, both sexes; resting to proliferative zone transition; juvenile, pubertal
edges.timescale: a daughter pair rotates into column alignment within hours of division; the column accumulates over days
edges.notes: Written as required_for rather than correlates_with because a polyclonal column would falsify the mechanism, not merely weaken the correlation.

edges.magnitude: tibial linear growth rate reduced ~65% in Ghr-null vs ~35% in Igf1-null between P20 and P40; chondrocyte proliferation and chondrocyte number significantly reduced in Ghr-null only
edges.context: mouse, proximal tibial growth plate, proliferative zone, postnatal days 20-40 (peak GH effect); sex not stated; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The Ghr-null/Igf1-null contrast is the cleanest available separation of GH-dependent from IGF-1-dependent chondrocyte proliferation: proliferation is normal in Igf1-null but reduced in Ghr-null.

edges.magnitude: germinal (resting) zone hypoplastic in Ghr-null mice; the same zone is ENLARGED in Igf1-null mice
edges.context: mouse, proximal tibial growth plate, resting/germinal zone, postnatal days 20-40; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Opposite-direction phenotypes in Ghr-null and Igf1-null germinal zones are the strongest single argument that GH acts on the resting zone by an IGF-1-independent route.

edges.magnitude: labelled-cell ratio (GH leg / contralateral control leg) 1.95 +/- 0.13 after 12 d local intratibial GH (1 ug/day) with continuous [3H]thymidine
edges.context: hypophysectomised rat, proximal tibial germinal (resting) zone, local unilateral infusion; contralateral leg internal control; sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile, pubertal (75-day-old)
edges.notes: Chu 2025 reaches the opposite net effect on pool size in mouse (GH DEPLETES the slow-cycling pool by driving committed division) while agreeing that GH acts directly on these cells; the two are reconcilable if GH drives their division rather than their self-renewal.

edges.magnitude: NULL RESULT: labelled-cell ratio 0.96 +/- 0.04 after 12 d local intratibial IGF-I (10 ug/day) - no stimulation of the slowly cycling germinal cells, versus 1.95 +/- 0.13 for GH in the same experiment
edges.context: hypophysectomised rat, proximal tibial germinal/resting zone, local unilateral infusion; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: This is a scientific null and is the discriminating datum for the dual effector hypothesis: IGF-I acts only on the proliferation of chondrocytes already recruited out of the germinal layer.

edges.magnitude: conditional Ghr deletion in growth plate stem cells impairs their ability to generate chondrocytes; GH reduces the slow-cycling label-retaining pool by promoting committed division
edges.context: mouse, growth plate resting zone stem cells, postnatal; multiple transgenic lineage-tracing lines; sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile, pubertal (75-day-old)
edges.notes: Offers a mechanistic account of the declining long-term efficacy of GH therapy: sustained GH depletes the stem pool.

edges.magnitude: pulsatile GH (1.5 U/kg/day, one pulse per 3 h, 5 d) raised IGF-I mRNA 3-5 fold in rib growth plate and skeletal muscle; continuous infusion at the same dose was much less effective. In liver both patterns were equally effective.
edges.context: hypophysectomised male rat on T4 and glucocorticoid replacement, rib growth plate; 5-day patterned i.v. infusion; zone unknown (not reported), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Tissue-specific pattern decoding: the growth plate reads GH pulse shape, the liver does not. Direct experimental support for gh_pulse_pattern_hypothesis at the plate.

edges.magnitude: GH-stimulated IGF-1 expression in growth plate chondrocytes requires Stat5b; NF-kB p65 co-immunoprecipitates with Stat5b and the NF-kB inhibitor PDTC neutralises GH-driven metatarsal elongation and chondrogenesis
edges.context: rat, cultured metatarsal bones and primary growth plate chondrocytes; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: GH induction of BMP-2 expression in growth plate chondrocytes is lost when NF-kB p65 (a Stat5b partner) is inhibited
edges.context: rat, growth plate chondrocytes and cultured metatarsals; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: One of very few demonstrated routes from a systemic hormone into the BMP arm of the local network.

edges.magnitude: SOCS2, but not SOCS1 or SOCS3, transcript increased in cultured chondrocytes after GH challenge
edges.context: mouse, primary epiphyseal/growth plate chondrocytes and embryonic metatarsals; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Establishes the delayed negative-feedback loop locally within cartilage, not only in liver.

edges.magnitude: GH-stimulated chondrocyte STAT1, STAT3 and STAT5 phosphorylation increased in Socs2-/- chondrocytes and abolished in SOCS2-overexpressing cells
edges.context: mouse, primary chondrocytes; gain- and loss-of-function; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), peripubertal (6-week-old)

edges.magnitude: Socs2-/- growth plates 24% wider (P<0.001); tibiae 8% longer (P<0.001) and 18% broader (P<0.001); mice 6% longer overall
edges.context: mouse, 7-week-old Socs2-/- vs wild-type littermates, tibia; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), neonatal, peripubertal (1-day-old; 6-week-old)

edges.magnitude: proliferative zone 10% wider (P<0.05) in Socs2-/- tibia; chondrocyte proliferation increased in Socs2-/- at 6 weeks
edges.context: mouse, 6-7 week-old Socs2-/- vs wild-type, tibial growth plate; proliferative zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), neonatal, peripubertal (1-day-old; 6-week-old)

edges.magnitude: hypertrophic zone 14% wider (P<0.001) in Socs2-/- tibia; increased number of phospho-STAT5-positive hypertrophic chondrocytes
edges.context: mouse, 6-7 week-old Socs2-/- vs wild-type, tibial growth plate; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), neonatal, peripubertal (1-day-old; 6-week-old)

edges.magnitude: Igf2 expression elevated by GH in Socs2-/- (but not wild-type) metatarsals, while Igf1 transcript and protein were unchanged; GH failed to promote growth when the IGF receptor was blocked
edges.context: mouse, embryonic and postnatal metatarsal organ culture, 12 days; zones resolved in source: proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone, perichondrium, male only
edges.notes: Suggests the local GH growth effect is IGF-receptor-dependent but IGF-1-INdependent, with IGF-2 as the candidate ligand.

edges.magnitude: in uraemic rats growth plate JAK2 protein fell while GHR and STAT5 protein were unchanged, alongside reduced growth plate IGF-I and VEGF immunostaining and a widened hypertrophic zone
edges.context: rat, 5/6 nephrectomy vs pair-fed control, 20 days old, tibial growth plate; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile (20-day-old)
edges.notes: Locates the lesion of uraemic GH resistance at JAK2 within the plate, not at the receptor.

edges.magnitude: Socs2-/- mice show accelerated growth plate fusion and increased osteoarthritis vulnerability despite greater bone length
edges.context: mouse, Socs2-/- vs wild type, postnatal to adult; zones resolved in source: proliferative zone, hypertrophic zone, male only
edges.notes: SOCS2 presence DELAYS fusion: its loss accelerates it. Growth acceleration and premature fusion travel together here, which is the same trade-off seen with estrogen.

edges.magnitude: proliferating chondrocyte cycle time shortened from 11 d (untreated hypophysectomised) to 4.5 d with IGF-I and to 3 d with GH; stem-cell cycle time 50 d -> 15 d (IGF-I) and 8 d (GH)
edges.context: hypophysectomised rat, proximal tibial growth plate, proliferative and germinal zones; quantitative autoradiography and stereology; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Sign '-' because the parameter is a duration: IGF-I shortens it. The rare case where an endocrine input is quantified as a cell-cycle time rather than a labelling index.

edges.magnitude: proliferating cell cycle time 11 d -> 3 d; stem cell cycle time 50 d -> 8 d under GH infusion
edges.context: hypophysectomised rat, proximal tibial growth plate, germinal and proliferative zones; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: duration of the hypertrophic phase shortened from 6 d to 4 d with IGF-I and to 2.8 d with GH
edges.context: hypophysectomised rat, proximal tibial hypertrophic zone; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: hypertrophic phase duration 6 d -> 2.8 d under GH
edges.context: hypophysectomised rat, proximal tibial hypertrophic zone; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes 30% smaller in linear dimension in Igf1-null mice, accounting for most of the 35% deficit in long bone growth rate; hypertrophic cells smaller at every level of the zone

edges.magnitude: rising 1,25(OH)2D between 2 and 5 weeks coincides with resolution of rachitic hypertrophic zone expansion in Npt2a-null mice; the effect is VDR-dependent
edges.context: mouse Npt2a-null model of hypophosphataemia, tibial growth plate; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: FGF23 binding to FGFR3 was ENHANCED in the presence of soluble alpha-Klotho; knocking down FGFR3 abolished the FGF23/sKL suppression of metatarsal growth, as did neutralising anti-FGF23 antibody

edges.notes: Answers the question directly: in CARTILAGE the FGF23 receptor is FGFR3, not the FGFR1c used in the proximal renal tubule. FGF23 therefore converges on exactly the receptor whose gain-of-function causes achondroplasia.

edges.magnitude: FGF23 alone did not suppress metatarsal growth; suppression required co-incubation with soluble alpha-Klotho, which forms a complex with FGF23 via the KL1 repeat and enhances FGF23-FGFR3 binding
edges.context: mouse metatarsal explant culture; Hyp mouse in vivo for the sKL arm; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: FGF23 plus soluble alpha-Klotho suppressed metatarsal linear growth and reduced chondrocyte proliferation; intraperitoneal sKL in Hyp mice shortened the proliferating zone and reduced proliferation WITHOUT altering circulating phosphate
edges.context: mouse, metatarsal explants and Hyp (XLH model) mice in vivo; proliferative zone; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: Phosphate-independent: this dissociates the growth defect of XLH from the mineralisation defect, and predicts that burosumab should improve growth by more than phosphate correction alone.

edges.magnitude: length of the proliferating zone diminished by FGF23/sKL ex vivo and by i.p. sKL in Hyp mice
edges.context: mouse, tibial/metatarsal growth plate, proliferative zone; sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)

edges.magnitude: FGF23/sKL suppressed Ihh expression and exogenous Ihh protein PARTIALLY rescued the suppression of metatarsal growth
edges.context: mouse metatarsal explant culture; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: IHH is therefore a shared downstream node for FGF23, glucocorticoid (e00065) and mTORC1/nutrition (e00036) - three unrelated systemic inputs converging on one local ligand.

edges.magnitude: not measured
edges.context: growth plate cartilage; FGF23, Klotho and FGFR1 are all detectable in porcine growth plate by qPCR and immunohistochemistry, but no functional test of FGFR1 as the cartilage FGF23 receptor exists; species unknown, zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), peripubertal (6-week-old)
edges.notes: Raimann shows the components are co-located; Kawai shows the FUNCTION runs through FGFR3. Whether FGFR1c carries any of the signal in cartilage is untested.

edges.magnitude: FGF23 forms a protein complex with soluble alpha-Klotho through the KL1 internal repeat

edges.magnitude: leptin 0.5-1.0 ug/mL widened the chondroprogenitor zone by up to 64% in a dose-dependent manner with increased BrdU incorporation; HIGHER concentrations were inhibitory. Leptin also stimulated proliferation of isolated fetal rat osteoblasts and chondrocytes at >=1e-11 M.

edges.notes: Genuinely biphasic in the same experiment, which matters because obese children have chronically high leptin - the descending limb may be the physiologically relevant one.

edges.magnitude: leptin increased IGF-I receptor protein and mRNA in condylar chondrocytes and the progenitor population; in calorie-restricted mice leptin produced a marked increase in growth plate IGF-IR expression
edges.context: mouse mandibular condyle and tibial growth plate; 60%-of-normal chow restriction model; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source), juvenile
edges.notes: A concrete mechanism for how an adipose-derived energy signal sets the plate's GAIN on the somatotropic axis rather than acting as a growth factor in its own right.

edges.magnitude: leptin increased overall epiphyseal growth plate size by 11% and gave significantly greater tibial length than untreated pair-fed animals; in adult male mice 20 injections of 43 ug/day over 4 weeks increased growth plate thickness

edges.magnitude: testosterone INHIBITED [3H]thymidine uptake by cultured human long-bone growth plate chondrocytes, in the same screen in which IGF-I, IGF-II, TGF-beta, FGF-1, FGF-2, FGF-18 and PDGF-BB were potent stimulators and FGF-10 and BMP-2/-4/-6 were inhibitors

edges.notes: Direction is opposite to the clinical picture of the male pubertal growth spurt, and consistent with the view that the spurt is driven by AROMATISED estrogen plus GH amplification rather than by androgen acting on the chondrocyte. Reinforced by chagin2009, in which AR agonism and antagonism had no effect on cultured fetal rat metatarsal elongation.

edges.magnitude: NULL RESULT: neither AR agonists nor AR antagonists altered longitudinal growth of cultured fetal rat metatarsal bones, despite AR protein being demonstrable in 41-65% of human growth plate chondrocytes depending on zone
edges.context: fetal rat metatarsal organ culture (functional test) versus human proximal tibial growth plate biopsies, Tanner 1-5, both sexes (expression); proliferative zone
edges.notes: Receptor presence without demonstrable function. The largest unexplained discrepancy in the sex-steroid arm of this seam.

edges.magnitude: insulin significantly enhanced fetal rat metatarsal growth, and rapamycin abolished the response through a selective effect on the hypertrophic zone with no change in BrdU incorporation
edges.context: fetal rat (E19-E20) metatarsal explant; hypertrophic zone, sex unknown (not reported in source)

edges.magnitude: in human primary chondrocytes FGF21 upregulated basal and GH-induced SOCS2 and inhibited GH-induced STAT5 phosphorylation and GH-induced COL2 and ALP expression; serum FGF21 was inversely associated with change in length SD score in very preterm infants (beta -0.415, P<0.005)
edges.context: human paediatric primary chondrocytes in vitro; observational cohort of very preterm infants from birth to term-equivalent age; zone unknown (not reported), sex unknown (not reported in source)
edges.notes: Supersedes nothing but adds the human arm: SOCS2-mediated local GH resistance in cartilage is demonstrable in HUMAN chondrocytes and correlates with human linear growth failure, not only in Socs2-null mice.

edges.magnitude: not measured
edges.context: growth plate chondrocyte; MCT8 is the canonical T3 transporter but growth is largely normal in human MCT8 deficiency, and in mouse ATDC5 cells and resting-zone chondrocytes Mct10 (not Mct8) is the abundant transporter, with Mct10 knockdown reducing T3 uptake by up to 44% (P<0.05); sex unknown (not reported in source), age/stage unknown (not reported)
edges.notes: The transporter that actually gates T3 entry into human growth plate chondrocytes has not been identified. If it is MCT10 rather than MCT8, the normal stature of Allan-Herndon-Dudley patients is explained and the cartilage T3 supply is under separate genetic control from brain T3 supply.

edges.magnitude: 14q32.2 hypomethylation lowers IGF2 expression at 11p15.5, producing a transcriptional signature shared with Silver-Russell syndrome
edges.context: human, 60 genetically confirmed Temple syndrome patients (31 UPD(14)mat, 22 epimutation, 5 deletion); zone unknown (organism-level readout, no zonal resolution), both sexes (male and female), fetal, juvenile, childhood, pubertal, adult (6 years old; mean age 4.8 year; mean age 36 year)
edges.notes: Single transcriptional-profiling study for the trans effect; graded D on that basis even though the Temple phenotype itself is A-grade.

edges.magnitude: chondrocyte-specific Adrb2 knockout accelerates the proliferative-to-hypertrophic transition, which the authors give as the most likely cause of the reduced long bone growth; so intact beta-2 signalling RESTRAINS the transition. Direction only - no rate was extracted
edges.context: mouse, chondrocyte-specific conditional knockout, tibia and femur at 6, 12 and 40 weeks; both sexes (male and female); zones resolved in source: proliferative zone, prehypertrophic zone, hypertrophic zone; juvenile, adult
edges.timescale: weeks to months - phenotype read at 6, 12 and 40 weeks
edges.notes: Closes the coverage gap the Phase 7 run generated: the atlas had NO autonomic input to the growth plate and no gap asserting the absence. Graded D - one conditional knockout, no replication, no human data. The systemic and osteoblast-specific knockouts of the same receptor move bone mass the OPPOSITE way, so this sign is specific to the cartilage compartment.

edges.magnitude: chondrocyte-specific Adrb2 knockout reduces long bone growth (direction only)
edges.context: mouse, chondrocyte-specific conditional knockout; both sexes (male and female); zone unknown (organism-level readout, no zonal resolution); juvenile, adult
edges.notes: See g_l3adrn_001 - no human observation of any kind exists for this link.

edges.magnitude: in 543 children with CKD stages 2-4 with 2-3 biannual measurements each, plasma c-terminal FGF23 was stable in most; children in rapidly-rising FGF23 trajectory groups had lower eGFR, higher serum phosphorus, proteinuria and anaemia, and FGF23 trajectory independently predicted progression to kidney failure
edges.context: human, 543 children, CKD in Children (CKiD) study, median age 12 y at enrolment, CKD stages 2-4; zone unknown (organism-level readout, no zonal resolution); sex unknown (not reported in source); juvenile, pubertal
edges.timescale: years - biannual sampling with longitudinal trajectory modelling
edges.notes: Closes the FGF23/CKD-MBD coverage gap: both endpoint nodes existed and no edge joined them. correlates_with and sign unknown DELIBERATELY - this is an observational trajectory association with kidney-failure progression, not a demonstration that FGF23 causes the growth failure, and signing it would assert more than the study shows. traversal_usable stays false by relation type, which is the correct consequence.

wu2013.retraction_reason_resolved: AUTHOR WITHDRAWAL for DATA INTEGRITY, not editorial retraction and not an interpretation failure. Withdrawn by Wu, Kharitonenkov, Dam, Jockers and De Luca; Tal Grunwald could not be reached. Stated grounds, verbatim in substance: in Fig 1C lanes 1 and 2 of the actin immunoblot are the same as lanes 3 and 4; in Fig 2C lanes 1 and 4 of the LEPROT immunoblot are the same and lanes 1 and 3 of the LEPROTL1 immunoblot are the same; and there is a splice in the LEPROTL1 immunoblot. The authors affirm the results and conclusions reflect the work done in their laboratory, and withdrew to preserve the accuracy of the literature. DISPOSITION CONSEQUENCE: the duplicated and spliced blots ARE the LEPROT/LEPROTL1 measurement the atlas depended on, so the observation does not survive the interpretation. both_invalid is now EVIDENCED rather than defaulted.
